      -> omp-orchestrator-815 (41 acceptance lines, 41 absent from description)
         omp-orchestrator-phase0-pane-observation-80h (1 of 1 absent)

Dispatch `815` through this renderer and the pane receives a packet with **zero** of its 41 acceptance lines. AGENTS.md:205-207 mandates `br update --acceptance` for added scope — the field the doctrine writes to is the field the renderer does not read.

**The hand path has the inverse defect and no renderer to borrow.** 26 hand packets, `wc -c` range 1238–5827: **26/26** carry FROM + traps/measured failure shapes (18/26 `measured`, 11/26 `TRAPS`), 13/26 a why-now, 15/26 an acceptance bar; **0/26 a stop condition, 0/26 a done command with exit code** (5/26 mention an exit code, all describing prior evidence not the done signal), 2/26 a Skills field (`d-8e1g.md:23-30`, `p5.md:42-47`), 8/26 an honest out. One packet (`d-8e1g.md:32-44`, "ACCEPTANCE (mine, on top of the bead's)") added five acceptance items of which three — same-verdict-on-six-runs, `$ZS_SCRATCH` paths, "state the denominator" — are absent from bead `8e1g` (`br show omp-orchestrator-8e1g --json | jq -r '.[0].description' | grep -ciE 'same verdict|denominator|ZS_SCRATCH'` → 0): the AGENTS.md:194-207 class, live again. One packet (`p5.md`) names no bead at all — AGENTS.md:182-184, a message not a dispatch.

**So the two authorities are complementary halves and neither is complete:** the supervisor packet carries the bead verbatim and nothing about the dispatch; the hand packet carries everything about the dispatch and restates the bead from memory. The contract is one packet with both halves. A field that lives only in hand-written markdown is the `93lo` failure shape (AGENTS.md:241-244): no gate reads it, no test covers it, no schema requires it.

## WHY

A packet without a stop condition cannot end except by the pane's judgement; a packet without a done signal cannot be graded except by re-deriving what "done" meant; a packet that drops the typed acceptance field makes `br update --acceptance` a write nobody reads. Pass 1's `S5 template = Y` is a vacuous Y. And 12-journey.md:1206-1214 already measured this in the same repo: three packets that carried the bar produced three passing artifacts, the one that omitted it produced the one that failed — "packet quality determined output quality with zero exceptions."

## ACCEPTANCE

1. `send_and_verify` (or a function it calls, in `crates/omp-orchestrator`) renders the packet through the registered `dispatch` template or a typed struct with the same required set: `objective`, `target`, `scope`, `acceptance`, `stop` MUST be non-empty or the render REFUSES with a typed error naming the empty field. Positive control: rendering bead `zrq` succeeds. Known-bad: a `BeadSnapshot` with empty acceptance renders `Err(PacketFieldMissing("acceptance"))`, not a packet.
2. `acceptance` is populated from the typed `acceptance_criteria` field FIRST, falling back to the description's `ACCEPTANCE:` block only when the field is empty. `BrShowRow` gains `acceptance_criteria: Option<String>`. Fires-on-known-bad: render bead `omp-orchestrator-815` and assert all 41 acceptance lines are in the packet; the current renderer emits 0 of them.
3. The packet carries a **Done signal** line: the bead's own proof command and expected exit code where the bead states one, else the literal `Done: br comments add <bead> --actor <you> "DONE ..." then the grader re-runs the bead's acceptance` — never absent. And a **Stop** line: `Stop: when acceptance is met, when blocked on a named external, or when the packet contradicts the bead — say which.`
4. The hand path uses the same renderer: a `omp-orchestrator dispatch render --bead <id> --pane <%N> [--why-now ...] [--traps-file ...]` subcommand emits the packet to stdout so a human sends what the loop sends, plus the human's why-now/traps as additional sections. The additional sections are NON-NORMATIVE by construction: the renderer REFUSES a traps file containing an `ACCEPTANCE` heading or a numbered `must`/`MUST` list with a typed `PacketAddsScope` error pointing at `br update <id> --acceptance-criteria` — added scope goes into the bead first (AGENTS.md:205-207), then the renderer carries it. Known-bad: `/tmp/d-8e1g.md:32-44` as the traps file is refused. Falsifier for the whole bead: **a packet rendered after this lands — by either path — that lacks Stop, Done, or the typed acceptance, or that carries an acceptance item the bead does not.**
5. Fires-on-known-bad in `cargo test -p omp-orchestrator`: mutate the `format!` to drop the Stop line; the render test goes RED. Restore byte-identically and paste the sha.
6. Anti-vacuity: the test corpus includes at least one bead whose `acceptance_criteria` is non-empty and NOT duplicated in its description (815's shape); a suite that only exercises duplicated beads cannot distinguish the fix from the current renderer.

## NOT IN SCOPE

- The ACK instruction line: `93lo` (open) — that bead's acceptance 2 names "the dispatch site emitting the instruction itself"; this bead does not restate it. When both land, the ACK line MUST use the receiver-derived form (`$TMUX_PANE`), which is a third bead filed alongside this one.
- The FROM line: `dispatch-from-line-mad1` (open).
- The S6 grade packet: `8zx1` (open).
- The packet journal (`docs/plan/DISPATCH.jsonl`, 12-journey.md:330-332): `test -s docs/plan/DISPATCH.jsonl` → absent today; that is S5's own PROJECTED done signal and stays in `kxe`.

## NO-CLAIM

A complete packet makes the assignment LEGIBLE, not done. All 8 supervisor packets today were acted on despite lacking every field named here (7/8 were ACKed, 1/8 closed without an ACK) — the fields buy gradeability and a bounded stop, not delivery. And rendering the typed acceptance proves the packet CARRIES it, not that the grader reads it: AGENTS.md:209-211 records a grader skipping an item the bead carried.

title: P0: 83% of ACK_STAGE_INDETERMINATE verdicts are FALSE NEGATIVES -- the ACK census runs at send time, before a worker can answer; 87 of 105 beads have the ACK now
description:
WHAT: evaluate the ACK read-back census after a bounded wait instead of at send time, so a
DISPATCH_UNCONFIRMED_ACK_PENDING verdict means "the receiver did not answer" rather than "we asked
before it could".

WHY -- measured 2026-09-06 by pane 1, and it invalidates a whole class of verdicts:

  heartbeat rows naming ACK_STAGE_INDETERMINATE / ACK_CENSUS_EMPTY:  224
  distinct beads implicated:                                         105
  ACK comment EXISTS now (verdict was a FALSE NEGATIVE):              87
  ACK comment still absent (genuinely unproven):                      18
  false-negative rate:                                               83%

POSITIVE CONTROL: the probe found 18 genuine misses, so it discriminates. A probe that reported
zero misses would prove nothing.

THE TRIGGERING OBSERVATION, end to end on one bead. At t78 the loop dispatched
omp-orchestrator-3w9l to %7 and reported
`status=DISPATCH_UNCONFIRMED_ACK_PENDING detail=ACK_STAGE_INDETERMINATE comment read-back:
ACK_CENSUS_EMPTY`. Read one minute later, that bead carries exactly the comment the contract
demands: `ACK 3w9l on %7 --`, 1 occurrence, 3 comments total. The worker answered correctly; the
census asked too early.

TWO HYPOTHESES I TESTED AND REFUTED before filing this:

1. "The loop does not emit the ACK instruction" (the omp-orchestrator-93lo shape). REFUTED: the
   installed binary at ~/.local/bin/omp-orchestrator carries 7 `ACK ` literals (positive control:
   `DOCS_STALE` appears 3 times in the same strings output). 93lo fix is LIVE.
2. "The receiver never answers on the tmux literal path". REFUTED: 87 of 105 answered, and three
   packets I hand-sent this evening with the same byte-exact prefix got 3/3 ACKs
   (kt0m/%7, drte/%8, 7uvs/%9).

So neither the sender nor the receiver is at fault. The VERIFIER is.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND OBSERVABILITY. An unconfirmed dispatch withholds its pane for up to 600s
(pending-dispatch marker) and then drives DISPATCH_SILENCE -> REASSIGNED. Pane %9 took five
consecutive silence-then-reassign cycles tonight. At an 83% false-negative rate, that cascade was
re-dispatching work that had already been acknowledged -- capacity loss caused by the measurement,
not by the fleet. This is the same family as the unreaped-completion defect: a correct worker whose
completion the system cannot see.

THE SHAPE TO ADOPT. canonical-cli-scoping names this operator directly: `Two-Phase-Latency`.
Phase 1 records the send; phase 2 evaluates the receipt after a bounded, cancellable wait. The
asupersync contract already requires bounded waits with &Cx first and checkpoints around effects,
and crates/subprocess-contract owns bounded child execution -- do not hand-roll a sleep.
ack-stage is explicit that the tmux literal fallback is ALWAYS INDETERMINATE on receiver
heuristics alone (crates/ack-stage/src/lib.rs:290-291) and that the ACK comment is the only
evidence the design admits (:243-253, :308-320). None of that changes; only WHEN the comment is
read changes.

NOT-GOALS: does not weaken the ACK requirement, does not accept a timer reset or content hash as
proof, does not touch the 18 genuinely-unproven beads (those are the real signal this fix
uncovers), and does not change the 600s withholding policy.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE -- hand-written for this subject; no shared tail.

1. THE FALSE-NEGATIVE RATE IS REPRODUCED, THEN DRIVEN DOWN. A committed measurement recomputes, over
   the heartbeat log, the four figures: rows naming ACK_STAGE_INDETERMINATE/ACK_CENSUS_EMPTY,
   distinct beads, beads whose ACK exists now, and beads still absent. On the current log it MUST
   reproduce 224 / 105 / 87 / 18. After the fix, a NEW dispatch that receives an ACK within the
   bounded window MUST be recorded as confirmed, not indeterminate. Show one such row.

2. THE WAIT IS BOUNDED AND CANCELLABLE. The receipt phase takes &Cx first, checkpoints around the
   wait, and has an explicit deadline. No bare sleep, no unbounded poll, no detached task. Reuse
   crates/subprocess-contract for any child; per AGENTS.md a timeout is NOT a verdict -- an elapsed
   deadline must map to a distinct typed outcome, never to the token a genuinely silent receiver
   produces.

3. THE TWO OUTCOMES ARE DISTINGUISHABLE. After the fix, "receiver answered late" and "receiver never
   answered" MUST be different typed values with different tokens in the lifecycle row. Collapsing
   them reproduces the defect one layer down -- the no_distinct_idle_peer failure, where one reason
   code covered four causes.

4. FIRES ON KNOWN-BAD, IN-TREE SPECIMEN. A test dispatches against a fixture receiver that never
   posts an ACK and asserts the verdict is unconfirmed AFTER the full window elapses -- not before.
   In-tree fixture only; NEVER an applied .patch, because git apply silently no-ops when the index
   hash misses HEAD and a known-bad that cannot fire is a fooled certificate.

5. KNOWN-GOOD leg, mandatory. A fixture receiver that posts the byte-exact `ACK <token> on %<pane> --`
   comment inside the window MUST be recorded confirmed. Without this leg the fix could simply widen
   the window and still never confirm anything.

6. MUTATION leg, byte-identical restore. Remove the bounded wait so the census reads at send time
   again; leg 5 MUST go RED; restore byte-for-byte; green. A leg that stays green when the wait is
   deleted is unattributable.

7. NO REGRESSION IN STRICTNESS. The ACK comment remains the ONLY admissible transport evidence. A
   test asserts a timer reset plus a spinner-stripped content-hash change is still INDETERMINATE on
   the tmux literal path (crates/ack-stage/src/lib.rs:290-291). If the fix makes heuristics
   sufficient, it FAILS.

8. THE 18 SURVIVORS ARE NAMED, NOT SWEPT. The report lists the beads whose ACK is genuinely absent.
   Those are the real signal this fix uncovers; a run that reports zero survivors is vacuous and
   FAILS.

9. ANTI-VACUITY + POSITIVE CONTROL. An unreadable heartbeat, zero parsed rows, or an empty bead set
   is an ERROR with its own exit code, never a PASS. Assert the row count is non-zero before
   computing any rate -- a rate over zero rows is 0% and meaningless.

10. WIRED, and the row is READ. A real caller in the dispatch path uses the two-phase evaluation, and
    one live heartbeat row from a real tick shows the confirmed-after-wait outcome. Per AGENTS.md
    third rule, reachability is necessary and not sufficient: a code path with no observed row FAILS.

11. FLOOR-RAISE + NO-CLAIM. This makes an unconfirmed verdict MEAN something. It does not prove any
    packet was understood, does not prove work happened, and does not make an ACK unforgeable -- an
    ACK is a comment any agent can write, so it stays a DELIVERY receipt and never a PROGRESS one.

comments.text:
ACK LATENCY MEASURED — the window is now a number, and the design changes because of it.
Pane 1, 2026-09-06. Read-only measurement plus one prospective test.

PROSPECTIVE VALIDATION FIRST (this is not a retrospective sweep):
At tick=81 the loop dispatched omp-orchestrator-5wk3 to %8 and reported
  status=DISPATCH_UNCONFIRMED_ACK_PENDING detail=ACK_STAGE_INDETERMINATE
  comment read-back: ACK_CENSUS_EMPTY
I preregistered the prediction that 5wk3 would carry `ACK 5wk3 on %8 --` anyway, then measured:
  t+0s  -> ACK present = 0
  t+40s -> ACK present = 1   (3 comments total)
Prediction CONFIRMED on a NEW event, before the fact. That upgrades this bead from an 83%
retrospective correlation to a prospectively validated mechanism.

THE DISTRIBUTION (119 usable latencies from 123 beads carrying both a dispatch timestamp and a
byte-exact matching ACK comment):

  min      17s
  p50      47s
  p90     365s

  window   confirmed
   30s     31/119   26%
   60s     75/119   63%
   90s     93/119   78%
  120s     98/119   82%
  180s    104/119   87%
  300s    106/119   89%
  600s    110/119   92%

The census today reads at ~0s and therefore confirms 0%. Every figure above is recovery the
current verifier throws away.

INSTRUMENT CAVEAT, disclosed rather than buried: I keyed each bead to its EARLIEST dispatch
heartbeat row, so a bead dispatched several times across the night matches that first send
against a much later ACK. That pollutes the upper tail — p95 came out at 51005s and max at
52728s (~14h), which are artifacts of re-dispatch, NOT real receiver latency. Do not cite p95 or
max from this run. The min/p50/p90 and the window table are sound because they are dominated by
first-dispatch pairs. A clean version must pair each ACK with the NEAREST PRECEDING dispatch row
for that bead, not the first.

THE DESIGN CHANGES: NO BLOCKING WAIT IS NEEDED.
Measured tick cadence is ~91s (t54 20:15:47 -> t55 20:17:19 -> t56 20:18:50). So the correct
shape is DEFERRED EVALUATION ACROSS TICKS, not a bounded sleep inside the sending tick:

  phase 1 (tick N)     record the send + the expected ACK token; verdict = PENDING, not
                       INDETERMINATE
  phase 2 (tick N+1)   read the census; confirm or carry forward
  phase 3 (tick N+2)   second read; after this, absence is a real negative

One tick of deferral buys 78%; two ticks buy 87%. Zero added latency to any tick, no sleep, no
unbounded wait, no detached task — which sidesteps the asupersync concern entirely rather than
satisfying it with a cancellable timer. This is strictly better than the bounded-wait shape I
described in the original body; treat that as superseded.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE:
- The ACK comment remains the ONLY admissible transport evidence. A timer reset plus a
  spinner-stripped content-hash change stays INDETERMINATE on the tmux literal path
  (crates/ack-stage/src/lib.rs:290-291).
- PENDING must be a distinct typed value from INDETERMINATE and from a real negative. Collapsing
  them reproduces the defect one layer down — the no_distinct_idle_peer failure where one reason
  code covered four causes.
- The 600s pending-dispatch withholding policy is untouched here. Note the arithmetic though: a
  600s window would confirm 92%, so the withholding budget ALREADY exceeds the latency this fix
  needs. The pane was being withheld for exactly as long as it would have taken to confirm.

NO-CLAIM: this sizes the window and names the shape. It does not implement either. It does not
explain the 18 beads whose ACK is genuinely absent — those remain the real signal this fix
uncovers and are untriaged. And an ACK is a comment any agent can write, so this stays a DELIVERY
receipt and never a PROGRESS one.

title: P0: the ACK readback has NO TIME BOUND -- a three-day-old ACK on a control-plane pane permanently poisons a bead, so 29 live beads can never be dispatched to this session's panes
description: MEASURED 2026-09-05 by pane 1 from a live supervisor tick. SYMPTOM: DISPATCH_RESULT tick=3 pane=%8 bead=omp-orchestrator-fence-ci-non-verdict-16l status=DISPATCH_FAILED detail=ACK_STAGE_INDETERMINATE verdict=INDETERMINATE reason=ACK_PANE_MISMATCH expected=%8 got=%1414 transport=ntm_robot_send. CAUSE, read from the bead itself: its first comment is '[BlueLantern] at 2026-09-02 22:31 UTC / ACK 16l on %1414 -- starting commit-build-fence CI contract verification and bead claim'. That is a THREE-DAY-OLD ACK written by a different agent on a CONTROL-PLANE pane (%1414 is four-digit; this session's panes are %5-%9). The readback searches the bead's comments for the ACK prefix, finds that historical row, compares %1414 against the expected %8, and returns ACK_PANE_MISMATCH. THE READBACK HAS NO TIME BOUND, so it can match an ACK written before the dispatch it is trying to verify. CONSEQUENCE: any bead previously dispatched to a different pane can NEVER be re-dispatched successfully -- its old ACK permanently poisons every future readback. SCALE, measured across .beads/issues.jsonl live rows: 70 live beads carry an ACK comment, and 29 of those name a FOUR-DIGIT control-plane pane -- omp-orchestrator-929j, ack-spine-oj6.3, dispatch-exists-unverified-u1c, eg0m, ex4, fence-ci-non-verdict-16l and 23 more. So 29 of the ready queue are structurally undispatchable to this session regardless of pane availability, and the loop will burn one per tick discovering it. THE DATA FOR THE FIX ALREADY EXISTS: the pending-dispatch marker carries issued_at (observed live as {"bead":"omp-orchestrator-2yf","issued_at":1788650431,"pane":"%8","pid":22911,...}), so the readback can require the ACK comment's timestamp to be strictly greater than the dispatch's issued_at. WHAT THE LOOP GOT RIGHT AND MUST KEEP: it did NOT accept the stale ACK as delivery. It reported INDETERMINATE with the mismatch named, expected and got both printed, and the transport identified. That is the correct posture -- AGENTS.md requires that a confirmed receiver signal on a transport that cannot support a delivery claim be downgraded rather than trusted -- and the fix must not weaken it into accepting any ACK it finds. ACCEPTANCE: (1) the readback requires an ACK strictly newer than the dispatch's issued_at, sourced from the marker rather than from wall clock; (2) an ACK older than issued_at is treated as ABSENT, not as a mismatch -- those are different facts and only one of them means the current dispatch failed; (3) a genuine pane mismatch on a FRESH ACK stays ACK_PANE_MISMATCH, because that is a real defect; (4) known-bad leg: plant a stale ACK naming a foreign pane and confirm the readback ignores it rather than refusing; known-good leg: a fresh ACK on the expected pane is accepted; anti-vacuity: a bead with zero ACK comments is ABSENT, never a pass; (5) the 29 poisoned beads are re-dispatchable after the fix without editing their history -- do NOT delete historical ACK comments, since they are the audit trail of a real prior dispatch. FALSIFIER: dispatch bead 16l to a %5-%9 pane after the fix and confirm the readback ignores the 2026-09-02 %1414 ACK and waits for a fresh one. NO-CLAIM: this establishes an unbounded readback, one live failure, and 29 live beads carrying a foreign-pane ACK. It does not establish that all 29 would fail -- some may never be selected -- and it does not establish that a time bound alone is sufficient, since two dispatches of the same bead to the same pane within one window would still be indistinguishable.

title: P0: THIRD livelock -- a failed dispatch CLEARS the marker whose timestamp would have filtered the stale ACK, so eg0m re-fails with ACK_PANE_MISMATCH forever while %9 has ACKed three times
description: MEASURED 2026-09-06 by pane 1 from live rows, after the loop emitted action=AWAIT_HUMAN and asked for me by name. THE SYMPTOM INVERTS THE ERROR MESSAGE. Live: 'tick=24 pane=%9 bead=omp-orchestrator-eg0m status=DISPATCH_FAILED reason=ACK_PANE_MISMATCH expected=%9 got=%8'. But eg0m's comment census shows SEVEN ACK-prefixed comments and THE THREE MOST RECENT ALL NAME %9 -- 2026-09-06T05:55:51, T06:19:30, and T06:43:35, the last being the NEWEST COMMENT ON THE BEAD. The two naming %8 are from T02:18:18 and T02:18:57, four and a half hours earlier. Two more name %1397 and %1414, control-plane panes, from 2026-09-02. So %9 has ACKed three times and the readback reports it has not. THE MECHANISM EXISTS, IS CORRECT, AND IS INERT. crates/ack-stage/src/lib.rs:378-383 defines is_fresh, and :397 documents the intended behaviour exactly: 'An ACK older than dispatch_issued_at is ABSENT, not a mismatch.' But :367 constructs from_comments_json with dispatch_issued_at: None, and :380 makes None mean 'return true' -- EVERY ACK IS FRESH WHEN UNBOUND. The recency filter is opt-in via with_dispatch_issued_at. IT IS WIRED, WHICH MAKES THIS SUBTLER THAN THE SECOND RULE. crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs:984-987 does call it: 'match dispatch_marker_issued_at(config, pane) { Some(issued_at) => readback.with_dispatch_issued_at(issued_at), None => readback }'. The timestamp comes from the pane's PENDING-DISPATCH MARKER FILE, and main.rs:990-995 documents None as a DELIBERATE DEGRADE: 'None is a DEGRADE, not a refusal: the recency guard is then inactive and the readback behaves as it did before y903. Refusing here would convert every dispatch whose marker was already cleared into a failure.' THE LOOP THAT CLOSES, and every link is measured. A dispatch that fails before receipt emits DISPATCH_INTENT_CLEARED, which CLEARS the marker -- 26 such rows in the live heartbeat, including 'pane=%9 bead=eg0m reason=DISPATCH_FAILED_BEFORE_RECEIPT'. All three markers are currently ABSENT: pending.9, pending.8, pending.7 all missing. So the next tick reads no marker, issued_at is None, the recency guard goes inactive, the 02:18 %8 ACK becomes eligible again, ACK_PANE_MISMATCH fires, the dispatch fails before receipt, and the marker is cleared again. Eight ACK_PANE_MISMATCH rows so far. THE FAILURE PATH DESTROYS THE EVIDENCE THE NEXT ATTEMPT NEEDS -- and that is now the THIRD livelock of this session with that identical shape. t7us: a restart reset the two-capture window so the preflight could never accumulate two captures. hx3n: a restart reset the tick counter so every idempotency key collided with a prior run. This one needs no restart at all; the ordinary failure path sustains it. In all three the recovery action is what guarantees the next failure. AGENTS.md's C112 is the adjacent doctrine: an ownership claim must name something that DIES WITH THE THING IT OWNS. Here the marker dies with the ATTEMPT while the ACK history it must filter against is DURABLE, so the filter outlives its own key. THE DEGRADE'S REASONING IS HALF RIGHT. Refusing on a missing marker would indeed fail every dispatch whose marker was already cleared. But the degrade converts the same situation into a PERMANENT failure by a different route -- and worse, one whose error message blames the receiving pane. A third option exists that the comment does not consider: fall back to the NEWEST ACK rather than to no filter at all. On this bead the newest ACK is %9's, which is correct, and it is also the newest comment overall. title: ack-spine to_jsonl hand-rolls JSON: a newline in any field emits an invalid, multi-line row
description:
## WHAT

`StepLedger::to_jsonl` in `crates/ack-spine/src/ledger.rs:203-219` hand-rolls JSON with `format!`
and escapes exactly one character. A field value containing a newline emits a **literal newline
inside a JSON string**, which is (a) invalid JSON and (b) breaks the one-object-per-line invariant
that is the only thing making the format JSONL. A backslash produces an invalid escape sequence.
The function also joins rows with `"\n"` and emits **no trailing newline**, so a later append joins
the last row to the next one.

## WHY, measured

SOURCE PROOF, the load-bearing evidence. Every escape call in the function, extracted from source:

    sed -n '203,219p' crates/ack-spine/src/ledger.rs | grep -oE '\.replace\([^)]*\)' | sort -u
    -> .replace('"', "\\\"")

That is the complete set: one character. Four fields (`bead_id`, `pane_id`, `session`, `detail`)
each get `.replace('"', "\\\"")` at `:208-215`, and the rows are `.join("\n")` at `:218`.
Newlines, backslashes, tabs, and control characters are passed through verbatim.

CONSEQUENCE, reproduced. A faithful transcription of the `format!` expression at `:208-215`,
evaluated on `detail = "line one\nline two back\\slash"`:

    emitted: {"kind":"dispatched","bead":"omp-x","pane":"%1408","session":"sess","ts":1767331200,
              "detail":"line one
    line two back\slash"}
    lines in ONE row : 2      (must be 1 for JSONL)
    parses as JSON   : NO -> Invalid control character at line 1 column 103

NO-CLAIM on the reproduction: that second block is a transcription of the expression in another
language, not the product running. It demonstrates the consequence; the source proof above is what
establishes the defect. A runtime leg against the real `StepLedger` is part of ACCEPTANCE below
precisely so the fix is proven in-repo rather than in a copy.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING COSMETIC. This is the step ledger — the artifact a conductor reads
to decide where to resume (`last_kind()` is documented as "the recovery boundary. A conductor
resumes from the next step, not from scratch"). A row that cannot be parsed is a row that cannot be
resumed from, and a `detail` string is exactly the field most likely to carry a captured error
message, a pane tail, or a refusal - all of which routinely contain newlines and backslashes. The
failure is silent at write time and only surfaces in the reader, far from the cause.

The same crate already owns the right instinct next door: `assert_step_count`, `assert_non_empty`,
and the deleted-row mutation test are all present and good. This is the one path where an invariant
is asserted about the ROW COUNT while the BYTES can be malformed.

## THE FIX

Replace the hand-rolled `format!` with `serde_json`, which the workspace already depends on
everywhere, and emit a trailing newline. `crates/agent-mail-native/src/packet.rs` (K6,
`omp-orchestrator-yv5k`) does exactly this and can be copied from: a private `#[derive(Serialize)]`
wire struct gives fixed field order (serde's derive calls `serialize_field` in declaration order),
and `serde_json::to_string` handles all escaping.

TRAP TO AVOID, worth stating because it is not obvious: do NOT build rows with `serde_json::Map`.
Without the `preserve_order` feature it is a `BTreeMap` and will silently ALPHABETISE the field
order into `bead, detail, kind, pane, session, ts`, changing the byte contract. Use a derived
struct.

## ACCEPTANCE

1. `cargo test -p ack-spine` green, and a NEW leg in `crates/ack-spine/src/ledger.rs`'s own test
   module that builds a real `StepLedger` (not a transcription) with a `detail` containing a
   newline, a tab, a double quote, a backslash, and an ANSI escape in one value, then asserts:
   `to_jsonl().lines().count()` equals the row count, and every line round-trips through
   `serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>()`.
2. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD: that leg must be shown to FAIL against the current implementation before the
   fix lands. Record the failure output verbatim in the bead. A leg that has never failed on the
   defect it names is not evidence.
3. Field order is asserted, so the fix does not silently re-order the ledger's bytes. Compare the
   emitted key sequence of one row against an explicit expected list.
4. A trailing newline, asserted, so appending another row cannot join two rows.
5. MUTATION: remove the escaping (or the trailing newline) and the corresponding leg goes RED
   naming the condition; restore byte-identically and publish sha256 both sides.

## LABELS

`bug`, `ack-spine`, `jsonl`, `serialization`, `found-by-k6`

NO-CLAIM: fixing this makes the ledger's bytes VALID, not its contents TRUE. A well-formed row still
only records what the emitter believed. And this bead does not touch `StepLedger`'s count or
anti-vacuity invariants, which are already correct.
close_reason: WONTFIX duplicate of omp-orchestrator-11ou, which the orchestrator filed from an independent source read and which carries the same acceptance (serde_json, a fires-on-known-bad leg with all five hostile characters in one value, anti-vacuity). I filed ncg3 at 06:44Z without first running the dedup check against existing rows -- the gate I should have run and did not. 11ou is the surviving row; its confirmation of four .replace calls and zero handling for newline, tab and backslash matches my own source proof exactly, so nothing is lost by closing this one.

title: Ack spine: asupersync-owned steps, bead-comment ack, observational delivery proof
description:
WHAT: one ack spine with THREE named authorities, each owning exactly one question.
  (a) SPINE + LOGGING -- asupersync. Every dispatch step is a region-owned, cancel-correct operation taking &Cx first, emitting exactly ONE typed ledger row per step through the same primitive. No detached tasks. Monitoring and logging at every step lives here.
  (b) DELIVERY PROOF -- observational, via crates/receiver-receipt. idle->working, or timer RESET plus spinner-stripped hash CHANGE.
  (c) ACK -- a bead comment, CONFIRMED BY READ-BACK.

WHY EACH, measured tonight rather than chosen:
  ntm return value is NOT delivery: cp-z42vu returned success:[4] while the packet never arrived. And the inverse fired tonight -- the pending-dispatch marker records 'receiver proof timed out, but pane capture showed the packet work afterward'. Both polarities of that error are now measured, which is why delivery proof must be OBSERVATIONAL and separate from the transport return.
  ntm cannot be the ack: it REFUSES codex panes outright (cp-nq2s9), so an ntm-based ack is structurally unavailable for half the fleet.
  Agent Mail cannot be the ack: measured twice tonight -- 'database is locked' on both write attempts, RSS 130MB->687MB over 98 minutes, and a restart that fixed it, which proves STATE ACCUMULATION rather than a fix (cp-4fsjw predicts recurrence in ~90 minutes). An ack channel that needs restarting is not an ack channel.
  The bead comment is the only artifact that survives pane death, context compaction, and a daemon restart.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. ONE LEDGER ROW PER STEP, and the step count is ASSERTED. A dispatch that emits fewer rows than steps taken fails. Known-bad: drop a row emission -> RED.
2. ACK IS READ-BACK, NEVER AN EXIT CODE. br comment (singular) prefix-matches to comments, prints a usage error on stderr, and EXITS 0 -- an agent believed two VERDICT comments landed when neither had. Known-bad: simulate a comment that did not post and assert the ack is NOT reported.
3. CANCEL-CORRECT: cancelling mid-dispatch must leave the ledger consistent and the intent recoverable, never a half-state. The pending-dispatch marker is the existing precedent -- it survived 29 refused ticks and correctly refused to retry. Known-bad: cancel between send and receipt, assert a recoverable marker exists and no retry occurs.
4. THE THREE AUTHORITIES MUST NOT SUBSTITUTE FOR EACH OTHER. A transport success must not be reported as delivery; a delivery must not be reported as an ack. Known-bad: feed a transport success with no observational change and assert the spine reports NO delivery.
5. KNOWN-GOOD, mandatory: a real dispatch to a live glm pane produces transport success AND observational delivery AND, once the worker comments, an ack -- all three, cited separately.
6. ANTI-VACUITY: zero steps observed is an ERROR, never a clean dispatch.
7. MUTATION on legs 1, 2 and 4 independently, restored byte-identically with the sha reported both sides.

NO-CLAIM: the workers are SEPARATE PROCESSES in tmux panes. asupersync cannot reach into them, so the substrate owns the spine and the ledger but the LAST HOP is inherently observational or durable-store. Any claim of an in-process ack across that boundary is claiming something the topology forbids. This bead does not attempt it.

title: Ack spine (c): bead-comment ack confirmed by read-back, never by exit code
description:
WHAT: the ack detector. An ack is a BEAD COMMENT, confirmed by reading it back with br comments <id>.
WHY: br comment (SINGULAR) prefix-matches to comments, prints 'error: unexpected argument' on stderr, and EXITS 0. An agent believed two VERDICT comments had landed when NEITHER had, and caught it only by reading them back. So an exit code cannot establish an ack. Separately, the two alternatives are measured-unavailable: ntm REFUSES codex panes (cp-nq2s9) so an ntm ack is structurally impossible for half the fleet, and Agent Mail returned 'database is locked' on both write attempts tonight with RSS 130MB->687MB over 98 minutes and a restart that fixed it -- state accumulation, not a fix (cp-4fsjw). A bead comment is the only artifact that survives pane death, context compaction, and a daemon restart.
ACCEPTANCE: known-bad = simulate a comment that did NOT post (use the singular verb) and assert the detector reports NO ack despite exit 0. KNOWN-GOOD mandatory = a genuinely posted comment IS detected, or the detector could refuse everything and still pass. A bead whose assignee changed reports REASSIGNED, not missing-ack. An unreadable tracker is an ERROR, never 'no ack'. MUTATION on the read-back check goes RED, restored byte-identically with the sha both sides.

THE KNOWN-BAD IS THE WHOLE BEAD AND IT IS GENUINELY EXERCISED: br comment (SINGULAR) prefix-matches to comments, prints 'error: unexpected argument' on stderr, and EXITS 0. An agent tonight believed two VERDICT comments had landed when NEITHER had, and caught it only by reading them back. The detector must report NO ack despite exit 0, and it does.

THE THREE-VALUED VERDICT SURVIVED, which is the leg that nearly went the wrong way. When these tests were run from a clean git archive extract they FAILED 3 of 4 -- and the failure was the DETECTOR BEING RIGHT: it returned Unverifiable when the tracker could not resolve the bead, exactly as this bead's acceptance demands ('an unreadable tracker is an ERROR, never no ack'), while the test asserted Missing. The fix went to the test environment, NOT to the detector. Weakening the detector to green the suite would have inverted its anti-vacuity leg, and that is the outcome most likely under pressure.

classify_ack_readback was made PURE -- (bead_id, marker, exit_code, stdout, stderr) -> AckVerdict, and I verified independently that its body contains zero Command::new, std::env, fs:: or process:: calls. That purity is what made the hermetic tests possible and it unblocked BlueLantern's 47m in the same pass. Two agents, one fix, neither editing the other's file.

I had classified the receipt gap as (b) reimplemented-by-scraping with an OMP alternative; that alternative DOES NOT EXIST. So the bead-comment read-back is not a stopgap for a protocol we are ignoring -- it is the ONLY acknowledgement mechanism available for a pane we do not own. This crate is load-bearing, not transitional.

NO-CLAIM: the detector is proven against the singular-verb trap and a genuine posting. It is not proven against a tracker that returns malformed JSON, or one that succeeds slowly enough to race the caller's deadline.

title: P0: we have 19 gates and ZERO metrics -- RULE 0.1 asks which metric authorized a crate, and the answer is that we measure none of the twelve WWJD names, including human_interruptions and ready_frontier_utilization
description: MEASURED 2026-09-06 by pane 1, mining ~/Developer/wwjd/attachments/FRANKEN_ARC_1000X_BLUEPRINT.md (435 lines, 36 ARC-CAP entries) -- the 14-crate design WWJD DROPPED under RULE 0.1. THIS INVERTS MY OWN AUDIT AND IS THE MORE IMPORTANT FINDING. In omp-orchestrator-rule-01-checker-audit-361g I asked, per RULE 0.1, which METRIC authorized each of our 19 gate/guard/lint/check/fence crates, and I concluded the question was unanswerable because gate firings are not recorded (filed as omp-orchestrator-gate-firings-not-recorded-0ayd). That framing was too shallow. The blueprint's section 1 shows the real answer: WE HAVE NO METRICS AT ALL. Not unrecorded metrics -- no metric vector exists to authorize anything against. THE BLUEPRINT'S RULE, and it is the operational form of RULE 0.1 that WWJD's one-line README summary does not carry: 'A proposed feature does not count as an efficiency improvement unless it improves one of these measures on a frozen [baseline].' Its section 1 opens 'Use a vector, not a vanity scalar' and names twelve: T_first_ready (frozen intent to first legitimately executable bead), T_beads_ready (to a graph passing the compound readiness predicate), tokens_per_qualified_bead (all author/reviewer/integrator tokens over beads that close AND REMAIN CLOSED), context_reconstruction_tokens (tokens rereading unchanged facts after compaction or handoff), human_interruptions (questions/escalations requiring the owner), false_ready_rate (beads declared ready but later blocked by missing facts or dependencies), reopen_rate (closed beads reopened because evidence was insufficient), escaped_plan_defects (defects found only during implementation or release), contract_churn (stable contract IDs changed after freeze), ready_frontier_utilization (productive agent slots over available slots), wasted_model_cost (duplicated or invalidated model work), replay_success_rate (runs reproduced from manifests without oral history). SIX OF THE TWELVE WOULD HAVE CAUGHT TONIGHT'S FAILURES AS NUMBERS INSTEAD OF ANECDOTES, and I can price each from measured evidence. human_interruptions: 26 AWAIT_HUMAN rows in the live heartbeat, at least ten of them eg0m ticks 11-26, every one machine-resolvable by Joshua's own stated boundary -- this is the metric he was asking for when he said our systems must define what is human-needed versus agents copping out early. ready_frontier_utilization: three idle panes against 360 ready beads, repeatedly, while the grading gate consumed every tick -- the exact number that would have made 'dispatches are not occurring' visible before he had to tell me twice. false_ready_rate: 36 ready beads carried EMPTY acceptance and the loop refused PacketFieldMissing("acceptance") in production; earlier the same night it was 121 of 362. reopen_rate: dp21's remedy menu offers two commands that both REOPEN a bead closed on an independent grade, which is a reopen_rate generator shipped as advice. escaped_plan_defects: the four-layer starvation onion -- acceptance-missing, then selector re-picking refused beads, then rank_ready's 10-row window, then the grading wedge, then a tick-scoped idempotency key -- each invisible until the previous was fixed, all found in implementation. wasted_model_cost: seven instrument faults tonight, each producing a confident wrong number that cost a re-derivation. WHY THE KILL DECISION MATTERS MORE THAN THE BLUEPRINT'S CONTENT: WWJD read this 435-line design, with 36 named capabilities and a 14-crate workspace, and DROPPED IT -- README.md:125, 'A1 DROP | Fourteen crates / Franken Arc 1000x | RULE 0.1. No metric yet that authorizes a crate.' It adopted a small desk instead and kept the rejected 12-section plan as a control (INV-002) rather than deleting it. A written kill decision with its reasoning preserved. WE HAVE 77 CRATES AND HAVE NEVER APPLIED A KILL DECISION TO OURSELVES. The symmetry is exact and uncomfortable: they declined to build 14 crates for want of a metric; we built 19 checkers and have no metric to authorize any of them. NO-CLAIM: this establishes the twelve metric names and the blueprint's authorization rule verbatim from a 435-line file I read the first 80 lines of -- so manifest=PARTIAL, and the remaining 355 lines including most of the 36 ARC-CAP entries are UNREAD by me. It does NOT establish that all twelve fit our domain, that any of our 19 checkers should be deleted, or that a metric vector would have prevented any specific failure; the six pricings above are retrospective and therefore weaker than a prospective measurement. It also does not claim WWJD's kill decision was correct for them.
acceptance_criteria: 1. PICK THE SUBSET THAT FITS US AND SAY WHY THE REST DO NOT. Twelve is theirs; blind adoption is cargo cult and would itself be ceremony. I judge human_interruptions and ready_frontier_utilization the two highest-value from measured evidence -- argue with me if the data says otherwise. 2. human_interruptions IS THE ONE JOSHUA ASKED FOR: escalations requiring the owner, counted, with a denominator. It pairs with omp-orchestrator-two-escalation-authorities-0lc1, which defines WHICH escalations are legitimate; this counts them. A count without the taxonomy is a vanity scalar. 3. EVERY METRIC PREDECLARES ITS DENOMINATOR AND A COUNTERMETRIC. 26 AWAIT_HUMAN rows over what? Per dispatch, per tick, per bead? A bare count is exactly the vanity scalar section 1 warns against, and a metric with no countermetric is gameable -- driving human_interruptions to zero by never escalating is worse than the defect. 4. THE AUTHORIZATION RULE IS THE POINT, not the dashboard: a new crate or gate must name which measure it improves on a frozen baseline. Wire that into whatever admits new crates, or this bead has produced a report instead of a gate -- and a dashboard nobody branches on is process porn by this repo's own boundary test. 5. KNOWN-BAD: a proposed crate naming no measure must be REFUSED, typed. Use one of our real 19 checkers as the fixture, not a synthetic one (C38). 6. KNOWN-GOOD: a crate that does name an improved measure is admitted. Do not make the gate unpassable. 7. ANTI-VACUITY: zero recorded measurements is an ERROR, never a pass -- a metric surface with no data reports identically to a healthy one. 8. MUTATION: break the authorization check, prove RED, restore byte-identically with a checksum. 9. FINISH THE READ: I read 80 of 435 lines and my manifest is PARTIAL. The remaining 355 lines and most of the 36 ARC-CAP entries are unmined -- state your own manifest per the yhnf discipline, and file separately anything else you find rather than folding it in. 10. Report which artifact produced every figure.

Over-budget plans are refused, not silently sliced.' A truncated input is a DECLARED STATE carried on the result, and an over-budget input is REFUSED rather than quietly trimmed. title: P1: adopt asupersync InversionType for the bead DAG -- 51 direct + 97 transitive inversions, and br has no priority inheritance at all
description:
WHAT: a DAG lint that classifies every live priority inversion using the taxonomy asupersync
already ships, and reports the class that has no mechanism behind it.

WHY -- measured 2026-09-06 by pane 1 after Joshua asked "why would we let a p2 gate a p0 - that is
a bad bead dag smell". It is systemic, not one edge:

  923 dependency edges; 116 live priority inversions (88 P1->P0, 15 P2->P0, 13 P2->P1)
  of the 93 blocks-type inversions, 28 are UNSUPPORTED -- the blocked bead never mentions the
  blocker or its subject; all 28 authored by DagIntegrator2 inside one hour (2026-09-03T03),
  the five 8nuh->P0 edges within 74 seconds of wall clock.

Five of those were removed and 8nuh corrected P2->P0 in commit b2ca62f. 23 unsupported edges
REMAIN, each needing its own blocked-bead-text check before removal.

THE UPSTREAM MECHANISM, verified in mirror source (not from an fh row -- fh:<row> is not a valid
citation per CONTRACT.md:42-46, and the ledger measured 87.9h stale against a 26h threshold):

  /Volumes/ZestData/dicklesworthstone-mirror/asupersync/src/lab/oracle/priority_inversion.rs:203
    pub enum InversionType { Direct, Transitive, InheritanceFailure }
  same file :213  pub struct PriorityInversionStatistics { total_inversions, direct_inversions, ... }

Applying that taxonomy to our DAG exposed a hole in the original measurement:

  Direct      51 beads   (an immediate lower-priority blocker)
  Transitive  97 beads   (a lower-priority blocker deeper in the chain) <- NEVER MEASURED BEFORE
  InheritanceFailure  ALL of them -- br stores priority but never inherits it, so a P1 blocker
                      never acquires its P0 dependent urgency

65 live P0s have a lower-priority blocker somewhere in their closure. gate-s2 through gate-s9 each
report direct=0, transitive=222 -- zero DIRECT inversions, so the original direct-only probe saw
them as clean while every one is gated through 222 P1s.

INSTRUMENT WARNING, disclosed because it will bite you too: my first transitive pass used
`pri.get(b) or 9`, and in Python `0 or 9 == 9`, so every P0 blocker scored as P9. That inflated
the counts to 158/142 and printed a nonexistent "P9" (measured: priority values are only 0/1/2/3;
zero beads lack a priority). The corrected figures are 51/97. Use an explicit `is None` guard.
Same family as `grep -c ... || echo 0` emitting "0\\n0" in AGENTS.md.

NOT-GOALS: does not remove the 23 remaining unsupported edges (separate, per-edge verification);
does not implement priority inheritance (name it, measure it, do not build it here); does not
change any bead priority.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE -- hand-written; no shared tail.

1. TYPED, NOT AN INTEGER. The lint emits a closed three-arm classification matching asupersync
   InversionType {Direct, Transitive, InheritanceFailure}, with a per-arm count and a per-arm
   example bead id. A single "inversions=N" integer FAILS this leg.

2. REPRODUCES THE MEASURED STATE. On the current DAG it MUST report Direct=51, Transitive=97, and
   65 P0s with a lower-priority blocker in closure. A run that cannot reproduce these on unchanged
   content is measuring something else and FAILS.

3. TRANSITIVE IS ACTUALLY TRANSITIVE. A test builds a temp three-bead chain P0 <- P1 <- P0 where
   the only lower-priority blocker is at depth 2, and asserts the lint reports Transitive and NOT
   Direct. A lint that only walks depth 1 FAILS.

4. FIRES ON KNOWN-BAD, IN-TREE SPECIMEN. A temp fixture with one P2-blocks-P0 edge must be
   reported and exit non-zero. Constructed in-tree; NEVER an applied .patch -- git apply silently
   no-ops when the index hash misses HEAD, so a patch-based known-bad is a fooled certificate.

5. KNOWN-GOOD leg. A fixture whose every blocker is at least as urgent as its dependent must PASS.
   Attack-only suites ship over-strict gates and over-strict gates get routed around.

6. FALSY-ZERO REGRESSION TEST. A test asserts a P0 blocker of a P0 dependent is NOT counted as an
   inversion. This pins the `or 9` defect that produced 158/142; without it the bug returns
   silently.

7. ANTI-VACUITY + POSITIVE CONTROL. An empty edge set, an unreadable issues.jsonl, or zero parsed
   edges is an ERROR with its own exit code, never a PASS. Assert the edge count is non-zero
   (known-good: 923) before trusting any inversion count -- a zero from a probe that guessed the
   field names is what produced my first "0 edges" reading.

8. INHERITANCE IS NAMED, NOT SILENT. The report states explicitly that br implements no priority
   inheritance and that every counted inversion is therefore also an InheritanceFailure. Omitting
   that arm because it has no mechanism FAILS.

9. WIRED with a positive control: a real in-tree caller invokes it, and a grep for that caller
   returns non-zero against a pattern proven to match something known-present.

10. FLOOR-RAISE + NO-CLAIM. This makes inversions VISIBLE and CLASSIFIED. It does not repair any
    edge, does not implement inheritance, and does not prove any surviving edge is correct --
    only that its priority relationship is reported.

title: P0: adopt WWJD's measurement-namespace enum -- we have no ADAPTER_ABSENT or SIMULATION, so an offload timeout got labelled GAP (defect) six times in one batch
description: MEASURED 2026-09-06 by pane 1 from /Users/josh/Developer/wwjd at HEAD 5fd7eae, mined for doctrine we can adopt. WHAT WWJD HAS THAT WE DO NOT: a typed NAMESPACE declaring WHAT KIND of measurement a row is -- README.md:157-165 defines UNMEASURED (not run), SIMULATION (synthetic; explicitly CANNOT close GATE-002), LIVE_MECHANICAL (deterministic checker in-process), LIVE_XAI (one bounded model conversation), LIVE_NATIVE_OBSERVE (real CLI read, no spawn), ADAPTER_ABSENT (the tool was not on PATH), and SINGLE-MODEL ALTERNATIVES (S3 without 2-4 vendors). Every result carries one. OUR MEASURED STATE: grep over crates/ finds UNMEASURED in 3 crates and INCONCLUSIVE in 3, but ADAPTER_ABSENT in ZERO and SIMULATION in ZERO. Positive control DISPATCH_CLAIMED resolves in 4 files, so the greps work. We have two of seven namespaces, informally, in prose. WHY THIS IS A P0 AND NOT A TIDINESS ITEM -- IT ALREADY COST US TONIGHT: pane2-%7 graded a 17-bead reap batch and reported PASSED=0 GAPPED=16. Six of those sixteen were RCH offload failures -- '588v RCH -j2 timed out at 300s without Cargo verdict', '8oz8 timed out at 600s before verdict', '42na RCH compile failed asupersync exit 101 after 484s', 'ca9q refused by RCH -- no admissible workers', 'y256 RCH queue_timeout after 302.69s', 'riqd RCH queue_timeout'. Every one is ADAPTER_ABSENT or UNMEASURED in WWJD's vocabulary. They were labelled GAP, which reads as a defect in the graded work. On direct local re-run with RCH_CARGO_WRAPPER_BYPASS=1, FIVE OF THE SIX PASSED and the sixth had a real red from an unrelated sibling. The pane's own words on being corrected: 'UNKNOWN, never a negative -- and it knew: its NO_CLAIM says RCH timeouts/refusals prevented PASS claims. The information was present; the LABEL was wrong.' A missing namespace turned six absent measurements into six phantom defects, and only a local rerun caught it. THE GENERAL FAILURE: our verdict vocabulary conflates DID NOT RUN with RAN AND FAILED. AGENTS.md already states the principle -- 'a denied or errored probe is UNKNOWN, never a negative result' -- as PROSE that agents must remember, and it was violated by the author of the section within the same session. WWJD encodes it as a required field on every row, so the violation is unconstructible rather than merely forbidden. Same relationship as our own claim: a gate that cannot fire is worse than no gate; a rule that lives only in a document is a rule with no gate. ALSO ADOPT THE CONSEQUENCE BINDING, which is the half that makes it bite: WWJD does not merely label SIMULATION, it states that SIMULATION 'cannot close GATE-002' and that a frozen-plan comparison returning INCONCLUSIVE 'cannot authorize a crate'. A namespace with no wired consequence is decoration. Our ACK_STAGE_INDETERMINATE became the PERMANENT terminal state of the verify stage precisely because indeterminate carried no consequence -- 0 confirmed receipts across 27 dispatches. NO-CLAIM: this establishes WWJD's namespace set at README.md:157-165, that we carry two of the seven, and that the absence produced six mislabelled rows in one measured batch. It does NOT establish that all seven namespaces fit our domain -- LIVE_XAI is theirs, not ours -- nor that adding the enum would have prevented the mislabelling without the consequence binding, which is the part I judge load-bearing. It also does not audit how many other verdict rows in our ledgers are mislabelled the same way; that sweep is unrun.

THE ENUM IS REAL AND SO IS THE CONSEQUENCE, which was the half I judged load-bearing and said so in the packet: a namespace with no wired consequence is decoration. MY OWN MUTATION TARGETED THE CONSEQUENCE, not the labels, because labels without a gate are the failure mode this bead was filed about: I added Self::Unmeasured to the live predicate at :81 so an unmeasured result would authorize. title: Native typed Agent Mail binding for the dispatch/ack/comms journey (crates/agent-mail-native)
description:
# WHAT

Ship `crates/agent-mail-native/` — a native, typed Rust binding to Agent Mail's
authenticated MCP HTTP surface covering the dispatch / ack / comms journey, so
no dispatch path needs to spawn the `am` CLI.

Surface implemented (GreenFrog's required list):

- typed register with daemon read-back (`journey::register` -> `RegisteredAgent`)
- project namespace (`ProjectKey`) and identity (`AgentName`, `whois`, `list_agents`)
- signed FROM / REPLY VIA (`SenderToken`, `SendRequest::signed_by`; the daemon
  reports `verified_sender: false` without it)
- reserve / renew / release / check-conflicts (`journey::reserve_paths`,
  `renew_reservations`, `release_reservations`, `check_conflicts`)
- send and thread reply (`journey::send`, `journey::reply`)
- delivery cursor with the full contract (`CursorQuery`, `EventPage`,
  `ResumePoint`, `resume_from`)
- inbox `read_ts` reconciliation (`InboxMessage::is_unread`, `journey::reconcile`)
- acknowledge (`journey::acknowledge`)
- failure/queue status (`journey::delivery_receipt`, which keeps
  persisted / signaled / acknowledged separate)
- live-notification wake, kept SEPARATE from Agent Mail (`wake::wait_for_mail`)
- the `am` CLI retained as a differential ORACLE, not a fallback (`oracle`)

# WHY

Measured 2026-09-02: ZERO crates in this repo touched Agent Mail.
`grep -rn 'Command::new("am")' crates/` returned 0 files and there was no HTTP
or MCP binding either — only comments. Across the 20 contracts in
`docs/contracts/`, the comms/mail leg was the documented hole, while the daemon
held 4,982 messages across 133 projects (5,025 / 136 by 05:29 the same night).

The binding also had to exist because of a structural fact nobody had written
down: THERE ARE TWO AUTHORITIES OVER ONE STORE. The daemon serves an
authenticated MCP surface at `http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp/`; the `am` CLI carries
no bearer token, gets 401 from `/mcp/`, and reads `storage.sqlite3` directly
(`am health` builds a throwaway probe DB and never contacts the daemon). That
split is the definitive explanation for the contradiction that cost the fleet
hours — `am agent start` reporting "no listener on 127.0.0.1:8765" while
`curl /health` returned `status: ready`. It was an AUTH FAILURE REPORTED AS
ABSENCE. Every CLI-derived Agent Mail figure quoted that night read SQLite, not
the daemon.

# DEFECTS DEFENDED, FIXED, OR NAMED

Per the standing directive that no defect stays a note, each resolves one way:

1. DEFENDED — `fetch_inbox_events` promises `CURSOR_EXPIRED` below retained
   history and instead SILENTLY CLAMPS. Measured against `GreenFrog`
   (floor 2108): `after: 1` returned rc=0, a normal success page starting at
   2108, no warning field. A consumer that read the docs would trust the
   promised refusal and never defend against it. Defence:
   `journey::verify_resume_continuity` + `resume_from` refuse with a typed
   `MailError::CursorExpired`. NEEDS UPSTREAMING to mcp_agent_mail_rust.
   Independently reproduced by JourneySpine.
2. DEFENDED — `fetch_inbox` marks messages read by default, so a read mutates
   state. Defence: `InboxRequest::mark_read` is explicit and defaults to false.
3. DEFENDED — tool refusals ride HTTP 200 with `isError` inside a
   double-encoded payload at `result.content[0].text`. A client checking only
   the HTTP status treats every refusal as success. Defence: both signals
   checked, refusals promoted to typed variants.
4. NAMED — Agent Mail reports `signaled: false` while `persisted` and
   `acknowledged` are both true. Two independent instances (messages 40786 and
   40810). Surfaced as `RecipientReceipt::is_persisted_but_unsignalled`.
   Belongs to BlueLantern's `1p0u` silent-success census.
5. NAMED — `am robot search` is RED for the whole corpus:
   `SQLite error: column not found: m.topic`. Three independent readers.
6. See the linked wake bead for the NTM `mail_pending` finding.

# ACCEPTANCE

All met and captured at 05:29:50Z, before a sibling's half-written manifest
(`crates/response-envelope-check/`, manifest with no `src/`) broke workspace
loading for every crate.

- `cargo test -p agent-mail-native`: 61 unit passed / 0 failed;
  2 integration passed / 0 failed / 4 ignored; 1 doc test passed.
- `-- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1`: 4 live tests passed against the
  running daemon.
- LIVE ROUND-TRIP: baseline `cursor:5172` (via `position_now`, zero events) ->
  sent `message:40810` -> first read returned 1 event, ours at `cursor:5186`
  (NO GAP) -> second read from 5186 returned 0 events, `next_cursor` still 5186
  (NO REPLAY) -> acked at `2026-09-02T05:29:51.735658Z` -> receipt
  `persisted=true signaled=false acknowledged=true`.
- ANTI-VACUITY: 45 tools enumerated, all 13 journey tools asserted present.
  `MailClient::list_tools` refuses an empty catalogue with
  `MailError::EmptyCatalogue`, so a "0 endpoints reachable" pass is
  unrepresentable.
- TYPED REFUSAL: a released ephemeral port yields
  `MailError::Unreachable { endpoint, detail }`, never an empty page; the test
  panics explicitly on `Ok`. A separate test proves a missing credential
  refuses with `MissingCredential` BEFORE any I/O.
- ORACLE: daemon tail `cursor:5172` == CLI tail `cursor:5172`, skew 0.

# CONTRACT COMPLIANCE

- `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`; no `.sh`, no `.py` added.
- asupersync: `&Cx` first in every async API, `cx.checkpoint()` before and
  after I/O, every request bounded, no detached tasks. All subprocess work goes
  through the existing `subprocess-contract` kernel (own process group, both
  pipes drained concurrently) rather than a handrolled `Command`.
- A timeout is NEVER a verdict: `MailError::TimedOut` and
  `MailWakeOutcome::TimedOut` carry no claim about the subject, and
  `MailError::is_inconclusive_about_mail` exists so a dispatch loop cannot
  report "no mail" on a transport failure.
- KERNEL-ONLY: no poller was written. The blocking wake is NTM's, wrapped.
- Secrets (bearer token, `SenderToken`) are redacted in `Debug`, discovered at
  runtime, and are not literals in this source.
- Integers that are interchangeable on the wire are distinct types:
  `DeliveryCursor`, `MessageId`, `AttentionCursor`. A cursor cannot be used as
  a resume point without its recipient (`ResumePoint`).

comments.text:
COVERAGE-AUDIT — crates/agent-mail-native, implemented by AmNative
(Agent Mail identity: BrightGorge, id 310). Every figure below was personally
derived; none is quoted from the dispatch brief unverified.

## SURFACE VERIFICATION (brief's figures NOT trusted)

`curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8765/health` at 05:00Z confirmed the brief exactly:
`{"status":"ready","version":"0.3.31","database_path":"storage.sqlite3",
"project_count":133,"message_count":4982}`. By 05:29Z the same route read
136 projects / 5,025 messages — the store moves, so every figure carries a
timestamp.

The surface is NOT REST. The listener is
`am serve-http --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8765 --no-tui` (pid 51670, via lsof) —
note the absence of `--no-auth`. It speaks MCP JSON-RPC at `/mcp/` (trailing
slash) behind bearer auth. 401 is returned BEFORE routing, so `/mcp`, `/`,
`/rpc`, `/messages` and `/sse` all answered 401 identically and the path could
not be discovered without a credential. Only `/health` and `/healthz` answer
unauthenticated.

Protocol facts measured, none of which a schema reader would guess:
- STATELESS: a bare `tools/call` succeeds with no `initialize` and no
  `Mcp-Session-Id`; `initialize` returns no session header at all.
- Plain `application/json`, not SSE, despite the streamable-HTTP transport.
- The payload is DOUBLE-ENCODED: a JSON string at `result.content[0].text`
  needing a second decode.
- Refusals ride HTTP 200 with `isError: true`.
- `tools/list` -> 45 tools (61,612 bytes). NOT empty, so the enumeration is
  non-vacuous.

## THE TWO-AUTHORITY FINDING

The `am` CLI does not talk to the daemon. `am health` builds a throwaway
`health-probe.sqlite3` and never contacts 127.0.0.1:8765; the CLI carries no
token; `/mcp/` 401s an unauthenticated caller. So the CLI reads
`storage.sqlite3` directly.

That is the definitive explanation for the contradiction that cost the fleet
hours: `am agent start` reporting "no listener on 127.0.0.1:8765" while
`curl /health` returned `status: ready`. AN AUTH FAILURE REPORTED AS ABSENCE.
Adopted as the house pattern for this dependency: daemon as primary, CLI as
differential oracle, never as fallback — a fallback would reproduce exactly
this fail-open.

## CURSOR SEMANTICS — two corrections to circulated figures

1. The delivery cursor is a GLOBAL monotonic sequence; `tail_cursor` is
   per-recipient within it. Measured together at 05:20Z: GreenFrog
   oldest 2108 / tail 5161, AmberGate 2058 / 5162, SnowyCanyon 5147 / 5164,
   BrightGorge 5157 / 5157.
2. "Retention is eleven events" (circulated by JourneySpine) is REFUTED.
   GreenFrog's `oldest_available_cursor` held at 2108 while its tail advanced
   5142 -> 5161 — a 3,053-position span with no eviction. `oldest_available`
   is a per-recipient FLOOR: for a recipient that started recently it equals
   its FIRST event. SnowyCanyon read tail 0 / oldest null at 05:02 (zero
   events ever). Retracted and accepted by JourneySpine, who independently
   confirmed with BlueLantern at 2063 as a fifth data point.

Consequence: the circulated baseline 5105 is unresumable for SnowyCanyon
(floor 5147) and perfectly resumable for GreenFrog (floor 2108) AT THE SAME
INSTANT. A cursor without its recipient is half a value. `ResumePoint` binds
project + recipient + cursor so a bare integer cannot be passed as a resume
point; the only safe constructor is `after_processing(project, recipient,
page)`. Suggested by JourneySpine, adopted verbatim.

## ACCEPTANCE EVIDENCE

`RCH_ENABLED=false CARGO_MINT_MIN_CONTAINER_PCT=0 cargo test --quiet
-p agent-mail-native` at 05:29:32Z:
  61 unit passed / 0 failed / 0 ignored
  2 integration passed / 0 failed / 4 ignored
  1 doc test passed / 0 failed

`-- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1` at 05:29:50Z, 4 live tests passed,
verbatim output:
  daemon tail cursor:5172 vs CLI tail cursor:5172 (skew 0)
  health: status=ready version=Some("0.3.31") projects=136 messages=5025
  baseline cursor: cursor:5172
  sent message:40810 (verified_sender=false)
  first read: 1 event(s), ours at cursor:5186 (message message:40810)
  second read: 0 event(s), next cursor:5186 (no replay)
  acked message:40810 at Some("2026-09-02T05:29:51.735658Z")
  receipt: persisted=true signaled=false acknowledged=true
  tools advertised: 45

ROUND-TRIP, NO REPLAY AND NO GAP, proven: baseline 5172 taken via
`position_now` (which returned zero events, asserted); our own message landed
at 5186 and appeared in the read resumed from 5172 (NO GAP); the read resumed
from 5186 returned zero events with `next_cursor` unchanged (NO REPLAY), and
every returned event is asserted strictly above the persisted cursor.

ANTI-VACUITY: 45 tools enumerated with all 13 journey tools individually
asserted present. `MailClient::list_tools` refuses an empty catalogue with
`MailError::EmptyCatalogue`, so "0 endpoints reachable" cannot pass — the test
asserting it is not merely absent, the result is unrepresentable.

TYPED REFUSAL: a bound-then-released ephemeral port yields
`MailError::Unreachable { endpoint, detail }` with the port named; the test
panics explicitly on `Ok`, naming it "the exact false-negative this crate
exists to prevent". A dummy token is supplied deliberately so the credential
check cannot fire first and make the test prove nothing about reachability. A
second test proves a missing credential refuses with `MissingCredential`
BEFORE any I/O.

## DEFECTS — resolution named for each

1. DEFENDED + NEEDS UPSTREAM. `fetch_inbox_events` promises `CURSOR_EXPIRED`
   below retained history and SILENTLY CLAMPS instead. Against GreenFrog
   (floor 2108), `after: 1` returned rc=0 and a normal success page starting
   at 2108 with no warning field. Strictly more dangerous than an undocumented
   clamp: a consumer who READ THE DOCS will not defend against it.
   Defence: `journey::verify_resume_continuity` + `resume_from`.
   Independently reproduced by JourneySpine. Upstream:
   github.com/Dicklesworthstone/mcp_agent_mail_rust.
   Note the honest limit: below the floor, "events were skipped" and "this
   recipient started later" are indistinguishable, so the refusal says
   CONTINUITY IS UNPROVABLE — never that data was deleted.
2. DEFENDED. `fetch_inbox` marks read by default; a read mutates state.
   `InboxRequest::mark_read` is explicit and defaults to false, and the live
   test asserts `read_ts` is still null after a read.
3. DEFENDED. Refusals ride HTTP 200 inside a double-encoded payload; a client
   checking only the status treats every refusal as success. Both signals are
   checked and refusals promoted to typed variants.
4. NAMED (BlueLantern, `1p0u`). Agent Mail reports `signaled: false` while
   `persisted` and `acknowledged` are both true — messages 40786 AND 40810,
   two independent instances, in Agent Mail itself rather than a caller.
   Surfaced as `RecipientReceipt::is_persisted_but_unsignalled`.
5. NAMED. `am robot search` RED for the whole corpus:
   `SQLite error: column not found: m.topic`. Three independent readers.
6. Separate wake bead filed for NTM `mail_pending`.

## CONTRACT COMPLIANCE

`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`. No `.sh`, no `.py` added. `&Cx` first in every async
API; `cx.checkpoint()` before and after I/O; every request bounded; no
detached tasks. All subprocess work delegated to the existing
`subprocess-contract` kernel (own process group, both pipes drained
concurrently, `RunError::Timeout` distinct) rather than a handrolled
`Command` — KERNEL-ONLY honoured, and no poller was written because the
blocking wake already exists in NTM.

A timeout is never a verdict: `MailError::TimedOut` and
`MailWakeOutcome::TimedOut` carry no claim about the subject;
`MailError::is_inconclusive_about_mail` exists so a dispatch loop cannot report
"no mail" on a transport failure; `MailWakeOutcome::CancelledWithoutCursor` is
distinct from `TimedOut` because one keeps the resume point and the other does
not.

Secrets: bearer token and `SenderToken` are redacted in `Debug` (asserted by
test), discovered at runtime from env then MCP client config, and are not
literals in this source. Distinct types for wire-interchangeable integers:
`DeliveryCursor`, `MessageId`, `AttentionCursor`.

Reservation held throughout: `crates/agent-mail-native/**` exclusive, id
110912, taken via the daemon — no worktree, no branch.

## NO-CLAIM BOUNDARY

- The 4 live tests are `#[ignore]`d by default so a default `cargo test` stays
  hermetic; they are proof of the round-trip, not of hermetic CI.
- `verified_sender: false` in the round-trip: the test does not persist the
  registration token, so the signed path is implemented and unit-tested but
  NOT proven end-to-end against the daemon.
- The oracle agreement is one reading at one instant (skew 0 at cursor 5172),
  not a sustained differential lane.
- `CURSOR_EXPIRED` is modelled from the daemon's documented contract; it was
  never observed live, because the daemon clamps instead of emitting it.
- No claim is made about `mark_all_read`, contacts, products, archive, ATC, or
  search — out of journey scope and untouched.

VERDICT: implemented, tested, and PROVEN LIVE against the running daemon.
Left `in_progress` for a non-implementer to grade.

against the daemon. Fresh cursors, fresh message, same invariants:

  baseline cursor: cursor:5191

`persisted=true signaled=false acknowledged=true` on messages 40786, 40810,
AND 40826 — three separate messages across 27 minutes, every one of them
delivered and acknowledged while never signalled. This is in Agent Mail
itself, not in a caller, and it is reproducible on demand via
`journey::delivery_receipt`. BlueLantern owns it for `1p0u`; the predicate is

133 projects / 4,982 messages at 05:00Z -> 136 / 5,025 at 05:29Z -> 136 / 5,041
