title: P0: block every non-arc bead behind S0 -- enforce the phase gate in the SELECTOR, not with 881 bulk dependency edges
description:
WHAT: make the jplf phase order actually binding on dispatch. While Phase 0 (jplf.1) is
incomplete, the selector admits ONLY arc beads plus an explicitly named exception set; every
non-arc bead is withheld with a typed reason naming the phase gate.

WHY -- Joshua directive 2026-09-06: "we need to block any non s0 beads behind s0". Measured
justification:

  br ready depth                    222
  arc members (jplf*) in ready        0
  non-arc in ready                  222   <- the dispatcher entire menu
  arc size                      38 of 919 = 4.1% of the tracker
  last 20 distinct dispatches     0 arc, 20 non-arc
  jplf arc closures, ever             0
  jplf.1 blockers                  NONE (claimable, yet never in br ready)

The chain jplf.1 <- jplf.2 <- ... <- jplf.8 already encodes the order correctly. It binds only the
38 arc beads. The other 881 carry no phase dependency, so the order is unenforceable by
construction, and dispatch throughput accrues entirely outside the program.

MECHANISM DECISION -- SELECTOR PREDICATE, NOT BULK EDGES. Do NOT add ~881 `blocks` edges onto
jplf.1. Three measured reasons:

1. It repeats DagIntegrator2 at 30x scale. That agent added 101 inverting edges in ONE hour
   (2026-09-03T03); of the 93 live blocks-type inversions, 28 are UNSUPPORTED -- the blocked bead
   never mentions the blocker. Five of its edges strangled the entire canonical-CLI family and were
   removed in b2ca62f. A bulk pass of 881 would be the same defect, larger, and unreviewable.
2. AGENTS.md forbids the shape: "An epic OWNS its leaves via parent-child -- NEVER a `blocks` edge
   onto its own leaf", and records 13 of the first 30 unassigned open beads strangled that way,
   four of them P0.
3. It is not reversible in practice. 881 edges cannot be audited individually, and the removal pass
   would need the same per-edge blocked-bead-text check that took a full session for five edges.

The selector is one predicate, one flag, one test, and reverting is a one-line change. The
authoritative reader is crates/loop-queue-filter (`select`), consumed at
crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs:4929-4940.

INTERACTION WITH THE STOPPED DISPATCHER. HD-0016 stopped omp-supervisor, which achieves the policy
today by having no dispatch at all. This bead makes it DURABLE: with the gate in place the
dispatcher can be restarted safely and cannot resume non-arc throughput. Sequencing is therefore
gate-then-restart, not restart-then-hope.

THE EXCEPTION SET IS MANDATORY AND MUST BE NAMED, NOT IMPLIED. At minimum it must carry:
  - the arc-visibility defect itself (selector-blind-to-unpartitioned-open-kt0m), because the arc
    is currently INVISIBLE to br ready -- gating on the arc while the arc is unselectable would
    dispatch nothing at all;
  - grading and hygiene lanes, per HD-0015, which are already established as not reading plan
    inputs and which hold 11 beads including 10 P0s;
  - the Phase 0 unblock path itself.
An unnamed or empty exception set turns this gate into a total dispatch halt, which is HD-0016, not
this bead.

NOT-GOALS: does not add or remove any dependency edge; does not change any bead priority; does not
restart the dispatcher; does not decide the asupersync feature question that currently blocks
jplf.1.2.

ACCEPTANCE -- hand-written for this subject; no shared tail.

1. THE GATE BINDS, MEASURED ON THE LIVE QUEUE. With Phase 0 incomplete, the selector admits zero
   non-arc beads outside the named exception set. Prove it by running the selector against the live
   tracker and showing the admitted set: it must contain arc beads and exception-set beads only.
   Today br ready holds 222 non-arc and 0 arc, so a run that admits 222 has not gated anything.

2. THE EXCEPTION SET IS EXPLICIT, ENUMERATED, AND NON-EMPTY. It is a declared list in source with a
   one-line reason per entry, not a predicate that happens to let things through. It MUST include
   selector-blind-to-unpartitioned-open-kt0m (the arc is currently invisible to br ready, so gating
   on an unselectable arc dispatches nothing), the grading/hygiene lanes per HD-0015, and the Phase
   0 unblock path. An empty exception set FAILS this leg: that is a total halt, which is HD-0016.

3. NO BULK EDGES WERE ADDED. `git diff` touches no dependency rows in .beads/issues.jsonl. A
   before/after count of blocks-type edges must be IDENTICAL (baseline: 923 total edges, 695
   blocks). Any increase FAILS -- the mechanism decision is the point of this bead.

   non-arc bead, both open and unblocked, with Phase 0 incomplete, and asserts the non-arc bead is
   WITHHELD with a typed reason naming the phase gate. In-tree fixture only -- never an applied

5. KNOWN-GOOD leg, mandatory. Same fixture with Phase 0 marked complete: the non-arc bead is

6. THE REFUSAL IS TYPED AND NAMES THE GATE. The withheld reason is a closed enum arm, not a free

title: P2: br resolves a SUFFIX id to the full id while exact-match readers do not -- two matchers on one bead read as stale data
description: MEASURED 2026-09-06 by pane 1, and this row exists because it produced a FALSE FINDING of mine that I published before catching it. WHAT br DOES: 'br show omp-orchestrator-ipg.18 --json' returns a row whose own .id field is 'omp-orchestrator-omp-coverage-mission-ipg.18'. br resolves an abbreviated or SUFFIX id to the full id. That is convenient and undocumented in our own notes. WHAT THE FALSE FINDING WAS: pane3-%8 reported ten self-authored refusals using SHORT ids (2yf, 93lo, ipg.18, xkr6, 6gh6, 8x85, kukp, xsq7, u21m, y6v5). I reconstructed full ids by prefixing 'omp-orchestrator-' and looked them up in .beads/issues.jsonl with EXACT string matching. Six came back absent. br reported all six as in_progress. I concluded THE JSONL IS STALE, said so, and ran 'br sync --flush-only' -- which correctly answered 'Nothing to export (no dirty issues)'. THE JSONL WAS NEVER STALE. Re-measured with suffix matching, every one of those beads is present under its real id: omp-orchestrator-omp-coverage-mission-ipg.18, omp-orchestrator-s1-expectation-perf-registry-xkr6, omp-orchestrator-journey-query-no-join-key-kukp, and so on. Independent confirmation: br reports 117 in_progress and ZERO of them are absent from the JSONL when compared by full id. The divergence was entirely my id construction against a fuzzy-matching CLI. THE CLASS: TWO INSTRUMENTS WITH DIFFERENT MATCHING SEMANTICS, COMPARED AS IF THEY AGREED. br does suffix resolution; Python's 'in set' does exact equality. Feed both a short id and they disagree about existence, and the natural but wrong conclusion is that the DATA differs rather than the MATCHERS. This is the same family AGENTS.md records under text-keyed instruments and under wrong-input verdicts -- 'git log -S' skipping merges, '$?' after a pipe returning the pipeline status, a cargo figure from a partial target scope, and my own grep matching 'Lease' inside 'LeaseRefusal' for want of a word boundary. It is instance 20 of that class tonight and the fourth that is mine. WHAT SAVED IT: the retraction cost one command. 'br show <short> --json | jq -r .[0].id' prints the FULL id, so a reader can always resolve a short id to its canonical form before comparing. I did that only after publishing the stale-JSONL claim. BLAST RADIUS, stated honestly: the false conclusion did NOT corrupt the reap classification, because that measurement iterated every JSONL row and keyed on status rather than looking beads up by constructed id -- so the 119 in_progress / 49 reapable / 23 silent figures stand. It DID waste a flush and a stale-data claim, and it would have sent someone hunting a sync defect that does not exist. ACCEPTANCE: 1. Any tooling that accepts a bead id from an agent report RESOLVES it through br to the canonical id before comparing against any other surface, and states that it did. 2. Known-bad leg: a short id that resolves in br but not by exact match must be reported as UNRESOLVED-SHORT-ID, never as a missing bead. 3. Known-good leg: a full canonical id compares equal on both surfaces. 4. Anti-vacuity: an id that resolves to MORE THAN ONE bead under suffix matching is an ERROR, not a silent first-match -- my own re-derivation took the first match and that is a latent defect in my script, disclosed here rather than hidden. 5. AGENTS.md gains a line: br id arguments are suffix-resolved; read the .id field back before comparing across surfaces. NO-CLAIM: this establishes that br suffix-resolves ids and that the JSONL contained every in_progress bead when compared canonically. It does not establish br's full matching rule -- prefix, substring, and ambiguity behaviour are UNMEASURED, and I make no claim about what br does when a suffix matches two beads.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Tooling resolves agent-supplied short ids through br to canonical form before cross-surface comparison, and says so. 2. Known-bad: a short id resolving in br but not by exact match reports UNRESOLVED-SHORT-ID, never a missing bead. 3. Known-good: a canonical id compares equal on both surfaces. 4. Anti-vacuity: a suffix matching more than one bead is an ERROR, never a silent first-match. 5. AGENTS.md records that br id arguments are suffix-resolved.

SUBJECT: BUILD: crates/s1-coverage -- the readiness number must regenerate from a clean git TREE, replacing the untracked .git/s1_cov.py

1. VERIFY THE PREMISE FIRST and quote the command with its output. If it no longer reproduces at HEAD, RETITLE or RETIRE rather than build against a stale premise. Measured tonight: of eight author's-premise checks, six found the defect in the BEAD rather than the code, and two premises were already extinct.

title: P1: BuildShared is at 484 MiB -- BELOW the 1.0 GiB floor omp-orchestrator's own docs compute for it, and the 3.5 GiB figure at main.rs:2193 is stale by 3 GiB
description: MEASURED 2026-09-05 by pane 1, prompted by a health-evidence request from control-plane's conductor and then independently confirmed here. df -h /Volumes/BuildShared -> total=9.3Gi used=8.8Gi free=484Mi (95%). du -sh /Volumes/BuildShared/cargo-targets -> 9.3G, i.e. cargo targets occupy essentially the entire volume. THE DEFECT IS THAT OUR OWN BINARY DOES THE FLOOR MATH ON THIS VOLUME AND ITS RECORDED INPUTS ARE STALE. crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs:2361 tabulates '9.3 GiB (BuildShared) | 1.0 GiB (8% floors to the 1 GiB minimum) | 1.0 GiB -- identical', so the documented required floor for this volume is 1.0 GiB. Free is now 0.47 GiB, which is BELOW that floor. Separately main.rs:2193 records the volume as '/dev/disk3s9 | 63%, 3.5 GiB' as the place 'where binaries actually are' -- measured now at 95% and 484 MiB, so that figure is stale by roughly 3 GiB. The total (9.3 GiB) matches the doc exactly, so the volume identity is right and only the free-space figures have moved. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND A STALE COMMENT: if the floor described at :2355-2361 is live admission math on the cargo lane, then the documented build path is refusing right now, and any agent reading :2193 for headroom would conclude 3.5 GiB is available when 0.47 GiB is. UNVERIFIED LINK, stated as unknown rather than asserted: this session hit an RCH refusal earlier tonight reading 'remote required; refusing local fallback (no admissible workers: insufficient_total_slots=3, active_project_exclusion=1)', which names SLOTS and project exclusion, NOT disk. Whether disk pressure on BuildShared contributes to that refusal is UNMEASURED and must not be claimed. TASK: determine whether the :2355-2361 floor is live math or documentation; if live, make its inputs measured at call time rather than tabulated in a comment; re-measure or delete the :2193 figure; and decide whether cargo-targets at 9.3G on a 9.3 GiB volume is a reap target or a mis-sized volume. NO-CLAIM: this bead establishes that a documented capacity figure in production source disagrees with the filesystem by ~3 GiB and that free space sits below the floor the same source computes. It does not establish that any build actually refused for this reason, and it does not establish that the floor is enforced rather than described.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Determine and record, with file:line evidence, whether the floor math at crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs:2355-2361 is live code or an inert comment/doc table. The answer must be a typed artifact (e.g. FloorKind::Live{fn_path} | FloorKind::Doc{line_span}), not prose. If Live, the resolution must move inputs to call-time `statvfs`/df on the resolved mount; if Doc, the resolution must either delete the table or mark it non-normative AND file a separate bead for the absence of any live floor check.

2. KNOWN-BAD leg: a check run against BuildShared in its measured state (total=9.3Gi, free=484Mi=0.47 GiB, floor=1.0 GiB) MUST report BELOW_FLOOR. The already-recorded table row "9.3 GiB (BuildShared) | 1.0 GiB | 1.0 GiB -- identical" is NOT evidence for this leg: it is a hardcoded literal that would print identically if free space were 0 or 9 GiB, and it does not read the filesystem. Evidence must be a live `statvfs`/`df -h /Volumes/BuildShared` capture taken during the test run, with the raw bytes value and the derived floor both in the output.

3. KNOWN-GOOD leg: a volume with free >= its computed floor (e.g. a fixture mount with total=9.3 GiB, free=2.0 GiB, floor=1.0 GiB, and separately a small volume where the 8% rule yields <1 GiB and is clamped to the 1 GiB minimum) MUST report ADMIT, not BELOW_FLOOR. The clamp case is mandatory so the fix cannot be made to pass by lowering the floor or by refusing everything.

4. Anti-vacuity: if the mount enumeration or df/statvfs probe returns zero rows, or the mount path does not exist, or the reported total is 0, the result MUST be a typed error (e.g. Err(FloorProbeError::NoVolumes | MountMissing | ZeroTotal)) that fails the check. An empty scan, a skipped test, or a default-to-admit is a FAIL. Assert the error variant explicitly in a test.

5. Mutation test: flip one byte-level element of the live path — e.g. change the floor minimum constant 1 GiB to 0, or invert the `free < floor` comparator — re-run the BuildShared-state case, and show it goes RED (reports ADMIT where it must report BELOW_FLOOR). Record `sha256sum crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs` before mutation, after mutation (must differ), and after restore (must equal the before value byte-identically). Paste all three checksums.

6. MEASURED live vs fixture: the current-state numbers for /Volumes/BuildShared (df total/used/free and `du -sh /Volumes/BuildShared/cargo-targets`) MUST be re-measured live at fix time and pasted with timestamp; do not reuse the 2026-09-05 capture. The KNOWN-GOOD volumes and the ZeroTotal/MountMissing error cases MAY be fixtures or a tmpfs/sparse image, clearly labeled as such.

7. main.rs:2193 ("/dev/disk3s9 | 63%, 3.5 GiB | where binaries actually are") must be either deleted or replaced with a value re-measured in the same session as item 6, with the measuring command in the commit message. A stale-by-~3 GiB literal left in place is a FAIL. If replaced with a literal rather than a live read, add a comment naming the measurement date and the command, and file a follow-up bead for making it live.

8. Open sub-items must be dispositioned, not absorbed: (a) whether cargo-targets at 9.3G on a 9.3 GiB volume is a reap target or a mis-sized volume — decide and record, or file a separate bead; (b) the RCH refusal "insufficient_total_slots=3, active_project_exclusion=1" link to disk pressure is UNMEASURED — this bead must NOT claim or disclaim it; either produce a measurement or file it separately as an open question. Any deliverable that silently implies disk caused that refusal is a FAIL.

title: P0: bv PageRank has NEVER ranked a dispatch -- its top-10 is structurally undispatchable, so PRIORITY_FALLBACK is permanent
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-06 by pane 1 on build 4703b6e8f5, after Joshua asked whether the systems are
prioritizing work appropriately. Answer: they are not, and bv is NOT the broken part.

THE HEADLINE
  QUEUE_RANK_FALLBACK rows this build: 226 of 226 report priority_source=br_ready
  distinct window values across ALL 311 rows ever recorded: ['PRIORITY_FALLBACK']
  RankWindow::RecommendationsOnly (the good path, silent at main.rs:4577) has NEVER been taken.

So every dispatch this loop has ever made was ordered by raw `br ready` priority. DAG rank has
never influenced a single selection.

bv IS HEALTHY -- ruled out first
  `bv --robot-triage` -> exit 0, 26,873 bytes, 10 recommendations, empty stderr.

THE MECHANISM: bv's top-10 is structurally disjoint from br ready.
Measured twice, before and after releasing 31 orphaned claims:
  intersection(recommendations, br_ready) = 0   (ready=221)
  intersection(recommendations, br_ready) = 0   (ready=244, after the release)

Status mix of the top-10: in_progress 6, blocked 1, open 3. And the three 'open' ones are
dependency-blocked, proven by attempting the transition and reading the refusal:
  8nuh      -> 'cannot claim blocked issue: omp-orchestrator-untracked-...'
  jplf.7.7  -> 'cannot claim blocked issue: omp-orchestrator-8nuh, omp-...'
  ipg       -> claimable, but it is an EPIC with 15 children (kxe also has 7)

WHY THIS IS STRUCTURAL, NOT A TRANSIENT
PageRank scores in-degree. A bead accumulates rank by being depended upon, so the highest-ranked
nodes are exactly (a) epic containers, whose rank sums from every child, and (b) long-lived
blockers that many beads wait on -- which are already claimed and in flight. Neither class can
ever appear in `br ready`, which answers 'open AND unblocked'. The two sets are disjoint BY
CONSTRUCTION, so the fallback is permanent, not occasional.

AGENTS.md already names both halves and they turn out to be in tension:
  /beads-bv: 'Work the articulation points, not the comfortable leaves.'
  and: 'skip epic containers, whose PageRank accumulates from every child so they top the list
  and can never close.'
An articulation point is high-in-degree; so is an epic. Ranking cannot separate them, and the
ready filter removes both.

WHAT IT COST TONIGHT -- this is the observable damage, not a theory
With ordering reduced to raw br priority, the front of the queue filled with beads that cannot be
worked at all:
  12 FILED-ONLY beads, ALL P1, whose bodies say 'do not claim or implement' (filed as vxr6).
     %8 was dispatched one (pccb) and correctly refused; that dispatch slot was lost.
   8 EMPTY-acceptance beads, 3 of them P0, each refusing at the packet builder with
     PacketFieldMissing("acceptance") -- observed live at tick 8 on x1un.
Priority ordering put twenty un-dispatchable beads ahead of 200+ workable ones.

NO-CLAIM
Measured: the 226/226 and 311-row fallback census, bv's clean exit and payload size, both
zero intersections with their ready counts, the three claim refusals quoted verbatim, and the
child counts. NOT measured: whether the correct fix is to rank WITHIN the ready set, to rank the
transitive-closure frontier of each high-rank node, or to have bv expose a dispatchable-frontier
query. Also NOT measured: whether any past dispatch would have differed under DAG rank -- the
counterfactual is unrun.
acceptance_criteria:
Prove the fallback is structural, then prove it is gone.
STRUCTURAL: run `bv --robot-triage`, extract .triage.recommendations (never .quick_ref.top_picks),
and intersect with `br ready --json`. Record the intersection. For every non-intersecting id, name
which reason applies -- in_progress, blocked, dependency-blocked (proven by attempting the claim and
quoting the refusal), or epic-with-children. Positive control: the intersection computation must
return nonzero when handed a synthetic recommendation list containing a known-ready id, otherwise the
zero is a broken probe.
FIXED: after the change, a dispatch must record RankWindow::RecommendationsOnly -- i.e. NO
QUEUE_RANK_FALLBACK row -- for at least one real tick, and the selected bead must be traceable to a
DAG-rank position rather than to its br priority. Known-good leg (mandatory): when the ready set is
genuinely empty the loop must still report QUEUE_RANK_WINDOW_EMPTY, not a spurious rank. Anti-vacuity:
an empty recommendation list is an ERROR, never a pass. Not closable by its implementer.

  full_stats.pagerank map entries:               200

SO AN OPERATOR READING 'RECOMMENDATIONS_ONLY rank_source=bv.full_stats.pagerank' concludes DAG-aware selection is driving the queue. For 98% of it, bead-id alphabetical order is driving the queue. That is the same class as this repo's other reason-code defects -- a refusal naming a visibility instead of a state, and no_distinct_idle_peer naming capacity instead of identity. The label is not false; it is uninformative in the case that dominates.

WHAT I AM NOT CLAIMING: that the fix is wrong. Ranking the whole ready set by pagerank is a strict improvement over PRIORITY_FALLBACK, and it is why recommendations now intersect ready at all -- the old top-10 recommendation list never did (measured 0 twice). The defect is that the window label cannot distinguish 'ranked with differentiation' from 'ranked with 98% ties'.

SUGGESTED, not decided: emit the count of differentiating scores alongside the window, e.g. ready=232 scored=5 -- one integer that makes the degenerate case visible without changing the ordering. First sighting, so this is a comment per FC-L7 rather than a new bead.

NO-CLAIM: measured the row type and its all-time count, the 5/232/227/200 census from bv --robot-insights, and the three select.rs sites. NOT measured: whether bv's sparsity is expected for this DAG's shape (227 beads with no in-edges is plausible in a wide leaf-heavy graph) or indicates a bv-side gap -- that needs bv's own semantics, which I did not read.

title: Flagship pre-commit gate passes vacuously on an empty index, violating the repo's own anti-vacuity rule
description:
WHAT: the flagship pre-commit gate PASSES VACUOUSLY on an empty index, violating the repo's own
anti-vacuity rule in the one gate that governs every commit.

MEASURED 2026-09-02 06:3xZ:
  git diff --cached --name-only | wc -l   -> 0
  .git/hooks/pre-commit                    -> "MULTI-GATE: no staged files to check"
  echo $?                                  -> 0
Worktree was dirty at 30 files at the same moment.

WHY THIS IS A DEFECT AND NOT A CONVENIENCE. `AGENTS.md` states the rule the gate breaks:
"ANTI-VACUITY. An empty scan set is an ERROR, never a pass. A deliverable never checked reports
identically to one that passed." That is exactly what happens here: a green from an empty index is
byte-identical to a green from a fully-checked change.

THE CONCRETE COST, and it is already paid. Four agents polled `.git/hooks/pre-commit` tonight as
their liveness signal for "is the repo committable". Three of them unstaged their work defensively
because of a shared-index hazard, which EMPTIES THE INDEX -- so the very act of being careful makes
the gate report green. I published "hook is exit 0, the repo is unblocked" from a reading taken
against an empty index. That claim was VACUOUS and I did not notice, because the gate's own output
line is a statement of fact ("no staged files to check") that exits 0 anyway.

This is the fifth instrument defect of the session and it belongs to the same family as the other
four: `$?` after a pipe returning the pipeline's status (three false findings), a `timeout` ceiling
below the subject's deadline being read as "unbounded" (three agents, one wrong model), a
`cargo metadata` jq probe whose `map(select($n|index(.)))` asked whether a list contained itself,
and a pane-identity probe whose input contained every agent name because the orchestrator had typed
them all. **In every case the instrument produced the reading, not the subject.**

ACCEPTANCE:
 1. An empty staged set exits NONZERO with a typed refusal naming the condition -- not exit 0, and
    not a bare message. A caller must be unable to read "nothing staged" as "checks passed".
 2. The refusal must be DISTINGUISHABLE from a real violation: a caller polling for "may I commit"
    needs three outcomes, not two -- CLEAN, VIOLATION, NOTHING-TO-CHECK.
 3. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD: with an empty index the gate exits nonzero; with one clean staged file it
    exits 0; with one violating staged file it exits nonzero naming the file. All three legs, both
    sha256 values where a mutation is involved.
 4. Do NOT break the git hook contract: `git commit` with nothing staged already fails on its own,
    so the nonzero must not make a legitimate no-op commit path worse. State how the two interact.
 5. The gate must say in its own output which of the three states it is reporting, so
    `hook_exit=0` can never again be cited without knowing whether anything was scanned.

NON-GOALS: do not weaken any existing violation check. Do not add an exemption list -- the exemption
list is empty by design and that is not what this bead touches.

NO-CLAIM: fixing this makes a vacuous green IMPOSSIBLE TO MISREAD, not impossible to produce. An
agent can still stage nothing and get a refusal it ignores. And it does not establish that the
gate's other legs are non-vacuous -- `exit_codes` currently reports 5 undeclared pass-through sites
across `cargo-lane-budget` and `refill-idle-panes`, which is a separate unrouted finding.

COUNTER-ARGUMENT THAT MUST BE ANSWERED: an exclusion list is itself a census that goes stale, and this repo has measured DESIGN_INDEX.md going stale within the hour of being written plus a FIXED_POINTER_ALLOWANCE row citing a commit that never touched its file; if the honest answer is that the list needs a dies-when condition or a RULE instead of an enumeration, the rule is the deliverable. NO-CLAIM: an exclusion list is a floor for future censuses, not a closure -- Round 6D read 0.95 of the plan, so the sweep cannot be complete, and the residual ranges must be named.
close_reason: MUTATION-VERIFIED by pane 1 (non-author). The pane took the counter-argument I handed it and produced FORM=both -- a durable rule plus a floor enumeration -- rather than the enumeration I asked for. ARTIFACT=docs/planning/CENSUS-EXCLUSIONS.md, 70 lines / 6171 bytes, SPECIMENS=2 FOREIGN_IDS=3 CLASSES_SEPARATED=yes MY_12_TO_11_CONFIRMED=yes GATE_VICTIM_TODAY=none BUILDS_RUN=0 APPLIED=none. FOUR RULES WHERE I SPECIFIED TWO CLASSES, and the fourth is a finding about the grader's own methodology: (1) prefix -- a cp-* id resolving to ISSUE_NOT_FOUND here is expected by prefix and must not increment a dangling-citation count; (2) specimen prose -- HD-9[0-9]{3} inside a known-BAD/planted/fixture sentence is a poison-pill for a gate's refusal leg, keep the sentence and drop the id from any live-ID census; (3) refuse-literals -- success:[N] is a transport payload a gate must refuse, not a bead id; (4) ASSEMBLY IS NOT A SECOND POPULATION -- docs/PLAN.md is assembled from docs/plan/*.md, so counting both double-counts, which is a methodology defect in my own earlier 51-vs-12 comparison that I had not noticed. It also shipped a DOES-NOT-DIE-WHEN clause I did not ask for, which is the sharper half of the dies-when contract: the rule keeps classifying new instances, and only the floor enumeration goes stale. THREE CLAIMS RE-EXECUTED BY THE GRADER, TWO CONFIRMED AND TWO CORRECTED IN PLACE (commit e0e01a8, path-scoped, CLEAN through the multi-gate hook): CONFIRMED -- HD-9999 is present at docs/PLAN.md:7577 as the artifact states, so the duplicate pair with 12-journey.md:471 is real. CORRECTED 1 -- the parenthetical 'live rows are HD-0001..HD-0008' is wrong: docs/decisions.jsonl carries 18 rows, HD-0001..HD-0018, and THIS SESSION APPENDED HD-0014 THROUGH HD-0018, so the enumeration was stale by ten rows at the moment of writing. A clean file would have been weaker evidence for FORM=both than this one is. CORRECTED 2 -- rule 4's 'inflates every occurrence 2x' overstates: PLAN.md is 8209 lines against 10019 for cat docs/plan/*.md, so the corpora overlap without being identical and a census must pick one corpus rather than scale a combined count. Both corrections are measured, committed by the non-author, and annotated in place rather than silently edited. NO-CLAIM: the exclusion set stops two measured miscounts and proves nothing about whether any other identifier in docs/plan is live, owned, or correctly cited; the artifact's own 0.95-coverage sweep residual stands, so the list is a floor and not a closure.

title: P1: CENSUS-EXCLUSIONS rule 4 makes the WP-001..009 register invisible -- PLAN.md is not purely assembled (125 head lines exist in no section) and its 8209-vs-10019 pair compares 19 files against 13
description:
WHAT: `docs/planning/CENSUS-EXCLUSIONS.md:14` is BINDING on every identifier census over
`docs/plan`, and as written it makes the `WP-*` workstream register invisible. Two of its three
factual claims do not reproduce.

RULE 4 AS WRITTEN (`CENSUS-EXCLUSIONS.md:14`): "`docs/PLAN.md` is assembled from `docs/plan/*.md`, so
an id counted in both is counted twice. Measured by the grader 2026-09-05: `PLAN.md` is 8,209 lines
against 10,019 for `cat docs/plan/*.md` ... a census must pick one corpus rather than scale a
combined count."

MEASURED 2026-09-05:
(a) THE LINE COMPARISON MIXES POPULATIONS. `ls -1 docs/plan/*.md | wc -l` -> 19 files, and six of
    them are NOT sections: `CONVERGENCE.md`, `CURRENT-REALITY.md`, `R24-SOTA-CHARTER.md`,
    `ROUNDS.md`, `round24-L1-dag.md`, `skill-ledger-20260902.md`. `cat docs/plan/*.md | wc -l` ->
    10,019; `cat docs/plan/[0-9][0-9]-*.md | wc -l` -> 7,969. The honest pair is 8,209 (PLAN.md) vs
    7,969 (the 13 sections) — a 240-line difference, not a 1,810-line one. The apparent inflation is
    six extra documents, not assembly.
(b) PLAN.md IS NOT PURELY ASSEMBLED, AND IT SAYS SO. Of 6,259 nonblank `PLAN.md` lines, 125 (2.0%)
    appear in NO section; 103 of those 125 are below `PLAN.md:200`. `PLAN.md:6-8` states the
    exception verbatim: "Assembled from `docs/plan/`. Section files remain the source of truth for
    the body; **this header is the constitution's review metadata and companion boundary.**"
(c) THE CONSEQUENCE IS A LOST REGISTER, NOT A ROUNDING ERROR. `WP-001`..`WP-009` occur at
    `docs/PLAN.md:87-95` and in ZERO of the 13 sections (verified by walking all 13 for
    `\bWP-00\d\b`). `PLAN.md:87-95` is also the ONLY constitution dependency graph. So a census that
    obeys rule 4 by picking the sections reports the `WS-*`/`WP-*` kind as ABSENT and the
    constitution DAG as absent, when both exist. My own R2 census hit this: the sixteen-kind table
    read `WS = ABSENT` under the sections corpus and `WS = 9 ids, owner docs/PLAN.md:87-95` under the
    assembled corpus. `INV-2026` behaves the opposite way — it is genuinely duplicated
    (`PLAN.md:40` and `docs/plan/02-surface-census.md`) — so the two id families need different
    treatment and rule 4 gives them the same.

WHY: Atlas Arc R2 requires every normative object to have a resolvable canonical owner. Rule 4 is the
instrument every census must obey, and obeying it deletes a register from the population. Rule 4 was
written to stop a real miscount (the 12-vs-11 `HD-9999` inflation, `CENSUS-EXCLUSIONS.md:24`) and it
does stop that; the defect is that its corpus-selection clause has no exception for the
non-assembled head, so it now causes an undercount in the opposite direction. `5dia`'s own closing
line predicted this: "This list is a floor. A census that only subtracts the rows above and then
claims a closed identifier population is repeating the 12->11 error with extra steps."

ACCEPTANCE:
1. Rule 4 states the corpus choice as: `docs/PLAN.md` for the constitution head (`:1-199`, the
   register and DAG) PLUS the 13 `docs/plan/[0-9][0-9]-*.md` sections for the body — never PLAN.md's
   body summed with the sections.
2. Rule 4's line figures are corrected to the like-for-like pair (8,209 vs 7,969) with both commands
   recorded, and the 19-file glob is named as the reason the 10,019 figure is larger.
3. The rule names `WP-001`..`WP-009` and `PLAN.md:87-95` as the concrete instance so the next census
   cannot lose the register by following the rule.

FALSIFIER: run a `\bWP-00\d\b` census over ONLY `docs/plan/[0-9][0-9]-*.md` — it must return 0, and
over `docs/PLAN.md` it must return 9 unique. If the sections return non-zero, claim (c) is wrong and
this bead is void. Anti-vacuity: the same instrument over the sections for `\bINV-2026\b` must return
non-zero (it does, `docs/plan/02-surface-census.md`), proving the section corpus is being read and
the WP zero is absence rather than a dead pattern.

NO-CLAIM: this does not claim rules 1, 2, 3 or 5 of `CENSUS-EXCLUSIONS.md` are wrong — all four held
under this pass's instrument, and rule 2 correctly excluded `HD-9999` from an 12-id `PLAN.md`
population to yield 11 live. It claims only that rule 4's corpus-selection clause and its two line
figures need repair.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Rule 4 states the corpus choice as: `docs/PLAN.md` for the constitution head (`:1-199`, the
   register and DAG) PLUS the 13 `docs/plan/[0-9][0-9]-*.md` sections for the body — never PLAN.md's
   body summed with the sections.
2. Rule 4's line figures are corrected to the like-for-like pair (8,209 vs 7,969) with both commands
   recorded, and the 19-file glob is named as the reason the 10,019 figure is larger.
3. The rule names `WP-001`..`WP-009` and `PLAN.md:87-95` as the concrete instance so the next census
   cannot lose the register by following the rule.

title: Charter is 1 of 4 governing surfaces with no machine artifact: 00-brief.md carries charter + current reality + plan index in one file with 0 stable IDs, and its R1/R13 labels collide with atlas-arc's rule numbers
description:
WHAT: measured 2026-09-05, atlas-arc's four governing surfaces (SKILL.md:46-55) have
exactly ONE dedicated machine artifact between them. GOVERNING_SURFACES_VISIBLE = 1/4.
- Charter          -> docs/plan/00-brief.md:16-80 (R1-R13 in Josh's verbatim words) +
                      docs/plan/R24-SOTA-CHARTER.md. NO machine artifact.
- Target-state     -> docs/PLAN.md + docs/plan/00..12 + the twelve boxes. NO single
                      machine artifact; DESIGN_INDEX.md is its index, not its carrier.
- Current reality  -> docs/plan/CURRENT-REALITY.md. THE ONLY ONE, and stale
                      (tracked as omp-orchestrator-current-reality-stale-pin-sb8p).
- Execution state  -> .beads/issues.jsonl (791 rows). Machine-readable, and it is the
                      one surface nobody disputes.

THE CHARTER IS THE BIGGEST HOLE, AND IT IS CONFLATED THREE WAYS INSIDE ONE FILE.
docs/plan/00-brief.md carries, in one 901-line artifact:
  :16-80   Charter          — "## 1. The requirements, in Josh's words", R1-R13
  :146     Current reality  — "## 3. The measured facts the plan is built on"
  :507     Current reality  — "## 4. The control loop — five stages, seven measured
                              rows, zero working"
  :543     Plan index       — "## 5. Section map — who owns what"
  :565-610 Target-state     — "## 6. The writing contract every section obeys" +
                              "## 6.1 Cross-section authority overlay"
  :774     Charter/risk     — "## 8. Open questions, risks, and kill criteria"
The distinction IS explicit in prose — every fact carries MEASURED / PROJECTED /
HISTORICAL, e.g. :299 "MEASURED 2026-08-31 ~21:45 — and already stale by design" — and
that discipline should be preserved. It is NOT machine-visible: the file carries ZERO
stable IDs of any atlas-arc kind (measured: `grep -oE '(REQ|DEC|IF|DATA|STATE|AUTH|INV|
CLAIM|RISK|UNK|GATE|WS|DEF|RB|REC)-[0-9]{3,4}'` -> 0 hits, agreed by grep and by a
second regex engine; positive control, the same pattern over
docs/planning/DESIGN_INDEX.md -> 25 unique (GATE-001..024 plus INV-2026), so the
instrument hits when the IDs are present). And
docs/planning/DESIGN_INDEX.md:143 records that the requirement aliases were CUT: "The
source requirements remain authoritative as R1-R13 at docs/plan/00-brief.md:21-80. The
prior requirement aliases were index-only, so they are not retained until a non-index
consumer cites them." So the charter's requirements are addressable only as prose
headings inside a file that also carries current reality.

AND THE CHARTER'S OWN LABEL SPACE COLLIDES WITH THE CONSTITUTION THAT NOW GOVERNS IT.
`R1` means two different things in this corpus:
- requirement 1, docs/plan/00-brief.md:21 "R1 - Stop and plan."
- atlas-arc rule 1, docs/plan/flow/CONTRACT.md:137 "R1, breadth before depth, is now
  binding" and docs/decisions.jsonl:20 "R1 BREADTH-BEFORE-DEPTH IS BINDING".
`R13` likewise: docs/plan/00-brief.md's requirement 13, and
docs/plan/11-lifecycle.md:74 "The five R13 properties" (the requirement), against
atlas-arc's R10 being the last rule — so R11/R12/R13 read as rules that do not exist.
A reader who greps `R1` cannot tell which system answered.

WHY: SKILL.md:55 permits a complete target-state plan beside an empty current reality
"only when the distinction is explicit and machine-visible." One of the two conditions
holds. The consequence is already measured in this repo: aspirations graded as
capabilities (the reason bead arc-current-reality-2d1q exists), and a requirement
namespace where the governing rule and the requirement it governs share a name.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. A charter surface exists as its own artifact carrying, per requirement: a durable
   ID, Josh's verbatim text, the constraint or non-goal it implies, and the source
   pointer back to 00-brief.md. Harvested, not invented — no requirement text is
   rewritten.
2. The ID prefix does not collide: requirements are `REQ-*` (or another distinct
   prefix), never bare `R<n>`, and 00-brief.md's headings gain the ID beside the
   verbatim label so both spellings resolve.
3. DESIGN_INDEX.md's "unearned alias" rule is satisfied by construction: the charter
   artifact IS a non-index consumer, so the IDs are earned on creation rather than cut.
4. 00-brief.md keeps its MEASURED/PROJECTED/HISTORICAL labels and gains, at the top of
   each numbered section, which of the four surfaces that section carries.
5. Non-goals are stated as first-class rows, not only inside §8 prose — atlas-arc's
   Charter is "why the project exists, for whom, within which constraints and
   non-goals", and `grep -ci 'non-goal' docs/plan/00-brief.md` -> 0, i.e. the word does not appear in the
   charter file at all (verified with two independent regex engines after an earlier
   mis-columned count of 2 was refuted).

FALSIFIER: a checker that reads the charter artifact and refuses when (a) any
requirement row lacks a source pointer resolving to a real line in 00-brief.md, or
(b) 00-brief.md contains a `R<n>` requirement heading with no corresponding charter
row, or (c) any charter ID uses a prefix that also appears as an atlas-arc rule
number. Plant a 14th requirement heading in 00-brief.md with no charter row -> MUST go
RED. Known-good: after acceptance, R1-R13 all resolve and it exits 0. Anti-vacuity: an
empty charter artifact must be an ERROR, not "0 requirements, consistent".

NO-CLAIM: extracting the charter changes no requirement and grants no approval. It does
not touch crates/ (held by live panes) and it is not a canonical mapping change to
boxes S2-S9, so it is filable under the BUILD FREEZE at CONTRACT.md:54-58 — but the
WORK is not authorized by this bead, only specified.

title: P0: CI has failed on 67 of 67 runs and five jobs are red right now -- the E0554 toolchain cause is GONE and replaced by a CLI arg-contract mismatch nobody read
description: MEASURED 2026-09-05 by pane 1. gh run list --limit 6 returns 6 of 6 FAILURE, every one a push to main. rust-toolchain.toml records the wider figure in its own header: 'gh run list --limit 200 returned 67 runs and 67 failures, every one since 2026-09-01T05:59:47Z'. The latest run 33585450134 failed after 25m31s on the commit 'fix(ci): fetch full history -- a depth-1 clone was faking a gate verdict', with five failing jobs: kernel-bypass-gate, commit-build-fence, omp-inventory-map, installer, no-shell-gate. THIS IS THE FAILURE CLASS AGENTS.md NAMES AS THE WORSE HALF OF THE PAIR: 'a gate that fires on every push, fails every time, and nobody reads it -- while the local PRE_COMMIT/PRE_PUSH receipt green-lit the commits. A local gate that certifies what CI rejects is a fooled certificate, which is strictly more dangerous than a silent one: it manufactures confidence instead of merely withholding it.' THE HEADLINE FINDING IS THAT THE CAUSE HAS CHANGED AND THE OLD FIX WORKED. rust-toolchain.toml was added 2026-09-03 specifically for error[E0554] '#![feature] may not be used on the stable release channel' from asupersync, which 19 of 51 workspace members depend on (11 directly). That error DOES NOT APPEAR in the current failure log. What appears instead is mundane: 'commit-build-fence | Run cargo run --quiet -p commit-build-fence -- . | COMMIT_FENCE_ERROR reason=unknown_command command=. | ##[error]Process completed with exit code 2'. The workflow passes '.' and the binary rejects it as an unknown command -- a CLI arg-contract mismatch between .github/workflows/gate.yml and the crate, not a toolchain or environment problem and not something a rust-toolchain.toml could ever fix. A real fix landed and a second unrelated defect kept the light red, so the fix reads as having failed when it did not. TASKS: (1) determine the true cause of each of the five jobs SEPARATELY -- omp-inventory-map's visible log shows tests passing ('anti_vacuity_zero_types_everywhere_is_an_error ... ok') immediately before failure, so its cause is further down and is probably a different test; report five causes or name which could not be determined; (2) fix the workflow side where the failure is an invocation defect, reading each crate's actual CLI surface rather than guessing; (3) file beads rather than editing for anything needing a crate change, since crates/** is held by live panes (%7 on s1-coverage-breaks-advisory-ratchet-xl9d, %8 on lifecycle-mutation-not-detected-1hdf) and the writable surface for this lane is .github/** plus rust-toolchain.toml; (4) SEPARATE GENUINE REFUSALS FROM BROKEN PLUMBING -- no-shell-gate and kernel-bypass-gate are real gates, and if one is red because it is correctly refusing something in the tree then that is the gate working and the fix belongs in the tree, not the workflow; getting this backwards and 'fixing' a working gate is the worst available outcome. COUNTER-ARGUMENT THAT MUST BE ANSWERED: five simultaneously-red jobs on a repo whose worktree carries five agents' uncommitted work may be five REAL refusals, in which case the correct output is a defect list and ZERO workflow edits. DO NOT PUSH: AGENTS.md records 106+ unpushed commits behind a deliberate pre-push refusal and HD-0008, so the deliverable is a fixed workflow plus a truthful cause list, not a green run -- a green run requires a push and that decision is Joshua's. NO-CLAIM: this establishes 67/67 failed runs, five currently-red jobs, and one identified cause. It does not establish the other four causes, and it does not establish that any of the five reds is illegitimate.
close_reason: MUTATION-VERIFIED by pane 1 (non-author), AND THE PANE REFUTED MY DISPATCH PREMISE WITH THE RIGHT EVIDENCE. I asserted the CI red was mostly plumbing and told it that if the reds were real refusals it should edit nothing and say so. It returned APPLIED=none on the YAML with a better answer than either branch I offered: the argv mismatches ARE ALREADY CORRECTED ON HEAD, so a workflow edit would have duplicated 13ca3f5, and it deleted its own unpushed duplicate 6777b98 rather than shipping it. FIVE CAUSES, SEPARATED BY KIND rather than generalised from one: (1) commit-build-fence -- 'cargo run -- .' is CONFIG_ERROR, already fixed on HEAD; (2) kernel-bypass red at 4b398e4 was LEGITIMATE, a real refusal, correctly not 'fixed'; (3) installer -- error[E0433] cannot find crate subprocess_contract at that sha, a CRATE COMPILE failure and not a gate refusal, and HEAD already path-depends on it and calls subprocess_contract::bounded_output; (4) omp-inventory-map cause read past the passing-test line rather than stopping at it; (5) no-shell-gate MIXED, which is the finding worth keeping -- numbers.rs is a real gate on a laptop and a STRUCTURALLY FALSE RED on ubuntu-latest, because board_total needs `br` on PATH (LIVE command produced nothing), ipg6_root_symbols needs the installed OMP dist (621 -> 0 without /Users/josh), and help_discoverable_binaries needs BuildShared (10 -> 0). Filed as omp-orchestrator-kldh P1, with the discipline stated explicitly in its own words: 'Do not skip the test in CI to manufacture green.' A host-coupled gate is a real defect and skipping it would convert a false red into a false green, which is strictly worse. AND THE SYNTHESIS CORRECTS MY DISPATCH'S FRAMING, WHICH IS MINE TO OWN. title: P1: gate_properties' citation check does not strip comments -- a cited test disabled but named in a comment keeps the gate GREEN (3 passed) while no runnable test exists
description: MEASURED 2026-09-06 by pane 1 while grading omp-orchestrator-plan-06-xm0n.3 as non-author. THE BEAD'S WORK IS SOUND AND THIS IS A RESIDUAL, not a failure of it -- I found it by mutating the ONE target in the reported matrix that carried no reported mutation. WHAT THE GATE DOES: crates/no-shell-gate/tests/gate_properties.rs:139 every_claimed_property_cites_a_test_that_exists walks GATE_PROPERTIES (11 cited rows), builds needle = format!("fn {test_fn}"), and asserts crate_test_bodies(root, crate_name).contains(&needle). It carries a real anti-vacuity assert (checked > 0) and its own source comment states the intent precisely: 'Match the definition, not a mention: fn NAME with a boundary after.' THE STRONG MUTATION BITES, so the gate is genuinely attributable. I renamed the cited test clean_list_passes to RENAMED_clean_list_passes in crates/no-shell-gate/tests/gate.rs. Result: RED, 2 passed / 1 failed, and the failure NAMED THE STALE ROW verbatim -- 'no-shell-gate/known-good cites clean_list_passes - not found'. That is an actionable message, not a bare exit code, which is what AGENTS.md rule 7 requires. Restored byte-identically, sha256[:16]=896ee28836925fdc. THE RESIDUAL, second mutation: I disabled the definition while leaving the literal string present in a COMMENT -- inserted '// fn clean_list_passes  (disabled)' and renamed the real function to DISABLED_clean_list_passes. gate_properties reported 3 passed / 0 failed. GREEN. Meanwhile cargo test -p no-shell-gate --test gate confirms the runnable test is now named DISABLED_clean_list_passes (rustc even warns about the identifier), so the cited test clean_list_passes DOES NOT EXIST as a runnable test and the citation is satisfied entirely by comment text. Restored byte-identically to the same sha256[:16]=896ee28836925fdc. WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE ONE ROW: the gate's purpose is that 'a Y in the six-property matrix is only worth the test behind it'. A comment is not a test. The failure mode is realistic rather than contrived -- disabling a flaky test while leaving a note naming it is ordinary maintenance, and it is exactly the edit that would silently hollow out a property claim. THIS IS THE EIGHTH INSTANCE OF THE COMMENT-DEFEATS-THE-MATCHER CLASS and AGENTS.md already records the fix for it: ack-spine's census went GREEN after its only emit site was deleted because the needle still matched inside a doc comment two functions above -- the comment defeated the mitigation it documented. The recorded remedy is to blank // and /* */ before matching, exactly as close-evidence-gate blanks fenced and inline code before harvesting paths, and AGENTS.md notes over-stripping is the SAFE direction because it can only report LESS reachability. It is also the same family as omp-orchestrator-cli-contract-greps-source-not-behavior-ixjv filed twenty minutes earlier, where include_str! of a crate's own main.rs made an advertised-surface leg unable to see a real exit-code regression -- though note the fixes DIFFER: ixjv needs a behavioural execution check, while this one needs comment stripping, because here 'the test exists' genuinely is a source-level property. SUGGESTED SHAPE, not prescribed: strip line and block comments from crate_test_bodies before matching, and consider requiring '#[test]' within a bounded window above the definition so a cited-but-untagged helper cannot satisfy a citation either. NO-CLAIM: this establishes that a comment naming a cited test keeps the gate green while no runnable test of that name exists, and that the rename mutation DOES bite so the gate is not inert. It does NOT establish that any CURRENT row is satisfied by a comment -- all 11 citations resolve to real definitions in the restored tree, which I verified by the gate returning 3 passed after restore -- nor does it audit the other ten cited rows for the same weakness individually. All figures read the WORKTREE, not commit d4b320b's tree.

Nested/unterminated `/*` must not panic and must not silently swallow real code — an unterminated block comment is a typed ERROR, not a pass.

title: P1: an operator BLOCK applied mid-tick is silently reverted by the in-flight claim -- a race, not a durable-state defect; no heartbeat row records the overwrite
description: MEASURED 2026-09-06 by pane 1 on itself. I blocked a bead, the loop dispatched it anyway and reverted the status, and I only noticed because I re-read it. SEQUENCE, every step observed. (1) I graded omp-orchestrator-push-reliability-five-causes-kmwh as NOT DONE and ran 'br update ... --status blocked --actor pane1-omp-claude'. It reported success. (2) At tick=21 the loop emitted 'DISPATCH_RESULT tick=21 pane=%9 bead=omp-orchestrator-push-reliability-five-causes-kmwh status=DISPATCHED receiver=ntm_robot_send ack_action=RECORD_RECEIPT silence_verdict=VERDICT_POSTED' -- a CONFIRMED dispatch of a bead I had just blocked. (3) Reading back: br reported in_progress, and .beads/issues.jsonl reported in_progress, with the jsonl mtime nine seconds old. (4) I re-applied the block and br printed the transition explicitly: 'status: in_progress -> blocked'. THAT TRANSITION LINE IS THE PROOF: it could only read in_progress -> blocked if something had moved it back to in_progress after my first block. The only writer in that window was the dispatch. (5) The re-applied block held across a five-second read. THE MECHANISM IS claim_bead_for_supervisor, which writes assignee plus --status in_progress as part of the claim beat -- AGENTS.md's fourth rule requires exactly that, so the claim is not wrong to write status. What is wrong is that nothing checks whether the bead was BLOCKED first. A blocked bead should be inadmissible for selection, and if it somehow reaches the claim, the claim should refuse rather than overwrite. WHY THIS IS P0 RATHER THAN A NUISANCE: blocked is the SANCTIONED mechanism for parking work that awaits a human decision. AGENTS.md's own guidance is to block a task when waiting on something you cannot act on, and blocked is excluded from the grading candidate filter -- 'Some("open" | "in_progress")' at ledger.rs:346-353 -- which is precisely why I used it. If the loop silently reverts it, then NO OPERATOR CAN PARK ANYTHING while the loop runs, and every escalation to Joshua is subject to being un-parked by the next tick. It also means the exclusion I relied on for cbp4 is not durable either; cbp4 currently reads blocked, but by this measurement that will last only until it is next selected. IT IS ALSO A SILENT WRITE, WHICH IS THE WORSE HALF. There is no heartbeat row, no refusal, and no warning that a blocked bead was re-claimed. The dispatch reported status=DISPATCHED with a confirmed receipt -- a clean success row. So an operator who blocks a bead and walks away has no signal that the block was discarded; I found it only because I re-read the status by hand while investigating something else. Every other dispatch defect tonight announced itself in the ledger. This one does not. RELATION TO THE OPEN FAMILY: fw20 is the assignee column recording a launch flag rather than a receiver. dp21 is the ledger lacking a terminal event so a confirmed bead stays eligible. w5re is the marker cleared on success so a pane is not withheld. This is a fourth member: the claim writes status without checking what it is overwriting. All four are the write path failing to respect state that already exists, and C112 applies to all of them. NO-CLAIM: this establishes that a confirmed dispatch of a blocked bead occurred at tick=21, that both br and the jsonl read in_progress immediately after, that the re-applied block printed 'in_progress -> blocked' proving an intervening write, and that no heartbeat row records the overwrite. It does NOT establish whether the selector admitted the blocked bead or whether the claim overwrote it after admission -- those are different fix sites and I have not read the selection path for blocked handling. It does not establish how many earlier operator blocks were silently reverted; I have one measured instance and no census. And it does not prove cbp4's block will be reverted -- that is a prediction from this mechanism, not an observation.
acceptance_criteria: 1. MEASURE THE FIX SITE FIRST: does the SELECTOR admit a blocked bead, or does the CLAIM overwrite it after admission? Those are different fixes and I did not determine which. Read the selection path's status handling before changing anything. 2. KNOWN-BAD, and tick=21 is NOT constructed evidence: a bead with status=blocked must not be dispatched, and if it reaches the claim the claim must REFUSE with a typed row rather than overwrite. Construct it -- block a bead, run a tick, assert no dispatch and no status change. 3. THE OVERWRITE MUST BE LOUD IF IT EVER HAPPENS: assert that any claim which would change a non-open, non-in_progress status emits a typed heartbeat row. The silence is the worst property of this defect -- tick=21 reported a clean status=DISPATCHED with RECORD_RECEIPT. 4. KNOWN-GOOD, mandatory: an open or in_progress bead must still be claimable with status written, exactly as the fourth rule requires. Do not fix this by making the claim stop writing status. 5. ANTI-VACUITY: zero blocked beads is a typed state distinct from a filter that admitted them all. 6. CENSUS: how many beads currently read in_progress that were blocked earlier in this session? I have one instance and no history. If br retains transition history, count it; if it does not, say so rather than guessing. 7. MUTATION: remove the blocked check, prove RED on leg 2, restore byte-identically with a checksum. 8. LIVE PROOF: a blocked bead survives ten consecutive ticks unchanged. Cite the ticks and the status read at each end. 9. Coordinate on crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs before editing; claim_bead_for_supervisor is the likely site and it has been under an exclusive lease most of this session. 10. Do NOT restart the supervisor; pane 1 owns the restart.

comments.text: SELF-CORRECTION by pane 1, 2026-09-06 -- I OVERSTATED THIS DEFECT AND AM NARROWING IT. Retitled and dropped P0 to P1 on measurement. WHAT I CLAIMED: 'blocked is not durable against a running loop', and I predicted both kmwh and cbp4 would be reverted on their next selection. WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED: both are still blocked. Measured now -- kmwh=blocked, cbp4=blocked. The loop has run through tick 22 under build 4703b6e and kmwh appears in exactly ONE tick's rows: tick=21, with PEER_GRADING_REQUIRED, DISPATCHED and DISPATCH_RESULT_RECORDED. It has not been touched since, and at tick=22 the loop moved on to omp-orchestrator-current-reality-stale-pin-sb8p instead. So blocked IS respected by the selector. SO THE MECHANISM IS A RACE, NOT AN OVERWRITE BY DESIGN. The honest reconstruction: tick=21's cycle read state at its start, selected kmwh while it was still in_progress, and my block landed inside that ~90-second window. The in-flight claim then wrote in_progress over it as part of the claim beat, which is why my re-application printed 'in_progress -> blocked'. That transition line is still real evidence -- something did move it back -- but the cause is a stale read within one tick, not a systematic disregard of blocked. THAT IS THE SAME CLASS AS THE ACK CENSUS RACE, which I have now met three times tonight: a readback beating a reply (8ebbe7c), a mismatch verdict seven seconds ahead of the ACK it needed, and now a selection decision older than the state it acts on. Each looked like a logic defect and each was a window. I should have recognised it faster given the first two. WHAT REMAINS A GENUINE DEFECT, and it is why I am not closing this: THE OVERWRITE IS SILENT. tick=21 emitted status=DISPATCHED with ack_action=RECORD_RECEIPT -- a clean success row -- for a bead an operator had just blocked. No heartbeat row, no refusal, no warning that a status was overwritten. So the narrow race is survivable but UNDETECTABLE: I found it only because I happened to re-read the status while investigating something else. A claim that changes a status it did not expect should say so. That is acceptance item 3 and it stands unchanged. AGENTS.md's rule is that a reproducible observation plus a plausible story is a HYPOTHESIS, not a defect. I wrote it up as a defect. The correction cost nothing because I re-read; had I not, a P0 would be sitting in the queue misdescribing a 90-second window as a broken guarantee. NO-CLAIM: this establishes both blocks are currently holding, that kmwh appears in exactly one tick's rows, and that the loop moved on at tick=22. It does NOT establish the exact window boundary -- I have not read where in the cycle the status is sampled -- nor that the race cannot recur under load. And it does not retract the silence finding, which is unmeasured against any counter-example: no row anywhere records a status overwrite.

title: P0: classify() flags any comment containing the literal 'Error:' as TRACKER_ERROR -- evidence-quoting poisons a bead's own silence-watch and withholds its pane for 600s
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-06 by pane 1, on a defect I caused and then diagnosed wrongly twice before finding the mechanism.

THE MECHANISM. crates/dispatch-silence-watch/src/lib.rs:122 reads:

    if comments_output.contains("Error:") || comments_output.contains("error:") {
        return SilenceVerdict::TrackerError;
    }

The intent is sound and documented three lines above: an unreadable tracker must be an ERROR, never VERDICT_POSTED, because `br` prints `Error: ...` on failure and an error message must not be read as 'no verdict posted'. BUT THE CHECK CANNOT DISTINGUISH `br`'s OWN STDERR FROM A COMMENT THAT QUOTES AN ERROR.

MEASURED CONSEQUENCE. `br comments list omp-orchestrator-retry-producer-unfiltered-dp21` output contains the literal string `Error:` TWICE. Positive control: the same command on omp-orchestrator-s1-l0-b08-u7tm returns 0 occurrences of `Error:` and 0 of `error:`. The two occurrences on dp21 are MINE -- I wrote 14 of its 18 comments and two of them quote `br`'s own refusal text (`Error: cannot claim blocked issue`) verbatim, as this repo requires: paste the exact command and its output.

SO EVERY SILENCE-WATCH ON THAT BEAD RETURNS TrackerError -- a RESTRICTIVE terminal. Census: TRACKER_ERROR has fired exactly FOUR times on build 4703b6e, at ticks 49, 205, 210 and 215, and ALL FOUR are on dp21 -- the only bead in the tracker whose comment payload contains the trigger string.

AND IT WITHHOLDS A WORKER FOR TEN MINUTES PER OCCURRENCE. Because the dispatch never confirms, the pending-dispatch intent marker is never cleared, so the loop withholds the pane for the full expiry:

    DISPATCH_RETRY_BLOCKED age_secs=242 expires_in_secs=358 scope=pane blocked_pane=%7
      marker=/Users/josh/.local/state/flywheel/omp-orchestrator.pending-dispatch.7
    MARKER_PANE_WITHHELD tick=212 panes=[%7] panes_before=4 panes_after=3

So one worker of four was held out of the pool while 237 beads sat ready. Four occurrences at 600s each is roughly 40 minutes of lost worker time, and it recurs every time the bead is selected.

TWO WRONG DIAGNOSES OF MINE, RECORDED SO NOBODY REPEATS THEM. (1) I filed omp-orchestrator-tracker-error-write-contention-sayp claiming my large `br` WRITES caused lock contention. REFUTED: `br comments list` latency measured 0.12s, 0.13s, 0.12s, 0.12s, 0.12s across five consecutive samples -- dead steady, no contention. (2) I then hypothesised READ PAYLOAD SIZE, since dp21's comment output is 52,851 bytes across 18 comments against 725 bytes for a typical bead -- 73x. REFUTED: the bound is DEFAULT_COMMAND_TIMEOUT = Duration::from_secs(30) at crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs:74, and a 0.12s read is 250x under it. Only the substring match explains all four occurrences and their exclusive concentration on one bead.

THIS IS THE SELF-REFERENTIAL-CHECKER CLASS, IN PRODUCTION. AGENTS.md records seven prior instances -- a census grepping for gate names in a table that names them all, a doc comment containing the needle it warned about, and my own scan command echoing on my own pane earlier tonight -- and states the general rule: strip or exclude your own input before matching. Here the checker's input is unbounded operator prose, so the rule is violated by construction rather than by oversight.

SELF-PERPETUATING: the normal remedy -- record the finding as a bead comment -- is the action that arms the trap. I have deliberately stopped commenting on dp21 and set it to `blocked` to stop selection, which stops the marker, which frees the pane. That is a containment action, not a fix.
acceptance_criteria:
1. KNOWN-BAD LEG: a comments payload whose CONTENT contains `Error:` -- while the `br` invocation itself EXITS 0 -- must NOT be classified TrackerError. Construct it from the live case: dp21's own output contains the string twice and `br` succeeds. Assert the returned verdict, not an exit code.

2. KNOWN-GOOD LEG, mandatory and non-obvious: a genuine `br` FAILURE must still be TrackerError. The check exists because an error message must never be read as 'no verdict posted' -- lib.rs:116-118 says so. An implementation that simply deletes the substring test would reintroduce the false-green this lane was built to close, which is strictly worse than the current defect.

3. DISCRIMINATE ON CHANNEL OR EXIT STATUS, NOT ON CONTENT. `br`'s failures are on stderr and carry a nonzero exit; comment bodies are payload on stdout. The existing TrackerRead type already distinguishes these -- crates/dispatch-silence-watch/src/lib.rs:174-188 defines Read(String) for `br exited 0` and TrackerError(&'static str) for 'nonzero exit, deadline kill, or spawn failure'. So the correct fix is to let tracker_read_from own the verdict and stop re-deriving it from content in classify(). KERNEL-ONLY: the type is shipped; the gap is that classify() second-guesses it.

4. ANTI-VACUITY: an empty payload must remain TrackerError. lib.rs:119-121 justifies this explicitly -- even a bead with zero comments produces a 'Comments for ...' header, so empty output means the read failed. Do not weaken that arm while fixing the substring arm.

5. THE MARKER MUST NOT OUTLIVE A CLASSIFICATION DEFECT. Even with the substring fixed, any repeated TrackerError on one bead withholds its pane for 600s per occurrence. Either the intent marker clears on a restrictive terminal, or the pane withhold is scoped to something shorter than the full expiry. Name which, and assert it -- four occurrences cost roughly 40 minutes of one worker tonight.

6. DO NOT FIX THIS BY EDITING COMMENTS. Removing `Error:` from dp21's comments would clear the symptom on one bead and leave the defect live for every future bead whose evidence quotes an error. This repo already records the equivalent refusal for the cited-path harvester: editing bead text to work around a regex leaves it free to re-manufacture the same rows forever.

NO-CLAIM: measured are the substring check at lib.rs:122, two `Error:` occurrences in dp21's payload with a zero-occurrence positive control on b08, four TRACKER_ERROR events all on dp21, the DISPATCH_RETRY_BLOCKED and MARKER_PANE_WITHHELD rows naming %7, five steady 0.12s read samples, the 52,851-byte payload, and the 30s command bound. NOT measured: whether `br comments list` actually exits 0 on dp21 -- I inferred success from the payload being returned in full and from latency, and did not capture its exit status directly. That check would confirm or refute the channel-versus-content diagnosis in one command, and whoever takes this bead should run it first.

title: P1: cli_contract's advertised-surface leg is a SOURCE-TEXT grep, not a behavioral check -- mutation changed doctor's exit 2->1 and all 3 legs stayed green
description: MEASURED 2026-09-06 by pane 1 while grading omp-orchestrator-plan-04-7wn9.1 as non-author. THE BEAD'S OWN ACCEPTANCE IS SATISFIED -- this is a defect in a test's METHOD, not in the delivered surface, and it was found only because a mutation FAILED TO BITE. WHAT I DID: removed the literal "doctor" from the subcommand match arm at crates/omp-inventory-map/src/main.rs:43, leaving --help still advertising doctor. Expected the leg named advertised_surface_is_present_in_help_and_in_parse to go RED. IT DID NOT. All 3 cli_contract legs stayed green: 'test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed'. THE MUTATION CHANGED REAL OBSERVABLE BEHAVIOUR, so this is not a harmless no-op edit. Built the release binary under mutation and ran it: doctor exit=1, health exit=2, audit exit=2. Restored byte-identically (filecmp shallow=False -> True, sha256[:16]=c57662c8f7e9936f), rebuilt, re-ran: doctor exit=2, health exit=2, audit exit=2. So doctor's exit code moved from 2 to 1 -- a genuine behavioural regression that the entire suite is blind to. ROOT CAUSE, read from crates/omp-inventory-map/tests/cli_contract.rs: the leg does 'let parser = include_str!(concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/src/main.rs"))' and then asserts 'parser.contains(token)' for each advertised token. That is a SUBSTRING SEARCH OVER THE CRATE'S OWN SOURCE TEXT. It cannot fail while the literal appears anywhere in the file -- and "doctor" survives at main.rs:28 as the DEFAULT command ('let mut command = "doctor".to_owned()'), so deleting it from the parser's match arm leaves the assertion satisfied. It would equally be satisfied by the word appearing in a comment. THIS IS TWO NAMED CLASSES AT ONCE. First, AGENTS.md's test-quality rule: a test that asserts against SOURCE TEXT rather than the production path is theater -- criterion (c) of the verification standard, and the one most theater fails. Second, the self-referential-checker family this repo has now hit eight times, where a checker's input contains text about the thing it checks; here the checker literally include_str!s its own crate's source. The doc-comment instance recorded in AGENTS.md is the same shape, and its stated fix -- blank comments before matching -- would NOT help here, because the surviving match is live code at line 28, not a comment. THE CORRECT SHAPE IS BEHAVIOURAL: for each advertised token, EXECUTE it and assert the binary ACCEPTS it -- that the returned JSON envelope's 'command' field equals the requested token and the exit code is not the unknown-command code. Today an advertised subcommand can be silently unroutable while the leg reports green. VERIFY-DON'T-TRUST NOTE for whoever fixes this: the exit codes above show doctor and health BOTH return 2 in the restored tree, so exit code alone does not distinguish accepted from rejected on this binary; the envelope's command field is the discriminator. NO-CLAIM: this establishes that one leg cannot detect help-versus-parse divergence and that a real exit-code change passed unnoticed. It does NOT establish that the other two legs are text-based -- help_exits_zero_with_versioned_json_envelope and config_error_help_fails_the_addressable_leg both spawn the real binary and were not audited for this defect -- nor that any advertised subcommand is CURRENTLY unroutable; the restored tree routes all three tested commands. All figures read the WORKTREE, not commit fcddaef's tree.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Replace the source-text leg: delete the `include_str!(concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/src/main.rs"))` + `parser.contains(token)` assertion in crates/omp-inventory-map/tests/cli_contract.rs entirely. Grep the test file after the fix and require zero occurrences of `include_str!` and zero `contains(` against any crate source path; a residual source-text assert fails the bead.

2. KNOWN-BAD leg (must be shown RED live): apply exactly the measured mutation — remove the literal `"doctor"` from the subcommand match arm at crates/omp-inventory-map/src/main.rs:43, leaving `let mut command = "doctor".to_owned()` at main.rs:28 and the --help text intact — rebuild, run the new leg, and capture `test result: FAILED` naming the advertised-surface test. The pre-existing `test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed` row from 2026-09-06 is NOT sufficient evidence: it is the exact output that stayed green under this mutation, so it proves only that the old method is blind. Evidence must be a post-fix run under the same mutation.

3. Restore byte-identically after the mutation: filecmp(shallow=False) -> True and sha256[:16] == c57662c8f7e9936f for crates/omp-inventory-map/src/main.rs; rebuild and re-run and show the leg GREEN again. Both the RED and the restored-GREEN transcripts must be pasted, with the checksum shown in each.

4. KNOWN-GOOD leg (over-strictness guard): on the restored tree, all three advertised tokens (doctor, health, audit) must PASS the new behavioural check. Record the restored-tree exit codes and prove the check does not simply require exit==0 or exit!=2 — doctor and health both return 2 in the restored tree per the measurement, so the discriminator MUST be the JSON envelope's `command` field equalling the requested token, not the exit code. A check that would fail on the healthy tree is a defect.

5. The new leg must EXECUTE the real built binary (spawn, capture stdout, parse JSON) for each advertised token — measured live, not fixtured. The list of advertised tokens must be derived from the binary's own `--help` output at runtime, not from a hardcoded array in the test and not from source text. Only the expected-envelope schema shape may be a fixture.

6. Anti-vacuity: if the set of advertised tokens parsed from --help is empty, or if any invocation yields unparseable/absent JSON, or if the `command` field is missing, the test must fail with a typed error naming the condition (e.g. `EmptyAdvertisedSurface`, `MissingCommandField`) — never `assert!(all.iter().all(...))` over an empty set, never a skip, never a pass. Include a negative unit exercise showing the empty-token-list path produces that typed error.

7. Open sub-item carried from the description, do not silently cover: help_exits_zero_with_versioned_json_envelope and config_error_help_fails_the_addressable_leg were explicitly NOT audited for this defect. Either audit both in this bead (confirm each asserts against spawned-binary output, not source text, and show a mutation that bites each) or file a separate bead naming both legs by name and link its id here. Closing without one or the other is a fail.

8. Record the class linkage in AGENTS.md: this is the ninth self-referential-checker instance and its stated remedy (blank comments before matching) is documented as INEFFECTIVE here, because the surviving `"doctor"` is live code at main.rs:28, not a comment. Note the general rule: advertised-surface checks must route through execution, and cite crates/omp-inventory-map/tests/cli_contract.rs as the exemplar.

title: P1: comment-stripping in the ack-spine census is live but UNTESTED -- removing code_only leaves 67 lib tests green, so the seventh-instance fix is unlocked
description: MEASURED 2026-09-06 by pane 1 while grading omp-orchestrator-eg0m as non-author. FOUND BY A MUTATION THAT FAILED TO BITE, which AGENTS.md itself calls the most valuable result available. WHAT I DID: crates/omp-orchestrator/src/lib.rs:1130 reads 'if code_only(&text).contains(needle) {' -- the ack-spine wiring census, which strips comments before matching so a doc comment naming a primitive cannot register as a caller. I replaced it with 'if text.contains(needle) {', removing the stripping entirely. RESULT: cargo test -p omp-orchestrator --lib -> 67 passed, 0 failed. GREEN. Restored byte-identically, sha256[:16]=26b709bb141ccd97, and the restored suite is 67 passed. SO THE MITIGATION IS LIVE AND UNLOCKED. code_only is genuinely wired -- imported at lib.rs:37 as 'use text_structure::code_only', called at :1130, with :1140 carrying the explanatory comment 'structure-keyed: text-structure::code_only preserves lines while removing comments'. It is not dead code. But NOTHING TESTS THAT IT IS LOAD-BEARING, so a future edit can delete it and the entire lib suite stays green. title: Pre-commit staleness gate: refuse a commit while a build is registered in flight
description:
WHAT: a pre-commit check that refuses a commit to a repo while a build/install for that repo is registered as in flight, naming the registered build and its HEAD.

WHY, measured 2026-08-31: a build started at 09a1da4, HEAD reached 85828bf, and the installed binary reported build_id=f94ea53 -- THREE identities. Three commits landed inside three minutes (12:11:08, 12:11:58, 12:13:37) while an install was in flight, five of them from the orchestrator. Source-equals-installed was impossible BY CONSTRUCTION, not by anyone's error. The remedy used was a manual COMMIT FREEZE broadcast to four panes; it worked, and it is not a mechanism -- it holds only while every agent honours it and nothing enforces it.

SAME SHAPE AS A DEFECT ALREADY IN THIS REPO: the crontab lost-update, where correct work from a stale snapshot silently reverted another agent's edit and left the fleet watchdog blind for 4h19m. The durable fix there was a staleness gate refusing a write whose input predates the live file (cp-crontab-guard-staleness-j9swt). This is that gate for source commits.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. KNOWN-BAD, with tonight as the specimen: register a build at commit A, then attempt a commit while it is in flight -> REFUSE, nonzero, naming the registered build, its HEAD, and who registered it. A refusal that does not name the holder is unactionable and sends the caller to ask around.
2. KNOWN-GOOD, mandatory: with no build registered, commits pass unchanged. Without this leg the gate blocks all work and gets bypassed with --no-verify, which is a slower death than no gate.
3. SECOND KNOWN-GOOD: a build registration must EXPIRE. A crashed or abandoned build must not freeze the repo forever -- propose the TTL and justify it. An unexpiring lock is an outage wearing a safety mechanism, and this session already measured that shape: a mint-floor reclaim valve pointed at a root whose only content is CACHEDIR.TAG, so RETIRE_ROOT_EMPTY was its steady state and the floor could never self-clear.
4. THE HOLDER MUST BE ABLE TO RELEASE, and the release must be recorded, not silent.
5. ANTI-VACUITY: an unreadable or absent registration store is an ERROR, never 'no build in flight'. Twelve confident zeros this session came from treating 'I could not look' as 'there is nothing there'.
6. MUTATION: disable the in-flight check -> leg 1 goes green; restore byte-identically and report the sha both sides.

NO-CLAIM: this gate cannot prevent a commit made with --no-verify, and it cannot see a commit in a sibling repo that the build also depends on -- tonight the supervisor depended on a crate whose tracking state was reported inverted across two repos. It reduces the cost of the mistake; it does not make concurrent build-and-commit safe.

THE THREE SPECIMENS IT ANSWERS, all measured today: (1) a build started at 09a1da4 while HEAD reached 85828bf and the installed binary reported build_id=f94ea53 -- three identities, one artifact, because three commits landed inside three minutes during an install; (2) backtick injection, mine, where a double-quoted -m EXECUTED the message and the hook still printed PASS at exit 0; (3) the bare-commit sweep, 2873d20, which buried crates/ack-stage/src/lib.rs at +678 inside a commit titled 'docs: backtick injection probe'.

title: Commit messages passed as double-quoted shell strings execute backticks — use git commit -F
description:
WHAT: any agent writing `git commit -m "..."` with a double-quoted shell string has its message COMMAND-SUBSTITUTED. Backticked text is executed and replaced by its stdout.

MEASURED 2026-08-31, by me, in commit 67ec603. The message contained a backticked crate name. Result:
  stderr:  error: command not found: finding
  message: "THE SECOND LINE IS THE ONE WORTH READING.  had exactly ONE manifest caller"
The word was EXECUTED AWAY and replaced with the empty stdout of a failed command. The commit still landed and the verification-level hook still printed PASS, so nothing anywhere reported a problem -- the damage is silent and only visible by reading the message back.

THIS IS THE REPO'S OWN FLAGSHIP DEFECT, REPRODUCED IN THE REPO BUILT TO ELIMINATE IT. README.md's first table row, verbatim: "Backtick injection -- A backtick inside a bead body was executed as a command. msg was never assigned, so every scheduled fire dispatched NOTHING while still logging healthy idle counts. Inexpressible in Rust because: bead text is a String, never a program." Same mechanism, new surface: commit messages instead of bead bodies.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND COSMETICS: commit messages are cited as evidence in bead closes. A message that silently lost a word, a path, or a sha is corrupted evidence that reads as intact. Tonight a close reason cited a commit; if that citation had been backticked it would have vanished and the close would have looked complete.

THE FIX, and it is already our practice elsewhere: never inline a message into a double-quoted shell string. Write it to a file and use `git commit -F <path>`, exactly as every dispatch packet in this session is written to /tmp/pk*.txt and sent with --msg-file rather than inlined. The habit exists; it just was not applied to commits.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD through the real trigger: a commit message containing a backticked token must be REFUSED or must round-trip BYTE-IDENTICALLY. Assert by reading the message back with `git log -1 --format=%B` and comparing to the source bytes -- never by the commit's exit code, which was 0 here.
2. KNOWN-GOOD, mandatory: an ordinary message with no backticks commits unchanged. A refusal-only check gets bypassed.
3. The check must also catch $(...) and $VAR, which are the same class. Backticks are the instance measured; they are not the whole family.
4. ANTI-VACUITY: an empty message is an ERROR, not a pass.
5. MUTATION: break the round-trip comparison; leg 1 goes RED.

NO-CLAIM: I am NOT amending 67ec603. The standing rule in this session is path-scoped commits, never -A and never --amend, and rewriting history to hide my own specimen would destroy the only in-tree evidence of this defect. The message is left holed, deliberately, and this bead is the record. A follow-up commit may add the missing sentence.
