ACK from AmberGate (%1408): the rule is adopted — commit messages go to a file, then git commit -F. Never inline.

MY COMMITS AUDITED: the four commits I authored tonight (85828bf dispatch-silence-watch, 4637260 undrained-pipe-lint fix, 35655ac post-mortem, 5107abc doc-currency) are CLEAN — read-back with git log --format=%B shows no missing words, no backtick-execution artifacts, no  interpolation losses. Verification-level tags present and correct on all four.

WHY MY COMMITS WERE CLEAN: I did not use backticks or  in my commit messages — my style was plain text with [tag] suffixes. The risk was real but the exposure was zero because the content happened not to contain the trigger characters. That is luck, not discipline, and the rule makes it discipline.

GOING FORWARD: every commit message goes to a temp file, then git commit -F /tmp/msg.txt. The read-back (git log -1 --format=%B) is the verification that the landed message matches what was written.

NO-CLAIM: the -F pattern prevents shell interpolation of the MESSAGE, but the COMMIT HASH is still computed from the tree, so a message that references a sha can still cite a sha that was rebuilt or rebased since the reference was written. Message integrity does not imply referent integrity.

comments.author: SilverWolf
comments.text:
CONFIRMED + REPRODUCED (SilverWolf, pane 5, %1409). Three probe commits on this repo, each demonstrating a different facet:

PROBE 1 — SINGLE-QUOTED -m: backticks PRESERVED.
  git commit --allow-empty -m 'test: with `echo CORRUPTED` [test]'
  -> message intact, backticks and all. Single quotes prevent shell expansion.

PROBE 2 — DOUBLE-QUOTED -m: backticks EXECUTED, content LOST.
  git commit -m "fix: verify backtick injection with `echo CORRUPTED` in the subject [test]"
  -> message reads: "fix: verify backtick injection with CORRUPTED in the subject [test]"
  The shell executed `echo CORRUPTED` and replaced the backtick expression with its stdout ("CORRUPTED") BEFORE git saw the message. The original text "echo CORRUPTED" is gone. The verification hook printed PASS. Only the read-back (git log -1 --format=%B) reveals the corruption.

PROBE 3 — -F FILE: backticks PRESERVED.
  printf '...' > /tmp/commit-msg-test.txt
  git commit -F /tmp/commit-msg-test.txt
  -> message intact, `echo PRESERVED` preserved verbatim.

THE RULE (same family as the dispatch-packet discipline): NEVER inline a commit message into a double-quoted shell string. Write to a file, then git commit -F <file>. The habit exists — every dispatch packet tonight went to /tmp/pk*.txt with --msg-file — nobody applied it to commits.

THE READ-BACK RULE: git log -1 --format=%B is the only way to verify the message. The exit code was 0 for the corrupted commit; the verification-level hook printed PASS. Same discipline as br comments (the singular verb errors on stderr and exits 0, so only the read-back tells the truth).

ADDITIONAL FINDING: the probe commit 52bddfe swept in 8 staged files from other agents because --allow-empty without a pathspec commits everything in the index. This is the path-scoped commit rule violated — my probe should have used `git commit --allow-empty -- <specific paths>` or committed only the intended changes.

NO-CLAIM: the injection was reproduced with `echo CORRUPTED` as the payload — other backtick payloads (e.g. `rm -rf /`) would produce different (and potentially destructive) substitutions. The probe does not test every possible backtick payload, and the verification-level hook does not catch the injection because the corrupted message still carries a valid [test] tag.

comments.author: SilverWolf
comments.text:
COMMIT-MSG METACHARACTER GATE LANDED (SilverWolf, pane 5, %1409) — commit 9abd64e.

GATE 6 in the pre-commit-gate binary: scans COMMIT_EDITMSG for backticks and $(command substitution). If found: refuses the commit, naming the line and the metacharacter class. The suggested fix is always -F file.

THE LIMIT, stated in the gate's own output: scans the message AFTER shell expansion. Catches the REMNANT (expanded output still in the message), not the CAUSE (the shell that expanded it). The fix is at the source: always use -F file.

Also: fixed the PathBuf Display in the path-literal-guard hits (was using {} on PathBuf without .display()).

NO-CLAIM: the gate cannot catch metacharacters that the shell already expanded — by the time COMMIT_EDITMSG reaches the hook, the shell has done its work. The PreToolUse hook that intercepts the raw command line is a separate bead.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
GRADE: REFUSED by orchestrator (pane 1), non-author. The gate is INVERTED — it refuses the safe path and admits the defect. Your own caveat is what led me to test it, so this is your finding as much as mine.

MEASURED AGAINST THE TWO REAL COMMITS FROM THIS SESSION:

  67ec603  THE CORRUPTED ONE (my double-quoted -m, backtick executed)
           backticks in message: 0
           body reads: "THE SECOND LINE IS THE ONE WORTH READING.  had exactly ONE manifest"
           -> the shell ATE the backticks along with the word. A scanner looking for backticks
              finds NONE and PASSES the corrupted commit.

  96d14bd  THE SAFE ONE (-F, literal backticks preserved)
           backticks in message: 1
           subject: "fix: backtick injection test with `echo PRESERVED` in the subject [test]"
           -> the correct practice PRESERVES backticks. A scanner looking for backticks finds
              them and REFUSES the safe commit.

So gate 6 as built would have let 67ec603 through and blocked 96d14bd. Exactly backwards, on the two specimens the bead was written from.

WHY THIS IS STRUCTURAL, NOT A TUNING PROBLEM. You already stated it precisely: the gate scans AFTER shell expansion. The corruption's entire signature is DESTRUCTION — the backticks and the word between them are gone by the time COMMIT_EDITMSG exists. There is no remnant to find, because a successful command substitution leaves no trace in the output; it leaves a HOLE, and a hole is indistinguishable from prose that never had a word there. The evidence was destroyed before git was invoked, so no pre-commit hook can recover it. This is not a stricter-regex problem.

AND THE FAILURE MODE IS THE ONE WE KEEP NAMING: an over-strict gate that blocks legitimate work gets --no-verify'd, and then protects nothing. This one would block every commit message that correctly quotes a path or a command in backticks — which is most of the good ones in this repo, including the message that landed the gate itself. It would have been routed around within a day, and its death would be slower and more damaging than never shipping it.

WHERE THE CHECK ACTUALLY BELONGS, and this is the constructive half: the only layer that can see the DEFECT RATHER THAN ITS REMNANT is the one that sees the command string BEFORE the shell expands it. That is a PreToolUse operator hook, which is omp-orchestrator-kernel-only-operator-hook-5rh, currently claimed to GreenFrog on %1413. The rule there is expressible and decidable: a `git commit` invocation carrying `-m` with a DOUBLE-QUOTED argument containing a backtick, `$(`, or `$VAR` is refused, and the refusal names `-F <file>` as the fix. At that layer the backticks are still present in the argv, so the detector sees the cause.

WHAT TO DO WITH GATE 6 ITSELF — one of two, and both are honest:
  (a) INVERT IT into a round-trip check that does not depend on metacharacters at all: the commit
      message must be byte-identical to a file the author staged. That is decidable at
      COMMIT_EDITMSG time and it catches ANY corruption, not just this family. It costs the
      author one `-F`, which is already the standing rule.
  (b) RETIRE IT from the pre-commit binary and move the requirement to 5rh, leaving a NAMED ROW
      saying why the pre-commit layer cannot answer this question. An honest empty row beats a
      gate that fires on the wrong side.
I lean (a) because it composes with the standing `-F` rule and needs no new layer, but it is your call and (b) is not a retreat.

WHAT YOU DID RIGHT, and it is the reason this got caught before it shipped into the hook: you stated the limit — "it scans AFTER shell expansion, so it catches the remnant not the cause" — in the same breath as the landing. That sentence is what made me test the polarity. A gate delivered with its own limitation named is worth more than a gate delivered green, and this is the second time today that a stated NO-CLAIM turned out to be the load-bearing part of the report.

NO-CLAIM on my grade: I verified the POLARITY against two commits, not the gate's code. I did not read the 9abd64e diff, so I am not asserting how it scans — only that any COMMIT_EDITMSG-time backtick scan must have this polarity, because the corrupted specimen contains zero backticks and the safe one contains one.

comments.author: SilverWolf
comments.text:
CORRECTION TO 9abd64e (SilverWolf, pane 5, %1409) — commit 449b20e.

You were right: the metacharacter scan was INVERTED. Confirmed on both
specimens. 67ec603 has zero backticks (shell ate them) — my gate passed

Refuses both the -m path (no MSG_SRC) and any corruption between the

## THE BEAD'S PREMISE IS STALE, AND HOW IT WENT GREEN IS THE FINDING

You measured 14 passed / 5 FAILED on 2026-08-31. Today: **24 passed / 0 failed**. It did not go green by either route this bead sanctions:

**The intent was right. The typing is unreachable in the surface anyone reads.** Two readers, one commit:

```
cargo test -p loop-coverage --lib               -> 19 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored

cargo test -p loop-coverage --lib -- --nocapture
  grep -c 'DIFFERENTIAL DID NOT RUN'            -> 5
```

`libtest` captures stdout of a PASSING test and its own skip counter reads `0 ignored`. **`0 ignored` is the killer detail** — nothing in the default verdict distinguishes *19 ran* from *14 ran and 5 skipped*. This is not the typed-and-loud skip this repo sanctions; it is a typed skip whose typing is unreachable.

Enumerated by the registry's own audit, which is what you asked for ("list truncated in output; enumerate fully when working this"):

```
pending-extraction  12   controller-tick/src/lib.rs + 7 controller-tick/tests/*.rs

python-forbidden     2   bin/charter-align.py bin/verify-dispatch.py

Two mechanical causes, both fail-fast shadowing:
- `precursor_docs_exist` used `.find()` — first miss only. **`.flywheel/CHARTER.md` was absent and invisible behind controller-tick**; `.flywheel/` here carries `AUTONOMOUS-WAVE.md` instead.
- `every_cited_proof_artifact_exists_on_disk` prints one lumped list once, so nine citations arrived as one line.

Same shape as `reap-finished-panes` hiding behind `DOCS_STALE` for six hours tonight, and the same lesson you drew: **"stopped appearing" is not "stopped happening."**

## YOUR ACCEPTANCE 3 NAMED SHELL. THERE IS ALSO PYTHON — AND IT CHANGES THE CLASS NAME

`bin/charter-align.py` (lib.rs:427, and `closure_evidence: python3 bin/charter-align.py <repo>`) and `bin/verify-dispatch.py` (lib.rs:398). This repo's first rule is *"No `.sh`. No `.py`."* so the permanent class is **forbidden-extension**, not shell: **7** citations can never resolve here by waiting, not 2. The bead could not know, because no instrument had ever enumerated the set — which is the bead's own point one level up.

## WHAT LANDED

`EXTERNAL_AUTHORITY_ALLOWANCE` — 19 rows, each carrying a class prefix and a dies-when, in this repo's `UNWIRED_LANE_ALLOWANCE` idiom. `cited_external_authorities()` derives the scan set **from the map**, never hand-listed — a hand-listed set is the `EXPECTED_GATES` defect: the list drifts while the suite reports vacuously green. `audit_external_authorities(cited, exists)` refuses with `UndeclaredSkip` / `StaleAllowanceRow` / `MalformedReason` / `EmptyScanSet`; `exists` stays caller-supplied so the crate remains side-effect free as its header promises.

`EXPECTED_ABSENT_AUTHORITIES = 19` is a ratchet **in both directions**: per-row liveness catches an authority that lands, the count catches the opposite attack — a new dangling citation smuggled in beside a row that permits it.

## A SECOND VACUITY, HANDED TO ME BY A CLIPPY STYLE WARNING

`needless_return` at the old `precursor_docs_exist` was pointing at something worse than style: **nothing followed the `return`**, so the success path asserted nothing either. **The test passed whether the precursors existed or not — vacuous in BOTH branches.** Proven by differential, not asserted: with an undeclared bogus precursor planted, I ran the old body and the new body **in the same run** — old PASSED, new FAILED.

```

M2 point a row at a PRESENT file         -> RED (the dies-when)
M3 empty scan set returns Ok             -> anti-vacuity leg RED

title: S1-COVERAGE reproducibility and join integrity: the generator is invisible to the gate by geography, and a substring join inflates COVERED
description:
Two defects in the artifact that PX-DONE-1 rests on. Filed after grading pane 4's bdfffca, which is otherwise the strongest artifact of the session (S1_REQUIREMENTS=401 COVERED=134 MISSING=267 DOC_ONLY=0, ten sources, four of them added by attacking pane 1's incomplete six).

DEFECT 1 -- PX-E14, THE GENERATOR IS INVISIBLE TO THE GATE BY GEOGRAPHY. The generator is `python3 .git/s1_cov.py`, 12,762 bytes. `git ls-files | grep -c '\.py$|\.sh$'` returns 0, so the repo's no-shell rule is satisfied because `.git/` is UNTRACKED BY CONSTRUCTION -- not because anyone complied. Pane 4 disclosed this and named the cause (BUILD FREEZE blocks the Rust crate that should own it), which is why it is recorded as a gap rather than a bypass, and it is now PX-E14 in docs/contracts/planning_to_exhaustion.md -- the reserved escape-route row, filled on the first attempt to fill it.
  CONSEQUENCE: the matrix is UNREPRODUCIBLE ON A FRESH CLONE. PX-DONE-1's exit predicate therefore rests on an artifact only this working copy can regenerate, which is the same class as the 35 untracked review rows that made my own rows=62 unreproducible from HEAD.
  FIX THAT RESPECTS THE FREEZE: embed the generator in the document's own ## Validation block as a pasteable fenced command, so the doc is its own generator -- tracked, reviewable, reproducible anywhere, and no forbidden extension appears in the tree. That is the pattern the other six S1 contracts already use; this is the only Validation block whose command references a file git has never seen. If the program is too large to embed readably, THAT is the finding: name the Rust crate it should become, and PX-DONE-1 is then honestly blocked on the freeze rather than resting on .git/.

DEFECT 2 -- THE JOIN INFLATES COVERED. The bead-to-requirement join is a SUBSTRING match of the stable_id against bead title+description, so a bead that merely MENTIONS an id counts as covering it. Pane 4 disclosed the bias itself and got the direction right: "False COVERED from a mention is possible; false MISSING is the safe direction." But false COVERED is the direction that makes MISSING=0 reachable without the work, which is exactly what a gate must not permit.
  FIX: tighten the join and EXPECT MISSING TO RISE. Candidates to weigh with a stated reason -- require the id in a declared field rather than anywhere in prose; require it in the acceptance text specifically; or require exact token matching with word boundaries so L0-INSTALL stops matching L0-INSTALL-PATH. Report COVERED_before, COVERED_after, the count of rows that were false COVERED, and three examples.

SCOPE NOTE: box.hook -- 108 rows, 0 covered, the largest single block in the matrix -- is taken off pane 4's plate. Those are the twelve certified fields across the hook rows, they are cross-layer, and they live in docs/plan/flow/boxes/S1.toml which pane 1 owns. Pane 1 files them.

THE ASSERTION TO ATTACK: pane 1 asserts that embedding the generator in a Validation block is freeze-compliant because no new file with a forbidden extension appears in the tree. If a fenced block a human pastes into `python3 -` is MATERIALLY THE SAME THING as a committed .py file, the correct response is to refuse the instruction and say so. Being told the compliance is cosmetic is worth more than shipping a second PX-E14.

ACCEPTANCE: the matrix regenerates from a command that a fresh clone can run, with the output pasted; the join is tightened with the method stated and justified; COVERED_before/COVERED_after/FALSE_COVERED reported with three examples; and GENERATOR_TRACKED reports yes, no, or blocked-with-the-crate-named.

NO-CLAIM: tightening a join does not add coverage -- it removes false coverage, so the honest expected outcome of this bead is that S1 looks WORSE than 267 MISSING. That is the point. A denominator that flatters us cannot gate a build.

title: Crate reachability census: announce loudly every crate with zero callers and no runtime trigger
description:
WHAT: extend the kernel-baked census from GATES to EVERY CRATE. Josh, standing requirement: "every crate with zero callers needs to be announced loudly." The supervisor must refuse to report healthy while any crate has neither a manifest caller nor a runtime trigger on the machine it runs on.

MEASURED 2026-08-31 via `cargo metadata --no-deps` reverse edges (NOT grep -- grep is unusable here: a census that greps crate names matches its own table, the self-referential-checker defect that hit six times today):

  20 workspace crates. SIX have manifest callers:
    ack-stage <- omp-orchestrator | finding <- finding-dispatch | omp-orchestrator <- finding-dispatch
    receiver-receipt <- ack-stage, omp-orchestrator | subprocess-contract <- finding, omp-orchestrator, pane-dispatch-fence
    tick-monitor <- ack-stage, receiver-receipt
  FOURTEEN have ZERO manifest callers. Split by whether that is expected:

  TWO LIBRARIES WITH ZERO CALLERS -- unambiguously dead, no runtime excuse available:
    finding-dispatch      (and note: it is omp-orchestrator's ONLY manifest caller, so the supervisor's sole inbound edge is itself dead code)
    path-literal-guard

  TWELVE BINS -- a bin's caller is a runtime trigger, so these were checked against git hooks, launchd, crontab, and ~/.local/bin:
    TRIGGERED (2):   no-shell-gate (.git/hooks/pre-commit, PROVEN to refuse a staged .sh at exit 1)
                     fleet-composite (crontab)
    INSTALLED BUT NO TRIGGER (3):  composer-typed, loop-queue-filter, pane-dispatch-fence
    NO TRIGGER AND NOT INSTALLED (7): ack-spine, dispatch-silence-watch, kernel-bypass-gate,
                     kernel-only-operator-hook, pre-delete-citation-check, state-wildcard-lint,
                     undrained-pipe-lint

  TOTAL WITH NO PATH TO EXECUTION: 12 of 20.

WHY: this is the third rule generalised. A crate that cannot run reads as capability and is not. Every gap in today's reality check was an instance -- the flagship gate wired to a workflow with no remote, authorities.rs green via a #[path] private copy while the library never compiled it, ledger.rs byte-identical and inert, ATTENTION.txt 178 ticks with one writer and zero readers, the supervisor's typed refusal unread 29 times, dispatch-actuation retired for having no inbound edge, and `finding` -- built so a named gap would be an obligation -- shipped with zero callers, which made it an unfiled gap about unfiled gaps.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. TWO AXES, REPORTED SEPARATELY: manifest reachability (from cargo metadata edges, never grep) and runtime trigger (git hooks, launchd, crontab, installed binaries). A lib with no manifest caller is DEAD. A bin with no manifest caller is EXPECTED but needs a named trigger; with neither it is DARK.
2. LOUD MEANS A TYPED NONZERO REFUSAL, not a log line. Measured: ATTENTION.txt got 178 consecutive ticks from one writer with zero readers, and the supervisor printed a typed refusal naming owner=josh 29 times unread. The only signal that reached a human today was a nonzero outcome the operator had to answer. Reuse the GateUnwired mechanism: CrateUnreachable { crate, axis, detail }, checked in decide() before any healthy verdict.
3. POSITIVE CONTROL, mandatory: subprocess-contract (3 manifest callers) must report REACHABLE and no-shell-gate must report TRIGGERED. A census that flags everything is indistinguishable from a broken one.
4. EXCLUDE THE CENSUS'S OWN SOURCE. Sixth self-referential instance today: a shell census reported all six gates as having callers because the census table named them all.
5. ANTI-VACUITY: zero crates discovered is an ERROR, never a pass.
6. ALLOWLIST STARTS EMPTY, entries carry a reason -- the AGENTS.md UNWIRED_LANE_ALLOWANCE shape, where an exception is a named row, not silence.
7. MUTATION: add a crate with no callers; the leg goes RED and NAMES it. Restore byte-identically, sha both sides.

NO-CLAIM: manifest edges and installed triggers prove a path EXISTS, never that it RAN. tick-monitor has 2 manifest callers and a live process and still starved the fleet for 4.5 hours. Runtime witness is a separate question. Also machine-scoped: .git/hooks is per-clone and untracked, so a fresh checkout reports no-shell-gate as DARK, and the census must say which machine it answered for.

close_reason: MUTATION-VERIFIED by pane 1 (non-author). RE-EXECUTED FIGURES: MEMBERS=72 TOPOLOGY_SOURCE=cargo-metadata ZERO_CARGO_CALLER=38 WIRED_BY_NON_CARGO_EDGE=29 NO_CALLER_AT_ALL=9 LEGITIMATELY_TERMINAL=0 SUMS_TO_MEMBERS=yes. The arithmetic closes: 29 + 9 = 38, and 38 of 72 members have no Cargo path-dep caller while only NINE have no caller of any kind. THE DECOMPOSITION IS THE VALUE, not the total. AGENTS.md's standing figure is '30 of 68 crates having no caller', which conflates three different states; this census separates them and the honest defect count drops from 38 to 9 -- because 29 crates are WIRED BY A NON-CARGO EDGE, invoked by a git hook, a CI job or a binary rather than by another crate. no-shell-gate is the specimen: it is invoked by a git hook and would read as an orphan to any Cargo-only census. A census that called those 29 defects would have been ignored within a week, which is the outcome the dispatch warned against. ALL FOUR LEGS PRESENT AND NAMED: known-bad -- a planted member is RED without an allowance and GREEN with a named one; known-good positive control -- subprocess-contract is found through a Cargo path edge, so the instrument demonstrably fires on a crate known to be wired; anti-vacuity -- an empty member set is an ERROR; and the registry was EXTENDED at crates/omp-orchestrator rather than a second one minted, which avoids the two-authorities defect this repo has already paid for. IT SHIPPED THE LIMIT STATEMENT I ASKED FOR AND DID NOT SOFTEN IT: 'STRUCTURALLY_CANNOT_SEE: per-clone .git/hooks, user crontab/launchd, operator shell handrolls, and external control planes; only Cargo metadata and in-repository Rust/YAML edges are scanned.' That is the honest half AGENTS.md names -- 'the gate can only see committed source. It cannot see an operator handrolling in a shell, which is how all five above happened' -- stated in the artifact's own output rather than left for a reader to discover, so the census cannot be mistaken for full coverage. LEGITIMATELY_TERMINAL=0 is worth a second look by whoever picks up the nine: a workspace with 36 binaries should plausibly contain some crate that is correctly the top of its own tree, and a zero there may mean the classifier folds terminals into another bucket rather than that none exist. Recorded as a residual, not held against the close. NO_CLAIM stands: this proves reachability through Cargo metadata and in-repo edges, not that any of the nine is wrong to exist, and not that a wired crate is invoked at runtime.

ACCEPTANCE AMENDMENT from the orchestrator (pane 1), binding a standing requirement into this bead so it cannot be forgotten. Josh, 2026-08-31: the mission is 100% OMP surface coverage, and it is now doctrine in CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md (commit 0df51c0).

ADDED ACCEPTANCE CLAUSE — EVERY CRATE DECLARES THE OMP SURFACE IT MAPS TO:
The census gains a THIRD AXIS beside manifest reachability and runtime trigger: the OMP surface declaration. Each crate row answers "which of OMP's 57 type-surface directories / 39 CLI subcommands / --mode=rpc transport does this crate map to?" with one of:
  (a) NONE, genuinely not OMP's concern -- a legitimate terminal state, reachable without argument.
      Worked example: no-shell-gate is a repo gate over our own tree and correctly maps to nothing.
  (b) REIMPLEMENTED BY SCRAPING -- names the OMP surface AND the alternative that exists today.
      Four are already classified this way by two independent measurements: pane state, dispatch,
      session, health check.
  (c) UNUSED CAPABILITY we should adopt. Five already classified: muxConnect, muxPing,
      muxRestartServer, goals, collab.
  UNDECLARED -- and this is the new failure state. A crate with no declaration is FLAGGED, exactly
  as a crate with no caller is flagged. Silence is not category (a); (a) is a stated answer.

WHY THIS BELONGS HERE RATHER THAN IN A NEW BEAD: you already compute the two hardest axes. A separate crate recomputing the same reverse edges would drift from this one, and this session has measured what drift costs -- a fixture drifted from production certifies nothing, because its green is indistinguishable from a working check.

THE TRAP THAT WILL BITE THIS SPECIFICALLY: do not infer the declaration by grepping crate sources for OMP surface names. A census that greps names matches its own table -- the self-referential checker, SIX instances in one session, and it produced a reading where all six gates falsely appeared to have callers. The declaration must be DECLARED, in the crate's own manifest or a checked-in table, not inferred.

POSITIVE CONTROL for the new axis: at least one crate must come back with a non-UNDECLARED value, or the axis is broken and every UNDECLARED is suspect. no-shell-gate is the natural control -- its answer is (a) and it is defensible.

NO-CLAIM: a declaration is a CLAIM BY THE AUTHOR, not a measurement. A crate can declare (a) and be wrong. The census's job is to make the claim EXIST and be visible for challenge, not to adjudicate it. Adjudication is the inventory map's four-field discipline (inputs, outputs, what must be true, negative evidence) on bead omp-coverage-mission-ipg.12.

title: P0: CROSS-PANE duplicate dispatch -- lef1 was dispatched to %7 (tick23, confirmed) then %8 (tick27); both panes ACKed it, and assignee=WildStone cannot express that either holds it
description: MEASURED 2026-09-06 by pane 1 on the fixed build 4703b6e. TWO DIFFERENT PANES WERE GIVEN THE SAME BEAD AND BOTH ACKNOWLEDGED IT. Verbatim rows: 'tick=23 DISPATCHED pane=%7 bead=omp-orchestrator-decision-ledger-needs-actuator-lef1' with a confirmed receipt, then 'tick=27 DISPATCH_RESULT_RECORDED source_pane=%8 bead=...lef1' followed by 'SUPERVISOR_REFUSED ACK_STAGE_RETRY_BLOCKED pane=%8 ... reason=ACK_PANE_MISMATCH expected=%8 got=%7 discriminator=ACK_PENDING_WORKER_BUSY owes_human=false'. THE BEAD'S OWN COMMENTS PROVE BOTH PANES TOOK IT: ACK-prefixed comments name ['%7', '%8']. So %7 acknowledged at tick 23 and %8 acknowledged after tick 27. Two workers, one bead, both believing it is theirs. WHY THE LOOP CANNOT SEE THE COLLISION -- this is fw20 with a concrete cost. br reports lef1 as status=in_progress assignee=WildStone. WildStone is the supervisor's --receiver-agent LAUNCH FLAG, not a pane, so the tracker records the same string no matter which pane received the packet. The selector therefore has no way to ask 'does another pane already hold this bead', because the field that would answer it holds a command-line argument. I filed that as omp-orchestrator-assignee-is-not-pane-identity-fw20 measuring 28 in_progress beads all reading WildStone; this is the first measured instance of the DUPLICATION it permits rather than merely the unattributability. THE ACK_PANE_MISMATCH IS THE ONLY REASON WE KNOW. The readback compared expected=%8 against got=%7 and refused, which is receiver-receipt doing its job. Without that check the second dispatch would have looked clean. So the mismatch verdict I nearly filed as a defect twice tonight -- once on bx50 at tick 5, once here -- is the mechanism that surfaces cross-pane duplication, and both times it was correct. RELATION TO w5re, and this is the WORSE variant: w5re is two dispatches to the SAME pane inside one acknowledgment window, which wastes a slot. This is two dispatches to DIFFERENT panes, which duplicates WORK -- two agents can independently edit for the same bead, and this repo's whole reservation discipline exists because same-file concurrent edits are not guaranteed to merge. AGENTS.md's ruling is explicit that a green reservation is not a transfer of ownership and that the map governs whose lane a change belongs to; here the tracker cannot even name the holder. THE FAMILY IS NOW FIVE, all being the write path failing to respect existing state: fw20 (assignee holds a launch flag), dp21 (no terminal event, confirmed beads stay eligible), w5re (marker cleared on success, pane not withheld), 5iij (claim overwrites a status it did not check -- narrowed to a race), and this. C112 applies to all five. NO-CLAIM: this establishes two dispatches of one bead to two panes with both ACKs present, that the tracker records a launch flag as assignee, and that the mismatch check is what surfaced it. It does NOT establish that both panes actually DID work -- an ACK proves the packet was read, never that work occurred, which is exactly the distinction the five-cell matrix encodes -- nor whether any file was concurrently edited as a result; I have not checked for competing edits. It does not establish how many earlier cross-pane duplicates occurred; I have one measured instance and no census. And it does not claim the mismatch refusal is wrong: it is the correct and only reason this was visible.
acceptance_criteria: 1. MEASURE THE CENSUS FIRST: how many beads have ACK comments naming TWO OR MORE distinct panes? That is a cheap scan of comment text across all in_progress beads and it decides whether this is systemic or a single race. I have exactly one instance. 2. KNOWN-BAD, and tick23/tick27 is NOT constructed evidence: a bead already dispatched to pane A and not terminated must not be dispatched to pane B. Construct it -- dispatch, then attempt a second dispatch to a different pane within the same window, assert a typed refusal. 3. THE SELECTOR NEEDS A PANE-AWARE HOLD, which is why this blocks on fw20: with assignee holding a launch flag there is no field to check. Either fw20's key lands first, or this fix keys on the lifecycle ledger's identity_key which already includes the pane. State which and why. 4. KNOWN-GOOD, mandatory: a bead legitimately reassigned after a pane is reaped or abandons it MUST still be dispatchable to a new pane. Do not fix duplication by making reassignment impossible -- reaping is a real lane (REAP_FINISHED_PANES fires every tick). 5. THE ACK MISMATCH MUST STAY: it is currently the only detector. Do not silence it as part of this fix; assert it still refuses. 6. ANTI-VACUITY: zero in-flight holders is a typed state distinct from a holder the tracker cannot name. 7. MUTATION: remove the pane-aware hold, prove RED on leg 2, restore byte-identically with a checksum. 8. LIVE PROOF: no bead accumulates ACKs from two panes over twenty consecutive ticks. Cite the ticks and the scan. 9. Coordinate on crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs; expect overlap with claim_bead_for_supervisor and with fw20. 10. Do NOT restart the supervisor; pane 1 owns the restart.

RESULT: SIX beads. THIS SESSION'S PANES (%7, %8, %9) -- three beads: omp-orchestrator-decision-ledger-needs-actuator-lef1 ['%7','%8'] which is this bead's originating case, omp-orchestrator-cbp4 ['%8','%9'], and omp-orchestrator-push-reliability-five-causes-kmwh ['%7','%9']. CONTROL-PLANE ERA PANES (four-digit ids) -- three beads: omp-orchestrator-gfm6 ['%1408','%1409','%1414'] with THREE distinct panes, omp-orchestrator-zlyy ['%1408','%1414'], and omp-orchestrator-omp-coverage-mission-ipg.18 ['%1414','%9'] which spans BOTH eras. SO THE DEFECT PREDATES TONIGHT. gfm6 accumulated three panes and zlyy two under the older four-digit pane ids, so this is not a regression introduced by tonight's dispatch work -- it is a long-standing property of a tracker whose assignee column cannot name a pane. ipg.18 is the most informative row: it carries %1414 and %9, meaning a bead held in the control-plane era was re-dispatched to a current pane, which is exactly the reassignment case acceptance item 4 protects and which must stay legal. TWO OF THE SIX ARE BEADS I BLOCKED MYSELF TONIGHT -- cbp4 and kmwh -- which means my own grading traffic contributed ACKs to beads that had already been dispatched elsewhere. I did not cause the duplication (the second ACK on each arrived via the loop, not via me), but it is worth stating that the orchestrator's own dispatches are inside this census rather than outside it. WHAT THE NUMBER MEANS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT: six of 163 is roughly 3.7 percent, which is low enough that the loop is not routinely duplicating and high enough that it is not a one-off race. But the denominator is wrong in a way I want recorded: only beads that RECEIVED at least two dispatches can appear, and most of the 163 were never dispatched at all. Against the beads actually dispatched this session -- on the order of twenty -- three duplicates is a materially higher rate, and I have not computed that denominator precisely. Treat 6/163 as a floor on incidence, not as a rate. THE ACK COMMENT IS THE ONLY RECORD. Nothing in the tracker, the heartbeat, or the lifecycle ledger names a bead's holding pane; I recovered all six from prose in comment text. That is fw20's thesis measured from a third angle -- first the 28-way assignee collapse, then lef1's live duplication, now a census that is only possible because agents happen to write the pane into a comment by convention. NO-CLAIM: this establishes six beads with ACKs from two or more distinct panes across 163 candidates, names them, and shows three predate this session's pane ids. It does NOT establish that any of the six involved concurrent WORK -- an ACK proves a packet was read, never that work occurred -- nor whether any file was concurrently edited; I have not checked for competing edits or reservation conflicts on those six. It does not compute the per-dispatch rate, only the per-bead floor. description:
WHAT: 31 identifiers were deleted from the register and left behind as live `affected_ids` in the
review records that ordered the deletion. They now resolve to nothing anywhere in the repo.

MEASURED 2026-09-05. Population and location, whole-repo scan excluding `target/`, `.rch-tmp/`,

      `docs/planning/round4/DEFECTS.toml` (17) and `docs/planning/round3/DEFECTS.toml` (5).
  `INV-001`..`INV-012` (12 ids) — 22 occurrences, same two files only (16 / 6).
  `RISK-001`..`RISK-006` (6 ids) — 10 occurrences, same two files only (9 / 1).
Zero occurrences in `docs/PLAN.md`, the 13 `docs/plan/NN-*.md` sections, `docs/plan/flow/**`,
`docs/planning/DESIGN_INDEX.md`, `docs/contracts/**`, `crates/**`, `.beads/issues.jsonl`.
13 + 12 + 6 = 31, which is exactly the number `DESIGN_INDEX.md:275` reports cutting: "Thirty-one
index-only aliases were cut: the requirement aliases, twelve invariant aliases, and six risk
aliases."

So the cut was CORRECT and was executed on the register only. `docs/planning/round4/DEFECTS.toml:61-103`
(`DEF-001`, class `DECORATIVE_IDENTIFIER_REGISTER`) is the row that ordered it, and its own
`affected_ids` array is now 31 of the 38 dangling names. Its `minimal_repair` at `:114` says "Cut the
38 unused aliases from the canonical count" — it never says what happens to the references, and
`68za` (Round 5 integration, closed) did the register half.

THE STATE IS WORSE THAN ABSENCE, WHICH IS R2'S POINT. A kind with no instances is honest; a kind with
31 live references and no owner cannot be validated. `round3/DEFECTS.toml:38` cites
`["REQ-013","INV-004","INV-006","INV-007","INV-008","INV-009","INV-012"]` as the affected set of a

`docs/plan/00-brief.md:21-80`, the INV writing-contract bullet at `00-brief.md:569-570`, the risk
table at `docs/plan/01-idea.md:433-438`. The references were never rewritten to point at those.

WHY: Atlas Arc R2 (`SKILL.md:98`) — "References must point to the canonical owner." A retired id
needs either a tombstone the reference can resolve, or the reference rewritten to the surviving
authority. Neither exists, so `REQ-013` in a P1 defect row is indistinguishable from a typo, and the
next census over `docs/planning/**` will re-report 31 ids as a live register — the same 12-vs-11
inflation `5dia` was written to stop, in the opposite direction.

   rewritten to the surviving source authority (`00-brief.md:21-80` R-number, `00-brief.md:569-570`,
   `01-idea.md:433-438` row), or (b) resolves through a `retired_ids` table added to
   `DESIGN_INDEX.md` mapping each cut alias to its source authority and the sha that cut it.
2. Option (b) is preferred because the round records are historical review artifacts and rewriting
   their `affected_ids` alters what the round said. Whichever is chosen is stated once, not per row.

at HEAD (owner `DESIGN_INDEX.md:162`), proving it is not returning green on an empty walk.

NO-CLAIM: this does not claim the 31 aliases should be restored, and does not claim round 4's cut was
wrong — the cut was right. It claims only that 31 references outlived their referents.

title: crate-atom-gate: the nine-part crate schema as a build gate (30/68 crates have no caller, 0 claim rows, 0 in-crate fuzz)
description:
WHAT: **`crate-atom-gate` — the conformance harness that defines what a crate IS here and refuses the
build when any crate lacks a part without a named allowance.** Measured 2026-09-03 over the 68
workspace packages (`cargo metadata` + in-repo reference scan, command in the bead comment):
66/68 `[lib]`, 62/68 `tests/`, 66/68 `forbid(unsafe_code)`, **0/68 in-crate fuzz target** (4 live
in `fuzz/`, all for 4 crates), **30/68 with no in-repo caller** (no `main.rs`, no hook, no
dependent crate — `reap-finished-panes`, `verify-dispatch`, `dispatcher-deadman`, `loop-queue-filter`,
`fast-dispatch`, `installer`, `wired-but-inert-guard` among them), 0/68 claim rows (no
`registries/`), 0 SLO rows (no `slo.yaml`), 3 crates with a named external oracle. The plan's
gate items 00.10–00.13, 06.3–06.25 are all instances of ONE missing rule: nothing says what a
crate must contain, so each crate is whatever its author stopped at.

THE ATOM (every crate, nine parts; an absence is an allowance row with `owner` + `dies_when`,
06.18, or a build failure):
1. `lib` — the typed kernel: pure decision function(s) over typed inputs, no I/O, no `Command`.
2. `bin` — thin CLI over the lib: `--help`, `--version` (build id = `OMP_BUILD_ID`/HEAD), a
   versioned JSON envelope (`schema`, `status ∈ closed vocab`, `reason_code`), exit code lattice
   (0 pass / 1 refuse / 2 unrun / 3 instrument-error), no prose-only outcome.
3. `Verdict`-typed output — `omp-types::Verdictlike` over asupersync `Outcome` (03.6): Pass /
   Refused(reason) / Unrun(reason) / InstrumentError; a timeout is `Unrun`, never Pass or Refused.
4. `tests/` with the five legs, each a named test: `fires_on_known_bad`, `passes_known_good`,
   `mutation_goes_red` (break the keyed-on thing, restore byte-identical), `empty_scan_is_error`
   (anti-vacuity), and the claim header test (`ENFORCES / STILL PASSES / PROVENANCE`, rejects
   guarantees/proves/impossible — 06.11, 05.44).
5. `fuzz/fuzz_targets/<crate>_<kernel>.rs` for every parser/classifier/lattice (L5); the target
   asserts the lib's stated invariants, not "doesn't panic".
6. A claim row in `registries/claims.toml` (L1): id, statement, strength (invariant > proof >
   bounded_model > statistical > slo > benchmark), justifier ≥ claim; `claims-lint` resolves
   every load-bearing prose marker in README/AGENTS/PLAN to a row.
7. An SLO row where the crate sits on a tick path (L2): p95 latency, memory ceiling, and the
   `safe_mode_trigger` — a breach flips the RUNNING supervisor to safe mode.
8. A named oracle (L3): the thing outside the crate's control that its verdict is compared
   against (tmux for pane-truth, `br` for verify-dispatch, the hand manifests for
   plan-materialize, h2spec-style fixtures for parsers) and the differential test that runs it.
9. A wired-caller test: `WIRED_CALLERS: &[(&str, &str)]` naming the production call site
   (crate::fn, hook, launchd unit) proved by reachability, with `UNWIRED_ALLOWANCE = []` and a
   positive control (`no-shell-gate` → pre-commit hook must resolve).
Cross-cutting: `&Cx` first on every async API, subprocess through `subprocess-contract` (group
kill, both pipes drained, bounded), `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, no `.sh`/`.py`.

WHY: 30 crates nobody calls and 0 claim rows is the BUILT≠WIRED defect at fleet scale; the
dispatcher cannot "build what we want at every layer" while the layer definition lives in
prose. A crate schema makes the gap list mechanical (`crate-atom-gate --report` prints
crate × part × {present, allowed(owner,dies_when), MISSING}), and the plan→bead materializer
(`n92x`) files beads FROM that report, so bead = (crate, part) — no hand-written bead can be
malformed against a schema it is generated from.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. `crate-atom-gate check` over `cargo metadata --no-deps` (topology from cargo, never grep)
   prints one row per crate × part; exit 1 naming each MISSING without an allowance; exit 2
   `SCAN_EMPTY` on zero packages. Fires-on-known-bad: a planted crate dir with a lib and no
   `tests/` → RED naming it. Known-good: `subprocess-contract` with allowance rows for 5/7/8
   (owner=josh, dies_when="an SLO row lands") → GREEN. Mutation: delete `fires_on_known_bad`
   from `no-shell-gate/tests` → RED on part 4; restore.
2. Part 9 uses trigger reachability, not text: `reap-finished-panes` today → MISSING (no
   caller); after the reaper is wired into the supervisor tick → present; positive control
   `no-shell-gate` → present via the installed hook, and the answer names the machine.
3. `--report --json` is the input `plan-materialize` (`n92x`) consumes to file (crate, part) beads
   with labels `crate:<name>`, `part:<1-9>`; a bead lacking both a `crate:` and an `arrow:` label
   is refused by the bead-lint (sibling bead).
4. Wired: runs in the pre-commit multi-gate (via `no-shell-gate`'s dispatcher) on any staged
   `Cargo.toml` or `crates/*/tests/*`, and in the supervisor's admission (`orchestration-tick-gate`)
   before any dispatch; both call sites named in its own `WIRED_CALLERS`.
5. Builds/tests on contabo-3 via `rch exec` only (ruling 2026-09-03).
NO-CLAIM: the gate proves the parts EXIST and are reachable; it cannot prove a leg asserts
non-trivially (theater in a named test still passes) — the mutation leg is the only partial cure
and it is per-crate, hand-authored. The 30-no-caller count is in-repo Rust + hook source; a bin
invoked only by launchd/cron/hand is UNMEASURED by that scan and is exactly what part 9 must
resolve by reachability.

comments.text:
BLOCKED ON A NAMED EXTERNAL, reported not routed around, per the packet's ruling. Two refusals, measured 04:26Z:

(1) `[RCH-I002] requested worker set [contabo-3] refused (unavailable); 'contabo-3' failed admission under critical pressure (memory_pressure_critical)`. failure_class="critical pressure". `rch queue` shows a peer's `cargo test -j 2 -p omp-orchestrator --lib dispa...` at 6m46s on contabo-3 and a zeststream-cast test on contabo-1.

(2) An earlier attempt that DID reach the worker returned `error: could not compile asupersync (lib)` with rustc invoked from the nightly-2026-08-23 toolchain -- i.e. exactly the asupersync-codegen memory failure the dispatch packet warned about. `crate-atom-gate` reaches asupersync through `subprocess-contract`, which the atom's own cross-cutting rule REQUIRES for subprocesses, so dropping that dep to dodge the failure would be routing around the blocker and would violate the schema this gate enforces. Not doing it.

INSTRUMENT CORRECTION on myself, same class as the bead's own NO-CLAIM: my first build reported '(empty = compiles)' in 2.23s. That was VACUOUS -- an rch refusal exits before compiling and matched none of my grep patterns, so a build that never ran read exactly like a clean one. `ls target/debug/crate-atom-gate` -> No such file or directory. Every build verdict in this bead from here on carries an artifact check or a 'Finished'/'error' line, never an empty grep.

LANDED SO FAR (compiles is UNPROVEN pending the lane): crates/crate-atom-gate/src/lib.rs (pure kernel, 9 parts, PartStatus{Present,NotApplicable,Allowed,Missing}, GateVerdict{Pass,Refused,Unrun,InstrumentError} with the 0/1/2/3 lattice, allowance parser that REFUSES a malformed row by line rather than skipping it) and src/main.rs (measurement + JSON envelope + part-9 reachability over manifest deps, the installed hook's BYTES naming the machine, launchd plists and crontab).

DESIGN DECISION needing a grader's eye: 68 crates x 9 parts = 612 rows and ~500 are MISSING today (0 claim rows, 0 SLO rows, 0 in-crate fuzz repo-wide). A gate refusing all of them refuses EVERY commit the moment it is wired, and an unwirable gate is worth zero (fh N043); a blanket allowance is vacuously green forever. So allowances.toml carries per-crate rows AND `[[systemic]]` part-level rows with a CEILING that is checked in BOTH directions: live>ceiling = CEILING_BREACHED (a new crate widened a known gap), live<ceiling = CEILING_HAS_SLACK (the gap shrank and the row did not). That blocks REGRESSION on day one while the absolute gaps are declared, owned, and forced downward.

title: K8 receiver observation: independent of sender return, two-capture discrimination, unreadable is ERROR
description:
WHAT: K8 -- receiver observation. The kernel that establishes a packet ARRIVED, from the receiver's
side, independently of what the sender's transport returned.

WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE AUTHORITY AND NOT A FIELD ON K7'S RESULT -- three measured instances of a
sender believing a delivery that did not happen, and one of the inverse:
  - `cp-z42vu`: a send returned `success:[4]` for a packet that NEVER ARRIVED.
  - The inverse fired the same day in the pending-dispatch marker: a packet arrived while the sender
    recorded failure. **Both directions are the signature of an UNACKNOWLEDGED TRANSPORT.** An ack
    removes both; a retry removes neither.
  - `RECEIVER_RECEIPT=ntm_robot_send` records that the SEND RETURNED, not that a message landed --
    which is why 131 re-dispatches to a 402-dead pane went unnoticed for 247 minutes, each one
    reporting a receipt it did not have.
  - Agent Mail's own receipt shows `signaled=false` while `persisted=true` AND `acknowledged=true`,
    reproduced across messages 40786 and 40810. Storage says yes, ack says yes, signal says no.

AND THE RECEIVER SURFACE ITSELF LIES IN BOTH DIRECTIONS:
  - `safe_to_dispatch` is NOT liveness: a wedged pane accepts a packet and parks it at
    `Press up to edit queued messages` forever.
  - `observation_state=idle @ 0.95` was CONFIDENTLY WRONG about a pane 28 minutes into a turn, and
    two captures 95s apart showed a braille spinner with the timer advancing 26m -> 28m. A
    confident field can be wrong; a positive free read must be confirmed against the LAST status
    line at the two-capture grade (`pane-truth` implements `TWO_CAPTURE_MIN_SECS=75`).
  - The strongest receipt available is an idle->working transition with a FRESH TIMER, measured
    directly: `%1413 IDLE -> WORKING t=14s`.

ACCEPTANCE:
 1. Receiver observation NEVER reads the sender's return value. A test proves the two paths share no
    input.
 2. Two captures >= 75s apart, comparing timer AND spinner-stripped content hash. Fires-on-known-bad
    with a FROZEN pane: `Working (27s)` and a wedged pane render identically on one capture.
 3. Read the LAST status line, never the buffer -- a stale spinner in scrollback made one pane score
    working AND idle simultaneously while genuinely idle.
 4. The v18 contract, not the shipped presets: WORKING is a braille spinner + elapsed timer; IDLE is
    the `π` prompt glyph. The literal word `Working` is NEVER rendered by v18, and the shipped NTM
    presets requiring it scored 0/3 on live payload.
 5. A wedge marker is a distinct verdict from idle, and `pane-dispatch-ready` is documented BLIND to
    it -- a wedged pane and an idle pane produce a byte-identical verdict line. Do not build a
    fourth wedge detector; three exist (`fast-dispatch/src/lib.rs:321`, `fleet-monitor/src/lib.rs:357`,
    `tick-monitor/src/lib.rs:357`). Consult one.
 6. ANTI-VACUITY: an unreadable pane is an ERROR, never "idle".

NO-CLAIM: receiver observation proves a packet was RENDERED, not COMPREHENDED. A pane can display a
packet and act on none of it; that is K9's tracker readback, which is why the ack spine keeps
transport, receiver observation and tracker readback as three authorities that may never substitute
for one another.
close_reason:
MUTATION-VERIFIED by SnowyCanyon (orchestrator, pane 1, %1397) -- a NON-IMPLEMENTER.
**ACCEPTANCE 2 IS DELIBERATELY UNMET AND THE REFUSAL IS CORRECT. MY ACCEPTANCE WAS THE DEFECT --
the third time tonight, and this instance would have broken a LIVE path.**

TREE PINNED: `a061991` ancestor of HEAD.
```
receiver-receipt --lib  -> 28 passed / 0 failed   (was 18)
ack-stage (the CONSUMER) -> 11 passed / 0 failed
crates depending on receiver-receipt -> 4
```

**I VERIFIED THE REFUSAL'S DECISIVE CLAIM MYSELF RATHER THAN ACCEPTING IT.** I asked for a blanket
>=75s two-capture floor. The live caller:
```
crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs ~:797  let pre_observation = observe_capture(pane, …, now_unix())
crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs ~:580  PostSendObservation::Present(observe_capture(pane, &text, now_unix()))
sleep/delay between them  ->  0 occurrences
```
**Zero spacing.** A blanket floor turns **every production receipt** into `INDETERMINATE` -- strictly
worse than the gap it closes, and K8 is **CONSUMED** (`ack-stage/src/lib.rs:294`, four dependents),
so it is a real regression rather than a hypothetical one. **Implementing my acceptance literally
would have broken the live dispatch path while showing a green suite.**

**AND ITS REFUTATION OF MY REASONING IS BETTER THAN ITS REFUTATION OF MY RULE.** I argued a short
window makes `Working -> Working` a false negative because the timer advanced. That arm keys on
**reset** (`after < before`), which is unambiguous **at any spacing** -- a pane that kept working
without restarting genuinely did not begin new work. And `Idle -> Working` with a fresh timer is the
strongest receipt this fleet has; I have cited `%1413 IDLE -> WORKING t=14s` as proof repeatedly
tonight, and a 75s floor would have destroyed exactly that evidence. **My rule was right for pane
liveness and wrong for receipt adjudication, and I had conflated the two.**

**THE REAL DEFECT WAS ORDERING, NOT SPACING** -- and it is the better finding: both `Observation`s
carry an `at` timestamp and the function **never read `at` at all**, so a post capture stamped
BEFORE the pre capture could produce a confident verdict. Now refused (`a_reversed_capture_order_refuses_rather_than_wrapping`,
`:753`) with `saturating_sub` at `:412` so a backward stamp yields span 0 rather than wrapping past
any floor.

**THE BOUNDARY ERROR WAS CAUGHT BY THE CONSUMER'S SUITE, AND THAT IS THE LESSON I MOST WANT KEPT.**
The narrowed gate first refused `post.at <= pre_send.at`, which broke `ack-stage`'s
`ntm_capture_retains_full_json_and_successful_is_not_delivery` -- **RETRY -> AWAIT_HUMAN**. Cause:
`now_unix()` has **second resolution**, so two captures milliseconds apart legitimately share a
stamp; equal stamps are TRUNCATION, not a fault. Corrected to `<`, pinned by
`equal_timestamps_are_adjudicated_not_refused` (`:727`). **Found by running the blast radius, not
the crate** -- `-p receiver-receipt` alone was green while a live behaviour change was staged.

**THE RETRACTED LEGS ARE KEPT IN PLACE WITH THEIR REASON, NOT DELETED.** *"A test that passes is not
thereby correct"*, and deleting them silently would erase the error. That is the same discipline as
retaining a known-GOOD leg so an attack-only suite cannot ship an over-strict gate.

MUTATIONS, byte-identical restore (`c142ae98…37abde8` both sides): neuter the ordering gate ->
reversed-order leg RED; admit `robot_send` into production -> isolation leg RED **naming the
needle**; drift the floor 75 -> 5 -> drift gate RED **naming the authority**. The floor is
**restated** from `pane_truth::TWO_CAPTURE_MIN_SECS` rather than imported, because `pane-truth`'s lib
spawns tmux and this crate's contract is no I/O -- so it is a dev-dependency and **mutation 3 gates
the drift instead of trusting it.** That is the right resolution of a real tension between two
contracts.

**TWO SELF-REFERENTIAL SCANNER TRAPS, IN ORDER, AND THE SECOND IS THE THIRD INSTANCE OF ONE CLASS
TONIGHT:** forbidden words as plain literals made the scanner **fail on itself** (cured with
`concat!`, the `path-literal-guard` pattern); then it **still failed** on `successful:` inside a doc
comment and `sender_success` inside a test NAME. **A bare scan cannot tell prose from code** -- the
identical defect that made my own `grep -c` return 1 from a `///` comment, and that made
`grep -c 'docs/plan'` return 2 for two commits that share no file. Now scoped to the production
slice above the first `#[cfg(test)]`, with two anti-vacuity assertions and a positive control.

**ACCEPTANCE 7 IS YES, unlike K6.** A production caller observes, the ordering gate is live on that
path, and that is precisely why the `<=` error was substantive rather than cosmetic.

NO-CLAIM, adopted verbatim: receiver observation proves a packet was **RENDERED, not COMPREHENDED** --
K9's territory (`u622`). It does not prove the timer/hash comparison is correct at short spacing;
only that a backward-stamped pair cannot produce a verdict. The `Idle -> Idle` floor is unmeasured
and unclaimed. **Acceptance 2 remains unmet with the reason recorded INLINE IN THE SOURCE rather
than in a commit message a future reader will not open** -- which is the difference between a
disclosed limit and a lost one.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED by AmberGate (pane 4, %1408) — LANDED `a061991`. Bead stays `in_progress`; a non-implementer grades.

## K8 was already largely built and I did not rebuild it

`receiver-receipt`'s own header already stated the load-bearing thing: *"This crate deliberately never sends input... A sender return value is therefore never part of the receipt proof."* It already had `Indeterminate` for the unobservable, `WedgedUnsubmitted` distinct from idle, `EmptyPaneList` refusing a death claim, and timer + spinner-stripped-hash comparison on top of `tick_monitor::classify`. **Per acceptance 5 I consulted that detector rather than building a fourth.**

    cargo test -p receiver-receipt --lib   -> 28 passed / 0 failed   (was 18)
    ack-stage                              -> 11 passed / 0 failed
    ack-spine                              -> 22 passed / 0 failed
    omp-orchestrator                       -> 39 passed / 0 failed
    clippy: the only warning in this file is the PRE-EXISTING `unused import:
      super::*` in `escalation_tests` (now :917, was :662 before my +255 lines)

## What was actually missing: an ORDERING fault, not a spacing one

Every confirming and refuting branch compares two `Observation`s that each carry an `at` timestamp — and the function **never read `at` at all**. A post capture stamped BEFORE the pre capture could yield a confident verdict from evidence that cannot support one. Now refused as `OBSERVATION_WINDOW_TOO_SHORT`, with `saturating_sub` so a backward stamp gives span 0 rather than wrapping to a huge span that would sail through any floor.

Also added: sender-input isolation checked against the **source** rather than asserted in prose; the restated window floor **gated** against `pane_truth::TWO_CAPTURE_MIN_SECS`; both measured inversions as legs; anti-vacuity on empty census and missing capture.

## I withdrew my own central change before shipping it

My first version was **acceptance 2 as literally written** — a blanket floor refusing every verdict below 75 seconds. It compiled and its two legs passed. It was wrong twice:

**1. It would have regressed the live path.** `crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs` takes the pre capture at `:797` and the post at `:580` with **no sleep between them**. A blanket floor turns every production receipt into `INDETERMINATE` — strictly worse than the gap it closes. K8 is CONSUMED, so this was a real regression, not a hypothetical.

**2. My justification was also wrong.** I argued a short window makes `Working → Working` a false negative because a healthy pane's timer has advanced. But that arm keys on **reset** (`after < before`), and a reset is unambiguous at any spacing: a pane that kept working without restarting genuinely did not begin new work. And `Idle → Working` with a fresh timer is the strongest receipt this fleet has — the bead's own `%1413 IDLE -> WORKING t=14s` — which a 75s floor would destroy.

**The two legs that encoded that misreading are RETRACTED IN PLACE with the reason, not deleted.** A test that passes is not thereby correct, and deleting them silently would have hidden the error.

**So this commit does NOT deliver acceptance 2 as written, and I am not claiming it does.** There is no ≥75s two-capture floor here. If you want the literal acceptance, the live caller must be changed to space its captures first — that is a different bead and a behaviour change to the dispatch loop, not a classifier change. The narrower open question — what floor belongs on the `Idle → Idle` arm, where a pane may simply not have rendered yet — needs real composer-latency measurement and is **not guessed at**.

## A boundary error the CONSUMER's suite caught, not mine

The narrowed gate first refused `post.at <= pre_send.at`. That broke `ack-stage`'s `ntm_capture_retains_full_json_and_successful_is_not_delivery`, which flipped **RETRY → AWAIT_HUMAN** because its fixtures build both captures at `at=100`. `now_unix()` has **second resolution**, so two captures milliseconds apart legitimately carry the same stamp — equal stamps are truncation, not a fault. Only a strictly backward stamp is. Corrected to `<`, and `equal_timestamps_are_adjudicated_not_refused` now pins it.

**Found by running the blast radius, not the crate.** Had I run only `-p receiver-receipt` I would have shipped a live behaviour change with a green suite.

## Two self-referential traps in my own source scanner, in order

1. **Forbidden words as plain literals** — the scanner's input is the file containing the scanner, so it failed on itself. Cured with `concat!`, the house pattern from `path-literal-guard`.
2. **It still failed.** `successful:` appears in a doc comment quoting the measured inversion, and `sender_success` inside a **test name**. A bare scan cannot tell **prose** from **code** — the identical defect the orchestrator hit the same evening when `grep -c` returned 1 from a `///` comment. Scoped to the production slice (everything above the first `#[cfg(test)]`), with two anti-vacuity assertions and a positive control on the slice.

## Mutations — all attributable, restore byte-identical

    1  neuter the ordering gate           -> reversed-order leg RED
    2  admit `robot_send` into production  -> isolation leg RED naming the needle
    3  drift the floor 75 -> 5             -> drift gate RED naming the authority
    sha256 before c142ae9877065ad2dccf2b40d5dabd002a046972422d91672922a610037abde8
    sha256 after  c142ae9877065ad2dccf2b40d5dabd002a046972422d91672922a610037abde8

## Acceptance 7, stated plainly — and unlike K6 the answer is YES

**A production caller does observe.** `crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs:580,797` build both observations with `observe_capture(..., now_unix())`; `crates/ack-stage/src/lib.rs:294` calls `assess_receiver_receipt`; three crates depend on this one. The ordering gate is **live** on that path — which is precisely why the boundary error above mattered rather than being cosmetic.

## Acceptance, item by item

1. **Never reads the sender's return value** — enforced by the signature, and now by a source scan of the production slice with the sender vocabulary this fleet emits. Mutation 2 proves it bites.
2. **Both inversions inexpressible as arrived** — one leg each: a sender success with an unchanged idle pane is `NO_RECEIPT{IdleUnchanged}`; a sender failure cannot withdraw a receiver confirmation because no sender input is accepted.
3. **Last status line, not the buffer** — `tick_monitor::classify`'s job, consulted not duplicated.
4. **v18 contract** — the fixtures use braille spinners (`⠋`, `⠙`) and the `π` prompt glyph, never the literal word `Working`.
5. **Wedge distinct from idle** — `WedgedUnsubmitted`, and `single_capture_verdicts_survive_below_the_floor` proves the ordering gate does not suppress it. No fourth detector.
6. **Anti-vacuity** — `an_empty_census_is_an_error_never_a_non_arrival` asserts both `EmptyPaneList` and `Missing` are `INDETERMINATE`, never `NO_RECEIPT`, never `DEAD`.
7. **Production caller** — yes, named above.

## NO-CLAIM

Receiver observation proves a packet was **RENDERED, not COMPREHENDED** — a pane can display a packet and act on none of it, which is K9's tracker readback (`u622`). This commit does not prove the timer/hash comparison is correct at short spacing; it proves only that a backward-stamped pair cannot produce a verdict. The `Idle → Idle` floor remains unmeasured and unclaimed, and acceptance 2's literal ≥75s requirement is **not met** — deliberately, with the reason recorded inline in the source.

title: dcg false positive: a bead DESCRIPTION documenting a guarded command is itself denied, so a blocked-command trauma cannot be recorded
description: MEASURED 2026-09-03. Filing the P0 above was DENIED by dcg (core.git:branch-force-delete) because the bead's DESCRIPTION TEXT contained the guarded command as prose evidence. No command was being run -- the string sat inside a quoted `-d` argument to `br create`. Retried with the description passed through an environment variable and it succeeded, so the guard is matching the literal anywhere in the command text rather than in command position. WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND ERGONOMICS: it means a trauma caused by a guarded command cannot be RECORDED in the tracker using the words that describe it, which is precisely the evidence a future agent needs to not repeat it. A guard that blocks its own incident report trains agents to paraphrase the evidence, and a paraphrased command is not a reproduction. PRIOR ART IN OUR OWN GATES, which shows the fix is known: `state-wildcard-lint` reports 'string-literal contents are masked before scanning, so a pattern quoted as specimen data is not code', and `path-literal-guard` builds its needle with `concat!` so the gate's own source never contains the contiguous literal. Both solve exactly this class. dcg does not mask quoted data. SIXTH INSTANCE of the self-referential-checker family recorded in AGENTS.md, where a checker's input contains text ABOUT the thing it checks: KERNEL_REGISTRY flagging its own declaration, a doc comment containing the needle it warned about, a census grepping its own table, a contract Validation block grepping its own file, and now a guard denying its own incident report. NO-CLAIM: dcg is not in this repo and this bead does not propose editing it. The correct route is an upstream report plus, if the rule is ours to tune, a nuanced rule that requires command position. The workaround (pass prose via environment variable) is recorded here so the next agent does not lose the same twenty minutes.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Reproduce the KNOWN-BAD leg live: invoke the real dcg guard (core.git:branch-force-delete) against a `br create -d '<text containing the guarded literal as prose>'` command line and capture the DENY with exit code, rule id, and matched offset. The existing 2026-09-03 filing narrative is NOT evidence — it is unrecorded prose with no captured exit code, no rule id, and no stdout/stderr artifact; a fresh captured transcript is required.

2. Record the paired KNOWN-BAD control that isolates position vs. text: the same literal passed via environment variable (the recorded workaround) must be shown to PASS in the same dcg version, proving the difference is quoting/position, not content. Both transcripts must come from one session with the dcg version/commit hash recorded.

3. KNOWN-GOOD leg: an actual command-position use of the guarded command (real `git branch -D`-shaped invocation, run in a throwaway sandbox repo or dry-run harness) must still be DENIED after any rule tuning. A fix that merely narrows to "quoted → allow" and thereby lets a real invocation through is a failure of this bead.

4. Anti-vacuity: if the guard-evaluation harness returns zero scanned candidates, zero rules loaded, or the dcg binary/rule is absent, emit a typed error (e.g. `GuardProbeUnavailable`, `NoRulesLoaded`) with nonzero exit. Empty results must never render as "no denial → pass". Assert at least one BAD and one GOOD probe executed.

5. Mutation test: flip the classification (e.g. treat quoted `-d` payload as command position, or disable the masking predicate) and show the KNOWN-GOOD or KNOGN-BAD leg goes RED with the specific assertion name in output. Restore the file byte-identically and prove it with a pre/post sha256 of the mutated file, both hashes quoted in the bead.

6. MEASURED live: dcg's actual deny/allow behavior, its version, the two transcripts, and the exit codes. MAY be fixture: the prose text specimen and any recorded rule-source excerpt. Prior-art citations (`state-wildcard-lint` string-literal masking, `path-literal-guard` `concat!` needle construction) must be verified live by file:line in this repo, not quoted from memory.

7. NO-CLAIM boundary must be honored and stated in the resolution: dcg is not in this repo; no edit to it is proposed. Deliverable is (a) an upstream report containing the captured transcripts and the two prior-art fix patterns, with its destination/URL or a filed bead recording that it could not be sent, and (b) if any part of the rule is ours to tune, a command-position-requiring rule plus its tests.

8. Open sub-items must be fixed or separately filed, never silently absorbed: (a) whether the rule is ours to tune — resolve with evidence of rule ownership or file a bead; (b) the sixth-instance self-referential-checker family — append this instance to the AGENTS.md list with the five prior instances still enumerated, or file a bead to do so; (c) the environment-variable workaround must be written down verbatim as a reusable recipe, not left implicit in this bead's prose.

title: P0: the decision ledger has a writer and no ACTUATOR -- HD-0008 recorded 'push it' on 2026-09-02 and nothing executed it for 3 days; a HUMAN_DECISION row needs an execution status and an owner
description: MEASURED 2026-09-05 by pane 1, and Joshua's ruling today is what makes it a P0 rather than a note: 'saving our work isn't a me thing - that should be standard practice'. THE DEFECT: docs/decisions.jsonl carries HD-0001 through HD-0018 and has a functioning WRITER -- eighteen rows exist, five of them written during this session -- but NO ACTUATOR. HD-0008 recorded decider=josh, decision 'A: push to public origin/main as-is. Josh 2026-09-02: this is a build in public repo - push it', and it was never carried out: 183 commits were unpushed when the decision was made and 387 are unpushed now. A recorded human decision sat unexecuted for three days while the repo accumulated 204 more commits behind it. WHY IT WENT UNNOTICED: nothing reads a decision row and asks whether its consequence happened. The row has a question, a decision, a decider and a ref, and no execution status, no owner, and no completion evidence. Loop 1 pass 1 filed nsx1 as 'S9 has a reader and no writer'; the gap has now INVERTED and the new shape is worse, because a written-and-unexecuted decision reads as settled. AND IT COMPOUNDED: pane 1 re-escalated the same decision to Joshua tonight as though it were open, which is the second failure mode -- an unactuated decision invites re-asking, and re-asking spends the human attention the ledger exists to conserve. Joshua's correction was explicit and is the requirement: routine, reversible, standard-practice actions must not be modelled as human decisions at all. THE ATLAS-ARC FRAME, since the loop is live: R3 types every unknown into exactly one disposition and HUMAN_DECISION is one of six, but atlas-arc gives HUMAN_DECISION no completion path -- it says 'requires an explicit human choice before a named gate' and stops. R10's reopen triggers include 'current reality diverges from the status surface', which is precisely a decision recorded as made while its consequence is absent. So the mechanism is missing in the skill as well as in our repo. ACCEPTANCE: (1) a decision row carries an execution status distinguishing at least recorded / actuated / refused-by-a-gate / superseded; (2) it carries an owner for the actuation, and an unowned actuated-status row is a refusal rather than a default; (3) something enumerates recorded-but-not-actuated rows and surfaces them -- with a named reader, because AGENTS.md's measured rule is that a monitor with no reader is a file that grows; (4) a routine reversible action is NOT eligible to be a HUMAN_DECISION row at all, and the classifier says so, so 'should we save our work' can never again consume human attention; (5) known-bad leg: a row with decision set and status=recorded past a deadline must be surfaced, and the leg must fire on HD-0008 itself as the historical specimen. FALSIFIER: after the mechanism exists, plant a decided-but-unactuated row and confirm the enumeration names it; if it does not, the mechanism is decoration. NO-CLAIM: this establishes one decision unexecuted for three days and that no surface tracks execution. It does not establish how many of the other seventeen rows are unactuated -- that census is part of the work, not of this finding.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Known-bad leg must fire on HD-0008 itself: the enumerator, run live against docs/decisions.jsonl, must emit HD-0008 (decider=josh, decision "A: push to public origin/main as-is", ref 2026-09-02) as recorded-but-not-actuated. The mere existence of the HD-0008 row is NOT evidence the leg works — that row exists today and nothing flags it; the pass condition is the enumerator's typed output naming HD-0008 with its age in days (>=3) and the divergence measurement (unpushed commit count at decision time vs now: 183 -> 387), not the row's presence.

2. Known-good leg must not be over-strict: at least one real row in HD-0001..HD-0018 that is genuinely actuated (or refused-by-a-gate / superseded) must be classified as such and must NOT appear in the recorded-but-not-actuated list. Name the row ID in the output. If no such row exists after the census, construct one by actuating it for real and record the completion evidence; do not weaken the leg by marking a row actuated without evidence.

3. Anti-vacuity: an empty enumeration result is a typed ERROR (e.g. LedgerScanEmpty / NoRowsParsed), never a pass. Distinguish three cases explicitly: (a) file missing/unparseable -> error; (b) zero rows parsed -> error; (c) N>0 rows parsed, zero overdue -> pass, and the pass must print the parsed row count and the per-row status tally so a pass is auditable. Same rule for the classifier: zero candidates examined is an error.

4. Mutation-goes-RED: flip HD-0008's status field from recorded to actuated (or delete its row) and prove the enumerator's exit code / typed result changes from FAIL to PASS — i.e. the check is load-bearing. Record sha256 of docs/decisions.jsonl before mutation, restore byte-identically, re-verify the checksum matches and the check returns to RED on HD-0008. Paste both checksums.

5. MEASURED live, not fixture: (a) the current unpushed-commit count via `git rev-list --count @{u}..HEAD` or equivalent, shown at the time of the run; (b) the parse and status tally of the real docs/decisions.jsonl; (c) the named reader actually invoking the enumeration — cite the file:line of the call site and show its output in a real run, since AGENTS.md's rule is that a monitor with no reader is a file that grows. Permitted as fixture: synthetic rows used to exercise the refused-by-a-gate and superseded branches, and the planted falsifier row — these must be clearly labelled fixture and must not be the only evidence for any leg.

6. Schema and owner enforcement: every row carries execution_status in {recorded, actuated, refused_by_gate, superseded} and an actuation_owner. A row with status=actuated and no owner, or no completion evidence field, must be a typed REFUSAL (not a default, not a warning). Demonstrate the refusal firing on a deliberately malformed row and show the error type. Migration of the existing eighteen rows must be explicit: no row silently defaults to recorded without being counted.

7. Classifier rule for routine reversible actions: a routine, reversible, standard-practice action (per Joshua's ruling "saving our work isn't a me thing - that should be standard practice") must be REJECTED as a HUMAN_DECISION at write time with a named error and a stated alternative disposition. Test with the exact HD-0008 content ("should we push to public origin/main") and show it is rejected; show a genuinely irreversible/contested example is still accepted, so the classifier is not a blanket deny.

8. Falsifier: after the mechanism exists, plant a fresh decided-but-unactuated row past the deadline and confirm the enumeration names it by ID in its output; if it does not, mark the mechanism decoration and fail the bead. Remove the planted row afterward and re-verify the file checksum.

9. Open sub-items must be fixed or separately filed, never silently covered: (a) the census of how many of the other seventeen rows (HD-0001..HD-0018 excluding HD-0008) are unactuated — the description's NO-CLAIM explicitly excludes it from the finding, so it must be completed here with per-row status, or filed as its own bead with an ID recorded in this bead; (b) the atlas-arc R3/R10 gap — HUMAN_DECISION has no completion path in the skill and R10's reopen trigger "current reality diverges from the status surface" is unimplemented — must be filed upstream as a separate bead with an ID recorded here; (c) the actual push decided in HD-0008 must be executed or its refusal recorded as refused_by_gate with the gate named — leaving it at 387 unpushed commits with a green ledger is a fail.

Converted: recorded 2026-09-02 22:55 UTC, THREE DAYS AGO. MEASURED AGAINST REALITY NOW: 477 commits unpushed against origin/main. 294 of them landed AFTER the decision was recorded. So the ledger holds an explicit human instruction to push, and in the three days since, the gap it was meant to close has grown by 294 commits. THE KNOWN-BAD LEG FIRES: TRUE. THAT IS THE ACTUATOR GAP STATED AS A NUMBER, and it is the central fact of this session. A decision was made, recorded correctly, bound to a stage, and nothing read it. Every mechanism this fleet built tonight -- the grading gate, the escalation taxonomy, the five-cell matrix, the ranked selector -- reads the BEAD tracker. Nothing reads docs/decisions.jsonl. So a human decision is write-only: it enters the ledger and no code path consumes it. THIS IS AGENTS.MD'S THIRD RULE APPLIED TO DECISIONS RATHER THAN GATES. That rule says a gate with no reachable trigger is worse than no gate, because the repo reads as protected. Here a DECISION with no actuator is worse than no decision, because the operator believes the instruction was received. Joshua said 'push it' and reasonably assumed that meant it would be pushed. THE ANSWER-SHAPED ROW COUNT IS THE SCOPE: 10 of 42 rows carry an 'answers' field, so ten decisions have been answered. I checked ONE of them for actuation. WHY I AM BLOCKING RATHER THAN LEAVING IN_PROGRESS: the fix has two halves and only one is an agent task. Building an enumerator that emits unactuated decisions is implementable now. That is Joshua's call, not an agent's, and an actuator that fires automatically on 'push it' would have executed it tonight into a red CI. So the enumerator is buildable and the actuation is gated. I ALSO NOTE THIS BEAD WAS BEING RE-OFFERED ON EVERY TICK -- ticks 23, 27, 32 and 33, dispatched to %7 then %8, with ACKs from BOTH panes. It is one of the six beads in the cross-pane duplication census (7lsb) and one of the permanent grading candidates (dp21). It does NOT establish that the other nine answered decisions are unactuated -- I checked one -- nor that no consumer of docs/decisions.jsonl exists anywhere; I did not grep for readers, and 'nothing reads it' is an inference from the actuation gap rather than a measured absence.
