title: P0: DEF-001 is defined 7 times as 7 different defects across 7 DEFECTS.toml files, and DISPOSITIONS.toml makes 6 live references to a DEF-002 with 5 candidate owners
description:
WHAT: `DEF-*` is not one identifier space. It is SEVEN colliding ones, and the collision is on the
DEFINITION line, not on a reference.

MEASURED 2026-09-05, pattern `^\s*id\s*=\s*"DEF-\d+"` over `docs/plan/**` + `docs/planning/**`:
`DEF-001` is DEFINED seven times, as seven different objects:
  docs/plan/flow/unknowns/DEFECTS.toml:4    P0 class="self-referential-checker"
  docs/planning/round3/DEFECTS.toml:35      P1 class="NORMATIVE_CORPUS_OMISSION"
  docs/planning/round4/DEFECTS.toml:61      P1 class="DECORATIVE_IDENTIFIER_REGISTER"
  docs/planning/round6a/DEFECTS.toml:40     P1 class="STALE_ABSENCE_ACROSS_SECTIONS"
  docs/planning/round6b/DEFECTS.toml:57     P2 class="DANGLING_FORWARD_REF"
  docs/planning/round6c/DEFECTS.toml:97     P2 class="UNLABELED_CONSTITUTION_REFERENTS"
  docs/planning/round6d/DEFECTS.toml:45     P3 class="REF_WRONG"
Seven distinct severities and seven distinct classes under one name. `DEF-002` is defined five times
(`unknowns:16`, `round3:51`, `round4:119`, `round6a:56`, `round6c:139`); `DEF-003`..`DEF-006` three
times each. Distinct id STRINGS: 14. Distinct DEFINED OBJECTS: 21.

AND THE AMBIGUITY IS ALREADY BEING CONSUMED. `docs/plan/flow/unknowns/DISPOSITIONS.toml:3481, 3493,
3505, 3517, 3529, 3541` each carry the reference: "Empty first row is a dual-row ledger defect
(DEF-002), not a question." Six live references to a bare `DEF-002` that has five candidate owners.
The intended owner is `docs/plan/flow/unknowns/DEFECTS.toml:16` (class="dual-authority-ledger"), and
nothing in the reference says so. `docs/decisions.jsonl` also carries a bare `DEF-004`.

WHY: Atlas Arc R2, verbatim (`~/.claude/skills/atlas-arc/SKILL.md:98`): "Do not create duplicate IDs
for restatements. References must point to the canonical owner." `DEF-*` is R2's own review-defect
kind (`SKILL.md:94`) and R4 makes `DEF-*` the ONLY legal output of a review (`SKILL.md:113-127`), so
this is the one id family the process cannot afford to have ambiguous. Consequence: a grader told
"fix DEF-001" cannot determine which of seven defects is meant without being told the file, which
means the file — not the id — is the actual identifier. That is prose wearing a schedulable object's
clothes. It also silently breaks any future cross-round rollup: a `status = "open"` census over
`DEF-*` returns 21 rows under 14 names and cannot report which are the same defect re-found.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. Every `DEF-*` definition in `docs/plan/**` and `docs/planning/**` is unique repo-wide. The
   round-scoped form is the cheapest repair: `DEF-R3-001`, `DEF-R6C-001`, `DEF-U-001` for
   `flow/unknowns`. Rewriting history is not required — renaming in place is, because these files are
   read as live registers (`round6c/DEFECTS.toml:32` sets the current verdict).
2. The six `DISPOSITIONS.toml` references and the `docs/decisions.jsonl` `DEF-004` reference are
   rewritten to the new unique id.
3. A checker exists that parses `id = "DEF-*"` across both trees and refuses a duplicate.

FALSIFIER: the checker in acceptance 3 must report `DEF-001 defined 7x` against the tree at
`git rev-parse HEAD` BEFORE the rename, and 0 duplicates after. Anti-vacuity: plant an eighth
`id = "DEF-001"` in a scratch fixture copy and require the checker to count 8, so an empty or
unreadable scan set cannot pass as clean.

NO-CLAIM: this does not claim any of the 21 defect BODIES is wrong, and does not claim the round
records should be merged. It claims only that the seven objects cannot be addressed by their ids.
Positive control for the census instrument: the same pattern returns 24 unique `GATE-\d\d\d` and
finds `HD-9999` at `docs/plan/12-journey.md:471`, both known-present.

close_reason: MUTATION-NOT-REQUIRED / GATE-VERIFIED by pane 1 (non-author; created_by=AtlasArcPass2), 2026-09-06. The invariant this bead exists to establish HOLDS in the live tree, and it shipped a GATE rather than a one-off edit. RE-EXECUTED, not read: git show 6ba3260 --stat -> 'feat(def-ids): round-scope colliding DEF-* definitions [test]', touching crates/no-shell-gate/src/def_ids.rs (+205), crates/no-shell-gate/tests/def_ids.rs (+167), crates/no-shell-gate/src/lib.rs, docs/decisions.jsonl, docs/plan/flow/unknowns/DEFECTS.toml and DISPOSITIONS.toml. THE ACCEPTANCE IS MET ON ITS OWN TERMS. Item 1 required every DEF-* definition under docs/plan/** and docs/planning/** to be unique repo-wide, and named the round-scoped form as the cheapest repair. Measured: round3 carries DEF-R3-00N, round4 DEF-R4-00N, round6a DEF-R6A-00N, round6b DEF-R6B-001, round6c DEF-R6C-00N, round6d DEF-R6D-001 -- exactly the prescribed scheme. Across 7 DEFECTS.toml files there are 31 distinct DEF-* ids and ZERO duplicated across files, verified two independent ways: my own regex census over the toml tree, and a per-id collision map that reports each id appearing in exactly one file. Item 2 required the DISPOSITIONS.toml references and the docs/decisions.jsonl DEF-004 reference to be rewritten: DISPOSITIONS.toml files now contain ZERO bare DEF-00N references, and grep for DEF-004 in docs/decisions.jsonl returns 0. IT SHIPPED A GATE, WHICH IS WHY THIS CLOSE IS STRONGER THAN A DIFF REVIEW. cargo test -p no-shell-gate --test def_ids -> EIGHT legs, all passing, and their names are the acceptance: parse_accepts_definition_line_and_rejects_comments_and_other_families (comment stripping, the eighth-instance class this repo keeps paying for), missing_tree_is_an_error_not_a_pass, empty_scan_set_is_an_error_not_a_pass, files_with_no_def_ids_are_an_error_not_a_pass (three separate anti-vacuity arms, not one), unique_round_scoped_ids_are_clean (known-good), seven_def_001_definitions_report_defined_7x (the known-bad, keyed on the REAL historical collision the bead's title names), planted_eighth_def_001_reports_defined_8x (a planted mutation baked in as a permanent leg rather than run once by hand), and live_tree_def_ids_are_unique (a check against production data, not a fixture). I DID NOT RUN MY OWN MUTATION and state why rather than omitting it: planted_eighth_def_001_reports_defined_8x IS a mutation leg, permanently resident, asserting the counter increments when an eighth collision is planted. A hand mutation would duplicate a committed leg, and this repo's KERNEL-ONLY rule says not to handroll what a kernel provides. THREE BARE IDS SURVIVE AND ARE NOT A DEFECT, which I checked before closing rather than after: DEF-001 and DEF-002 in round6a/DEFECTS.toml, DEF-006 in round4/DEFECTS.toml. Each appears in exactly ONE file, so the uniqueness invariant is intact -- they are unscoped but not colliding. The bead's item 1 asks for uniqueness, which holds; full scheme consistency is a tidiness follow-on, not this acceptance. The gate's own live_tree_def_ids_are_unique passing is the authority on that. I RAN THE PREMISE CHECK FIRST AND IT INITIALLY LOOKED REFUTED, which is worth recording as method: my first census found 0 duplicates and I nearly reported the bead stale. Grepping DEF-001 directly found it in 3 files, only ONE of them a DEFECTS.toml -- the other two, CURRENT-REALITY.md and R2-ID-CENSUS.md, reference it rather than define it. So the distinction between DEFINITION and REFERENCE is what makes the bead's title ('defined 7 times') and the current state ('defined once') both true at their respective times. The fix landed at 6ba3260 and the title describes the pre-fix world. NO-CLAIM: this proves 31 distinct ids with zero cross-file duplication, zero bare DISPOSITIONS references, zero DEF-004 in decisions.jsonl, and eight passing gate legs including a live-tree check and a resident planted-collision mutation. It does NOT prove the three unscoped ids will never collide with a future round's numbering -- nothing enforces the DEF-R<round>- prefix on NEW ids, only uniqueness, so a future round4 addition of DEF-001 would collide and the gate would catch it after the fact rather than preventing it. That prefix-enforcement gap is worth its own bead and I am not filing one tonight; I have 19 open P0s of my own and this is a tidiness item. All cargo figures read the WORKTREE, not commit 6ba3260's tree.

title: P0: DOCS_STALE vetoes ALL dispatch on an authority that was conditional -- add a DEGRADED admission arm gated per packet class, and wire admission-reason (929 LOC, 0 callers)
description:
WHAT: (a) add a DEGRADED arm to the dispatch admission verdict so the loop can express "allowed
for packet classes that do not depend on the stale input"; (b) classify packet classes by their
actual input dependency, not by stakes-by-vibe; (c) wire `crates/admission-reason` (929 LOC, 17
tests, ZERO external callers) as the component that NAMES the gate on every degraded row; (d) keep
the full refusal for packet classes that DO depend on the stale input.

WHY -- the loop idled three workers for ~25 minutes on 2026-09-06 while ten P0s sat in `grading`,
and every layer behaved exactly as written. Measured, in the order that decided the design:

1. THE AUTHORITY IS NARROWER THAN THE GATE. `docs/decisions.jsonl` HD-0001 asks
   "The pending-dispatch fence for undrained-pipe-lint-w4j has held since 11:42:46 ... Clear it
   or hold it?" -> decision "CLEAR - tick loop continues", with
   `condition: CONDITIONAL - the tick loop continues only as long as docs are kept up to date`
   and `review_after: the next receiver-proof timeout`.
   That docs clause was a CONDITION ON CLEARING ONE FENCE on 2026-09-01. `main.rs:4904-4913`
   implements it as a PERMANENT UNCONDITIONAL VETO on every tick. And `review_after` has fired
   repeatedly since (ACK_STAGE_INDETERMINATE and five DISPATCH_SILENCE events on %9 tonight
   alone), so HD-0001 is overdue for review BY ITS OWN TERMS.

2. THE COUPLING IS PER-PACKET, NOT GLOBAL. Only three crates read `docs/PLAN.md`:
   `crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs` (the gate), `crates/plan-assemble/src/main.rs` (the
   writer), `crates/preregistration-gate/src/lib.rs` (the exemption list). NO dispatch path, NO
   grading path, and NO worker path reads it. The gate's own rationale --
   "a stale assembly makes every downstream dispatch send an agent to work from old knowledge"
   -- is therefore a property of what a PACKET points an agent at, not of dispatch itself.

3. THE PACKET RENDERER DOES NOT EMBED THE ASSEMBLY. `crates/omp-orchestrator/src/dispatch_packet.rs`
   contains ZERO occurrences of `PLAN.md`, `docs/plan`, or `read_to_string` (positive control:
   `PACKET_REFUSED_FILED_ONLY` appears once in the same file, so the grep works). It already
   exposes a distinct `render_grading_packet` at :293 -- the class seam exists in code today.
   A grading packet cites the bead's own acceptance criteria, which live in the bead, not the plan.

4. THE TYPE CANNOT EXPRESS THE STATE. `crates/omp-types/src/pane_observation.rs:30`
   `pub enum DispatchAdmissibility { Unknown, Allowed, Refused }` -- there is no DEGRADED arm.
   This is the same shape as the `redispatch_required` finding recorded on `zey6`: a real state
   with no arm in the enum reads as covered while being unreachable.

5. AUTO-REPAIR ALONE IS FALSIFIED -- do not ship only that. The obvious fix is "have the loop run
   plan-assemble before refusing", modelled on rch's typed
   `SelfHealingOutcome { Success, Failure, Skipped, Noop }`
   (verified at mirror `remote_compilation_helper/rch-telemetry/src/remediation.rs:315`, stable
   `as_str()` tokens and an `ALL` slice in declaration order). But TONIGHT it would have returned
   `Failure`: `plan-assemble` itself refuses with `PREREGISTRATION_ERROR evidence row lacks

   degradation is entered; it does not cover the case that actually idled the fleet. Ship the

1. THE ARM EXISTS AND IS EXHAUSTIVE. DispatchAdmissibility gains a Degraded arm carrying the

   acceptance and no plan document -- must be ADMITTED as Degraded. If it is refused, the change
   delivered nothing and FAILS.

   every class. Assert Allowed, not Degraded, on a fresh tree. A Degraded verdict on a fresh tree
   means the classifier is inverted.

   restore byte-for-byte; green. A leg that survives deletion of its own subject is
   unattributable -- the ack-spine census failure in AGENTS.md, where a doc comment containing the
   needle kept the gate GREEN after the emit site was deleted. Strip comments before any matching.

title: tick-monitor scored a pane blocked on an Ask dialog as WORKING/LIVE
description:
WHAT: on OMP v18 an Ask/approval dialog renders ABOVE the status line, and the status line remains LAST with an advancing spinner and timer. `classify` therefore scored a pane blocked on a human answer as `Working`, and `liveness` scored it `Live` indefinitely -- because the timer really does advance while the pane waits. A pane awaiting an answer was indistinguishable from a pane doing work.

HOW IT WAS FOUND: dogfooding, 2026-08-31 ~11:30Z. The operator reported the OPPOSITE polarity -- their own watcher scored %1413 GONE at 09:15Z on an Ask dialog, and specified the defect as 'dialog covers the status line -> classifier finds no model line -> Unproven -> dropped from capacity'. I went to reproduce that on a live pane and it DID NOT reproduce: %1372 had a dialog open and its last line was ' 26m . GPT-5.6-Luna . ~/Developer/control-plane', a perfectly readable status line. `last_status_line` returned it, spinner+timer matched, and the pane scored WORKING. So the specified failure was not mine; the real one was the same class as `Wedged` -- LOOKS BUSY, IS NOT -- and it was hiding a real escalation: %1372 sat 36 minutes on the arc-keepalive install approval reading as healthy work.

MEASURED IMPACT: the pane the whole fleet was waiting on (the gated binary install escalated to Joshua) was invisible to the conductor because it looked productive. A conductor polling for idle capacity would never surface it, and a conductor watching for frozen panes would never surface it either, because the timer was genuinely moving.

THE FIX (76bef30):
1. `PaneState::Dialog { timer_secs }` and `Liveness::Dialog { timer_secs }` -- ALIVE, NOT dispatchable, NOT free capacity, plus a new `needs_answer()` predicate. Answering is the action, not filling, so it is deliberately NOT folded into `is_free_capacity`.
2. `dialog_open()` is POSITIONAL, not shape-based. First attempt keyed on `line is box-framed AND contains a footer marker`. THAT SELF-POLLUTED: my own pane carries box-framed lines containing 'Esc cancel' because OMP renders tool-call blocks inside frames and my commands quoted the marker. Measured: 4 unframed + 3 framed matches in my own scrollback. The discriminator that survives is ADJACENCY -- the footer must sit within the three non-blank lines immediately above the status line. Same lesson as `in_citation_position` and as `last_status_line` anchoring on the LAST line: shape alone is not enough, because a dialog's text is shaped like content.
3. Checked BEFORE the spinner branch, like `Wedged`. Order is load-bearing: a dialog pane HAS a live spinner, so a spinner-first check scores it WORKING.
4. `vanished(prior, live_ids)` -- the ONLY death authority is absence from `tmux list-panes`. It returns EMPTY for an empty live list, because a failed scan must never produce a fleet-wide obituary.

TWO FURTHER BUGS THE TESTS CAUGHT, both the same `_ => 0` catch-all class:
- `save()` wrote `timer_secs: 0` for DIALOG, so the state file round-tripped the variant but lost the timer. Caught by the round-trip leg, not by review.
- `main.rs`'s JSON renderer had the SAME catch-all in a second place. The round-trip test could not see it because it never renders JSON. Caught only by comparing the live run (`timer_secs=0`) against the pane's own status line (which plainly read `35m`). Both now spell every variant explicitly; there is no wildcard left to absorb the next state.

ACCEPTANCE -- 49 tests + 44 selftest legs, and the gate BITES:
- planted VERBATIM live dialog capture (tests/fixtures/dialog_v18.txt, captured from %1372) -> asserts label 'DIALOG', not 'WORKING'
- planted normal working capture -> 'WORKING'; planted idle -> 'IDLE' (the new state does not swallow the old ones)
- planted SELF-POLLUTION capture: framed marker far from the status line -> NOT a dialog, and classifies 'WORKING'
- planted absent pane id -> reported dead; a pane WITH a dialog open in the same call -> NOT dead (asserting both in one test is what proves they are distinguished rather than merged)
- planted empty pane list -> nobody dead (anti-vacuity)
- Dialog is !is_dispatchable, !is_free_capacity, needs_answer
- state-file round trip preserves Dialog{timer_secs}
Every leg asserts a SPECIFIC state name. None asserts merely 'did not crash'.

MUTATION, both restored byte-identically (sha256 4a665ddff49a7010 before and after):
- delete the dialog branch from `classify` -> `planted_dialog_is_dialog_not_working` FAILED
- widen adjacency from 3 lines to the whole buffer -> `framed_marker_far_from_status_line_is_not_a_dialog` FAILED
So the detector and its narrowing are each independently attributable.

LIVE PROOF: `tick-monitor observe --session ''` now reports `%1372 DIALOG timer_secs=2160 liveness=DIALOG`, dispatchable=[], free_capacity=[]. Before the fix that pane reported WORKING/LIVE.

COMPILER AS A GATE, worth recording: adding the variant broke the exhaustive `(prev, now)` match with E0004 -- exactly as that match's comment promises ('If a new PaneState is added, this match must fail to compile rather than absorb it into Live'). The wildcard-free design caught a real omission at build time; the `_ => 0` catch-alls in `save` and the renderer, which were NOT wildcard-free, both shipped the bug.

NO-CLAIM -- what this classifier still cannot see:
- It recognises the dialog FOOTER strings measured on OMP v18 ('Enter select', 'Esc cancel', up/down move) inside a framed line adjacent to the status line. A dialog rendered WITHOUT those markers, or with the footer more than three non-blank lines above the status line, still reads WORKING. The marker list is a hand-maintained list mirroring a real set, which is the exact drift class fh C75 warns about.
- MODEL_MARKERS is likewise hand-maintained ('Opus 5', 'GLM 5.3', 'GPT-5.6', 'GPT-5.5'). A new model name makes `dialog_open` return false and the pane fall back to spinner classification -- fail-toward-WORKING, which is the wrong direction for this specific bug.
- It does not measure how long the DIALOG has been open. `timer_secs` is the pane's TURN timer, which was already running before the dialog appeared; it is an upper bound on dialog age, not the age.
- `vanished()` is a pure function and IS unit-tested, but it is NOT yet called from the observe path -- so tick-monitor still does not report DEAD in production. That is a BUILT != WIRED gap I am naming rather than leaving for a reader to discover, and it is the next thing to close.
- The operator's ORIGINAL specified defect (status line genuinely covered -> no model line found) is NOT fixed and NOT reproduced here; if some dialog shape does cover the status line, `classify` returns `Unproven`, which is fail-safe (excluded from capacity) but still reports the wrong reason. No capture of that shape exists in this repo to plant.

MUTATION-VERIFIED by orchestrator (pane 1, claude-opus-5) — wired, not just built.

This was the purest BUILT != WIRED instance in the repo, and the bead's own text
had already diagnosed it correctly.

WHAT WAS ALREADY BUILT (verified by reading, not assumed): tick-monitor classifies
this correctly. `PaneState::Dialog` exists with an accurate doc comment, is
constructed at `crates/tick-monitor/src/lib.rs:365`, labelled "DIALOG" at :247,
handled in liveness at :507 and :581, and `receiver-receipt/src/lib.rs:235-236`
checks for it. Detection: complete and tested.

WHAT WAS NOT WIRED: `crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs:393` folded "DIALOG" into
`is_working` and escalated NOTHING. The measured 36-minute stall on %1372 would
have happened again today, with the classifier right and the supervisor ignoring it.

I FIRST REPORTED THIS WRONG, recorded because the correction is the useful half: my
grep for `Dialog` found nothing in crates/omp-orchestrator and I concluded "the loop
cannot see it." It CAN — it uses the string "DIALOG". That turned a "blind" verdict
into a "mishandles" verdict, which is materially worse and needed a different fix.

THE FIX separates two questions the old code conflated:
  is_working     CAPACITY — do not dispatch there, the pane IS occupied  (unchanged)
  awaits_human   HEALTH   — nobody is coming unless a human is told      (new)

`SupervisorDecision::AwaitingHuman { panes }` is checked BEFORE capacity, because it
is the one condition the loop cannot resolve by working harder. Emits:

  AWAITING_HUMAN panes=%1372 owner=josh next_action=answer-the-open-dialog

VERIFIED IN THE SHIPPED RELEASE BINARY (`strings` finds AWAITING_HUMAN twice plus
the next_action string), not only in source — the distinction this repo keeps paying
for.

THREE TESTS, 39/39 in-crate, 121 suites / 476 assertions workspace-wide:
  a_pane_on_a_dialog_escalates_to_a_human_and_does_not_read_as_working
  a_working_pane_does_not_escalate_to_a_human   — KNOWN-GOOD leg; without it the
      gate is over-strict in the direction that gets it routed around, since every
      busy fleet would page a human
  a_dialog_pane_is_not_dispatchable_capacity

THE FIXTURE DISAGREED WITH PRODUCTION AND THE THIRD TEST CAUGHT IT. The test helper
derived `is_working` from `liveness` alone, so a "DIALOG" fixture reported NOT
working while production reported working — `fh C38`, a fixture drifted from
production, whose green is indistinguishable from a working check. Helper now mirrors
main.rs exactly.

THE ENUM DISCIPLINE PAID TWICE: the new variant broke two exhaustive matches
(main.rs:1085, finding-dispatch/src/lib.rs:27) as COMPILE ERRORS. A wildcard in
either place would have silently swallowed the new state. finding-dispatch now turns
the decision into durable work whose acceptance criteria name the negative leg.

NO-CLAIM: this escalates a dialog the CLASSIFIER detects. It does not prove the
classifier detects every dialog shape v18 can render. The v18 status-line history
(shipped presets required a literal "Working" that v18 never renders; 0/3 on live
payload) and sibling bead lifecycle-phantom-landing-ma1 both say the rendered
surface changes without notice, and this is still a regex over rendered text. The
typed `session` root — 78 files, 499 symbols, zero imported — remains the real fix
and remains unadopted.

comments.text:
WIRED + OBSCURED (933c2eb) -- closing my own BUILT != WIRED gap, and correcting the fail-safe excuse I offered for the covered-status-line case.

=== 1. vanished() NOW HAS A NAMED PRODUCTION CALLER ===
crates/tick-monitor/src/main.rs:202, inside `observe_core`:
    let dead = tick_monitor::vanished(&prior.panes, &ids);
Rendered at main.rs:314 as `"dead_panes":{"ids":[...],"count":N}`. A value computed and never printed is still unwired, so the render is part of the wiring, not a nicety.

Ordering matters and is asserted by construction: the call sits AFTER the two existing refusals -- `pane_ids` returns Err on a tmux timeout (a timeout is not an empty fleet) and observe refuses an empty pane set outright -- and `vanished` independently returns empty for an empty list. Three independent guards, because the failure mode here is a fleet-wide obituary generated from a failed scan.

WIRING PROOF, and it bites: `vanished_has_a_production_caller_in_the_binary` reads main.rs and asserts the call site plus both rendered fields, WITH a positive control asserting the scan can report absence (a grep that can never miss is not evidence -- fh N043 is this repo failing exactly that way). MUTATION: replaced the call with `let dead: Vec<String> = Vec::new();` -> test FAILED; restored, green. NO-CLAIM on its class: this is a SOURCE-level check, the same mechanism no-shell-gate's wired_lanes uses. It proves a call site EXISTS in the production binary; it does not prove that site executes. That is the live run below, and it is a different kind of evidence.

LIVE PROOF, planted known-bad + real positive, all 34 panes of this box:
  tick 1 seeded 34 panes into a scratch state file
  injected `pane\t%99999\tWORKING\t120\t7\t1788170000` -- a pane id that does not exist
  tick 2 -> dead_panes {"ids":["%99999"],"count":1}
           attention  {"panes":["%1372:DIALOG"],"count":1}
           dispatchable []
The planted absent id is reported dead; the REAL dialog pane, present in tmux, is NOT reported dead and instead lands in attention. Both halves in one run, which is what proves DEAD and DIALOG are distinguished rather than merged.

=== 2. THE COVERED STATUS LINE: I WAS WRONG THAT FAIL-SAFE WAS ENOUGH ===
I wrote 'classify returns Unproven -- fail-safe but wrong reason'. The operator's correction is right and it is not stylistic: Unproven is DROPPED FROM CAPACITY, and dropping is precisely how a live pane goes untended. Their watcher scored %1413 GONE at 09:15Z on this shape.

But their FIX is also not right, and they said so: after it, it produced a FALSE DIALOG on %1414 at 09:38Z when a box-drawing region briefly covered a pane mid-work at 26/26. So the third state must NOT be Dialog. A covered status line is an OBSERVATION failure; a dialog is a pane WAITING FOR AN ANSWER. Inferring the second from evidence for the first invents a blocker that does not exist -- and a conductor that believes a working pane is waiting on it will interrupt real work.

THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE PRIOR OBSERVATION, NOT THE SHAPE OF THIS CAPTURE. A pane that carried a model-name line last tick and carries none now is alive and OBSCURED. A pane that never carried one is a shell. This reuses the crate's existing two-capture mechanism rather than adding a new heuristic, and it cannot produce the %1414 false positive: that pane's prior state was Working, so it reads OBSCURED (attention: LOOK), never DIALOG (attention: ANSWER).

IMPLEMENTATION: `Liveness::Obscured` -- !is_dispatchable, !is_free_capacity, !needs_answer, needs_attention. The now-Unproven check MOVED from above the `prev` resolution to below it, so the prior state is available; and `pane_id_mismatch` was moved ABOVE it, because comparing a prior observation from a DIFFERENT pane is not evidence about this one. `needs_attention()` is deliberately NOT filtered by --exclude-pane: the conductor's own pane can be obscured or prompting too, and 'not worker capacity' is not 'need not look'.

FIXTURE PLANTED -- the thing I previously said I could not plant. I wrote 'no capture of that shape exists in this repo to plant' and left the behaviour untested. Synthesised it instead: `COVERED`, a box-drawing region occupying the last lines with NO dialog footer. Five legs, each asserting a SPECIFIC name:
  a_covered_status_line_is_not_a_dialog          -> dialog_open false, classify UNPROVEN
  a_covered_pane_that_was_working_is_obscured    -> OBSCURED, needs_attention, !dispatchable, !needs_answer
  a_shell_pane_stays_unproven_and_is_never_obscured -> UNPROVEN (prior Unproven)
  a_covered_pane_with_no_prior_is_unproven       -> UNPROVEN (one capture is not a liveness claim)
  a_dialog_still_beats_a_covered_frame           -> DIALOG survives; OBSCURED does not swallow it

MUTATION, both restored byte-identically (sha256 d6299265c5e13b84 before and after):
  A: Obscured arm -> Unproven  -> a_covered_pane_that_was_working_is_obscured_not_dropped FAILED
  B: fire Obscured regardless of prior -> a_shell_pane_stays_unproven_and_is_never_obscured FAILED
So the state AND its prior-state discriminator are each independently attributable. Leg B is the one that matters: without it, 'no model line -> alive and obscured' would relabel every shell pane as a live agent needing attention and the attention list would be permanently noisy -- an over-strict gate, which gets routed around.

STANDING: 56 tests (22 lib + 34 integration) + 44 selftest legs, all green.

NO-CLAIM, updated:
- OBSCURED requires a PRIOR observation. On a cold start every covered pane reads UNPROVEN and is still dropped for exactly one tick. That is deliberate -- one capture is not a liveness claim -- but it is a real hole with a named duration.
- DIALOG_FOOTER and MODEL_MARKERS remain hand-maintained lists mirroring a real set (fh C75 drift class). A new model name makes `dialog_open` return false AND makes OBSCURED impossible to reach for that pane, because its prior would never be model-bearing either. The two failure modes compound rather than cancelling.
- `dead_panes` is now reported. Nothing ACTS on it -- no respawn, no bead, no escalation. It is an observation surface, and calling it 'death handling' would be the same overclaim I am closing here.
- The live proof used an INJECTED pane id, not an organically dead pane. It proves the code path fires on an absent id; it does not prove behaviour during a real pane teardown race, where the pane may vanish between `list-panes` and `capture-pane`.
- I did not re-verify the operator's %1413/%1414 measurements; they are cited as reported. My legs are planted against synthesised and verbatim-captured shapes in this repo.

title: the tree is not green: 17 failing suites behind a receipt claiming 0, blocking 106 unpushed commits
description:
WHAT: **the tree is not green, the receipt says it is, and CI has been red for 67 consecutive runs.**
Get to an honestly green workspace so `git push` can proceed and 106 commits stop sitting on one
disk.

MEASURED 2026-09-02, by running the suite rather than reading a receipt:
```
cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast   ->  203 suites reported, 17 FAILING
.flywheel/workspace-green.receipt       ->  failing_suites=0, recorded Sep 1 20:20
git rev-list --count origin/main..HEAD  ->  106 unpushed commits
gh run history (per AGENTS.md:82-92)    ->  67 runs, 67 failures, all unread
```

THE 17 FAILING SUITES, named:
```
tests/differential.rs        (x2, two crates)   tests/assembly_freshness.rs
tests/bead_shape.rs                             tests/build_identity.rs
tests/crate_contract_inventory.rs               tests/group_kill.rs
tests/hook_freshness.rs                         tests/line_cite_rot.rs
tests/numbers.rs                                tests/oracle_routing.rs
tests/round_stamp.rs                            tests/sender_identity.rs
tests/spawn_contract.rs                         tests/wired_lanes.rs
src/lib.rs                   (x2, two crates)
```

**WHY THIS GATES EVERYTHING ELSE.** Three layers of the same defect, each masking the next:
1. **The local receipt certifies green.** `failing_suites=0` is an ASSERTION by its caller — the
   gate's own docs say so: *"someone can record a green receipt without running anything, exactly as
   `touch` would."*
2. **The pre-push gate now refuses that receipt** because it predates the toolchain-parity check.
   That refusal is correct and it is what exposed layer 1.
3. **CI says red 67 times and nobody read it.** AGENTS.md: *"a local gate that certifies what CI
   rejects is a fooled certificate, which is strictly more dangerous than a silent one: it
   manufactures confidence instead of merely withholding it."*

ACCEPTANCE:
1. **Triage all 17 into three buckets, with evidence per suite:** (a) a real defect in production
   code, (b) a stale premise in the TEST (the tree moved and the assertion did not), (c) an
   environment/ordering artifact that a shared `target/` or a concurrent writer produced.
   **Bucket (b) is expected to be large** — `line_cite_rot`, `numbers`, `bead_shape`,
   `assembly_freshness`, `round_stamp` and `crate_contract_inventory` all assert facts ABOUT the
   repo, and the repo changed ~65 commits today.
2. **Fix (a) at source. For (b), fix the ASSERTION and say what moved.** Do not delete a leg to make
   the build pass — that is the failure the no-shell gate's own header warns about
   (*"a gate that arrives after the mess gets weakened to make the build pass"*).
3. **Never `--record 0` without running.** The count must be observed. A nonzero count writes no
   receipt and exits nonzero, which is the correct outcome until the tree is actually green.
4. **Anti-vacuity: a suite that reports `0 passed; 0 failed` is NOT a pass.** Measured twice this
   session — a shared `target/` produced `0/0` aggregations indistinguishable from a suite that ran
   and passed nothing. Check arity, not just absence of failures.
5. **State the denominator** in every figure: `--lib` or package aggregate. `--lib` hid a hard break
   twice on 2026-09-02 (K8 caught by the consumer's suite, K9 by the package: `--lib` green at 33/0
   while `tests/followup.rs` did not compile, six `E0061`s).
6. **When green: run the suite, record the observed count, push.** `git push` to our own repo is
   SAVING, not publishing, and is autonomous — 106 commits on one disk is the risk, not the push.

TRAPS, all measured tonight:
- `grep -c … || echo 0` prints `0` AND exits 1, yielding `"0\n0"`. Three occurrences after being
  documented.
- A literal `(` in a BRE pattern makes our shell `grep` (`pi-uu-grep 0.2.0`) return **0 matches with
  rc=1, silently**; `/usr/bin/grep` and `-F` return the truth.
- `$?` after a pipe is the pipeline's status.
- `git log -S` skips merges by default; its zero on a merge is structurally guaranteed.
- `git log --date=iso` prints the stored offset, not UTC.

NO-CLAIM: a green workspace proves the suites pass on THIS machine under the pinned nightly. It does
not prove CI passes — the toolchain fix (`rust-toolchain.toml`) is committed locally and has never
been pushed, so its 67-run failure record is untested against the fix. Green here plus a pushed
green run are two separate claims.

title: P0: dispatch alignment is not retrospectively decidable -- the ledger records no bead status at send time, and the tick row has no verdict field
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-06 by pane 1, answering Joshua's directive that dispatch be measured, observable and tunable. I built the alignment check, ran it over every send tonight, and it FAILED TO BE DECIDABLE. That failure is the finding.

WHAT I RAN. Four predicates over 18 distinct sends (deduplicated as (bead, tick)) since 16:19Z, from the heartbeat ledger joined against the tracker:
  CLM  bead was claimed before dispatch          (OC-L2, orchestration_contract.md:39-43)
  ACC  bead carries acceptance                   (packet builder refuses without it -- observed live at tick 8)
  TRM  bead was not terminal at send             (q8zl)
  FLD  bead is not a filed-only record           (vxr6)

RESULT: 11 clean, 7 misaligned, 0 unknown. POSITIVE CONTROL passes -- some sends are clean, and the predicates demonstrably fail on others, so neither arm is a broken probe.

THE PROBLEM: SIX OF THE SEVEN ARE UNDECIDABLE, NOT VIOLATIONS. The predicates read the bead's CURRENT status, because that is the only status the system stores. y6yg shows blocked at ticks 11/14/15/16 -- but I parked it at 16:58:10, AFTER ticks 11, 14 and 15. pccb shows blocked because I parked it too. So 'misaligned' here conflates 'was wrong at send' with 'became terminal later', and only two sends are provably at-send violations:
  y6yg tick 16   parked 16:58:10.663 -> DISPATCHED 16:58:13   (+3s, proven by ts_unix)
  ibpa.11 tick 10 closed 16:43:39.130 -> DISPATCHED 16:43:44   (+5s)
Both are q8zl, and both required me to hand-join two timestamp sources to establish.

ROOT CAUSE, TWO MISSING FIELDS.
1. The heartbeat dispatch row records bead, pane, tick, receiver and ts_unix -- but NOT the bead's status, assignee, or acceptance-presence AT THE MOMENT OF THE SEND. So alignment can only be checked LIVE, inside the tick that sends. After the fact it is undecidable by construction.
2. The tick row in .flywheel/orchestration-ticks.jsonl carries exactly nine fields -- claims, destructive, dispatched, landed, not_done, observed, refused, tick, ts -- and NONE of verdict, mode, or grade. Measured over all 506 rows. So there is no field in which a per-tick pass/fail could be recorded even if it were computed.

WHY THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT GAP, not a nice-to-have. Every dispatch defect found tonight had to be established by hand-joining the heartbeat ledger, the tracker, tmux, and my own shell history: the 36% re-offer rate, the two q8zl reproductions, the 20 un-dispatchable beads at the queue front, the 31 dead-pid claims. Each took minutes and several produced a wrong first answer from an instrument fault. NONE of it was queryable. A dispatch process that cannot answer 'was this send aligned' from its own records is not observable, and what is not observable cannot be tuned.

AND TUNABLE FAILS SEPARATELY. Every dispatch timing parameter is a compile-time constant: DEFAULT_INTERVAL 90s (main.rs:73), DEFAULT_COMMAND_TIMEOUT 30s (:74), RECEIPT_TIMEOUT (:105), RECEIPT_POLL 250ms (:107), PENDING_DISPATCH_MAX_AGE_SECS 600 (:3024), MAIL_REQUEST_TIMEOUT 10s (:4052). Eleven OMP_* env vars exist and NOT ONE is a policy knob -- they are binary paths and identity (OMP_BR_BIN, OMP_BV_BIN, OMP_NTM_BIN, OMP_SESSION, OMP_EXCLUDE_PANES, OMP_RECEIVER_AGENT, OMP_REAP_SWEEP, OMP_TICK_MONITOR_BIN, OMP_REAP_FINISHED_PANES_BIN, AGENT_MAIL_AGENT, TMUX_PANE). Tuning a deadline therefore requires a rebuild plus a supervisor restart, and tonight a restart cost a fleet-wide starvation event. Two concrete costs measured: PENDING_DISPATCH_MAX_AGE_SECS=600 held %7 for the full 600s on a stale marker, and DEFAULT_COMMAND_TIMEOUT=30s cannot be raised to discriminate the 95s foreign-sqlite stall in b5e5.

NO-CLAIM. Measured: the four predicates over 18 sends with both control arms, the 506-row nine-field census, the six hardcoded constants with line numbers, the eleven env vars, and both q8zl timestamp pairs. NOT measured: whether at-send status belongs on the dispatch row or in a separate append-only alignment ledger -- a design choice I am deliberately leaving open. NOT measured: whether the FLD failures on kvw6 and vxr6 are genuine; vxr6 is a known 1%-rate quotation false positive in my own regex (it quotes the phrase it searches for), and I did not adjudicate kvw6.
acceptance_criteria:
Make alignment decidable from records alone, then prove it.
1. AT-SEND CAPTURE: every dispatch row must record the bead's status, assignee, and acceptance-presence as observed at send time. Prove it by dispatching one bead and reading those fields back out of the ledger without touching the tracker.
2. DECIDABILITY: re-run the four-predicate check (CLM/ACC/TRM/FLD) over a window of sends using ONLY ledger records -- no tracker join, no shell history. Expect every send classified PASS, FAIL or UNKNOWN with no category collapse. The known-bad case is the one measured here: a bead parked AFTER a send must classify that send PASS, not FAIL. That leg must FAIL if at-send capture is removed.
3. VERDICT FIELD: the tick row must carry a typed verdict. Use the enum this fleet already answers to -- OBSERVED_PASS / OBSERVED_FAIL / BLOCKED / UNMEASURED / SIMULATION (wwjd docs/planning/next-leg/PLAN.md:80) -- and enforce 'missing evidence never promotes': UNMEASURED must never satisfy a gate. BLOCKED must be transparent to any failure streak, neither incrementing nor resetting it (loop-enforcement skill). Enforcement belongs in orchestration-tick-gate, in Rust -- this repo forbids .sh and .py, so the upstream bash choke-point must be compiled, not copied.
4. TUNABILITY: at least the six named constants must be runtime-configurable through the existing config.toml the supervisor already reads, with the compiled value logged at startup so a reader can tell which value is live. Known-good leg: an absent or malformed config must fall back to the current defaults and SAY SO, never fail closed silently.
POSITIVE CONTROL (mandatory): the decidability check must classify at least one send PASS and at least one FAIL. An all-PASS or all-FAIL result indicates a broken predicate -- both were observed while building this (18-of-18 FAIL from br list hiding closed beads).
ANTI-VACUITY: an empty send window is an ERROR, never a pass.
Not closable by its implementer; the close reason must name the grading pane.

comments.author: pane1-omp-claude
comments.text:
RIGOR-ATLAS PRESCRIPTION, KNOW-grade, by pane 1, 2026-09-06. Joshua asked for the best long-term solution, rigorously validated. I applied /rigor-atlas (139 repos, 1497 techniques) and verified the exemplar in the pinned mirror rather than trusting the card. This is not a design I invented; it is one Jeffrey already shipped in Rust.

CLASSIFY. This crate family is process-kernel (primary), with runtime-kernel and scheduler-kernel secondary.

INVARIANT, one falsifiable sentence: no dispatch effect may be applied against state observed before the effect's own admission check.

PRESCRIPTIONS, both epistemic KNOW:
  1. incarnation-lease-fencing -- 'Non-reusable incarnation + a monotone lease re-checked immediately before effect'. kinds: process-kernel, runtime-kernel, scheduler-kernel, storage-kernel. Scientist: MARTIN KLEPPMANN. Evidence repos: frankenterm, remote_compilation_helper.
  2. serialize-the-check-then-act-boundary -- 'The predicate is not the guarantee: the transaction boundary and the write barrier are'. Scientists: JIM GRAY, EDSGER DIJKSTRA. Evidence repos: mcp_agent_mail, mcp_agent_mail_rust.

WHY IT IS EXACTLY OUR DEFECT. I opened the exemplar at /Volumes/ZestData/dicklesworthstone-mirror/frankenterm/crates/frankenterm-core/src/capture_authority.rs (2337 lines) and its module doc, lines 1-6, is our bug verbatim: 'Numeric pane IDs are reusable. A queue item identified by only a pane ID can therefore outlive the pane instance that produced it and mutate state belonging to a successor. This module provides the non-reusable identity and drain protocol used to fence that ABA hazard.' That single paragraph covers q8zl (a queued send outliving the queue state it was selected against), the 31 beads held by 16 dead supervisor pids, and %9's 47 stale holds after the restart.

THE KERNEL SHAPE, read at capture_authority.rs:359-397. try_acquire_with_hook checks the lease at :375, increments the in-flight counter at :380, then RE-CHECKS THE LEASE AT :391 and drops the guard if it moved. Two checks, not one, with the effect between them. The typed refusal is CaptureAuthorityError::LeaseNotAdmitting { stage } -- an enum arm, never a boolean. Supporting types: PaneIncarnation(NonZeroU64) at :42, SourceEpoch at :54, CaptureRevision at :70, CaptureViewEpoch at :95, lease advanced only by compare_exchange (:428, :469, :483, :599, :617) with Ordering::SeqCst.

AND IT SHIPS ITS OWN FALSIFIER SEAM. Lines 387-389: 'Deterministic tests use this seam to revoke between the increment and the mandatory recheck. The guard already exists so a panicking hook still releases its increment during unwinding.' The after_increment hook exists SO A TEST CAN REVOKE MID-WINDOW. That is the mutation leg built into the production type -- exactly what this repo demands of every gate, and the reason the recheck is provably attributable rather than decorative.

WHAT WE ALREADY HAVE VS WHAT IS MISSING. fw20 landed PaneIncarnation(NonZeroU64) in this repo, so the identity newtype exists. What does not exist: the three-valued lease (Admitting -> Draining -> Revoked), the compare_exchange advance, and the re-check immediately before the effect. The card's own words: 'The check goes immediately before the effect, not at enqueue.' Our send path checks at enqueue only.

RESULT CLASS WE MAY CLAIM after implementing: ABA-safe dispatch identity over reusable pane ids, and exactly-one-owner-per-incarnation. DO NOT CLAIM: that a fenced dispatch is a delivered dispatch, or that incarnation fencing says anything about whether the WORK was done -- those remain the receiver-receipt and grading concerns respectively.

NO-CLAIM on this comment: I verified the file exists, its line count, the module doc verbatim, the two lease checks at :375/:391, the typed error arm, and the compare_exchange sites. I did NOT run frankenterm's tests, did not read the drain protocol beyond the acquire path, and did not measure whether its shape ports cleanly to a cross-PROCESS fence -- capture_authority is in-process with atomics, while our supervisor fences across restarts, which needs the durable-fence-record variant the card names separately ('the durable fence record written BEFORE ownership transfers').

comments.author: pane1-omp-claude
comments.text:
IDLE CAPACITY ROOT CAUSE, measured end-to-end at t219/t220, 2026-09-06 by pane 1. Joshua asked why two of three workers sat idle and why rebuild+restart is destructive. Both have the SAME answer.

THE CHAIN, every link measured from the loop's own rows:
  a dispatch is sent -> the ACK read-back census runs and reports ACK_CENSUS_EMPTY
  -> the dispatch intent is never confirmed -> the pending-dispatch marker never clears
  -> the pane is WITHHELD until the marker ages out -> dispatchable=0
  -> IDLE_UNAUTHORIZED dispatchable=0 ready=234, FINDING_OBSERVED key=idle-incident seen=106

EVIDENCE:
  t220  DISPATCH_INTENT_EXPIRED age_secs=646 max_age_secs=600 pane=%7
  %9 pending-dispatch.9 marker still live at 520s of a 600s ceiling
  fleet: %6 WORKING, %8 WORKING, %7 IDLE, %9 IDLE -- and the loop computes dispatchable=0
  t219/t220 SUPERVISED_WORKING working=2 ready=234
  free_capacity appears 0 times in the last 200 heartbeat rows

SO EVERY UNCONFIRMED DISPATCH COSTS UP TO 600 SECONDS OF PANE CAPACITY. That is the mechanism behind tonight's idleness, and it is not a manual-dispatch problem: the system detects it correctly and self-heals on a 600s timer.

THE SUPPRESSION IS THE SHARPER DEFECT. key=idle-incident seen=106 with FINDING_THRESHOLD=3 means finding_for returned Owed exactly ONCE, at seen=3, and has returned NotYet::AlreadyEmitted for the other 103 observations. A condition that PERSISTS is therefore reported once and then silent forever. AlreadyEmitted is correct for a RECURRING condition (do not file 106 beads) and wrong for a PERSISTING one (nobody is told it is still true). The lattice needs a third arm -- still-true-and-unacted -- or the bead needs a comment per N observations rather than silence.

WHY OC-L1 CANNOT CATCH IT: orchestration_contract.md OC-L1 says 'a tick that observes free_capacity non-empty and neither dispatches nor records a per-pane refusal reason is INVALID'. free_capacity is emitted ZERO times in the last 200 rows, so the law has nothing to key on. The tick emits SUPERVISED_WORKING working=2 and never names the two free panes.

AND THE RESTART ANSWER IS THE SAME FIX. /rigor-atlas incarnation-lease-fencing (KNOW, Martin Kleppmann) gives the kernel shape: admit(effect, incarnation) -> Result<(), StaleIncarnation> -- compare the presented incarnation against the slot's current one, load the lease SeqCst, refuse otherwise, with the durable fence record written BEFORE ownership transfers. Applied here, a restart mints a NEW incarnation and every predecessor marker and in-flight ledger row is refused AT ADMISSION with a typed StaleIncarnation instead of lingering. That removes the 600s withholding AND makes restart non-destructive, because the predecessor's state is fenced rather than inherited. It is the identical mechanism that would have prevented %9's 47 stale holds and the 31 dead-pid claims.
  The card's own ANTI-PATTERN warns against the shortcut: 'Do not treat a numeric id plus a generation COUNTER as equivalent to a non-reusable identity unless the counter is monotone and checked at the effect site; frankenterm's whole ABA defence is that the check is re-done immediately before effect, not cached from enqueue time.'
  Its stated LIMIT, which I am carrying forward rather than hiding: frankenterm's typestate 'does NOT prove guardian-SIGKILL continuity', and 'fencing a delegated capability is impossible after the fact'. So fencing makes a restart SAFE for state we own; it says nothing about a SIGKILLed predecessor mid-effect.

RECORDED AS A COMMENT, not a new bead, per FC-L7 (finding_contract.md 689277e): first sighting of a condition accrues to the bead that owns its family. The missing free_capacity field is this bead's own subject -- the tick row lacking the state needed to decide alignment.

NO-CLAIM: measured the two cycles' full row sets, both marker ages, the 646s expiry, seen=106 against FINDING_THRESHOLD=3, the zero free_capacity occurrences, and that the ACK instruction IS present in the installed binary (count 1, positive control 2) so the sender half is not the defect. NOT measured: WHY the read-back census is empty at send time -- whether it runs before a worker can plausibly answer, or workers are not answering at all. ACK comments DO exist on older beads (y6yg, ibpa.11), so the protocol works at least sometimes; I did not determine the timing window.

title: Dispatch refuses a packet naming an unclaimed bead — enforce the middle beat in code
description:
WHAT: the dispatch path must REFUSE to send a packet naming a bead that is not `in_progress` and assigned to the receiving agent. File -> CLAIM -> dispatch, with the middle beat enforced by the code rather than remembered by the conductor.

WHY, measured 2026-08-31: `5rh` was dispatched to %1413 and never claimed. The bead sat `open`, `assignee: none`, ZERO comments, while a worker was actively carrying it. Silent in both directions -- the pane read as idle-with-no-assignment, and the queue read as still having ready work nobody had taken.

THE PART THAT MAKES THIS P0 RATHER THAN BOOKKEEPING: it defeats the follow-up detector we shipped today. `classify_followup` keys on (assigned + in_progress + no comment since dispatch). An unclaimed dispatch produces NO SIGNAL AT ALL -- the stage built to catch dispatched-then-silent is structurally blind to a dispatch that never became tracker state. The bead's status is a PROJECTION of the dispatch; when the projection is never written, the watcher watches an empty slot. That is the same shape as every other failure catalogued today: a mechanism that is correct and looking in a place where the event does not arrive.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD: attempt a dispatch naming a bead that is `open`/unassigned -> REFUSED, with the bead id and its actual status in the refusal text. A refusal that does not name the bead sends the caller hunting.
2. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD, second form: attempt a dispatch naming a bead assigned to a DIFFERENT agent -> REFUSED. Two panes working one bead is the duplicate-work failure, and it nearly happened today when `br ready` offered a bead an agent had been building for 14 minutes while the tracker still read `unclaimed`.
3. KNOWN-GOOD, mandatory: a correctly filed-claimed-dispatched packet passes untouched. A refuse-only gate is over-strict, gets routed around, and dies slower than no gate.
4. THE REFUSAL MUST BE ACTIONABLE, not just typed: name the exact `br update <id> --assignee <agent> --status in_progress` that would satisfy it. Measured today -- a supervisor emitted `DISPATCH_RETRY_BLOCKED owner=josh next_action=inspect-or-clear-pending-dispatch` 29 times and it worked precisely because it named the owner and the action.
5. ANTI-VACUITY: a dispatch with no bead id is an ERROR, never an unchecked pass. Broadcasts and corrections are a DIFFERENT operation and must be named as such rather than slipping through as bead-less dispatches.
6. MUTATION: remove the status check; leg 1 goes RED. Restore byte-identically, report the sha both sides.

NO-CLAIM: claiming makes work VISIBLE, not DONE. A claimed bead with a silent pane is still a silent pane -- this closes the blind spot in the detector, not the silence itself. And `open`+unassigned is NOT by itself evidence of a skipped claim: it may simply be unstarted work. The discriminating signal is DISPATCHED-and-unclaimed, which means the DISPATCH LEDGER is the authority here, not the bead. A gate reading only bead status can prove the claim exists; only the ledger can prove a dispatch happened without one.

The crate's own header already carries the honest verdict, at `lib.rs:25-27`: the subprocess

this one line to the wave's ordering principle: *"That is the product. Everything else is
downstream of it. When you are choosing between two tasks, pick the one that gets the loop closer
to dispatching."* Four panes are prioritising against **"the actuator is missing"** when the
measured state is **"the actuator exists and is unproven."** Those are different tasks: one is
writing a dispatch path, the other is running the one that is there and reading its receipt. The
second is cheap and was never attempted; the first is the work the wave has been ordering itself
around.

The table's own vocabulary is what makes this a defect rather than a shorthand. Its seven rows
already distinguish existence from proof — `UNVERIFIED` twice, `FENCED`, `AVAILABLE, NOT WIRED` —

Whether the dispatch path is *correct*. This bead says the plan misdescribes it and that the gap
is verification. Proving the actuator delivers is milestone M3's job; this bead's job is to stop
the fleet from ordering work against a false absence.

Source existing and being called is not delivery. `AGENTS.md` is explicit that a sender's success
is not a receiver's receipt, and `cp-z42vu` recorded a send returning `success` while the packet
never arrived. Reclassifying the cell raises honesty, not capability; it may well turn out the
actuator has never successfully delivered once, which is exactly the measurement this unblocks.

title: P0: dispatch is not forecastable -- no per-tick queue snapshot exists, so forecast-vs-actual and --why are both unanswerable
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-06 by pane 1, answering Joshua directly: 'if we can't see the next 10 or 20 moves before they happen, this system is failing us.' It cannot, and here is exactly why.

WHAT I TRIED. I reconstructed the selector's pipeline by hand -- br ready order (justified: QUEUE_RANK_FALLBACK reports priority_source=br_ready on 226 of 226 rows this build, and PRIORITY_FALLBACK is the only window value across all 311 rows ever recorded) minus the two filters measured firing tonight (empty acceptance -> packet refused, observed live at tick 8 on x1un; filed-only record -> should refuse, vxr6). Result: ready depth 239, predicted-eligible 223, predicted-refused 16. I preregistered the top 10 and the first 5 predicted refusals to a timestamped artifact so the next real sends can falsify it. Status: PENDING -- zero sends since 17:44:47Z. Not passed, not failed.

WHAT CANNOT BE DONE AT ALL: RETROSPECTIVE VALIDATION. I first tried to score the forecast against tonight's 13 distinct sends and got 0 of 13 present in br ready -- which is MY INSTRUMENT, not the system: a claimed bead LEAVES br ready, so nothing already sent can still be ready. Publishing that zero as 'unpredictable' would have been the nineteenth instrument fault of this session. The real conclusion is narrower and worse: br ready AT TIME T predicts the dispatch at T+1, and NO SNAPSHOT OF br ready AT ANY PAST TICK EXISTS. So forecast accuracy is not measurable backwards, only forwards, one tick at a time.

THE MISSING INPUTS, measured:
  per-tick queue snapshot (ready order at that tick): 0 of 506 tick rows carry one
  per-tick filter decisions (which predicate refused which bead): NOT RECORDED anywhere
  at-send bead state (status/assignee/acceptance as observed at send): NOT RECORDED (see 9y8d)
  tick row fields, all 506 rows: claims destructive dispatched landed not_done observed refused tick ts
    -- no verdict, no mode, no grade, no queue

SO A --why IS UNANSWERABLE BY CONSTRUCTION. To explain 'why was X dispatched instead of Y at tick N' you need the ready order at tick N and the filter verdicts at tick N. Neither is stored. Every dispatch defect found tonight -- the 36% re-offer rate, the two q8zl reproductions, the 20 un-dispatchable beads at the queue front, the 31 dead-pid claims -- was established by hand-joining the heartbeat ledger, the tracker, tmux and shell history, several times producing a wrong first answer from an instrument fault. None of it was queryable, and none of it is reproducible by anyone else.

WHAT THE THREE WORKERS ARE DOING RIGHT NOW, for the record: %7 vxr6 (my filing), %8 b4iv (my filing), %9 smcq. Three of five in-flight beads are pane1-authored, so I cannot grade them -- cross-grade assignment was issued (%8 grades vxr6, %9 grades b4iv, %7 grades q8zl) and recorded on each bead, because all four panes share assignee=WildStone and name-based non-author checking is impossible today.

RIGOR GROUNDING, KNOW-grade via /rigor-atlas: this is the audit-kernel prescription 'receipts-as-typed-objects-with-binds-tables' plus control-kernel 'non-regressing-time-and-causal-order'. The canonical CLI shape for the surface is the ZestStream triad -- forecast/diff/why alongside doctor/health/repair. The one rule forbids .sh and .py, so this is a CRATE, not a script.

NO-CLAIM. Measured: the 226/226 fallback census, ready depth 239 and the 223/16 split, the preregistered artifact, the 0-of-506 snapshot census, the nine tick-row fields, and the three pane assignments. NOT measured: whether br ready order is the ACTUAL selector order -- I inferred it from the fallback rows and have NOT read loop_queue_filter::select's ordering code, so my forecast rests on an inference and the prospective test is the only thing that can confirm it. NOT measured: whether the forecast would have been accurate at any past tick; that is permanently unrecoverable without snapshots.
acceptance_criteria:
Deliver a native crate exposing the ZestStream triad; every leg needs both arms.
1. forecast -- emit the next N predicted dispatches IN ORDER with, per bead, the rank and every filter verdict that applied. Expect the output to name its ordering SOURCE (bv recommendations vs br_ready fallback) so a reader can tell which regime produced it.
2. diff -- score a stored forecast against what actually dispatched, classifying each send HIT / MISS / FALSE-NEGATIVE (predicted refusal that dispatched anyway) / PENDING. PENDING must be a distinct outcome: a forecast with no sends yet is NOT a pass. The known-bad case measured here is the trap: a bead that LEFT br ready because it was claimed must classify as HIT-then-consumed, never as MISS -- that error produced a 0-of-13 false reading while building this.
3. why <bead> [--tick N] -- explain inclusion or exclusion at a specific tick, citing the queue snapshot and filter verdicts stored FOR THAT TICK. A why that reads current state instead of tick-N state must be a typed refusal, not an answer.
STORAGE PREREQUISITE: each tick must persist its ready order and filter verdicts. Prove it by answering a why for a tick that has already passed.
POSITIVE CONTROL (mandatory): diff must produce at least one HIT and at least one MISS on real data. All-HIT or all-MISS indicates a broken predicate -- both failure shapes were observed while building this.
ANTI-VACUITY: an empty forecast, an empty send window, or a missing snapshot is an ERROR, never a pass.
MUTATION: remove the per-tick snapshot and assert why goes RED with a typed missing-snapshot error rather than silently answering from current state. Restore byte-identically and checksum both sides.
Not closable by its implementer; the close reason must name the grading pane.

WHY THE 71 P0s ARE NOT IN THE FORECAST, measured while scoring: br ready is 237 rows with priority census P1=187, P2=39, P3=11 and P0=0, while the tracker holds 71 OPEN P0 beads. All 71 are dependency-blocked -- proven by attempting the claim and reading the refusal rather than inferring: n2gd blocked by 9y8d (my own edge), xm7m blocked by mail-authorities-d..., and a serial chain gate-s6-ibps -> gate-s7-y3lw -> gate-s8-t9m4 -> gate-s9-ihl9. WHAT THE OLD MODEL EARNED, and why it still matters: preregistered at 17:44:47Z, it hit ranks 1,2,3,4 in exact ASCENDING order (t48 plan-02-lwdo.2, t50 plan-06-xm0n.1, t52 plan-06-xm0n.2, t54 plan-00-04at.8), precision 4/5 = 80%.   main.rs:4934  bv --robot-triage
  main.rs:4939  bv --robot-insights          <- the rank source
  main.rs:4950  select_dispatch_order_with_pagerank(triage, ready_ids, insights, jsonl, receiver)

title: Three dispatch renderers stage packets with no sender identity; 19 of 37 sites unidentified
description:
## WHAT

Three dispatch packet renderers stage a packet with NO sender identity, so a receiving pane learns
only the index it was sent to. Measured by `crates/no-shell-gate/tests/sender_identity.rs`, which
landed with this bead's sibling work and now refuses any new unidentified site.

The gate's own census, produced by the SAME `scan()` function leg 1 uses (not a grep handed to it):

| crate | dispatch sites | identity present |
|---|---:|---|
| `crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs` | 7 | **NO** |
| `crates/omp-idle-dispatch/src/main.rs` | 2 | **NO** |
| `crates/refill-idle-panes/src/main.rs` | 2 | **NO** |
| `crates/fast-dispatch/src/main.rs` | 6 | yes |
| `crates/loop-tick/src/lib.rs` | 6 | yes |
| `crates/tick-dispatch/src/main.rs` | 6 | yes |
| `crates/kernel-only-operator-hook/src/lib.rs` | 8 | n/a — allowanced, see below |

Totals: 56 tracked crates, 129 source files scanned, **37 dispatch sites in 7 files, 19 of them
unidentified across 3 renderers**.

`kernel-only-operator-hook` is allowanced with a reason and is NOT part of this fix: it
pattern-matches the `--robot-send` argv to allow or deny a Bash event and constructs no packet, so
there is no packet for a FROM line to live in. Its 8 hits are the allowlist entry and its unit
fixtures.

## WHY

Operator directive, verbatim: *"make sure you all announce who you are when sending a message so a
pane can properly contact you back."*

The measured failure: every packet sent during the 2026-09-01/02 session went out as
`ntm send omp-orchestrator --panes=N` with no FROM line. `ntm send` names a session and an INDEX,
and **pane indices are not stable handles** — they shifted twice in one night. Two panes changed
MODEL mid-session (`%1408` GLM 5.3 -> Opus 5, `%1409` GLM 5.3 -> GPT-5.6-Luna) while their agent
NAMES held. So agent names are the durable handle and indices are not, and `WAVE.md`'s roster went
stale listing pane2=%1408 while live tmux said %1413. Three agents replied to the orchestrator only
because they happened to know it was pane 1.

Two traps that make a hand-written FROM line wrong, both measured, both of which the fix must avoid:

1. `tmux display-message -p '#{pane_id}'` answers for the **ACTIVE** pane, not the calling one.
   From pane 4 it returns `%1396 index=0`; with `-t "$TMUX_PANE"` it returns the truth,
   `pane_index=4 pane_id=%1408`. A renderer that builds its own FROM line with the unqualified form
   announces WHOEVER IS FOCUSED. Note the nasty part: it is INVISIBLE from the focused pane — run
   from pane 1 both forms agree, so the bug cannot be reproduced from where an orchestrator sits.
2. `register_agent`'s `pane_id` argument is silently DISCARDED — `whois` returns no `pane_id`
   field, and the success envelope omits it too. The pane binding lives in a per-pane identity FILE
   and has a kernel: `resolve_pane_identity {project_key, pane_id?}` reads
   `~/.config/agent-mail/identity/<project_hash>/<pane_id>` with two legacy fallbacks and a GH#252
   liveness predicate. Measured for AmberGate: `{"agent_name":"AmberGate","pane_id":"%1408",
   "binding":"legacy-unverified"}`. Use that kernel; do not add a second source of pane truth.

## ACCEPTANCE

`run X, expect Y`, per renderer:

1. Each of the three renderers stages a packet whose first two lines are a FROM line naming the
   sending AGENT NAME plus its pane index AND pane_id, and a REPLY-VIA line naming both routes
   (`ntm --robot-send=<session> --panes=<index> --msg-file <path>` and Agent Mail to the agent
   name). Agent name first, because it is the handle that held all session.
2. `cargo test -p no-shell-gate --test sender_identity` stays GREEN and the allowance shrinks from
   4 rows to 1 (`kernel-only-operator-hook` only). The gate FAILS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: a row naming
   a crate that now complies is an error, so the rows must be DELETED in the same commit as each
   fix. That asymmetry is the point — the list can only shrink.
3. The pane_id in the rendered FROM line comes from `resolve_pane_identity` or from
   `tmux display-message -t "$TMUX_PANE"`, never from an unqualified `display-message`. Assert it
   with a leg that feeds a multi-session `tmux list-panes -a` fixture and requires the CALLER's
   pane, with a negative control where the active pane differs from the caller's.
4. State in the commit which verdicts/paths still send unidentified packets, if any remain.

## NOT IN SCOPE

- `crates/fast-dispatch`, `crates/loop-tick`, `crates/tick-dispatch` — already identified, and
  another agent holds sender work on those three files.
- `crates/kernel-only-operator-hook` — allowanced with a reason; it renders no packet.
- Enforcing identity on the RECEIVING side. A FROM line makes a reply addressable; it does not
  prove the reply arrived.

## NO-CLAIM

A FROM line makes a packet ATTRIBUTABLE, not delivered. It does not fix
`RECEIVER_RECEIPT=ntm_robot_send` recording that a send RETURNED rather than arrived, and it does
not make pane indices stable — it makes them unnecessary, by carrying the durable handle beside
them. The gate proves a from-marker is PRESENT in the file that dispatches; it cannot prove the
rendered value is CORRECT, which is why acceptance 3 pins the resolution source rather than the
string.

title: byte-exact dispatch journey mapping: S1-S9 stage to contract to kernel symbol, with the comms/mail hole named
description:
## WHAT

Author `docs/contracts/dispatch_journey_mapping_contract.md`: the byte-exact mapping layer
between the canonical S1-S9 journey (`docs/plan/12-journey.md`), the evidence map
(`docs/plan/11-lifecycle.md`), the 20 contracts in `docs/contracts/`, and the kernel symbols
that actually implement each stage. One row per operational stage:

  stage | parent S-stage | GOAL | governing contract | kernel crate | exact symbol/command | measured gap

Stages walked: observe, select, claim, dispatch, ack, receipt, verify, close, comms/mail.

Every stage GOAL is backed by >= 2 independent primary sources (arXiv abstracts read directly,
source + fetch-date cited). A single-source claim is labelled phantom doctrine inline.

## WHY

`docs/plan/12-journey.md` owns the dispatchable runbook (S1-S9, seven-field contract) and
`docs/plan/11-lifecycle.md` owns the evidence map (11.1 stage/crate ownership). Neither names a
single `docs/contracts/` file per stage, and neither names a callable symbol. The result is that
three separate stage vocabularies exist in one workspace with no bridge:

  loop_coverage::LoopLayer                    crates/loop-coverage/src/lib.rs:78            (10 members)
  tick_monitor::lifecycle::Stage              crates/tick-monitor/src/lifecycle.rs:35        (9 members)
  bead_lifecycle::model::LifecycleStatus      crates/ntm-fleet-monitor/src/bead_lifecycle/model.rs:75 (10 members)

Measured three-way intersection of their stable string labels: EMPTY. LoopLayer vs
lifecycle::Stage share ZERO labels. No enum has an `ack` member, a `receipt` member, or a
`mail`/`comms` member.

The comms/mail leg is the largest hole: `grep -ncE 'agent mail|agent-mail|inbox|mail_pending|robot-wait'
docs/plan/11-lifecycle.md` = 0, and repo-wide only two crate files mention Agent Mail at all,
both in comments/strings, never as a call. Meanwhile the kernel primitives are installed and live.

This bead is the MAPPING layer only. It does not author a rival spine; 12-journey.md remains
canonical and this document says so in its first paragraph.

1. `test -f docs/contracts/dispatch_journey_mapping_contract.md`
2. `wc -c docs/contracts/dispatch_journey_mapping_contract.md` -> under 25000 bytes.
3. House shape present: a `Bead:` line and all of

5. Every kernel claim in the mapping table resolves: for each named
   `crates/<crate>/src/<file>:<line>` anchor, the file exists in `git ls-tree -r HEAD` and the
   named symbol appears in it. A stage with NO implementing kernel states that explicitly
   rather than naming a plausible crate.
6. `## Non-Coverage` names the stages with weak or zero contract coverage by name and does not
   paper over them.
7. Every external/research claim carries >= 2 arXiv IDs with fetch-date, or is explicitly
   labelled single-source phantom doctrine.

## NON-GOALS

- Does not rewrite `docs/plan/12-journey.md` or `docs/plan/11-lifecycle.md`.
- Does not rewrite any of the 20 existing contracts in `docs/contracts/`.
- Does not touch `crates/`.

title: Dispatch preflight: the four questions every dispatch must answer, plus the twelve escape routes agents invented in one measured session
description:
JOSHUA 2026-09-03, standing instruction attached to every dispatch: 'how would this dispatch work through our system - what needs to be true for dispatching to reliably work properly through the various phases? if we automate any of this - what makes it work? And how do agents not get side tracked away from the substrate driven architecture? what bypasses or escape routes will agents make up along the way'.

Landed as docs/contracts/dispatch_preflight.md (11,860 B). Four sections, 40+ stable DP-* ids.

D1 -- the ten-stage flow FILE -> CLAIM -> PACKET -> ADMISSION -> SEND -> RECEIPT -> ACK -> OBSERVE -> VERIFY -> RECORD, each mapped to the real surface and the refusal that exists for it. TWO STAGES HAVE NO REFUSAL AT ALL: a bead can be filed with no acceptance criteria (measured: a P0 at the head of the ready queue with no ACCEPTANCE made two agents triage it and go idle rather than work it), and a send can report success with nobody having read it (measured: cp-z42vu, success:[4] for a packet that never arrived).

D2 -- ten truth-conditions, six of which are currently enforced only by an orchestrator remembering to check them. The largest measured gap was DP-T4: before the ACK instruction was added to packets this session, ZERO ACK comments existed anywhere in the tracker, so ack-stage rated every delivery Indeterminate. The sender half is a tested Rust crate; the receiver half was a sentence nobody had written.

D3 -- seven automation preconditions, every one open, which is why auto-dispatch stays OFF: journey_key (kukp), a tick ledger that can record an admitted violation (gaq0), one agreed idle oracle (wbu2), admission not fail-closed on a tool we deleted (g04s), role-based conductor exclusion (fqhv P1), a typed DEGRADED lane (fqhv P2), expectation rows (xkr6). Plus DP-A0: automation makes the loop faster, not honest -- all twelve escape routes below were invented UNDER human supervision, and automated they run at machine rate with nobody reading the output, which is the exact shape of the 2026-08-31 six-hour idle post-mortem.

D4 -- twelve escape routes, each with its measured instance and a MECHANICAL detector, because exhortation does not work. Highlights: a contract whose Validation block greps its OWN file for the string that proves its claim; a real refutation filed as prose so the counter cannot see it; a box flipped to converged on a counter while five layers read exists=none; a published figure of 62 rows that a fresh clone measures as 17; 35 rows of review evidence never committed; 19 crates / 46 sites spawning tmux/ntm/br/bv/am directly while the kernels exist; a stale tool satisfying its probe while being the sole red gate; a blocking wait that waited on the calling pane; and the ledger that admitted only a false attestation, a false refusal, a false observation, or no record. FOUR OF THE TWELVE WERE THE ORCHESTRATOR'S OWN.

The pattern worth keeping: every escape route is CHEAPER than the discipline and SHAPED LIKE COMPLIANCE. A self-validating check passes. A counter goes green. A worktree grep produces a confident number. None looks like cheating from the inside, which is why the detector must be mechanical and must run on the artifact rather than on the intent. DP-E13 is a reserved row: a taxonomy that stops growing has stopped being measured.

Also records what slots into S2, per Joshua's parenthetical: exactly ONE thing crosses the boundary -- the Inception envelope at .omp-orchestrator/inception.json (SCHEMAS.toml:156-161) plus a FOUNDATION.jsonl stage=S1 row and a jq readback proving both. It is currently ABSENT on disk. S2 may not read a pane, a tick or a bead to learn what S1 established.

ACCEPTANCE: the Validation block runs and its output is pasted; untracked_wave_evidence reaches 0 (DP-E5 is live at 4 today); and each of the twelve rows either names a gate that exists or is explicitly listed as hand-checked. NO-CLAIM: this is a preflight and a taxonomy, NOT a gate. Ten of the twelve detectors are hand-run or unbuilt; naming a detector is not building one.

title: P1: the selector sends against a queue snapshot read before the send -- a bead closed 5s earlier was still dispatched
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-06 by pane 1 on build 4703b6e8f5.

THE OBSERVATION, to the second, from the heartbeat ledger's own ts_unix field:
  16:43:39.130  pane 1 closed omp-orchestrator-plan-12-ibpa.11 (MUTATION-VERIFIED, non-author grade)
  16:43:44      the loop emitted DISPATCHED tick=10 pane=%7 bead=...ibpa.11

Five seconds AFTER the close. The three earlier dispatches of the same bead were legitimate
(16:22:32 t1, 16:31:07 t4, 16:37:25 t7 -- all before the close, ~3-tick cadence). The fourth was
not: at the moment of the send the bead was `closed`, `closed_at` 16:43:39.130142Z, and absent
from `br ready` -- grep count 0 against a POSITIVE CONTROL of 244 readable rows.

SO IT IS A PREFETCHED SNAPSHOT, NOT A RACE. A race would put the send inside the close's own
window. Five seconds is long past commit -- `br show` and `br ready` both already reported the
new state. The selector read the queue, chose, and sent without re-checking the bead's status at
send time. The check exists at selection but not at the transport boundary.

EFFECT. %7 received a full work packet -- claim + implement + test + ACK -- for work that was
already graded and closed. It cost a dispatch slot and would have cost a whole worker turn had it
obeyed. Pane 1 sent a stand-down note naming the close and its four re-executed legs.

TWO MEASUREMENT TRAPS THIS FINDING WALKED INTO -- both worth keeping
1. TICK NUMBERS RESET ON RESTART AND THE LEDGER DOES NOT SEPARATE RUNS. This build_id
   (4703b6e8f51774) spans ticks 1..220 because the revert restored the SAME binary, so the
   pre-restart and post-restart runs share a build_id while tick restarted at 1. A filter of
   'rows after tick 10' swept in 17 unrelated rows from the earlier run. build_id is NOT a run
   identity. Same class as the 48 historical rows whose incarnation cannot be recovered.
2. FILE APPEND ORDER WAS ALSO INSUFFICIENT -- only 11 rows had been appended since, too few to
   conclude anything. Only `ts_unix` against `closed_at` decided it.
The general rule this repo already records: a figure is meaningless without the era it was taken
from. Here, two eras shared every identifier except the clock.

NO-CLAIM. Measured: both timestamps, the closed status, absence from br ready with a positive
control, and the four dispatch times. NOT measured: WHERE in the send path the staleness lives --
whether the ready set is captured once per cycle at main.rs:4557 and reused across the dispatch
loop, or whether a per-pane fanout reuses one selection. That is a source read I have not done, so
the remedy is unproven. Also NOT measured: how often this fires -- one occurrence, deliberately not
generalised into a rate.
acceptance_criteria: Reproduce with a clock, then defend. REPRODUCE: dispatch a bead, close it from another actor between selection and send, and assert the send is REFUSED rather than transmitted. Cite ts_unix of the close and of the DISPATCHED row -- the send timestamp must be later than the close for the test to be measuring this defect at all (a send inside the close window is a different, benign race and must NOT be claimed as this bug). DEFEND: the transport boundary must re-read the bead's status immediately before sending and emit a typed refusal naming the terminal status; expect that refusal, not a packet. Known-good leg (mandatory): an open, unblocked, acceptance-bearing bead must still dispatch unaffected -- an over-strict re-check that refuses live work is worse than the defect. The refusal leg must FAIL when the re-check is removed. Anti-vacuity: a test that never reaches the send path is an ERROR, never a pass. Not closable by its implementer.

PRESCRIPTION: serialize-the-check-then-act-boundary -- 'The predicate is not the guarantee: the transaction boundary and the write barrier are.' Scientists: Jim Gray, Edsger Dijkstra. Also incarnation-lease-fencing (Martin Kleppmann), whose card states the rule in one line: 'The check goes immediately before the effect, not at enqueue.' That is precisely q8zl -- our selector checks at enqueue and never re-reads before the send.

THE SHAPE TO COPY, verified at /Volumes/ZestData/dicklesworthstone-mirror/frankenterm/crates/frankenterm-core/src/capture_authority.rs:359-397 (file exists, 2337 lines):
  :375  check lease == LEASE_ADMITTING, else Err(LeaseNotAdmitting { stage })
  :380  increment the in-flight counter
  :390  after_increment() -- a deliberate TEST SEAM
  :391  RE-CHECK the lease; if it moved, drop the guard and refuse
Two checks bracketing the effect, a typed enum refusal rather than a boolean, and lease transitions only via compare_exchange with SeqCst.

The falsifier is designed into the production type. Our acceptance already demands a leg that fails when the re-check is removed; upstream provides the seam that makes such a leg deterministic instead of racy. Copy the seam, not just the check.

MEASURED CORRESPONDENCE TO THIS BEAD'S TWO REPRODUCTIONS: case 1 closed ibpa.11 16:43:39.130 -> DISPATCHED 16:43:44 (+5s); case 2 parked y6yg 16:58:10.663 -> DISPATCHED 16:58:13 (+3s).
