title: P0: is_dispatchable=true while liveness=NEWLY_IDLE -- the selector offers a pane the preflight then refuses, and a restart resets the evidence
description: MEASURED 2026-09-06 by pane 1 from a live livelock. TWO SURFACES DISAGREE ABOUT ONE PANE. The selector offers a pane because is_dispatchable is true; the preflight then refuses it because liveness is not CONFIRMED_IDLE. Verbatim, five consecutive ticks: 'DISPATCH_PREFLIGHT_REFUSED bead=<b> pane=%9 verdict=refuse reason=Refused { reason: SingleCaptureLiveness } pane_dispatchable=true two_captures=false packet_complete=true'. THE COUPLING: crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs:1868 computes 'two_captures: pane_observation.is_dispatchable && pane_observation.liveness == "CONFIRMED_IDLE"'. So the preflight demands BOTH, while selection demands only is_dispatchable. When they disagree, every dispatch to that pane is refused while the pane keeps being selected. MEASURED DISAGREEMENT: a long-running observer reports %9 as state=IDLE liveness=CONFIRMED_IDLE and %8 as state=IDLE liveness=NEWLY_IDLE, while the freshly-restarted supervisor read %9 as offering-but-not-confirmed. The cause is that liveness is derived from the OBSERVER'S OWN capture history, and the supervisor keeps a separate state file from the CLI (main.rs:317 passes config.tick_monitor_state). A restarted supervisor therefore holds exactly ONE capture and every pane reads NEWLY_IDLE on tick 1. WHY THIS WAS A LIVELOCK AND NOT A SLOW START: run_supervisor returned Err on the refusal, main exited 1, and the restart policy restarted it -- so the next tick was ALSO tick 1 with ONE capture. THE RESTART DESTROYED THE EVIDENCE THE NEXT ATTEMPT NEEDED. Beads smcq, plan-02-lwdo.2, plan-06-xm0n.1 and plan-06-xm0n.2 were each CLAIMED (assignee=supervisor:NNNNN) and then intent-cleared on successive passes, so the loop churned tracker state while making zero progress, reaching restarts=6 before I stopped it. THE EXIT HALF IS FIXED at c68a70c: a per-tick refusal now writes its row, prints to stderr, and CONTINUES. That converts a restart loop into a visible standing condition. IT DOES NOT FIX THIS BEAD. The disagreement remains, and with the exit fixed the loop will now refuse the same pane every tick forever instead of restarting -- more observable, equally unproductive, and it will still claim-and-clear a bead per tick unless selection and preflight are reconciled. WHICH SIDE IS WRONG IS A REAL DESIGN QUESTION, stated rather than assumed: (a) the SELECTOR should not offer a pane whose liveness is not CONFIRMED_IDLE, so the two predicates become one -- simplest, and it means a freshly restarted loop dispatches nothing until it has two captures, which is CORRECT per the receiver-receipt contract and merely delays the first dispatch by one interval; or (b) the PREFLIGHT's two_captures should read retained window evidence the way omp-orchestrator-dispatchable-window-is-one-shot-u8nw made dispatchable do, so a restart inherits prior captures from the state file instead of starting blind. Option (b) is strictly better if the state file genuinely persists prior observations -- u8nw landed exactly that retention -- and it would mean a restart is not a blindness event at all. I have NOT measured whether the supervisor's state file survives its own restart with usable prior rows, and that measurement decides between (a) and (b). ALSO NOTE: claiming a bead BEFORE the preflight refuses is its own defect -- DISPATCH_CLAIMED preceded DISPATCH_PREFLIGHT_REFUSED in every one of the five ticks, so the tracker recorded four claims for work never sent. Per AGENTS.md's fourth rule the claim is meant to make a dispatch visible; a claim followed immediately by an intent-clear makes it visible and false. The preflight should run BEFORE the claim. ACCEPTANCE: 1. Selection and preflight agree on one predicate, or the selector demonstrably never offers a pane the preflight will refuse. 2. Known-bad: a pane with exactly one capture must still be REFUSED -- the two-capture rule is the receiver-receipt contract and must not be weakened to make this pass. 3. Known-good: a pane with two captures and CONFIRMED_IDLE is dispatched, so the fix is not 'refuse everything'. 4. No bead is CLAIMED before the preflight authorises the dispatch; a claim implies a send. 5. Anti-vacuity: a supervisor with no capture history reports a typed NOT_YET_PROVABLE standing condition, never a silent no-op tick. 6. Mutation: break the reconciled predicate, confirm RED, restore byte-identically with a checksum. 7. Live proof: a restarted supervisor reaches a real dispatch without an intervening refusal, or refuses for exactly one interval and then dispatches. NO-CLAIM: this establishes the disagreement, the coupling site, the livelock mechanism, and that four beads were claim-and-cleared. It does not establish whether the supervisor's state file retains prior captures across a restart -- that is the unmeasured fact that decides the fix -- and it makes no claim that either candidate option is correct.

title: P0: tick-monitor dispatchable is a ONE-SHOT -- it populates on the second capture and empties on the third, so any repeated or single observer sees [] and no refill lane can ever see capacity
description: MEASURED 2026-09-05 by pane 1 immediately after installing the fixed tick-monitor under vgf. THREE CONSECUTIVE OBSERVATIONS with three panes genuinely IDLE and no work dispatched between them: capture1 (discarded, warm-up) then capture2 -> {"dispatchable":["%7","%8","%9"],"count":3,"free_capacity":["%7","%8","%9"]} then capture3, taken seconds later -> {"dispatchable":[],"count":0,"free_capacity":["%7","%8","%9"]}. free_capacity stays correct across all three; DISPATCHABLE POPULATES ON THE SECOND CAPTURE AND EMPTIES ON THE THIRD. The two-capture liveness window is consumed by the observation that satisfies it, so the verdict does not survive the next read. CONSEQUENCE, and it explains the original symptom completely: any caller that observes ONCE sees [] because one capture cannot satisfy the rule, and any caller that observes REPEATEDLY -- which is what a monitor loop does -- sees a nonzero dispatchable at most every other read and [] the rest of the time. So refill-idle-panes, the conductor's own probes, and any scheduled sweep will almost always read zero capacity while panes sit idle. That is the 178-tick and free_capacity_streak=101 blindness in its final form: the number was not merely unread, it was structurally almost always zero. WHY THIS IS NOT THE SAME BEAD AS vgf: vgf's cause was the capacity partition consulting liveness only, so a recognised-idle pane with no prior capture was never counted; that is fixed and verified from the installed binary. This is a separate defect in the SURVIVAL of the verdict rather than its computation. ACCEPTANCE: (1) dispatchable must remain populated while the pane remains idle AND the two-capture evidence remains fresh, rather than being consumed by the read; (2) freshness must be a stated duration with the captures' timestamps, not an implicit one-shot -- AGENTS.md's rule is two captures at least 75s apart comparing timer AND spinner-stripped content hash, so the verdict's validity window is derivable and should be reported alongside it; (3) an observation that cannot yet satisfy the rule must be a TYPED not-yet-provable outcome distinct from 'no capacity', because those two are opposite facts and currently render identically as []; (4) idempotence leg: N consecutive observations with no intervening state change must return the same dispatchable set for all N; (5) known-bad leg: a pane that goes busy between captures must drop OUT of dispatchable. FALSIFIER: observe three times with no dispatch between and confirm all three agree; if capture3 differs from capture2 the defect stands. NO-CLAIM: this establishes non-idempotence across three live captures. It does not establish that the window is too short rather than wrongly consumed, and it does not establish that any refill lane would have dispatched had it seen the capacity.

title: Consume abort / abort_and_prompt / new_session / switch_session for wedge recovery and pane provisioning
description:
WHAT: **Consume `abort` / `abort_and_prompt` / `new_session` / `switch_session` for wedge recovery
and pane provisioning** — replacing the recovery ladder's `tmux send-keys Escape` / kill-and-relaunch
and `reap-finished-panes`' capture heuristics. All four are RETIRE in `SURFACE-MAP.jsonl` on the
grep-only probe; `new_session`/`switch_session`/`abort_and_prompt` have ZERO beads.

WHY: a wedged pane (`Wedged`, `Dialog`, `ProviderError402`) today owes a human because the only
remedies are keystrokes into a TUI; `abort_and_prompt` is exactly "drop the parked packet and send
this one", and `new_session` is the typed form of "reap and refill" that `refill-idle-panes` does by
hand. The supervisor's own restart under launchd loses every worker's session identity — `switch_session`
is how a restarted supervisor re-binds to workers it spawned (topology (a)).

ACCEPTANCE (run X, expect Y):
1. `AckAction::Unstick` on an RPC-owned pane → `abort` (typed response cited); `Redispatched` →
   `abort_and_prompt`; capacity refill → `new_session`; supervisor restart → `switch_session` to the
   recorded session ids (persisted in the ack-spine ledger, never re-derived from tmux titles).
2. Fires-on-known-bad: a parked packet (the `46y7` footer) on an RPC pane is cleared by `abort` and the
   pane reads idle via `get_state` within one cycle; the tmux path is the known divergence.
3. Known-good: `abort` on an idle session is a typed no-op, not an error; capacity accounting unchanged.
4. Restart proof: kill the supervisor, restart, `switch_session` re-binds N of N workers (N cited from
   the ledger); zero re-dispatch of a bead already ACKed (the `zlyy` K3 invariant, fuzzed in `ed52`).
5. Mutation: send Escape via tmux instead of `abort` → leg 2 RED; restore.
NO-CLAIM: topology (a) only; under (b) `switch_session` semantics for foreign sessions are UNMEASURED
(spike `R1`).

title: P0: double-dispatch to one pane -- the pending marker is cleared on dispatch SUCCESS, so it cannot withhold a pane during the acknowledgment window; %7 holds two in_progress beads from ticks 50 and 51
description: MEASURED 2026-09-06 by pane 1 from supervisor logs at ticks 50 and 51, while I was deliberately holding %7 idle for a rebuild -- the loop filled it twice. THE OBSERVATION, verbatim from the process log: 'OBSERVATION tick=50 states=%5=UNPROVEN,%7=IDLE,%8=WORKING,%9=WORKING free_capacity=1 dispatchable=1' then 'DISPATCH_PREFLIGHT verdict=autonomous bead=omp-orchestrator-stage-reparent-census-01jo pane=%7 pane_dispatchable=true two_captures=true packet_complete=true'. Ninety seconds later: 'OBSERVATION tick=51 states=%7=IDLE,%8=WORKING,%9=IDLE free_capacity=2 dispatchable=1' then 'DISPATCH_PREFLIGHT verdict=autonomous bead=omp-orchestrator-unrun-vs-clean-indistinguishable-p2eg pane=%7 pane_dispatchable=true two_captures=true packet_complete=true'. TWO BEADS DISPATCHED TO %7 IN CONSECUTIVE TICKS. Tracker confirms both landed: stage-reparent-census-01jo status=in_progress assignee=WildStone, and unrun-vs-clean-indistinguishable-p2eg status=in_progress assignee=WildStone. THE PANE WAS NOT WEDGED, which I checked before blaming it: no tmux pane anywhere carries the 'Press up to edit queued messages' marker, and %7 subsequently reads WORKING t=60. So it simply took longer than one 90-second tick to transition IDLE to WORKING after receiving the first packet, and during that window it was GENUINELY idle with two stable captures. two_captures=true was CORRECT both times. THE DEFECT IS THE MISSING GUARD, not the observation: the loop has no notion of 'I dispatched to this pane and have not yet seen it acknowledge or go WORKING'. The pending-dispatch marker exists for precisely this -- write_dispatch_intent per pane -- but DISPATCH_INTENT_CLEARED fires in the SAME TICK as a successful dispatch with reason=VERDICT_POSTED, so the marker never survives to withhold the pane on the next tick. Measured earlier tonight: 26 DISPATCH_INTENT_CLEARED rows, and markers pending.7, pending.8, pending.9 all ABSENT while dispatches were in flight. THIS IS THE mgdz MECHANISM ONE LAYER OVER, and that makes three instances of one shape tonight. t7us: a restart reset the two-capture window so the preflight could never accumulate two captures. hx3n: a restart reset the tick counter so every idempotency key collided. mgdz: a FAILED dispatch clears the marker whose timestamp would have filtered a stale ACK. This one: a SUCCESSFUL dispatch clears the marker that would have withheld the pane. In every case the clearing is the thing that breaks the next decision, and here it is the success path rather than the failure path -- which is why it survived the mgdz analysis. AGENTS.md's C112 is the doctrine: an ownership claim must name something that DIES WITH THE THING IT OWNS. The marker dies with the DISPATCH ATTEMPT; the acknowledgment window it needs to guard outlives it. THE COST IS REAL WORK LOSS, not just noise: %7 can only work one bead. The other is claimed in the tracker, assigned, in_progress, and unworked -- invisible as a leak because both rows look healthy. classify_followup keys on assigned + in_progress + no comment since dispatch, so it will eventually see one, but nothing distinguishes 'silent worker' from 'never actually started because the pane was doing something else'. AND IT INFLATES THE UNCONFIRMED BACKLOG: both beads emitted ACK_STAGE_INDETERMINATE with ACK_CENSUS_EMPTY, so a double-dispatch produces two unconfirmed rows from one pane's capacity. That is a plausible contributor to AWAIT_HUMAN standing at 26 against RECORD_RECEIPT at 4, though I have not attributed specific rows. NO-CLAIM: this establishes two consecutive dispatches to one pane with both claims landing, that the pane was idle and unwedged at both observations, that two_captures was correct, and that the intent marker is cleared on success in the same tick. It does NOT establish how many prior double-dispatches occurred -- that census is unrun -- nor that %7 will actually drop one of the two beads; it may work both sequentially. title: P2: pane 1 armed two overlapping inbox-monitor --watch jobs on one agent+project; both settled on the SAME arrival, so one event produced two notifications
description: MEASURED 2026-09-05 by pane 1 against itself. Two background inbox-monitor --watch jobs (bg_5 and bg_16) were armed on the same agent PlumTiger and the same project /Users/josh/Developer/omp-orchestrator, and BOTH settled on the identical arrival: each returned verdict=mail_waiting, unread=1, next_cursor=6062, persisted_cursor=6056, oldest_from=WildStone, oldest_subject='R6B FRESH-EYES: no cycles; Round 4 wrong refuted'. bg_16 settled after 18 polls / 185s and bg_5 after 78 polls / 879s, so the earlier-armed watch was still running when the later one was armed and both consumed the same event. ONE ARRIVAL PRODUCED TWO NOTIFICATIONS. Cause is mine and mechanical: I re-armed the wake after each reap without cancelling the prior arm, on the assumption that a settled watch retires itself; a watch that has not yet fired is still live. THIS IS THE SAME CLASS AS THE tick-monitor LEDGER CONTENDED DEFECT REPAIRED EARLIER IN THIS SESSION, where two watchers on one ledger made 'last_tick' advance on the wrong cadence and silently disabled the two-capture liveness rule -- there the symptom was gap_secs_too_short reported as no error. Here the harm is smaller but the shape is identical: two readers of one cursor stream, where the second reader's settle is indistinguishable from a fresh arrival. CONSEQUENCE TO GUARD: a conductor that treats each settle as a distinct arrival will double-count completions, and the ntm-fleet-monitor lifecycle rules explicitly require that 'duplicate events with the same idempotency key replay the prior result' rather than register as progress -- next_cursor=6062 was identical across both settles and is exactly such a key. FIX: cancel the prior watch before arming a new one, or key notifications on next_cursor so a repeat cursor replays rather than re-notifies. NO-CLAIM: no work was double-dispatched as a result of this instance, because the second settle arrived after the reap it duplicated; that is timing, not a guarantee, and the guard is still missing.
acceptance_criteria:
1. KNOWN-BAD leg (must be reproduced live, not assumed): arm two overlapping `inbox-monitor --watch` jobs on agent PlumTiger + project /Users/josh/Developer/omp-orchestrator (second armed while first is still un-fired), deliver ONE arrival, and show both settle with identical next_cursor=6062 / persisted_cursor=6056 / oldest_from=WildStone. Pre-fix this MUST emit two notifications; the existing bg_5/bg_16 transcript in the description is NOT sufficient evidence — it is a historical narration with no reproducible harness, no cancel-attempt, and no assertion recorded, so it cannot go RED after a regression.

2. KNOWN-GOOD leg: two watches armed on DIFFERENT (agent, project) pairs, or on the same pair but separated by an intervening distinct arrival (next_cursor 6062 then 6070), must both notify normally. The fix must not collapse legitimately distinct arrivals or suppress a second agent's watch; assert exactly 2 notifications in each of these cases.

3. Second KNOWN-GOOD leg: a single watch armed, fired, reaped, and then re-armed AFTER the prior arm is confirmed retired must notify on the next arrival. Fix must not leave the agent permanently un-watched (silent-starvation failure mode is worse than double-notify).

4. Anti-vacuity: the harness must enumerate live watch jobs for the (agent, project) key and assert the discovered set is non-empty and contains ≥2 entries in the bad leg. Zero watches discovered, zero settles observed, or an empty notification log is a typed error (e.g. `WatchScanEmpty`) that FAILS the test — never an implicit pass. Same for the idempotency-key set: an empty set of observed next_cursor values is `CursorSetEmpty`, an error.

5. Mutation test: with the fix in place, revert exactly one of (a) the pre-arm cancel of the prior watch, or (b) the next_cursor idempotency-key dedup, and show the bad leg goes RED (2 notifications for 1 arrival). Record sha256 of the patched file before mutation and after restore; the two checksums must be byte-identical and both printed in the bead close-out.

6. MEASURED-LIVE vs FIXTURE: the overlapping-arm race, the two settles, and the notification count MUST be measured live against a real inbox-monitor process and a real cursor file — timing (18 polls/185s vs 78 polls/879s) may be compressed but the concurrency must be genuine. The mail body/subject and the arrival injection may be a fixture. A fully mocked watch loop does not satisfy item 1.

7. Assert the ntm-fleet-monitor lifecycle rule explicitly: a duplicate event whose idempotency key (next_cursor) matches a previously-notified key must REPLAY the prior result — same payload, marked `replayed=true` — and must not increment any completion/progress counter. Test asserts the conductor's completion count is 1, not 2, after both settles.

8. The description's NO-CLAIM ("no work was double-dispatched … that is timing, not a guarantee") is unmeasured. Either add a test that a double-settle arriving BEFORE the reap does not double-dispatch work, or file a separate bead for conductor-side double-dispatch guarding and cite its ID here. Do not close this bead treating the timing accident as coverage. Likewise, the shared-shape link to the tick-monitor contended-ledger defect must be either verified as already fixed (cite the repair) or filed separately as a shared-abstraction bead.

title: the close readback is policy with no enforcement: a typed refusal becomes a null in every naive reader
description:

Unread}` -- so a fabricated verdict is now unconstructible. **It does not perform the readback**, by

**FILED BECAUSE THE IMPLEMENTER ASKED ME TO NAME THE SHAPE RATHER THAN GUESS IT** -- *"I would rather
you name the shape than have me guess it"* -- which is the `6aff8f6` rule (a dispatch-only
instruction is an unrecorded requirement) correctly pointed back at the orchestrator.

WHY IT MATTERS, measured on me repeatedly tonight: **`br`'s close policy refuses a prose reason, and
the refusal scrolls past in-pane while the agent believes the close landed.** Adjacent measured
failures in the same family, all mine:
- `br update --assignee` with `--transition-comment` and no status change is REFUSED
  (*"transition comments and workflow-policy bypasses require a real status transition"*) -- my
  `--json` reader printed nothing useful until I read the exit status.
- `br update --status in_progress` on a blocked bead is REFUSED (`cannot claim blocked issue`) -- my
  reader printed `status=None assignee=None` and **I dispatched the bead anyway.**
- `br list --json` **excludes closed by default** (`-a` required, `--state all` unsupported), so a
  closed-count probe returned **0** while ten `br show` probes read `closed`.
**Every one is a typed refusal or a scoped default that a naive reader converts into a null or a
zero.**

ACCEPTANCE:
1. A helper that closes a bead AND reads the status back, returning a typed outcome distinguishing
   **closed** / **refused-with-the-refusal-text** / **unread**. `Unread` must be first-class, per
   K9's reasoning: folding "I did not look" into either other answer is what produced the fabricated
   constant it replaced.
2. **It MUST read the process exit status, not only parse stdout JSON.** A refusal emits no JSON and
   a JSON-only reader sees an empty field, which is exactly how a blocked-bead dispatch got sent.
3. **Anti-vacuity: an unreadable tracker must be an ERROR, never "closed".** A readback that cannot
   reach the tracker and reports success is strictly worse than no readback.
4. Fires-on-known-bad: close with a prose reason -> the helper reports `PolicyRefused` **carrying the
   refusal text**, not a generic failure. And a positive control: a sanctioned prefix reports
   `Closed`, so the helper can succeed as well as refuse.
5. **`br show` returns a BARE list while `br list` wraps rows in `.issues`** -- a leg must pin both
   shapes, because guessing that jq path produced four false findings in one session.
6. MUTATION: make the readback ignore the exit status -> leg 2's blocked-bead case goes RED. Restore
   byte-identically.
7. Assert on emitted TEXT per gate rule 7.

NO-CLAIM: a readback proves the tracker's STATE, not that the close was DESERVED. K9 already records
that enforcing the prefix proves a reason has a sanctioned SHAPE, not that its evidence is good --
`DONE: shipped` passes and says almost nothing. This bead closes the loop between "I ran close" and
"the tracker agrees", and nothing more. **Acceptance 5 of K9 -- that a bead closes on a
NON-IMPLEMENTER's grade -- remains a process rule with no code checking it, and this bead does not
change that.**

title: pane-truth: ExitCode::from(selftest(&rules) as u8) truncates -- a live twin of n34x, and undeclared AND unscanned
description:
WHAT: `crates/pane-truth/src/main.rs:49` is `return ExitCode::from(selftest(&rules) as u8);` while
`crates/pane-truth/src/lib.rs:695` is `pub fn selftest(rules: &PaneTruthRules) -> i32`. **Verified
live from source by SnowyCanyon, not taken on report.** A failure count of 256 truncates to **0** --
printing RED while exiting SUCCESS. Structurally identical to `omp-orchestrator-n34x`
(`cargo-lane-budget`), fixed at `dc617e2`.

WHY IT IS WORSE THAN THE ORIGINAL: the argument `selftest(&rules)` contains `(` and `&`, which
`passthrough_chain` (`exit_codes.rs:237-258`) rejects, so the site is **undeclared AND unscanned** --
the registry gate never demanded a row for it, and never will. The `cargo-lane-budget` instance was
at least *in* the scan set. This one is invisible to the mechanism built to catch exactly it.

**`pane-truth` IS THE FLEET'S GROUND-TRUTH ORACLE**, which is what makes the latency matter: a
selftest that prints RED and exits 0 is a broken oracle reporting itself healthy, and every
dispatch decision keyed on it inherits that.

ACCEPTANCE -- repeat the `n34x` proof, scoped, no new invention:
1. Apply the same remedy shape: a total `selftest_exit_code(i32) -> u8` returning `u8` LITERALS, so
   no numeric conversion remains on the path. Do NOT narrow `selftest`'s own signature if any test
   pins it -- check first and say which.
2. Reuse the existing RED code; add nothing to the closed 1-4 band. The count stays in the MESSAGE.
3. Known-bad FIRST, as an assertion of the mechanism before the fix: `assert_eq!(256_i32 as u8, 0)`,
   then refuse 256, 512, 65536, -1, `i32::MIN`.
4. An equivalence leg: the new conversion equals `reachable as u8` for `{0,1}`, so behaviour
   diverges ONLY where the old path was wrong.
5. **TWO MUTATIONS, and M2 is the one that matters** -- M1: restore `as u8` -> the truncation leg
   goes RED. M2: break ONLY the message half, leaving the code correct -> **exactly one leg fires**,
   proving the message assertion is independently load-bearing. Restore byte-identically both times
   and diff against recorded shas. An exit-code-only suite is blind to M2.
6. Assert on emitted TEXT per gate rule 7, never on an exit code alone.
7. Anti-vacuity: the suite must not pass on zero rules. An empty rule set is an ERROR.

NON-GOALS: do NOT sweep the other 20 census sites. Seven forward a value that could grow
(`tick-dispatch` x8, `verify-dispatch:54`, `loop-tick/main.rs:54`, `loop-driver` x2,
`loop-queue-filter:18`, `dispatcher-deadman:165`, `fleet-monitor:437`) and are UNEXAMINED beyond
reading the expression -- they are not claimed broken and are not in this bead.

NO-CLAIM: latent, not observed. `pane-truth`'s selftest would need to produce >=256 failures to
trigger it. Filed because the twin proves the class is not closed, and because this instance cannot
be caught by the registry gate at all.

comments.author: ExtractTwo
comments.text:
## `e4wp` DONE — `c990c0a` + `90327c8`, mutation-verified, and one flake I introduced and then fixed

### Gate rule 8 first (acceptance 6 of `n34x`, standing practice now)

```
git rev-parse --short HEAD                       → 90327c8
git status --porcelain -- crates/pane-truth      → EMPTY
git ls-tree -r --name-only HEAD -- crates/pane-truth
      → src/lib.rs, src/main.rs, tests/top_level.rs
```
Every figure below describes `90327c8`. Both commits reported
`CLEAN: all staged files passed the multi-gate checks`, `COMMIT_EXIT=0`, path-scoped, message
from a file with `OMP_MSG_SRC=<file>`.

### BOTH SITES IN THE FUNCTION, not only the reported one

The bead named `main.rs:49`. `main.rs:51` was `ExitCode::from(run_live(&session, &rules) as u8)`
— the identical narrowing, one line below, in the same function. `run_live` returns `i32`
(0 or 4). Fixing only the reported site would have reproduced the failure `admission-reason`
records in its own source: *"six crates shared this shape; fixing only the one that fired would
have left five live."* OracleGate independently named `:49,51`; my bead named `:49`. Both are
fixed.

### Acceptance 1 — TWO remedies, deliberately different, and the difference is behavioural

**Nothing pins `selftest`'s signature.** I checked, as acceptance 1 requires: the only caller
is `main.rs:49`, and no test calls `selftest` directly — `tests/{mutation,top_level}.rs` invoke
the binary with `--selftest`. So narrowing the signature was available here, unlike in `n34x`
where OracleGate's range test pinned it. I still did not, because narrowing to `u8` makes a
count *representable* rather than *forbidden*, and the count must not be the code.

- **`selftest_exit_code(i32) -> u8`** — total, both results are `u8` LITERALS, no numeric
  conversion on the path. The `n34x` shape exactly. `selftest`'s reachable domain is `{0, 1}`
  (every arm is a literal `return 1` or the final `0`), so the collapse is the identity there.
- **`run_live_exit_code(i32) -> u8`** — a **CHECKED** conversion (`u8::try_from`, never `as`),
  identity on `0..=255`, mapping anything unrepresentable to a non-zero code. **Not** a
  literals-only collapse, and the reason is behavioural: `run_live` returns `4` for
  cannot-observe, and `tests/differential.rs:103` compares that code against the shell oracle
  with `assert_eq!(shell_rc, rust_rc)`. Collapsing `4` would change an observable exit code in
  a crate that has **no equivalence oracle in this repo** to verify the change against. Stated
  as acceptance 1 asks, with the deviation named rather than smuggled.

**`260` is the case that separates a checked conversion from a wrapping one**, and it is the
sharpest argument for `run_live`: `260 as u8 == 4`, so the old cast could have made an
out-of-range verdict silently **impersonate the real cannot-observe code**. Pinned as an
assertion, both directions.

### Acceptance 2 — no new code

`SELFTEST_RED_EXIT` is the **existing** `1`; `XC-001` already documents 1 as "a gate refused"
and a RED selftest is that meaning. Nothing lands in the closed `1`–`4` band. The count stays
in the message.

### Acceptance 3, 4, 5 — mutation-verified, three mutations, all restores byte-identical

Digests before any mutation:
```
29a464263f27746ab258c6dd3e6757d4c9e5a69b2ccbbc41c65e57b7d09b3549  src/lib.rs
fbeed6a0be68998d75f7cc1d1d430d4a354b0dc2556ca6cdb28aee68542d1d84  src/main.rs
9124a6371d8eabbffba24f4cf580ad7f5c93e2b613e3d5b62607d4df3adefd1f  tests/top_level.rs
```

**M1 — restore `as u8`** (`selftest_exit_code` body → `failures as u8`):
```
tests::selftest_exit_code_does_not_truncate_at_256 --- FAILED
  lib.rs:1128: failures=256 truncated to a SUCCESS exit; the e4wp defect is back
tests::the_emitted_token_and_the_status_cannot_disagree --- FAILED
  lib.rs:1198: the token says FAIL while the exit code says SUCCESS — the e4wp defect
test result: FAILED. 16 passed; 2 failed
```
→ `RESTORE1_BYTE_IDENTICAL=yes`

**M2a — flip the emitted token, leave the code correct**: fires my leg **and** the pre-existing
`selftest_runs_through_top_level_entrypoint`, because that leg happens to assert the PASS
string. Two legs, so it does not prove isolation. → `RESTORE2A_BYTE_IDENTICAL=yes`

**M2b — emit BOTH verdict tokens, code untouched**: fires
`the_live_oracle_verdict_and_exit_status_agree` **ALONE**. All 18 lib legs green, and the
pre-existing top-level leg green — it still sees `SELFTEST PASS` and status 0, so it cannot
express this mutation at all.
```
the_live_oracle_verdict_and_exit_status_agree --- FAILED
  top_level.rs:39 anti-vacuity: the oracle emitted neither verdict token, or both
test result: FAILED. 1 passed; 1 failed
```
→ `RESTORE2B_BYTE_IDENTICAL=yes`, and re-verified after the de-flake below
(`RESTORE3_BYTE_IDENTICAL=yes`).

**M2b is the acceptance-5 proof, not M2a.** Exactly one leg, and it is a mutation the existing
suite is *structurally* blind to: an oracle emitting both verdicts satisfies
`contains("SELFTEST PASS")` and `status == 0` simultaneously. That is what "independently
load-bearing" means here.

### Acceptance 7 — anti-vacuity asserted in the legs, not in a sibling floor

Every case loop asserts its own arity (`assert_eq!(checked, 6)` / `4`), because a loop that
iterated zero times reports identically to one that checked every value. The live-oracle leg
carries an `xor`: a run emitting **neither** token, or **both**, is an ERROR — that is the
assertion M2b trips.

I also probed the rules surface for a real vacuity and found none:
`pane-truth --selftest --mutation --disable-rule busy_markers` →
`SELFTEST FAIL two_capture_liveness baseline=IDLE mutated=IDLE`, **rc=1**. Correct: FAIL
emitted, non-zero status.

**MEASUREMENT TRAP worth recording** — my first read of that same command said **rc=0** and it
was wrong. I had piped it through `tail -2`, so `$?` was `tail`'s status, not the binary's. In
a session whose whole subject is "the emitted text and the exit code disagree", the instrument
that reads the exit code through a pipe manufactures exactly the defect being hunted. Re-measured
with `out=$(...); rc=$?`.

### THE FLAKE I INTRODUCED, and why it is a second commit rather than a quiet amend

`c990c0a`'s leg was **flaky**: 1 of 5 runs against the pinned tree read **21 passed / 1 failed**,
finishing in 0.03s with an **empty** stdout — not a timeout. Three earlier runs had read 22/0,
which is exactly the shape of a figure nobody can trust.

**Root cause, and it is not in my leg.** `run_external` (`src/lib.rs:117`) stages the child's
output in a temp dir named `pane-truth-child-{pid}-{nanos}` and `remove_dir_all`s it on the way
out. Two callers in the **same test binary** share the pid, so when the nanosecond stamps
collide one call deletes the other's staging directory and reads back nothing. **Nothing
exercised that before**: this crate had exactly one `run_external` caller per binary until my
leg became the second.

`90327c8` scopes the fix to the leg — it now uses `Command::output`, which drains both pipes
itself and stages nothing, so it cannot participate in the collision. **8 consecutive runs
22/0**, then **5 more at `90327c8`: 22/0 every time.** The `run_external` defect is REPORTED,
not patched: it is not this bead's subject, and patching a shared helper to quiet one test is
how a real bug gets buried. Filed as finding E1 below.

Two commits rather than an amend because five agents share this checkout and rewriting a landed
commit is destructive; and because "the leg I added was flaky and here is why" belongs in the
history, not erased from it.

### Figures at `90327c8`

```
RCH_ENABLED=false CARGO_MINT_MIN_CONTAINER_PCT=0 timeout 900 ~/.cargo/bin/cargo test --quiet --no-fail-fast -p pane-truth
→ 22 passed / 0 failed   (5 consecutive runs; baseline before this bead was 17 passed / 0 failed)
```
Suites: lib 18, main 0, differential 1, mutation 1, top_level 2, doc-tests 0. Five new legs:
`selftest_exit_code_does_not_truncate_at_256`,
`run_live_exit_code_preserves_its_codes_and_never_yields_success_by_accident`,
`exit_codes_agree_with_the_old_cast_on_the_reachable_domain`,
`the_emitted_token_and_the_status_cannot_disagree`,
`the_live_oracle_verdict_and_exit_status_agree`.

`no-shell-gate --test exit_codes` → **10 passed / 0 failed** (includes OracleGate's new
`no_declared_pass_through_row_outlives_its_site`). `cargo-lane-budget` → **11 passed / 1
failed**, unchanged, the one failure still the EE-P4 shell oracle.

### RESOLVED: the 10-vs-11 disagreement on `cargo-lane-budget`

Not a doc-test. The grade's per-suite list was `lib 6, main 0, conformance 4, differential 0/1`
= 10 and **omitted `tests/top_level.rs`**, which contributes 1. Full enumeration:
```
Running unittests src/lib.rs      → 6 passed
Running unittests src/main.rs     → 0 passed
Running tests/conformance.rs      → 4 passed
Running tests/differential.rs     → 0 passed; 1 failed
Running tests/top_level.rs        → 1 passed     ← the missing suite
Doc-tests cargo_lane_budget       → 0 passed
```
6 + 0 + 4 + 0 + 1 + 0 = **11 passed / 1 failed**. Doc-tests are present and contribute zero, so
they were not the cause either way.

### FINDINGS

**E1 — `run_external`'s staging directory is not unique per call.**
`src/lib.rs:118-125` keys the temp dir on `{pid}-{nanos}` with no thread id or counter. Two
concurrent callers in one process can collide; the loser reads an empty stdout and gets a
plausible-looking `Ok` result rather than an error. Measured: 1 in 5 runs, 0.03s, empty stdout.
Latent for as long as this crate had one caller per test binary; it fired the moment there were
two. This is a **silent-success** shape — the helper returns `Ok` with a `false` reading rather
than failing — in the crate that is the fleet's ground-truth oracle. Not patched here; wants
its own bead.

**E2 — shared `target/` makes suite counts non-deterministic across agents.** Two of eight runs
returned `0 passed / 0 failed` with no test output at all, from build/lock contention with
other agents in the shared checkout. A `0/0` aggregation is indistinguishable from a suite that
ran and passed nothing, so any script that sums `test result` lines can silently report a
vacuous green. My aggregation now reports the raw pair rather than a boolean, which is why I
caught it, but the general hazard is real and belongs next to gate rule 8: **a cargo figure
needs its tree pinned AND its arity checked.**

**E3 — the census disagreement with OracleGate is not reconciled, deliberately.** They derive
32 sites / 13 crates using the scanner's balanced-paren argument reader; my `grep -rnE` derived
22 / 11. Their extra ten are nested-call forms my regex cannot see (`exit_for(&inner.verdict) as
u8`, `print_report(&check(&config)) as u8`, four `loop_tick::selftest_*() as u8`). **Their
instrument is better and I am not averaging the numbers** — two differently-shaped instruments
disagreeing is the argument for a leg, not for prose. `pane-truth` was in their category 3
("local `-> i32` returning literals"), alongside `loop-tick`, which is now the remaining
instance of my class.

### NO-CLAIM

- **Latent, not observed.** `pane-truth::selftest` would need ≥256 failures to trigger the
  truncation, and it is fail-fast — it returns on the first failing leg, so today it can only
  return 0 or 1. Fixed because the twin proves the class is not closed, and because this
  instance **cannot be caught by the registry gate at all**.
- **This does NOT establish that `pane-truth`'s exit contract is otherwise correct.** The crate
  has no equivalence oracle in this repo: `tests/differential.rs:73` looks for
  `<repo>/bin/pane-truth.sh` and, when absent, prints
  `DIFFERENTIAL DID NOT RUN: … reason=missing_external_oracle` and **returns green**. So its
  differential leg is currently a no-op that reports as a pass — the same EE-P4 hole as
  `cargo-lane-budget`, but silent instead of red. I did not change it and I am not claiming
  agreement with the shell.
- The new legs pin the **truncation** and the **text/status agreement**, not the **semantics**:
  nothing asserts that six selftest fixtures are the right six, or that cannot-observe should
  be `4`.
- **The 20 other census sites are untouched**, per the non-goal. Seven forward a value that
  could grow and are UNEXAMINED beyond reading the expression.
- `run_live_exit_code`'s identity on `0..=255` means a *child-derived* code in that range still
  passes through unchanged. That is deliberate and unverified against any oracle.
- No `.sh` or `.py` added; `git ls-files bin/` still 0. `docs/` untouched.

Bead left `in_progress`, assignee ExtractTwo, for a non-implementer to grade. Not closed.

title: dispatch_key_model: stateful fuzz of the marker/ACK lifecycle (K1-K4) on an extracted pure fn
description:
WHAT: **Stateful fuzz target `dispatch_key_model` for the pending-marker / ACK lifecycle — the K1-K4
invariants of `zlyy`, which no test could state because the logic lives inline in `main.rs`
(:1551-1670 PendingDispatch, :2620-2657 marker arms, :2858 selection).**

PREREQUISITE (shared with zlyy): extract the decision into a pure function in a kernel crate —
`fn resolve(marker: MarkerState, ack: Option<AckAt>, now: u64, prior_dispatches: u32) ->
MarkerVerdict { ClearAckReceived{late_secs} | BlockLive{expires_in} | Expire | Undatable }` — with
no I/O. The supervisor calls it; the fuzz target and the model drive it.

Op enum (frankenterm wire_envelope shape): `Dispatch{key}`, `AckArrives{key, at}`, `Tick{now}`,
`WorkerReturnsOpen{key}`, `MarkerCorrupt{key}`. Model: a `BTreeMap<key, {sent_at, acked: Option<at>,
sends: u32}>`. Invariants asserted after EVERY op:
- K2: `acked.is_some()` ⇒ the verdict is `ClearAckReceived`, never `Expire`/`BlockLive`.
- K3: `sends ≤ 1` for any key with an ACK (a key with an ACK is never sent twice).
- K1 (rendering half, once `send_and_verify` is typed): `render(verdict) == "DISPATCH_FAILED"` ⇒
  verdict is `Failed`.
- K4: `owner(tick n) == owner(tick n+1)` for the claim-owner string.
- Undatable never clears; a corrupt marker owes a human, never expires silently.

ACCEPTANCE: 1. the pure fn exists and `main.rs` calls it (grep both, positive control on an existing
kernel call). 2. target compiles in `fuzz/` (`cargo build --manifest-path fuzz/Cargo.toml`, lane).
3. Fires-on-known-bad: plant "expiry ignores ack" (drop the ack check) → target RED within 60s, cite
the artifact; restore byte-identical. 4. 5-minute run clean (runs, exec/s, cov in the ledger row).
5. The io3h trace from zlyy (ACK at +8s, expiry at +601s, re-dispatch at +694s) is a committed seed
that the model REFUSES. Built on joshs-brain, executed here at -jobs=1.

ruling (retire) is withdrawn. The orchestrator's proposed reason for wiring — an asupersync
per-step cancellation/checkpoint ledger — is **REFUTED**; the actual reason is narrower and is
stated below. Read the narrow reason, because building to the refuted one produces the wrong thing.

## THE FACT THAT DECIDED IT: THE HEARTBEAT HAS NO COMPLETION RECORD

AmberGate probed all 6,305 heartbeat rows, matching each of `ack-spine`'s 11 `StepKind` variants
against both `status` and `detail`:

    BeadSelected       342 rows   CARRIED (untyped, in detail)
    PacketSent         209        CARRIED
    ReceiverTimedOut   617        CARRIED
    GradeRequested      19        CARRIED
    AckReadBack         13        CARRIED
    ReceiverVerified     7        CARRIED
    PacketRendered       0        ABSENT ENTIRELY
    FenceChecked         0        ABSENT ENTIRELY
    GradeReceived        0        ABSENT ENTIRELY
    Closed               0        ABSENT ENTIRELY
    Redispatched         0        ABSENT ENTIRELY

**Four of the five absent kinds are the CLOSE HALF of the loop.** `Closed`, `GradeReceived`,
`Redispatched` are exactly the three facts a grader needs to answer *"did this dispatch finish"*,
and none exists in 6,305 rows. The heartbeat records dispatch richly and records completion not at
all. Retiring `ack-spine` deletes the only typed home for them.

**Second fact, subordinate but real:** every CARRIED row is a **substring of a free-text `detail`**,
not a typed field. There is no `ACK_STAGE_*` value in `status` at all — `ACK_STAGE_INDETERMINATE`
(6), `ACK_STAGE_RETRY_BLOCKED` (7), `ack_readback_missing` (7) all live inside `detail`. So the ACK
evidence the protocol just made authoritative is matchable by substring and by nothing else, whereas
`StepKind` is an enum a consumer can match exhaustively with compiler checking.

## WHAT WAS REFUTED, RECORDED SO NOBODY REBUILDS IT

The orchestrator's falsifier proposed that `oj6.1`'s "asupersync step ledger" captures per-step
cancellation or checkpoint state the heartbeat flattens. Measured: 51 `cancel|checkpoint` hits in
`crates/ack-spine/src/`, 10 in `ledger.rs`, and **0 inside `StepRecord` itself** —
`StepRecord = { kind, bead_id, pane_id, session, ts_unix, detail }`. `Cx` RUNS the steps and is
never recorded about them. Field for field the heartbeat is **richer**, carrying `build_id`, `pid`,
`tick`, and `repo`, none of which `StepRecord` has. **The inversion is about step COVERAGE and
TYPING, never about cancellation.**

## THE PREREQUISITE THAT DEFINES CORRECT WORK HERE

`ack-spine`'s emit sites live ONLY in `crates/ack-spine/src/{main.rs,spine.rs}` — nothing outside
the crate emits a `StepRecord`, so **its ledger holds no production data today.** Wiring means
**the supervisor EMITS through it**. Adding a manifest dependency so the census turns green is the
census defect just fixed in `kwo9`, running backwards: a caller that exists to satisfy a gate.

  2. **At least the three completion kinds are emitted:** `Closed`, `GradeReceived`,

  3. `census_gates` reports no unwired gate, and the supervisor's `GateUnwired` refusal clears —

  4. Fires-on-known-bad: removing the supervisor's emit site turns the census RED. A census that

  5. Anti-vacuity: a ledger with zero rows must not read as success. An empty ledger after a

  6. Positive control retained: `subprocess-contract` continues to report 24 manifest callers.
  7. The bin-vs-lib remedy text stays correct: a bin with no callers must never be told to acquire

## The defect

51 of 58 supervisor cycles refused on `unwired=ack-spine`; zero dispatches since the
`54d8574` install. And the ledger it gated on held no production data: `ack-spine`'s
emit sites lived only inside its own crate.

Five of eleven `StepKind` variants appeared in ZERO of 6,305 heartbeat rows, and
**four of the five are the close half** — `Closed`, `GradeReceived`, `Redispatched`,
`FenceChecked`, `PacketRendered`. The heartbeat records dispatch richly and
completion not at all, so it could answer *"what did we dispatch"* in detail and
**could not answer "did anything finish"** at all.

## LIVE, and the classifier discriminates on real data

Nine production rows from the 209 real `DISPATCHED` rows, via a copy of the live
heartbeat so nothing polluted the fleet ledger:

```
SPINE_COMPLETIONS_RECORDED steps=9      kinds: {grade_received: 4, closed: 5}

grade_received + closed   qfa      close_reason=DONE c00bd6f ...
grade_received + closed   q10      close_reason=DONE - unblocked without ...
grade_received + closed   6q5      close_reason=DONE - send-vs-receipt ...
grade_received + closed   2z2.2    close_reason=WONTFIX by SnowyCanyon ...
closed ONLY               ipg.11   close_reason=COMPLETE: coverage table ...
```

**`ipg.11` got `closed` and NOT `grade_received`**, because `COMPLETE:` is not one of
the four prefixes `br`'s close policy admits. That is the distinction firing on
production data, and it surfaces a finding I am not fixing here: a close reason in
active use that the policy list does not contain.

And the gate: `GATE_UNWIRED unwired=ack-spine` is gone from a live `--once` run; the
tick now reaches `SUPERVISED_WORKING`.

## The census keys on the EMIT SITE, not on Cargo.toml

`eg0m` forbids the shortcut by name — *"adding a manifest dependency so the census
turns green is the census defect just fixed in `kwo9`, running backwards."* A
manifest edge is an **upper bound** on use, never use; the same distinction that made
`finding` show 375 grep hits against 2 real edges.

So `ack-spine`'s row is measured by `crates_emitting`, which scans other crates'
source for the step primitive. **A bespoke probe, not a hand-written verdict** — it
reads the tree exactly as the hook and workflow probes do. `leht`'s defect was
hand-listed MEMBERSHIP and two HARDCODED verdicts; this is neither.

`subprocess-contract` stays the manifest-reachable positive control, so both probe
kinds are exercised.

## THE MUTATION THAT DID NOT BITE, AND WHAT IT FOUND

M1 removed the supervisor's only emit site and the census **stayed GREEN**. The needle
was still matching — **inside the doc comment two functions up that warns about
exactly this.** I assembled the needle from parts so the code would not contain it,
then wrote the literal in the sentence explaining why. **The comment defeated the
mitigation it documented.**

Seventh self-referential-checker instance in this repo and my second today; the first
was a `path-literal-guard` refusal where the sentence explaining the forbidden literal
contained the literal. Fixed generally rather than locally: `rust_sources_contain` now
strips `//` and `/* */` before matching, so no file's prose can register as an
emitter. Mirrors `close-evidence-gate`, which blanks fenced and inline code before
harvesting paths.

**A mutation that fails to bite is the most valuable result available** — a passing
suite told me nothing here, and the fix is now stronger than the one I set out to
verify.

## Mutations — all five bite; byte-identical restores verified with `cmp`

```
M1 remove the emit site, keep Cargo.toml   -> 3 legs RED  (after the comment-strip fix)
M2 treat every close as graded             -> ungraded-close + prefix legs RED
M3 starts_with -> contains                 -> prefix leg RED (the heartbeat's own defect)
M4 ignore already_recorded                 -> idempotence leg RED
M5 allow an empty dispatch cycle           -> anti-vacuity leg RED
```

M1's first attempt did not compile, which proves nothing; retried as a compiling
removal with the signature intact. M3 is the substring-vs-prefix defect this whole
change exists to replace: every carried kind in the heartbeat is a substring of
free-text `detail`, and `StepKind` is an enum a consumer matches exhaustively.

## A PRE-EXISTING LEG BROKE, AND IT WAS RIGHT TO

`a_binary_with_no_invocation_site_is_named_as_one` pinned `ack-spine` as its
bin-with-no-invocation-site specimen — so it failed on a change that FIXED the thing
it was watching. Its own message said *"if that changed, update this leg
deliberately"*, and this is that update.

Pinning a different crate rebuilds the same fragility. The property that matters is
the **pairing**: a reason naming the binary class must belong to a crate that really
ships a bin, and a reason naming the library class to one that does not. That detects
the substitution the old `any()` could not, without depending on which crate happens
to be unwired today — and it is `eg0m` acceptance 7 asserted generally instead of on
one specimen.

## What was REFUTED, recorded so nobody rebuilds it

The proposed reason for wiring — an asupersync per-step cancellation/checkpoint
ledger — is refuted and the module says so at the top.
`StepRecord = { kind, bead_id, pane_id, session, ts_unix, detail }` carries **zero**
cancel/checkpoint fields, and field for field the heartbeat is **richer**: it has
`build_id`, `pid`, `tick`, `repo`. `Cx` runs the steps and is never recorded about
them. The wiring is about step COVERAGE and TYPING.

## Verification

```
cargo test -p omp-orchestrator  -> 51/50/11/1/3/3/2/6/8/4, 0 failed
cargo clippy --all-targets      -> 0 rows in the files I own
live --once                     -> gate cleared, 9 completion rows, tick reaches SUPERVISED_WORKING
```

## NO-CLAIM

* **The effect closures are empty.** These record steps the supervisor already
  performs on the adjacent lines; moving the effects inside `step` would restructure
  a live dispatch path mid-wave. What `step` still buys is real — a cancellation
  checkpoint either side of each record, and `assert_step_count` refusing a row no
  step produced — but this is post-hoc observation, not an execution wrapper.
* **Acceptance 1's dispatch-path rows are UNOBSERVED.** The nine live rows are all
  completion kinds from the reconcile pass. `BeadSelected`, `FenceChecked`,
  `PacketRendered` and `PacketSent`/`Redispatched` are wired and compile, and no real
  dispatch has occurred since — the fleet had zero free panes on every probe run.
* `crates_emitting` proves a **call site exists in another crate's source**, not that
  it executes. A call inside a `#[cfg(test)]` module in a peer's `src/` would count.
* Acceptance 6 asks that `subprocess-contract` "continues to report 24 manifest
  callers"; it reports **40**, and 40 crates do declare the dependency. The 24 is a
  drifted figure. The leg asserts the class rather than a count, because pinning one
  would fail on every new dependent.
* One package run showed `target_ownership` RED with `duplicate key ... loop-driver`
  from a peer's transient `src/bin/` directory. It vanished before I could reproduce
  it, and the suite is green now. **A failure I cannot reproduce is not a defect** —
  reported, not filed.

description:
PERSONA 2 -- THE CONTROL-KERNEL ESTIMATOR. Kind: control-kernel (his: slb, storage_ballast_helper).
**This is the missing kernel. Everything else in the repo is bookkeeping around a decision that has
no estimate behind it.**

WHAT: build the typed estimator + decision rule that dispatch currently lacks.

1. **`PaneStateBelief`** -- a posterior over pane state from observations, not a boolean. Entity:
   `bayes-theorem`. Today `tick-monitor` maps a braille spinner to an enum; a stale scrollback
   spinner has produced a confident wrong verdict (measured: one pane scored working AND idle
   simultaneously).
2. **`DispatchDecision = argmin_a Sum_s P(s|evidence) * L(a,s)`.** Entity:
   `bayes-risk-loss-matrix`. The loss matrix is the artifact: **interrupting real work and leaving a
   pane idle beside a ready queue are NOT symmetric costs**, and today nothing states their ratio.
   Atlas evidence: `franken_networkx` -- *"the runtime's compatibility gate is a statistical
   decision rule, not a threshold."*
3. **`should_observe_again()`** -- entity `sequential-decision-optimal-stopping`: observe again iff
   expected marginal information gain > cost of delay. **This REPLACES the flat 75s floor**, which
   the orchestrator specified, an implementer implemented, watched pass, and withdrew because it
   would make every production receipt INDETERMINATE (`crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs` captures
   pre and post with ZERO spacing). Bead `omp-orchestrator-artb` holds that open question; this
   closes it with math instead of a guess.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. A crate with the three types above. `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`.
2. **The atlas's own falsifiable invariant, as a property test: for every simplex posterior, every
   reported expected loss >= -1.** Cite it.
3. The loss matrix is DATA (a typed table), not inline constants, so the asymmetry is reviewable.
4. Fires-on-known-bad: a posterior concentrated on `Working` must not produce `Dispatch`; a uniform
   posterior must produce `Observe` or `Refuse`, never `Dispatch`.
5. **Anti-vacuity: zero observations must yield the PRIOR and a typed `Insufficient`, never a
   decision.** An empty evidence set and a confident one must not collapse.
6. MUTATION: make the decision ignore the loss matrix -> the asymmetry leg goes RED. Restore
   byte-identically.
7. Wire it into ONE real caller and say which. BUILT != WIRED.

  ./rigor kind control-kernel
  ./rigor entity sequential-decision-optimal-stopping
  ./rigor entity bayes-risk-loss-matrix
  ./rigor apply --kind control-kernel --result "decision under uncertainty"

NO-CLAIM required: a posterior is only as good as its likelihood model; state where the likelihoods
come from and that they are ASSUMED, not measured, until someone measures them. Check
`ANTI-PATTERNS.md` before porting -- 500+ claims in the corpus were refuted or doc-only.

title: The ACK instruction is hand-typed in two media and drifted from the parser twice today: 32/32 ACKs carry a sender-dictated pane id, and the 15:21 $TMUX_PANE template dropped ' -- ' so 5 ACKs incl. supervisor ipg.19 are unparseable (RETRY_BLOCKED x6 after a 33s ACK)
description:
WHAT: **the ACK instruction is a hand-typed string in two media, and it drifted from the parser twice in one day: 32/32 ACK comments carry a pane id the SENDER typed (proving arrival, never identity), and the 15:21 template that fixed the dictation dropped the parser's ` -- ` separator, so 5 of today's ACKs — including the one on a live supervisor dispatch — are unparseable and the loop is still reporting `DISPATCH_RETRY_BLOCKED` on a bead that was ACKed 33 seconds after dispatch.** The fix for `93lo` (the dispatch site emits the ACK line) will bake in whichever contamination it copies unless the line is specified as receiver-derived AND generated from the same source the parser reads.

## MEASURED 2026-09-02

**The tracker, whole population** (650 comments across 240 beads, `br comments list <id> --json` per bead):

    ACK-prefixed comments                            32   (24 today, 8 on 08-31)
    pane given as a literal %N                       32   (100%)
    author = josh  (no --actor, identifies nobody)   18   (14 of today's 24)
    ACK whose pane/agent came from the RECEIVER       1   -> 20:57:41Z  omp-orchestrator-leht  GreenFrog
                                                          "ACK leht-grade on %1413 agent=GreenFrog title=omp-orchestrator..."

That one row is the first uncontaminated identity in the tracker's history. It came from `/tmp/grade-lane-1413.md:7-12`, the first packet to say *"Run `$TMUX_PANE` yourself. Every ACK I collected today has a pane id I dictated inside the template, so all ~26 prove arrival and none proves identity — I supplied the answer inside the question."*

**The 15:21 template is byte-incompatible with the parser.** `p2.md:3`, `p3.md:3`, `p4.md:3` render `"ACK <tok> on $TMUX_PANE"` — no ` -- ` suffix. `crates/ack-stage/src/lib.rs:247-248` builds `format!("ACK {token} on {pane_id} -- ")` and `:251` requires `starts_with(prefix)`. Measured over every ACK posted after that template shipped:

    br comments list <bead> --json | jq '.[] | select(.text|startswith("ACK ")) | .text|test("^ACK [^ ]+ on %[0-9]+ -- ")'
      i0kp    21:23:05Z GreenFrog    [ACK i0kp on %1413]        parseable=false
      kxe.1   21:23:05Z BlueLantern  [ACK kxe.1 on %1414]       parseable=false
      eg0m    21:21:27Z AmberGate    [ACK eg0m on %1408]        parseable=false   (the 20:43 BlueLantern one, from d-eg0m's dictated template, parses)
      oj6.3   21:33:24Z BlueLantern  [ACK oj6.3 on %1414]       parseable=false   (its 21:31 sibling parses)
      ipg.19  22:00:54Z AmberGate    [ACK ipg.19 on %1408]      parseable=false   <- SUPERVISOR dispatch, build a3ab48d

And the loop's verdict on ipg.19, `~/.local/state/flywheel/omp-orchestrator.heartbeat.jsonl` filtered `ts_unix>=1788386421`:

    22:00:21Z DISPATCH_CLAIMED  pane=%1408 receiver_agent=AmberGate
    22:00:54Z                   <- AmberGate posts "ACK ipg.19 on %1408" (33s after dispatch: the pane HAD the protocol)
    22:01:00Z SUPERVISOR_REFUSED ACK_STAGE_RETRY_BLOCKED action=AWAIT_HUMAN
    22:01:01Z 22:02:32Z 22:04:03Z 22:05:34Z 22:07:05Z 22:07:14Z DISPATCH_RETRY_BLOCKED   <- still firing while this audit ran

The pane learned the protocol from a hand packet whose template had drifted, applied it faithfully to a loop dispatch, and the loop called a human. `93lo`'s failure shape — "the sender half is a tested crate, the receiver half is a sentence in markdown that no gate reads" (AGENTS.md:241-244) — reproduced with the sentence PRESENT and merely misspelled.

**The 26 hand packets, by ACK form** (`grep -c 'ACK \S+ on %[0-9]+'` vs `grep -c '\$TMUX_PANE'` per file, mtime order):

    before 13:03 local  13 packets   ACK line absent (93lo)                    p5 ack-reset d-bl d-gf d-ag d-y6v5 d-8e1g d-6fot d-kyq5 d-tvu5 d-hsv d-uvo d-kwo9
    13:03 – 14:42        7 packets   ACK line present, pane DICTATED as %N     d-ex4(%1414) ack-t00(%1409) d-iad(%1413) d-iis6(%1408) ack-u1c(%1409) d-fr6(%1409) d-eg0m(%1414)
    14:57 – 15:22        5 packets   pane DERIVED via $TMUX_PANE               grade-lane-1413 reengage-1414 p4 p2 p3
                                     ...of which 3 DICTATE the actor instead   p2 `--actor GreenFrog`  p3 `--actor BlueLantern`  p4 `--actor AmberGate`
    other                1 packet    grade-6fot (a grade report; no ACK)

So the pane-id half was fixed at 14:57 and the agent-name half regressed at 15:21: `p2.md:3` reads `br comment add ... --actor GreenFrog "ACK i0kp on $TMUX_PANE"` — the sender chose the name. The resulting rows (`21:23:05Z GreenFrog i0kp %1413`, `21:23:05Z BlueLantern kxe.1 %1414`, `21:21:27Z AmberGate eg0m %1408`) read as agent-authored and are exactly as unproven as the josh-authored ones.

**Why it matters, measured on the same pane the same day** (`/tmp/reengage-1414.md:27-37`): three sources disagreed about `%1414` — the orchestrator's ACK map said `BlueLantern (3) AND MistyCrane (1)`, the agent-mail identity file said `SapphirePanther` (31h old, `binding: legacy-unverified`), `pane_title` said `cod_2`. The ACK map was built from ACKs whose `%1414` the orchestrator had typed and whose assignee the orchestrator had set; it was the orchestrator's assumption echoed back, and it was wrong once already that day (MistyCrane is `%1409`). `gfm6` records the assignee-field half of this; this bead is the ACK half.

**The renderer has no ACK line at all** (`crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs:1197-1200`, `grep -c 'ACK ' main.rs` → 0 in the packet format), so on the loop path there is nothing to contaminate yet. `93lo`'s acceptance 2 says the dispatch site must emit the instruction; it does not say what the instruction must contain. Emitting `ACK {token} on {pane}` with the supervisor's `pane` variable interpolated — the obvious implementation, and the one every hand packet used for four hours — reproduces the defect in Rust.

**The parser side is already indifferent** — `crates/ack-stage/src/lib.rs:243-253` matches the prefix `ACK <token> on <pane_id> -- ` and compares `<pane_id>` to the dispatched pane. A receiver-derived `$TMUX_PANE` that expands to the same `%N` satisfies it byte-for-byte; a receiver-derived one that expands to a DIFFERENT `%N` is the finding (wrong pane received the packet), which the dictated form can never produce.

## WHY

An ACK exists to answer "did the packet reach the pane and agent I meant?" If the sender supplies the pane and the agent, the answer is a copy of the question and the protocol proves only that `br comments add` works. `iis6` (the 30s ACK window) and `93lo` (the missing instruction) both spend engineering on making the ACK arrive; neither is worth it if the arriving ACK carries no information. This is Joshua's 2026-09-02 line — *"if we can't identify which agent — exactly — is connected to a bead, and if they are live or active or not, we have a failing system"* — applied to the one artifact that was supposed to identify them.

## ACCEPTANCE

1. The ACK instruction, wherever it is rendered (the `93lo` renderer fix, and every hand packet until then), is the literal
   `br comments add <bead> --actor "$(agent name you resolve yourself)" "ACK <token> on $TMUX_PANE -- agent=<same name> title=$(tmux display-message -p -t "$TMUX_PANE" '#{pane_title}')"`
   with **no `%N` and no agent name typed by the sender**. `-t "$TMUX_PANE"` is load-bearing (`3kpc`, `mad1` acceptance 3: the unqualified form returns the ACTIVE pane, measured `%1396` from inside pane 4).
2. Fires-on-known-bad: `ack-stage` (or a thin check beside it) REFUSES an ACK whose `<pane_id>` does not match the dispatched pane with a typed `AckPaneMismatch{expected, got}` — and the test plants exactly that: dispatch to `%1413`, ACK arrives `on %1414`. Today's parser treats mismatch as "no ACK"; the mismatch is a finding and must be named as one.
3. Known-good leg: a real dispatch to a live pane whose agent runs the derived line yields an ACK whose `%N` equals the dispatched pane AND whose `agent=` equals the comment's `author` — both read back from `br comments list --json`, cited separately.
4. Positive control on the census: `br comments list` over the tracker after one wave shows ≥1 ACK with `agent=` and `author` equal and non-`josh`; the count of `author=josh` ACKs does not grow.
5. Anti-vacuity: a wave with zero ACKs is `ERROR`, not "no identity problems" — 0 rows reads identically to a fleet where nobody was asked.
6. **The instruction text and the parser share one source.** `ack-stage` exports `pub fn ack_instruction(bead_id: &str) -> String` (the shell line above, built from the same `token`/prefix code `:247-248` matches), and the renderer/hand path emit THAT string. Round-trip test: render the instruction for a bead, substitute `$TMUX_PANE=%1413` and the agent name as a shell would, post the resulting comment into a fixture, and assert `matching_comment_for` returns it. Mutation: drop the ` -- ` from the instruction and the round-trip goes RED — that is today's 5 unparseable ACKs as a test.
7. Falsifier for the bead: **a packet rendered after this lands whose ACK instruction contains a literal `%[0-9]+`, a sender-chosen `--actor <Name>`, or a prefix that `ack-stage::matching_comment_for` does not match.** One such packet refutes the fix.

## NOT IN SCOPE

- Emitting the ACK line from the renderer at all: `93lo`.
- The assignee field's five incompatible naming schemes and dead `supervisor:<pid>` holders: `gfm6`.
- Sender identity (FROM line): `dispatch-from-line-mad1` / `nfgc`.
- The 30s ACK window: `iis6`.

## NO-CLAIM

A receiver-derived ACK proves the packet reached THAT pane and THAT process posted a comment. It does not prove the agent name is truthful (any process can pass any `--actor`), does not prove the work, and does not survive a pane restart — `3kpc`'s file-based binding is the durable half. An ACK is a delivery receipt, never a progress one (AGENTS.md:255-258).

description:
WHAT: (a) make `state-wildcard-lint`'s refusal NAME file and line, and (b) resolve its 2 findings,
which together with path-literal-guard are blocking EVERY commit in this repo.

MEASURED 2026-09-02 04:5xZ. `.git/hooks/pre-commit` -> exit 1:
  "MULTI-GATE REFUSED: 2 violation(s):
     path-literal-guard: 17 hardcoded home-path literal(s): crates/slb-guard-fail-closed/src/main.r
     state-wildcard-lint: 2 finding(s)"

state-wildcard-lint names NOTHING: "2 finding(s)" and no path, no line, no snippet. AGENTS.md's own
gate doctrine says a finding that does not name the replacement is not actionable, and this one does
not even name the offence. An agent hitting this cannot act, and pane 5 -- whose staged work is

description:

WHY: MEASURED 2026-09-01: panes %1408 and %1409 (GLM 5.3 Flash) hit HTTP 402 and stopped working; the status line still rendered the idle `π` glyph, so `tick-monitor observe` reported `%1408` in `free_capacity` and the supervisor refilled it 131 times (see the sibling bead on the re-dispatch loop). %1409 died mid-edit of `crates/installer/src/lib.rs` and left the workspace unbuildable. title: Exit 1 and exit 2 each carry three unrelated meanings
description:
## WHAT

Exit `1` carries **three unrelated meanings** across 32 crates and 89 literal sites, and exit `2`
carries three more across 34 crates and 118 sites. Split them so a caller can distinguish a
refusal from a broken tool without reading stderr.

Registered as `XC-001` and `XC-002` in `docs/error_codes/exit_code_registry.md`.

## WHY

Measured 2026-09-01. `crates/no-shell-gate/src/bin/pre-push-gate.rs` emits **exit 1** for both:

- `PRE_PUSH_GATE_REFUSED` at `:312, :321, :366, :375, :384, :402, :416, :434` — the gate WORKED
  and correctly refused.
- `PRE_PUSH_GATE_ERROR` at `:287, :303, :340, :427` — the gate DID NOT RUN: unknown flag,
  non-integer argument, unwritable receipt, and an empty `git ls-files` scan.

Same code, same file. A caller checking `$? -eq 1` cannot tell "your push is not allowed" from
"the thing that decides is broken", and on 2026-09-01 an agent read one as the other. Two of the
four session misreads reduce to this.

Exit 1 also serves as a usage error at 2 sites, and `ExitCode::FAILURE` (51 sites of
`SUCCESS`/`FAILURE` combined) folds into it.

Exit 2 is the mirror: dominantly a usage error (50 of 118 sites carry a `usage` message), but
`OracleCompareVerdict::Unmeasurable` maps to 2 at `crates/oracle-compare/src/lib.rs:103`,
`EXIT_USAGE = 2` at `crates/fleet-composite/src/main.rs:14`, and `PLAN_ASSEMBLE_ERROR` exits 2.
**It also collides with the `cargo` mint wrapper's own exit 2** (`CARGO_LANE_IDENTITY_UNSAFE`,
`CARGO_LANE_ISOLATED_TARGET_REQUIRED`, and 7 more markers at `~/.local/bin/cargo`), so a 2 from a
`cargo test` line has three possible owners.

`crates/oracle-compare/src/lib.rs:99-104` already shows the shape to copy —
`Agree`/`Disagree`/`Unmeasurable` as 0/1/2, a verdict and its absence given different codes.

## ACCEPTANCE

`run X, expect Y`:

1. `cargo test -p no-shell-gate --test exit_codes` stays at 7 passed with the new codes documented
   (the gate refuses any code lacking an `XC-*` row, so the registry must be edited in the same
   commit).
2. A leg proving separation, in whichever crate is split first: given an input that makes the gate
   REFUSE, expect the refusal code; given an input that makes the gate itself fail (unwritable
   receipt path), expect the DIFFERENT error code. Both arms asserted, so an all-one-code
   implementation fails.
3. `grep -c 'ExitCode::from(1)' crates/no-shell-gate/src/bin/pre-push-gate.rs` must fall, and the
   remaining sites must all be one meaning — stated in the commit which meaning.

New codes come from the **5..=63 unallocated band** named in the registry's §5 reservation table,
never from 64..=78 (`sysexits.h`) and never from 102..=125 (toolchain and wrappers).

## NOT IN SCOPE

Renumbering every crate. Take `pre-push-gate` first because it is the measured misread, then the
other gates as they are touched. A sweep across 32 crates in one commit is how a caller breaks
silently.

## NO-CLAIM

Splitting the code does not make any caller check it. Nothing here proves that a consumer reads
the new code rather than `!= 0`, and the marker prefixes remain the authoritative signal until
consumers are audited — a separate bead.

title: Corpus doc #13: exit code registry with enforced does-not-mean column
description:
## WHAT

Document #13 of 78 in `docs/plans/plan_to_write_the_document_corpus.md`, and the widest single gap
against the corpus: asupersync carries `docs/error_codes/` with 45 documents; we carried **zero**
while exit codes were scattered across 51 bin targets with nothing describing them.

Register every exit code this workspace **emits** (12 distinct) and every foreign code it
**receives**, one row per code with: code, emitting crates, what it MEANS, **what it does NOT
mean**, and the operator's next action. Reserve the number space. Name every code carrying two or
more meanings. Change no code — renumbering breaks callers and is a separate bead.

## WHY

Four exit codes were misread by agents on 2026-09-01, one of them by the pane that filed this:

- `103` read as a TEST RESULT because `0 passed 0 failed` printed beside it — a failure path
  emitting something shaped like data. The session's most expensive misread.
- `75` read as a build failure; it was `CARGO_MINT_CONTAINER_EXHAUSTED`, the disk-floor refusal.
- `127` read as "`bin/check.sh` is untracked", a repo defect that did not exist; the real cause was
  a stale worktree.
- `1` read as both "the gate is broken" and "the gate correctly refused" — and it is genuinely
  both, on different lines of the same file.

Before this document, `git grep -c --no-index -E '^//[/!].*\bexit' -- 'crates/*/src/*'` answered
**0 files** against a positive control of **102** files carrying `//!` docs at all. No crate
documented its own exits. The load-bearing column is therefore **does NOT mean**, not **means**.

## ACCEPTANCE

Re-run, do not read:

```
$ cargo test -p no-shell-gate --test exit_codes -- --nocapture
```

Expect **7 passed**. The legs:

1. `every_emitted_exit_code_is_documented` — re-derives the emission set from all `.rs` files under
   `crates/*/src` and fails naming `file:line` for any code with no `XC-*` row.
2. `an_empty_scan_set_is_an_error_not_a_pass` — anti-vacuity; a zero-file scan returns a NAMED
   error, never an empty complaint list.
3. `a_planted_undocumented_code_is_caught` — fires-on-known-bad; a temp fixture emitting
   `ExitCode::from(213)` must be flagged.
4. `a_planted_documented_code_passes` — known-good; `ExitCode::from(2)` must pass. Without this leg
   an over-strict gate looks green, and an over-strict gate gets routed around.
5. `every_row_carries_a_does_not_mean` — refuses any row with an empty or placeholder
   `does NOT mean` cell, or fewer than 6 columns, or fewer than 12 emitted rows.
6. `the_scan_floors_seeded_from_this_suites_own_measurement_hold` — floors seeded from THIS
   suite's own scan (123 files, 12 codes, 18 pass-through sites), never from a neighbouring count.
7. `every_pass_through_site_is_declared` — every site forwarding a child's code must appear in §6.

Mutation leg, run at authoring time and reproducible: delete the `XC-004` row from the registry
(asserted to exist exactly once first) and leg 1 goes RED with
`EXIT_CODE_UNDOCUMENTED code=4 at crates/loop-switch/src/main.rs:75`; restore byte-identical
(sha256 `53ca7c5353cce9efdb3aa9da547b7f2d4efc917182aababc828e271d69732f9a`) and all 7 pass.

Structural bar, `docs/contracts/asupersync_process_grade.md`: all seven markers present, 32 stable
IDs, 19,142 bytes against a 25 KB ceiling, `## Non-Coverage` and `## NO-CLAIM` both present.

## NOT IN SCOPE

- **No renumbering, no code change.** Not one `ExitCode::from` was touched. The collisions are
  documented and filed separately.
- stderr marker registry (`PRE_PUSH_GATE_*`, `CARGO_MINT_*`, `RCH-Exxx`) — its own document.
- Emitters outside `crates/*/src`: test binaries, fixtures, build scripts, shell wrappers.

## NO-CLAIM

Documenting a code does not make any caller emit it correctly. The suite proves PRESENCE OF A ROW,
never truth of a row — a wrong `does NOT mean` cell passes every leg. It cannot tell a correct `1`
from a wrong `1`, because both are `1`; that is the defect the registry names and does not fix.
`XC-EXT-RCH`'s integer 103 is recorded as OBSERVED, not reproduced: two probes tonight returned 1
and 124 instead, and `rch schema export` ships 100 string codes with zero numeric exit mappings.

title: EXIT_CONFIG bound to two values; 78 bound to two names; 75 to five meanings
description:
## WHAT

Three constant/value collisions in the exit-code space, all measured, none inferred. Documented as
`XC-064`, `XC-075` and `XC-078` in `docs/error_codes/exit_code_registry.md`; this bead fixes them.

1. **`EXIT_CONFIG` is bound to two different values.**
   - `crates/fleet-composite/src/main.rs:16` — `const EXIT_CONFIG: u8 = 64;`
   - `crates/pane-dispatch-fence/src/main.rs:18` — `const EXIT_CONFIG: u8 = 78;`
   64 is `EX_USAGE` in `sysexits.h`; 78 is `EX_CONFIG`. One of the two is misnamed, and the
   `fleet-composite` one is the wrong one.

2. **`78` is bound to two unrelated names.**
   - `crates/fleet-monitor/src/lib.rs:413` — `pub const EXIT_CANNOT_OBSERVE: i32 = 78;`
   - `crates/pane-dispatch-fence/src/main.rs:18` — `EXIT_CONFIG = 78`
   "I could not observe the fleet" and "your configuration is wrong" are different operator
   actions from the same integer.

3. **`75` carries five meanings**, three ours and two foreign.
   - `crates/loop-driver/src/lib.rs:17` — `EXIT_CONCURRENT` (another instance holds the lock)
   - `crates/pane-dispatch-fence/src/main.rs:16` — `EXIT_BUSY` (the pane is busy)
   - `crates/installer/…` — `INSTALLER BLOCKED`
   - `~/.local/bin/cargo` — `CARGO_MINT_CONTAINER_EXHAUSTED` and
     `CARGO_MINT_PEAK_WOULD_BREACH_FLOOR`, both exit 75
   All five are honestly `EX_TEMPFAIL` "retry later", which is why 75 is the least harmful of the
   three — but `75` was misread as a build failure on 2026-09-01, so the retry semantics are not
   reaching the reader.

## WHY

Derived at commit `d48615c`:

```
git grep -n --no-index -E '^\s*(pub )?const EXIT_[A-Z_]+' -- 'crates/*/src/*'
```

A name bound to two values means a reader who has learned one crate is confidently wrong in the
next. A value bound to two names means a reader with only the integer cannot recover the meaning
at all. Both are the class the registry documents and this bead removes.

The precedent worth copying is foreign: `~/.local/bin/cargo:388` emits
`"exit_code":75,"is_gate_verdict":false` — the only emitter on this machine that ships the
refusal/failure disambiguation **in data** rather than in a prefix a human has to notice.

## ACCEPTANCE

`run X, expect Y`:

1. `git grep -h --no-index -oE 'const EXIT_[A-Z_]+: [ui][0-9]+ = [0-9]+' -- 'crates/*/src/*' |
   sort -u` — every constant NAME appears exactly once with one value; no name has two values.
2. A new leg in `crates/no-shell-gate/tests/exit_codes.rs`:
   `no_exit_constant_name_is_bound_to_two_values` — the scanner already builds
   `consts: BTreeMap<String, BTreeSet<u16>>`, so the assertion is that every set has len 1. The
   leg must be shown RED against today's tree (it will name `EXIT_CONFIG = {64, 78}`) before the
   fix lands, and GREEN after.
3. `cargo test -p no-shell-gate --test exit_codes` stays at 7+ passed, with the registry rows
   edited in the same commit — the gate refuses any code lacking a row.
4. Every renamed constant's call sites updated in the same commit, and the commit states which
   `sysexits.h` code each one now claims.

## NOT IN SCOPE

The 75 family is documented rather than renumbered here: three "retry later" meanings sharing
`EX_TEMPFAIL` is defensible, and the two foreign ones cannot be changed by us at all. The fix for
75 is the `is_gate_verdict` field in emitted JSON, not a new integer — file separately if wanted.

## NO-CLAIM

Fixing the names does not make any caller distinguish the codes; `!= 0` remains the dominant check
in the tree, and this bead does not audit consumers. And renaming `EXIT_CONFIG` in
`fleet-composite` changes an OBSERVABLE contract — anything scripting against 64 from that binary
breaks, which is why the acceptance requires the call-site sweep in the same commit.
