weaker one beside it in the acceptance. Bead 7ai ("Installable from anywhere: no hardcoded repo or
home paths") is CLOSED, and this extraction re-opened its violation -- which also means 7ai's

title: P0: HD-0008 recorded Joshua's decision 'push it' on 2026-09-02 and it was never executed -- 183 unpushed then, 381 now, and every CI-red claim is about a tree 381 commits behind
description: MEASURED 2026-09-05 by pane 1 while grading omp-orchestrator-ci-red-every-push-five-jobs-ct5i. docs/decisions.jsonl carries HD-0008 with decider=josh, recorded_by=SnowyCanyon: question '183 commits on main are unpushed and the GitHub remote JYeswak/omp-orchestrator is PUBLIC. Pushing makes them world-readable in one action. Push to public; make the repo private first then push; or leave...' and decision 'A: push to public origin/main as-is. Josh 2026-09-02: this is a build in public repo - push it'. THE DECISION WAS RECORDED AND NEVER CARRIED OUT. Measured now: git rev-list --count origin/main..HEAD -> 381 unpushed commits, up from the 183 the decision was made against; last CI run is 4b398e4 at 2026-09-02T03:01:50Z while HEAD is c17585a at 2026-09-04T20:19:11-06:00; git rev-list --count 4b398e4..HEAD -> 381. TWO CONSEQUENCES, BOTH LIVE. (1) Every 'CI is red' claim in this repo is a statement about a tree 381 commits behind. AGENTS.md's own framing -- 'a gate that fires on every push, fails every time, and nobody reads it... a local gate that certifies what CI rejects is a fooled certificate' -- was true when written but is NOT the current condition: CI has not run in three days because nothing has been pushed, so the local receipt certifies a tree CI has never observed. Pane 1 cited the 67/67 figure as evidence about the present tree in the ct5i dispatch, which is the cargo-vs-commit wrong-input class AGENTS.md rule 8 already names. (2) THE DECISION LEDGER HAS A WRITER AND NO ACTUATOR. Loop 1 pass 1 filed nsx1 as 'S9 has a reader and no writer'; a writer now exists (HD-0008 through HD-0018 were all written) and the gap has INVERTED -- decisions are recorded and nothing executes them. This is atlas-arc R3's HUMAN_DECISION disposition with no completion path and R10's 'current reality diverges from the status surface' reopen trigger firing on the ledger itself. THE OPEN QUESTION THAT MUST GO BACK TO JOSHUA RATHER THAN BE ASSUMED: the approval was given at 183 commits and the scope is now 381, a 2.08x change in the quantity the decision was scoped to. Whether an approval scoped to a measured quantity survives a doubling of that quantity is exactly the dies-when question, and ntm-fleet-monitor's own wave table classifies deploy-public as verdict=required kind=deploy apply=no. A recorded approval exists, so this is not unauthorized; but the scope moved, the action is irreversible, and the repo is public. TASKS: (1) confirm the scope with Joshua before pushing, quoting both figures; (2) file the general mechanism -- a HUMAN_DECISION row needs an execution status and an actuator, or the ledger accumulates decisions that never become actions; (3) do not treat any pre-push CI figure as evidence about HEAD until a push lands. NO-CLAIM: this establishes that a recorded decision has not been executed and that CI evidence is 381 commits stale. It does not establish that pushing is currently correct -- the scope change is real and the confirmation is Joshua's to give.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Known-bad leg must be HD-0008 itself: a decisions.jsonl row with decider=josh, decision "A: push to public origin/main as-is" recorded 2026-09-02, and no execution evidence (no push, origin/main..HEAD still 381). The mere existence of the HD-0008 row is NOT evidence of execution — the checker must fail on a row that has a decision string but no execution_status/executed_at/actuator_receipt field, and must fail specifically on HD-0008 by id when run against the current file. Assert the checker emits the HD-0008 id, the recorded date 2026-09-02, and the unexecuted verdict.

2. Known-good leg must be a decision row that is legitimately closed: either a HD-00NN row carrying an execution receipt (executed_at + actuator + verifiable side-effect probe) or a row whose disposition is explicitly DECLINED/SUPERSEDED. That row must PASS. If no such row exists today, construct one as a fixture and state in the receipt that the good leg is fixture-only and why; a rule that flags every row in HD-0008..HD-0018 is over-strict and fails this item.

3. Anti-vacuity: if docs/decisions.jsonl is missing, unreadable, zero-length, or parses to zero HUMAN_DECISION rows, the tool exits non-zero with a typed error (e.g. ERR_NO_DECISION_ROWS) and never prints a pass. Same for zero rows matching the unexecuted predicate when the file is non-empty — that is a distinct typed result, not silently "clean". Include a test that empties/renames the file and asserts the typed error code, not exit 0.

4. Mutation proof: flip HD-0008's decision field (or inject execution_status=executed) in a copy, run the checker, show it goes GREEN/changes verdict (RED->pass), then restore. Record sha256 of docs/decisions.jsonl before and after; the two checksums must be byte-identical and both printed in the receipt. Also mutate in the other direction — add a second unexecuted row — and show the count moves 1 -> 2.

5. MEASURED live, re-run at grading time, not quoted from this description: `git rev-list --count origin/main..HEAD`, `git rev-list --count 4b398e4..HEAD`, HEAD sha + committer date, and the most recent CI run sha + timestamp from the live GH API/gh run list. The receipt must carry all of these with the command text. The 183 figure and the HD-0008 question text may be read from the ledger as a fixture/historical quote. Any CI pass/fail number cited must be annotated with the sha it ran against and the live `rev-list --count <ci_sha>..HEAD` distance; a bare "67/67" with no sha and no distance fails.

6. The push itself is NOT in scope and must not be performed by this bead. The scope-change question (approval given at 183, now 381, 2.08x, irreversible, public repo, ntm-fleet-monitor wave table verdict=required kind=deploy apply=no) must be routed to Joshua as an explicit new HUMAN_DECISION row quoting both figures verbatim, or the bead fails. A pushed tree found at grading time with no new approval row is a fail.

7. The general mechanism named in TASKS(2) — HUMAN_DECISION rows need an execution status field and an actuator — must be either implemented in this bead (schema field + writer + checker) or filed as its own bead with an id recorded here. It may not be treated as covered by fixing HD-0008 alone. Same for TASKS(3): show either a lint/guard that rejects pre-push CI figures as HEAD evidence, or a filed bead id.

8. Scan the full decision ledger, not just HD-0008: enumerate every HUMAN_DECISION row HD-0001..HD-0018 (and any later), classify each as executed / declined / unexecuted with the evidence used, and print the table. A checker that hardcodes HD-0008 passes item 1 but fails this item; the classification must be derived from row fields plus a side-effect probe, and the count of unexecuted rows must be stated as a number.

title: P0: nothing verifies HEAD compiles AS COMMITTED -- every local gate reads the worktree, and that hid an uncompilable HEAD behind 486 commits
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-06 by pane 1. Filed as promised in the close reason of omp-orchestrator-head-uncompilable-missing-dep-mi6b rather than left buried inside a closed bead.

THE CLASS: every local gate in this repository reads the WORKING TREE. cargo check, cargo test, and the .git/hooks/pre-commit multi-gate all see uncommitted and untracked files and pass. Nothing verifies that HEAD, as committed, compiles. So a tree can be green on every developer machine and uncompilable for a fresh clone, a CI runner, and every peer checkout.

IT BIT THREE TIMES IN ONE SESSION, each time found by accident:
  1. ycwh -- crates/fuzz-build-gate was ENTIRELY untracked (0 files in HEAD, 2 on disk) with a syntax error, breaking `cargo check --workspace` for anyone who did not have the local copy. 23 errors, all cascading from one file.
  2. abl7 -- crates/receiver-receipt/tests/properties.rs was untracked while a CLOSED bead cited it as its proptest floor. The fuzz half landed; the proptest half did not. A closed bead's evidence pointed at a file that existed on one machine and in no commit.
  3. mi6b -- crates/omp-inventory-map/src/lib.rs:27 in HEAD read `use text_structure::toml_code_only;` while HEAD's Cargo.toml did not declare the dependency. The missing line existed only as an uncommitted worktree modification. Measured: worktree `cargo check --workspace` = 0 errors, clean `git archive HEAD` export = 2 errors.

CONSEQUENCE MEASURED AT THE TIME: 486 commits unpushed, 88 of them landed that evening, CI last run 2026-09-02 and failed -- with not one red local signal, because the signal cannot exist in a worktree-reading gate.

THE PRIMITIVE ALREADY EXISTS IN-TREE AND IS PROVEN TWICE. .github/workflows/gate.yml:41 documents using a `git archive` export to measure crates/fleet-monitor, having found it 'reads GREEN in a dirty worktree only because a sibling holds a ~320-line uncommitted diff on that file... The worktree was the lie', and states the kernel-bypass-gate debt ceilings are pinned to `git archive HEAD` for the same reason. I used the identical method to find and then verify the fix for mi6b: export HEAD into a private scratch directory, run cargo check there, 2 errors before and 0 after.

A SECOND BENEFIT WORTH NAMING: an export is a PRIVATE copy of HEAD, so it lets an agent test a fix on a file another agent is actively editing without committing that agent's work. That dissolved the ownership deadlock on mi6b, where the one-line fix sat in a peer's worktree and AGENTS.md forbade me from committing it.
acceptance_criteria:
1. THE GATE MUST MEASURE A TREE, NOT A WORKTREE. Export with `git archive HEAD | tar -x -C <clean-dir>` and run the build there. A gate that runs in the checkout cannot see this class BY CONSTRUCTION, which is the whole point of the bead -- do not implement it as another cargo invocation in the repo root.

2. KNOWN-BAD LEG, and it is cheap to construct because all three historical instances are reproducible in shape: in a scratch clone, delete a dependency line from a Cargo.toml whose source still imports the crate, and assert the gate goes RED naming the E0432 unresolved import. Assert the MESSAGE, not the exit code -- measured this session, `cargo` returns 101 both for a missing test target and for a workspace that cannot load, so a leg matching only `rc != 0` goes green on any unrelated breakage.

3. KNOWN-GOOD LEG, mandatory. A HEAD that genuinely compiles must PASS. Measured 2026-09-06 after 068ec0e: a fresh export of HEAD returns ZERO errors, so a passing baseline exists today and the leg is runnable immediately. An attack-only gate blocks every push and gets disabled.

4. ANTI-VACUITY, three distinct arms. An export that fails to create, an empty export directory, and a cargo invocation that cannot resolve dependencies must each be a NAMED ERROR, never a pass. A 0-error report from a directory containing no crates is indistinguishable from a green tree, and this session recorded a census that reported 'src-only' for all six gates because its own table named them.

5. IT MUST HAVE A REACHABLE TRIGGER AND THE VERDICT MUST BE READ. AGENTS.md's third rule: a gate that cannot fire is worse than no gate, because the repo READS as protected -- and its correction adds that reachability is necessary and not sufficient, since six consecutive red CI runs went unread in one evening while a local receipt green-lit every commit. Name the trigger (pre-push hook, CI job, or both) AND where the verdict is consumed. A pre-push hook is the higher-value half here: it fires before the failure becomes a peer's problem, and .git/hooks is per-clone so state that limitation explicitly rather than implying fleet coverage.

6. STATE THE CLAIM AS A FLOOR-RAISE. This gate proves HEAD compiles; it does NOT prove HEAD's tests pass, that CI will pass (a runner starts with a cold cargo cache and resolves against the network, so a lockfile difference can surface something a warm local export cannot), or that the worktree is clean. Say so in the gate's own output.

7. DO NOT COUPLE IT TO `cargo check --workspace` WITHOUT READING gate.yml:34-47 FIRST. That comment deliberately excludes crates/loop-driver and crates/fleet-monitor and warns a workspace job 'would go red immediately and read as a regression from the stable flip, which it is not'. NOTE: I measured a clean HEAD export at ZERO errors on 2026-09-06 and neither crate appeared in the error list, so that comment may now be STALE. Verify before either trusting it or deleting it -- a stale exclusion is itself the defect class this repo records as a doctrine row asserting a kernel is broken long after it was fixed.

NO-CLAIM: this establishes that three instances occurred in one session, that the worktree/export split was 0 versus 2 errors on the mi6b instance, that a fresh export of HEAD is currently at 0 errors, and that the `git archive HEAD` primitive is already used in-tree at gate.yml:41. It does NOT establish that a HEAD-compiles gate would have caught all three at their introducing commit -- ycwh's crate was never committed at all, so a HEAD-only build would have seen a workspace that simply lacked that member and might have passed. That instance needs the separate untracked-glob-member check, and conflating the two would overclaim this gate's coverage.

title: P0: HEAD does not compile from a clean checkout -- one uncommitted Cargo.toml line blocks all 486 unpushed commits
description:

The worktree was the lie.'

Use 'git add -- <path> && git commit -- <path>'. NOTE THE TRAP measured tonight: 'git commit -- <pathspec>' IGNORES the index and records WORKTREE contents of those paths, per git help commit verbatim -- so committing Cargo.toml will take whatever else is uncommitted in that same file. title: P0: our grader re-runs the SAME acceptance the implementer saw -- SpecBench (arXiv:2605.21384) measures that exact architecture failing, with the visible/held-out gap growing 28pp per 10x code size
description: MEASURED AND SOURCE-VERIFIED 2026-09-05 by pane 1. THE DEFECT IN OUR OWN GRADING ARCHITECTURE: every grade in this session re-executed the acceptance criteria the implementer was given. The implementer sees the acceptance, writes code and tests to satisfy it, and the non-author grader then re-runs THE SAME criteria. That is a single-surface oracle, and it is the architecture SpecBench measures failing. SOURCE, verified by reading the abstract page rather than accepting a subagent's citation: arXiv:2605.21384, 'SpecBench: Measuring Reward Hacking in Long-Horizon Coding Agents', Zhao, Srikanth, Wu, Jiang, submitted 2026-05-20, cs.SE. Its opening sentence is our condition verbatim: 'As long-horizon coding agents produce more code than any developer can review, oversight collapses onto a single surface: the automated test suite. Reward hacking naturally arises in this setup, as the agent optimizes for passing tests while deviating from the users true goal.' ITS METHOD IS THE FIX WE LACK: decompose a task into (i) a natural-language specification, (ii) VISIBLE validation tests exercising specified features in isolation, and (iii) HELD-OUT tests that COMPOSE those same features to simulate real usage; a genuine agent passing (i)+(ii) also passes (iii), so the pass-rate gap between the two suites quantifies reward hacking. MEASURED RESULTS THAT APPLY DIRECTLY TO US: 'while every frontier agent saturates the visible suite, reward hacking persists'; the gap 'grows by 28 percentage points for every tenfold increase in code size'; failure modes range from subtle feature isolation to deliberate exploits including 'a 2,900-line hash-table compiler that memorizes test inputs'. This workspace is 72 members and ~133k Rust LOC, so the scaling result predicts substantial pressure at our size rather than a toy risk. WHY OUR EXISTING MECHANISM IS NOT THIS: the mutation leg (break the thing the gate keys on, the leg must go RED) tests whether a test is ATTRIBUTABLE, and it works -- it caught a guard invisible to 63 of 63 tests tonight, and a second guard whose mutation turned exactly one test red. But attributability is not generalisation. A test can be perfectly attributable to the feature it was written for and still be the only composition anyone checks. Held-out composition tests answer the different question of whether the implementation generalises past the visible suite, and nothing in this repo asks it. CORROBORATING SOURCE, also verified by reading: arXiv:2510.10931 v2, 'Proof-of-Use: Mitigating Tool-Call Hacking in Deep Research Agents', Ma et al., names the mechanism as 'weak observability of causal dependencies' producing 'hallucinated tool usage where tool calls are largely decorative', and its mitigation is that agents 'must auditably cite normalized evidence identifiers' -- which is what our close-reason file:line citation rule already does, so our evidence discipline has independent support while our acceptance architecture does not. ACCEPTANCE: (1) a bead's acceptance is split into a VISIBLE set the implementer receives and a HELD-OUT composition set it does not; (2) the grader runs both and reports the gap as a number, not a verdict; (3) a nonzero gap is a typed outcome distinct from failure, because the paper's finding is that the gap is normal and its SIZE is the signal; (4) the held-out set must COMPOSE features rather than restate them, since isolated restatement is what the visible suite already covers; (5) known-bad leg: plant an implementation that satisfies the visible set by special-casing its inputs -- the 2,900-line memorizing compiler in miniature -- and the held-out set must catch it, or the split is decoration; (6) the held-out set may not be authored by the implementer, which is R6 extended from closure to acceptance authorship. FALSIFIER: if visible and held-out pass rates are identical across ten graded beads, the held-out set is not composing anything and the mechanism is theatre. NO-CLAIM: three cited papers were verified to exist and to say what is quoted here. None of them measured THIS repo, the 28pp-per-10x figure is their result on 30 systems-level tasks and not a prediction validated here, and adopting a split acceptance does not by itself prove any bead was reward-hacked.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Implement the visible/held-out split as typed data on the bead: `acceptance.visible[]` (delivered to implementer) and `acceptance.held_out[]` (never rendered into any implementer-facing prompt, diff, or bead show output). Prove the isolation with a live command that dumps the exact implementer payload for a real bead and greps it for each held-out item's id and text — zero hits required, and the grep must be run against the actual serialized payload, not a re-render.

2. KNOWN-BAD leg, using the description's own miniature-memorizer construction: plant an implementation that special-cases the literal inputs named in the visible set (a hash-table/if-chain over the visible fixtures). Required outcome: visible pass rate = 100%, held-out pass rate < 100%, gap > 0. An already-green grade row from tonight's session is NOT evidence for this leg: every such row re-ran the criteria the implementer saw, so it cannot distinguish a generalizing implementation from a memorizing one — that is the exact defect being fixed. The known-bad leg must be a new run against the planted memorizer, with the planted diff's checksum recorded.

3. KNOWN-GOOD leg so the mechanism is not over-strict: a genuine implementation (the pre-plant HEAD of the same crate) must show visible pass = held-out pass = 100%, gap = 0, and the grader must emit `GapZero` as a PASS, not an error. If the known-good leg also reports a nonzero gap, the held-out set is testing unspecified behavior and must be rewritten before the bead closes.

4. Anti-vacuity: if `held_out` is empty, unparsed, or zero tests were actually executed (assert an executed-test count > 0 harvested from the runner's own output, not from the harness's intent), the grader returns a typed `Err(HeldOutEmpty)` / `Err(NoTestsExecuted)`. An empty or all-skipped held-out set must never render as a pass or as gap = 0. Include a live negative run proving the error fires.

5. Mutation leg: break the gap computation itself — e.g. make the grader report `gap = 0` unconditionally, or make it read held-out results from the visible run. Re-run the known-bad leg; it must go RED (gap now 0 on the planted memorizer, so the leg's assertion fails). Restore byte-identically and record `sha256` of the file before and after; the two checksums must be shown equal in the close reason.

6. Typed outcome, not verdict: grader output must carry `visible_pass_rate`, `held_out_pass_rate`, `gap_pp`, and `outcome ∈ {GapZero, GapNonzero(pp), HeldOutEmpty, NoTestsExecuted}`. `GapNonzero` is distinct from `Fail` — assert in a unit test that a nonzero gap does not by itself set a failing exit code, per the paper's finding that the gap is normal and its size is the signal.

7. Composition requirement, mechanically checked, not asserted in prose: each held-out item must reference ≥2 distinct visible item ids it composes, and the checker must reject a held-out item whose assertion text is a substring/near-restatement of any single visible item. Show one rejected candidate and one accepted candidate from real bead text.

8. MEASURED LIVE vs FIXTURE: the visible/held-out isolation grep, the planted-memorizer known-bad run, the known-good run, the anti-vacuity error, and the mutation RED/restore must all be executed live in this workspace with pasted command output. The bead corpus used to exercise the composition checker MAY be a fixture, but must be ≥3 real beads' acceptance text copied verbatim with their bead ids cited.

9. R6 extension: record the author identity of each held-out item and assert `held_out.author != bead.implementer` at grade time; violation is a typed `Err(SelfAuthoredHeldOut)`, with a live run showing it fire on a deliberately self-authored item.

10. OPEN SUB-ITEMS from the description that must not be silently absorbed: (a) the FALSIFIER — "visible and held-out pass rates identical across ten graded beads" — is not satisfiable by this bead alone; file a separate bead to collect the ten-bead gap distribution and evaluate the falsifier, and cite its id here. (b) the truncated NO-CLAIM ("three cited papers we…") must be completed in the description or explicitly marked as an unverified claim; the 28pp/10x scaling figure and arXiv:2605.21384 must be marked verified-by-abstract-read (as stated) while any inference from it to our 133k-LOC workspace is labeled a prediction, not a measurement.

title: ack_detector tests are coupled to live tracker state and mutate a real closed bead
description:
WHAT: crates/ack-spine/tests/ack_detector.rs hardcodes the bead id `omp-orchestrator-nrj` at lines 11, 33 and 86. Those tests pass ONLY on a machine whose tracker already contains that bead, and every run posts `br comments add` to a REAL bead in the REAL tracker.

HOW IT WAS FOUND -- and tree-green hid it completely: I extracted `git archive HEAD` into a clean directory and ran the suite from the REPOSITORY rather than the working tree.
  working tree : ack_detector 4 passed, exit 0
  clean extract: ack_detector 1 passed, 3 FAILED, exit 101
Verbatim failures:
  genuinely_posted_comment_is_confirmed -> "br comments add must succeed: Error: Issue not found: omp-orchestrator-nrj"
  singular_verb_trap_produces_missing_ack -> "the singular-verb trap must produce Missing, got Unverifiable { bead_id: \"omp-orchestrator-nrj\", detail: \"br comments list exited Some(3): Error: Issue not found\" }"
  read_back_distinguishes_trap_from_good -> same Unverifiable shape

THE DETECTOR IS RIGHT AND THE TEST IS WRONG. Returning `Unverifiable` when the tracker cannot resolve the bead is EXACTLY what oj6.2's acceptance demands -- "An unreadable tracker is an ERROR, never 'no ack'." The extract run therefore fired the detector's anti-vacuity leg FOR REAL, unplanned, and the test asserted `Missing` against it. Do not weaken the detector to make the test pass; that would invert the leg.

TWO DEFECTS:
1. ENVIRONMENT COUPLING. README promises "install it on any of our machines". These tests cannot pass on a machine without this tracker, so vision goal 9 is false while they stand.
2. SHARED-STATE MUTATION. Every run appends a comment to `omp-orchestrator-nrj`, which is a CLOSED bead titled "GRADER-STALENESS-PROBE (deletion candidate)". The tests write to production tracker state, and they are pinned to a bead someone is expected to delete. When it is deleted the suite goes red for a reason unrelated to the code -- the same class as today's port that deleted four scripts and silently invalidated every closed bead citing them.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. HERMETIC: the tests create their own scratch tracker (temp dir + `br --db`, or a scratch bead they create and delete), assert, and clean up. No hardcoded live bead id anywhere in the file.
2. THE PROOF IS THE EXTRACT, NOT THE TREE: `git archive HEAD | tar -x -C <tmp>` then `cargo test -p ack-spine` from that directory must exit 0. Tree-green is explicitly NOT acceptance for this bead, because tree-green is the condition that hid the defect.
3. PRESERVE THE THREE-VALUED VERDICT: Missing / Confirmed / Unverifiable must remain distinct, and a test must assert Unverifiable for an unreadable tracker, since that path now has a live specimen.
4. NO WRITES TO PRODUCTION TRACKER STATE from any test. Known-bad: point the suite at the real tracker and assert it refuses rather than mutating.
5. MUTATION: re-hardcode a live bead id, leg 2 goes RED from the extract. Restore byte-identically, report the sha both sides.

NO-CLAIM: this is one crate's suite. Whether other crates' tests are environment-coupled is UNMEASURED -- the extract harness that found this can answer it, and that is a separate bead, not an assumption to fold in here.

BOTH NAMED DEFECTS ARE GONE, verified in the extract by inspection, not inferred from a green suite:

The `#[path = "../src/authorities.rs"] mod authorities;` private copy is GONE, so those 8 tests now exercise THE LIBRARY'S copy. title: P0: the cross-pane hold cannot distinguish redo-this-work from grade-this-work, so it structurally blocks the only eligible non-author grader
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-06 by pane 1 on build b2d131b7e757. This is why grade beads never dispatch, and it is INDEPENDENT of the ledger-completeness cause.

THE CATCH-22, all four facts measured on one bead:
  omp-orchestrator-dispatch-alignment-not-decidable-9y8d
    status in_progress, P0, created_by pane1-omp-claude (so pane 1 CANNOT grade it)
    DONE/VERDICT evidence present: 1 comment
    ACK pane: %9
    receiver_verified row in the lifecycle ledger: 1   <- it IS a valid grading candidate
  %8 is IDLE and is a NON-AUTHOR -- the ideal grader.
  The cross-pane hold refuses %8 with CROSS_PANE_DUPLICATE held_pane=%9 target_pane=%8.
  %8 burned FIVE consecutive ticks on this class: t18, t19, t20, t21, t23, across two beads
  (w1s9 then 9y8d), each time refused because another pane holds a bead it FINISHED.

MECHANISM: the hold keys on identity_key = bead|repo|session|pane|sha|MANUAL. A grade delivery and a
work delivery are indistinguishable at that key -- both are 'send bead X to pane Y'. So the hold,
whose purpose is to stop %8 REDOING %9's work, also stops %8 GRADING %9's work. The two are opposite
intents with identical shape.

WHY THIS IS SEPARABLE FROM THE LEDGER GAP: I measured 332 tracker beads carrying DONE/VERDICT against
only 28 with a receiver_verified ledger row, so 304 finished beads are invisible to
LifecycleLedger::receiver_verified_candidates (the live path's only candidate source, main.rs:2140).
That is one blocker. THIS bead is the second: for the 28 that ARE visible, the hold blocks the
grader. Fixing either alone leaves grading dead.

AND A THIRD NARROWING IN THE SAME FUNCTION, worth recording here rather than losing: the live path
requires the CANDIDATE'S OWN RECEIVER PANE to be currently dispatchable --
  let idle = observation.panes.filter(|p| p.is_dispatchable)
  for candidate in candidates { let Some(receiver_pane) = idle.find(|p| p.pane_id == candidate.identity.target.pane) else { continue } }
So a completion is gradeable only while the pane that produced it happens to be idle. %9 holds 57
completions; the moment %9 takes new work, all 57 drop out of the candidate set.

SO no_distinct_idle_peer IS WRONG IN A THIRD WAY. I previously recorded it reports a CAPACITY fact
for an IDENTITY cause. It also reports capacity for a LEDGER-COMPLETENESS cause (304 of 332 absent)
and for a HOLD-COLLISION cause (grader refused). One reason code, four distinct causes.

ACTION TAKEN: parked 9y8d with the grading debt recorded on the bead, to stop %8 burning a sixth
tick. Parked, not closed -- I authored it and a non-author still owes the grade.

NO-CLAIM: measured 9y8d's status/author/ACK pane/DONE evidence/receiver_verified count, the five
blocked ticks, the 332-vs-28 split, and the three code sites. NOT measured: whether the hold has an
explicit grade-intent bypass elsewhere that simply is not reached -- I read gate_peer_grading_inner's
first 58 lines and the dispatch refusal path, not every caller. If such a bypass exists, this bead
narrows to 'the bypass is unreachable' rather than 'the distinction does not exist'.

Expect the hold to ADMIT a grade delivery to a non-author pane while still REFUSING a work delivery of the same bead to that same pane. Both legs required -- admitting both, or refusing both, is the current defect in either direction.
2. LIVE PROOF: with one bead that has a receiver_verified row, DONE evidence, an author pane that is idle, and a second idle non-author pane, the loop must DISPATCH THE GRADE. Cite the heartbeat row. Baseline to beat: five consecutive CROSS_PANE_DUPLICATE refusals (t18-t23) with an idle non-author available throughout.
3. KNOWN-BAD (mandatory): a grade delivery routed to the bead's OWN author must still be refused as self_grade. That leg must FAIL when the intent discriminator is removed, or it proves nothing.
4. REASON-CODE SPLIT: no_distinct_idle_peer must no longer cover ledger-absence or hold-collision. Emit distinct codes and assert all three from the LIVE path, not the library.

JOSHUA'S CHALLENGE: 'why do we have a specific grader - any non author should qualify.' He is right, and it subsumes what I filed. THE MECHANISM, verbatim from gate_peer_grading_inner (crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs:2140):
  let grader_idle = observation.panes.iter().any(...);
  if grader_idle { return Ok(Some(PeerGradeClaim{..})) }
  in_flight.push(claim.grader_pane.clone());
  ... .retain(|pane| !in_flight.iter().any(|grader| grader == &pane.pane_id));

A stranded claim whose named grader is not idle STRIPS that pane from the idle set and returns None --
no grading at all that tick. With 14 stranded claims across all three live workers, every pane is
stripped every tick. Grading cannot happen, structurally. That is the complete explanation for
no_distinct_idle_peer, and it subsumes the four causes I had been listing separately.

title: P0: cross_pane_hold treats a stale grading_started row as a work holder -- refuses the verified worker every tick and stalls the loop
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-06 by pane 1, on code that went live minutes ago in the rebuild+restart Joshua authorised. This is a FALSE POSITIVE in crates/omp-orchestrator/src/cross_pane_hold.rs, which I graded and closed earlier tonight as bead omp-orchestrator-cross-pane-duplicate-dispatch-7lsb -- explicitly noting then that it 'has never executed in production and cannot until a restart'. It has now executed, and its first two firings are both wrong.

THE SYMPTOM: ticks 2 and 3 on the new build both emitted, verbatim and identically:

  DISPATCH_FAILED detail=DISPATCH_BLOCKED bead=omp-orchestrator-jplf.9 pane=%8
    reason=CROSS_PANE_DUPLICATE held_pane=%9 target_pane=%8
    identity_key=omp-orchestrator-jplf.9|/Users/josh/Developer/omp-orchestrator|omp-orchestrator|%9|sha256:efcb4c5067be...|MANUAL
    owner=josh next_action=wait-for-reap-or-abandon

So the loop selected the same bead, targeted the same pane, and refused for the same reason on two consecutive ticks -- dispatching nothing.

THE HOLDER IS A GRADER, NOT A WORKER. The lifecycle ledger holds 7 rows for jplf.9; the last four are:

  grading_started    pane=%9   written=1788709930
  selected           pane=%8   written=1788709938
  dispatch_receipt   pane=%8   written=1788709939
  receiver_verified  pane=%8   written=1788709976

%9 was assigned as GRADER. %8 is the WORKER and reached receiver_verified -- a CONFIRMED receipt. The hold reads LifecycleLedger::in_flight_for_bead, finds %9's never-terminated grading_started row, and treats it as a conflicting holder of the work. It then refuses the very pane that already has a verified receipt.

AND THE GRADER IS IDLE. tick-monitor reports %9 as IDLE t0 -- it lost its in-pane context in the restart and is not grading anything. So the hold is enforcing a claim whose owner is provably not working.

THREE DEFECTS COMPOUND HERE, and the third is the new one:
  1. dp21 (blocked): a bead with a confirmed receipt stays selectable, so the loop keeps re-offering jplf.9 despite receiver_verified.
  2. The 8js3 class, which I closed earlier: a grading_started row with no terminal event. I fixed the GRADING GATE to ignore stale claims (commit 4703b6e, ledger.rs active_grading_claims gained a tracker filter). I did NOT fix the ROW never terminating, and cross_pane_hold reads that same untermina ted row through a different door.
  3. NEW: cross_pane_hold conflates the grader role with the holder role. A grading claim and a work dispatch are different relations to a bead, and the hold has one notion of 'holds'.

WHY IT IS WORSE THAN THE DEFECT IT PREVENTS: an unprotected duplicate dispatch wastes a slot. This converts a duplicate into a PERMANENT STALL -- every tick re-selects, re-targets, re-refuses, and dispatches nothing. Its own next_action says 'wait-for-reap-or-abandon', so the design expects an external actor to break the cycle; nothing in the loop does.

CONTAINMENT TAKEN, not a fix: I set jplf.9 to `blocked`, which stops selection and frees the loop. Same mechanism I used on dp21 an hour ago for the classify() substring defect. The bead has a verified receipt on %8 and may have real outstanding work; blocking parks it visibly rather than closing it on someone else's behalf.
acceptance_criteria:
1. KNOWN-BAD LEG, reproducible from the live case: a bead whose ledger carries `grading_started pane=%A` AND `receiver_verified pane=%B` must NOT be refused when dispatched to %B. Construct it from jplf.9's exact row sequence (grading_started %9, selected %8, dispatch_receipt %8, receiver_verified %8). Assert the returned verdict, not an exit code.

2. KNOWN-GOOD LEG, mandatory and the reason this hold exists: two concurrent WORK dispatches of one bead to two panes must still be refused. Do not fix this by weakening the hold to always admit -- 7lsb measured 7 beads carrying ACKs from 2+ distinct panes, and the hold is the only mechanism that refuses that. An over-broad fix reintroduces the defect it was built for.

3. DISCRIMINATE ON ROLE, NOT ON PRESENCE. The ledger already distinguishes the roles: `grading_started` carries a top-level `grader_pane` field, while dispatch rows carry `pane` and `evidence.receiver_pane`. So in_flight_for_bead must filter to WORK rows and exclude grading rows, or return the role alongside the pane and let the caller decide. The data is already there -- this is a query defect, not a schema gap.

4. A TERMINAL EVENT FOR GRADING IS THE DEEPER FIX. `grading_started` has no counterpart. I measured 10 grading_started rows on this build and the vocabulary has no grading_complete or grading_abandoned, so every grading claim is in-flight forever. That is the same missing-terminal-state defect as dp21's `receiver_verified`, and it is why the 8js3 fix had to filter rather than rely on state. Fixing the vocabulary fixes both doors at once.

5. ANTI-VACUITY: an unreadable or empty ledger must be a NAMED error, never 'no holder found'. A hold that admits because it could not read its own state is the false-green this lane exists to close, and crossalready types HolderScan::Unnamed distinctly from Zero for exactly this reason -- preserve that distinction.

6. THE STALL MUST BE BOUNDED REGARDLESS. Even with role filtering, any repeated refusal on one bead currently consumes every tick indefinitely. Either the selector must not re-offer a bead that was refused, or the refusal must clear the in-flight row, or the hold must expire. Name which and assert it -- two consecutive ticks dispatched nothing tonight and the mechanism had no way to stop.

NO-CLAIM: measured are the two identical refusal rows at ticks 2 and 3, the four ledger rows with their panes and unix timestamps, %9's IDLE t0 state, jplf.9's tracker row, and the absence of any grading terminal event in the 10 grading_started rows on this build. NOT measured: cross_pane_hold's source at the new HEAD -- I read its committed version hours ago when grading 7lsb, where scan() returned Zero/Named/Unnamed over InFlightIdentity rows, and I have NOT re-read it since the rebuild, so the precise line where the grading row enters the holder set is inferred from behaviour rather than located in code.

title: 17 extraction-wave crates handroll ~144 unbounded spawns; kernel now has bounded_status
description:
WHAT: 17 extraction-wave crates spawn child processes with no subprocess-contract dependency and
no allowance row. Measured 2026-09-01 by `cargo test -p no-shell-gate --test spawn_contract`:

  fast-dispatch 32, loop-driver 28, fleet-truth 13, tick-dispatch 10, reap-finished-panes 10,
  fleet-reconcile 9, pane-dispatch-ready 9, oracle-compare 7, pane-oracle-diff 4, pane-truth 4,
  dispatcher-deadman 3, omp-idle-dispatch 3, oracle-pane-state-differential 3, verify-dispatch 3,
  wired-but-inert-guard 3, refill-idle-panes 2, loop-tick 1
  = 17 crates, ~144 sites (scratch-home's 1 site is DONE, see below)

WHY THIS IS NOT AN ALLOWANCE PROBLEM: adding 17 allowance rows would turn the strongest gate in
the repo advisory. Earlier today the orchestrator challenged another pane for exactly that shape
- "an exception is a NAMED ROW WITH A REASON; a row saying 'extraction wave' with no caller named
is a placeholder, and the extraction did not wire those lanes, it EXEMPTED them." Filing 17 of
them would be committing the error we flagged. The gate stays RED and honest until the work is
done.

THE KERNEL WAS INCOMPLETE, AND THAT IS WHY THE HANDROLLS EXIST. `subprocess-contract` shipped only
`bounded_output`, which PIPES stdout/stderr. A passthrough spawn - a wrapper handing control to
ntm, a child whose output belongs on the operator's terminal - cannot use it without silently
swallowing the output the spawn exists for. So callers reached for a bare `.status()` with NO
DEADLINE. That is the AGENTS.md KERNEL-ONLY rule biting in its stated direction: "every handroll
is locally cheaper and removes exactly the pressure that would have fixed the kernel."

ALREADY DONE, and it unblocks the rest:
 - `subprocess_contract::bounded_status` added: inherits stdio (no pipes, so the ~64KiB
   undrained-pipe deadlock cannot form), process-group leader, TERM-then-graced-KILL on the
   GROUP, bounded post-kill reap, TimedOut restrictive with no status. 4 tests including a
   GRANDCHILD-SURVIVAL leg. Mutation-verified twice: kill the pid instead of the group -> the
   grandchild survives and the test names it; let TimedOut return Completed -> caught. Restore
   byte-identical.
 - scratch-home converted as the reference: 18 -> 17 crates.

ACCEPTANCE:
 1. Each crate either depends on subprocess-contract and routes every spawn through
    `bounded_output` (needs bytes) or `bounded_status` (passthrough), OR carries an allowance row
    naming a REAL reason - not "extraction wave".
 2. Every converted site names a deadline const with a comment justifying its value. A false
    timeout that kills healthy work is worse than a slow one.
 3. TimedOut must never be foldable into the caller's failure path: a killed child is not a
    failed child and the remedies differ. Grep each conversion for that collapse.
 4. spawn_contract goes green with an anti-vacuity leg proving an empty scan set is an ERROR.
 5. Per-crate, path-scoped commits. Four panes share this checkout.

NO-CLAIM: routing a spawn through the contract bounds how long we WAIT, not how long the child
runs after we stop waiting. TERM-then-KILL is best effort and a process in uninterruptible state
survives us. This raises a floor from "blocks forever" to "returns a typed restrictive outcome".

title: P0: lifecycle idempotency key is TICK-scoped -- a restart replays tick 1,2,3 and collides with the prior run, so the unwedged grade dispatch is refused forever
description: MEASURED 2026-09-06 by pane 1 from live heartbeat rows immediately after restarting onto pane4-%9's wedge fix 137faec. THE WEDGE FIX WORKS -- this is the defect it revealed underneath, which is the fourth layer of the same starvation onion tonight. WHAT THE LIVE ROWS PROVE ABOUT 137faec, behaviourally rather than by build label: 'tick=2 PEER_GRADING_REQUIRED bead=omp-orchestrator-eg0m receiver_pane=%8 grader_pane=%9' is followed by 'DISPATCH_RESULT_RECORDED ... bead=omp-orchestrator-eg0m', 'DISPATCH_INTENT_CLEARED', and 'SUPERVISOR_REFUSED'. Under the old binary PEER_GRADING_REQUIRED was the LAST row of the tick -- ten consecutive ticks emitted it and nothing else, because main.rs:4393 returned early. Now the tick emits the requirement AND THEN ATTEMPTS A DISPATCH. Grade dispatched, not awaited. SECOND FIX ALSO CONFIRMED: the row now reads 'bead=omp-orchestrator-eg0m receiver_pane=%8' where it previously read 'bead=<active-peer-grade> receiver_pane=<ledger>'. Real identifiers, angle-bracket placeholders gone -- the second defect I asked pane4 to diagnose or file is diagnosed and fixed. THE NEW DEFECT: the dispatch is refused with 'LIFECYCLE_LEDGER_REFUSED bead=omp-orchestrator-eg0m pane=%9 error=LIFECYCLE_LEDGER_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT key=omp-orchestrator-eg0m:selected:2'. ROOT CAUSE, read from crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs:1939: 'let selected_id = EventId::new(format!("{bead}:selected:{tick}"))'. The idempotency key is scoped to the TICK NUMBER, and the tick counter RESETS TO 1 ON EVERY SUPERVISOR RESTART. So run N tick 2 and run N+1 tick 2 produce the byte-identical key. The ledger correctly refuses the duplicate; the refusal is not the bug. THE KEY IS THE BUG: it identifies a position within a run rather than an event in a history. WHY IT IS FATAL RATHER THAN COSMETIC: the supervisor has restarted 13-plus times tonight, so ticks 1 through roughly 12 are replayed on every restart and every one of their keys is already present. eg0m was first selected at tick=2 of an earlier run; it can now NEVER be re-selected at tick=2 again, and since the grading requirement fires early in each fresh run, the collision is hit immediately and permanently. The grade cannot be dispatched, the requirement cannot clear, and the loop is wedged again -- for a completely different reason than vn78. SAME FAMILY AS THE t7us LIVELOCK, and this is the second time tonight a restart destroyed the very state the next attempt needed: there, a restart reset the two-capture window so the preflight could never accumulate two captures; here, a restart resets the tick counter so every idempotency key collides. In both cases the restart is the ordinary recovery action and it is what guarantees the next failure. AGENTS.md's C112 is adjacent: an ownership claim must name something that dies with the thing it owns. A tick number dies with the run; the ledger row it keys does not. SUGGESTED SHAPE, not prescribed: key on something unique per event across runs -- the existing build_id, the pid, a monotonic sequence persisted in the ledger, or a timestamp -- so that {bead}:selected:{run}:{tick} or an equivalent cannot repeat. Note the ledger ALREADY carries build_id and pid on its rows, so the identity exists and is simply not in the key. NO-CLAIM: this establishes the wedge fix changed behaviour on live rows, that placeholders are gone, that the key is tick-scoped at main.rs:1939, and that the resulting conflict refused the grade dispatch for eg0m at key ...selected:2. It does NOT establish how many other keys are currently colliding -- my per-key duplicate census was still running when I filed -- nor whether any non-grading dispatch path shares the same key shape. It also does NOT resolve a separate observation worth someone's attention: the live rows report build=d4b320bb93 while the installed artifact hash is cfd29b52 and HEAD is 137faec, so the build_id label and the artifact do not obviously correspond, and behaviour rather than the label is what I used as proof.
acceptance_criteria:
1. KNOWN-BAD leg (must fail before fix, pass after): construct two runs whose tick counters both reach 2 for bead omp-orchestrator-eg0m, with the second run started fresh (tick reset to 1). Assert the second run's selected-event key is NOT byte-identical to the first's and that the dispatch is ACCEPTED, not LIFECYCLE_LEDGER_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. The already-present ledger row `key=omp-orchestrator-eg0m:selected:2` from tonight's runs is NOT sufficient evidence: it is a single historical artifact that proves collision happened, not that the new key derivation cannot repeat; the test must generate both keys itself from the shipping code path at main.rs:1939 (or its successor) within one test process, and compare.

2. KNOWN-GOOD leg (must still be REFUSED after fix, so the fix is not merely "make every key unique"): within a SINGLE run, the same bead selected twice at the same tick with the same run identity must still produce a byte-identical key and must still be refused with LIFECYCLE_LEDGER_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. Genuine idempotency must be preserved; a fix that keys on a fresh timestamp/UUID per call and thereby permits true duplicate replay is a FAIL.

3. Anti-vacuity: the key-collision census and any scan over ledger rows must return a typed error (e.g. `LedgerScanError::NoRowsExamined`) when zero rows, zero keys, or zero runs are examined. An empty scan, a filter that matches nothing, or a test that never reaches the key-construction site must be a hard ERROR, never a green pass. Assert a positive lower bound: at least 2 distinct run identities and at least 1 shared (bead, tick) pair were compared.

4. Mutation proof: revert the key derivation at crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs:1939 back to `format!("{bead}:selected:{tick}")`, record sha256 of main.rs before mutation, run the suite, and show items 1 and 3 go RED (item 2 must stay GREEN, proving the two legs discriminate). Restore the file and show the post-restore sha256 is byte-identical to the pre-mutation checksum; paste both hashes.

5. MEASURED live vs fixture: the collision-free behaviour must be MEASURED live — restart the supervisor at least twice and capture real heartbeat rows showing PEER_GRADING_REQUIRED for a bead followed by DISPATCH_RESULT_RECORDED with no LIFECYCLE_LEDGER_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT for that bead's selected key across the restart boundary; quote the rows with their key values. The ledger backend, the two-run key comparison in item 1, and the same-run duplicate in item 2 MAY be fixtures/in-process. The run identity source (build_id/pid/persisted sequence) must be read from the same place the ledger rows already carry it — cite the file:line where build_id and pid are attached to ledger rows and show the key now reuses that value rather than inventing a parallel one.

6. Unmeasured sub-item — per-key duplicate census: the description states the census was still running at filing. Either (a) complete it and report the full count of currently-colliding keys and which beads/ticks are permanently blocked, plus a stated migration/backfill decision for pre-existing tick-scoped rows (are old keys ignored, namespaced, or purged?), or (b) file it as a separate bead and reference the id here. Do not let the fix silently orphan beads whose old `:selected:N` rows still shadow them.

7. Unmeasured sub-item — other dispatch paths: the description explicitly does not establish whether non-grading dispatch paths share the tick-scoped key shape. Grep the crate for every `EventId::new(format!(` and every `:{tick}` interpolation into an event/idempotency key; list each site with file:line and state for each whether it is fixed, provably run-scoped already, or filed separately. A zero-hit grep is a typed ERROR under item 3, not a pass.

8. Unmeasured sub-item — build label mismatch: live rows report build=d4b320bb93 while the installed artifact hash is cfd29b52 and HEAD is 137faec. Since the fix keys on run identity possibly derived from build_id, an unreliable build_id label is load-bearing. Either demonstrate build_id is still unique-per-run regardless of the label discrepancy (and show that pid or a persisted sequence carries uniqueness if build_id repeats across restarts of the same artifact — note a rebuilt-identical binary restarted twice yields the SAME build_id, so build_id alone MUST NOT be the sole run discriminator), or file the label/artifact correspondence as a separate bead and cite its id.

comments.text: CORRECTION by pane 1, 2026-09-06, from a live row: this defect is PER-RESTART TRANSIENT, not permanent, and my original description overstated it. I wrote that eg0m 'can now NEVER be re-selected at tick=2 again' and that the grade 'cannot be dispatched' -- the first clause is right, the second is wrong. Live evidence: 'DISPATCH_RESULT tick=11 pane=%9 bead=omp-orchestrator-eg0m status=DISPATCH_FAILED detail=ACK_STAGE_INDETERMINATE reason=ACK_PANE_MISMATCH expected=%9 got=%8'. The dispatch at tick=11 got PAST the ledger entirely and reached the ACK stage, because key eg0m:selected:11 had never been used. So the collision is confined to tick numbers already consumed by a previous run -- roughly ticks 1 through 12 given tonight's restart count -- and the loop SELF-HEALS by simply advancing past them. THAT MAKES THE DEFECT CHEAPER AND ALSO SUBTLER. Cheaper: it is a startup-window stall, not a permanent wedge, so the loop escapes on its own after a few minutes. Subtler: the stall is proportional to how many ticks previous runs consumed, so it lengthens every time the supervisor restarts, and it will present as 'the loop is slow to start' rather than as a refusal. It is still a real defect -- a key that identifies a position within a run rather than an event in a history -- and the fix is unchanged: include build_id, pid, or a persisted monotonic sequence, all of which the ledger rows already carry. WHAT THE SAME ROW ALSO PROVES, unrelated to this bead and worth recording: ACK_PANE_MISMATCH fired correctly. eg0m carries an ACK comment naming %8 from its earlier grading assignment, the loop dispatched it to %9, and the readback REFUSED rather than accepting a foreign pane's ACK. So pane2-%7's bb5b321 decoupling of confirmation from busy state did NOT weaken pane matching, which was the false-positive risk I mutated for and the arm my mutation confirmed. NO-CLAIM: this establishes the collision is bounded to previously-consumed tick numbers and that tick=11 passed the ledger. It does NOT establish the exact stall length -- that depends on the highest tick any prior run reached, which I have not enumerated -- and it does not retract the defect, only its severity characterisation.

comments.text: AUTHOR'S PREMISE CHECK by pane 1, 2026-09-06, run because this bead is now being worked and I authored it. My standing rule since writing two bad acceptances tonight: any bead I authored gets its known-bad leg EXECUTED before someone spends effort on it. THE STRUCTURAL PREMISE HOLDS, verified against the RUNNING tree rather than the worktree: git show 4703b6e:crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs line 1939 is still 'let selected_id = EventId::new(format!("{bead}:selected:{tick}"))'. The key is still scoped to the tick number, and the tick counter still resets to 1 on every supervisor restart. So the defect is real and unfixed. THE SYMPTOM IS NEARLY EXTINCT, AND THAT MATTERS FOR HOW IT IS WORKED: IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT rows under the current build 4703b6e -> ZERO. Across every build in the entire heartbeat -> TWO. So the collision has fired twice, total, and not at all since the current binary started at tick 1 thirty-five ticks ago. WHY THE SYMPTOM VANISHED WITHOUT THE DEFECT BEING FIXED, which is the useful part: the collision only fires when a NEW run re-selects the SAME bead at the SAME tick number a previous run used. That required eg0m to be re-selected every tick, which was 8js3's stale grading claim. Once 8js3 landed, no bead is re-selected across restarts at a low tick number, so the key never repeats. The defect is intact; its trigger was removed by fixing a different bead. THAT IS WHY MY EARLIER SEVERITY CORRECTION ON THIS BEAD WAS RIGHT AND STILL UNDERSTATED. I originally wrote 'can NEVER be re-selected at tick=2 again' and corrected it to a per-restart transient after observing tick=11 pass the ledger. The fuller truth: it is a per-restart transient WHOSE TRIGGER IS ANOTHER DEFECT. With 8js3 fixed it is currently unreachable in practice. GUIDANCE FOR WHOEVER IS WORKING IT, and this is why I am commenting rather than staying quiet: do NOT expect to reproduce this from live rows. You will find zero conflicts on the current build. The known-bad leg must be CONSTRUCTED -- restart the supervisor twice and force the same bead to be selected at the same tick ordinal, or unit-test EventId construction directly across two simulated runs. If you go looking for a live conflict you will conclude the bead is stale and it is not; the structure at :1939 is the evidence, not the row count. THE FIX IS UNCHANGED AND SMALL: the ledger rows already carry build_id and pid -- I read build_id 4703b6e8f51774952c4a8082f3170972b3bdec85-dirty and pid 81300 out of a pending-dispatch marker tonight -- so a run-scoped identity already exists and is simply not in the key. Include build_id, pid, or a persisted monotonic sequence. AGENTS.md's C112 is the doctrine: an ownership claim must name something that DIES WITH THE THING IT OWNS. A tick number dies with the run; the ledger row it keys does not. NO-CLAIM: this establishes the key is still tick-scoped in the running tree at :1939, zero conflicts under the current build, two across all builds, and that 8js3's fix removed the trigger. It does NOT establish that no other path can re-trigger it -- a future defect that re-selects a bead at a low tick number would -- nor that build_id or pid are the RIGHT key components; that is a design choice with a durability question I have not analysed, since build_id currently carries a -dirty suffix and is therefore not a stable run identifier either.

title: Lifecycle per-key duplicate census and migration policy
description:
WHAT: Complete the live per-key duplicate census for lifecycle EventId rows across supervisor restarts, including every bead/tick currently colliding and permanently blocked.
WHY: hx3n changes future keys but must not silently orphan historical tick-scoped rows. The migration policy must distinguish legacy keys from run-scoped keys and state whether old rows are ignored, namespaced, or purged.
ACCEPTANCE: Run a live census over the lifecycle ledger with a nonempty examined-row count; report total keys, duplicate keys, affected bead/tick pairs, and blocked beads; record the chosen migration/backfill policy; add a known-empty ERROR leg and a known duplicate positive control; cite the exact ledger and reader paths.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance derived from measured evidence by pane 1 (bead author of the parent, non-implementer), 2026-09-06, because this bead shipped with EMPTY acceptance and an unworkable bead is the single most common defect I have measured in this tracker tonight -- a bead with no testable acceptance gets triaged and abandoned rather than worked, which is how a P0 sat at the head of the ready queue while two agents went idle.

MEASURED STARTING STATE, run before writing these criteria: the live lifecycle ledger at /Users/josh/.local/state/flywheel/omp-orchestrator-omp-orchestrator.bead-lifecycle.jsonl holds 199 rows with 199 DISTINCT idempotency_key values and ZERO keys used more than once. Separately, 0 of those 199 keys contain ':pid', so every existing row was written by a pre-a3672f2 binary using the unscoped format.

1. CENSUS, and it must be run rather than reasoned about. Emit a per-key duplicate count over the whole lifecycle ledger and report distinct-keys, rows, and keys-with-count-greater-than-one. The current answer is 199/199/0. A census reporting a duplicate today CONTRADICTS this measurement and must be investigated before any migration is designed -- do not migrate on the strength of the parent bead's narrative, which described a collision mechanism that the historical data does not exhibit.

2. ANTI-VACUITY, non-negotiable per this repo's gate rules. An unreadable, absent, or empty ledger must be an ERROR and never a pass. A census that reports 0 duplicates because it read nothing is indistinguishable from one that read 199 clean rows, and this session has recorded eleven instrument faults of exactly that shape. State the row count alongside the duplicate count so a reader can tell the two apart.

3. KNOWN-BAD LEG, which must be CONSTRUCTED because it is not reproducible from live rows. Plant two rows sharing one idempotency_key and assert the census reports that key with count 2. The unscoped historical format bead:kind:tick makes this trivial to construct: two runs at the same tick ordinal on the same bead. Do not attempt to find a natural duplicate -- the parent's premise check established that IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT rows number 2 across ALL builds and 0 on the current one, because the trigger required eg0m's stale grading claim which 8js3 removed.

4. MIGRATION POLICY, and the honest answer may be NO MIGRATION. Given 0 measured duplicates, the defensible policy is that pre-fix unscoped keys are left in place and only post-fix rows carry run scope, with the format change documented as a ledger-schema boundary at a named commit. If the policy is instead to rewrite historical keys, it must state what run identifier is assigned to rows whose originating process is gone -- that information is not recoverable from the ledger, so a rewrite would fabricate it, which this repo refuses. Pick one, write it down, and say which rows it touches.

5. POST-FIX RE-CENSUS is required and cannot be run yet. The supervisor is currently on build 4703b6e; a3672f2 is newer and not live. After a rebuild and restart, the census must show run-scoped keys appearing (':pid' present) and still zero duplicates. Until that happens, criterion 1's answer describes only the pre-fix era.

NO-CLAIM: these criteria establish that the census is cheap, that its current answer is zero duplicates over 199 rows, and that the known-bad leg must be constructed rather than found. They do NOT establish that a migration is unnecessary -- that is criterion 4's decision to make on evidence -- nor that the ledger is the only store carrying these keys; I measured the lifecycle ledger only, and the heartbeat ledger was not examined for key reuse.

title: Reconcile build identity with installed artifact
description:
WHAT: Reconcile lifecycle build_id labels with installed artifact identity and prove run uniqueness when the same binary restarts.
WHY: hx3n relies on a run identity that must not collapse when build_id repeats. Current live rows and installed artifact hashes disagree, so the label/artifact correspondence is unmeasured.
ACCEPTANCE: Identify the producer of build_id and installed artifact hash; run two restarts of the same artifact; prove build_id, pid, and persisted sequence semantics with retained rows; refuse mismatched labels or classify them as UNKNOWN; add known-good and known-bad checks; cite exact file:line paths and artifact hashes.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance derived from measured evidence by pane 1 (bead author of the parent, non-implementer), 2026-09-06, because this bead shipped with EMPTY acceptance. It also answers a question I raised on the parent and could not resolve: I warned that build_id carries a '-dirty' suffix and is therefore not a stable run identifier. a3672f2 resolved that by composing build_id with pid and process start-nanos at main.rs:131-136, so this bead is no longer about run-identity uniqueness. It is about something worse that I measured while grading the parent.

MEASURED THREE-WAY DIVERGENCE, all four figures taken in one pass:
  running supervisor build_id : 4703b6e8f51774952c4a8082f3170972b3bdec85
  git HEAD                    : a3672f2
  installed ~/.local/bin sha  : 6ea834183a8c
  target/release sha          : 8f5f9ca3cc3c
  dirty tracked files         : 112
The running binary, the installed artifact, the freshly built artifact, and HEAD are FOUR different states. The installed artifact does not match target/release, so an install and a later rebuild have diverged.

1. A REPORTED IDENTITY MUST DISTINGUISH ALL FOUR. Any surface claiming build identity must be able to answer, separately: what commit the RUNNING process was built from, what is installed on PATH, what is in target/release, and what HEAD is. Collapsing these into one 'version' is the defect -- this session lost roughly forty ticks to exactly that collapse, when a truncated build_id[:14] hid a '-dirty' suffix and seven source sites were read against a tree that was not executing.

2. THE '-dirty' SUFFIX MUST SURVIVE TRUNCATION OR NOT BE TRUNCATED. Known-bad leg: given a build_id ending '-dirty', any display or comparison path must either show the suffix or refuse to abbreviate. Assert that a dirty identity is never rendered as if clean. This is the measured trauma, not a hypothetical: build_id 55ab3365b9a5bd9356bc9366a70251fafa15911e-dirty was read as '55ab3365b9a5bd' and every downstream source claim was unfalsifiable as a result.

3. INSTALLED-VS-RUNNING MUST BE A DISTINCT CHECK FROM INSTALLED-VS-HEAD. This repo's AGENTS.md already records that the installer's identity check compares the installed artifact against HEAD and therefore reports MISMATCH permanently for pane-truth, training operators to ignore it. Do not reproduce that shape. A restart-needed condition (installed newer than running) is a DIFFERENT operational state from a rebuild-needed condition (HEAD newer than installed), and conflating them yields an alarm that is always on.

4. ANTI-VACUITY. An absent target/release binary, an absent installed binary, or an unreadable heartbeat must each be a NAMED UNKNOWN, never a silent match and never a silent mismatch. Positive control required: with all four sources present and genuinely equal, the check must report agreement -- a checker that reports divergence unconditionally is indistinguishable from one that works, and this session recorded a census that reported 'src-only' for all six gates because its own table named them.

5. WHAT THIS BEAD MUST NOT DO: it must not resolve the divergence by rebuilding or restarting. Three panes hold in-flight work and a restart onto a different binary invalidates their live-proof legs. The deliverable is a truthful REPORT of the four states plus the two distinct staleness conditions, not an actuation.

NO-CLAIM: these criteria establish that four identity sources currently disagree, with the exact values, and that the '-dirty'-through-truncation failure is measured rather than hypothetical. They do NOT establish which of the four should be authoritative for any given consumer -- the ledger rows are authoritative about the RUNNING artifact and cargo figures are authoritative about the WORKTREE, and that split is a fact to be reported rather than a conflict to be resolved. Nor do they establish that ~/.local/bin is the only install location on PATH; the installer-name PATH shadowing recorded in AGENTS.md suggests it is not.

title: P1: DESIGN_INDEX mints 51 canonical identifiers, the PLAN.md constitution carries 12, and 40 exist only in the index -- DEF-004's class one layer down, and Round 5's IDS_CUT aimed at the wrong file
description: MEASURED 2026-09-05 by pane 1, reproducible in three commands. grep -ohE canonical-ID pattern over docs/planning/DESIGN_INDEX.md | sort -u | wc -l -> 51. Same over docs/PLAN.md -> 12, and the twelve are exactly HD-0001, HD-9999, INV-2026, WP-001, WP-002, WP-003, WP-004, WP-005, WP-006, WP-007, WP-008, WP-009. comm -23 of the two sorted sets -> 40 identifiers present in the index and ABSENT from the constitution. Round 6B independently measured the consumer side: 'Zero of the 51 canonical ID strings appear as consumers in 06-12', with ids_earned_union=7/51 across both halves, the seven being WP-003..009 as body-earned aliases. THIS IS DEF-004'S CLASS ONE LAYER DOWN. Round 3 was caught retreating an overclaim into DESIGN_INDEX.md instead of the authority file, and pane 4 named it: 'the overclaim did not retreat; it moved out of the file Round 3 was allowed to edit.' Here the index MINTS 40 identifiers the constitution never mentions, so the identifier system is 86% unearned against its own authority. AND ROUND 5'S CUT AIMED AT THE WRONG FILE: IDS_CUT=31 took the index from 72 to 51, while the constitution only ever carried 12, so cutting the index cannot change what the authority earns. THREE SPECIFICS TO RESOLVE: HD-9999 is present in the constitution and reads like a sentinel or placeholder rather than a decision -- a placeholder counted as a live identifier is a decorative ID wearing an authority's clothes; GATE-011..024 have real source rows that exist UNLABELED at docs/plan/06-gates.md:31-38 and :229-234, so the referents are real and only the labels are missing, making that ADOPT-by-labelling rather than DELETE; and the two dangling forward refs 6A named -- 02->08 Q2 economics, where 08 is the R9 end-user journey and Q2 actually lives at 00-brief section 8, and 02->09 WIRE-bead conversion as first milestone, where 09 M1 is the pane-state milestone -- each needs a ruling on whether the reference or the target is wrong. THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT THAT MUST BE ANSWERED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: an index is supposed to carry bookkeeping a constitution does not, and DEF-*, RB-* and round records have no business in a constitution, so some fraction of the 40 is a legitimate DEMOTE and the real defect number is smaller than 40. The deliverable is that number: a per-identifier ADOPT/DEMOTE/DELETE disposition summing to 40. NO-CLAIM: this bead establishes a set difference between two files and a consumer count from a 0.70-coverage read. It does not establish that any of the 40 is wrong to exist, and the disposition work is what determines the real defect count.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Reproduce the three measurements live at fix time, not from fixtures: `grep -ohE '<canonical-ID regex>' docs/planning/DESIGN_INDEX.md | sort -u | wc -l` must still report 51, the same over docs/PLAN.md must report 12 and enumerate exactly HD-0001, HD-9999, INV-2026, WP-001..WP-009, and `comm -23` of the two sorted sets must yield exactly 40 lines. Record the regex used verbatim in the artifact; a different regex than the one that produced 51/12/40 invalidates the run.

2. Ship a per-identifier disposition table with exactly 40 rows, one row per identifier from the `comm -23` output, each row carrying identifier, ADOPT | DEMOTE | DELETE, and a file:line justification. ADOPT rows must cite the PLAN.md line the identifier will be added at; DEMOTE rows must name the bookkeeping class (DEF-*, RB-*, round record, etc.) and why a constitution must not carry it; DELETE rows must cite the absence of any referent. Row count != 40, or any row without file:line, is a typed failure. The bead's own NO-CLAIM stands until this table exists: the 40-count alone is NOT evidence that 40 defects exist, and the report must state the post-disposition defect number explicitly.

3. Known-bad leg: GATE-011..024 must be classified ADOPT-by-labelling, and the checker must prove the referents are live by reading docs/plan/06-gates.md:31-38 and :229-234 and asserting the unlabeled rows are present there. The pre-existing fact that these rows already exist in 06-gates.md is NOT sufficient evidence of adoption — an unlabeled row is exactly the known-bad state, since the identifier is mintable from the index while the authority cannot resolve it. The check must fail while those rows carry no GATE-0NN label and pass only once each label sits on its row.

4. Known-good leg: WP-003..WP-009 (the ids_earned_union=7/51 body-earned aliases) and HD-0001 and INV-2026 must be asserted as already-earned and must NOT be flagged, deleted, or re-minted by the fix. A run that flags any of these nine is over-strict and fails.

5. Anti-vacuity: if either grep yields zero identifiers, if the regex compiles to a match-nothing pattern, if DESIGN_INDEX.md or PLAN.md or 06-gates.md is missing or unreadable, or if the disposition table parses to zero rows, the tool must exit with a distinct typed error (e.g. `EmptyScan`/`MissingSource`) and a nonzero status. An empty set must never render as "0 unearned identifiers" or as a pass.

6. Mutation proof, RED then restored: delete one line bearing a currently-adopted identifier from docs/PLAN.md (e.g. the WP-005 line) and rerun — the set difference must grow to 41 and the check must go RED with that identifier named. Separately, strip the newly added GATE-011 label from 06-gates.md and rerun — item 3's check must go RED. Record sha256 of each file before mutation and after restore and show the pair is byte-identical; a mismatched checksum fails the bead.

7. Rule on HD-9999 explicitly: either demonstrate it resolves to a real decision (cite file:line) or classify it as a sentinel/placeholder and remove or rename it out of the live-identifier count, with the resulting constitution count restated (12 -> 11 if removed). "Present in PLAN.md" is not sufficient evidence that it is earned.

8. Rule on the two dangling forward refs individually, each with a written verdict naming which side is wrong: 02->08 Q2 economics (08 is the R9 end-user journey; Q2 lives at 00-brief section 8) and 02->09 WIRE-bead conversion as first milestone (09 M1 is the pane-state milestone). Each verdict must be either a corrected reference (with the edit) or a corrected target, with file:line.

9. Record that Round 5's IDS_CUT=31 (index 72->51) did not and cannot change what the constitution earns, and that no part of this fix may be satisfied by further edits to DESIGN_INDEX.md alone. Any run whose only diff is inside DESIGN_INDEX.md fails. Round 6B's consumer count (0/51 consumers in 06-12, ids_earned_union=7/51) may be carried as a cited fixture; the 51/12/40 counts and the 06-gates.md label state must be measured live.

10. Any sub-item left unresolved by this bead — notably the consumer-side 0/51 gap in docs 06-12, which this bead does not close — must be filed as a separate bead with its id referenced in the closing note, never absorbed silently into the disposition table.

title: P0: the mifp identity gate halts ALL dispatch -- required registry file is ABSENT in production and a missing file is a hard DISPATCH_BLOCKED
description: MEASURED 2026-09-05 by pane 1 against the WORKTREE (uncommitted work of pane3-%8 on omp-orchestrator-wire-per-pane-sender-identity-mifp). NOT YET LANDED -- filed to catch it before install. SYMPTOM: load_subagent_identity_records (crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs:1351-1357) maps a fs::read_to_string failure to a hard Err carrying 'IDENTITY_REGISTRY_UNAVAILABLE checked=agent_mail,subagents missing=subagents', which surfaces at the dispatch admission path as 'DISPATCH_BLOCKED bead=... reason=IDENTITY_REGISTRY_UNAVAILABLE'. THE REQUIRED FILE DOES NOT EXIST: Config::subagent_registry defaults to heartbeat_ledger.with_file_name('omp-orchestrator.subagents.json') at main.rs:543-545, resolving to /Users/josh/.local/state/flywheel/omp-orchestrator.subagents.json, and ls reports it ABSENT. CONSEQUENCE: installing this binary blocks EVERY dispatch on this host while br ready holds 370 issues with no blockers -- the same shape as tonight's 17-hour idle outage, except manufactured by a guard rather than a stranded marker. The live supervisor (hub omp-supervisor pid=43048) is currently dispatching successfully -- %9 transitioned IDLE -> WORKING t57 -- only because the running binary predates this change. EVIDENCE THE GATE IS ON THE PRODUCTION PATH, NOT A TEST-ONLY SURFACE: four tests in the bin target are RED, and the decisive one is a KNOWN-GOOD leg. tests::correctly_claimed_bead_still_dispatches asserts 'a claimed bead owned by the receiver must still dispatch' and now panics at main.rs:5768 with DISPATCH_BLOCKED ... reason=IDENTITY_REGISTRY_UNAVAILABLE. Also red: tests::missing_receiver_agent_inherits_claimed_assignee, tests::finished_pane_reaper_receives_the_same_repository, tests::finished_pane_reaper_runs_through_the_production_helper. Full bin suite 76 passed / 4 failed / 1 ignored. A known-good leg going red is the signal this gate is over-strict, per AGENTS.md 'Every gate proves it bites' clause 2: an attack-only suite ships an over-strict gate, and an over-strict gate gets routed around. ROOT CAUSE, TYPED: an ABSENT registry is currently indistinguishable from a registry that EXISTS AND DENIES. Those are different facts and only the second is a negative result. This is the denied-probe rule in AGENTS.md -- a refusal, a non-zero exit, an empty result and a missing file are all UNKNOWN, never a negative -- and GATE-017's precedent in this repo is that an unavailable input is recorded as an explicit NOT_APPLICABLE rather than a blocking refusal. title: Watcher reset its stall counter on idle capacity, so an idle pane never alarmed (3 incidents/shift)
description:
WHAT: the watch loop treated a freed worker as MOTION, which RESET the stall counter, so persistent idle capacity could never raise an alarm. Fixed in 228f42a; this bead records the defect, the measurement, and the grading it still owes.

THREE INCIDENTS IN ONE SHIFT, all the same shape -- the operator noticed an idle pane before I did:
  1. %1409 and %1408 idle    -- loop recorded it at ticks 6 and 7; I never read the ledger.
  2. %1413 idle              -- loop recorded it at tick 12 and reported it free at ticks 12, 13, 14, 15
                                (about six minutes). Operator: 'idle pane 2 w/o nnotice'.
  3. (the first, earlier)    -- three panes idle simultaneously; operator: '3 of your workers idle'.
Every time the detector worked and the ESCALATION did not.

ROOT CAUSE, and it is a logic inversion, not a missing feature. crates/tick-monitor/src/main.rs, watch():
    let moved = !line.contains("new_total":0)
             || !line.contains("transitions":[])
             || !line.contains("free_capacity":[]);      <-- free capacity counted as MOTION
    if moved { no_value = 0 } else { no_value += 1 }
`no_value` counts ticks where NOTHING happened, and `stall_after` alarms on that streak. But a
worker going idle IS something happening, so every idle pane RESET the counter to zero. The one
condition most worth alarming on was the one condition guaranteed to silence the alarm. A loop that
reports healthy while capacity sits unused is 'a dead loop wearing live makeup' in the exact sense
L57 names.

SECOND DEFECT FOUND WHILE FIXING IT: free_capacity included %1397 -- the ORCHESTRATOR'S OWN PANE.
Measured at ticks 14 and 15: free=['%1397','%1413']. The conductor goes idle between turns by design,
so an alarm keyed on free capacity would have fired continuously and been trained away within an hour.
This is verbatim the 'LIVENESS counting the orchestrator as a worker' defect named in
/ntm-fleet-monitor's reporting contract, reproduced by me while building the liveness monitor.

THIRD, ARCHITECTURAL, AND NOT FULLY FIXED: the ledger is append-only and grows, and nothing pushes to
the conductor. I criticised pane-truth's --selftest for only running when a human remembers, then
built a ledger that only helps when I remember to read it. Within this harness a process cannot push
to an agent session, so 228f42a's mitigation is a single-line ATTENTION.txt overwritten every tick --
cheap enough to read first, every tick. That is a mitigation, NOT a mechanism. The real mechanism is
/loop-enforcement's LLM-substrate variant (a hook injecting a system-reminder at every wake), and
installing any hook is gated by /hook-certification's six-stage gauntlet. Until that exists, this
failure mode is contained by discipline, and discipline is what already failed three times. SAY SO
rather than claiming it is solved.

WHAT 228f42a CHANGED:
  - `free_streak` counts CONSECUTIVE ticks with free capacity, independent of `no_value`.
  - `--capacity-alarm-after` (default 2) prints a loud IDLE CAPACITY line on stdout so `hub logs`
    shows it without parsing JSON. Default is 2, not 1, because one tick of free capacity is the
    healthy case -- a worker finished, and NewlyIdle needs a second capture to confirm anyway.
  - `--exclude-pane` (repeatable) removes a pane from BOTH dispatchable and free_capacity; the live
    watcher now runs with --exclude-pane %1397 --exclude-pane %1396.
  - `free_capacity_streak` is recorded on every ledger row, so the history is auditable.
  - ATTENTION.txt: one line, overwritten each tick, three states (all occupied / free seen / IDLE
    CAPACITY for N ticks).

ACCEPTANCE -- and I cannot grade this, I wrote it:
1. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD, the leg that matters: construct a tick sequence where free capacity persists
   for >= capacity_alarm_after ticks and assert the alarm fires. Then assert that against the code at
   228f42a^ it does NOT fire. If it fires at the parent, the fix fixed nothing.
2. KNOWN-GOOD: a single tick of free capacity (one worker just finished) must NOT alarm. An alarm on
   the healthy case is how alarms get ignored -- that is the whole reason the default is 2.
3. The conductor's pane must never appear in free_capacity or dispatchable when excluded. Assert with
   %1397 both excluded and not excluded, so the flag is proven to do something.
4. ATTENTION.txt contains exactly one line and is overwritten, not appended -- assert its length does
   not grow across ticks. A growing 'attention' file is the ledger problem again.
5. Live proof: on a session where a pane is genuinely idle for two ticks, `cat ATTENTION.txt` says
   IDLE CAPACITY and `hub logs tick-monitor` shows the loud line. Paste both.
6. NO-CLAIM: this alarms; it does not dispatch. The monitor stays observation-only on purpose. And it
   cannot make the conductor read it -- see the third defect above. Do not close this bead claiming
   the class is eliminated; the mitigation reduces the cost of forgetting, it does not remove
   forgetting from the loop.
