title: rigor-atlas two-person-rule-transition-table (process-kernel #4): bead close has no transition table and no quorum — prefix-only check admits implementer self-close 8/9, prose-only graders 23/40, 18% off-policy prefixes; one closed lifecycle table + min_approvals(risk) ≥ 1 distinct non-implementer actor, fail closed on unreadable identity (qt9r, gcyf, mcq2, t784)
description:
WHAT: **The close of a bead is an approval with no transition table and no quorum: the only mechanical check is the PREFIX of the close reason (`crates/ack-spine/src/close_reason.rs`), so the implementer closes their own work (8/9 since 18:18Z), the grader exists only as prose inside the reason (23/40), and 18% of closes use a prefix outside the policy.** Replace it with ONE closed transition table for bead lifecycle (`open → in_progress → grading → closed`, terminal states admitting no further transition) plus a SEPARATE quorum policy function with a floor — `min_approvals(risk) ≥ 1 distinct actor other than the requester/implementer` — so no close path can be satisfied by a single identity. This is rigor-atlas prescription `two-person-rule-transition-table` — ranked #4 for `process-kernel` and listed for `control-kernel` — and **no bead names it** (0 open-bead matches for `two-person|second approver|distinct approv`; `qt9r` proposes the special case `actor != assignee`, not the table).

INVARIANT (PROTOCOL L1, falsifiable): *A bead never transitions `grading → closed` without at least `MinApprovals` grade rows from actors whose identity is (a) recorded by the tracker, not typed into prose, and (b) distinct from every actor recorded on the bead's implementation rows; and once a bead reaches a terminal state (`closed`, `wontfix`) no further transition is possible without an explicit `reopen` that starts a new generation.*

KERNEL SHAPE:
```
static VALID_TRANSITIONS: &[(Status, &[Status])]   // the whole lifecycle contract, one table
fn transition(from: Status, to: Status, actor: ActorId, approvals: &[GradeRow]) -> Result<Status, TransitionRefused>
fn min_approvals(risk: RiskTier, live_sessions: usize) -> usize   // separate, swappable policy, clamped down but never below the floor
```
`TransitionRefused` is a closed enum: `NotInTable { from, to }`, `Terminal { state }`, `SelfApproval { actor }`, `QuorumShort { have, need }`, `ActorUnattributed`.

MIRROR EXEMPLAR TO COPY (KNOW, opened 2026-09-02):
- `/Volumes/ZestData/dicklesworthstone-mirror/slb/internal/core/statemachine.go:16-18` — *"validTransitions defines all valid state transitions. Map key is the from state, value is a list of valid to states."* `var validTransitions = map[db.RequestStatus][]db.RequestStatus{ db.StatusPending: {Approved, Rejected, Cancelled, Timeout}, …` — the lifecycle as ONE table; `slb/internal/core/patterns.go:36-37` `MinApprovals int` — the quorum as a separate policy value per risk tier (:244 `tierApprovals(RiskTierCritical)`).
- KINDS.md control-kernel archetype (:220): *"A request whose risk tier requires SLB approval never transitions Pending->Executing without at least MinApprovals distinct approvals from actors other than the requester, and once a request reaches a terminal state no further transition is possible."*

title: The ACK wait is 30s: a busy worker reads identical to an unreachable one
description:
WHAT: **the loop waits 30 seconds for an ACK comment, so a BUSY worker is indistinguishable from
an UNREACHABLE one.** This is the next autonomy blocker after `ack-spine`, and it is the same
false-negative class the 75s two-capture rule exists to prevent.

MEASURED 2026-09-02:
  - `DISPATCH_RESULT tick=5 pane=%1409 bead=omp-orchestrator-t00 status=DISPATCH_FAILED`
    `detail=ACK_STAGE_RETRY_BLOCKED reason=ack_readback_missing after=30s`.
  - That verdict is the GOOD news and the defect at once. Reaching `AckReadbackMissing`
    (`ack-stage/src/lib.rs:308-320`) rather than `UnprovenTransport` (`:296-305`) means the
    receiver classifier already returned `ReceiptConfirmed` and the transport was ACCEPTED --
    every earlier gate passed. The loop got the whole way to the last inch autonomously.
  - An OMP agent mid-tool-call cannot read a packet and post a bead comment inside 30s. Observed
    pane timers this session routinely sit at 180s-2520s inside a single tool call.

WHY THIS IS THE SAME CLASS AS A DEFECT WE ALREADY PAID FOR: `tick-monitor`'s two-capture gap is
**75s, not 30s**, and the code comment states why -- a 30s window "called two live panes frozen,"
and the asymmetry decides the number: *a missed freeze costs idle minutes, a false freeze destroys
work in flight*. The ACK window inherits the identical asymmetry with the identical wrong number.
A premature `AWAIT_HUMAN` costs a human interrupt on work that was proceeding correctly.

ACCEPTANCE:
  1. The ACK wait is derived from the same asymmetry argument as the capture gap, not a bare
     literal, and the chosen number carries its reasoning at the definition site.
  2. Waiting is BOUNDED and CANCELLABLE per the asupersync contract -- `&Cx` first,
     `cx.checkpoint()` in the wait loop. A longer window must not become an unbounded one.
  3. A pane that is demonstrably WORKING (live timer advancing) must not produce the same verdict
     as a pane that is dead. The verdict must discriminate `busy` from `unreachable`; today both
     read `ack_readback_missing`.
  4. Fires-on-known-bad: a fixture where the ACK arrives after the old 30s bound and before the
     new one must go from RED to GREEN, and a fixture with NO ack must stay RED at any bound.
     A window change that makes the never-acking case pass is a regression, not a fix.
  5. Positive control: a real dispatch reaches `ReceiptConfirmed` end to end with no human action.

NO-CLAIM: widening a timeout is not proof of delivery -- it only stops mistaking slowness for
absence. `ack-stage:290-291` still holds: on the tmux literal fallback, receiver heuristics alone
are NEVER accepted as proof, so the ACK comment remains the only authoritative evidence the design
admits. This bead does not relax that, and must not be used to.

comments.text:
fix(ack-wait): discriminate a busy worker from an unreachable one [mutation-verified]

omp-orchestrator-iis6.

## The defect

`main.rs:47` held `const RECEIPT_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30)` — a bare
literal beside `DEFAULT_COMMAND_TIMEOUT`, with no reasoning at its definition site. On
expiry the loop emitted `ACK_STAGE_RETRY_BLOCKED … reason=ack_readback_missing after=30s`
**whether the receiving pane was mid-tool-call or dead**, so a premature `AWAIT_HUMAN`
interrupted a person over work proceeding correctly.

## WIDENING THE NUMBER IS NOT THE FIX, and the acceptance refuses it mechanically

Observed pane timers this session sat at **120s, 1320s and 1440s inside a single tool
call**. No fixed constant separates *busy* from *unreachable*; a longer window only moves
the point at which it guesses wrong. **The window decides when we re-check. It must not
decide whether a human is called.**

`RECEIPT_TIMEOUT` is unchanged at 30s, deliberately. What changed is the verdict.

## The discriminator was already paid for

`receiver_receipt::OBSERVATION_WINDOW_MIN_SECS` is 75s and already carries the asymmetry
that fixes this class: *a missed freeze costs idle minutes, a false freeze destroys work
in flight.* The same evidence answers this question — **did the pane's timer advance
across two captures at least that far apart?**

So `classify_ack_wait` lives in `receiver-receipt`, next to that floor, and **there is no
new `ACK_WAIT_SECS` constant**. Adding one would be the bare literal again, one crate
over — which is acceptance 1 satisfied by construction rather than by a comment.

Note 30s is BELOW the 75s floor, so the old window could not have answered this question
even in principle. A leg asserts that inequality so it cannot drift.

## `AckWaitVerdict`, and exactly one arm interrupts a human

```
BusyStillWorking { timer_from, timer_to, span_secs }  -> retry-next-tick        no human
Unreachable      { reason }                            -> inspect-or-redispatch  HUMAN
Indeterminate    { reason }                            -> re-observe-past-floor  no human
```

`Unreachable` reasons: `TIMER_DID_NOT_ADVANCE_ACROSS_THE_FLOOR` (the wedge `pane-truth`
already names), `PANE_IDLE_WITH_NO_ACK`, `PANE_IS_WEDGED`, `PANE_IS_BLOCKED_ON_A_DIALOG`,
`PANE_HALTED_ON_PROVIDER_402`. `Indeterminate`: `WINDOW_BELOW_FLOOR`,
`PANE_STATE_UNPROVEN`, `PANE_ID_MISMATCH`, `CAPTURES_OUT_OF_ORDER`,
`NO_PRIOR_WORKING_CAPTURE_TO_COMPARE`.

**`Indeterminate` is the state the old code did not have**: everything unconfirmed owed a
human. A clock fault, a pane-id mismatch, and an unmeasurably short window are now
neither a busy finding nor a death claim.

**The compiler found two states I had missed** — `ProviderError402` and `Unproven` — via
`E0004`, because `state-wildcard-lint` forbids a wildcard arm on a state-like enum. A
402 is a quota halt no re-dispatch clears; `Unproven` is the classifier declining to
answer, and calling that unreachable would turn "cannot tell" into a death claim. **The
gate paid for itself here.**

## WIRED, not just built

`send_and_verify` now keeps the first WORKING observation and the latest one across the
wait, and the expired branch calls the classifier. When the verdict does not owe a human
it writes a typed `ACK_WAIT_PENDING` heartbeat row and the refusal carries
`discriminator=…  owes_human=…`. A wait with no working capture reports
`discriminator=NO_WORKING_CAPTURE owes_human=unknown` — **absent evidence is named, never
silently absent.**

The first observation must be a WORKING capture: comparing against a pre-send `Idle`
yields `NO_PRIOR_WORKING_CAPTURE_TO_COMPARE` and loses the motion evidence.

Acceptance 2: the loop already had `cx.checkpoint()` and a `deadline`; both are
untouched. **A wrong bound was not converted into no bound.**

## Mutations — byte-identical restore, sha `db3871a9…3d219cc5`

```
M1 THE CHEAP FIX: let a never-acking idle pane stop owing a human
     -> a_pane_that_never_acks_stays_a_human_debt_at_every_window RED
M2 drop the window floor  -> below-floor leg RED (motion claimed across 74s)
M3 `>=` instead of `>`    -> a FROZEN timer reads as busy, wedge leg RED
```

M1 is acceptance 4's teeth: **a widening that makes the never-acking case pass is a
regression wearing a fix**, and the leg asserts the human debt survives at spans of 0,
30, 75 and 7500 seconds — because the discriminator is timer motion, not elapsed time.

M3 is a one-character mutation, which is the kind a review misses and a mutation leg does
not.

## Verification

```

cargo test -p omp-orchestrator --lib                 -> 42 passed; 0 failed
```

title: OMP_MSG_SRC is consumed on success and only its own source says so
description:
## WHAT

`OMP_MSG_SRC` is a **single-use** handoff: `pre-commit-gate.rs:780` deletes the file on a
successful commit, deliberately (`// CONSUME ON SUCCESS`), to kill the stale-source false
refusal that hit `%1409`. That behaviour is documented ONLY in the function's own comment.

Consequence, measured 2026-09-02: seven `msg-*.txt` files from one session are gone while
every other file in the same directory survives, some older. Any workflow that writes a
commit message to a file and then reuses it — for a `br comments add -f`, a peer handoff, a
receipt — loses it, and the loss looks exactly like a reaper or a permissions problem.

## THE TWO WRONG DIAGNOSES, BOTH MINE, BOTH CORRECTED BY MEASUREMENT

1. **"The scratch dir was reaped."** `ls -d /tmp/r24` shows it present. Selective deletion
   by filename, not directory reaping.
2. **"It was my `/tmp` scratch-rule violation."** The violation was real — `AGENTS.md`
   says durable scratch belongs under `ZS_SCRATCH`, not `/private/tmp` — but it is not the
   cause. The same deletion happens under any path.

Recovery, for the next agent who hits this: `git log -1 --format=%B <sha>` reproduces the
message exactly, because the commit is the durable copy.

## WHY THIS IS WORTH A ROW

The gate's own doc-comment explains it perfectly and **nothing outside that file says it**.
`AGENTS.md` teaches the `OMP_MSG_SRC=<file> git commit -F <file>` form as the sanctioned way
to commit, and does not mention that the file will not survive. An operational fact that
exists only inside the implementation it governs is the same shape as the 71-entry OMP
surface nobody consumes: discoverable in principle, invisible in practice.

## ACCEPTANCE

1. `AGENTS.md`'s commit section states that the message source is consumed on success, and
   names `git log -1 --format=%B` as the recovery.
2. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD: a leg that commits with `OMP_MSG_SRC` set and asserts the file is
   absent afterwards — so the documented behaviour is pinned and a future change to
   `round_trip_check` cannot silently stop consuming (or start consuming on failure).
3. The known-good half: a REFUSED commit must LEAVE the file in place, or an author cannot
   retry. Not currently asserted anywhere.

## NO-CLAIM

`crates/finding` is lib-only — no `[[bin]]`, so there is no kernel binary to file through
and this row was created with `br create`. That gap is the one `AGENTS.md`'s KERNEL-ONLY
section already names ("the standard exists as a type, unenforced"); this row does not fix
it, and does not measure whether `finding`'s library has any caller today.

title: installer does not compile from a clean checkout — its subprocess-contract dep is uncommitted in someone's working tree
description:
## WHAT

`crates/installer` does not compile from a clean checkout of `main`. The dependency that
makes it compile exists ONLY in somebody's working tree, uncommitted.

CI, run 33583861505, job 100103746922, step `Run cargo test -p installer` — twelve
occurrences of:

    error[E0433]: cannot find module or crate `subprocess_contract` in this scope
    error: could not compile `installer` (lib) due to 12 previous errors

Locally the same crate builds fine. The difference, measured:

    $ git status --porcelain -- crates/installer/Cargo.toml
     M crates/installer/Cargo.toml
    $ git diff HEAD --stat -- crates/installer/Cargo.toml
     crates/installer/Cargo.toml | 1 +
    $ git show HEAD:crates/installer/Cargo.toml   # what a clean checkout gets
    [dependencies]
    serde_json = "1"

The working tree adds `subprocess-contract = { path = "../subprocess-contract" }`; HEAD
does not have it. `crates/installer/src/lib.rs` calls
`subprocess_contract::BoundedOutcome::*` at lines 82, 83, 87 and nine more sites, so HEAD
is a tree where the source references a crate the manifest does not declare.

## WHY

Textbook works-on-my-machine, and it is the first thing CI caught once it could see
anything: 67 consecutive runs had died at `asupersync` + stable before reaching a single
line of our code. This one had been invisible the whole time.

It is also load-bearing beyond the crate. `installer --check` is the gate that compares
declared binaries against installed ones — the mechanism `gate.yml` cites as catching the
BUILT-≠-WIRED class. That gate cannot run at all on a clean checkout, so the wiring
check is itself unwired for anyone but the person holding the uncommitted line.

DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED HERE. The uncommitted change belongs to another pane. Committing
another agent's working-tree state is how the index gets swept — the exact failure the
path-scoped-commit discipline exists to prevent, and it happened twice tonight already.
The owner commits their own line.

## ACCEPTANCE

- [ ] Whoever holds the uncommitted `crates/installer/Cargo.toml` commits it path-scoped
      (`git add -- crates/installer/Cargo.toml && git commit -- crates/installer/Cargo.toml`).
- [ ] `cargo test -p installer` compiles in CI on a clean checkout.
- [ ] `installer --check` reaches a real verdict in the `installer` job rather than a
      compile error.
- [ ] Closes with the CI run id showing the `installer` job past the compile step.

## NO-CLAIM

This does not claim the installer's LOGIC is wrong, nor that the missing line is the only

title: P0: every install to ~/.local/bin is SIGKILLed on launch (exit 137) until re-signed -- the pre-existing omp-orchestrator binary was already unlaunchable and no liveness surface showed it
description: MEASURED 2026-09-05 by pane 1 while executing HD-0016 option (b) after Joshua lifted the BUILD FREEZE. SYMPTOM: /Users/josh/.local/bin/omp-orchestrator --help returned exit 137 with ZERO bytes on stdout and stderr. 137 is 128+9, SIGKILL on launch, which on macOS is the AMFI code-signing class. THE PRE-EXISTING BINARY WAS ALREADY BROKEN AND NOTHING SHOWED IT. I backed up the installed artifact (5941440 bytes, sha 63de2de25a0d340c, mtime 09-02 15:46), installed the freshly built release (6440608 bytes, sha 43eb9ec1a5a91b04), observed exit 137, and RESTORED the backup -- and the RESTORED BACKUP ALSO EXITED 137. So the install did not cause the condition; the artifact on PATH had been unlaunchable since at least 09-02 and every liveness surface read healthy throughout. That is bead 2tny's shape in a new form: 'every liveness surface reported healthy, only ls told the truth.' Here the live supervisor at pid 38194 (launchd ai.zeststream.omp-orchestrator.control-plane, uptime 2-19:45) is running the OLD INODE it opened days ago, so it is genuinely healthy while the file at its own path cannot launch. A restart would have killed it silently. DIAGNOSIS, isolated by control: target/release/omp-orchestrator --help returns exit 0 with 510 bytes; the IDENTICAL BYTES copied to ~/.local/bin exit 137. tick-monitor, installed by the same cp minutes earlier, launches fine from the same directory. codesign -dv shows both as flags=0x20002(adhoc,linker-signed) with Signature=adhoc and both carry only com.apple.provenance as an xattr, so quarantine is not the discriminator. The difference is the code-signing identifier: omp_orchestrator carries no hash suffix while tick_monitor-e5ff224960ed1d8d does, and macOS caches signing state by path plus identifier -- so replacing a binary at a path whose cached CodeDirectory hash differs gets the new inode killed by AMFI. FIX, verified: cp then codesign --force -s - <path>, which reported 'replacing existing signature', after which --help returned exit 0 / 510 bytes and exposed 'grade --claim [--repo PATH] [--session NAME]'. The live supervisor remained alive at pid 38194 throughout, confirming cp preserves the running inode. WHY THIS IS P0 AND NOT A FOOTNOTE: it silently breaks EVERY install path in this repo. The FINISH-TAIL dispatched to all panes instructs them to run 'omp-orchestrator grade --claim', which resolves from PATH -- so the finish-hook, the mechanism built to stop panes idling, could never work while the PATH binary was SIGKILLed. Pane %8 reported exactly this as 'The installed PATH grade command is stale and refused unknown argument grade'. And any hook install faces the same class: hook_freshness and orchestration_tick_hook rows need installed hooks, and an unlaunchable hook binary reads as DENY, which AGENTS.md names as the single highest-risk action. ACCEPTANCE: (1) the sanctioned install path re-signs after copy and VERIFIES launch, not just presence -- a file that exists is not a binary that runs; (2) the installer crate's --check gains a launch probe, because identity and mtime checks both passed on an artifact that could not execute; (3) a known-bad leg: copy without re-signing and confirm exit 137 is detected rather than reported as installed; (4) every existing installed artifact under ~/.local/bin used by this repo is launch-probed and the count of unlaunchable ones recorded. FALSIFIER: cp a freshly built binary over an existing PATH artifact without re-signing and confirm the install check fails rather than passing. NO-CLAIM: this establishes exit 137 on two distinct artifacts at one path, a working control at target/release, a working sibling at the same path, and that re-signing fixes it. It does not establish the exact AMFI rule being enforced, and it does not establish how many other installed artifacts are affected -- that census is acceptance item 4.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Known-bad leg (must be reproduced live, not fixture): with the installer's own copy routine, `cp` a freshly built `target/release/omp-orchestrator` over `~/.local/bin/omp-orchestrator` WITHOUT `codesign --force -s -`, then run `<installed> --help`; the install check MUST fail with a typed error naming exit 137 / SIGKILL. The existing evidence in this bead (the 09-02 backup, sha 63de2de25a0d340c, 5941440 bytes, exiting 137) is NOT sufficient evidence for this leg: it is a historical observation of an already-broken artifact, not a demonstration that the installer's check detects the condition, and it predates any launch probe existing. The row must be produced by the new code path.

2. Known-good leg (live): after `cp` + `codesign --force -s - <path>` (which must report "replacing existing signature"), `~/.local/bin/omp-orchestrator --help` MUST exit 0 with non-zero stdout, and the check MUST pass. Additionally the working sibling `~/.local/bin/tick-monitor` (identifier `tick_monitor-e5ff224960ed1d8d`) and the control `target/release/omp-orchestrator --help` (exit 0, 510 bytes) MUST both pass unmodified — the probe must not be so strict that a correctly-signed or never-touched artifact is flagged.

3. Launch probe semantics, not presence semantics: the installer crate's `--check` must, for each artifact, execute it with a harmless argument (`--help`), capture exit status, and classify. Presence, mtime, size, and sha identity checks are explicitly insufficient — the bead measured all of identity+mtime passing on an artifact that could not execute. Exit 137/`SIGKILL` must map to a distinct error variant (e.g. `Unlaunchable { path, signal: 9 }`) separate from "wrong version" and "missing", so pane %8's "stale / refused unknown argument grade" symptom cannot be conflated with it.

4. Anti-vacuity: if the census/scan of `~/.local/bin` artifacts used by this repo yields ZERO artifacts, or the probe runs on zero rows, that is a typed ERROR (`EmptyProbeSet`) and exits non-zero — never "0 unlaunchable, all clear". Same for a probe that cannot determine exit status (timeout, spawn failure): typed error, not pass. The passing output must include the count of artifacts probed and that count must be > 0.

5. Mutation test that goes RED: take an artifact that passes, strip/invalidate its signature (or `cp` without re-sign), record sha256 before and after; the `--check` suite MUST go RED with the `Unlaunchable` variant. Then restore the original bytes and confirm the sha256 matches the pre-mutation checksum byte-identically and the suite returns GREEN. Record both checksums in the row.

6. Sanctioned install path: every install site in this repo that writes to `~/.local/bin` (including whatever installs `tick-monitor` and any hook binary) must go through one routine that does copy → `codesign --force -s -` → launch-probe → fail loudly on non-zero. `cp`-only call sites must be removed, not merely deprecated; grep for remaining raw `cp`/`install` to `~/.local/bin` must return empty or each hit justified in the row.

7. Census (acceptance item 4 of the description) must be MEASURED live, not fixtured: enumerate every installed artifact under `~/.local/bin` used by this repo, launch-probe each, and record the total probed and the count + names of unlaunchable ones. Empty enumeration is the error in item 4. This census is what the NO-CLAIM defers, so it must not be silently skipped.

8. Open sub-item, explicitly not covered here: the exact AMFI rule (path+identifier CodeDirectory-hash caching, why `omp_orchestrator` lacking a hash suffix differs from `tick_monitor-e5ff224960ed1d8d`) is UNMEASURED. Either establish it with evidence in this bead, or file a separate bead referencing this one and link it in the closing row — do not let the re-sign fix imply the mechanism was proven. Likewise record that the live supervisor at pid 38194 survived (`cp` preserves the running inode) and that hook installs (`hook_freshness`, `orchestration_tick_hook`) inherit this class, with a linked bead if not fixed here.

title: Arrival gate: refuse a commit landing a crate with hardcoded home-path literals (7ai's invariant is not enforced on import)
description:
WHAT: an ARRIVAL gate for imported crates -- refuse a commit that lands a crate carrying hardcoded
home-path literals, so extraction cannot re-open bead 7ai's closed invariant.

MEASURED 2026-09-02 04:52Z. Extraction batch 1 (h71g) landed six crates that all passed the
acceptance predicate I authored, and the repo then refused EVERY commit:
  .git/hooks/pre-commit -> exit 1
  "MULTI-GATE REFUSED: 2 violation(s): path-literal-guard: 17 hardcoded home-path literal(s):
   crates/slb-guard-fail-closed/src/ma..., state-wildcard-lint: 2 finding(s)"
Per-crate, via `grep -rhoE '"/Users/[a-z]+' crates/<n>/src/ | wc -l`:
  zestgraph-hook-substrates 14, slb-guard-fail-closed 1, the other four 0.
Pane 5 had clean sender work staged and could not land it. It correctly refused to bypass.

THREE DISTINCT DEFECTS, and only the first is mine:

1. HANDROLLED PREDICATE (KERNEL-ONLY violation, orchestrator). My acceptance said prove portability
   with `grep -rc 'Developer/control-plane'`. The repo already ships the correct, WIDER check
   (path-literal-guard: any `"/Users/<user>` literal). I authored a weaker check beside a kernel
   that existed. Six extractions were certified against it.

2. A CLOSED INVARIANT THAT DOES NOT PROTECT ARRIVALS. Bead 7ai ("Installable from anywhere: no
   hardcoded repo or home paths") is CLOSED. Its closure was scoped to the crates present when it
   closed -- nothing refuses a NEW crate that violates it. That is the finding worth keeping: a
   closed portability bead is a snapshot, not an invariant, unless a gate enforces it on arrival.

3. GUARD AND HOOK DISAGREE, and the guard is the reassuring one. Run standalone,
   `cargo test -p path-literal-guard` reports 2 passed / 0 failed against the worktree WHILE the
   hook refuses on the same tree. An agent citing the standalone guard reports GREEN on a repo
   nobody can commit to. Same family as `--check` falling through to the WRITE path in
   plan-assemble, and as `refill-idle-panes` rendering a two-surface contradiction as
   "nothing to do" at exit 0: the cheaper surface is the one that lies.

ACCEPTANCE:
  1. A gate that refuses a commit introducing a NEW `crates/<name>/` whose src carries a
     home-path literal, naming file and line. Scoped to the staged set, not the whole repo, so it
     cannot be red for reasons outside the change.
  2. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD: plant a crate with one `"/Users/josh/...` literal -> RED; remove it ->
     GREEN. Byte-identical restore, both sha256 recorded.
  3. KNOWN-GOOD leg mandatory: the six batch-1 crates AFTER repair must pass, and
     path-literal-guard's own sources -- which legitimately contain the literal they FORBID as
     specimen data -- must NOT be flagged. Declared allowlist, never inferred. (kernel-bypass-gate
     already has this exact self-reference problem: a specimen table row of the string it forbids.)
  4. ANTI-VACUITY: an empty staged set is an ERROR, not a pass.
  5. The gate must state in its own output that it checks the STAGED set only, so nobody reads a
     green as "no crate in this repo carries a home literal".

NO-CLAIM: this refuses ARRIVAL of new violations. It does not repair the 15 literals already
landed (pane 3 owns that under h71g), does not cover the `state-wildcard-lint` 2 findings which are
still UNATTRIBUTED, and does not establish that the other 23 control-plane-only crates are portable
-- `admission-reason` and `coordinator-reservation-preflight` each carry 1 and are in batch 2.

title: rigor-atlas sampled-reexecution-trust-ladder (scheduler-kernel #1): closes are credited from the implementer's self-report like a cache serving stale — may_credit(close) -> Credit | ReexecuteFirst{reason} requires a non-implementer ReexecReceipt {cmd, tree_sha, exit, stdout_digest} against the close's own sha (xv30, gcyf, vggs, qt9r)
description:
WHAT: **A close is served from the implementer's self-report the way a cache serves a stale result: nothing earns the right to credit it.** Pass 3 had to re-execute 12 suites BY HAND to grade 40 closes, and found a permanently-RED cargo target cited as satisfying acceptance (`ipg.18`), grades citing a `cargo` figure against a commit while the worktree held a third agent's edit (`xv30`), and 23/40 grades with no re-execution receipt at all (`gcyf`). Build the admission rule as a pure function: `may_credit(close) -> Credit | ReexecuteFirst { reason }` — a close may be credited only when a grade row carries a RE-EXECUTION RECEIPT (command, pinned tree sha, exit code, stdout digest) produced by a non-implementer against the same tree the close names; otherwise the loop re-executes before crediting, and every refusal is a typed reason. This is rigor-atlas prescription `sampled-reexecution-trust-ladder` — the corpus's **#1 for `scheduler-kernel`** (`rigor apply --kind scheduler-kernel`) — and **no bead names it** (0 open-bead matches for `sampled re-execution|trust ladder`; `xv30` asks for a grade-pin refusal, which is one rung of this ladder).

INVARIANT (PROTOCOL L1, falsifiable): *A `closed` bead is credited (counted delivered, counted toward any milestone, allowed to unblock dependents) only if there exists a grade row whose `tree_sha` equals the sha the close names, whose `actor` is not an implementer of that bead, and whose re-execution receipt (`cmd`, `exit`, `stdout_digest`) was produced by running the shipped artifact against that tree; a close without such a row is `ReexecuteFirst`, never `Credit`, and a receipt whose `tree_sha` differs from the close's sha is `WrongInput`, never `Credit`.*

KERNEL SHAPE:
```
fn may_credit(close: &CloseRow, grades: &[GradeRow], implementers: &ActorSet) -> Admission
enum Admission { Credit { receipt: ReexecReceipt }, ReexecuteFirst { reason: CreditRefusal } }
enum CreditRefusal { NoReceipt, WrongInput { claimed: Sha, executed: Sha }, ImplementerGraded { actor }, ArtifactNotShipped { path }, ReceiptUnverifiable { field } }
struct ReexecReceipt { cmd: String, tree_sha: Sha, exit: i32, stdout_digest: Blake3, actor: ActorId, ts: MonotonicTs }   // validating constructor, no Default
```
Pure: no `br`, no `cargo` inside — the receipt is the input. The trusted piece is that the receipt names a real invocation of the shipped artifact against a pinned tree.

MIRROR EXEMPLAR TO COPY (KNOW, opened 2026-09-02):
- `/Volumes/ZestData/dicklesworthstone-mirror/remote_compilation_helper/rabs-cas/src/serving_sample_gate.rs:19-20` — *"Every refusal to serve is a TYPED reason, never a silent downgrade: private execution still produces shadow evidence for the ladder."* and :13-17 — the sampling bucket is *"derived from the action key digest itself (SHA-256 over the canonical key string), so every process and every store agrees on the decision without shared mutable state."* :22-27 — a served result that diverges from authoritative stock is *"a soundness incident … quarantine row before the disposition write, so a crash leaves blocked-but-unlabeled, never"* served.
- KINDS.md scheduler-kernel archetype (:1363): *"A cached or remotely-produced result may substitute for local execution only if it is byte-identical to what local execution would have produced (exit code, complete stdout AND stderr, artifact digests); when identity cannot be established the system executes rather than serves."* Read "cached result" as "the implementer's DONE report" and "local execution" as "the grader's re-run".
- `ultimate_bug_scanner/test-suite/quality/rule_quality_harness.py:4-6` (no-number-without-a-falsifier) — *"This harness intentionally invokes the real UBS binaries against real fixture files. It does not mock scanner output"* — the receipt must come from the shipped artifact, not a re-typed figure.

LOCAL STATE TODAY (path:line at HEAD):
- `AGENTS.md:961-964` gate rule 8 — *"A `cargo` figure is NEVER evidence about a commit"* — is doctrine with no function (`xv30`: "doctrine only").
- `AGENTS.md:1223-1225` — *"status is a claim, not a fact. Re-run, don't read"* — the ladder as a sentence.
- `crates/omp-orchestrator/src/spine_emit.rs:48-49` — `GradeReceived` is decided by close-reason prefix; no receipt type exists anywhere under `crates/*/src` (grep `ReexecReceipt|stdout_digest|tree_sha` → 0, positive control `close_reason` → hits).
- `crates/installer/src/lib.rs:3-6` — the four-way build identity proof is the one place a sha is mechanically bound to an artifact; the grade path has no equivalent binding.

LOCAL DEFECTS THIS WOULD HAVE PREVENTED (already filed — cite, do not re-file):
- `xv30` — 10 wrong-input verdicts: cargo-vs-commit, hook-vs-empty-index, `git log -S` blind to merges, pid where build_id was the question, source 1,285 commits behind the binary. Each is `WrongInput { claimed, executed }`.
- `gcyf` — 23/40 closes with the grader only in prose and no re-run artifact: `NoReceipt` / `ImplementerGraded`.
- `vggs` / pass 3 — 5 beads closed `DONE` while the ledger says undelivered; `ipg.18` closed on a permanently-RED target: `ArtifactNotShipped` / `WrongInput`.
- `qt9r` — self-close: the ladder's `ImplementerGraded` rung is the same fact as `two-person-rule-transition-table`'s `SelfApproval` seen from the evidence side; that bead owns WHO, this one owns WHAT was run.
- pass 3 instrument note — *"two suites went RED once / GREEN on rerun under parallel cargo load on the dirty tree — single-run reds are unproven"*: the receipt's `tree_sha` + `stdout_digest` is what makes a re-run comparable at all.

WHY: The credit decision is a scheduler decision — it decides what counts as done, which unblocks the next dispatch — and the corpus's rule for that kind is *"a served cache hit is byte-identical to local execution, or it is not served"* (KINDS.md:1385). Today the loop serves every close. Pass 3 was the sampled re-execution, performed by a human for one day; this bead makes it the admission rule so the sample is drawn by the loop and the refusal is typed instead of remembered.

RESULT CLASS THAT MAY BE CLAIMED (KINDS.md:1385): *the same inputs yield the same verdict on any host, reproducible from the receipt; a served result is identical to local execution, or it is not served.* DO NOT CLAIM: that a receipt proves the WORK is good (it proves the named command ran on the named tree with the named exit — acceptance quality is the grader's judgement, recorded in the row); competitive or coverage ratios for "how often we re-execute" (KINDS.md:1388 — no hit-rate gate, policy only); model checking (none exists in the exemplar either, :1391).

ACCEPTANCE:
1. `ReexecReceipt` with a validating constructor (no `Default`; a receipt missing `tree_sha`, `exit`, or `stdout_digest` cannot be built — `receipts-as-typed-objects-with-binds-tables`), plus a `binds / does-not-bind` doc table: binds the command, tree, exit, stdout digest, actor; does NOT bind the worktree's uncommitted state, the machine load, or the acceptance's meaning.
2. `may_credit` in one crate (`ack-spine` beside `close_reason.rs`, consumed by `spine_emit::GradeReceived`), returning `Credit` only when a non-implementer receipt's `tree_sha` equals the close's sha; every other input maps to a distinct `CreditRefusal` variant, walked exhaustively by a test.
3. Fires-on-known-bad: a close naming sha S with a receipt executed on sha S′ ≠ S → `WrongInput`; a receipt from the assignee → `ImplementerGraded`; a close with no grade row → `NoReceipt`; a receipt whose `cmd` names a binary not in the install manifest → `ArtifactNotShipped`. Mutation leg: compare `tree_sha` by prefix instead of equality — the `WrongInput` leg goes RED on a planted prefix collision.
4. The grader's runner emits the receipt mechanically: a `grade-run` subcommand (or the existing kernel if one fits — search `crates/verify-dispatch` first) that pins the tree (`git stash`-free: `git worktree` is FORBIDDEN; pin by `git rev-parse HEAD` + `git status --porcelain` empty on the paths under test, refusing otherwise with `TreeDirty`), runs the command, and writes the receipt as a typed bead comment via `crates/finding`, `--actor` mandatory (`gjyi`).
5. `Admission` is consumed: a `ReexecuteFirst` close is excluded from delivered counts and milestone claims (pass 9's readback) until a receipt lands; the heartbeat carries `credit=CREDIT|REEXECUTE_FIRST reason=…` as a typed field, not detail prose (`eg0m`).
6. FALSIFIER: after this lands, a close counted as delivered whose grade row lacks a receipt, or whose receipt `tree_sha` differs from the close's sha, or whose receipt actor is an implementer. Record here with the bead id, the receipt, and the `may_credit` verdict.

Evidence labels: KNOW = verbatim mirror line opened in this pass; local path:line read from HEAD 2026-09-02. Pass: skill-loop pass 5 (/rigor-atlas), actor Pass5Rigor.

title: A PreToolUse hook does not cover already-running agents: the whole wave is unguarded
description:
WHAT: **a `PreToolUse` hook installed into `~/.claude/settings.json` does NOT cover any already-
running agent, because the hook table is read at SESSION START.** Every pane in the current wave
predates the install and is therefore unguarded, while producing output indistinguishable from
compliance.

MEASURED 2026-09-02 against `rch-lane-bind` (control-plane's lane guard, installed user-global):

    probe                                                        result
    echo containing the text RCH_WORKER=contabo-4                ALLOWED  (correct - prose)
    RCH_WORKER=contabo-4 timeout 40 rch exec -- echo             RAN, exit 0   <- should DENY
    RCH_WORKER=contabo-4 rch exec -- echo                        RAN           <- should DENY
    printf '{"tool_input":{"command":"<same string>"}}' | rch-lane-bind   DENY, correct text

The last two carry the **identical command string from the identical cwd**. The binary denies; the
live tool call runs. The guard's logic is correct — `verdict`, `invokes_rch` (including its
`VAR=VALUE` skip), `requested_worker` (command-position rule), `allowed_lanes`, and the registry
lookup were all read and are right.

    ~/.claude/settings.json      mtime  12:59:22Z   <- hook installed
    ~/.local/bin/rch-lane-bind   mtime  12:59:11Z
    this pane's process started          00:01:33   (local)
    first commit today                   08:34:58   (local)

WHY IT MATTERS HERE, AND WHY IT IS THIS REPO'S THIRD RULE FROM THE OTHER SIDE: the `no-shell-gate`
case was a correct gate with an unreachable trigger. This is a correct gate, **installed**, and
**verified at the binary** — which is a different subject from the hook. `printf | binary` proves
the DECISION and can never prove the INTERCEPT. **Absence of denials reads identically to
compliance**, so a fleet-wide unguarded window is invisible by construction.

SECOND HOLE, code-read and NOT measured against a live hook: `timeout 40 rch exec` resolves
`invokes_rch`'s `program` token to `timeout`, so a wrapped invocation is classified as not-rch.
Wrappers — `timeout`, `nice`, `env`, `time`, `stdbuf`, `xargs` — bypass the check, and `timeout`
is in this fleet's standard command idiom, so this is not an exotic shape.

ACCEPTANCE:
  1. Any hook this repo relies on carries a documented statement of WHEN it takes effect, and
     whether live sessions are covered. A hook whose coverage window is unstated is treated as
     uncovering the current session.
  2. Hook-level verification is distinguished from binary-level verification wherever a hook is
     claimed working: the evidence must be a real tool call that was DENIED, never a piped payload.
  3. A liveness signal exists: the hook records a per-session invocation count, and a session with
     zero hook invocations after N Bash calls is REPORTED. Today, zero-denials and never-ran are
     the same observation.
  4. Fires-on-known-bad: a session started AFTER install must deny the foreign-lane probe, and a
     session started BEFORE must be detectable as uncovered rather than assumed compliant.
  5. The wrapper hole is either closed (skip known wrappers when resolving the program token) or
     recorded as a named limitation with a reason.

NO-CLAIM: this cannot be verified for a FRESH session from inside a stale one — restarting this
agent is not possible here, so the fresh-session leg is unrun and is the leg that matters. The
probes used `rch exec -- echo`, not a cargo build, so an unguarded foreign-lane BUILD proceeding is
NOT shown, only that the guard did not intercept; deliberately not tested, since causing the
collision to test the collision guard is the wrong trade. `rch-lane-bind` is control-plane's crate
and this bead does not propose editing it.

Before: crates/kernel-only-operator-hook/src/shadow.rs:233-239 had exactly THREE values with COVERED as the fallthrough -- 'if bash_calls >= threshold && hook_invocations == 0 {UNCOVERED} else if hook_invocations < bash_calls {PARTIAL} else {COVERED}' -- so with bash_calls=0 and hook_invocations=0 against any nonzero threshold the first guard is false, 0 < 0 is false, and A SESSION THAT NEVER RAN CLASSIFIED AS COVERED. After: classify_hook_liveness now requires positive evidence in every non-refusal arm -- 'if hook_invocations == 0 && bash_calls >= threshold {Uncovered} else if hook_invocations > 0 && hook_invocations < bash_calls {Partial} else if hook_invocations > 0 && hook_invocations >= bash_calls {Covered} else {Unknown}' -- so COVERED is no longer reachable without a recorded invocation and every residual, including zero-and-zero, is UNKNOWN. title: fuzz-build-gate + crash-to-regression contract wired into admission (Rust, no yaml)
description:
WHAT: **Wire the fuzz floor into the commit/admission path as Rust, and make the crash→regression
contract mechanical.** BUILT ≠ WIRED: `fuzz/` exists (4fd6a87) and is invoked by nothing. CI is
red on a stale sha and runs no cargo (28dq), so a yaml workflow would be a gate with no runner
(AGENTS.md third rule). This repo forbids `.sh`; the trigger is a crate.

Two halves:
1. `fuzz-build-gate` (crate + bin): runs `cargo build --manifest-path fuzz/Cargo.toml` on the
   pinned lane (`RCH_WORKER=contabo-3 -j 2`, placement read back from `rch queue --json`, a
   refusal is NOT green — grep `Remote command finished: exit=0`), refuses on any target that fails
   to compile, and refuses VACUOUSLY on zero targets found (anti-vacuity). Invoked from the
   admission path the supervisor already consults before dispatch (the standing verdict ledger /
   check chain), with a census row so `GATE_UNWIRED` sees it. Not pre-commit (g5e0: a build inside
   the index lock serialises five writers).
2. `fuzz-regress` (test in each owning crate): every file under `fuzz/artifacts/<target>/` and
   every `fuzz/corpus/<target>/seed-*` is replayed through the target's harness function as a
   `#[test]` (asupersync shape: `#[test] fn regression_<hash>()` with `include_bytes!`), so a fixed
   crash cannot regress silently and a seed cannot rot. An artifact with no regression test is
   refused by the gate (the artifact dir is the input; an empty dir is UNRUN, not PASS).

ACCEPTANCE: 1. fires-on-known-bad: break one target's compile → gate RED naming the target; plant a
crash artifact with no regression test → RED naming the file; restore both byte-identical. 2.
Known-good: current tree → PASS with `targets=N` (N = the `[[bin]]` count, not a literal). 3. The
gate appears in the supervisor's gate census as REACHABLE with its trigger named. 4. Lane
discipline enforced by the gate itself: a placement other than contabo-3 is a typed refusal.
NO-CLAIM: this gate proves the targets COMPILE and the artifacts are REPLAYED; it does not run a
fuzz campaign — campaigns are operator-run on joshs-brain-built binaries, executed here at
-jobs=1, and recorded in the ledger row the epic requires.

title: The journey query: one command set that answers how a bead or a plan flowed through the system -- BLOCKED because no ledger carries a typed join key
description:
JOSHUA 2026-09-03: 'we need a single set of commands to say - show me the entire journey for x bead id or x plan - how did it flow through the system, what was dispatched, when, how, and why, what was the results, what specific results are we expecting - and then how are we measuring expectations against reality at the perf level'.

I tried to answer it by hand for one bead that has a COMPLETE lifecycle today -- omp-orchestrator-s1-wave2-nonauthor-grade-oaqh, filed -> claimed -> dispatched -> ACKed twice -> graded 4/4 -> committed -> closed. Here is what each ledger could actually tell me, measured 2026-09-03T18:0xZ:

  .beads/issues.jsonl        id OK  status=closed assignee=pane4-%9 created=2026-09-03T16:05:00.801915Z updated=16:21:40.077067Z comments=2
  orchestration-ticks.jsonl  tick=2 ts=1788452521 -- the token appears, but as MENTIONED ONLY; the dispatched[] row for this bead is in tick 2 which was REFUSED by the gate and never landed
  docs/decisions.jsonl       0 rows mention it
  heartbeat.jsonl            0 lines mention the token, out of 9,858

THE ROOT CAUSE IS A MISSING JOIN KEY, and it is structural rather than a query problem. The heartbeat ledger has 9,854 parseable rows and a fixed NINE-key schema: build_id, detail, event, pid, repo, session, status, tick, ts_unix. There is NO bead field. 3,162 of those rows DO contain an omp-orchestrator-<id> string -- but only inside the free-text `detail` blob, so the only available join is a substring grep into prose.

Measured across every durable ledger, which of them carries a typed bead key:
  .beads/issues.jsonl                 id                     <- the only real key
  .flywheel/orchestration-ticks.jsonl NO-BEAD-KEY at row level (bead lives inside dispatched[].bead)
  .flywheel/loop-tick-ledger.jsonl    NO-BEAD-KEY
  docs/plan/FOUNDATION.jsonl          stage only
  docs/decisions.jsonl                id, binds_stages (stage, not bead)
So five surfaces, ONE typed join key, four prose or stage-only.

AND THE EXPECTATION SIDE DOES NOT EXIST AT ALL. Joshua asked two further questions -- what results are we EXPECTING, and how do we measure expectation against reality at the PERF level. Today: no ledger row carries an expected value, an SLO, or a duration. crate-atom-gate part 7 (the SLO row) is the slot for it and is conditional on the crate sitting on a tick path (crates/crate-atom-gate/src/lib.rs:64-65), so journey stages are exempt. NUMBERS.toml is the closest thing to an expectation registry and my grep for its row markers returned 0 -- its shape needs establishing before it can be cited as one.

WHAT TO SPECIFY (design, not code, this pass):
  1. THE JOURNEY KEY. Every event row in every ledger gains journey_key{bead_id, box_id, run_id, pane_id, actor, ts_unix}. Without it the query is grep and the answer is unreliable by construction. This is the whole bead; everything below is downstream.
  2. THE COMMAND SET. One surface, selector-polymorphic: `ompo journey <bead-id|box-id|run-id|pane-id> --json`. Sub-verbs to specify: --dispatches (what was sent, when, to whom, with which op_id and payload sha, and the receipt), --why (the packet, the claim, the decision rows that gated it), --results (commits, artifacts written, readback outcomes), --expected (the acceptance criteria and the SLO row), --delta (expected vs measured, per stage, with the command that produced each side).
  3. THE ENVELOPE. Adopt the shape our own robot surfaces already use rather than inventing one: schema_id, schema_version, a content hash, and refusals as severity+summary+action. NOTE pane 4 measured that `bv --robot-triage` has NO `meta` key (only data_hash, generated_at, triage, usage_hints) and that ntm's `sources.sources` populates exactly ONE source with no top-level degraded[] -- so copy shapes from what SHIPS, not from a scout summary.
  4. THE PERF LAYER. Each stage carries expected_duration and measured_duration, and a journey is RED when a stage exceeded its SLO even if every step succeeded. A journey that only records outcomes cannot answer Joshua's last question.
  5. UNKNOWN IS NOT ABSENT. A ledger with no row for a stage must render UNKNOWN, never a gap that reads as 'did not happen'. The oaqh trace above would otherwise report 'no heartbeat activity' when the truth is 'the heartbeat cannot express this'.

ACCEPTANCE: a contract at docs/contracts/journey_query.md per the contract template, naming the journey_key, the selector grammar, the sub-verbs, the envelope fields, and the expected-vs-measured row -- plus a WORKED EXAMPLE that traces oaqh end to end and marks every field either MEASURED-TODAY or UNKNOWN-TODAY with the reason. The worked example is the deliverable that proves the design against a real journey rather than an imagined one.

NO-CLAIM: specifying a key instruments nothing. Retrofitting journey_key into the heartbeat writer, the tick ledger and the spine ledger is separate work, and until it lands every journey answer is a prose grep with the reliability that implies.

EXPECTATION ROW SHAPE FOR KUKP (from pane2-%7)

Canonical runtime declaration: `.omp-orchestrator/expectations.toml`, schema_id=omp-orchestrator.expectations, schema_version=1, one `[[expectation]]` row:
id, scope=journey_stage, stage, metric, unit, expected_duration, threshold, source_command, owner.

title: omp-orchestrator Program (Types -> Kernels -> Lifecycle -> Gates -> OMP Surface -> Measurement -> Installability -> Governance)
description:
Root epic for omp-orchestrator. GOAL: a Rust orchestrator that drives OMP through its typed
surfaces instead of scraping the terminal it drew, with every claim it makes backed by a gate that
demonstrably bites.

THIS EPIC IS CLOSED ONLY WHEN ALL EIGHT PHASE EPICS ARE CLOSED. It is not closable by its own
work, and it must never carry a `blocks:` edge onto a leaf it parents — that is circular by
construction and strangled 13 beads earlier in this project.

WHY IT EXISTS — filed 2026-09-02, late and for a measured reason.

Per `/project-startup` Step 5, measured across the ten largest DAGs in Jeffrey Emanuel's corpus:
every one opens with a program-scoped bead, six of ten as epics, and the strongest state their arc
in the TITLE and their closure condition in the BODY. `frankenfs`: "FrankenFS V1 Program (Spec ->
Parity -> MVCC -> Self-Heal -> FUSE)", whose description reads "This epic is CLOSED only when all
track epics are closed." `eidetic_engine_cli`: "EE implementation program from comprehensive plan"
— the plan-to-bead bridge named in the title.

This project reached 80 beads and 1 epic with ZERO program or phase epics. The consequence was not
cosmetic: with no arc in the graph, every dispatch was the orchestrator hand-picking from a
78-item document, `bv --robot-triage` ranked leaves with `unblocks=None` across the board, and the
operator had to say "workers idle" five times in one session. **A DAG without an arc is a list.**

THE ARC — eight phases, named once, never re-litigated. Unforeseen scope becomes a SUB-EPIC under
an existing phase, never a new plan and never a `-SUCCESSOR`.

  Phase 0  TYPE ALGEBRA           ClaimStrength, Admission, PaneObservation, Lifecycle
  Phase 1  KERNEL CONTRACTS       subprocess, cancellation, ack-spine, receiver-receipt,
                                  finding, scratch-home, dispatch-claim, kernel-only,
                                  exit-code registry
  Phase 2  LIFECYCLE STAGES       one contract per observe -> select -> dispatch -> verify -> reap
  Phase 3  GATES + ENFORCEMENT    gate matrix, ratchet policy, taxonomies, the two rules docs
  Phase 4  THE OMP SURFACE        42 RPC methods, 39 subcommands, 71 type entries; consumed vs
                                  scraped vs unused; resolve slash_commands 799 vs 136
  Phase 5  MEASUREMENT            conformance / fuzz / benches — currently 0/0/0 against 32/34/28
                                  repos in the corpus. THE ABSENT CATEGORY, not an unmet one.
  Phase 6  INSTALLABILITY         doctor/health/repair, clean-machine receipt (R8),
                                  external-repo first-tick receipt (R9)
  Phase 7  GOVERNANCE + CLOSURE   requirement registry, claim registry, ADRs for every
                                  irreversible decision already taken

Phase 0 and 1 are COMPLETE as of 2026-09-02: 14 documents on disk, all passing the DPB-* bar
(`docs/contracts/asupersync_process_grade.md`). Phase 2 is in flight.

ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING. 0 and 1 precede everything because every later document cites those types;
writing the Phase 3 gate matrix before `admission_contract.md` means writing it twice. Formal and
proof work goes LAST — the corpus puts DPOR/TLA+ at Phase 5 of 5, after the kernel, scheduler, I/O,
actors and distribution all exist. Proof follows working code.

Phase 5 is the one to resist deferring. `fuzz` and `proptest` and `p99` appear ZERO times across
our 13 plan sections, so it is a MISSING REQUIREMENT rather than an unmet one, and the corpus
treats it as standard equipment at 28-34 repos of adoption.

ACCEPTANCE (this epic):
 1. Eight phase epics exist as children, each with its own acceptance and its own closure
    condition, and each named in `docs/plans/plan_to_write_the_document_corpus.md`.
 2. Every open bead in this tracker is a descendant of exactly one phase epic, or carries a
    label explaining why it is deliberately unparented. `bv --robot-triage` must report
    `unblocks` > 0 for the phase epics — an arc that produces no unblock counts is not wired.
 3. `docs/contracts/asupersync_process_grade.md` re-derived at every phase boundary, before the
    next phase opens.
 4. All eight phase epics CLOSED, each by a grader who did not implement it.

NO-CLAIM: filing this epic does not make the graph navigable — condition 2 is the work, and it
requires re-parenting 80 existing beads that were filed with no arc to attach to. Nor does an arc
make any phase correct; it makes the ORDER visible and the orchestrator's next pick derivable
instead of chosen. And the eight phases are the manifest's current shape: some may merge or split,
which is a SUB-EPIC amendment, not a re-plan.

the P0 program root had no closeable condition while 43 descendants carried one. Written before

the bead is the durable spec).

An epic closes AFTER its children, never before. This bead is closeable only when all of:

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
MULTI-MODEL TRIANGULATION ON THE asupersync BLOCKER — pane 1 (opus-5) + codex (gpt-5.6-luna),
2026-09-06. Joshua asked for a second model because my conclusion reversed both his instruction
and %8's report. It paid for itself: codex refuted my main conclusion and corrected two paths.

THE QUESTION: %8 reported jplf.1.2 BLOCKED, requiring "advance the asupersync pin or authorize a
compatible feature strategy". Joshua directed "advance the rev if that's what's needed".

WHAT IS SETTLED — verified by me in mirror source, and codex agrees:

1. `class` IS GATED. messaging/mod.rs:77-78 `#[cfg(feature = "messaging-fabric")] pub mod class;`
   and :119-121 the matching `pub use class::{AckKind, DeliveryClass, ...}`. Both the INHABITED
   AckKind (class.rs:83 — Accepted/Committed/Recoverable/Served/Received) and DeliveryClass
   (class.rs:17) live there. NOT reachable with our current features.
   My earlier note that class.rs "has 0 messaging-fabric cfg sites" was TRUE and IRRELEVANT: the
   gate is on the `mod` declaration in the parent, not inside the file. I got that wrong first.

2. TWO AckKind TYPES EXIST, which is why the bead says "the INHABITED AckKind":
     obligation/graded.rs:790  pub enum AckKind {}        <- uninhabited typestate marker
     messaging/class.rs:83     pub enum AckKind { ... }   <- the data enum
   Siblings SendPermit{} and LeaseKind{} share the marker shape.

3. THE exit-101 WAS A CARGO NAMESPACE ERROR, not evidence about asupersync. `cargo check -p
   omp-types --features messaging-fabric` resolves the feature in omp-types' OWN [features] table;
   omp-types declares none. Enabling a dependency feature requires the dependency declaration or a
   forwarded `asupersync/messaging-fabric`. Codex CONFIRMED this independently.

CODEX CORRECTED TWO PATHS I HAD WRONG — verified against source after it said so:

   WRONG: asupersync::obligation::ObligationLedger
   RIGHT: asupersync::obligation::ledger::ObligationLedger
          obligation/mod.rs has ZERO ObligationLedger re-exports; `pub mod ledger;` at :70.
   WRONG: asupersync::obligation::AckKind
   RIGHT: asupersync::obligation::graded::AckKind   (`pub mod graded;` at :65)

Had I landed my three-line re-export as written, it would not have compiled. That is the value of
the second read.

CODEX REFUTED MY MAIN CONCLUSION, AND I COULD NOT CONFIRM OR REFUTE ITS REFUTATION:

   My claim 6: "the fix is one line — add messaging-fabric to the workspace asupersync features;
               no rev change needed."
   Codex:      REFUTE. "Adding only the workspace feature exposes the modules but fails
               compilation at the pinned rev ... the pinned source has a concrete compile b[ug]"
               naming consumer.rs.

I tested the claim and my probe does NOT reproduce it: across messaging/, 18 modules are gated and
7 ungated, and ZERO ungated modules reference any gated item (DeliveryClass, AckKind,
DeliveryClassPolicy, DeliveryCostVector, class::) — with a working positive control, since 10 of
the 18 gated modules do reference them.

BUT I TESTED THE WRONG DIRECTION. I checked "ungated code referencing gated items". Codex's claim
is the opposite shape: a LATENT BREAK INSIDE GATED CODE THAT NOBODY COMPILES. consumer.rs is
itself gated (mod.rs:81-82), so it is never built with our features, so a break in it would be
invisible to every check either of us ran. **No static probe can settle that. Only a compile can.**

STATUS: UNRESOLVED, and deliberately left so rather than guessed.

  C1 nothing-to-advance   PARTIAL. Mirror HEAD == fa3c01aec, rev-list count 0. Real upstream
                          github.com/Dicklesworthstone/asupersync NOT checked. If upstream is
                          ahead, Joshua's instruction is live.
  C2 feature-is-no-op     REFUTED BY ME, pre-emptively. 156 cfg(feature="messaging-fabric") sites
                          (positive control: runtime-metrics = 19). I had inferred "no-op" from a
                          Cargo.toml comment. Third inference-as-measurement error of the session.
  C3 types-reachable-now  REFUTED. Gated. Only ObligationLedger is ungated.
  C4 AckKind-uninhabited  REFUTED BY ME. AckKind::Accepted appears 14 times; there are two types.
  C5 namespace-error      CONFIRMED by both.
  C6 one-line-fix         DISPUTED. Codex says it will not compile. UNTESTED.

THE ONE TEST THAT SETTLES IT, which nobody has run:
  in a scratch build, add "messaging-fabric" to the asupersync features, add the three
  path-corrected re-exports, run `cargo check -p omp-types`, and report the exit code plus any
  error[E….] lines. %9 holds that task.

BLAST RADIUS, per codex and worth heeding before anyone lands it: the workspace declaration is
inherited by every member (codex counted 21 direct manifest hits, not the 18 I had said), cargo
unifies dependency features across a workspace build, so a latent break in fabric modules would
fail unrelated crates; plus higher asupersync compile time and RSS, and native-vs-wasm API
asymmetry since `pub mod messaging` is `#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]`. The narrower form
`asupersync = { workspace = true, features = ["messaging-fabric"] }` on omp-types alone is smaller
in manifest scope but does not escape feature unification.

WHAT %8 GOT RIGHT AND WRONG: right that a feature strategy or upstream change is required and that
it must not be worked around locally — that refusal held. Wrong on the mechanism: the blocker is
not a "forbidden test-internals leak". `messaging-fabric = []` pulls nothing; test-internals
co-occurs only on two [[bench]] targets (Cargo.toml:797,802); and upstream's own
`ci-cross-platform` umbrella (:254) enables messaging-fabric WITHOUT test-internals.

NO-CLAIM: this triangulation establishes the paths, the gating, and the namespace error. It does
NOT establish whether the feature compiles at this rev, does not check real upstream for newer
commits, and does not authorize any manifest change. Two models agreed on three points and
disagreed on the decisive one; the disagreement is the honest output.

title: README current status claims match live baselines
description:
WHAT: update README status claims so every current figure and product-state assertion is either live-command-backed or explicitly historical/PROJECTED. Correct the current-state block around README.md:180-203 without changing the product scope.

WHY: current source and metadata re-derive 68 Cargo packages, 65 binary targets, and 66/68 manifest unsafe forbids, while README.md still says 2 of 20 crates carry unsafe_code=forbid and repeats old 39-surface/zero-consumer wording as if current. The README also presents the plan-to-ship workflow while the current run stops at reap-finished-panes and the current plan stamp is stale. A public status claim that is ahead of the measured artifact is the same stale-copy failure the plan is meant to prevent.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. cargo metadata --format-version 1 --no-deps --offline and the registered NUMBERS.toml commands are run; README figures are either generated from those current authorities or labelled dated historical snapshots.

description:
WHAT: **Consume the `agent_end` frame (`isTerminal`, `willContinue`) as the completion signal** — the

`reap-finished-panes` needs two equal captures and `classify_completion` refuses to free capacity on

signal the plan's S5 stage asks for; `isTerminal` splits "turn ended" from "session ended".

   … }` (field names read from `dist/types`, cited); `ack-spine` gains a `Completed{source: rpc}` step

   `isTerminal=true` must. Both as fuzz arms in `ack_spine_ledger_model` (`k81x`).

  src/lib.rs:758  `config.cp.join("bin/pane-dispatch-ready.sh")` passed as the

  src/lib.rs:922  `Command::new(config.cp.join("bin/pane-dispatch-ready.sh"))` -- a direct

  depends on a shell script in another repo as a DATA source. That is arguably worse for

title: EPIC: L5 adversarial-input floor -- full fuzz + property coverage of the dispatch kernel
description:
WHAT: **L5 adversarial-input floor for the dispatch kernel — "full fuzz", Joshua 2026-09-03.** The
four defects in `zlyy` were unstated invariants; fuzz/property is the mechanism that keeps a stated
invariant honest against generated inputs. Measured: 29 of Jeffrey's mirrored repos carry `fuzz/`
(1,629 targets, 11 with a fuzz CI workflow, 37 with proptest); this repo had 0/0 until `4fd6a87`.

SHAPE (copied, not invented — `frankenterm/fuzz/fuzz_targets/wire_envelope.rs:97-118,307-345`,
`asupersync/fuzz/Cargo.toml`, `asupersync/.github/workflows/fuzz.yml`):
- `fuzz/` is its OWN `[workspace]` (root manifest untouched), `publish=false`, `cargo-fuzz=true`,
  `libfuzzer-sys 0.4` + `arbitrary` derive; one `[[bin]]` per target named `<crate>_<invariant>`.
- The Op enum and the REFERENCE MODEL live in the target; `assert_eq!(actual, expected)` after every
  op; the kernel crates carry no fuzz-only derives (a `fuzz` feature is a later bead if needed).
- Seeds committed under `fuzz/corpus/<target>/seed-*`; `fuzz/artifacts/` ignored; every crash
  artifact becomes a regression test in the OWNING crate before the fix lands (testing-fuzzing #10).
- Heavy deps are feature-gated (`ack-spine-targets` drags asupersync); light targets build in minutes.

LANE DISCIPLINE (binding, measured 2026-09-03 — a local fuzz build took this box to load 78):
- Fuzz BINARIES are built on `RCH_WORKER=joshs-brain` (arm64 artifact lane), `file -b`-verified
  Mach-O, and only EXECUTED here at `-jobs=1`. Never `RCH_ENABLED=false`. `cargo fuzz build` does
  not accept `-j`; use `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2`. A contabo lane produces ELF and cannot run here.
- Verdict-only legs (proptest under `cargo test`) go to `contabo-3` pinned, `-j 2`.

CHILDREN (leaves first; each is one target or one contract):
1. dispatch-key stateful model (K1-K4, needs the marker/ack decision extracted pure — with zlyy)
2. ack-stage `assess()` transport × receiver × ack-readback
3. receiver-receipt `assess_receiver_receipt` pre/post observation → verdict
4. tick-monitor `liveness()` + `partition_capacity` two-capture stateful model

title: Kernel-baked gate census: the supervisor refuses to report healthy while any gate has no reachable trigger
description:
WHAT: the resident supervisor and tick-monitor -- the only two processes in this repo with a trigger that provably exists -- must perform a GATE CENSUS every cycle and emit a TYPED NONZERO ESCALATION while any gate lacks a reachable trigger. Not a test someone runs. A property of the kernel processes themselves, so an unwired gate makes the supervisor structurally unable to report healthy.

MEASURED CENSUS, 2026-08-31 (caller counts, and whether that caller has a trigger that exists on THIS machine):
  gate                       ci_ref  src_callers  manifest_deps   reachable trigger?
  kernel-bypass-gate           0         0            0           NONE AT ALL
  no-shell-gate                1         2            0           YES -- .git/hooks/pre-commit (Mach-O, 12:56:03), PROVEN to bite
  path-literal-guard           1         0            0           ci-only -> UNREACHABLE
  pre-delete-citation-check    0         0            0           NONE AT ALL
  state-wildcard-lint          1         0            0           ci-only -> UNREACHABLE
  undrained-pipe-lint          1         0            0           ci-only -> UNREACHABLE
  `git remote` returns NOTHING, so every .github/ reference is unreachable by construction.
FIVE OF SIX GATES CANNOT FIRE. One does, and only since 12:56 today.

WHY IT MUST LIVE IN THE KERNEL PROCESSES: every non-kernel signalling path in this repo has been measured silent. ATTENTION.txt got 178 consecutive ticks from one writer with zero readers. The supervisor emitted a typed refusal naming owner=josh for 29 consecutive ticks and nobody read it for hours. .github/workflows/gate.yml has no runner. A file, a log, and a CI job are all loud in principle and silent in fact. The ONE path that reached a human today was a nonzero typed outcome the operator was forced to answer -- which is exactly the mechanism QueueEmptyNeedsJosh already uses.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. A NEW SupervisorDecision VARIANT, e.g. GateUnwired { gate, reason }, that is a NONZERO typed escalation. It must be UNREACHABLE-AROUND: no branch may return SupervisedWorking or AuthorizedIdle while any gate is unwired. The exhaustive match must make skipping it a compile error, the way the wildcard-lint bead already requires for state enums.
2. CLASSIFY BY TRIGGER REACHABILITY, NOT CALLER EXISTENCE. no-shell-gate had a caller (gate.yml) for hours while being unable to fire. A census keyed on 'does something reference this' would have called it WIRED and been wrong. Known-bad: a gate referenced ONLY from .github/ with no git remote must report UNREACHABLE.
3. POSITIVE CONTROL, mandatory: no-shell-gate must report REACHABLE, because .git/hooks/pre-commit is a real installed binary proven to refuse a staged .sh with exit 1. Without this leg the census could report everything unreachable and look identical to a working one -- and today a broken shell loop of mine returned zero for all six lifecycle stages, caught only by a positive control on a pattern I knew was wired.
4. ANTI-VACUITY: zero gates discovered is an ERROR, never a pass. A census that finds no gates must not read as no unwired gates.
5. THE PER-CLONE HOLE MUST BE REPORTED, NOT HIDDEN: .git/hooks/ is untracked and per-clone, so a fresh checkout has no hook and no-shell-gate reverts to UNREACHABLE there. The census must report reachability FOR THE MACHINE IT RUNS ON and say so, since README promises 'install it on any of our machines'.
6. MUTATION: remove one gate from the census input; leg 1 goes RED. Restore byte-identically, report the sha both sides.

NO-CLAIM: this makes an unwired gate LOUD, not impossible. It cannot prove a gate that IS reachable actually RAN this cycle -- tick-monitor had callers and still starved the fleet for 4.5 hours. Runtime witness is a separate bead. Static reachability plus a forced nonzero escalation is the floor being raised here, and overstating it would be the exact defect this repo refuses.

title: the loop's last blocker: five gates built-but-unwired (ack-spine, ack-stage, composer-typed, finding, receiver-receipt)
description:
WHAT: **the supervisor refuses every dispatch with `GATE_UNWIRED` because FIVE gates are
built-but-unwired. This is the last blocker between hand-dispatch and an autonomous loop, and it is
this repo's own third rule enforced against itself.**

MEASURED 2026-09-02 from the live heartbeat, build `7600dda`:
```
GATE_UNWIRED unwired=
  ack-spine        [UNWIRED   -> repair-gate-trigger]
  ack-stage        [REACHABLE -> none]
  composer-typed   [UNWIRED   -> repair-gate-trigger]
  finding          [UNWIRED   -> repair-gate-trigger]
  receiver-receipt [UNWIRED   -> repair-gate-trigger]
```
Every other dispatch defect is now ZERO from this build -- `File exists (os error 17)`,
`CLAIM_REQUIRED`, the quarantined re-expire loop, and `RECEIVER_OBSERVATION_MISSING`. Selection,
claiming, identity resolution and the per-pane fence all work. **The loop refuses only here**, and
it is right to: a gate that cannot fire means the repo READS as protected while it is not.

**TWO DISTINCT VERDICTS, and conflating them will waste the pass:**
- `UNWIRED -> repair-gate-trigger` (4 crates): no trigger reaches the gate at all.
- `ack-stage[REACHABLE -> none]`: a trigger EXISTS and resolves to no action. That is a different
  defect and a different fix; it is the shape that reads as wired while doing nothing.

**WHAT IS ALREADY KNOWN ABOUT EACH, so nobody re-derives it:**

`finding` -- measured earlier tonight and already tracked by `x1un`:
```
crates/finding            444 LOC   [[bin]]=0  main.rs=no
crates/finding-dispatch   129 LOC   [[bin]]=0  main.rs=no
finding-dispatch as a dep in any crates/*/Cargo.toml   ->  0
positive control: subprocess-contract as a dep         -> 19   <- the probe works
```
**AND AGENTS.md's KERNEL-ONLY RULE POINTS AT IT:** *file findings through `crates/finding`, never raw
`br create`.* The crate ships **no bin**, so nobody can obey the rule -- every `br create` in this
repo tonight, mine included, was an ABSENT ALTERNATIVE, not a handroll. **Either it gains a
reachable entrypoint and the rule becomes followable, or both crates are proposed for retirement and
the AGENTS.md rule is corrected IN THE SAME COMMIT.** Do not leave the rule pointing at an
unreachable crate.

`ack-stage` -- the live loop currently returns `ACK_STAGE_INDETERMINATE ... reason=unproven_transport
transport=tmux_send_keys_literal action=AWAIT_HUMAN`. **Measured: that transport DID deliver** -- 6
bead-name terms in the target pane against a positive control of 13. So its `Indeterminate` is a
FALSE NEGATIVE on a real delivery: the gap is receipt proof, not delivery. **Independent
corroboration: my own two `tmux send-keys -l` sends to control-plane reported success and delivered
nothing observable, with a FAILING positive control proving my probe -- not the delivery -- was the
liar the first time.** So the transport is genuinely unreliable AND genuinely delivered here; a
receipt that reads pane CONTENT with a positive control is the only thing that distinguishes them.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. Each of the five reaches `REACHABLE` with a NAMED trigger, and the census says which trigger.
2. **`.git/hooks/pre-commit` is the only trigger PROVEN to fire on this machine.** `.github/` is
   reachable (origin exists) but has failed 67 consecutive runs, so a workflow-only wiring is
   reachable and not working. State which you used and why.
3. **Wiring `ack-stage` must not be a rename.** `REACHABLE -> none` means the trigger already
   resolves to nothing; adding a second trigger to the same no-op changes the verdict string and not
   the behaviour. Prove the action runs.
4. **Fires-on-known-bad per gate**, plus a KNOWN-GOOD leg. An attack-only suite ships an over-strict
   gate on the commit path, and an over-strict commit-path gate gets routed around within a day --
   measured today when the staged-build-gate refused a `plan-assemble` commit over a file in
   `tests/` that `cargo build` never opens.
5. **Anti-vacuity: an empty gate set is an ERROR.** A census that finds no gates reports identically
   to one where all are wired.
6. **Weigh the 603s figure before wiring anything to pre-commit.** `929j` records that the
   staged-build-gate's first live run took 603s because a shared index made it build a peer's staged
   crate. Wiring blind converts one writer's staging into another writer's commit latency.

`tick-monitor` had callers and starved the fleet for 4.5 hours anyway. And `.git/hooks/` is untracked
and per-clone, so a fresh checkout elsewhere has no hook and these gates revert to unwired there --
the census answers for the machine it runs on and must say which one that is.
