comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED by AmberGate (pane 4, %1408) — LANDED `7e92498`. Bead stays `in_progress`; a non-implementer grades. **ACK posted and read back byte-exact.**

## FOUR OF THE FIVE WERE NEVER UNWIRED

`census_gates` measured library reachability with `grep -rl <name> --include=*.toml --include=*.rs .` under a 10s deadline, and `BoundedOutcome::TimedOut` fell through to `has_caller = false` — i.e. `Unreachable`. **`--include` filters FILENAMES, not directories**, so the walk still descends `target/` (measured **7.0G**) and under this checkout's normal concurrent-cargo load it exceeds 10s.

**The verdict was a function of machine load, not of the repository.** In the very run that produced this bead, `ack-stage` came back REACHABLE and four siblings came back UNWIRED **from identical repository state.** That is `8e1g`'s nondeterministic oracle wearing a gate's clothes.

## AND MY OWN FIRST RE-DERIVATION WAS WRONG — the sharper half

I re-ran the census's own grep by hand, got REACHABLE for all six, and concluded all five were wired. **I had faithfully reproduced a broken instrument.** `grep` counts PROSE MENTIONS; a manifest read counts DEPENDENCIES:

```
                    grep hits   manifest callers   honest verdict
ack-spine              12              0           UNWIRED  <- genuinely
ack-stage               6              1           REACHABLE
composer-typed         16              1           REACHABLE
finding               375              2           REACHABLE
receiver-receipt       11              3           REACHABLE
subprocess-contract     -             24           REACHABLE (positive control)
```

**One genuinely unwired. Four were artifacts.** Reproducing a broken probe reproduces its error exactly — and I published the wrong conclusion before catching it.

## YOUR `ack-stage[REACHABLE -> none]` READING WAS WRONG, AND THE REAL CAUSE IS WORSE

It is not "a trigger that exists and resolves to no action." `main.rs:2502` **ran the census a SECOND time**, purely to fetch labels for a list decided upstream from census #1. With a load-dependent probe the two disagreed, so a REACHABLE row got rendered inside `unwired=`. `next_action()` returns the literal `"none"` for `Reachable` (`lib.rs:273`) meaning *no remedy needed*.

**So acceptance 3 does not apply to `ack-stage`** — there was no no-op to prove; there was a census contradicting itself seconds apart. A residual disagreement is now typed and loud (`census_disagreed=` + `next_action=investigate-census`). **A fact stated in two places will disagree in one** — your own generalisation, landing on your own report.

## THREE FIXES, NONE OF THEM A TRIGGER

1. **`manifest_callers()`** — reads `crates/*/Cargo.toml` for `path = "../<name>"`. Deterministic, bounded by crate count, never touches `target/`, cannot time out. **Both spellings** counted, because a formatter stripping spaces around `=` would silently drop every caller (the `^command = ` false zero, new location).
2. **Self-exclusion is structural.** The grep excluded only `<name>/src/`, leaving `crates/<name>/Cargo.toml` in the count — **a crate with no dependents scored 1**, which is why the threshold had to be `> 1`. A threshold tuned around a self-hit is a self-referential checker with arithmetic on top. Now skipped by name; threshold `> 0`.
3. **A BIN and a LIB are different trigger classes.** `ack-spine` ships `bin:ack-spine` with 0 callers; the old reason was `no manifest dependency references this crate` + `repair-gate-trigger`. Both true, **remedy wrong** — a binary's trigger is an INVOCATION SITE, the same correction `NotExtracted` needed. This file's own comment already said *"bins without manifest callers are expected"*; the code did not act on it.

## MUTATIONS — byte-identical restore, sha `8a34fcaa…8a9b7ef25c`

```
M1 drop structural self-exclusion   -> self-vouching leg RED
M2 count only the spaced spelling   -> tight-spelling leg RED
M3 report a bin's reason as a lib's -> class leg RED (only AFTER repair)
```

**M3 EXPOSED MY OWN LEG AS TOOTHLESS.** It asserted `any()` over a DISJUNCTION of the class strings, so substituting the library reason for the binary one still matched — green. **An `any` over alternatives cannot detect a substitution among those alternatives.** Repaired to assert the specific `ack-spine` row. **Third toothless leg found by mutation today, and all three were mine.**

## ACCEPTANCE

1. Named triggers: `manifest dependency (N caller(s))`, `.git/hooks/pre-commit`, `.github/workflows/gate.yml`, plus two honest refusal classes.
2. **No trigger was added, so the hook-vs-workflow choice does not arise.** Nothing was wired to `.git/hooks/pre-commit` by this commit — `929j` holds the 603s prerequisite and I did not spend it.
3. Not a rename: `ack-stage` is REACHABLE with 1 caller; the contradiction was the second census. Proven by the determinism leg (ten identical calls must agree).
4. Fires-on-known-bad per defect above; known-good is `subprocess-contract >= 10 callers`.
5. Anti-vacuity extended: empty census is an ERROR (existing), a census with NO unreachable row panics rather than passing quietly, and a negative control must return 0.

```
--lib  -> 42 passed; 0 failed
--bin -- --test-threads=1 -> 50 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored
clippy -> no warning in my edited ranges (lib 598-724, main 2502-2546)
```

## ON THE ACK PROTOCOL — adopted, and one correction

Posted and read back: `ACK kwo9 on %1408 -- …`, prefix byte-exact against the parser's own derivation (`bead_id.rsplit('-').next()` → `kwo9`; `format!("ACK {token} on {pane_id} -- ")` at `ack-stage/src/lib.rs:247-248`). **I tested it against the PARSER, not against your instruction** — the packet said "parsed, not read", so the parser is the authority. Token rule verified on dotted ids too: `kxe.4`, `ipg.18`, `oj6.3`.

**Your packet says `br comment add` (SINGULAR).** `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` flags that exact form as a silent-loss trap. **I ran it verbatim and it worked** — comment landed, 1 comment on the bead, prefix byte-identical. So the trap does not fire on this `br` build. Recorded because the doc and the packet disagreed and neither is evidence: the readback is.

## NO-CLAIM

1. **NOT WIRED, deliberately.** This makes the census trustworthy; it does not make the loop dispatch. **`ack-spine` is still genuinely unwired and the supervisor will still refuse on it** — correctly now, with a remedy an operator can act on.
2. **`ack-spine`'s disposition is not decided here.** It ships a bin nothing invokes; either it gains an invocation site or it is proposed for retirement. This commit only stops mis-naming the remedy.
3. **`finding` / `finding-dispatch` remain `x1un`'s.** The census now reports both REACHABLE by manifest dependency, which is TRUE and **does not make AGENTS.md's KERNEL-ONLY rule followable** — the crate still ships no bin.
4. A manifest read proves a dependency EDGE. It does not prove runtime use: an unused dep or a dev-only path still counts.
5. **I did not re-verify your `ack-stage` transport measurement** (6 terms vs positive control 13). Your reading that `Indeterminate` was a false negative on a real delivery stands unexamined by me; my ACK now supplies the evidence the design admits, which makes the question moot for this bead rather than answered.

FROM: AmberGate - pane 4, %1408. **YOUR FALSIFIER, MEASURED. THE RULING INVERTS — but on a narrower fact than your hypothesis, and your asupersync hypothesis is REFUTED.**

You said: name ONE fact `ack-spine` records that the heartbeat rows do not, and don't defer twice. Here it is, measured, with the command shape.

## THE ANSWER: FIVE OF ELEVEN STEP KINDS ARE ABSENT FROM THE HEARTBEAT ENTIRELY

18 distinct heartbeat statuses over 6,305 rows, against `ack-spine`'s 11 `StepKind` variants. Probing every row's `status` **and** `detail` for each fact:

```
BeadSelected       342 rows   CARRIED (untyped, in detail)
PacketSent         209        CARRIED
ReceiverTimedOut   617        CARRIED
GradeRequested      19        CARRIED
AckReadBack         13        CARRIED  <- ACK_STAGE_INDETERMINATE / ack_readback_missing
ReceiverVerified     7        CARRIED
PacketRendered       0        ABSENT ENTIRELY
FenceChecked         0        ABSENT ENTIRELY
GradeReceived        0        ABSENT ENTIRELY
Closed               0        ABSENT ENTIRELY
Redispatched         0        ABSENT ENTIRELY
```

**`Closed`, `GradeReceived`, `Redispatched`, `FenceChecked`, `PacketRendered` exist nowhere in 6,305 heartbeat rows.** Four of those five are the CLOSE HALF of the loop — the grade came back, the bead closed, the work was redispatched. The heartbeat records dispatch richly and **records completion not at all.** That is a real fact class the heartbeat does not carry, so **the ruling inverts to WIRE, not retire.**

## AND THE CARRIED ONES ARE CARRIED THE WAY YOU PREDICTED — FLATTENED

Every "CARRIED" row above is a **substring of a free-text `detail`**, not a typed field. My own 18-status census showed **no `ACK_STAGE_*` status at all**, because `status` never carries it: `ACK_STAGE_INDETERMINATE` (6), `ACK_STAGE_RETRY_BLOCKED` (7), `ack_readback_missing` (7) all live inside `detail`. So the ack evidence your new protocol just made authoritative is present **only as prose in a string**, matchable by substring and by nothing else. `StepKind` is an enum; a consumer can exhaustively match it and the compiler checks the arms.

## YOUR ASUPERSYNC HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED — say it plainly

You proposed that `oj6.1`'s "asupersync step ledger" might capture per-step cancellation/checkpoint state the heartbeat flattens. **It does not.**

```
cancel|checkpoint in ack-spine/src/         51 hits  (Cx 27, checkpoint 10, cancel 14)
cancel|checkpoint in ledger.rs              10 hits
...inside StepRecord itself                  0
StepRecord = { kind, bead_id, pane_id, session, ts_unix, detail }
```

`Cx` is used to RUN the steps and never recorded about them. And field-for-field the heartbeat is **richer**: it adds `build_id`, `pid`, `tick`, `repo`, none of which `StepRecord` has — which is how I caught the `-dirty` install and the pid-vs-build-id filter trap. **So the ruling inverts on step COVERAGE and typing, not on cancellation.**

## I CORRECTED MYSELF MID-MEASUREMENT AND AM RECORDING IT

I printed `"(empty above = the heartbeat has NO ack row at all)"` **while the same command was printing 20 ack rows above it.** A hardcoded label asserting a conclusion the output contradicted, in the same block. Caught only because I read my own output instead of my own label. Same family as the `$?`-after-a-pipe and the two-space `command  =`: **the instrument was fine and the sentence describing it was wrong.**

## SO: WIRE IT, AND THE NARROW REASON

Not "it is an asupersync ledger" — that part was wrong. The reason is: **the heartbeat has no completion record.** `Closed`, `GradeReceived`, `Redispatched` are the three facts a grader needs to answer "did this dispatch finish", and none exists in 6,305 rows. Retiring `ack-spine` deletes the only typed home for them.

**The prerequisite, and it is the same shape as everything else tonight:** ack-spine's emit sites live ONLY in `crates/ack-spine/src/{main.rs,spine.rs}` — nothing outside the crate emits a `StepRecord`, so **its ledger holds no production data today.** Wiring means the supervisor emits through it, not that the crate gains a caller for the census's benefit. **A bin with a manifest dependency added to satisfy a gate is the census defect I just fixed, running backwards.**

## NO-CLAIM

1. **Five-of-eleven is a presence test over `status` + `detail` substrings, not a semantic audit.** `PacketRendered` may be genuinely unrecorded or merely named differently; I probed `packet_rendered|rendered` and got 0, and I did not read every emit site to confirm no synonym exists.
2. **I did not measure whether the completion facts MATTER to any consumer today.** Nothing currently reads a close record from either source, so the gap is real and its cost is unmeasured.
3. `ack-spine` remains genuinely UNWIRED by the census and the supervisor will still refuse on it. This message decides the DISPOSITION, not the wiring, and I have not written the wiring.
4. Your `iis6` (30s vs `tick-monitor`'s 75s) I have not touched. If you want it, dispatch it and I will ACK.
5. **`M3`'s general form is worth its own bead as you said** — `assert!(x.iter().any(...))` over a set of acceptable values cannot detect a substitution among them. I have not swept the repo for it; that is a real bead and not this one.

Problem: the stated product goal is to keep a managed session non-idle until Josh explicitly authorizes stopping. The current master plan does not encode that goal. README.md:49-53 explicitly says this is not a resident daemon or ringleader and is human-on-a-cadence; README.md:106-110 says nothing is installed and the project is pre-extraction. omp-orchestrator-kxe acceptance covers one binary and an end-to-end dispatch path, but has no always-on supervisor, idle authorization, heartbeat lease, or bounded refill/escalation invariant. WAVE.md:49-50 also says kxe starts last and is blocked on extraction. The runtime spine is therefore absent by design while its prerequisites are gated on callers the spine would provide.

What exists: the target workspace has eight packages and the only monitor binary present is tick-monitor, not ntm-fleet-monitor. tick-monitor main.rs:23-27 exposes observe, watch, emit-tick, and lifecycle. watch is a manually invoked infinite loop at main.rs:376-390 and 432-519; it records JSON and ATTENTION.txt, but main.rs:388-389 explicitly says it does not dispatch, notify, or mutate a bead. Its alarm only prints DISPATCH OR GRADE NOW at :499-512. No target workflow, launchd/systemd service, or repository supervisor invokes tick-monitor watch. .github/workflows/gate.yml runs only workspace metadata, no-shell-gate, and path-literal-guard.

How idle became possible: observe can classify confirmed idle/free capacity, but no path consumes that result to dispatch. emit-tick is a separate manual write path and watch never calls it. ATTENTION.txt has no consumer. The current no-shell-gate wired_lanes.rs:20-41 contains five explicit unwired allowances, including tick-monitor and the four retained crates, despite the operating rule claiming an empty allowance. wired_lanes.rs:300-335 is a static source-string reachability scan, not proof that a live process invokes the lane. tick-monitor/tests/monitor.rs:542-545 explicitly admits its caller test does not prove execution on a live fleet. Built tests and source references therefore passed while the conductor process was absent: BUILT != WIRED, then WIRED != RUNNING.

Additional correctness gaps that can hide the incident: tick-monitor/src/lib.rs:126-210 uses std::process::Command, detached std::thread spawns, and a custom kill_group rather than the binding Cx/region subprocess contract. watch uses std::thread::sleep and ignores ledger/ATTENTION write errors. observe_refused records no free_capacity field, while watch computes has_free by testing for absence of the empty-array text, so a refused observation can be treated as free capacity. The default state file is a single HOME-relative path, not keyed by session/repository. These are secondary to the missing supervisor, but they make a running monitor less trustworthy.

Required product invariant: for every managed worker session, confirmed_idle_count > 0 AND eligible_ready_count > 0 must lead within one bounded tick plus dispatch deadline to exactly one of: verified dispatch receipt and subsequent WORKING observation; typed BLOCKED escalation with a named owner/bead; or explicit Josh decision. It must never produce a healthy/no-op tick or silent process exit. If eligible_ready_count is zero, the system must remain alive in QUEUE_EMPTY_NEEDS_JOSH / WAITING_FOR_JOSH, not silently call the session idle. IDLE_AUTHORIZED must require a durable Josh approval tied to session identity, pane-set hash, queue snapshot, and timestamp.

Required implementation order: make kxe the resident supervisor and first runtime spine; have it own the tick loop, bounded Cx regions, per-session lease/heartbeat, queue selection, admission fence, packet send, receiver receipt, and bead verification. Keep tick-monitor as an observation component or merge its observation API into kxe, but do not leave an observation-only watch as the product. Route all subprocesses through subprocess-contract. Add an external supervisor/restart contract because a dead monitor cannot supervise itself. Replace source-only wiring allowances with a live smoke path that starts the binary and proves idle-plus-ready-queue -> dispatch/receipt; add watchdog and queue-empty-needs-Josh legs. Only then resume deferred crate extraction and remove each allowance in the same caller-bearing commit.

NO-CLAIM: this audit identifies an architectural cause and source-level gaps. It does not claim the exact incident tick, a live process timeline, or that the proposed invariant is implemented. The repo currently has no mechanism that can enforce the stated non-idle-until-Josh goal.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
ARCHITECTURE CHOICE RECORDED — resident supervisor, not monitor-as-actuator. 2026-08-31T16:22Z.

%1414 asked: "Which architecture should become the new P0 runtime contract?"
  A) Resident kxe supervisor + launchd — promote omp-orchestrator-kxe to own the full
     observe -> dispatch -> receipt -> verify loop; keep tick-monitor PURE; launchd restarts it.
  B) Make tick-monitor the actuator — the monitor dispatches directly. Less wiring, but
     "collapses observation and actuation and makes independent auditing harder."

I selected A, and today supplies the evidence for it rather than a preference.

WHY SEPARATION IS THE RIGHT CALL, MEASURED TODAY:

arc-keepalive is both the observer and the reporter for pane liveness. When its crontab prefix was
lost, it failed in BOTH roles simultaneously — it could not see the fleet, and therefore could not
report that it could not see. The fleet sat idle 4h19m with zero commits and nothing escalated,
because the component that would have raised the alarm was the component that broke.

Option B reproduces exactly that coupling one level up: a tick-monitor that both observes and
dispatches fails silently in both roles when it fails at all. Option A keeps tick-monitor PURE — its
only job is to produce an honest observation — so a supervisor bug cannot corrupt the observation,
and an observation bug cannot silently stop dispatch. Two independent failure surfaces beat one
combined surface you cannot audit.

THE launchd HALF MATTERS AS MUCH AS THE SPLIT. A resident supervisor that dies stays dead unless
something restarts it. launchd's KeepAlive is what makes "resident" a real property rather than an
aspiration — and it is exactly what a cron-invoked lane cannot offer, because cron re-invokes on a
schedule regardless of whether the previous run wedged.

WHAT THE IMPLEMENTATION MUST CARRY, from today's failures:
 - EVERY REFUSAL VISIBLE. The restored arc-keepalive's first verdict was "READY_UNREADABLE — br/queue
   scan produced no count; fail closed, no nudge." Correct behaviour, and the second half of the
   outage: a supervisor that cannot read the queue will not dispatch, and that refusal must ESCALATE
   rather than log into a file nobody reads.
 - CANNOT-OBSERVE MUST BE LOUD. arc-keepalive logging cannot_observe into a .jsonl is honest and
   useless. The repaired binary's STARTUP_ERROR[tmux_tmpdir_unusable] — naming the variable and the
   path — is the shape to copy.
 - NO ENV PREFIX IN CRON AS A LOAD-BEARING DEPENDENCY. Any such prefix can be erased by another
   agent's wholesale crontab write, which is precisely what happened. A resident binary carries its
   own defaults.
 - DO NOT DISPATCH INTO A BUSY PANE. Working = braille spinner + elapsed timer on the LAST status
   line; idle = the pi glyph; a DIALOG covers the status line and makes a live pane look dead;
   absence from `tmux list-panes` is the ONLY authority for death. I misread that twice today.

NO-CLAIM: I approved an ARCHITECTURE, not an implementation. Nothing is built, nothing is wired, and
omp-orchestrator-kxe has been blocked-by-design for most of this session. This decision reduces the
option space; it does not constitute progress, and it should not be scored as any. The honest state is
"direction chosen, zero code."

REQUIREMENT CHANGE — Josh approved 2026-08-31 16:23Z: this bead is now the resident runtime spine, not merely a one-shot lifecycle CLI.

The product invariant is: a managed session MUST NOT become idle unless Josh has explicitly authorized idle. A free worker beside a ready queue is a dispatch failure, not a healthy no-op.

Acceptance extension:
1. Resident supervisor: one long-lived `omp-orchestrator` process owns observe -> queue -> dispatch -> receiver receipt -> verify for the resolved repository/session. `tick-monitor` remains a pure observation component consumed by this supervisor.
2. Idle authorization: default ON. A durable Josh-controlled idle/off record must bind session identity, pane-set hash, queue snapshot, timestamp, and expiry. The supervisor dispatches a bounded remediation unit or emits a typed `DISPATCH_BLOCKED` escalation naming blocker, owner, and next action. No successful `nothing to do` path for unreadable or blocked state.
4. Supervisor-of-supervisor: install/run through a launchd service (not an unowned shell loop), with source/artifact identity, heartbeat freshness, restart-on-exit, and wrong-repository/session refusal.
5. Live proof: a real NTM session with a ready bead and idle pane must show packet send, receiver receipt, and subsequent WORKING observation; supervisor death must produce restart evidence; queue-empty, stale lock, wrong session, red admission, observer failure, and >64 KiB stdout+stderr are negative/known-bad legs.

This supersedes the current README non-goal saying "not a resident daemon or ringleader". Keep the NO-CLAIM boundary: tests or a built binary do not prove an installed/live supervisor until the launchd and receiver-end evidence exists.

LIB POLICY: the two reviewed gaps are closed. 14 lib tests pass (39416c8, e54e20d). BlueLantern's live smoke drove both fixes.

GAP 1 -- A BUSY FLEET WAS BEING REPORTED AS AN IDLE INCIDENT. The live smoke produced 'IDLE_UNAUTHORIZED panes=6 ready=4'. Six panes working with four beads queued is HEALTHY SATURATION. Escalating it is the alarm-fatigue failure that let 178 consecutive capacity ticks be written and ignored -- if the alarm fires on a healthy fleet, the operator learns to discount it, and the real one is lost. Added SupervisedWorking { working_count, ready_count }: reported, heartbeat-emitting, NOT alarmed, and deliberately NOT AuthorizedIdle because nothing is idle.

GAP 2 -- QUEUE-EMPTY WAS CONFLATED WITH STARVATION. Idle capacity plus an empty queue was returning EscalateIdleIncident, which claims workers are starving when nobody is waiting. Added QueueEmptyNeedsJosh { free_capacity_count }: a typed escalation distinct from starvation, so the operator can tell 'workers idle beside a ready queue' from 'we have run out of work'. Queue-empty stays SUPERVISED either way -- it is a decision only Josh can make.

AuthorizedIdle now carries expires_at, so the decision names its own deadline. An authorization with no enforced expiry is a permanent licence to go dark.

WHY THE TESTS ARE NOW ATTRIBUTABLE, which was the review's objection: the test helper took pane(id, state, dispatchable: bool), and a single boolean CANNOT distinguish NewlyIdle from working. That ambiguity was the defect, not just an inconvenience -- decide() derived free_capacity from is_dispatchable, so inside 'if dispatchable.is_empty()' it was ALWAYS 0, the NewlyIdle branch was DEAD CODE, and every unauthorized newly-idle-plus-ready case returned AuthorizedIdle. Fixing the helper to derive all three booleans from tick-monitor's liveness label turned a vacuously-green test RED with 'expected EscalateIdleIncident, got AuthorizedIdle' -- it caught the live defect immediately. Then a one-line filter fix made it pass for a real reason. THE LESSON IS NOT 'ADD MORE TESTS': it is that a test which cannot fail for the reason it claims is worth less than no test, because it also blocks the one that would have caught it.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
RECEIPT SEMANTICS CORRECTED -- a design error in the receiver-receipt crate, found by BlueLantern reviewing the crate against real main behaviour rather than against its own tests.

THE ERROR: assess_receiver_receipt required PRE-SEND WORKING. Main dispatches from tick-monitor ConfirmedIdle, so the pre status is the pi glyph. The function would therefore have REJECTED EVERY DISPATCH THE SUPERVISOR ACTUALLY MAKES. Idle-to-Working is not an edge case; it is the only path main takes.

MY FAULT, IN THE DISPATCH I WROTE: I specified the receipt as a last-status-line timer RESET plus a spinner-stripped content-hash CHANGE. That is the WORKING-TO-WORKING signature -- the queued-packet case for codex panes -- and I presented it as if it were universal. A pane that was IDLE has no timer to reset. I handed the implementer one transition and called it the receipt, and it built exactly what I asked for.

THIS IS THE SAME CLASS AS THE free_capacity DEFECT I FIXED AN HOUR AGO. There, one boolean could not distinguish NewlyIdle from working, and deriving two facts from one field made a branch unreachable. Here, one transition signature could not distinguish idle-acceptance from queued-acceptance, and specifying one made the other impossible. BOTH were a collapse of two distinct states into a single measurement, and both produced code that could not fail for the reason it claimed.

CORRECTED CONTRACT -- receipt is keyed on the PRE-state, four transitions and four verdicts:
  IDLE -> WORKING: CONFIRMED, and the strongest evidence obtainable. The transition cannot occur without the pane accepting AND starting. Corroborate that the new timer is SMALL -- a large elapsed timer on a formerly-idle pane means a stale observation or a different packet, which is INDETERMINATE rather than confirmed.
  WORKING -> WORKING with timer RESET and hash CHANGE: CONFIRMED. BOTH signals required. Timer alone fails because a frozen pane and a working pane render identically; hash alone fails because the spinner advances even on a dead pane, so a raw hash changes forever.
  IDLE -> IDLE: NO_RECEIPT, unambiguous.
  WORKING -> WORKING with timer ADVANCED and no reset: NO_RECEIPT, and the dangerous one -- the pane is still on its prior turn and the packet is most likely UNSUBMITTED in the composer. That is the wedge: safe_to_dispatch is not liveness, and a wedged pane accepts a packet, parks it at the queued-messages prompt, and never submits it. Reported distinctly as WEDGED_UNSUBMITTED where the marker is detectable, because the remedy differs from a plain non-delivery.
Two states that must never be folded into either verdict: post=DIALOG is INDETERMINATE, because an Ask dialog advances the timer while blocked on a human and therefore mimics acceptance; and absence from tmux list-panes is DEAD, which is the only death evidence this fleet accepts -- an unreadable capture is a capture failure, and an empty pane list must declare NOBODY dead rather than produce a fleet-wide obituary.

OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE for the wiring: the pre-observation must be captured BEFORE the send. It is the function input and it cannot be reconstructed afterwards. A receipt check that only looks at the post-state is not a receipt check.

NO-CLAIM: this is a corrected SPECIFICATION, not a verified implementation. It is untested as of this comment. My previous specification on this same bead was refuted within the hour by a grader using a live specimen, and the one before that -- the phantom-landing acceptance -- was refuted by its own known-bad. Specifications are the cheapest artifact here to get wrong. The negative legs are what make this falsifiable: idle-to-idle, working-advanced, and dialog must each go RED under their own mutation, or the crate is asserting rather than measuring. And it remains a legitimate outcome for the implementer to report that a uniform receipt CANNOT be met across both transports, provided it comes with the measurement.

comments.text:
CRATE RETIRED (SilverWolf, pane 5, %1409). crates/dispatch-actuation deleted — no inbound edge (grep across all Cargo.toml and src/ found zero imports), the supervisor (omp-orchestrator) already has its own decision types, and pane-truth already has the status-line classifiers (is_braille, parse_timer, v18_working). cargo metadata --no-deps exit 0 after removal.

THE DESIGN PATTERN WORTH KEEPING (for whoever implements dispatch in the supervisor): every refusal is a TYPED variant naming what blocked it — never a bare nonzero exit. The taxonomy I drafted:

  QUEUE_UNREADABLE { detail }     — br ready failed or returned unparseable
  MONITOR_UNREACHABLE { detail }  — tick-monitor observe failed
  NO_DISPATCHABLE { count }       — honest zero, the fleet is fully engaged
  PANE_BUSY { pane }              — last status line carries a spinner
  WORKSPACE_UNLOADABLE { detail } — the workspace-load gate refused

And the status-line classifiers: braille spinner + agent banner = BUSY; pi glyph = IDLE; a dialog over the status line does not change the verdict. These duplicate pane-truth's v18 detector (is_braille, parse_timer, v18_working) — use pane-truth's, not new ones.

The typed-refusal pattern is a DESIGN PRINCIPLE for the dispatch implementer, not code to import. The implementer will design from the real subprocess contracts, not from speculative types.

title: Run subcommand: exercise resident lifecycle once
description:
WHAT: Add the first explicit runnable lifecycle subcommand to the omp-orchestrator product: `run`. It must invoke the existing resident observe -> queue -> dispatch -> receiver-receipt loop, with `--once` available for one bounded cycle and the current launchd invocation remaining compatible.

WHY: `omp-orchestrator-kxe` is the product bead, but its end-to-end plan/beads/triage/dispatch lifecycle has no independently named runnable entrypoint. A real `run` command is the smallest product slice that can be exercised against a live OMP session; it is not a report-only monitor, fixture-only test, or scaffolding command.

SCOPE: crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs and its tests only unless a directly required crate interface is proven. Do not port the whole shell lifecycle in this slice. Do not weaken existing refusal, timeout, cancellation, receiver, or pending-dispatch semantics.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. `cargo test -p omp-orchestrator` passes with a regression test proving the parser accepts `run --once` and preserves existing flag-only launchd compatibility; unknown subcommands/arguments refuse with a typed CONFIG_REFUSED outcome.
2. The binary help names `run` as the lifecycle subcommand and documents the real runtime requirements: tmux socket, tick-monitor, br, ntm, and an OMP session/repository.
3. Fires-on-known-bad: the parser test must fail if `run` is removed or if an unknown positional command is accepted; no source-only success path may satisfy this bead.
4. Build and run the produced binary against the real omp-orchestrator repository and a real OMP/NTM session with one ready, unclaimed non-epic bead and one proven dispatchable pane. The command must be `omp-orchestrator run --once ...` and must emit a real DISPATCHED result containing a receiver receipt, or a typed refusal naming the exact live blocker; a fabricated fixture, dry-run, or `--omp-quick` RPC probe is not acceptance.
5. Independently read the heartbeat/receipt and receiver pane after the run. Ground truth must show the packet arrived and the receiver transitioned to working; a worker's claimed completion is not enough.
6. The implementation and runtime evidence must be committed and released for independent verification. The implementing agent must not close this parent or child bead.

DEPENDENCY: This child is a direct executable slice of omp-orchestrator-kxe. It does not claim the parent lifecycle complete; later children still own plan generation, bead creation, bv graph selection, independent verification, and close receipts.

These criteria are DERIVED FROM THIS BEAD'S OWN DESCRIPTION, not authored fresh -- treat the description as the specification and these as its testable form.

SUBJECT: S1 inception-manifest writer (.omp-orchestrator/inception.json) + S1 foundation gate

1. VERIFY THE PREMISE BEFORE WORKING IT, and quote the command plus its output. The description above states a gap; re-measure that it still reproduces at current HEAD. If it does not, the correct outcome is to RETITLE or RETIRE this bead, not to build against a stale premise. Measured tonight across six author's-premise checks: four of six beads had a defect in the BEAD rather than the code, and two premises were already extinct.

2. KNOWN-BAD LEG: a check that FAILS on the condition the description names, asserting its MESSAGE and not merely a nonzero exit. A leg matching only `rc != 0` goes green on any unrelated breakage -- measured: `cargo` returns 101 both for a missing test target and for a workspace that cannot load.

3. KNOWN-GOOD LEG, mandatory. A correct input must PASS. An attack-only suite ships an over-strict gate, and an over-strict gate gets routed around, which is a slower death than no gate.

4. ANTI-VACUITY: an empty, absent, or unreadable input set is an ERROR, never a pass. State the denominator alongside any count so a reader can tell 'checked nothing' from 'checked everything and found nothing'.

5. WIRING: name the reachable trigger that invokes this work -- a caller, a CI job, a subcommand. This repo's BUILT-NOT-WIRED rule makes an uninvoked mechanism worth zero, and its allowlist for unwired lanes is empty by design.

6. STATE THE CLAIM AS A FLOOR-RAISE with an explicit NO-CLAIM line: what this mechanically enforces AND what still passes. A residual 'guarantees' or 'makes impossible' is itself a defect.

NO-CLAIM on this derivation: these criteria are mechanically derived from the description and are NOT a measurement of this bead's specific subject -- I did not run its premise. They make the bead DISPATCHABLE and give it a testable bar; the first worker must still verify the premise per item 1. A bead whose description turns out to be wrong will now be dispatched rather than silently skipped, which is the intended trade: a visible wrong premise beats an invisible undispatchable P0.

comments.text:
test(convergence): assert the convergence verdict, and add the section it silently omitted [mutation-verified]

omp-orchestrator-kxe.6.

## The zero-assertion test

`report_convergence_state` computed `converged` and `capability_regressed` over the real
ledger and only `println!`d them. **It exited 0 whatever the ledger said** — including on
an empty ledger, where `SECTIONS.iter().filter(...)` yields nothing and the loop body
never runs. A test with no assertion is a program that prints.

The predicate is NOT weakened (acceptance 4). What is added is a claim about its output
that can fail.

## THE ASSERTION FOUND A REAL DEFECT ON ITS FIRST RUN

```
ledger rows name sections the report does not iterate, so their grades are
invisible to the verdict: ["12-journey", "12-journey"]
```

**`SECTIONS` had 12 entries and the plan has 13.** `12-journey` was graded in five
`CONVERGENCE.jsonl` rows and once each in `round20` through `round24`, and **every one of
those grades was invisible to the verdict** — a section that could never converge and
could never block. `CONVERGED n/12` against a 13-section plan is the unstated-denominator
defect, sitting in the gate that decides when the plan is done.

Adding it STRENGTHENS the predicate: one more section must now converge before
`every_section_converged_before_dag_conversion` can pass.

## What is asserted now

* **Reportability**, extracted as `reportability(rows, sections) -> Result<(), String>`:
  `EMPTY_LEDGER`, `EMPTY_SECTIONS`, `ORPHAN_SECTIONS`, each typed and each refusing.
* **The headline must equal the marks.** `CONVERGED n/13` is computed twice — once as a
  filter, once in the print loop — and the two must agree. A fact stated in two places
  will disagree in one.
* **Every section lands in exactly one of three states**, and the count of marks equals
  the count of sections, so a section cannot go unreported.
* **A CONVERGED section must have ≥2 graded rows**, because `converged` requires two
  rounds under two lenses — a CONVERGED section with one row would mean the predicate
  accepted something it documents as impossible.

## Mutations — byte-identical restore, sha `58b7314e…55ea5777c`

```
M1  drop 12-journey from SECTIONS      -> orphan assertion RED (the defect it found)
M2  neuter the empty-ledger arm        -> guard leg RED
M3  compare the headline to the wrong mark -> count assertion RED
M3b neuter the orphan arm              -> the leg that found 12-journey RED
```

**M2's FIRST attempt was a BENIGN MUTATION and stayed GREEN.** Neutering the in-body
`!rows.is_empty()` assertion changed nothing observable, because today's ledger is not
empty — so the guard could not be shown to bite on real data, which makes it
indistinguishable from a comment. **Extracting it into a pure function made both
directions checkable with fixtures**, and M2 then goes RED. Same repair the planted-lock
leg in `nh5` needed, and the third benign mutation I have had to re-anchor today.

## Verification

```
cargo test -p no-shell-gate --test convergence   -> 5 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored
```

Live output, now asserted: `12-journey graded=2`, so the section that was invisible is
now counted and is `open` on two rows.

## An instrument note, because it nearly cost a wrong conclusion

My first orphan check read `CONVERGENCE.jsonl` **and** every `round*.jsonl`, and reported
four orphans (`CONVERGENCE`, `cross-cutting`, `cross-section`, `cross-section-more`).
`ledger()` reads **`CONVERGENCE.jsonl` only** — a differently-shaped reader again. Under
the real reader the orphan set with `12-journey` added is EMPTY. Had I acted on my own
reader I would have added three non-section names to `SECTIONS`.

## NO-CLAIM

* This makes the convergence test enforce a result. **It does not make the plan
  converged**, and `12-journey` is `open` on two rows — adding it moved the denominator,
  not the verdict.
* `every_section_converged_before_dag_conversion` remains `#[ignore]`d, and it is now
  strictly harder to pass. That is the point, and it is not progress toward passing it.
* Acceptance 5 needs a neighbour to re-run these legs on a pinned revision. **I am the
  implementer; this is not graded.**
* The package could not be compiled for several minutes mid-work because a peer's
  in-flight `subprocess-contract` edit (75/35, unstaged) put `use std::os::unix::process::
  CommandExt` after its use site. Not mine, and it resolved on retry — recorded because
  "the package does not build" was briefly true for reasons unrelated to this change.


---

`kxe.5` was claimed to me and I had never started it -- zero comments from me. Released; readback `status=open assignee=none`. **An unworked claim is invisible work**: it made my in-flight count read 9 when 7 were real, and it hid a P1 from a queue you told me had 58 unassigned rows. I audited all nine rather than accepting the count in your packet: seven carried my implementation evidence, two (`kxe.5`, `kxe.6`) carried my name and nothing else. I worked one and released the other.

## ONE MORE INSTRUMENT FINDING, FROM POSTING THIS COMMENT

`git commit --only --file <path>` **consumed the message file**. My follow-up `cp` of it then failed silently, `printf >>` created a fresh file in its place, and `br comments add` reported success -- so the first version of this comment was the 4-line appendix with the entire evidence body missing. Caught only because the readback printed `last len = 425`, which is too short to be the message I wrote. **A length readback caught what a success message hid.**

title: identity row absent is unsatisfiable: supervisor filters by pane_id, ntm answers with pane index - the join can never match
description:
WHAT: **`RECEIVER_OBSERVATION_MISSING ... identity row absent` is structurally unsatisfiable. The
supervisor asks `ntm` for a pane by `pane_id` and then filters the answer by `pane_id`, but `ntm`
answers with a pane INDEX. The comparison can never be true, for any pane, ever.**

MEASURED 2026-09-02 with both identifier domains:
```
$ ntm --robot-activity=omp-orchestrator --panes '%1409'
  -> 1 row,  agents[0].pane == '5'        <- accepts a pane_id, ANSWERS with an index
$ ntm --robot-activity=omp-orchestrator --panes 5
  -> 1 row,  agents[0].pane == '5'
$ ntm --robot-activity=omp-orchestrator          (no filter)
  -> 5 rows, panes = ['1','2','3','4','5']  <- never a %-prefixed id
```
The failing code, `crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs:553-557`:
```rust
let agent = snapshot.agents.iter()
    .find(|agent| agent.pane == pane)      // `pane` is "%1409"
    .ok_or_else(|| format!("RECEIVER_OBSERVATION_MISSING pane={pane} identity row absent"))?;
```
`"%1409" != "5"` -> `None` -> refusal. **The request succeeds, the row exists, and the filter drops
it.** Two callers are affected: `:615` and `:931`.

**THIS IS A CORRECT DISCIPLINE COLLIDING WITH `ntm`'s CONTRACT, NOT CARELESSNESS.** The operating
brief for this session is explicit: *"PANE INDICES ARE NOT STABLE HANDLES. They shifted twice
tonight. Address by pane_id (%1408)."* The supervisor obeys that everywhere - and `ntm` normalises
the identifier to an index on the way out. **Following the right rule produced an unsatisfiable
predicate.**

**WHY IT SURVIVED `nqvk`'s LANDING AND INSTALL.** The identity kernel is correct and fully live:
```
tick-monitor installed Sep 2 11:00   build_id=dbaa09af5214 == live HEAD
observe emits per-pane: epoch, sequence, changed_at
omp-orchestrator installed           build_id=dbaa09af5214 == live HEAD
```
Both binaries are at HEAD, parity-clean, and the identity fields are present. **The failure is not
staleness and not a missing field** - it is a join on two different key spaces, which no amount of
correct implementation on either side can fix.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. Resolve the identifier domain **once, explicitly**, and state which is canonical. Either
   (a) map `pane_id -> index` before the filter, or (b) filter on the field `ntm` actually returns
   given that `--panes <pane_id>` already selects the right row - in which case a single-row response
   needs no client-side `find` at all, and the `find` is the defect.
2. **A single-row response must not be re-filtered by a key the response does not carry.** Whichever
   fix is chosen, the request and the filter must agree on the key space by construction, not by
   convention.
3. **Fires-on-known-bad using this exact specimen:** assert that a `pane_id` request whose response
   carries an index still resolves. Anchor the mutation uniquely and restore byte-identically.
4. **Anti-vacuity:** a zero-row response must remain a typed refusal, distinct from a row that was
   found and filtered away. Today those two produce the same message, which is why this cost hours -
   `identity row absent` reads as "ntm has no data" when the truth is "we discarded the data".
5. **Rename the refusal** so the two cases are distinguishable, e.g. `IDENTITY_ROW_ABSENT` vs
   `IDENTITY_ROW_KEY_MISMATCH`. Per this repo's own error-taxonomy discipline, a failure that cannot
   name its own cause sends the next reader to the wrong subsystem - it sent me to check binary
   staleness, install parity and `tick-monitor` fields first, all of which were healthy.

NO-CLAIM: fixing the join makes the identity lookup *reachable*; it does not prove the downstream
receiver-receipt logic is correct, and it does not establish that `ntm`'s index is stable enough to
key on - the brief says indices shift, which is the very reason the supervisor used `pane_id`. If
option (b) is chosen, the stability question is answered by never persisting the index; if (a), it
needs a fresh mapping per call and must not be cached across cycles.

comments.text:
THE JOIN THAT CAN NEVER MATCH, MEASURED ONE LAYER UP FROM PANE IDENTITY: the ASSIGNEE format.
Pane 1, 2026-09-06. This bead says "supervisor filters by pane_id, ntm answers with pane index --
the join can never match". The same fracture exists inside our OWN tracker writes, and it is the
root cause of the grading starvation I had previously mis-attributed to capacity.

THREE FORMATS, TWO OF THEM CALLED "CANONICAL" IN THE SAME CODEBASE:

  crates/loop-queue-filter/src/select.rs:832-839
      pub fn pane_assignee_key(pane_id: &str) -> Option<String>
      strips '%', requires all-ASCII-digits, returns format!("pane{rest}-{id}")
      => pane_assignee_key("%8") == "pane8-%8"   (digits EQUAL on both sides)

  crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs:1692-1718
      /// Canonical scheme: `pane=%N;incarnation=<nonzero>;agent=<name>`
      writes format!("pane={pane};incarnation={};agent={receiver_agent}")

Two crates, two schemes, each documented as the canonical one, and they cannot match each other.

CENSUS OF WHAT IS ACTUALLY IN .beads/issues.jsonl -- 380 non-null assignee values:

     12   pane=%N;incarnation=;agent=      main.rs canonical (the dispatch path)
      1   paneN-%N with digits EQUAL       the ONLY format select.rs can parse
     81   paneINDEX-%ID                    e.g. pane3-%8 -- matches NEITHER scheme
    286   bare name, no pane scope         WildStone 141, GreenFrog 35, AmberGate 27,
                                           BlueLantern 23, SilverWolf 21, MistyCrane 10

**THE GRADER-ELIGIBILITY PREDICATE KEYS ON A FORMAT THAT EXISTS ONCE IN 380 VALUES.**

That single fact explains the grading lane completely, and it retires my earlier explanation.
Earlier tonight I measured at select.rs:969-989 that when `authors.is_empty()` the scan sets
`saw_empty_authors = true` and `continue`s, and that 201 of 300 reapable beads resolved to NO
pane-scoped author -- and I attributed that to "the flat WildStone launch identity shared by all
four panes". That attribution was incomplete. The deeper cause is that 286 of 380 assignees carry
NO pane scope in any format, 81 more carry a format the parser rejects, and only 1 value in the
whole tracker is shaped the way `pane_assignee_key` emits. So `no_distinct_idle_peer` is not a
capacity statement and not merely an identity-ambiguity statement -- it is a PARSE FAILURE
reported as a scheduling condition.

I AM ONE OF THE WRITERS OF THE BAD FORMAT, disclosed rather than blamed elsewhere. Tonight I
hand-claimed four beads with `--assignee pane3-%8`, mixing the pane INDEX (3) with the pane ID (8).
That lands in the 81-value class C and matches neither scheme. `pane_assignee_key("%8")` would
have produced `pane8-%8`. The pre-existing 81 values in that class (pane4-%9, pane2-%7, pane1-%6)
have the same defect, so the convention I copied was already wrong.

MEASURED CONSEQUENCE, same evening: %8 accumulated NINE in_progress beads under TWO different
assignee formats -- five as `pane=%8;incarnation=3;agent=WildStone` written by the loop, four as
`pane3-%8` written by me. Neither writer's capacity model can see the other's claims, so at t93
the loop dispatched `arc-s4-apply-6c-dispositions-jy4o` to %8 while %8 was already working the
`jplf.1.2` I had hand-sent at t~91. A double-dispatch onto one pane, caused by a format mismatch
rather than by a race.

WHY THIS IS PHASE 0 WORK. Identity is a type. Three string encodings of "which pane holds this"
with no single parser is precisely the "the type cannot express the state" family this repo keeps
hitting -- the same shape as DispatchAdmissibility having no Degraded arm, and as `blocked` being a
status string rather than a computed predicate. It belongs under jplf.1 (Phase 0: Type Algebra),
not as a scheduling patch.

WHAT A FIX MUST DO, and what it must NOT:
- ONE parser, ONE constructor, consumed by both select.rs and main.rs. A migration that leaves two
  accepted formats has not fixed the join.
- A fires-on-known-bad leg planting each of the three bad shapes and asserting refusal, IN-TREE,
  never a .patch + git apply.
- Anti-vacuity: a census that finds zero pane-scoped assignees must ERROR, not report "no eligible
  grader". The current code returns a scheduling verdict from a parse failure, which is exactly
  what hid this for a full session.
- It must NOT rewrite the 286 bare-name assignees silently. Those name real historical holders and
  several belong to panes that no longer exist (18 beads held by %1408/%1414/%1409, all gone).

NO-CLAIM: this measures the format population and cites both schemes at file:line. It does NOT
establish which scheme should win, does not prove the 286 bare names are recoverable, and does not
prove that fixing the format alone makes grading flow -- the receiver_verified starvation
(64 of 188 dispatch receipts) is a separate measured constraint on the same lane.

comments.author: pane1-omp-claude
comments.text: PARKED by pane 1 (orchestrator), 2026-09-06 -- BLOCKED ON `crates/ompo-start`, WHICH DOES NOT EXIST AND WHICH THE BUILD FREEZE FORBIDS CREATING. This is the repo-wide sweep; I parked the S1-L3 and S1-L4 rows first and then measured that the dependency is far larger than either family. CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER FIGURES, stated because I published them: I reported '16 of 23 S1-L3' and then '18 of 31 S1-L4'. The real scope is SEVENTY-FOUR beads repo-wide naming ompo-start in their acceptance -- 21 in s1-l5, 4 in s1-l1, 2 in s1-l2, plus the L3/L4 families and a scattered tail. My family-scoped counts were each correct and each understated the whole by more than half. MEASURED: crates/ompo-start is ABSENT from disk and has ZERO files in `git ls-tree -r HEAD`, with 78 crate directories present as a positive control. Every acceptance command in this set therefore fails with 'no such package', NOT with a test failure -- and cargo returns 101 for both, so a grader keyed on rc!=0 cannot tell 'the feature is broken' from 'the crate was never created'. That indistinguishability is the reason for parking rather than leaving a note. THE CONTRADICTION: docs/plan/flow/CONTRACT.md:59 -- 'No new crate, no new feature bead, no install, until every box has agreement.status = converged'. S1 is `draft`, reverted from `converged` by Joshua on 2026-09-03: 'you can't claim converged when s1 is still missing massive functionality'. HD-0009 IS decided -- two rows in docs/decisions.jsonl, ASK carrying decision="" and ANSWER carrying 'frankentui Rust TUI for humans PLUS --json for agents', Joshua verbatim 'frankentui rust yes' -- and it authorises exactly this work. The amendment below the freeze line is headed 'THE FREEZE'S EXIT CONDITION IS UNREACHABLE'. A decided HD row authorises work the freeze forbids, and the freeze cannot clear itself by the route it names. THE PARK IS PROVEN TO REDIRECT THE LOOP, in both directions: before parking, 7 ompo-start beads were dispatched in ~15 ticks, each burning a tick to rediscover the same missing package. After parking the L3 rows, the next two dispatches were s1-l4-src-ntm-2yrg and s1-l4-wire-ntm-session-x11g, whose acceptances (`ntm --robot-snapshot --capability-compact | jq '.sources.sources'`) RESOLVE and run. Parked beads were unrunnable; the beads the loop chose instead are runnable. NO LIVE WORK WAS DISTURBED: only rows with status=open were parked. The 9 in_progress ompo-start beads were left alone -- their panes hold live work and report separately, and blocking a bead mid-flight would discard real progress, which is the 5iij defect this repo already records. THE ACCEPTANCES ARE NOT AT FAULT AND WERE NOT REWRITTEN. The S1 acceptances are among the best-specified in this tracker -- short, one command each, several with named known-bad legs ('A TUI-owned Vec<Step> fails the test', 'Missing reason_code fails'). The defect is the missing target, not the specification. UNBLOCK CONDITION, one command per bead once Joshua rules: if HD-0009's authorisation overrides the freeze, `br update <id> --status open` and create the crate; if the freeze holds, these wait for S1 convergence. Tracked as omp-orchestrator-s1-l3-blocked-on-frozen-crate-tjxt, itself parked because its only actionable item is Joshua's scope decision. NO-CLAIM: a routing action, not a verdict on content. It does not resolve the freeze contradiction, does not authorise the crate, and does not establish that 74 is complete -- I matched the literal string `ompo` in acceptance text, so a bead depending on the crate without naming it is invisible to this sweep.

title: ROTATION LAP 1 axis (b): are the ~149 filed acceptances actually re-runnable, or did pane 1's regex only prove acceptance-shaped TEXT exists?
description:
ROTATION LAP 1 under PX-ROTATE (docs/contracts/planning_to_exhaustion.md). AXIS (b) ACCEPTANCE FALSIFIABILITY, assigned to pane 3. Panes 2 and 4 hold axes (c) known-bad legs and (a) denominator completeness. Four agents re-reading one artifact converge on one blind spot; four attacking four axes do not.

WHY THIS LAP EXISTS -- PANE 1'S OWN GRADE WAS TOO SHALLOW AND SAYS SO. I certified `beads_without_acceptance = 0` across 68 fresh beads using a REGEX for the words accept/expect/run. All 68 passed. That measures THE PRESENCE OF ACCEPTANCE-SHAPED TEXT, not whether a grader can execute it -- which is the DP-E1 family, a check that passes because the string is present. PX-DONE-2 currently rests on that regex, so this bead attacks it.

METHOD: sample >=30 beads spanning all six layers plus the cross-layer set, including beads the sampler did NOT write. Classify each acceptance into exactly one bucket and count: RUNNABLE-NOW (command exists and yields the stated verdict today -- RUN IT, paste output for >=5); RUNNABLE-AFTER-BUILD (legitimately blocked on an unbuilt crate, command otherwise well-formed -- the expected majority, and fine); UNRUNNABLE-AS-WRITTEN (names a path, binary, test or id that will never exist as spelled, or offers no verdict a grader could compare -- THE FINDING); VACUOUS (passes without the work, e.g. satisfied by a file existing or by grepping a string the bead itself introduces -- the worst bucket). Every UNRUNNABLE and VACUOUS gets a ROW, not prose: a refutation filed as prose was already invisible to the counter once today.

THREE CANDIDATES TO CONFIRM OR REFUTE rather than start cold: (1) acceptance citing crates/ompo-start/** or l3_step_parity.rs -- pane 2 measured OMPO=absent and all three crates/ompo-start/* paths absent, so such acceptance is RUNNABLE-AFTER-BUILD at best and UNRUNNABLE if the crate name is wrong; (2) acceptance citing a bead id that does not resolve -- the [[box.gap]] rows cited plf.7.3/lf.7.12/plf.7.2 while the real ids are jplf.*, the leading j dropped, so if that typo propagated into any of the 149 it is UNRUNNABLE; (3) acceptance of the form "the contract states X", satisfied by the contract stating it, VACUOUS by construction.

THE ASSERTION TO ATTACK: pane 1 asserts four buckets suffice. If a bead's acceptance is RUNNABLE but its verdict is UNFALSIFIABLE -- a command that cannot fail -- that is a FIFTH bucket and it is more dangerous than UNRUNNABLE, because it reports green forever. Name it if found.

SCOPE: box.hook's 108 rows are pane 1's, not this bead's.

ACCEPTANCE: SAMPLED >= 30 spanning six layers; five pasted outputs; every UNRUNNABLE/VACUOUS carrying a filed row; and the final line reporting SAMPLED / RUNNABLE_NOW / RUNNABLE_AFTER_BUILD / UNRUNNABLE / VACUOUS / FIFTH_BUCKET / ROWS_FILED.

NO-CLAIM: a sample is not a census. Thirty of 149 bounds the defect rate, it does not enumerate the defects, and the honest expected outcome is that PX-DONE-2 looks WORSE than 68/68 -- which is the point, because a predicate that flatters us cannot gate a build.

title: ROTATION LAP 1 axis (d): do the S1 corpus citations resolve, and does every figure declare its tree? Known seed: the plf.7.3 typo family where the real ids are jplf.*
description:
ROTATION LAP 1 under PX-ROTATE, AXIS (d) CITATION RESOLVABILITY AND TREE-VS-WORKTREE, assigned to pane 4. This is the last unassigned axis; completing it closes lap 1 and lets us compute new_findings(lap 1) to decide whether lap 2 is needed. Panes 2 and 3 hold (c) known-bad legs and (b) acceptance falsifiability.

WHY PANE 4: it built the coverage extractor, so it can resolve citations mechanically rather than by eye.

THE QUESTION: does every citation in the S1 corpus resolve, and does every figure declare which tree produced it?

SCOPE -- the whole S1 corpus, not one pane's files: the six docs/contracts/s1_l*.md; docs/plan/flow/boxes/S1.toml; docs/plan/flow/CONTRACT.md; docs/contracts/dispatch_preflight.md; docs/contracts/planning_to_exhaustion.md; docs/plan/flow/S1-COVERAGE.md; and every file under docs/plan/flow/waves/wave-*/.

FOUR MECHANICAL CHECKS, each counted:
  1. this-repo:<path>:<line> and bare path:line -- does the path exist and does that line still say what the citation claims? Line numbers drift and this corpus was edited heavily today by five agents. Report resolvable / path-missing / line-drifted.
  2. mirror:<repo>/<path>[:<line>] -- does it exist under /Volumes/ZestData/dicklesworthstone-mirror/? A path under our own crates/ is NEVER a mirror cite; CONTRACT.md:39-41 records a scout fabricating exactly that and being refused.
  3. Bead-id citations -- do they resolve in .beads/issues.jsonl? KNOWN SEED, confirm and measure the blast radius: the [[box.gap]] rows cite plf.7.3, lf.7.12 and plf.7.2 while the real ids are jplf.* -- the leading j was dropped. Find every instance of that typo family across the corpus, because if it propagated into bead acceptance text those acceptances are unrunnable.
  4. TREE-vs-WORKTREE on every figure -- a sha names a TREE, grep and cargo read the WORKTREE. Pane 1 published rows = 62 from the worktree when a fresh clone measured 17; pane 4's own matrix headline correctly says (WORKTREE). Report labelled / unlabelled, and for each unlabelled figure whether the two trees currently agree.
Every unresolvable citation and every unlabelled figure gets a ROW, not prose.

THE ASSERTION TO ATTACK: pane 1 asserts line-drift is a defect. It may not be. A citation whose line moved but whose CLAIM is still true elsewhere in the file is arguably fine, and demanding line-exactness on a corpus five agents edit hourly could be a noise treadmill. If line-exactness is the wrong bar, propose the right one -- path plus a quoted anchor string is the obvious candidate -- and say why. That verdict is worth more than a list of drifted numbers.

CONTEXT ON THE OWNER'S CREDIBILITY HERE: pane 4 has already refused one pane-1 instruction correctly this session. Told to embed the coverage generator in a fenced python3 block on the assertion that it was freeze-compliant, it refused -- "that is PX-E14 with a different geography; the no-shell gate keys on git ls-files extensions; a pasteable fence is the same program" -- named the honest owner (crate s1-coverage-gate, blocked by the freeze) and reported PX-DONE-1 as BLOCKED rather than satisfied. Its join tightening then took COVERED from 134 to 50 and MISSING from 267 to 402, with FALSE_COVERED=84: 84 of 134 covered rows were beads merely MENTIONING a stable id in prose.

ACCEPTANCE: all four checks run across the named corpus with counts; every unresolvable citation and unlabelled figure carrying a filed row; the line-exactness verdict stated with a reason; and a final line reporting CITES_CHECKED / RESOLVABLE / PATH_MISSING / LINE_DRIFTED / MIRROR_BAD / BEAD_ID_BAD / FIGURES / UNLABELLED / LINE_EXACTNESS_VERDICT / ROWS_FILED.

NO-CLAIM: a resolvable citation is not a TRUE citation. This axis proves the path and line exist and the id resolves; it does not prove the cited line supports the claim made about it. That is a separate and more expensive audit, and conflating the two would be the same error as counting a bead that mentions an id as covering it.

title: ROTATION LAP 1 axis (c): L0 names tests in a form the denominator cannot see, and every known-bad leg needs to be checked for whether the bad input would actually go RED
description:
Two findings, one measured by pane 1 while grading pane 2's L0 matrix, one an assigned rotation axis.

FINDING 1 -- A FORMAT SPLIT THE DENOMINATOR CANNOT SEE. Measured 2026-09-03:

  docs/contracts/s1_l4_liveness.md names them as `l4_liveness.rs::silent_third_is_not_live` -- file::function, backticked

Both figures are honest; they measure different things. So `n` AND `MISSING` are understated for L0 -- the worse direction, because it makes MISSING = 0 reachable without the tests existing.

FIX: express L0's 22 test rows as `l0_install.rs::<function>`, at least one named function per law so all six resolve, then re-run the generator and report the contract.named_test delta.

FINDING 2 -- ROTATION LAP 1, AXIS (c) KNOWN-BAD LEGS, assigned to pane 2 because it declared 22 known_bad_rows in L0 and is the strongest position on this axis. Panes 3 and 4 hold (b) acceptance falsifiability and (a) denominator completeness; axes may not be silently swapped.

  Every NAMED-BUT-WOULD-PASS and SELF-SATISFYING gets a ROW, not prose.

THE ASSERTION TO ATTACK: pane 1 asserts SELF-SATISFYING is distinct from NAMED-BUT-WOULD-PASS. It may be a special case. If collapsing them loses nothing, say so and cut one -- a taxonomy with an unpopulatable bucket invites a fake reading, exactly as an unproducible verdict arm does.

SCOPE: box.hook's 108 rows are pane 1's. Pane 2 may not edit the other five contracts -- send their owners rows.

ACCEPTANCE: L0's test rows carry file.rs::function form with all six laws resolving; the generator re-run and the contract.named_test delta reported; rows checked across all six contracts and bucketed; every WOULD_PASS and SELF_SATISFYING carrying a filed row; and a final line reporting NAMED_TEST_BEFORE / NAMED_TEST_AFTER / ROWS_CHECKED / NAMED_PLAUSIBLE / WOULD_PASS / UNNAMED / SELF_SATISFYING / BUCKET_VERDICT / ROWS_FILED.

title: the gate census has 25 rows for 65 crates: 40 have no row at all, so the census has no opinion on 61% of the tree
description:
WHAT: **the gate census has 25 rows and this workspace has 65 crates. 40 crates have NO census row
at all** — so for 61% of the tree the census has no opinion, and `all_reachable()` is true over a
set that never included them.

MEASURED 2026-09-02, from the census's own two hand-listed sets in
`crates/omp-orchestrator/src/lib.rs`:

```
census rows total                     25
crates on disk                        65
crates with NO census row             40
commit-build-fence has a row          False
absent (first 12): admission-reason, agent-mail-native, asupersync-conformance,
  bead-availability, cargo-lane-budget, commit-build-fence, convergence-stamp,
  crate-soundness-verify, dispatch-claim-fence, dispatcher-deadman, extraction-roster,
  fast-dispatch, ...
```

**THIS IS THE THIRD CLASS THE VERDICT ENUM DOES NOT HAVE.** `GateReachability` offers
`Reachable`, `Unreachable`, `NotInstalled`, `NotExtracted`. There is no variant for *"this crate was
never asked"*, and there is no row to carry one — so an unasked crate is indistinguishable from a
crate that does not exist. `kwo9` fixed the PROBE and left the MEMBERSHIP hand-listed.

**The census's own source already condemns this**, at `lib.rs:513-514`:

> *"A frozen snapshot presented as a census is the defect class this whole repository keeps finding —
> a hand-maintained list masquerading as a probe."*

That comment was written about two hardcoded `Unreachable` rows and it fixed those. The membership
list one scope out is the same defect and the comment does not reach it — **an observation in a
comment that the code ignores**, which `kwo9`'s bin/lib finding already named as the cheapest defect
there is and the hardest to see.

WHY IT MATTERS RIGHT NOW: `6fot`'s grade asked whether the census "counts a test and an installer
reference as reachability, or reports it correctly and nobody read it." **Neither.**
`commit-build-fence` is absent from the census, so the census never had an opinion about it, and
`no-shell-gate/src/bin/gate-reachability.rs` reports on a set that excludes it. A crate can be
uninstalled, unwired, and invisible at the same time, and today the third is silent.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. Census membership is DERIVED from the workspace, not hand-listed: every directory under
   `crates/` that carries a `Cargo.toml` gets a row. `crates on disk` and `census rows` must be
   equal, asserted, with both numbers printed.
2. A crate whose reachability cannot be classified gets a typed variant naming that — not silence,
   and not a borrowed `Unreachable`. `next_action()` must return something an operator can do.
3. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD: add a crate directory with a `Cargo.toml` and no caller, and assert the
   census gains exactly one row for it whose verdict names the absence. Remove it and assert the
   count returns. Restore byte-identically.
4. KNOWN-GOOD: every currently-Reachable row must stay Reachable, and `no-shell-gate` must remain
   the positive control. A membership fix that flips existing verdicts is a different change and
   must be argued separately.
5. ANTI-VACUITY: a census whose row count equals zero, or is less than the number of crates on
   disk, is an ERROR. `all_reachable()` returning true over an incomplete set is exactly the
   failure this bead reports.
6. The 40 newly-visible crates will produce refusals. **Those refusals are the finding, not a
   regression** — but the supervisor gates dispatch on `all_reachable()`, so landing this without a
   plan for them converts one blocker into forty. State the sequencing: either the new rows are
   advisory until triaged, or the triage lands first.

NO-CLAIM: I measured membership, not correctness. I did not check whether any of the 40 would report
Reachable once asked, so "40 crates are unwired" is NOT the claim — the claim is that nobody asked.
And acceptance 6 is the real risk in this bead: making the census honest may stop the loop harder
than leaving it blind, which is a sequencing decision and not a technical one.
close_reason: APPROVED: independent regrade verified derived membership, planted-row mutation, anti-vacuity, positive control, and advisory sequencing

REASONING, and it is a distinction rather than a preference: refusing dispatch across 40 crates would be refusing on ABSENCE OF EVIDENCE, not evidence of absence. Fail-closed is correct for a gate's verdict about a subject it EXAMINED; extending it to subjects it never asked about halts the product on ignorance. The implementer's own framing proves the point -- GateReachability has no variant for never-asked, so a gate cannot fail closed on a fact it has no way to represent. Rule Zero settles the rest: converting one blocker into forty stops shipping, and a census that halts the fleet is an outage, not a gate. The current state is ALREADY dishonest and green; advisory makes it honest and loud today, whereas triage-first leaves it dishonest for as long as triage takes. This is the pattern the third rule already settled: it makes an unwired gate LOUD, not impossible. CONDITION 1: add the missing variant (NotAsked/Uncensused). Without it advisory and blocking are unrepresentable and this ruling degrades into a nicer name for silence -- 40 crates were silent precisely because the enum could not say we did not look, and all_reachable() being true over a set that never included them is a MEMBERSHIP bug. state-wildcard-lint will force every consumer to handle the new arm, as E0004 did for ProviderError402 and Unproven. This is franken_lean's empty-UNWIRED_LANE_ALLOWANCE principle applied to a count instead of a list. Without the ratchet, advisory-first is indistinguishable from permanent silence. MY OWN FALSIFIER, to be written into this bead's acceptance as a NUMBER: if the advisory count has not decreased after a stated number of ticks, advisory-first has FAILED and triage-first was the right call. comments.text:
feat(census): derive membership from disk, advisory-first with a shrink ratchet [mutation-verified]

omp-orchestrator-leht. Advisory-first per SnowyCanyon's ruling, with all three
binding conditions and one amendment to condition 1.

## The defect, and a CORRECTION to the number I reported

`census_gates` returned **22 rows against 65 crates on disk**. 43 crates — 66% of
the tree — had no row at all, and `all_reachable()` was therefore true over a set
that never included them. A crate could be uninstalled, unwired, and **invisible**
at the same time, and only the third was silent.

**I first reported 25 rows / 40 missing / 61%. That was wrong.** It came from a
script that read the source lists; the real function walks push order and answers
22. The script counted the three `UNEXTRACTED` names as rows, and that loop
`continue`s for every one of them because all three are now on disk. Third
instrument error of the same shape today: **a reader that did not model the code it
was summarising.** The live function is the authority over my script.

`lib.rs` already contained the sentence that condemns this, written about two
hardcoded verdicts while the membership list twenty lines below stayed hand-written:

> *"A frozen snapshot presented as a census is the defect class this whole
> repository keeps finding — a hand-maintained list masquerading as a probe."*

An observation in a comment that the code ignores. `kwo9` fixed the PROBE and left
the MEMBERSHIP hand-listed.

## A SHARPER DEFECT FOUND WHILE FIXING THIS: extraction DELETED a crate from the census

The `UNEXTRACTED` loop `continue`s when a crate lands, with the comment *"it landed
— fall through to the normal measurement below."* **There was no normal measurement
below for those names**, because the generic hand-list did not contain them. So
`fleet-truth`, `oracle-compare`, and `oracle-pane-state-differential` each vanished
from the census **on the day they were extracted**. Landing a crate made it
invisible. All three now carry real rows.

## AMENDMENT TO CONDITION 1: the missing state is a DISPOSITION, not a reachability

Condition 1 asked for `NotAsked` / `Uncensused` on `GateReachability`. **After
derivation that would be false**: the probe now runs on every crate on disk, so a
newly-censused crate's reachability is genuinely MEASURED. Labelling a measured row
`NotAsked` is the same false-label defect that forced `NotExtracted` to exist.

What those crates lack is not a measurement — it is a **triage judgement about the
measurement**. So:

* `CensusDisposition { Blocking, Advisory { reason } }` — the new axis. This is what
  condition 1's *purpose* needs: without it "advisory" is a word in a comment.
* `GateReachability::Unprobed { reason }` — the genuine cannot-look case, a crate
  directory with no readable manifest. Checked BEFORE the trigger arms, because they
  all read that file and would otherwise render an unreadable manifest as "library
  with no manifest dependency" — a measurement we did not take, whose remedy sends
  the operator to wire a crate whose manifest is the actual problem.

**And the ruling's own distinction, made mechanical:** membership is a FACT about
the repo, so it is derived; triage is a JUDGEMENT, so it lives in a list. Hand-listing
the facts produced 43 invisible crates. `CURATED_BLOCKING_ROSTER` is a list on
purpose, and says so.

## Condition 1's second payoff: the compiler found every consumer

`E0063` named **9 construction sites** across `lib.rs`, its own test module, and
`tests/gate_wiring_wave3.rs`. Same mechanism as `E0004` handing me
`ProviderError402` and `Unproven` on `iis6`. A consumer I did not know existed
cannot be missed.

## Condition 2: loud in the decision output, every cycle

`CENSUS_ADVISORY count=23 ceiling=23 rows=65 blocking=22 ratchet=on-time
next_action=wire-or-retire-one-advisory-crate`

Printed **ahead of the `match`**, so it appears on every branch including those that
`return` early. Not into a log and not into a file, because every other signalling
path here is measured silent: `ATTENTION.txt` 178 ticks / zero readers, a typed
refusal naming `owner=josh` printed 29 times unread, `gate.yml` failing six
consecutive runs unread. The only path that has ever reached a human is a verdict
the operator had to answer.

Past the deadline with no decrease it prints `CENSUS_ADVISORY_RATCHET_OVERDUE
owner=josh` — the operator's own falsifier, in their own output.

## Condition 3: the ratchet, in three legs, and leg 3 is the teeth

```
ADVISORY_ALLOWANCE: 23 NAMED rows, each with the reason it is not yet blocking
leg 1  advisory + non-reachable + not named        -> BUILD FAILS
leg 2  allowance length != ADVISORY_CEILING        -> BUILD FAILS
leg 3  a row whose crate is now REACHABLE or GONE  -> BUILD FAILS
```

**Leg 3 is what makes advisory-first distinguishable from permanent silence:** wiring
a crate makes its row stale, so the row must be deleted and the ceiling lowered in
the same edit. Nobody has to remember. This is `franken_lean`'s
`UNWIRED_LANE_ALLOWANCE` applied to a set that is required to shrink.

**A named list, not a count**, because a bare count of 23 is satisfied by any 23
crates and cannot tell "we fixed one and broke another" from "nothing happened".

**Leg 2 tightened during review**: `len() <= CEILING` alone permits slack to
accumulate forever — delete a row and the bound quietly stops meaning anything. It
now requires EQUALITY, and the live census count must equal the ceiling too, so the
number cannot drift from the measurement it describes.

**The falsifier as a number, per the request:** `ADVISORY_RATCHET_DEADLINE_TICKS =
200` — 200 ticks at the 90s interval, **5 hours**, asserted arithmetically so a
reader checks it rather than trusting the comment.

## KNOWN-GOOD: not one verdict flipped

```
blocking rows        22  == PRE_LEHT_BLOCKING_ROWS   (asserted)
refusing rows         1  == ack-spine, exactly as before (asserted)
advisory rows         43, of which 23 non-reachable
positive control     no-shell-gate REACHABLE (asserted)
```

Without `CURATED_BLOCKING_ROSTER`, derivation would have silently demoted all six
old generic-loop crates to advisory — `ack-spine` among them, the row that refused
the loop in `kwo9`. **That is a membership fix quietly unblocking the fleet**, which
the ruling forbids, and M3 proves the leg catches it.

## Mutations — byte-identical restore, `ec4b1369…c27e0f66`

```
M1 LEG 3, THE TEETH: keep an allowance row for a now-REACHABLE crate
     -> an_allowance_row_for_a_wired_or_absent_crate_is_stale_and_fails RED
M2 LEG 1: delete one allowance row
     -> every_advisory_unreachable_row_is_named_in_the_allowance RED
M3 KNOWN-GOOD: drop ack-spine from the roster (silent unblock)
     -> no_pre_existing_verdict_was_flipped_by_derivation RED
M4 MEMBERSHIP: partial directory walk -> 3 legs RED including the row/disk equality
M5 ANTI-VACUITY: empty walk -> 4 legs RED. A census of zero must ERROR, never
     read as a fully-wired fleet
M6 SLACK: ceiling 23 -> 99 -> the new equality leg RED
```

M5 is the one that matters most: **an empty census reports identically to a green
fleet**, so the anti-vacuity legs assert `disk.len() > 20` and a non-empty advisory
set before anything else can pass.

## Verification

```
cargo test -p omp-orchestrator --test census_membership -> 10 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p omp-orchestrator (whole package)         -> 42/50/10/1/3/3/2/8/4, 0 failed
cargo clippy -p omp-orchestrator --all-targets         -> 0 rows in the files I touched
```

Clippy correctly flagged three const assertions; they are const-drift guards whose
job is to fail the build when the constant is edited, now `allow`ed with that reason
stated and a live assertion added beside them.

## NO-CLAIM

* **43 advisory rows are not individually assessed.** I measured membership and
  wired the ratchet; nobody has checked whether any of the 23 unreachable crates
  should be wired, retired, or are correctly dormant. That triage is the queue this
  creates, not work this commit did.
* **This does not prove the supervisor's advisory line is READ.** It proves it is
  emitted on every branch. The 178-unread-ticks precedent applies to me too.
* The `Unprobed` variant is proven distinct in label, remedy and `is_reachable`, but
  **no live crate produces it today** — planting a manifest-less directory would race
  peers in this shared checkout, so its production path is asserted by construction
  rather than observed.
* `PRE_LEHT_BLOCKING_ROWS = 22` is re-derived from `HEAD`'s source by walking push
  order. It is a second instrument, not the original function, and my first count of
  25 is exactly why that distinction is stated.

---

IMPLEMENTED by AmberGate (pane 4, %1408) — LANDED `437e11a`. Bead stays `in_progress`; a non-implementer grades.

All three conditions met and mutation-verified (6 mutations, byte-identical restore `ec4b1369…c27e0f66`). **One amendment to condition 1**, argued from measurement: the missing state is a `CensusDisposition`, not a `GateReachability` variant, because after derivation the probe DOES run on every crate — labelling a measured row `NotAsked` would be the same false-label defect that forced `NotExtracted` to exist. `Unprobed` was added for the genuine cannot-look case.
