omp-orchestrator-leht, follow-up to 437e11a. **Two defects in my own condition-2
work, both found by RUNNING the binary rather than reading the diff.**

## 1. A count printed after something that can refuse is not printed every cycle

The first version sat immediately after `decide()`. That reads as "every branch",
and it is not: **MEASURED against the current tree, the tick aborts at
`reap-finished-panes` BEFORE `decide` is ever called**, so the count printed on
zero of my probe runs.

```
$ omp-orchestrator --once --session omp-orchestrator
OBSERVATION tick=1 session=omp-orchestrator panes=5 ... free_capacity=1
SUPERVISOR_REFUSED reap-finished-panes exited=2 stderr=usage error: unknown argument --repo
```

The live build reaches `decide` on **39 of 39 ticks** (`GATE_UNWIRED 39 ==
SUPERVISOR_REFUSED 39` in the heartbeat), which is exactly why the placement bug was
invisible from the ledger — the ledger says the branch is reached, and it is, on the
INSTALLED build. Moved to the head of `run_cycle`, ahead of every kernel invocation
that can abort a tick.

The reap abort itself is NOT mine (`git blame` -> `4371bb98`, 09-01) and is filed
separately: the source passes `--repo` and the installed reaper rejects it.

## 2. A deadline already past is not a deadline

`ADVISORY_CEILING_RECORDED_AT_UNIX` was `1_756_845_000` — **one year off**. The live
run printed `CENSUS_ADVISORY_RATCHET_OVERDUE` on tick 1: 350,394 elapsed ticks
against a 200-tick deadline. A verdict true the instant it is recorded carries no
information and would have trained the operator to ignore the line — the fifth
instance today of a signal that is loud in principle and silent in fact.

The constant now records the moment it was set, and the decision is a PURE function
so both directions are checkable instead of only the one the clock happens to be in:

```rust
pub fn advisory_ratchet_overdue(now, recorded_at, interval, deadline_ticks,
                                advisory_count, ceiling) -> bool
```

**Third direction, which the inline version did not have:** past the deadline but
the count DECREASED returns `false`. The falsifier is about a stalled ratchet, not
elapsed time — without it the verdict would nag forever after 5 hours no matter how
much work landed.

                    next_action=wire-or-retire-one-advisory-crate

title: P1: wire lifecycle ledger reader into conductor wake
description:
WHAT: (a) wire LifecycleReader::wait_for_rows into the conductor wake path in crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs; (b) consume lifecycle rows newer than the persisted cursor for the active bead set; (c) preserve typed timeout/cancellation and do not fall back to mail-only wake.
WHY: the new reader is intentionally shipped without main.rs wiring because that file is owned by another lane. Until this bead lands, completion rows can exist without waking the conductor, so a green reader remains BUILT != WIRED.
ACCEPTANCE: cargo test -p ntm-fleet-monitor and cargo test -p omp-orchestrator pass without --workspace or release mode; production main.rs calls the reader at the wake decision seam; the caller passes &Cx first and checkpoints every wait iteration; no detached task exists; timeout is reported as typed TimedOut distinct from Empty; restart with the same cursor does not redeliver; a known-good completion row wakes the conductor; a missing completion row remains a typed timeout; the reader's cursor mutation leg is RED and restored GREEN; the completion-side writer is named and proven in-tree.
acceptance_criteria:
1. KNOWN-BAD leg (must be proven live, not assumed): with the ledger containing a completion row for an active bead written AFTER the persisted cursor, assert the conductor wake path in crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs returns a wake caused by that row (assert on the row id/seq carried into the wake decision, not merely "conductor woke"). Any pre-existing green row from mail-only wake is NOT sufficient evidence: mail wake and ledger wake are indistinguishable at the "woke" boolean, so the test must disable/starve the mail path (or assert the returned WakeCause::Lifecycle{row_seq}) and fail if wake occurs with mail as cause.

2. KNOWN-GOOD (anti-over-strict) leg: a ledger row that is (a) older than or equal to the persisted cursor, or (b) for a bead not in the active set, must NOT wake the conductor and must yield typed TimedOut after the configured deadline — proving the fix did not degrade into "wake on any row". Also assert a normal mail-only wake still works when no lifecycle rows exist.

3. Distinct typed outcomes: assert TimedOut != Empty as separate enum variants at the call site in main.rs — one case with zero matching rows and deadline elapsed => TimedOut; one case with an immediate empty poll/non-blocking read => Empty. Test must match on the variant, not on Result::is_err or a string.

4. Anti-vacuity: if the lifecycle scan returns zero rows AND zero candidate beads AND zero cursor state, the test harness must emit a typed error (e.g. NoLedgerRowsObserved) and FAIL — an empty scan set, an absent ledger file, or a skipped test is never a pass. Print the observed row count and cursor value in every leg.

5. Mutation leg (RED then byte-identical restore): record sha256 of crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs (and the reader source) before mutation; mutate the cursor comparison (e.g. `>` -> `>=` or drop the cursor filter entirely) and show the redelivery/known-bad test goes RED with the failing assertion text; restore and show `sha256sum` matches the pre-mutation digest exactly and the suite is GREEN again. Paste both digests.

6. Live vs fixture: MEASURED LIVE — the production call site in main.rs (cite file:line of the `wait_for_rows` call and of the `&Cx` first parameter), the checkpoint call inside every wait iteration, absence of any `tokio::spawn`/detached task on the wake path (grep evidence with file:line, empty grep result must be asserted as an explicit expected-empty check, not silence), and cargo test -p ntm-fleet-monitor + cargo test -p omp-orchestrator (no --workspace, no --release) exit 0 with test counts > 0. MAY BE FIXTURE — the ledger row contents and the bead set used to drive the cases.

7. Restart/no-redelivery: run the wake path, persist the cursor, restart the reader with that same persisted cursor, and assert the previously consumed row does NOT wake again (typed TimedOut), then append a new row and assert it DOES wake — proving the cursor advances and is durable, not that nothing ever wakes.

8. Open sub-item: "the completion-side writer is named and proven in-tree" is currently unmeasured. Either cite the writer's file:line and add a test that the writer's emitted row is the exact row consumed by this wake path (end-to-end, same schema/columns), OR file a separate bead for it and reference that bead id here — do not mark this bead complete with the writer silently assumed.

title: P1: WrongReceiverEvent guard is invisible to all 63 tests -- disabling it leaves the whole ntm-fleet-monitor suite green, so a grade can be pinned to a stale ReceiverVerified row
description: MEASURED 2026-09-05 by pane 1 while grading omp-orchestrator-wire-typed-lifecycle-ledger-h5o8. The ledger passes every acceptance leg -- all 7 row types present where 0 existed before, wired at a real binary call site (crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs:1565, LifecycleLedger::start immediately after 'dispatch preflight passed pane={pane}'), named known-bad legs at bead_lifecycle_ledger.rs:251 and :283, and cargo test -p ntm-fleet-monitor returning 63 passed 0 failed across 8 suites. THEN THE MUTATION LEG FAILED TO BITE. Disabling one guard in crates/ntm-fleet-monitor/src/bead_lifecycle.rs -- rewriting 'if receipt.receiver_event_id != receiver.id { return Err(LifecycleError::WrongReceiverEvent); }' as 'if false && receipt.receiver_event_id != receiver.id { ... }' -- produced 8 passed 0 failed on the ledger suite and 63 passed 0 failed ACROSS THE WHOLE CRATE. Nothing went red. Restored byte-identically, verified by filecmp and by git status --porcelain returning clean against HEAD, and the suite returned 63 passing. NOT ONE OF 63 TESTS CAN SEE THAT GUARD: a GradeReceipt naming the wrong receiver_event_id is accepted, and LifecycleError::WrongReceiverEvent is an error variant no test can prove is reachable. AGENTS.md states why this outranks a green run: 'A mutation that fails to bite is the most valuable result available: the suite was green, acceptance was satisfied on paper, and only deleting the subject showed the gate could not see it.' WHY THIS GUARD IS LOAD-BEARING WHERE THE TESTED ONES ARE NOT: the model already refuses the three invalid closes and the unnamed GradedFix, both with named tests. WrongReceiverEvent is the one that binds a grade to the exact delivery it grades. Without it a receipt can be pinned to a STALE ReceiverVerified row -- an earlier dispatch of the same bead, or a different pane's delivery -- and the lifecycle records a pass against work that was never received. That is ack-stage's AckReadbackMissing failure re-entering through the grade side, and it is the shape of tonight's %9 incident in which a completion reached the tracker while the conductor's mail-only wake never saw it. TASKS: (1) a test that fails under exactly that mutation, constructing a receipt whose receiver_event_id points at a different real ReceiverVerified row for the same bead (a stale one from a prior dispatch is the honest case) and asserting LifecycleError::WrongReceiverEvent, then re-running the mutation and pasting both results -- 'if false &&' must go RED and restored must go GREEN, because a test that passes both ways is not attributable; (2) sweep every other LifecycleError variant with the same mutation leg, starting with GraderMismatch at :281 which is adjacent and equally unverified, and report which variants no test can see; (3) report the denominator as <n> variants / <n> mutation-detected, because a crate with 63 tests and 4 of 11 variants unreachable-by-test is a different artifact from one with 11 of 11 and only the number distinguishes them. COUNTER-ARGUMENT THAT MUST BE ANSWERED RATHER THAN PATCHED: WrongReceiverEvent may be UNCONSTRUCTIBLE through the public API -- if LifecycleLedger only ever hands back the receiver row it just wrote, a caller cannot supply a mismatched id and the guard is a correctly-untestable defensive branch; if so, mark it declared-not-wired with a dies-when reason rather than manufacturing a test, since AGENTS.md explicitly forbids 'manufacturing a test to justify an identifier' and a named residual beats a fake leg. NO-CLAIM: one mutation on one guard establishes that this guard is invisible to the current suite. It does not establish that the guard is wrong, that the ledger is incorrect, or how many other variants share the gap -- the sweep is what determines that.
close_reason: MUTATION-VERIFIED by pane 1 (non-author) -- and this time the mutation BIT, which is the whole point of the bead. THE EXACT MUTATION THAT PREVIOUSLY LEFT 63 OF 63 GREEN NOW GOES RED. title: tick-monitor lifecycle attributes CITED SHAs as a bead's own landing, inflating LANDED_UNGRADED with phantom work
description:
WHAT: `tick-monitor lifecycle` harvests commit SHAs from a bead's PROSE and records them as that bead's own landing. A SHA cited as ANOTHER bead's evidence therefore promotes the citing bead into LANDED_UNGRADED, so the grading queue fills with beads where nothing was ever built.

MEASURED 2026-08-31, found by a grader disputing my premise rather than by me:
  tick-monitor lifecycle reported: omp-orchestrator-2lo  author=-  deps=0  landed=3f821d4
  git log --all --grep='2lo'      -> EMPTY. No commit references 2lo at all.
  git log -1 3f821d4              -> 'gate: no-shell-gate - fail the build on tracked .sh/.py [mutation-verified]'
                                    which is omp-orchestrator-4ak's work, not 2lo's.
  3f821d4 in 2lo's comments      -> present, as a CITATION, in a comment I wrote myself.
So the tool read my own cross-reference to a different bead's commit and reported it as this bead's implementation.

IMPACT, and it is a ROUTING-SAFETY defect rather than a cosmetic one. LANDED_UNGRADED is what I use to decide who grades what. A phantom row causes a grader to be dispatched at a bead with no artifact, which is a wasted slot under a build freeze when grading is the only work available. Worse, it is INDISTINGUISHABLE from real work in the output: the row carries a real SHA that resolves in git, so a conductor checking 'does the cited commit exist?' gets YES and proceeds. It took a grader re-deriving the premise -- `git log --grep` on the bead id -- to catch it. That check is exactly what the tool should be doing and is not.

THIRD DEFECT IN THIS TOOL IN ONE SESSION, and all three are the same failure of attribution:
  1. author= reads the current ASSIGNEE, not the implementer. Observed live: r3h flipped author=GreenFrog -> author=AmberGate when I routed AmberGate as its GRADER. I nearly handed a bead back to its own implementer.
  2. dangling SHA citations were counted as unresolvable commits -- fixed in fa5129e/b352af1 by requiring `in_citation_position` for marker words and excluding truncated sha256 content hashes.
  3. THIS: a SHA in citation position is still credited as a landing. Fix (2) narrowed which TOKENS count as commit-shaped; it never asked WHOSE commit a resolvable SHA is.

`git log --all --grep=2lo` was EMPTY and `3f821d4` is `4ak`'s gate work, present in

where nothing was built.

commit's own subject and body and looks for the bead id. A bead naming a commit is a
citation and proves nothing about authorship; only the commit can claim the bead.

than by review. They set `cited_only_shas` by hand on a `Unit` literal and asserted
the accessor and the render. Reverting the attribution check to `if true` — the exact
pre-fix behaviour — produced ZERO failing suites. The tests exercised the REPORTING
and never the DECISION.

That is a fooled certificate inside the commit that fixes a fooled promotion, and the
remedy was not a sharper assertion on the same shape. The decision is now a pure
function a test can call:

  pub enum CitationClass { Landed, BorrowedCredit, Dangling }
  pub fn classify_citation(exists: bool, names_bead: bool) -> CitationClass

Re-running the identical mutation — `(true, false) => Landed`, the pre-fix rule now
inside the decision — turns 1 suite RED naming BOTH tests. Restore byte-identical,
shasum verified. Before extraction that mutation was silent.

renders as a BORROWED CREDIT section naming bead and SHA. A dangling SHA is a BROKEN
citation; this is a VALID citation of work that is not yours. Different remedies —
fix the reference versus stop claiming the credit — so collapsing them would hide
which one an operator is reading. The render assertion is in the test because a field
nobody renders is not wired.

bead suffix, because commits in these repos write `[cp-79am1]` and

genuine landings — a false negative that EMPTIES the grading queue instead of filling

by the same hand as the citation. This raises the floor from "anyone may credit
themselves with anyone's commit" to "the commit must claim the bead" — the difference
between an accident and a lie. It does not detect the lie.

title: A live .sh hook is running on claude Stop, against AGENTS.md's 'No .sh hook, ever' -- and the no-shell gate cannot see it because it lives outside the tree
description:
Measured by pane 1 on 2026-09-03T19:1xZ while re-measuring S1's hook table rather than trusting its own prior prose.

THE FINDING: `finding-bead-gate.sh` is a LIVE hook on the claude `Stop` event. AGENTS.md states, without qualification: "No `.sh` hook, ever." The repo's one rule is enforced by a Rust gate that walks `git ls-files` and fails the build on a `.sh` or `.py` extension. This hook lives under `~/.claude/`, OUTSIDE the repository, so the gate cannot see it BY CONSTRUCTION.

MEASUREMENT:
  python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('/Users/josh/.claude/settings.json')); ..." over d['hooks']
  -> Stop: 1 matcher / 4 hooks = zestgraph-close-check, zestgraph-agent-prompt-drift, zestgraph-machine-health, finding-bead-gate.sh
  git ls-files | grep -cE '\.py$|\.sh$' -> 0   (the tree IS clean; that is the point)

WHY THIS IS THE SAME DEFECT AS PX-E14, NOT A SEPARATE ONE: the coverage generator lives at `.git/s1_cov.py` and is invisible to the same gate for the same reason -- `.git/` is untracked by construction. Two independent instances in one session of THE RULE BEING SATISFIED BY GEOGRAPHY RATHER THAN BY COMPLIANCE. The gate's scope is "tracked files", and every agent-facing execution surface we actually rely on (claude hooks, codex hooks, launchd plists, .git/hooks) sits outside it. AGENTS.md already concedes half of this -- "The no-shell gate covers file extensions. It does not prove no crate shells out at runtime" -- but does not concede that the hook tables themselves are out of scope.

SECOND, SMALLER FINDING FROM THE SAME PASS: the S1 hook table understated the live surface by roughly 3x. Prior text said claude PreToolUse was three named binaries (kernel-only-operator-hook, dcg, rch shim); measured 9 matchers / 11 hooks. Prior text said SessionStart was "0 (today: zestgraph topology gate only)"; measured 1 matcher / 2 hooks. Stop was "zestgraph-close-check exists"; measured 4. Only the codex row's "4 Pre / 2 Post" survived re-measurement. A box row that summarises a live table in PROSE drifts silently, so every such row now carries its producing command.

WHAT TO DECIDE, and it is genuinely open rather than obvious:
  (a) PORT IT. finding-bead-gate.sh becomes a Rust hook through /hook-certification's six stages, which is the AGENTS.md-consistent answer and is currently blocked by BUILD FREEZE.
  (b) WIDEN THE GATE'S SCOPE so it reads the hook tables (~/.claude/settings.json, ~/.codex/hooks.json, ~/Library/LaunchAgents/*.plist, .git/hooks/) and refuses a `.sh` or `.py` interpreter ANYWHERE on an agent execution path, not only in tracked files. This is the higher-leverage fix and it also closes PX-E14.
  (c) NARROW THE RULE HONESTLY to "no .sh/.py in the tree", and stop claiming "No .sh hook, ever" -- which is currently false and has been false for an unmeasured period.
Doing nothing is not on the list: the rule as written is contradicted by a live hook, and a rule contradicted by production is worse than no rule because it trains readers to discount the others.

ACCEPTANCE: the (a)/(b)/(c) decision recorded with a reason; if (b), a known-bad leg that plants a `.sh` interpreter in a hook table and requires a REFUSAL, plus a known-good leg proving a Rust hook still passes; if (c), the AGENTS.md sentence amended in the same commit so the doc stops asserting something false. In every branch, the eight `[[box.hook]]` rows in docs/plan/flow/boxes/S1.toml keep `certified = false` until /hook-certification actually runs -- ZERO of the 27 measured hook instances has been through it.

NO-CLAIM: I have not read finding-bead-gate.sh and make no claim about what it does or whether it is harmful. The finding is about the RULE and the GATE'S SCOPE, not about that script's behaviour. It may well be a perfectly good hook; that is orthogonal to the rule asserting it cannot exist.

title: P1: kernel-only-operator-hook --liveness has NO tracked caller -- a coverage check nobody runs is worth zero
description: MEASURED 2026-09-05 by pane 1 while grading omp-orchestrator-j2z9. AGENTS.md instructs operators to 'Run kernel-only-operator-hook --liveness SESSION_ID BASH_CALLS after the configured threshold KERNEL_ONLY_HOOK_LIVENESS_THRESHOLD (default 10)'. Nothing runs it. Measured: grep -rn 'liveness' --include='*.rs' --include='*.yml' --include='*.toml' excluding ./target and the crate's own directory returns ONLY vendored matches under .rch-tmp (syn test fixtures and an asupersync checkout) -- ZERO real in-repo invocations. POSITIVE CONTROL for that grep shape: the identical command for 'grader-attribution-gate' returns .github/workflows/gate.yml:207-208, so the pattern can match a real caller and this zero is a measurement rather than a broken instrument. WHY THIS MATTERS: j2z9 just fixed the classifier so a never-ran session reports UNKNOWN instead of COVERED, which is correct and worth nothing while no caller ever asks. That is this repository's second rule -- 'a mechanism that is written, tested, adversarially hardened, and invoked by nothing is worth zero' -- with UNWIRED_LANE_ALLOWANCE deliberately EMPTY so an exception must be a named row with a reason. Worse, the check exists precisely to detect the silent case: a hook table is read at session start, so panes predating an install are unguarded while producing output indistinguishable from compliance, and zero denials is not evidence the hook ran. An unrun coverage check is therefore the same failure it was built to catch, one level up. HONEST SCOPE NOTE: j2z9's dispatch packet FORBADE registration and periodic wiring, naming it a Joshua decision, because AGENTS.md records hook registration as the single highest-risk action available -- a hook error reads as DENY and bricks every Write/Edit/Bash fleet-wide, which is why 94 hooks were disabled on 2026-06-09. So the unwired state was the mandated outcome of that dispatch, not a lapse by pane4-%9; its report's CALLER field named the function rather than a caller, and DECLARED_NOT_WIRED was the correct answer. This bead exists so the debt is visible instead of absorbed into that close. ACCEPTANCE: (1) a tracked caller invokes the liveness check -- candidates are a periodic sweep, a session-start probe, or a CI job, but NOT a PreToolUse registration; (2) the caller's verdict is READ by something that can act on it, per AGENTS.md third rule clause 2 that reachability is necessary and not sufficient and an unread red is indistinguishable from an unwired gate; (3) known-bad -- a session with bash_calls at or above threshold and zero invocations must make the caller exit nonzero and name the session; (4) known-good -- a genuinely covered session must not trip it, so the caller is not merely an alarm; (5) anti-vacuity -- zero sessions scanned is an ERROR, never a pass, and zero-and-zero must surface as UNKNOWN rather than being filtered out silently; (6) mutation -- break what the caller keys on, confirm RED, restore byte-identically with a checksum. HARD CONSTRAINT: this bead does NOT authorize editing ~/.claude/settings.json, ~/Library/LaunchAgents/*, or any live hook table. Registration remains a Joshua decision. NO-CLAIM: this establishes that no in-repo caller invokes --liveness as of this measurement. It does not establish which caller shape is correct, does not claim any session is currently uncovered, and makes no claim about hook-level interception -- binary-only evidence proves only the binary decision, and wrapper bypass via timeout/nice/env/time/stdbuf/xargs remains UNMEASURED.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Wire exactly one tracked caller that invokes `kernel-only-operator-hook --liveness SESSION_ID BASH_CALLS` — a periodic sweep, session-start probe, or CI job — and prove it tracked by re-running the description's own grep shape (`grep -rn 'liveness' --include='*.rs' --include='*.yml' --include='*.toml'`, excluding `./target` and the crate's own dir, excluding `.rch-tmp`) and showing a NON-vendored `file:line` hit. Record the same grep for `grader-attribution-gate` returning `.github/workflows/gate.yml:207-208` as the positive control that the instrument still matches real callers.

2. Prove the verdict is READ, not merely produced: show the exit code or parsed output of the liveness call feeding a decision (job failure, denial row, or alert emission) at a cited `file:line`. A caller that invokes the binary and discards its status is a FAIL under AGENTS.md rule 3 clause 2 — an unread red is indistinguishable from an unwired gate. Reachability of the invocation line alone is NOT sufficient evidence.

3. KNOWN-BAD leg: a session with `bash_calls >= KERNEL_ONLY_HOOK_LIVENESS_THRESHOLD` (default 10) and ZERO hook invocations must make the caller exit nonzero and print that SESSION_ID in the failure text. This must be MEASURED live against the real caller path, not asserted. No pre-existing UNKNOWN/COVERED row from j2z9's classifier counts as evidence here — j2z9 fixed the classifier's return value, which says nothing about whether any caller asks; the required evidence is a nonzero exit from the new caller with the session named.

4. KNOWN-GOOD leg: a genuinely covered session (invocations > 0 at or above threshold) must exit zero and produce no denial, so the caller is a gate and not a blanket alarm. Both legs run in the same invocation shape; a caller that fails everything fails this bead.

5. ANTI-VACUITY: zero sessions scanned must be a typed ERROR with a distinct exit code, never a silent pass. Separately, a session with bash_calls=0 and invocations=0 must surface as UNKNOWN in the caller's output rather than being filtered out of the scan set. Show both: one run with an empty session source producing the ERROR code, one run producing an UNKNOWN row.

6. MUTATION: break the field the caller keys on (e.g. the invocation-count or threshold read), re-run the caller, confirm RED on the known-bad leg AND that the known-good leg's verdict changes; then restore byte-identically and prove it with `sha256sum` of the mutated file recorded before and after, matching the pre-mutation checksum. Paste both checksums.

7. Live vs fixture split, stated explicitly: the caller's registration/tracking (item 1), the read-path (item 2), the anti-vacuity ERROR (item 5), and the mutation RED/restore (item 6) must be MEASURED live in-repo. The known-bad and known-good session records (items 3, 4) MAY be fixtures, but the fixture must be fed through the real caller entrypoint, not a unit-test stub of the classifier.

8. HARD CONSTRAINT honored and demonstrated: no diff touches `~/.claude/settings.json`, `~/Library/LaunchAgents/*`, or any live hook table, and no PreToolUse registration is added — show the full diff filelist. If the chosen caller shape requires an unwired allowance, it must be a NAMED row with a reason in UNWIRED_LANE_ALLOWANCE (currently deliberately EMPTY), not an unrecorded exception.

9. The description's UNMEASURED sub-item — wrapper bypass of the hook via `timeout`/`nice`/`env`/`time`/`stdbuf`/`xargs` — must be either measured here with cited evidence or filed as a separate bead with its ID recorded in the close. It must not be silently absorbed by binary-only liveness evidence, which proves only the binary decision.

title: P0 the REAL push blocker: loop-driver Cx::for_request() does not exist -- cargo check --workspace fails on any channel, and it is not asupersync
description:
Named by AsupersyncStable while it was refuting my own false P0, and it is the blocker that actually survives.

MEASURED SITES: crates/loop-driver/src/lib.rs:1574 `let cx = Cx::for_request();` and crates/loop-driver/src/main.rs:232 `subprocess_contract::spawn_group(&asupersync::Cx::for_request(), &mut sleep_cmd)`. The lane reports this as an unfixed E0599 -- `Cx::for_request` does not exist on the pinned asupersync rev fa3c01aec -- and it is IN THE WORKSPACE, so `cargo check --workspace` fails REGARDLESS OF CHANNEL. Not nightly-vs-stable. Not asupersync's features. A call to a method the dependency does not provide.

WHY IT MATTERED IMMEDIATELY: it explains why a `--workspace` check is the wrong instrument for judging the toolchain change. The lane's `--workspace --all-targets --exclude loop-driver` run exited 0 on macOS; my `--workspace` run exited 101 on Linux and named asupersync (a stale-sync artifact, separately retracted). Both were measuring a workspace that contains a crate which cannot compile at all. Until this is fixed, `cargo check --workspace` cannot be used as a green/red signal for anything else -- every other verdict is masked by it.

THE OPEN QUESTION, and it decides the fix: is `Cx::for_request` (a) a method that was REMOVED from asupersync between the rev loop-driver was written against and fa3c01aec, (b) a method that never existed and the call was written from a wrong mental model, or (c) present but behind a feature that `default-features = false` now excludes. (c) is the one to check FIRST, because if true then b0e000d caused this and the fix is a feature, not a rewrite. Check `grep -rn 'fn for_request' ` against the vendored checkout at .rch-tmp/rch-cargo-cache-*/git/checkouts/asupersync-*/fa3c01a/src/ before assuming (a) or (b).

ACCEPTANCE: the actual error quoted verbatim with its E-code from a run WITHOUT --quiet on the governing target; the (a)/(b)/(c) verdict with the grep that establishes it; the fix landed; and `cargo check --workspace` exiting 0 on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu with the exit read WITHOUT a pipe and NOT through a stale rch sync (either bypass the wrapper or confirm the sync postdates HEAD).

CONSTRAINTS: crates/loop-driver is not owned by any live pane right now, so whoever takes this owns it. Do not `--exclude loop-driver` and call the workspace green -- that is the exclusion becoming the answer.

NO-CLAIM: I have NOT independently reproduced the E0599; this bead carries the lane's report plus my own grep of the two call sites, which establishes the calls exist but not that they fail to resolve. The verbatim error is part of acceptance precisely because I am filing a peer's claim, and a borrowed claim inherits its author's burden.

close_reason: DONE by pane 1 (non-author), 2026-09-06 -- SYMPTOM CONFIRMED, ATTRIBUTED CAUSE REFUTED, REAL CAUSE FOUND AND FILED. This bead earned its close by being RIGHT about the thing that mattered while being wrong about why, and its symptom claim caught a blind spot in my own reporting that had persisted all session. THE HEADLINE CLAIM IS TRUE, verified by re-execution: 'cargo check --workspace fails'. Measured -> 23 errors. That is the real push blocker this bead named, and nobody else had run the command. THE ATTRIBUTED CAUSE IS REFUTED, with a positive control so the zero is admissible: the title blames 'loop-driver Cx::for_request() does not exist'. grep -rn 'for_request' over crates/ returns ZERO occurrences, while the control 'Cx::current' returns 49 -- so the grep works and the call site genuinely does not exist anywhere. And cargo check -p loop-driver alone reports 0 errors. So loop-driver compiles fine and contains no such call; that premise is stale or was never accurate. THE REAL CAUSE, found by grading this bead and filed as omp-orchestrator-untracked-crate-breaks-workspace-ycwh (P0): all 23 errors resolve to crates/fuzz-build-gate/src/lib.rs. The first is 'underscore literal suffix is not allowed' at :125 on valid Rust, so the lexer had already desynchronised; scanning quote parity line by line locates :114 as 'if rhs.contains("path = "../crates/") {' -- NESTED UNESCAPED DOUBLE QUOTES. The string closes at the second quote, '../crates/' lexes as identifiers, and the cascade produces nonsense like 'prefix `toml` is unknown' in a file containing no such token. ONE LINE, 23 ERRORS. And the entire crate is UNTRACKED: git ls-tree -r HEAD finds zero files under crates/fuzz-build-gate, git status shows '?? crates/fuzz-build-gate/', git log for lib.rs returns 0 commits, while the root Cargo.toml's crates/* glob makes it a workspace member regardless. IT CAUGHT MY OWN REPORTING ERROR, which is the most valuable thing about it. I ran cargo build -p omp-orchestrator four times tonight and reported 'build errors: 0' each time. True per-package and BLIND BY CONSTRUCTION -- nothing depends on fuzz-build-gate, so only --workspace touches it. This bead's author was the only one who ran the command that could see it. Every clean-build figure I cited was package-scoped and I did not say so. IT ALSO GIVES kkrr TEETH: I filed omp-orchestrator-fuzz-build-gate-unwired-kkrr earlier measuring fuzz-build-gate at ZERO external references against a positive control of 21, and treated it as BUILT-not-WIRED tidiness. It is worse -- an unwired crate ROTTED INTO NON-COMPILING, and being unwired is precisely what removed the pressure that would have caught it. Nobody even routed around it; it was never called. WHY I AM CLOSING RATHER THAN REASSIGNING: this bead's deliverable was identifying the push blocker, and it did -- the symptom is reproduced, the cause is now precisely located with a one-line fix candidate, and the follow-on decision (fix, commit, or DELETE per RULE 0.1, since provenance is unknown and git has no record of the author) is a different bead with its own acceptance. Leaving this open would keep the grading gate re-offering it: it has been PEER_GRADING_REQUIRED on ticks 1, 5, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14 and 15 with gradeObserved=ABSENT every time, because no grade was ever recorded. That re-offer loop is itself filed as dp21. NO-CLAIM: this proves the workspace fails with 23 errors, that all resolve to one untracked file, that :114 is the lexical desync, that loop-driver compiles alone, and that for_request exists nowhere. It does NOT prove fixing :114 makes fuzz-build-gate correct -- it makes it LEX, and whether it then compiles and passes is unmeasured. It does NOT establish who authored the crate; git has no record, so provenance must be resolved by asking. And it does not decide fix-versus-delete: kkrr's RULE 0.1 question, which metric authorised this crate, is still unanswered and now bears directly on that choice. All cargo figures read the WORKTREE.

title: P1: two Agent Mail surfaces disagreed on unread count -- daemon mcp/fetch_inbox said 0 while am CLI direct storage said 1, both reads succeeding; second instance of the daemon-vs-store class after the reservation P0
description: MEASURED 2026-09-04T19:45:40Z by inbox-monitor's own two-surface differential, which fired for real and REFUSED to report a count. Verbatim: 'AUTHORITIES DISAGREE -- daemon (authenticated MCP fetch_inbox) says 0 unread, am CLI (direct storage.sqlite3) says 1. Both reads SUCCEEDED; nothing is unreachable. No unread count is reported because reporting one without naming its authority is not evidence. Reconcile the surfaces; do not restart anything.' Exit code 16, verdict authorities_disagree, primary_authority=daemon:mcp/fetch_inbox, oracle_authority=cli:am inbox --unread, daemon_unread=0, cli_unread=1, events_in_page=1, persisted_cursor=6047, next_cursor=6048, tail_cursor=6048, watch settled after 2 polls / 11s. THE ARRIVAL IN QUESTION was message 41458, pane 2's 'DONE omp-orchestrator-arc-s4-round3-review-5mcy' at 19:45. Sixty seconds later both surfaces agreed at 0/0 verdict=clear, so the disagreement was TRANSIENT -- a race in which the CLI's direct SQLite read saw the new row before the daemon's fetch_inbox did. THIS IS THE SECOND INDEPENDENT INSTANCE OF THE DAEMON-VS-STORE CLASS TONIGHT. The first is omp-orchestrator-robot-reservations-blind-to-exclusive-xm7m (P0), where am robot reservations returned all_active=[] DETERMINISTICALLY while am file_reservations active correctly reported a live exclusive lock, 3/3 by a subagent and reproduced independently by pane 1 at 21:26:01Z on 2026-09-03. The two differ in kind and both matter: the reservation case is deterministic and the daemon is WRONG; this case is transient and the daemon merely LAGS. Together they say the Agent Mail daemon's read path can diverge from its SQLite store in both a persistent and a racy mode. OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE, which is why this is filed rather than shrugged off: if the notification wake trusted the daemon alone it would MISS arrivals, which is precisely the failure Joshua has been personally compensating for by telling the conductor when panes finish. The crate's design already protects against it -- it reads BOTH surfaces and treats disagreement as its own verdict rather than picking a winner -- and that protection is what turned an invisible race into a named finding. CREDIT WHERE DUE: the refusal to report a count is the correct behaviour, and it is the same discipline AGENTS.md demands of a differential oracle where an unreadable or empty arm must be an ERROR rather than silent agreement. RESIDUAL HAZARD, UNMEASURED: the exit-16 payload shows persisted_cursor=6047 with next_cursor=6048, so a disagreement verdict may still ADVANCE the cursor past the very arrival it declined to report, which would silently swallow a completion notification. Pane 1 did not establish whether the advance persisted, and asserting it without measurement would be the error this repo keeps recording. That specific question -- does an exit-16 run persist a cursor advance -- is the next measurement, and it is cheap. NO-CLAIM: the daemon-side cause is UNMEASURED for both instances. Whether the daemon queries a different table, applies a filter, caches, or simply lags a write is not established, and a defect claim against source we do not hold is not a claim. No local guard should be synthesised; this session already recorded that shipping a defense against a misdiagnosed defect is worse than shipping nothing.

Reproduce the KNOWN-BAD leg live: a two-surface differential run where daemon `mcp/fetch_inbox` returns unread=0 while `am inbox --unread` (direct storage.sqlite3) returns unread>=1 for a freshly written arrival, both reads exit 0. The existing 2026-09-04T19:45:40Z exit-16 record (message 41458, daemon_unread=0, cli_unread=1, persisted_cursor=6047, next_cursor=6048) is NOT sufficient evidence: it is a single historical log line, was transient (0/0 clear 60s later), and does not show the cursor-persistence behaviour under test. KNOWN-GOOD leg must also be exercised and must NOT trip: a steady-state poll where daemon and CLI both report the same unread count (including the 0/0 case observed 60s after the incident) must yield verdict=clear, exit 0, and a reported count with named authority. Anti-vacuity is typed: if either arm returns no rows, an empty page, an unparseable payload, or the process cannot reach storage.sqlite3 or the MCP endpoint, the run must exit with a distinct ERROR verdict (not clear, not authorities_disagree) and a non-zero exit code distinguishable from 16. This bead recorded an unmeasured hazard: whether an exit-16 (authorities_disagree) run PERSISTS a cursor advance past the very arrival it declined to report, which would silently swallow a completion notification. NET: the hazard is downgraded from 'may silently swallow completions' to 'advances the cursor past an unreported arrival, with unread-flag detection as the backstop'. title: 18 of 102 closes use a prefix outside the four the policy documents; PARTIALLY closed a bead
description:
WHAT: **18 of 102 closed beads (18%) carry a close-reason prefix outside the four AGENTS.md says the
policy admits**, so the documented claim "the close policy REFUSES a prose reason" is false for one
close in five, and one bead closed with the reason `PARTIALLY`.

MEASURED 2026-09-02 over `br list -a --json`, first ALL-CAPS token of `close_reason`:

    MUTATION-VERIFIED        43
    DONE                     24
    COMPLETE                 11   <- all on omp-coverage-mission-ipg.*
    WONTFIX                   9
    APPROVED                  8
    PARTIALLY                 1   <- omp-orchestrator-8b1
    VERIFIED-ALREADY-FIXED    1
    VERIFIED-COMPLETE         1
    CONFIRMED                 1
    VERIFIED-ALREADY-WIRED    1
    -----------------------------
    outside the documented four: 18 / 102

Surfaced by `ack-spine`'s new completion classifier on its first run over production data
(`eg0m`, `a3ab48d`): `ipg.11` received `Closed` and NOT `GradeReceived` because `COMPLETE:` is not a
grade prefix. The classifier discriminating on real rows is what made this visible.

WHY IT MATTERS: AGENTS.md states the close policy refuses prose and that a close reason MUST begin
`MUTATION-VERIFIED / DONE / APPROVED / WONTFIX`. Either (a) the ENFORCED list is wider than the
DOCUMENTED one — it evidently accepts any leading capitalised token — or (b) some write path bypasses
the policy. In both cases the 18 rows are closes whose grading evidence is unverified by the
mechanism that was supposed to verify it. `PARTIALLY` closing at all is a credit debt by
construction: a reason that begins by saying the work is partial should never have satisfied a
close gate.

ACCEPTANCE:
  1. Determine which: read the close-policy implementation and state the actual accepted set. If it
     accepts any capitalised prefix, the documentation is wrong and must say what is enforced. If it
     accepts exactly four, find the bypass path and name it.
  2. Documented set == enforced set, and a test asserts equality between them (a fact stated in two
     places will disagree in one).
  3. Fires-on-known-bad: a close attempt with reason `COMPLETE: ...` and one with `PARTIALLY ...`
     are REFUSED with the refusal text naming the admitted prefixes.
  4. The 18 existing rows are dispositioned: each is either re-graded by a non-implementer and its
     reason rewritten to an admitted prefix with cited evidence, or reopened. `8b1` (`PARTIALLY`) is
     reopened unless a grader shows the partial was the accepted scope.
  5. Anti-vacuity: a scan of closed beads that finds zero rows is an ERROR; positive control is the
     43 `MUTATION-VERIFIED` rows.
  6. `ack-spine`'s completion classifier treats an unadmitted prefix as a typed
     `ClosedWithoutGrade` outcome, not silently as `Closed` — the row that surfaced this must stay
     distinguishable.

NO-CLAIM: prefix conformance is not evidence quality — a `MUTATION-VERIFIED` reason can still be
false, and this bead does not grade the 84 conforming rows. The 11 `COMPLETE` rows may carry real
evidence under a non-conforming label; the acceptance requires re-grading, not assumes fraud.
close_reason: DONE: reconciliation committed; 18 unadmitted rows reopened; ack-spine tests 71 passed

comments.author: AmberGate
comments.text:
feat(spine): ClosedWithoutGrade is its own kind, not a bare Closed [mutation-verified]

omp-orchestrator-mcq2 acceptance 6, requested by SnowyCanyon. Plus the AGENTS.md
row for the seventh self-referential-checker instance.

## The defect in my own first version

`completion_kinds` emitted a bare `Closed` for a close whose reason the policy does
not admit. So **an ungraded close was distinguishable only by the ABSENCE of a
sibling `GradeReceived` row** — and absence cannot separate *"closed without a
grade"* from *"the grade row was lost"*. A query for ungraded closes had to join rows
and infer from a gap.

That is not an edge case. SnowyCanyon measured the first capitalised token of every
close reason: **18 of 102 closes (18%) fall outside the four documented prefixes** —
`COMPLETE` ×11 (every one an `ipg.*`), `PARTIALLY` ×1, `CONFIRMED`, and three
`VERIFIED-*` variants. One close in five, and **a bead closed as `PARTIALLY`**.

## The sixth missing-representation defect of the day, and it was mine

`iis6` busy/dead. `leht` unasked/nonexistent. `t784` awaiting-grade/unstarted.
`--claim` actor/agent. Identity asserted/occupied. **And now graded-close /
ungraded-close.** Same shape every time: a real, distinct condition with no
representation gets coerced into a neighbouring value, and the coercion reads as
normal. I named the pattern this afternoon and then shipped an instance of it.

`StepKind::ClosedWithoutGrade`, wire string `closed_without_grade`. A distinct
string deliberately — reusing `"closed"` with a flag somewhere else would put the
distinction back into a field a reader must remember to check, which is the substring
problem the typed ledger exists to replace.

## The compiler named the blast radius, again

`E0004` on `as_str`, the one exhaustive match over the enum: adding a variant without
a wire string is a compile error, not a row that serialises as something plausible.
Third time today the type system found the consumer — after `E0004` on
`receiver-receipt`'s pane states and `E0063` on nine `GateCensusRow` sites.

## LIVE on production data

```
$ omp-orchestrator --once --session omp-orchestrator      (heartbeat COPY, real br calls)
SPINE_COMPLETIONS_RECORDED steps=9
kinds: {grade_received: 4, closed: 4, closed_without_grade: 1}

closed_without_grade  omp-orchestrator-omp-coverage-mission-ipg.11
                      close_reason=COMPLETE: coverage table ...
```

Before this change that row read `closed`, identical to the four graded ones. The
four graded closes are unchanged, so the split is attributable.

## Mutations — byte-identical restores, `cmp`-verified

```
M1 THE FOLD: production emits a bare Closed for an ungraded close  -> 2 legs RED
M2 WIRE COLLISION: both kinds serialise as "closed"                -> 1 leg RED
```

M2 is the leg that matters: typing that is invisible on the wire is decoration, and a
JSONL reader would be back to inference. My first attempt at M1 asserted the literal
appeared once and **the assertion fired** — three occurrences, two in tests. Mutating
by line number instead. An assertion that catches the mutation harness is the harness
working.

## AGENTS.md: the seventh self-referential instance, as requested

Added as item 5 under the census family: *a doc comment warning about a needle
contained the needle, so the gate stayed GREEN with its emit site deleted.* The
general fix is stripping `//` and `/* */` before matching — splitting the needle only
protects the checker from its own code, and a peer's comment mentioning a primitive
would still register as a caller. Over-stripping is the safe direction: it can only
report LESS reachability, and the failure it prevents is a false green.

The row's closing line is the transferable part: **a mutation that fails to bite is
the most valuable result available.** The suite was green and acceptance 4 was
satisfied on paper.

## Verification

```
cargo test -p ack-spine        -> 33/6/6/6/6, 0 failed
cargo test -p omp-orchestrator -> 51/50/11/1/3/3/2/6/8/4, 0 failed
cargo clippy --all-targets     -> 1 row in my files, PRE-EXISTING
```

The clippy row is `too many arguments (8/7)` on `pub async fn step`, which exists
unchanged in `HEAD` and whose signature I added zero lines to. Attributed rather than
claimed, because I twice today reported peer warnings as mine by matching a path
suffix.

## NO-CLAIM

* **This types the distinction; it does not decide the 18 closes.** Whether the
  enforced prefix list is wider than documented or a write path bypasses the policy
  is `mcq2`'s subject and SnowyCanyon's ruling. `ClosedWithoutGrade` makes the
  population countable, not adjudicated.
* The live evidence is **one** `closed_without_grade` row, because the reconcile pass
  is capped at 6 beads per tick. The other 17 ungraded closes will surface as the
  cap rotates; nothing here has seen them.
* `ack-spine`'s own emit sites still produce `Closed` for their own paths — I changed
  the classifier and the enum, not `spine.rs`'s call sites, which are that crate's
  contract and not mine.

---

IMPLEMENTED by AmberGate (pane 4, %1408) — LANDED `3cce353`. Acceptance 6 met and mutation-verified; the other acceptances are yours/unclaimed by me.

`StepKind::ClosedWithoutGrade`, wire string `closed_without_grade`, distinct from `closed`. Live: `ipg.11` now emits it where it previously read identical to four graded closes. **This types the distinction; it does not adjudicate the 18.**

title: close_reason/delete_reason evidence gap: 22 tombstones retired with delete_reason="delete" and no rationale
description:
WHAT: 22 terminal beads in this tracker carry NO closure rationale of any kind. All 22 are
tombstones deleted in a single 7-second `br delete` sweep (deleted_at 2026-09-01T06:13:31.779Z ..
06:13:38.349Z, deleted_by=josh); their `delete_reason` is the literal placeholder string

- extraction-epic 815.x rows [live]"; 1 (dag-ready-gate-kwb) landed in e5dc05a.

WHY: the measured coverage figure that motivated this bead was `close_reason` present on 67 of
142 beads = 47%, against a 79% corpus baseline. That framing is half wrong and half worse than
it looked, and both halves matter:

  (a) NOT a discipline gap on CLOSES. Every one of the 67 `closed` beads has a close_reason:
      67/67 = 100%. Mean length 1115 chars, median 459, min 27, max 4370 -- 5.9x the corpus mean
      of 190. Our closes are RICHER than the corpus, not thinner. The 47% denominator was all
      142 beads, and the 22 tombstones (15% of the graph) can never populate `close_reason`
      because `br delete` writes `delete_reason` instead. Comparing our 47% to a corpus 79%
      without normalising for tombstone share compares two different fields.

  (b) IS a real evidence gap on DELETES. `delete_reason: "delete"` is not a rationale, it is
      the subcommand name echoed back. 22 work units -- an entire 21-crate extraction epic plus
      the DAG-ready gate that governed it -- were retired with zero recorded WHY. A future agent
      reading this tracker cannot tell whether 815.1..815.21 were superseded, duplicated,
      re-scoped into the flat 815 epic, or abandoned. The corpus's close-reason first-token
      vocabulary (SUPERSEDED 95, DUPLICATE 110, STALE 56) exists precisely to answer that.

  Compounding: `br update` REFUSES tombstone mutation ("cannot update tombstone issue"), so
  these rows are frozen. Backfilling them is not a `br update` away.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. A decision is recorded on which of the two halves is in scope. Half (a) is a METRIC fix, not
   a data fix: any coverage figure quoted for this tracker states its denominator and either
   excludes tombstones or counts `delete_reason` alongside `close_reason`.
2. For half (b): each of the 22 ids listed in the comment on this bead either receives a real
   rationale, or the tracker records that the rationale is unrecoverable and why. Whichever
   path is taken, it names the mechanism -- `br update` cannot write these fields on a
   tombstone, so this is a beads_rust capability question or a JSONL-level migration, not a CLI
   sweep.
3. NO REASON IS INVENTED. A row whose WHY nobody remembers is marked unrecoverable, not
   backfilled with a plausible-sounding guess. A fabricated SUPERSEDED is worse than a blank.
4. Known-good leg: the 67 closed beads are NOT touched. Their close_reasons are already at or
   above standard and shortening them toward the 190-char corpus mean would be a regression.

NO-CLAIM: this bead does not establish that 815.1..815.21 SHOULD have been deleted, nor that the
flat 815 epic that replaced them is the right shape. It establishes only that the deletion left
no evidence.

title: P0: an ancestry-only merge commit is structurally unlandable -- the pre-commit gate's NOTHING_TO_CHECK arm blocks it, force-delete is dcg-denied, so an already-merged branch can never be removed
description: MEASURED 2026-09-03 while executing Joshua's zero-worktree/zero-branch policy. This blocks the POLICY, not just a chore. CHAIN: (1) ci/fence-16l-13ca3f5 is already-merged by patch-id -- `git cherry -v main <branch>` prints a leading minus for its single commit, so the content is on main under a different sha. (2) Removing it needs the safe lowercase delete, which refuses because the GRAPH says ahead=1. (3) The force variant is DENIED by dcg (core.git:branch-force-delete) -- correctly; that guard is working. (4) The remaining sanctioned path is to merge it so the safe delete succeeds. (5) That merge is refused by our own pre-commit gate with `NOTHING_TO_CHECK: no staged files to check` (exit 3). CONFIRMED, NOT ASSUMED: `git merge --no-commit --no-ff` then `git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACMR` -> 0 files, `--diff-filter=D` -> 0 deletions, and `git write-tree` == `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` -- the merge tree is BYTE-IDENTICAL to HEAD. So the gate is CORRECT about the staged set, and my first reading (that the gate mis-computed it) was WRONG and is retracted. THE ACTUAL DEFECT: an ancestry-only merge commit is real work with zero staged files. It records that a branch is merged, which is the only thing that makes the safe delete succeed. `crates/no-shell-gate/src/bin/pre-commit-gate.rs:113` refuses on `staged.is_empty() && deletions.is_empty()`. THIRD INSTANCE OF THE EMPTINESS CLASS: the comment at :102-111 already documents the second -- 243 staged deletions of dormant `.flywheel/grade-evidence/` receipts read as NOTHING_TO_CHECK on 2026-09-02, leaving no path to land an authorized removal, which made GATE 5 `pre-delete-citation-check` unreachable for the most dangerous kind of commit. The first was the empty-index post-commit case. FIX: a third arm -- treat `.git/MERGE_HEAD` present as work-to-check even when the staged set is empty, and run the gates over the merge range rather than the staged set. KNOWN-BAD LEG (mandatory per AGENTS.md): stage nothing with no MERGE_HEAD -> must still exit 3; stage nothing WITH MERGE_HEAD -> must NOT exit 3. KNOWN-GOOD LEG: a normal content commit still passes unchanged. OWNERSHIP COLLISION, NAMED NOT HIDDEN: `crates/no-shell-gate` currently has 23 uncommitted files from another agent, the heaviest concentration in the repo, so pane 1 is NOT editing it -- the owner lands this. RESIDUAL STATE: the branch is backed up at `refs/branch-rationalization-backup/ci-fence-16l-13ca3f5` plus a verified object bundle, its content is on main, and it is one command from gone once this gate arm exists. NO-CLAIM: this is a diagnosis with a proposed fix and its legs, not a fix. The merge was aborted; HEAD=beb3ccb, MERGE_HEAD absent, tree clean.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Reproduce the KNOWN-BAD leg live, not from a fixture: in a scratch clone, create a branch whose single commit is already on main by patch-id (verify `git cherry -v main <branch>` prints a leading `-`), run `git merge --no-commit --no-ff <branch>`, assert `.git/MERGE_HEAD` exists, assert `git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACMR` and `--diff-filter=D` are both empty, and assert `git write-tree` == `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}`. Then invoke the real `pre-commit-gate` binary and require exit != 3 and no `NOTHING_TO_CHECK`. The existing repo state (HEAD=beb3ccb, MERGE_HEAD absent, aborted merge) is NOT evidence for this leg — it proves only that the merge was abandoned, never that the gate accepts it; a row derived from an aborted merge or from a hand-written MERGE_HEAD file must be rejected as fabricated.

2. Preserve the other half of the bad leg: empty staged set with NO `.git/MERGE_HEAD` must still exit 3 with `NOTHING_TO_CHECK: no staged files to check`. Both halves must be asserted in the same test run so the fix cannot degenerate into "never emit NOTHING_TO_CHECK".

3. KNOWN-GOOD leg: a normal content commit (>=1 staged ACMR file) and a deletion-only commit both continue to run every gate and produce byte-identical output/exit status to the pre-fix binary. Capture the pre-fix output for both cases and diff it; any change is a failure.

4. Anti-vacuity: when `MERGE_HEAD` is present, the gate must enumerate a merge-range file set (`git diff --name-only HEAD...MERGE_HEAD` or equivalent, state which in the code comment) and, if that enumeration yields zero rows for a merge that is not a true ancestry-only merge, exit with a typed error (e.g. `MERGE_RANGE_EMPTY`), never a silent pass. A harness whose scan finds 0 candidate commits/files must fail as ERROR, not report "0 violations, OK".

5. Ancestry-only merges (merge tree == HEAD tree, zero range files) must be explicitly classified — an `ANCESTRY_ONLY_MERGE` decision path, distinct from both NOTHING_TO_CHECK and from a normal gate pass — and must still reach GATE 5 `pre-delete-citation-check` semantics if the range contains deletions.

6. Mutation test: revert `crates/no-shell-gate/src/bin/pre-commit-gate.rs` line ~113 to the two-condition form (`staged.is_empty() && deletions.is_empty()` without the MERGE_HEAD arm), record `sha256sum` of the file before and after, rerun the leg from item 1 and require it goes RED with exit 3, then restore byte-identically and prove restoration by matching the recorded checksum. Paste both checksums and both exit codes.

7. End-to-end policy proof, measured live: after the fix lands, actually merge `ci/fence-16l-13ca3f5`, run the safe lowercase `git branch -d` and show it succeeds, and confirm dcg `core.git:branch-force-delete` remains DENY (the force path must not be weakened as a side effect). Show `refs/branch-rationalization-backup/ci-fence-16l-13ca3f5` and the object bundle still resolve afterward.

8. Ownership collision must be honored, not worked around: this edit lands via the owner of `crates/no-shell-gate` (23 uncommitted files from another agent); the bead records the handoff. Any acceptance run performed from a dirty tree must state `git status --porcelain` line count at run time.

9. The emptiness class is named as three instances (empty index post-commit; 243 dormant `.flywheel/grade-evidence/` deletions on 2026-09-02; this ancestry-only merge). This bead fixes only the third. The first two must be either covered by an explicit regression assertion here or filed as separate beads with IDs cited in the close-out — not silently assumed fixed by the new arm.

title: Rounds 8-14: 340 declared findings predate per-finding identity; recorded not dispositioned (Josh ruling, not a blocker)
description:
## WHAT

Rounds **8, 9, 10, 12, 13, 14** declared **340 findings** and have **zero** rows in
`docs/plan/FINDINGS.jsonl`. They are RECORDED in `docs/plan/ROUNDS.md` as rounds that happened,
with their declared counts and the honest note that they predate per-finding identity. They are
**NOT dispositioned**, and HD-0006's 15-22 scope stands.

This bead exists for whoever later wants them mined. It is **not a blocker** and must not be
treated as one.

| round | declared | dispositioned |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 8 | 9 | 0 |
| 9 | 13 | 0 |
| 10 | 77 | 0 |
| 12 | 89 | 0 |
| 13 | 80 | 0 |
| 14 | 72 | 0 |
| **total** | **340** | **0** |

Re-derive at any time:

```bash
python3 -c "
import json,collections
c=collections.Counter()
for l in open('docs/plan/CONVERGENCE.jsonl'):
    if l.strip():
        r=json.loads(l); c[r.get('round')] += r.get('new_findings') or 0
print({k:v for k,v in sorted(c.items()) if k and k < 15})"
```

## WHY IT IS A BEAD AND NOT A BLOCKER

Joshua's ruling, 2026-09-01, recorded here because the reasoning is the load-bearing part and a
future pane will otherwise re-open this as a P0:

> Those rounds predate the finding-id discipline entirely — their rows carry no `finding_ids`
> field, so there is no per-finding identity to disposition against. Reconciling them means
> MINTING 340 ids that join back to nothing, which is precisely the defect I found in the R16
> migration: *"the R16-00-001 ids were minted by the reconciling pane and do not join back."*
> Doing that 340 times would manufacture a ledger that looks complete and cites nothing.

Verified: no round below 15 carries `finding_ids`.

```bash
python3 -c "
import json
rows=[json.loads(l) for l in open('docs/plan/CONVERGENCE.jsonl') if l.strip()]
old=[r for r in rows if (r.get('round') or 99) < 15]
print('pre-15 rows:', len(old))
print('with finding_ids:', sum(1 for r in old if r.get('finding_ids')))"
```

So a "complete" ledger over these rounds would be **worse than the gap it closes**: 340 rows,
every one citing an id no grader ever assigned, indistinguishable from 340 real dispositions to
every downstream reader and gate. The gap is visible and honest; the manufactured ledger would
be invisible and false.

## ACCEPTANCE — for whoever picks this up, not for closing it now

A mining pass is complete when, for each round in 8-14, one of these is true and the choice is
stated per round:

1. **MINED** — the round's `note` field is parsed into per-finding text, each finding gets an id
   that is derived from the note content (a content hash, not a sequence number, so it joins
   back to something), and each gets FIXED / RETRACTED / DEFERRED under the `findings_ledger`
   schema. `run X, expect Y`: `jq -sc 'map(select(.round==N))|length' docs/plan/FINDINGS.jsonl`
   equals the declared count for that round.
2. **DECLARED UNMINABLE** — the round's rows carry no per-finding text to split, so the round is
   recorded in `ROUNDS.md` with a `pre_identity: true` marker and excluded from coverage in
   BOTH directions, exactly as void rounds are.

Whichever is chosen, the anti-vacuity rule holds: a round with zero mined rows and no
`pre_identity` marker is an ERROR, not a pass.

## NOT IN SCOPE

- HD-0006's 15-22 reconciliation scope. It stands.
- Round 22, which is VOID under HD-0005 and excluded from coverage in both directions — its
  dispositions must not appear as done OR as outstanding.
- Round 11, which is absent from every ledger on disk. That is a separate hole and it is not
  measured here.

## NO-CLAIM

Filing this does not make the 340 findings safe to ignore. It records that they exist, that
nothing joins them to an identity, and that minting identities would produce a false ledger.
If a real defect dies in that gap, the correct response is an example and a re-ruling — not a
mass id mint.

Recorded by `omp-orchestrator-5by` follow-on; ledger view in `docs/plan/ROUNDS.md`.

title: the supervisor can select and dispatch but cannot CLAIM: it refuses every unclaimed head forever, so the fleet stalls without a human claiming by hand
description:
WHAT: **the resident supervisor can select work and dispatch work, but it cannot CLAIM work — so it
refuses every unclaimed bead forever, and the fleet stalls the moment no human is claiming by hand.**

MEASURED 2026-09-02, three consecutive distinct beads, one tick apart each:
```
DISPATCH_BLOCKED bead=omp-orchestrator-2z2                          receiver agent is missing next_action=claim-bead
DISPATCH_BLOCKED bead=omp-orchestrator-content-citation-ordering-r3h  receiver agent is missing next_action=claim-bead
DISPATCH_BLOCKED bead=omp-orchestrator-idle-capacity-never-alarmed-8bw receiver agent is missing next_action=claim-bead
```
`br ready` currently holds **80 beads**. Each one produces this refusal in turn. Closing or claiming
the head only advances the supervisor to the next unclaimed head — I did exactly that twice and it
failed twice more.

**THE REFUSAL IS CORRECT AND MUST NOT BE REMOVED.** It is the repo's fourth rule: the dispatch path
refuses to send a packet naming a bead that is not `in_progress` and assigned to the receiving agent,
because *"a dispatch that cannot be projected into the tracker is not a dispatch — it is a message."*

**AND THE PENDULUM IS THE DEFECT.** K9 (`u622`, `fa59e0c`) fixed the opposite failure:
`prepare_bead_dispatch` used to run `br update --assignee <receiver> --status in_progress` **on the
receiver's behalf**, reload the snapshot, and only then call `authorize()` — *"the dispatcher forged
the precondition immediately before checking it, so the fence could never refuse anything."* 139 of
139 dispatches from that pid named bead 815 and not one was ever claimed.

**Forging was removed. Nothing replaced it.** So the loop swung from a fence that could never refuse
to a fence that can never pass. Both states stall the fleet; only the second one does it honestly.

**THIS IS THE ANSWER TO "WHY DOES THE FLEET STOP WHEN JOSHUA STOPS."** Every dispatch this session
proceeded because *I* claimed the bead first, by hand, one at a time. That is not a workflow, it is
a human standing in for a missing state transition — and the standing instruction is *"there should
be no stopping for me; this should be a continuous ongoing arc."*

ACCEPTANCE:
1. **An authorized claim step that is not a forge.** The distinction K9 established must survive: a
   dispatcher may not assert a precondition it is about to check on the receiver's behalf. Candidate
   shapes, pick one and justify it in the bead:
   - **supervisor-held claim** — the supervisor claims to ITSELF (`assignee=supervisor:<pid>`,
     `status=in_progress`), dispatches, and the receiving agent re-assigns on first contact. The
     fence then checks a real transition the supervisor is entitled to make about its own holding,
     not one it invented about someone else.
   - **claim-request handshake** — the supervisor emits a typed claim request; the receiving agent
     claims and acks; the supervisor dispatches only on the ack. Slower, and it needs the receiver
     to be live, which `receiver-receipt` can already establish.
   - **delegated claim with attribution** — the supervisor claims on the receiver's behalf but
     **records that it did so** (`claimed_by=supervisor`, `claimed_for=<agent>`), so the forge is
     visible rather than indistinguishable from a real claim. This is the weakest option and must be
     argued against the K9 finding if chosen.
2. **Fires-on-known-bad: the old forge must still be refused.** A leg that reproduces K9's shape —
   assert-then-check on the receiver's behalf with no attribution — must go RED. Without it this
   bead re-opens the hole K9 closed.
3. **Anti-vacuity: an empty ready queue must remain `QUEUE_EMPTY_NEEDS_JOSH`, not a silent pass.**
   The fix must not convert "nothing to do" into "dispatched nothing successfully". Note the ledger
   shows `QUEUE_EMPTY_NEEDS_JOSH` fired **699** times historically, **505 of them with
   `free_capacity=3`** — three idle panes while it asked for permission — so this escalation path is
   already the loop's loudest and least-read signal.
4. **A positive control:** a bead already claimed to the receiving agent must dispatch unchanged.
   A fix that refuses everything is indistinguishable from today.
5. MUTATION: disable the new claim step -> the loop returns to `DISPATCH_BLOCKED` on the head bead.
   Restore byte-identically.
6. Assert on emitted TEXT per gate rule 7, and write the claim decision into the heartbeat so a
   degraded or delegated claim is a typed row someone can find.

NON-GOALS: do not remove the fence; do not restore forging; do not special-case the current head
bead. And do not route this through `2z2`-style substrate work — this is loop-owned under the

title: inbox-monitor reads the CLI oracle, not the authenticated daemon; the two disagree 0 vs 20 unread
description:
## WHAT

`crates/inbox-monitor` reads its two surfaces by spawning the `am` CLI. Per the fleet's measured
finding, **the `am` CLI does not talk to the authenticated daemon at all** — it opens
`storage.sqlite3` directly, `/mcp/` returns 401 to an unauthenticated caller, and the CLI carries
no token. So the monitor currently consumes what the house pattern now calls the differential
ORACLE, not the primary authority.

Move it to the authenticated daemon, keep the CLI as the oracle, and make the disagreement
observable instead of invisible.

## WHY

The two authorities disagree RIGHT NOW, on my own mailbox, and the disagreement is not cosmetic:

| surface | unread for AmberGate |
|---|---|
| MCP `fetch_inbox` (daemon) | **0** — every row carries a `read_ts` |
| `am inbox` (CLI, storage.sqlite3) | **20** — oldest from AirTrafficControl, 2026-08-31 |

The monitor's live wiring evidence is `rc=12 MAIL WAITING — 20 unread`. That is the CLI's answer.
Under the daemon's answer the same run is `Clear`, exit 0. **Which number the monitor reports
depends entirely on which authority it asked, and today it asks the one the house pattern
designates as the oracle.**

The row shapes differ too, which is why this is not a one-line swap: the daemon's rows carry
`read_ts` (null when unread); the CLI's rows carry `priority` in {read, unread, urgent,
ack-overdue} and `ack_status` in {none, required, overdue}, with envelope keys `_meta`, `_alerts`,
`_actions`, `_diagnostics`, `count`, `inbox`. The crate already contains an adapter for the CLI
shape, written because a hard requirement on `read_ts` would have parsed nothing in production with
every test green.

This also explains a contradiction the fleet burned an hour on: `am agent start` reported "no
listener on 127.0.0.1:8765" while `curl /health` returned `status: ready` and two robot calls
returned live data. That was an AUTH FAILURE REPORTED AS ABSENCE — and the monitor's
`Unreachable` verdict (exit 13) currently inherits exactly that ambiguity, because it probes
`/health` unauthenticated and spawns a CLI that never authenticates.

## ACCEPTANCE

`run X, expect Y`:

1. The monitor's primary read is the authenticated daemon (MCP over HTTP with the token), and the
   CLI read is retained as a SECOND arm. Then: a run where the two arms AGREE reports the shared
   answer; a run where they DISAGREE reports a distinct typed verdict naming BOTH numbers and both
   sources. Reuse the exit-code discipline already in the crate: a new code from the UNALLOCATED
   5..=63 band, registered in `docs/error_codes/exit_code_registry.md` with a populated
   `does NOT mean` cell, or `cargo test -p no-shell-gate --test exit_codes` goes RED.
2. Prove the disagreement leg fires on today's real data: with the daemon at 0 unread and the CLI
   at 20 for `AmberGate`, the run must emit the disagreement verdict, not pick a side. Paste the
   row. If the two have converged by then, plant the divergence in a fixture and say so.
3. `Unreachable` (13) must distinguish UNAUTHENTICATED from ABSENT. A 401 is not an absent
   listener. Assert both arms: a reachable-but-unauthorized daemon and an actually-absent one must
   not produce the same detail string.
4. `cargo test -p inbox-monitor` stays GREEN with every existing leg intact — the 13 that landed
   plus the cursor-floor legs. Report the `test result:` line.

## NOT IN SCOPE

- Fixing `am robot search` (RED on four independent readers: `column not found: m.topic`, while
  `.schema messages` shows `topic TEXT COLLATE NOCASE`, so the fault is the query builder's ALIAS).
  That is the hardening epic's first fix-at-source task.
- The daemon's silent CLAMP on an out-of-window `--after` cursor. Measured by me: asked from 1 for
  GreenFrog, served from 2108, rc=0, and NO error/code/status key anywhere in the payload — 2,107
  positions skipped behind a normal success shape. Already DEFENDED in `agent-mail-native` and
  upstreamed; the monitor's own client-side floor guard covers it.
- Changing which surface owns read state. This bead makes the disagreement LOUD; deciding which
  number is true is a separate question with a separate owner.

## NO-CLAIM

Consuming the daemon does not make the daemon right. It makes the monitor consume the designated
primary and makes a two-authority disagreement observable — which is strictly more than picking the
convenient arm silently, and strictly less than knowing whether 0 or 20 is the truth. Nothing here
establishes that; it establishes that a monitor reporting one of them without saying which authority
answered is not evidence.

IMPLEMENTED by AmberGate (pane 4, %1408) — LANDED `409e170`. Bead stays `in_progress`; a non-implementer grades.

**THE BEAD'S PREMISE IS REFUTED, and the refutation names its own cause.** The recorded "daemon: 0 unread, every row carries a `read_ts`" does not reproduce. With `mark_read: false` the daemon reports **96 unread of 128** rows, 32 carrying a non-null `read_ts`, against the CLI's **20**. `fetch_inbox`'s `mark_read` **defaults to TRUE** — a read that omits it CONSUMES the unread state it was measuring, and a second read then honestly reports zero with every returned row stamped. **Acceptance 2, live:** `exit=16`, `daemon_unread: 96`, `cli_unread: 20`, `primary_authority: daemon:mcp/fetch_inbox`, `oracle_authority: cli:am inbox --unread`. Neither side picked.

**Acceptance 3, proved live and not only in a unit test:** `HTTP_BEARER_TOKEN=bogus` → exit 13 `reason=unauthorized`; `AM_MCP_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9/mcp/` → exit 13 `reason=absent`. Same code, different typed reason, opposite remedies in the line.

**Acceptance 4:** `test result: ok. 19 passed; 0 failed` (26 legs across 4 suites). All 24 existing `classify` sites pass `NotConsulted`, so every prior leg tests exactly what it tested.

**Six mutations bite.** The registry gate also fired on my first row attempt — 5 cells where it wants 6, and it named the column.

**My instrument error, twice:** I tested the 401 arm by overriding `AGENT_MAIL_TOKEN`, which `discover()` does not read (it reads `HTTP_BEARER_TOKEN` / `AGENT_MAIL_BEARER_TOKEN`, then a client-config file) — and briefly read the resulting success as "the daemon does not enforce auth". Raw `curl` returns **401** for both a bogus token and no header. **My test was wrong, not the code.** Separately worth knowing: the token this fleet exports is not one of the two the kernel consults.

**NO-CLAIM:** consuming the daemon does not make it right. Also — the two arms are compared by THIS crate's `unread()` on the CLI side and the daemon's `unread_only` filter on the other; those are different definitions of unread and could explain part of the gap. Out of scope, not investigated.
