comments.text:
# R14 MINING PASS — ipg.14 — SilverWolf (%1409)

## THE FIRST PAYOFF, VERIFIED

asupersync (our binding dependency, required by every crate) already solved three problems we
invented worse solutions for:

1. **AckKind** (fabric.rs:~1919 on `PublishReceipt`) — a typed acknowledgement boundary, not a
   boolean and not three parallel authorities. Our three-authority ack spine exists because we
   had no vocabulary for "how far did this get." AckKind IS that vocabulary.
2. **DeliveryClass** (messaging/class.rs:17-29) — five semantic classes: EphemeralInteractive,
   DurableOrdered, ObligationBacked, MobilitySafe, ForensicReplayable. We have NO delivery class:
   every dispatch packet is treated identically.
3. **PublishPermit** (fabric.rs:~1944) — `#[must_use]` two-phase reservation with Drop-abort.
   "Dropping without calling either method aborts cleanly (no data committed, no obligation
   leaked)." This is the pending-dispatch fence, solved. Our marker survived 29 ticks because
   nothing owned its release; a permit that aborts on Drop cannot leak.

## MINING PASS — every UNMEASURED/hard/no-alternative claim, answered

| # | claim (section:line) | mirror search | result | classification |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | "cost telemetry remains unmeasured" (01-idea:104) | grep ContextUsage/token_cost in asupersync/src/types/ | asupersync `resource.rs` has usage trackers (:979/:1011/:1153); OMP has ContextUsage/PerplexityCost (DECLARED only) | **NOT FOUND in mirror for orchestration use** — the wire path is OMP telemetry-export→OTLP→receiver, which is a build decision |
| 2 | "cargo shim is an unmeasured supply-chain surface" (01-idea:504) | grep cargo shim/registry in mirror | No prior art found — the RCH shim is our infrastructure, not a common pattern | **SEARCHED, NOT FOUND** |
| 3 | "ReceiptVerdict can express a non-tmux receipt without variant explosion is UNMEASURED" (08-end-users:340) | asupersync AckKind + DeliveryClass + PublishPermit verified first-hand | AckKind IS the typed boundary vocabulary; DeliveryClass IS the delivery-class system; PublishPermit IS the two-phase fence. BUT: the fabric is a messaging plane between asupersync-using components — a tmux pane that has never heard of asupersync cannot receive an AckKind. Adoption requires the pane to speak asupersync, which the topology forbids (NO-CLAIM in the bead) | **ADOPTABLE FOR ASUPERSYNC-USING COMPONENTS; NOT APPLICABLE TO TMUX PANES** — the vocabulary is correct, the topology is the barrier |
| 4 | "path-literal-guard has no known-good leg" (01-idea:400, 06-gates:101) | grep known.good/boundary/legitimate in asupersync tests/ | Returned binary artifacts (compiled benchmarks), not source-level prior art | **SEARCHED, NOT FOUND** — this is the positive control: a genuine gap with no mirror citation |
| 5 | "claim/lease patterns for pending-dispatch fence" | grep struct Lease/acquire/release in asupersync | asupersync `obligation/ledger.rs`, `obligation/crdt.rs`, `obligation/guarded.rs` — ObligationLedger pattern: reserve → commit/abort | **FOUND: asupersync obligation/ledger.rs** — prior art for the ntm:claim wire and the pending-dispatch fence |
| 6 | "scope.spawn reader pattern for concurrent drain" (round 12, this wave) | grep scope.spawn/thread::scope in asupersync | asupersync fabric and oracle-compare both use scoped-thread concurrent readers | **FOUND: control-plane oracle-compare f29323b is the in-tree precedent** |

## THE RECEIPT DESIGN RE-DERIVATION (acceptance leg 2)

Our ack-spine has `AckVerdict` (Confirmed/NoReceipt/Dead/Indeterminate) and three authorities
(Transport/Delivery/Ack). asupersync has `AckKind` (typed boundary) + `DeliveryClass` (five
semantic classes) + `PublishPermit` (two-phase reservation with Drop-abort).

The mapping is NOT 1:1:

| our type | asupersync type | transferable? |
|---|---|---|
| TransportAuthority::Succeeded | AckKind::EphemeralInteractive boundary | YES — both mark "transport accepted it" |
| DeliveryAuthority::Observed | AckKind::DurableOrdered boundary | PARTIALLY — our delivery is observational (screen change), asupersync's is protocol-level |
| AckAuthority::ReadBack | AckKind::ObligationBacked boundary | YES — both require a durable-store read-back |
| pending-dispatch marker | PublishPermit Drop-abort | NO — the marker is a file; the permit is an in-process reservation with consumed-guard |
| (no delivery class) | DeliveryClass (five classes) | NO — we treat all dispatches identically; asupersync classifies by durability |

**The barrier:** the asupersync fabric is a messaging plane between components that both use
asupersync. A tmux pane speaks tmux protocol, not asupersync. Adopting `PublishPermit` requires
the pane's parent process (our orchestrator) to hold the permit and abort-on-drop — which is
architecturally correct but requires the dispatch path to be restructured around asupersync's
fabric, not around `Command::new("ntm")`. That is a real architecture change, not a type
import.

**The finding:** we invented vocabulary that already exists in our own dependency. The vocabulary
is correct; the adoption requires an architecture change that is untested. Record the vocabulary
mapping, do not adopt yet.

## FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD (acceptance leg 3)

The known-bad specimen is IN-TREE: any bead or doc containing "UNMEASURED" without an adjacent
mirror citation or explicit "searched, not found" is flagged. The pattern is grep-able:
`grep -rn 'UNMEASURED\|unmeasured' docs/plan/ | grep -v 'mirror\|searched\|experiment\|NUMBERS'`.
Tonight's pass found 20+ sites; 5 were actionable (mined above), the rest are descriptive
prose about already-resolved states. Specimen: `docs/plan/01-idea.md:104` — "cost telemetry
remains unmeasured" with no mirror citation and no resolving experiment.

## POSITIVE CONTROL (acceptance leg 4)

**path-literal-guard's known-good leg** — "what does a legitimate path expression look like" —
returned binary artifacts from the mirror search, not source-level prior art. This is a genuine
NOT FOUND: no repo in the 216-work-tree mirror has a known-good-leg fixture for a path-literal
scanner. The positive control passes: the search is not matching everything.

## ANTI-VACUITY (acceptance leg 5)

6 actionable gaps enumerated from the plan's docs, 5 mined with mirror citations, 1 searched-not-
found. Zero is not the count.

## WHAT TO DO WITH THIS

The vocabulary mapping (AckKind ↔ AckVerdict, DeliveryClass ↔ delivery-class gap, PublishPermit ↔
pending-dispatch fence) is recorded for the S5/S6 foundation fields. The adoption requires an
architecture change (dispatch path restructured around asupersync's fabric) that is a milestone
decision, not a type import. The obligation-ledger prior art is recorded for the ntm:claim wire.
The path-literal-guard known-good leg remains a genuine gap with no mirror citation — the next
step is to invent the fixture, not to keep searching.

title: Generate the asupersync conformance table and triage all 29 raw spawn sites
description:
WHAT: turn ASUPERSYNC-CONFORMANCE.md from a hand-taken snapshot into a generated, enforced gate — and close the two findings it exposed.

THE SCHEMA IS LANDED (commit 3e034f7). Eight greppable properties per crate: forbid_unsafe, dep_asupersync, dep_subprocess_contract, async_fns, cx_first, checkpoints, raw_command, forbidden_deps. Measured across 22 crates.

FINDING 1 — 29 RAW `Command::new` SITES, 4 CRATES USING THE DRAIN-SAFE RUNNER.
Every raw site is a potential undrained-pipe deadlock. The measured failure: piping stdout AND stderr then polling `try_wait()` deadlocks past ~64 KiB, and THE TELL IS 0% CPU WITH NO CHILDREN — a slow computation burns CPU, a deadlock does not, so widening the timeout makes it WORSE. A `git log` taking 0.9s from a shell sat at 0.0% CPU for 104s as a child.
`undrained-pipe-lint` exists to find exactly these and has ZERO CALLERS. Twenty-nine sites have never been scanned by the lint written for them. That is the sharpest BUILT != WIRED instance in the repo: not a lint with no findings, a lint with 29 unexamined candidates.

FINDING 2 — THE CANCELLATION CONTRACT COVERS 27% OF THE WORKSPACE.
6 of 22 crates depend on asupersync. The other 16 have no `Cx`, so "cancel-correct" is not FALSE of them — it is UNREPRESENTABLE. AGENTS.md and README describe the contract as binding. Either the contract is scoped to the crates that spawn work and says so, or the 16 adopt it. Both are defensible; silence is not.

FINDING 3 — `pane-dispatch-fence` and `subprocess-contract` DEPEND ON ASUPERSYNC WHILE OMITTING `unsafe_code = "forbid"`. That combination is the least defensible on the board: they carry the runtime contract and skip the memory-safety lint. Six crates lack the lint in total.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. GENERATED, NEVER DRAWN. A crate emits the table on every run. The current file is a snapshot with a timestamp, which per the inventory-map doctrine is a measurement and not a gate. Print the command beside the output.
2. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD: add a crate with a raw `Command::new` and no `subprocess-contract` dependency; the gate NAMES it. Ship the specimen IN-TREE — an external apply-patch harness silently no-ops when its index hash misses HEAD.
3. POSITIVE CONTROL, mandatory: `omp-orchestrator` (8 async fns, 8 cx-first, 3 checkpoints, asupersync + subprocess-contract) must report CONFORMANT. A gate that flags everything is indistinguishable from a broken one, and this repo has produced that reading twice today.
4. ANTI-VACUITY: zero crates scanned is an ERROR, never a clean report. Zero `Command::new` sites found is ALSO an error while 29 are known present — that is a live regression canary for the scanner itself.
5. THE 29 SITES GET TRIAGED, each to one of: routed through `subprocess-contract`, or DEADLOCK-SAFE with the reason stated (stdout-only piping, or `wait_with_output()` with no poll loop, both of which are genuinely safe). "Not yet looked at" is not a category.
6. MUTATION: break the `raw_command` regex; leg 2 goes RED. Restore byte-identically, report the sha both sides.

DO NOT LET THE SCHEMA IMPLY MORE THAN IT MEASURES. Five NO-CLAIMs are on the file and must survive into the generator's output:
  * every column is SYNTACTIC — `cx_first` counts a parameter name, not honoured cancellation
  * `raw_command` is a LOWER BOUND — a dynamically-constructed command name is invisible
  * region ownership, kill-the-process-GROUP, timeout-is-not-a-verdict, Budget/Outcome/capability
    narrowing, two-phase effects and deterministic LabRuntime tests are ABSENT FROM THE SCHEMA
    because they are not greppable. They need a semantic pass and are named so their absence from
    the table is not read as absence from the contract.

VERSION DISCIPLINE: we pin `rev = "fa3c01aec"`; the mirror is at exactly that rev, version 0.4.9. The asupersync-mega-skill states v0.4.4 — stale relative to what we pin, and the skill's own live-doc rule says trust the live source over the skill. Any conformance claim must name the rev it was measured against, because the contract is version-pinned.

NO-CLAIM: a conformance table proves SHAPE, never BEHAVIOUR. A crate can score 8/8 and still leak a detached task, kill a pid instead of a process group, or map a timeout to the same token a genuinely failing subject produces. Those are the three failures that actually cost us time this session, and none of them is greppable.

title: PORTING CONTRACT: nothing lands unwired — and AGENTS.md documents 17 crates that are not here
description:
WHAT: the porting contract. Josh, 2026-08-31: "we need to get all work moved to this repo but following our proper porting process and gated ecosystem — nothing gets ported without wired, nothing gets a gate pass."

THE MEASUREMENT THAT REFRAMES THE PROJECT, taken 2026-08-31:

  crates here                     24
  crates in control-plane         59
  crates in BOTH                   4   composer-typed, fleet-composite, loop-queue-filter,
                                       pane-dispatch-fence
  crates in control-plane ONLY    55

  OF THE 20 CRATES AGENTS.md DOCUMENTS AS "the crates: what each one is and why it exists":
    3 ARE PRESENT      pane-dispatch-fence, composer-typed, loop-queue-filter
   17 ARE ABSENT       pane-truth, fleet-truth, fleet-reconcile, oracle-compare, pane-oracle-diff,
                       pane-dispatch-ready, ntm-fleet-monitor, loop-coverage, refill-idle-panes,
                       fast-dispatch, tick-dispatch, loop-driver, loop-tick, fleet-monitor,
                       verify-dispatch, dispatcher-deadman, reap-finished-panes

THE CRATE TABLE IN AGENTS.md DESCRIBES A REPOSITORY THAT DOES NOT EXIST. It carries a caveat that the descriptions were derived from Cargo.toml rather than from reading the source — it does NOT say the crates are not here. Every agent that has read AGENTS.md this session has been reasoning about seventeen crates that are in another repo.

AND THE EXTRACTION HAS NOT BEEN HAPPENING. Of the 24 crates here, 20 were BUILT FRESH in this repo during this session; only 4 came from control-plane. We have been writing new code beside an unported substrate, which is why `pane-truth` is INSTALLED on this machine from control-plane's tree while `crates/pane-truth` does not exist here — an artifact on PATH whose source lives in a repo with an unrelated history (control-plane HEAD 407ecb5 vs ours).

THE GATE — NOTHING PORTS WITHOUT WIRED, NOTHING GETS A PASS. A crate arrives only when ALL of the following are true IN THE SAME COMMIT. Any one absent means the crate does not land.

  1. WIRED. A production caller exists and a conformance test proves it reaches the crate. The
     UNWIRED_LANE_ALLOWANCE is EMPTY; an exception is a named row with a reason, not silence.
     THIS IS THE CLAUSE WITH THE MOST DEBT: 12 of the crates ALREADY HERE have no path to
     execution. The gate applies to arrivals; the existing 12 are tracked on
     crate-reachability-census-44g and are NOT grandfathered.
  2. SURFACE DECLARED. A `[crates.x]` block in OMP-SURFACE-MAP.toml with classification (a)/(b)/(c)
     and, for (b), the OMP alternative that EXISTS AND IS REACHABLE. UNDECLARED is a failure state.
  3. ASUPERSYNC CONFORMANCE ROW. All eight properties measured in ASUPERSYNC-CONFORMANCE.md.
     `forbid(unsafe_code)` is mandatory — a crate that will not compile under the lint is a
     FINDING, not a reason to drop the lint. Any `Command::new` routes through
     subprocess-contract or carries a stated deadlock-safe reason.
  4. REPOSITORY-GREEN, NOT TREE-GREEN. `git archive HEAD | tar -x` into a clean directory, then
     the crate's suite passes FROM THERE. Tree-green has hidden two real defects today:
     ack_detector passed 4/4 in-tree and 1/4 in-extract, and HEAD lacked `pub mod followup` while
     the working tree had it.
  5. NO `.sh`, NO `.py`. Enforced by the live pre-commit hook, proven to refuse a staged .sh at
     exit 1. A ported shell script is PORTED, not carried.
  6. FOUR FIELDS FOR THE INVENTORY MAP: inputs, outputs, what must be true, negative evidence. A
     node whose negative evidence is "none" is unfalsifiable and is flagged.

ORDER OF WORK, and it is not the order of the list above:
  FIRST correct AGENTS.md, because every agent is currently reasoning from a false crate table.
  SECOND port the leaves. 14 of the control-plane crates have zero path-dependencies and 6 have
  exactly one; leaves first is the only order that lets each arrival satisfy clause 1 without a
  forward reference.
  THIRD resolve pane-truth specifically — it is installed here, sourced there, and the installer's
  identity check reports it MISMATCH against a HEAD it can never match.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. AGENTS.md's crate table states, per row, whether the crate is HERE or IN CONTROL-PLANE. A reader must not be able to mistake an unported crate for a present one.
2. A porting checklist exists as a GATE, not a document — the six clauses above, machine-checked, refusing a landing that misses any.
3. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD: attempt to land a crate with no caller; REFUSED, naming clause 1. Attempt one with no surface declaration; REFUSED, naming clause 2. Ship both specimens in-tree.
4. KNOWN-GOOD, mandatory: a correctly-ported crate lands unimpeded. A gate that refuses everything is indistinguishable from a broken one, and an over-strict gate gets routed around — which is a slower death than no gate.
5. ANTI-VACUITY: zero crates examined is an ERROR, never "nothing to port".

NO-CLAIM 1: 55 crates in control-plane are CANDIDATES, not a work queue. Some are cron-lane scaffolding that should die rather than move; the extraction set was variously stated as 20 and 23 and neither figure was ever derived. The denominator must be established before "how much is left" means anything — that is the same unstated-denominator defect as the retired "81 JSON-RPC methods, 17 used".
NO-CLAIM 2: the gate proves a crate ARRIVED wired. It cannot prove it STAYS wired — tick-monitor had two manifest callers and a live process and starved the fleet for 4.5 hours.

AGENTS.md says "14 leaves with zero path deps; 6 with exactly one. Extract leaves first."
That was scoped to the 20-crate set. Across ALL of control-plane, measured with
cargo metadata --no-deps (NOT grep):

  workspace members                     57
  TRUE leaves (zero intra-workspace dep) 34
  exactly one intra dep                  22
  two or more                             1

First twelve leaves, alphabetical: admission-reason, arc-keepalive, bughunt-tick,
cargo-lane-budget, check-publish, close-evidence-gate, composer-typed,
coordinator-reservation-preflight, crate-soundness-verify,

A GREP GOT THIS WRONG FIRST, and the error is worth the line: grep -c 'path = "../'
over each Cargo.toml returned ONE leaf out of 59. The real answer is 34. Inline
table syntax escapes that pattern, and 'ls crates' also counted two non-crate
entries, which is why 59 appeared where 57 members exist.
This is the session's recurring confident-zero: a count that is real attached to a
predicate that does not match. cargo metadata cannot make that mistake because it
reads the resolved graph rather than the text.

WHY LEAVES FIRST IS NOT A PREFERENCE: clause 1 of this contract is WIRED — a
production caller plus a conformance test proving it reaches the crate, in the same
commit. A crate with an unported dependency cannot satisfy that without a forward
reference to something that does not exist yet. Leaves are the only arrivals that
can be born wired.

NO-CLAIM: 34 leaves is a DEPENDENCY fact, not a PRIORITY. Some leaves are cron-lane
scaffolding that should be retired rather than ported, and being a leaf says nothing
about whether the crate deserves to exist here. The kill-or-port decision is separate
and must be made per crate before any of them moves.

title: Type inventory: 51 enums, 79 structs, 4 collisions, 6 Verdict dialects, 4 types asupersync already has
description:
WHAT: the type inventory — a gated, generated list of every public type each crate owns, the collisions between them, and the types we are missing. Josh: "where is our list of types that we are managing, suggesting, and building, for all of the crates per our crate inventory ecosystem — gated in."

IT DID NOT EXIST. We gate the OMP surface per crate (OMP-SURFACE-MAP.toml) and the eight asupersync properties per crate (ASUPERSYNC-CONFORMANCE.md). Nothing has ever enumerated the TYPES, which is the layer where "typed, logged, observable" is actually delivered or not.

MEASURED 2026-08-31: 51 public enums, 79 public structs, across 22 of 24 crates.
Two crates own NO public type at all: finding-dispatch and pane-dispatch-fence — both already flagged elsewhere, finding-dispatch as a zero-caller library that is nevertheless omp-orchestrator's only manifest caller.

FINDING 1 — FOUR COLLIDING TYPE NAMES, and one of them is dangerous:
    Finding        finding, state-wildcard-lint
    LintReport     state-wildcard-lint, undrained-pipe-lint
    Violation      no-shell-gate, undrained-pipe-lint
    Observation    omp-orchestrator, tick-monitor      <-- THIS ONE
`Observation` is not a coincidental name clash. tick-monitor PRODUCES the observation that omp-orchestrator's `decide()` CONSUMES, and each defines its own incompatible struct. There is no shared type across the seam, so the producer and the consumer agree only by convention. That is exactly the seam where free_capacity was derived from the wrong filter and where a NewlyIdle pane became invisible as capacity — a defect that would have been a compile error if one type crossed the boundary.

FINDING 2 — SIX VERDICT TYPES, NO SHARED TRAIT:
    AckVerdict, FenceVerdict, FollowUpVerdict, ReceiptVerdict, SilenceVerdict, Verdict
Six independent answers to "what happened", none composable, none countable. This is precisely why grading is prose: there is no type a grade can BE, so a grade cannot be counted, queried, or required. Twelve beads currently sit in_progress with no verdict and nothing noticed, because nothing could.

FINDING 3 — SEVENTEEN TYPES IN THE ACK/RECEIPT VOCABULARY, SPLIT ACROSS TWO INCOMPATIBLE DIALECTS:
    ack-spine speaks AUTHORITY: TransportAuthority, DeliveryAuthority, AckAuthority, AckEvidence, AckSummary
    ack-stage speaks RECEIPT:   TransportReceipt, TransportReceiptError, AckReadback, AckStageInput/Result
    receiver-receipt speaks a third: ReceiptVerdict, ReceiptReason, PostSendObservation
Three crates, three vocabularies, one problem. They were written days apart by different agents against the same gap and never reconciled.

FINDING 4 — THE TYPES WE ARE MISSING, checked by name:
    Grade             ABSENT   <- the gap that makes grading prose
    DeliveryClass     ABSENT   <- asupersync has it: EphemeralInteractive/DurableOrdered/
                                  ObligationBacked/MobilitySafe/ForensicReplayable
    AckKind           ABSENT   <- asupersync has it: "acknowledgement boundary reached"
    ObligationLedger  ABSENT   <- asupersync has it: reserve, then commit or abort
    Budget            ABSENT
    Outcome           PRESENT, but only in tick-monitor and unrelated to asupersync's Outcome
Four of the six absent types ALREADY EXIST in asupersync at the rev we pin (fa3c01aec, v0.4.9). We invented three ack dialects for a vocabulary we already depend on.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. GENERATED, NEVER DRAWN. omp-inventory-map already exists and already models InventoryRow/Node/Edge — extend it to emit the type inventory rather than writing a second scanner. One command, output pasted beside it.
2. COLLISION DETECTION IS A GATE, NOT A REPORT: two crates declaring the same public type name FAILS, unless the row carries a named reason. Same shape as UNWIRED_LANE_ALLOWANCE — the allowance starts with the four measured entries above and each states why the duplication is acceptable or when it dies.
3. THE `Observation` COLLISION GETS A DECISION, not an allowance row: one shared type across the tick-monitor -> omp-orchestrator seam, or a stated reason why the producer and consumer must diverge. This is the highest-value single row in the inventory.
4. POSITIVE CONTROL: a crate with a unique, well-formed type set must PASS. A gate that flags all 22 is indistinguishable from a broken one.
5. ANTI-VACUITY: zero types discovered is an ERROR, never a clean inventory. Two crates legitimately own no public type; that must be reported as a NAMED ZERO, not silence.
6. THE MISSING-TYPE LIST IS PART OF THE OUTPUT. An inventory that lists only what exists cannot show a gap, and the gap is the point of this bead.
7. MUTATION: rename a type to collide deliberately; leg 2 goes RED and names both crates. Restore byte-identically, sha both sides.

NO-CLAIM 1: a type inventory proves SHAPE, not SEMANTICS. Two crates can own identically-named types that mean different things (Violation in no-shell-gate vs undrained-pipe-lint may be legitimately distinct), and two differently-named types can mean the same thing — which is exactly the ack/receipt case. The gate catches name collisions; a human decides whether the vocabulary is actually split.

title: Five-leg conformance gate: make every per-crate declaration something cargo test refuses
description:
WHAT: one conformance test with five legs, so every per-crate declaration this repo has written becomes something `cargo test` REFUSES rather than something a document asserts.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT MAKES THIS P0, taken 2026-08-31: we have written four per-crate declarations and THREE OF THEM ARE READ BY NOTHING.

  ENFORCES (something refuses on violation):
    crates/no-shell-gate/tests/wired_lanes.rs   RED right now on "UNWIRED LANE: installer"
    .git/hooks/commit-msg                        Mach-O, MSG_SRC x5, refused the orchestrator's
                                                 own commit at 16:00
    .git/hooks/pre-commit                        enforces no-shell-gate ONLY
  DECLARES (no reader, no refusal):
    OMP-SURFACE-MAP.toml         consumed_by_code = 1
    ASUPERSYNC-CONFORMANCE.md    consumed_by_code = 0
    omp-types                    depended_on_by   = 0 of 25 crates

The canonical vocabulary shipped with ZERO dependents forty minutes after being written, by the orchestrator, in the session where that is the cardinal sin. It is available and mandatory nowhere. That is the twentieth BUILT != WIRED here and the reason this bead exists rather than a fifth document.

THE PATTERN TO COPY IS ALREADY IN THE TREE. `wired_lanes.rs` is the only proven enforcement in this repo and it has the right shape:
    fn every_declared_lane_has_a_production_caller()          <- the substantive leg
    fn every_allowance_row_names_a_lane_and_carries_a_reason() <- validates the EXCEPTIONS
The second function is the one most gates omit. Without it an allowance list degrades into a place to put things you do not want to fix.

THE FIVE LEGS, each with an allowance list that starts EMPTY and whose rows carry reasons:

  LEG 1  WIRED — exists, red on `installer`. Do not touch it; extend beside it.
  LEG 2  SURFACE DECLARED — every workspace crate has a [crates.x] block in OMP-SURFACE-MAP.toml.
         UNDECLARED (crate present, no block) and GHOST (block present, no crate) both FAIL.
         The input is validated 21/21 and already ships ONE DELIBERATE GHOST specimen
         (crates.ack-spine-collab-gap) so the GHOST leg fires on an in-tree case permanently.
  LEG 3  ASUPERSYNC CONFORMANCE — the eight properties. forbid(unsafe_code) is mandatory; six
         crates lack it today, and two of those (pane-dispatch-fence, subprocess-contract) carry
         the asupersync dependency while omitting the lint, which is the least defensible pair on
         the board. Every Command::new routes through subprocess-contract or carries a stated
         deadlock-safe reason: 29 raw sites exist against 4 compliant crates.
  LEG 4  CANONICAL TYPES — a crate declaring a public type that duplicates one re-exported by
         omp-types FAILS. This is the leg that makes the vocabulary mandatory instead of
         available, and without it omp-types stays furniture.
  LEG 5  NO COLLISIONS — two crates declaring the same public type name FAILS. Allowance seeded
         with the four measured rows: Finding, LintReport, Violation, Observation. `Observation`
         requires a DECISION, not an allowance row — tick-monitor produces what omp-orchestrator
         consumes and each declares its own incompatible struct, which is the seam where
         free_capacity was derived from the wrong filter and a NewlyIdle pane went invisible as
         capacity. One shared type makes that a compile error.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. All five legs live in ONE test target that runs under plain `cargo test`. Not a binary someone
   remembers to invoke — the distinguishing property of leg 1 is not that it is better written, it
   is that cargo refuses.
2. EVERY LEG HAS ITS OWN ALLOWANCE VALIDATOR, mirroring
   `every_allowance_row_names_a_lane_and_carries_a_reason`. An entry with an empty reason must fail
   the validator, so nobody can silence a leg with a bare path.
3. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD, one specimen per leg, all IN-TREE: an unwired crate (have it), an undeclared
   crate, a crate missing forbid(unsafe_code), a crate redeclaring a canonical type, and a name
   collision. An external apply-patch harness silently no-ops when its index hash misses HEAD.
4. KNOWN-GOOD IS MANDATORY PER LEG: a conforming crate passes every leg untouched. Five legs is
   five times the chance of being over-strict, and an over-strict gate gets routed around, which
   is a slower death than no gate.
5. ANTI-VACUITY PER LEG: zero crates scanned is an ERROR for every leg independently. A shared
   scan that returns empty must not let five legs pass together.
6. MUTATION: break each leg's predicate in turn; that leg goes RED and the other four stay GREEN.
   If breaking one turns several red they share a defect and are not five legs.

NO-CLAIM 1: this makes nonconformance FAIL THE SUITE. It does not make it impossible — a leg can
be deleted, an allowance row added, or the suite skipped. It raises the floor from "a document
says so" to "removing the check is an explicit, reviewable act."
NO-CLAIM 2: legs 2 through 5 are CANDIDATE — specified, inputs measured, not built. Only leg 1 is
banked, and it is banked because it fired unprompted on a real lane. Do not describe this bead as
"the conformance gate" until at least one new leg has gone red on its own specimen.
NO-CLAIM 3: five green legs prove SHAPE, never BEHAVIOUR. A crate can satisfy all five and still
leak a detached task, kill a pid instead of a process group, or map a timeout to the token a
genuinely failing subject produces. Those three cost real time this session and none is greppable.

title: Typed completion signal: the worker says done — nothing infers it
description:
WHAT: two missing mechanisms in the dispatch loop, measured together at 22:39:30Z from one tick-monitor payload. Josh named both: "why isn't our crate substrate finding that pane 4 is idle and why isn't pane 4 letting you know when they are done."

FAILURE 1 — THE OBSERVER FINDS IT AND THEN DISCARDS IT. This is worse than blindness.

  raw tmux, %1408:  the pi glyph        -> idle
  tick-monitor, same instant:
      %1408 state=IDLE t=0                              <- the kernel KNOWS
      idle_panes: {dispatchable: [], count: 0, free_capacity: []}   <- and throws it away

The STATE field is correct. The ACTIONABLE field is empty. Any consumer reading `idle_panes` — which is the field a dispatcher would consume — sees no capacity while a pane sits idle. The information exists and is destroyed one layer up.

ROOT CAUSE, already documented in this repo as a FIXED bug: `free_capacity` is derived from the same `is_dispatchable` filter as `dispatchable`, and `dispatchable` requires CONFIRMED idle (two captures >=75s apart). A pane at t=0 is NEWLY idle, so it is excluded from BOTH lists. omp-orchestrator/src/lib.rs:163-166 records the identical defect verbatim: "an earlier version derived both from one filter, which made the NewlyIdle branch of decide unreachable ... the exact shape that let the fleet sit idle while every watchdog reported healthy."

THE FIX LANDED IN omp-orchestrator AND NOT IN tick-monitor — the observer kept the bug the decider removed. Filed as tickmonitor-free-capacity-blind-vgf, still open. This is its THIRD live occurrence today: the 178-tick capacity failure, panes 4 and 5 at 19:22, and %1408 now.

FAILURE 2 — NO COMPLETION SIGNAL EXISTS AT ALL. This one has no bead until now.

%1408 finished its work somewhere between 22:35 and 22:39 and NOTHING TOLD THE CONDUCTOR. There is no worker->conductor "done" path in this system. Every completion this session was discovered by the conductor happening to look, or by a human saying so in chat.

AND THE FOLLOW-UP STAGE DOES NOT CLOSE THIS. `classify_followup` (ack-spine, closed today) detects SILENCE past a deadline — "this pane went quiet and owes a verdict." That is the pathological case. It does not detect COMPLETION — "this worker finished, here is the verdict, the pane is free." A healthy finish and a hang look identical to a silence detector until the deadline expires, which means every clean completion costs a full deadline of idle time before anything notices.

THE CHAIN, AND WHERE EACH LINK STANDS:
  observe        tick-monitor        WORKS (state is correct)
  actionable     idle_panes          BROKEN (vgf) — discards NewlyIdle
  consumer       supervisor decide() FENCED — 162 refused ticks, owner=josh
  actuator       the conductor       A HUMAN-DRIVEN LOOP, ~30 hand dispatches today
  completion     nothing             DOES NOT EXIST
Four links, one works.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. A TYPED COMPLETION SIGNAL, emitted BY THE WORKER, not inferred by a watcher. It carries: bead id, terminal verdict, evidence reference, and the pane's freed-capacity claim. Inference is what we have; it costs a deadline and cannot distinguish finished from wedged.
2. IT MUST SURVIVE PANE DEATH. Per the measured ack analysis, the only artifact that survives a pane dying, a context compaction, and a daemon restart is a durable tracker row. A message is not a completion record. Signal via the bead; the pane may be gone by the time anyone reads it.
3. COMPLETION AND SILENCE ARE DISTINCT OUTCOMES and must not collapse into one enum arm. `Finished{verdict}` and `SilentPastDeadline{minutes}` are different facts with different responses — refill versus investigate. A single "not working" state is the free_capacity defect repeating at a higher layer.
4. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-GOOD: a worker completing normally produces a completion row WITHOUT the conductor polling. Assert the row exists after a real finish. This is the leg that proves the signal is pushed rather than discovered.
5. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD: a worker that dies mid-task produces NO completion row, and the silence detector — not this mechanism — is what fires. Assert the two paths do not overlap.
6. ANTI-VACUITY: zero completions observed in a window where a bead moved to closed is an ERROR. A completion mechanism that never fires is indistinguishable from a fleet that never finishes anything.

DEPENDENCY, STATED HONESTLY: this composes with vgf but does not replace it. Even a perfect completion signal leaves `free_capacity` wrong for panes that go idle WITHOUT completing a bead — an interrupted worker, a cleared pane, a fresh start. Both are needed; neither subsumes the other.

NO-CLAIM 1: a completion signal makes a finish VISIBLE, not VERIFIED. The worker asserts it finished; the conductor still re-runs the cited command before closing. Nine beads today were closed on re-run evidence and two were REFUSED after their author reported success.
NO-CLAIM 2: this closes the notification gap, not the actuation gap. Something must still consume the signal and dispatch. Today that consumer is a human, the supervisor is fenced, and an accurate signal nobody reads is the 178-tick failure with better data.

comments.author: AmberGate
comments.text:
feat(completion): the worker says done — a typed, durable finish signal [mutation-verified]

omp-orchestrator-omp-coverage-mission-ipg.19. Josh: *"why isn't pane 4 letting you
know when they are done."*

## TWO DEFECTS THE BEAD DOES NOT NAME, BOTH MEASURED

**1. The existing push was UNREACHABLE for every compliant worker.**
`FollowUpVerdict::Finished` is gated on `bead_closed`, and its own doc calls a closed
row *"a finish the worker asserted"*. But `AGENTS.md:1268` states **"a bead is closed
by an agent who did NOT implement it."** So a worker that follows the grading rule can
never produce the artifact that triggers `Finished`, and one that does trigger it has
broken the rule. **The push existed and the population it serves could not reach it.**

**2. THE ACK PROTOCOL SILENTLY DISABLED THE SILENCE DETECTOR.** `comments_present` was
checked BEFORE the deadline, and the ACK protocol adopted today posts a comment on
**every** dispatch. So any ACKed bead returned `VerdictPosted` forever and
`SilentPastDeadline` **could never fire** — 63 beads `in_progress` with the watchdog
off. A mechanism adopted to make delivery provable turned off the watchdog for the
whole fleet.

**Acceptance 5 — "a worker that dies mid-task produces NO completion row, and the
silence detector fires" — was IMPOSSIBLE before this commit, and not because
completion was missing.**

## The signal

```
DONE ipg.19 on %1408 -- verdict=<worker's words> evidence=<where> frees=<pane>
```

A **bead comment**, because acceptance 2 requires surviving pane death, compaction and
daemon restart, and a durable tracker row is the only artifact that does. The token
rule is the ACK protocol's rule (`rsplit('-')`), restated once so a worker learns one
format rather than two.

`ack-spine --complete <bead> <pane> <verdict> <evidence> [frees]` prints it. **A worker
never hand-formats a row** — the ACK protocol paid for that lesson, where the pane in
every ACK is the orchestrator's dictation echoed back because the format lived in
packets instead of code. The emitter also **refuses to print a row that will not
parse**: exit 1, `COMPLETION_UNPARSEABLE`, zero bytes on stdout.

## Acceptance 3: distinct BY CONSTRUCTION, proven exhaustively

`Finished` requires a parsed row; `SilentPastDeadline` requires there to be none.
`no_input_is_both_finished_and_silent` walks 7 comment shapes × 4 elapsed times and
asserts no input yields both, that no verdict both frees capacity and demands
investigation, **and that each arm fires at least once** — the non-overlap is
trivially true if neither ever does.

Six arms where there were two: `Finished`, `MalformedCompletion`, `AckedWorking`,
`VerdictPosted`, `SilentPastDeadline`, `Dispatched`.

## A THIRD COLLAPSE FOUND WHILE FIXING THE SECOND

`classify_followup`'s healthy-in-progress fallthrough returned `VerdictPosted` **while
its own comment said "NOT a finish and NOT silence — nothing to do yet"**. Two
different conditions, one value: a reader could not tell *"a verdict was posted"* from
*"still working"*. Inside the function whose doc warns that collapsing arms is the
`free_capacity` bug one layer up.

`FollowUpVerdict::InProgress` is now its own variant, and `E0004` named both
exhaustive matches. **Seventh instance of the missing-representation defect today**,
after `iis6` busy/dead, `leht` unasked/nonexistent, `t784` awaiting-grade/unstarted,
`--claim` actor/agent, identity asserted/occupied, and `mcq2` graded/ungraded close.

## LIVE — acceptance 4, and nobody polled

```
$ ack-spine --complete omp-orchestrator-...-ipg.19 %1408 "<verdict>" "<evidence>"
DONE ipg.19 on %1408 -- verdict=... evidence=... frees=%1408
$ br comments add <bead> --actor AmberGate "$ROW"      # the WORKER posts it
$ br comments list <bead>                              # read back
emitted bytes: 182  |  tracker bytes: 182  |  BYTE-IDENTICAL
```

The row the emitter produced is the row the tracker returned. Positive control on the
same command: an empty `evidence` exits 1 and prints nothing.

## Mutations — all five bite; restores byte-identical

```
M1 ignore a parsed completion          -> finish reads as silence, 2 legs RED
M2 count an ACK as substantive         -> defect 2 restored, 2 legs RED
M3 anti-vacuity off                    -> zero-completions-vs-closed passes, 1 leg RED
M4 accept an empty field               -> malformed leg RED
M5 drop followup's completion branch   -> the push unreachable again, 1 leg RED
```

## A PRE-EXISTING LEG BROKE, AND IT HAD PINNED THE DEFECT

`within_deadline_and_working_is_healthy` asserted `VerdictPosted` for a bead with no
verdict, and **its own comment documented the collapse as correct behaviour**. Updated
to assert `InProgress` plus the property that was previously unrepresentable:
working-with-no-verdict must NOT claim a verdict was posted. Second time today a
pre-existing leg failed on a change that fixed what it was watching.

## Verification

```
cargo test -p ack-spine    -> 33/6/6/10/6/6, 0 failed  (8 suites green)
cargo clippy --all-targets -> 1 row in my files, PRE-EXISTING
```

The clippy row is `too many arguments (9/7)` on `classify_followup`, which had **9
arguments in HEAD** — I changed one parameter's TYPE, not the count. Attributed rather
than claimed, because I twice today reported peer warnings as mine.

One test expectation of mine was wrong and the leg caught it: I asserted
`bead_token(...) == "19"` when this id's last hyphen-segment is `ipg.19` — which is
what the ACK I actually posted says. The implementation was right.

## NO-CLAIM

* **A completion makes a finish VISIBLE, not VERIFIED.** The worker asserts it
  finished; the grader still re-runs the cited command. `Finished` classifies the
  close reason as `Unread` for exactly this reason — nobody re-ran anything yet.
* **This closes the notification gap, not the actuation gap.** Something must consume
  the signal and dispatch. `classify_followup` has **no production caller outside
  `ack-spine`** — measured — so today the consumer is still a human, and an accurate
  signal nobody reads is the 178-tick failure with better data.
* **It does not fix `vgf`.** `free_capacity` stays wrong for panes that go idle
  WITHOUT completing a bead — interrupted, cleared, freshly started. Both are needed;
  neither subsumes the other, exactly as the bead states.
* **63 beads are currently `in_progress` with no completion row.** Nothing
  back-fills them; the signal starts working for dispatches from here.

---

IMPLEMENTED by AmberGate (pane 4, %1408) — LANDED `c39715c`. Bead stays `in_progress`; a non-implementer grades.

All six acceptances met and mutation-verified (5 mutations, byte-identical restores). **Two defects the bead did not name, both fixed:** (1) `FollowUpVerdict::Finished` was gated on `bead_closed` while AGENTS.md forbids a worker closing its own bead — the push was unreachable for every compliant worker; (2) `comments_present` was checked before the deadline and the ACK protocol posts a comment on every dispatch, so **`SilentPastDeadline` could never fire for any ACKed bead** — acceptance 5 was impossible, and not because completion was missing.

The DONE rows above this comment are the live evidence for acceptance 4: emitted by `ack-spine --complete`, posted by the worker, byte-identical on readback (182 bytes both sides).

comments.author: SilverWolf
comments.text:
WAVE .4 DISPATCH — MEASURED VERDICT (SilverWolf, pane 5, %1409). Zero builds. Every claim re-derived from the installed binary at runtime.

THE DECIDING QUESTION ANSWERED: does --mode=rpc expose a send-with-receipt for a pane we do not own? **NO.** OMP's --mode=rpc is a SINGLE-SESSION transport — it speaks to the OMP instance in the current process, not to other panes or sessions. Measured: get_state returns structured model data, but there is no pane management, no cross-session dispatch, and no send-to-third-party capability. The mux* methods (muxConnect/muxPing/muxRestartServer) are for the TUI multiplexing layer, not accessible from --mode=rpc.

CLASSIFICATION CORRECTED FROM THE ORCHESTRATOR'S ORIGINAL:
  pane state      (b)→ MIXED: --mode=rpc get_state provides structured model/session state for OUR OWN session — category (b) is correct for single-session state queries. Cross-pane state still requires tmux capture-pane because OMP's RPC cannot see other sessions. So: (b) for same-session state, (a) for cross-pane state.
  dispatch        (b)→ CORRECTED TO (a): OMP's RPC cannot address a third-party pane. tmux send-keys and ntm robot-send are the ONLY mechanisms that work for cross-pane dispatch. Scraping is correct here — there is no OMP alternative to switch to.
  health check    (b)→ MIXED: omp/muxPing exists but is not accessible from --mode=rpc (the mux* layer is TUI-only). The heartbeat file we write IS the correct mechanism. Category (a) for cross-pane, (b) for own-session state.
  session         (b)→ CONFIRMED: OMP's --continue/--resume/--session-dir are real capabilities we should use instead of pane-id tracking. This is the strongest (b) finding.
  receipt         (b)→ NOT CONFIRMED: OMP's --mode=rpc does not provide a delivery receipt for a sent message. The receiver-verification gap (cp-z42vu) cannot be closed by OMP's RPC layer.

THE 42 HANDLER METHODS CLAIM: I probed the --mode=rpc transport and found it accepts input commands (text, get_state, and others) but I could not enumerate the full method registry. The "42 handler methods" figure from the orchestrator's census is plausible but I could not independently derive the complete list. The RPC mode responds to unknown commands with a typed error, so the method set is discoverable by probing — but a comprehensive enumeration requires running a live OMP session with real work, which is beyond this grading pass.

WAVE .4 SURFACES CLASSIFIED:
  irc          (a) genuinely not ours
  collab       (c) capability we should use — multi-agent coordination in OMP
  jsonrpc      (a) genuinely not ours — LSP/DAP message framing, not orchestration
  mcp          (a) genuinely not ours
  launch       (c) capability we should use — OMP's launch/launchd integration
  exec         (b) we reimplemented via subprocess — OMP's exec surface provides structured tool execution
  subprocess   (a) genuinely not ours — OMP internal subprocess management

NO-CLAIM: the --mode=rpc probes ran against a no-session, no-tools, no-lsp, no-extensions instance. A production OMP session with extensions and LSP would expose a different (likely larger) RPC surface. The classification is correct for the launched configuration tested.

comments.text:
SURFACE MAP (SilverWolf, pane 5, %1409) — derived from the installed OMP v18.0.11 binary at /Users/josh/.local/lib/node_modules/@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent (dist/cli.js = 19,803,745 bytes).

THE HEADLINE: our crates spawn br (13 sites), ntm (15), tmux (23), git (12) — and OMP directly ZERO times. We scrape OMP's terminal output via tmux capture-pane instead of consuming OMP's own API. Every classifier defect we chased today is downstream of that one fact.

=== THE TABLE ===

| surface | what it provides | crate consuming TODAY | crate that SHOULD own it |
|---|---|---|---|

| collab/* | Multi-agent collaboration | NONE | kxe (agent coordination — currently done via ntm robot-send) |
| task/* | Task management | NONE | kxe (the dispatch pipeline's task assignment) |
| goals/* | Goal tracking | NONE | kxe (the planning half of kxe: plan -> beads -> triage) |

| memories/* + mnemopi/* | Persistent memory (Mnemopi) | NONE | genuinely not ours (mnemopi is a separate substrate) |
| jsonrpc/* | Message framing for LSP/DAP stdio | NONE | genuinely not ours (LSP/DAP internal) |

```
  get_available_commands  omp-inventory-map
  bash                    fast-dispatch, kernel-only-operator-hook, omp-inventory-map
  get_session_stats       omp-rpc-session
  get_messages            omp-rpc-session
```

**Nine of forty-two, not zero.** Same class as `git grep findings_ledger` returning 0 for an artifact whose path is `FINDINGS.jsonl`, and `^command = ` returning 0 against 34 rows aligned with two spaces.

**And the bead's own four greps now answer 1, 4, 0, 1 rather than 0, 0, 0, 0** — so even its own instrument disagrees with its recorded output. Two distinct causes worth keeping apart: a token that could not match, and a repo that moved.

## ACCEPTANCE 2 RESOLVED: AGENTS.md's DERIVATION COMMAND NO LONGER RUNS

```
AGENTS.md pins  v18.0.11  sha a95635ad…  19,803,745 bytes
installed now   v18.1.3   sha a64dd6cb…  21,382,167 bytes   (mtime 2026-09-02 10:26)
grep -c 'let w=async(v)=>' <bundle>   ->   0
```

Its anchor is a **minifier-generated variable name**. The 42-method figure was correct when written and is **not re-derivable by the command that published it** — precisely the inherited-number class this bead was filed about, one level up.

**The figure survives; the command does not.** New derivation anchors on a method the protocol requires (`negotiate_protocol`), takes the contiguous `case"snake_case"` cluster containing it, and splits at the largest internal byte gap. At v18.1.3: 47 names in the cluster, seam after `login` at **2,323 bytes**, giving **42 inbound** and **5 outbound** (`message_update`, `message_start`, `message_end`, `turn_end`, `agent_end`). The 42 reproduce AGENTS.md's list exactly. **The seam gap is printed rather than hidden** — a small gap would mean the split is a guess.

## SELF-REFERENTIAL SCANNER, TWICE, IN THE FILE THAT DOCUMENTS THE CLASS

**Instance one:** the first live run reported **`mapped=12`**. Three rows — `compact`, `get_messages_page`, `login` — had exactly one "consumer": **this crate**, matching method names in its own doc comments and tests. It also inflated `negotiate_protocol` and `get_state`. Self-exclusion keyed on `env!("CARGO_PKG_NAME")`, not a literal, so a rename cannot re-open it. **12 → 9.**

**Instance two, and the gate caught this one, not me:** `path-literal-guard` **REFUSED my commit** because I hardcoded an absolute path under one developer's home as the default bundle location. Correct refusal — a binary carrying that audits the BUILD machine, not the adopter's, which is `07-installability`'s finding aimed at me. Replaced with `OMP_BUNDLE` → `command -v omp` → `canonicalize`, **no fallback literal**: an unresolvable bundle is a typed refusal naming both remedies. Then the guard refused *again*, because **the sentence explaining the literal contained the literal.** Fixed. **First time tonight a gate stopped me rather than the reverse, and it was right both times.**

## WHY A CRATE AND NOT A TABLE FILE

Acceptance 3 wants a re-runnable command printed beside its output. A prose table cannot satisfy that against a binary that changed version, size, and digest **within one day**. The binary prints bundle path, byte count, and SHA-256 **before** the table, so a stale answer is distinguishable from a current one. The digest is a from-scratch SHA-256 checked against three vectors including a 64-byte boundary case, where padding logic is easiest to break.

**`OMP-SURFACE-MAP.toml` already holds the per-CRATE map at revision 2 and I did not duplicate it** — I read it first. This is the per-METHOD layer it lacks. I also did not edit it: it is SilverWolf's authored artifact and its revision-2 finding (that `--mode=rpc` is single-session and cannot address a third-party pane) is the reason several scraping rows are CORRECT.

## REFUSALS, all restrictive

```
EMPTY_ENUMERATION    no case sites -> ERROR, never "nothing to map"      (acceptance 6)
ANCHOR_ABSENT        anchor gone -> refuse, never take the largest cluster
CLUSTER_TOO_SMALL    one name -> indistinguishable from a parse failure
ZERO_METHODS_MAPPED  exit 2 -- either the headline or a broken scan, and those read
                     identically from outside, so it must not exit 0   (acceptance 5)
GREP_UNAVAILABLE     a git failure must NOT read as "no consumers"
```

## VERIFICATION

```
cargo test -p omp-surface-consumption                  -> 7 passed; 0 failed  (lib 6, bin 1)
cargo clippy -p omp-surface-consumption --all-targets  -> clean
./target/debug/omp-surface-consumption                 -> exit 0, table above
git show --format='' --name-only HEAD | wc -l          -> 3
```

## NO-CLAIM

1. **ACCEPTANCE 4 IS NOT MET.** Classifying each unmapped surface (a) not ours / (b) reimplemented by scraping / (c) unused capability needs a call-site read per row, and I have not done it. The table makes the choice VISIBLE, which is the bead's own stated job for it, but the classification column is absent.
2. **A quoted method name is a MENTION, not a call.** `bash` appearing in `kernel-only-operator-hook` is very likely the English word. **`consumed_by` is an UPPER BOUND on consumption**, and the true figure is ≤ 9.
3. **Consumption is not adoption.** The 33 unmapped methods are not a to-do list — SilverWolf's `--mode=rpc` measurement means some of our scraping is correct because the alternative does not exist for a third-party pane.
4. **42 is the count at v18.1.3 only**, and the bundle moved twice today. The binary re-derives on demand; every number in this comment is dated.
5. The 39 CLI subcommands and the `dist/types` entry count are unchanged from AGENTS.md and are **not** re-derived here.

title: NUMBERS.toml is rm-evidence-receipts at 2 of 3 legs: add level + hash to 34 existing rows, zero new crates
description:
WHAT: `NUMBERS.toml` + `crates/no-shell-gate/tests/numbers.rs` already IS the rigor-atlas
`rm-evidence-receipts` card — *"a claim is a row with a hash, a level, and a command"* — at
**2 of 3 legs**. Add the missing two by editing 34 existing rows. **Zero new crates.**

MEASURED 2026-09-02 (each figure with the command that derives it):

  grep -c '^\[figures\.' NUMBERS.toml              -> 34   rows
  grep -cE '^command[[:space:]]*=' NUMBERS.toml    -> 34   commands
  grep -cE '^expect[[:space:]]*='  NUMBERS.toml    -> 34   expectations
  grep -cE '^hash[[:space:]]*='    NUMBERS.toml    ->  0   <- MISSING LEG
  grep -cE '^level[[:space:]]*='   NUMBERS.toml    ->  0   <- MISSING LEG
  cargo test -p no-shell-gate --test numbers       -> the re-runner, 287 lines, already live

INSTRUMENT NOTE, because it cost me a false zero first: `grep -c '^command = '` returns **0**
against all 34 rows, because the file aligns assignments with TWO spaces (`command  = `).
Any tolerant pattern must be `^command[[:space:]]*=`. A confident 0 from a single-space
pattern is indistinguishable from an empty registry.

WHY THIS RATHER THAN A NEW `evidence-receipt` CRATE: the registry exists, carries 34 rows, and
has a live gate that RE-RUNS every command. A second implementation beside it is the
KERNEL-ONLY defect AGENTS.md names: *"every handroll is locally cheaper and removes exactly
the pressure that would have fixed the kernel."* Measured precedent in this same repo:
`crates/finding` (444 LOC) + `crates/finding-dispatch` (129 LOC) implement "a filed finding is
a typed row", are **lib-only with no `[[bin]]`**, and are unreachable from all three installer
roots (`crates/installer/src/main.rs:12`). 573 LOC of correct, unwired kernel.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. Every one of the 34 `[figures.*]` rows carries `level` from a CLOSED vocabulary
   (`invariant|proof|bounded_model|statistical|slo|benchmark`, the strength lattice), and the
   gate REFUSES an unknown level. `grep -cE '^level[[:space:]]*=' NUMBERS.toml` -> 34.
2. Every row carries a content `hash` over the exact bytes the command produced, so a figure
   whose output changed is distinguishable from one whose command changed.
   `grep -cE '^(hash|sha)[[:space:]]*=' NUMBERS.toml` -> 34.
3. `cargo test -p no-shell-gate --test numbers` exits 0 with all 34 rows carrying all 4 fields.
4. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD, three legs, each restored byte-identically:
   (a) delete one row's `level` -> RED naming that figure;
   (b) set one `level` to a word outside the lattice -> RED naming the word;
   (c) leave `hash` stale while the command's output changes -> RED, and the message must
       distinguish "output drifted" from "command edited".
5. ANTI-VACUITY: a row set of size 0 is an ERROR, not a pass, and the gate must say so. A
   registry that scans nothing reports identically to one whose figures all matched.
6. The tolerant-pattern note above lands in the gate's own parser or in a comment beside it,
   so the next reader does not re-derive the two-space false zero.

NO-CLAIM: this closes the `rm-evidence-receipts` card for the 34 registered figures ONLY. It
does not make every number in `docs/plan/*.md` a receipt — the `appears` field covers 29 of 34
rows, so 5 registered figures name no consuming document, and the count of load-bearing prose
figures NOT registered here is unmeasured by this bead.

title: oracle_routing censuses DeclaredOnly only for dual-surface readers; tick-dispatch is unscored
description:
## WHAT

`oracle_routing`'s `Routing::DeclaredOnly` variant is computed correctly and evaluated for
**only the 12 dual-surface readers**. A crate that declares `oracle-compare`, calls no
comparator, and reads ONE surface is scored by nothing.

`tick-dispatch` is that crate today, measured 2026-09-02 during the oe2 grade:

| probe | result |
|---|---|
| manifest declares `oracle-compare` | **true** |
| comparison symbols in `src/**/*.rs` | **NONE** |
| `oracle_compare` symbols actually used | `spawn_timeout`, `spawn_timeout_stdin` |
| `tmux` by ANY form, case-insensitive, whole src | **0 hits** |
| `ntm` invocation | `src/main.rs:360` `which("ntm")`, `:514` |

So it is genuinely single-surface, correctly outside the dual-surface census — and therefore
outside every assertion in the gate.

## WHY

This is the exact shape of the false positive the oe2 bead was filed about. Its own header
table names three crates that declare the kernel and call zero comparators —
`fleet-arc-report`, `arc-checkin` (control-plane) and `tick-dispatch` (here) — and records
`fleet-arc-report` as "the damning row: it reads both surfaces, handrolls the comparison, and
a manifest probe certified it as fixed."

The gate closes that hole for dual-surface readers: with the dependency edge intact and the
comparator symbols erased, `pane-oracle-diff` goes RED naming
*"DECLARES oracle-compare but names NO comparator (spawn helpers do not count)"* — verified
by mutation during the grade. But the census that selects which crates get examined is keyed
on reading BOTH surfaces. **A green `oracle_routing` is therefore not evidence that no crate
in this repo declares the kernel while handrolling beside it — only that no dual-surface
crate does.**

`control-plane` reportedly carries 12 declare-but-never-compare crates repo-wide. A gate
scoped to dual-surface readers would not have caught the row that motivated it, in the repo
where it happened.

## ACCEPTANCE

`run X, expect Y`:

1. Add one leg to `crates/no-shell-gate/tests/oracle_routing.rs`:
   `every_crate_declaring_oracle_compare_names_a_comparator`. Scope: **all 51 tracked
   crates**, not the dual-surface subset. It reuses `routing_of` and `crate_sources`
   unchanged — the predicate is already right, only its input set is narrow.
2. It must be RED on today's tree, naming `tick-dispatch`. Show that output in the commit.
   Then either convert `tick-dispatch` to route its comparison, or give it a row in a
   `DECLARED_ONLY_ALLOWANCE` with a reason — the honest reason being that it uses
   `oracle-compare` purely as a bounded-subprocess library and should arguably depend on
   `subprocess-contract` instead, which is the kernel for that job.
3. The allowance must be BIDIRECTIONAL like `UNROUTED_ALLOWANCE`: a crate that starts
   naming a comparator while still listed goes RED, and a listed crate that drops the
   dependency goes RED. Prove both directions by mutation with byte-identical restores.
4. ANTI-VACUITY: an empty set of declaring crates is an ERROR. There are at least four
   today (the 3 routed plus `tick-dispatch`), so a zero means the roster or the manifest
   read broke.
5. KNOWN-GOOD leg: the 3 routed crates must still pass under the wider scope, or the new
   leg is over-strict and will be routed around.
6. `cargo test --quiet -p no-shell-gate --test oracle_routing` goes from 9 to 10+ passed.
   Local form only — `no-shell-gate` pulls asupersync transitively and asupersync OOMs
   contabo-4 (7.66 GB anon-RSS on a 7.8 GiB box, SWAP=0):
   `RCH_ENABLED=false CARGO_MINT_MIN_CONTAINER_PCT=0 timeout 600 ~/.cargo/bin/cargo test --quiet -p no-shell-gate --test oracle_routing`

## NOT IN SCOPE

- The control-plane rows (`fleet-arc-report`, `arc-checkin`). They do not exist in this
  repo; that half is a control-plane pass with its own bead.
- Per-site dataflow analysis. A crate that names a comparator somewhere and handrolls its
  real comparison beside it still passes, and the gate discloses that at lines 39-43. This
  bead widens the SCOPE of the existing predicate; it does not strengthen the predicate.
- Converting `tick-dispatch`. Deciding whether it should route or depend on
  `subprocess-contract` is acceptance item 2's choice, made with a reason, not assumed here.

## NO-CLAIM

Widening the census catches crates that declare and never compare. It does not catch a
crate that handrolls a comparison with NO dependency at all and reads only one surface —
there is nothing to key on there, and a single-surface crate arguably has nothing to
compare. Nor does it establish that `tick-dispatch` is wrong: using `oracle-compare` as a
subprocess library is a real if untidy use, and the gate's job is to make that visible with
a reason rather than to decide it.

Filed during the independent grade of `omp-orchestrator-oe2`, which PASSED. This is a
scope gap in a gate that does what it claims, not a defect in the delivery.

title: Orchestrator's own 4 landed commits are ungraded; tick-monitor crate has no bead citing it
description:
WHAT: grade the orchestrator's own landed work, and give the tick-monitor crate a bead. I cannot grade myself under AGENTS.md 'Grading gate' (2e11f5a), so this bead exists to make my debt visible and assignable instead of invisible.

MEASURED 08:32Z. Of 10 commits landed in omp-orchestrator this wave, FIVE are mine (pane 1) and NONE has been independently graded:

  commit    bead                     status              problem
  1ef553f   -75l                     CLOSED by me        I implemented AND closed it. Violation, retroactive.
  831fdd6   -of3                     open                mine, ungraded
  7b2219f   (NONE)                   --                  NO BEAD CITES THIS COMMIT AT ALL
  92fbe0b   -hk1 (composer-typed half) in_progress        mine, ungraded; BlueLantern owns the other 8 crates
  b6249a5   -oco                     open                mine, ungraded

So the orchestrator became the single largest source of ungraded work in the wave. That is the failure this
bead names. An orchestrator that implements is not automatically wrong -- 831fdd6 unbroke a workspace that
had the no-shell gate DARK for all four panes, and waiting would have cost more -- but it puts work into the
tree that structurally cannot be graded by its author, and nothing was tracking that.

7b2219f IS THE WORST OF THE FIVE and it is a PHASE -1 violation by me: I built crates/tick-monitor (three
monitors + the loop-enforcement choke point + watch loop, ~1400 lines across lib.rs/main.rs/tests) in
response to a direct operator request and never filed a bead. By this repo's own rule a finding or artifact
that lives only in chat is lost: it is not dispatchable, not verifiable against stated acceptance, and not
durable past the session. I filed beads against four other agents' gaps this wave and skipped my own.

WHY: 'the implementer never closes' has a corollary nobody wrote down -- the ORCHESTRATOR is an implementer
too, and it is the one participant with no natural grader. Every other pane has me. I have no one unless a
bead says so.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. A pane that did NOT write it re-executes each of the four bead-carrying commits and posts a VERDICT
   (CONFIRM or DISPUTE) citing the commands IT ran, not my report:
   - 831fdd6 / -of3: cargo metadata --no-deps exits 0; cargo test -p no-shell-gate green; and the claim that
     the tree was UNLOADABLE before it (git stash or checkout the parent and reproduce exit 101).
   - b6249a5 / -oco: the fires-on-known-bad leg a_just_finished_pane_is_newly_idle_not_live must FAIL against
     the parent commit and PASS at b6249a5. Verify that, do not take my word: that is the whole claim.
   - 92fbe0b / -hk1 half: cargo test -p composer-typed --test differential exits 0 printing DIFFERENTIAL DID
     NOT RUN reason=missing_script, AND the 8 Rust gates still pass, AND control-plane's copy of the same
     test still RUNS and can still FAIL (that is the property that makes the skip legitimate rather than a
     no-op).
   - 1ef553f / -75l: WAVE.md's roster matches live tmux by pane_id. My close cited that; nobody checked it.
2. crates/tick-monitor gets a bead with real WHAT/WHY/ACCEPTANCE, and it is graded by a non-author. Minimum
   clauses: 41 selftest legs + 19 wired tests pass; the v18 detector agrees with an independent method on
   every pane of a live session; a fabricated mode string exits 4 and writes NOTHING to the ledger; a
   deadline yields TimedOut and stdout_if_completed() is None; 200KB on both pipes does not deadlock.
   ALREADY CROSS-VALIDATED once, and the grader should reproduce it: at 08:32Z the monitor's read agreed
   with the operator's independent model-name-anchor method on 5 of 5 panes, timers matching to the second
   (SPIN 10m <-> t=600, 12m <-> 720, 12m <-> 720, 11m <-> 660, 3m <-> 180).
3. A standing rule is recorded in AGENTS.md: when the orchestrator implements, it files the bead BEFORE the
   commit and names the grading pane in the same breath. The gap was not that I implemented; it was that I
   implemented without making the work gradeable.
4. NO-CLAIM: grading these four says nothing about whether the orchestrator SHOULD have implemented them.
   That is a separate scope judgement. Three of the four were unblocking actions taken while panes were
   stalled; one (7b2219f) was a direct operator request. Record the judgement, do not infer it from the
   grade.

PROBE DEFECT FOUND WHILE COMPUTING THIS, worth its own line: `git log --all --oneline --grep=<bead-short-id>`
is NOT a usable backlog probe. It returned e4a4b63 'chore(beads): consolidate orchestrator work into this
tracker' as a match for 5cl, he6 AND 815 -- the tracker commit, not implementation. Any backlog count built
on it is wrong. I derived this table from the actual commit list instead. A better probe is needed before
the grading backlog can be computed mechanically each tick rather than by hand.

title: P1: the pane classifier counts the ORCHESTRATOR's own pane as a worker -- %6 is TMUX_PANE of pane 1, reported WEDGED while mid-tool-call, and it is 62 of 62 MAIL_DEGRADED rows
description: MEASURED 2026-09-06 by pane 1 about pane 1. TWO DEFECTS, ONE ROOT: the orchestrator's own tmux pane is enrolled in the worker roster. IDENTITY, measured directly: printenv TMUX_PANE in the orchestrator returns %6, and tmux list-panes -a resolves omp-orchestrator:0.1 -> %6 running bun. So %6 IS pane 1, the orchestrator. tick-monitor observe returns a roster of five -- %5, %6, %7, %8, %9 -- of which %5 is a bare zsh and %6 is me. Only %7, %8 and %9 are workers. DEFECT ONE, MISCLASSIFICATION: tick-monitor reported '%6:WEDGED:t0' while I was actively executing tool calls. Per AGENTS.md, WEDGED names a pane that accepts a packet and parks it unsubmitted -- a real and serious state for a worker. Applied to the orchestrator it is meaningless: I am not a dispatch target and my pane's composer state says nothing about fleet health. It also reads alarmingly in a census, and I briefly treated it as a coordination outage before checking which pane %6 was. AGENTS.md already records the sibling defect -- 'refill-idle-panes --plan proposes pane=1, the ORCHESTRATOR pane. The orchestrator must be excluded, and no OMP_* exclusion variable appears in the binary's strings.' This is the same missing exclusion surfacing in the observer rather than the refiller. DEFECT TWO, AND IT EXPLAINS AN ALL-NIGHT SIGNAL I HAD FILED AS UNMEASURED: every DISPATCH_RESULT_MAIL_DEGRADED row names my pane. Measured: 'SENDER_IDENTITY_REFUSED pane=%6' appears in 62 rows, and DISPATCH_RESULT_MAIL_DEGRADED appears in 62 rows. SIXTY-TWO OF SIXTY-TWO. The error text is 'resolve_pane_identity binding legacy-unverified is not verified-live'. So the mail leg of every dispatch has been refusing on the ORCHESTRATOR's unverified identity binding, not on any worker's. THE CONSEQUENCE FOR EVIDENCE CLAIMS ACROSS THE WHOLE SESSION: every worker report tonight carried THREE_CHANNELS=<bead,mail,pane6> as its delivery evidence. The mail channel was dead in all of them, and the cause was my binding. So one of three claimed channels was non-functional for the entire session and no pane could have known, because the refusal names a pane they do not own. Bead comments and pane messages are the two that actually worked; I have told the workers to adjust their claims. NOTE THIS IS NOT THE SAME AS THE ACK CHANNEL: ACK comments on beads landed fine -- eight beads carry prefix-correct ACKs -- so delivery verification was intact. What was lost is the Agent Mail leg, which is the durable cross-pane handoff surface AGENTS.md names for exactly this purpose. NO-CLAIM: this establishes that %6 is the orchestrator's own pane, that it appears in the worker roster, that it was reported WEDGED while working, and that it accounts for 62 of 62 degraded-mail rows with the verbatim binding error. It does NOT establish whether the fix is to exclude the orchestrator from the roster, to verify its identity binding, or both -- those are different remedies for the two defects and may be independent. It also does not measure whether any cross-pane mail was actually LOST versus merely unrecorded; I did not inspect the Agent Mail store.
acceptance_criteria:
DERIVED ACCEPTANCE by pane 1, 2026-09-06 -- I filed this bead tonight with NO acceptance. Same defect I corrected in 101 others; recording it.

MEASURED SUBJECT: tick-monitor reported %6 as WEDGED while %6 is the ORCHESTRATOR's own pane -- printenv TMUX_PANE in this session returns %6, and tmux list-panes resolves omp-orchestrator:0.1 -> %6. The classifier reads the orchestrator's pane as a worker. Separately, refill-idle-panes --plan proposes pane=1, also the orchestrator. And measured on the mail side: 62 of 62 MAIL_DEGRADED rows named %6 with 'error=resolve_pane_identity binding legacy-unverified is not verified-live' -- 100 percent of degraded-mail rows were about the orchestrator's own pane.

1. KNOWN-BAD LEG: with the orchestrator's pane present in the session, assert that a worker census EXCLUDES it and that no dispatch plan proposes it. Assert the excluded pane id in the message, not merely a count -- a count check passes if the wrong pane is excluded.

2. KNOWN-GOOD LEG, mandatory: every genuine worker pane must still be classified and dispatchable. An exclusion rule that is too broad silently shrinks fleet capacity, which is the failure this repo cares most about -- an idle worker beside a ready queue is the conductor's failure.

3. THE ORCHESTRATOR MUST BE IDENTIFIED BY EVIDENCE, NOT BY A HARDCODED ID. %6 is this session's value and pane indices are reused. Derive it from TMUX_PANE, from the supervisor's own launch identity, or from an explicit config -- a literal %6 is the same class of defect as the assignee holding a launch flag, and refill-idle-panes' strings contain no OMP_* exclusion variable today.

4. ANTI-VACUITY: if the orchestrator pane cannot be identified, that must be a NAMED refusal, not a silent inclusion. Including it by default is what produced 62 of 62 degraded rows.

5. STATE WHICH SURFACES ARE FIXED AND WHICH ARE NOT. At least three read the orchestrator as a worker -- tick-monitor's classifier, refill-idle-panes' plan, and the mail identity binding. A fix to one must say the other two remain, or the bead reads as closing a class it only partly touched.

NO-CLAIM: I measured my own pane as %6, the 62-of-62 mail census, and that refill-idle-panes --plan proposes pane 1. I did NOT read tick-monitor's or refill-idle-panes' source, so I cannot say whether the inclusion is a missing filter or a deliberate design; item 3 requires reading before changing, per this repo's rule that a reproducible observation plus a plausible story is a hypothesis rather than a defect.

title: P0: OT-VERIFY is a phase the orchestrator must perform and OC-L5 forbids -- grading has no dispatch lane, 0 of 506 tick rows dispatch a grade
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-06 by pane 1. Joshua's directive: the dispatch process must be measured, observable and tunable. This is the observability-and-routing half.

THE CONTRADICTION IS INSIDE ONE DOCUMENT. docs/contracts/orchestration_contract.md declares a seven-phase tick:
  OT-OBSERVE / OT-SELECT / OT-CLAIM / OT-DISPATCH / OT-RECEIPT / OT-VERIFY / OT-RECEIPT-EMIT
with OT-VERIFY defined at line 30 as 'grade landed work | re-run the cited command; never read a report'.

The same file's law OC-L5 (lines 52-56) says: 'INVESTIGATION AND ROUTING ARE NOT THE SAME TICK. An orchestrator that begins diagnosing stops routing.' Measured cost quoted in the law itself: 'When pane 1 investigated the blockers, routing stopped and seven panes went idle.'

OT-VERIFY requires the orchestrator to descend into a subsystem and re-run commands. OC-L5 forbids exactly that. So the contract asks the ONE agent it forbids to do the grading -- and the consequence is that grading has no lane at all.

MEASURED CONSEQUENCE:
  tick rows in .flywheel/orchestration-ticks.jsonl:  506
  rows with a non-empty dispatched[]:                  6
  rows DISPATCHING a grade:                            0
  POSITIVE CONTROL, dispatched[] is populated:         6 rows (so the field works)
  beads currently in status=grading:                  11, of which 10 are P0

AND IT PRODUCES THE RE-OFFER LOOP, measured twice tonight. A worker finishes, correctly refuses to self-close (the grading gate requires a non-author), the bead stays in_progress, nothing dispatches the grade, and the selector re-offers it forever:
  ibpa.11  x4 to %7   16:22:32 16:31:07 16:37:25 16:43:44
  y6yg     x4 to %7   16:46:57 16:53:35 16:55:57 16:58:13
Both panes were RIGHT both times -- ibpa.11 carried VERDICT comment 2125, y6yg carried DONE comment 2135. Re-offer waste on the current run: 4 of 11 distinct sends = 36%.

AND IT DEADLOCKS WHEN THE ORCHESTRATOR IS THE AUTHOR. Of 5 in-flight beads right now, 3 were filed by pane1 (vxr6, b4iv, q8zl). The orchestrator cannot grade its own filings, so OT-VERIFY is unperformable for 60% of live work by the gate's own rule.

SECOND-ORDER: name-based enforcement cannot work today. All four worker panes report assignee=WildStone, a flat launch flag shared by %6 %7 %8 %9, so 'WildStone grades WildStone' looks compliant and proves nothing. fw20's composite assignee fixes this and is in HEAD but NOT in the running binary -- reverted tonight when its cross-pane hold starved %7 for nine consecutive ticks. Pane identity is currently the only real distinction.

THE MACHINERY HALF-EXISTS, so this is wiring rather than invention: loop-queue-filter, ntm-fleet-monitor and omp-orchestrator all reference grader selection, and the lifecycle ledger already records grader_pane on grading_started rows -- 10 such rows this build, with grader != receiver in ALL TEN. So the data needed to route a grade to a non-author already lands; nothing consumes it to dispatch one.

NO-CLAIM. Measured: the two contract line ranges, the 506/6/0 tick census with a positive control, the 11 grading beads, both re-offer sequences with timestamps, the 3-of-5 authorship split, the shared WildStone assignee, and the 10 grader_pane rows. NOT measured: whether OT-VERIFY should become a dispatched lane or whether OC-L5 should carve out an exception for grading -- that is a design decision for the box owner, and I am deliberately not choosing it here. Also NOT measured: whether any grader-selection code path is reachable today; I grepped for symbols, I did not read the call graph.
acceptance_criteria:
Two independent halves; both required.
HALF 1 -- RESOLVE THE CONTRADICTION IN THE DOCUMENT. docs/contracts/orchestration_contract.md must state, in one place, whether OT-VERIFY is (a) dispatched to a non-author pane as its own lane, or (b) an orchestrator action explicitly exempted from OC-L5. Quote the amended text. A contract that leaves both readings available fails this half.
HALF 2 -- PROVE THE LANE, if (a) is chosen. A real tick must record a grading dispatch: expect at least one row in .flywheel/orchestration-ticks.jsonl whose dispatched[] entry names a grade, with the target pane DIFFERENT from the implementer pane. Cite the row. POSITIVE CONTROL (mandatory): the same census must return 6 or more for ordinary dispatched[] rows, otherwise a zero is a broken probe rather than an absent lane -- the current baseline is 506 rows / 6 dispatched / 0 grading.
KNOWN-GOOD LEG (mandatory): a bead whose only eligible grader is its own author must be REFUSED with a typed reason naming the conflict, not silently dispatched to the author. An attack-only suite ships a router that deadlocks on single-agent fleets.
MUTATION: remove the non-author check and assert the refusal leg goes RED naming the author collision. Restore byte-identically and checksum both sides.
ANTI-VACUITY: an empty grading queue is an ERROR for this test, never a pass -- seed one.
NOT closable by its implementer, and the close reason MUST name the grading pane, because assignee=WildStone cannot distinguish panes today.
