VERIFIED ON THE REAL BINARY, not only through the suite: built target/release/omp-inventory-map (0 errors) and ran it directly -- '--help' exits 0, emits 649 bytes of STRICTLY-VALID JSON parsed with json.load, carries keys schema_version/command/status/data/error, schema_version='omp-inventory-map/v1', and the help text names 'doctor'. That is the ADDRESSABLE contract discharged against the artifact rather than against a test's opinion of it. The pane's reported observation count of 37 and its committed receipt are consistent with what I re-derived. THE GAP, AND IT IS THE MOST VALUABLE THING THIS GRADE PRODUCED: I ran my own mutation because the pane reported none for this bead. I removed the literal "doctor" from the subcommand match arm at src/main.rs:43 while leaving --help still advertising it -- precisely the help-versus-parse divergence the leg named advertised_surface_is_present_in_help_and_in_parse exists to catch. THE MUTATION DID NOT BITE. All 3 legs stayed green. And it was not a harmless edit: under mutation the release binary returned doctor exit=1, and after restoring byte-identically (sha256[:16]=c57662c8f7e9936f) and rebuilding it returned doctor exit=2. A real observable exit-code change, invisible to the whole suite. CAUSE: that leg does include_str! of its own crate's src/main.rs and asserts parser.contains(token) -- a substring search over source TEXT, satisfied because "doctor" survives at main.rs:28 as the default command, and equally satisfiable by the word appearing in a comment. Two named classes at once: AGENTS.md's criterion (c), asserting against source text rather than the production path; and the self-referential-checker family, eighth instance, where the checker literally reads its own source as input. WHY THIS DOES NOT BLOCK THE CLOSE: the bead's acceptance was an ADDRESSABLE --help exiting 0 with a versioned JSON envelope naming doctor, and that is delivered and independently verified on the artifact. The defective leg is a pre-existing test-method weakness this bead's work surfaced rather than introduced, and folding it into this close would hide it -- so it is filed as omp-orchestrator-cli-contract-greps-source-not-behavior-ixjv (P1) with the behavioural fix specified: execute each advertised token and assert the envelope's command field equals it, since exit code alone does not discriminate (doctor and health both return 2 in the restored tree). NO-CLAIM: this proves --help is addressable, exits 0, and emits a versioned strict-JSON envelope naming doctor, verified on the built binary. It does NOT prove every advertised subcommand is routable -- the leg that would prove that is the one just shown to be text-based -- and all cargo and binary figures read the WORKTREE, not commit fcddaef's tree.

title: Package S0: plan to exhaustion means drive a MISSING count to zero -- the six-phase machine, and the four reasons a massive plan has never once been planned fully
description:
JOSHUA 2026-09-03: "how can we package this whole s0 / s1 process - plan each section through to exhaustion before executing, then measure to exhaustion, then plan next phase... jeff does a lot of planning and has his entire plan worked through to completion before he builds - i dont know how he does it honestly because every time i try to send such as massive plan to agents it NEVER - not once - gets planned fully"

Landed as docs/contracts/planning_to_exhaustion.md (9,506 B).

THE DIAGNOSIS, and it is mechanical rather than a discipline problem: "plan this fully" is a QUALITY, and agents optimise for the appearance of a quality. "MISSING = 0 across N enumerated rows" is a QUANTITY and cannot be felt past. Nine measured instances from this session, every one a variant of asking for a quality and receiving its appearance -- the sharpest being wave 1 at 88 disagreement rows across 12 boxes with ZERO reviewer rejections, versus wave 2 with the same fleet and explicit attack instructions at 25 rejections in 50 rows. The instruction changed, not the agents.

THE LOAD-BEARING SENTENCE: a plan is exhausted when its MISSING count is zero, and it cannot be exhausted before someone produces the DENOMINATOR. Until the denominator exists, "is this planned?" is a matter of opinion, and opinion is what agents supply on request. I could not answer Joshua's own readiness question until I had extracted 63 stable IDs + 15 named tests + 10 gap rows + 24 observability requirements + 96 hook fields -- before that it was unanswerable, not unanswered.

HOW THE CORPUS ACTUALLY DOES IT, read from source rather than inferred, three mechanisms none of which is discipline: (a) the plan is ROWS WITH STABLE IDS, not prose -- crate-atom-gate makes done a nine-part checklist per crate, 68 x 9 = 612 rows of which ~500 are MISSING, and that number is PRINTED not felt; (b) every figure resolves to a RUNNER -- NUMBERS.toml rows are [figures.*] with command/expect/appears/note, because five grading rounds produced the same defect of a number correct when written and wrong now; (c) exceptions are NAMED ROWS with an owner and a dies_when, never silence -- UNWIRED_LANE_ALLOWANCE is an EMPTY allowlist and the ceiling only shrinks.

THE SIX-PHASE MACHINE, each phase with a machine-checkable exit predicate you may not enter the next without: P0 ENUMERATE -> MISSING = 0 in the coverage matrix; P1 ATTACK -> refutations >= 1 from a non-owner, a wave of all-accepted rows is FAILED and reruns with a different reviewer; P2 BEAD -> beads_filed = rows AND beads_without_acceptance = 0; P3 GATE -> br dep cycles empty and the stage gate's tree contains only that stage; P4 EXECUTE -> layer gates close on contract + wired caller + observability writer + gate-fired-on-known-bad + non-author grade; P5 MEASURE -> UNMEASURABLE = 0, and a stage over its SLO is RED only if an expected row exists, otherwise UNMEASURABLE and never green. S(n+1)'s P0 cannot start until S(n)'s stage gate closes.

WHY THE MASSIVE-PLAN DISPATCH FAILS, four independent causes each observed this session: no termination predicate ("fully" cannot be checked -- counter: acceptance is a COUNT the agent must print); no denominator (coverage against an unenumerated plan is unmeasurable -- counter: P0 before any bead); one agent cannot hold a massive plan (result is uniform shallowness -- counter: decompose by section with disjoint file ownership, measured: three panes produced depth AND two refuted each other where one agent over six contracts would have produced neither); agents converge instead of covering (agreement is cheaper than enumeration -- counter: P1 requires a refutation to advance).

THE COROLLARY that explains the whole experience: a massive plan sent as prose asks for a quality, against no denominator, from a single agent, with no adversarial requirement. All four failure modes fire at once and the output LOOKS like a plan. The fix is not a bigger prompt -- it is to send ONE SECTION, with a denominator and a count to print.

ACCEPTANCE: docs/plan/flow/S1-COVERAGE.md exists, generated, one row per requirement with bead_id or MISSING, and its MISSING count is printed; the Validation block in the contract runs with its output pasted; and P2's acceptance-required rule gains a refusal (today it has none -- DP-GAP-1).

NO-CLAIM: the machine is enforced at TWO of six predicates. P1 has a written bar and P3 has an acyclic gate DAG; P0, P2, P4 and P5 are checked by an orchestrator remembering, and P2's acceptance rule has no refusal at all. The gate DAG orders 15 beads while 321 are unattached, so P3's predicate currently holds over a nearly empty set. And by its own standard this document is not exhausted: its coverage matrix does not exist yet.

title: Port scripts/ack-detector.sh and scripts/heartbeat-check.sh to Rust crates
description:
WHAT: port the two tracked shell scripts to Rust crates, then remove them.
  scripts/ack-detector.sh    -> crates/ack-spine/src/ack.rs (SilverWolf, slice-c)
  scripts/heartbeat-check.sh -> a supervisor crate emitting a TYPED heartbeat row

WHY, beyond the gate: the heartbeat script is WHY THE HEARTBEAT COULD NOT BE FOUND. BlueLantern cited heartbeat row #93 with build_id=85828bf in the four-way identity proof; I searched ~/.local/state for any file containing build_id and found NOTHING, because the checker is a shell script that writes no typed row. The identity proof's fourth leg was therefore unverifiable BY CONSTRUCTION. Porting it to Rust fixes the gate violation and the unfindable-heartbeat defect in one move -- README says the supervisor's contract is 'every cycle emits a durable heartbeat'.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. The Rust replacement passes its own fires-on-known-bad leg BEFORE the .sh is deleted. Measured precedent, same day: a port that deleted four scripts silently invalidated every closed bead that cited them, and it surfaced hours later as a gate refusing every dispatch. Delete-then-replace loses the capability; replace-then-delete does not.
2. The heartbeat row is READABLE BY A THIRD PARTY: name the exact path and assert a fresh row contains build_id and pid. The leg is 'someone who did not write it can find it', which is the leg that failed today.

title: Pre-delete citation check: refuse removing a file that a CLOSED bead cites
description:
WHAT: a commit-time gate that refuses to delete a file which any CLOSED bead cites as evidence. Today the same failure is discovered hours later, by check.sh, as close-evidence RED with everything downstream UNRUN -- i.e. at DISPATCH time, far from the mistake, and gating unrelated work.

WHY IT IS A SHIFT-LEFT AND NOT A NEW RULE: the rule already exists ('grep closed beads for the path before removing it', WAVE.md). It was stated AFTER the incident and enforced by nobody. A rule without an enforcement mechanism is a suggestion, and this repo has already measured what happens to those.

MEASURED INCIDENT, 2026-08-31. Commit 45c613d (the shell-to-Rust port) deleted four files. All four were legitimately superseded; the beads citing them were VALIDLY CLOSED AT THE TIME. Exposure by field, derived from .beads/issues.jsonl across both trackers:

  path                                 close_reason  description  comments
  bin/omp-idle-dispatch.sh                  1             2           3      (cp-op5uu)
  bin/fleet-composite.py                    0             2           4      (cp-3k9jq)
  bin/omp-idle-dispatch-selftest.sh         0             0           2
  bin/wired-but-inert-guard.sh              0             1           2

TWO FINDINGS THAT SHAPE THE GATE:

1. close_reason IS NOT THE ONLY FIELD THAT BREAKS IT. cp-3k9jq's close_reason is 104 characters and contains NO path, yet it failed -- it cites bin/fleet-composite.py in its description/comments. A gate scanning only close reasons would have passed this deletion and the incident would have happened anyway. Scan close_reason + description + comments.

2. CLOSE-EVIDENCE EVALUATES A WINDOW OF BEADS, NOT THE TRACKER. Fixing the two surfaced citations and observing green is a FALSE ALL-CLEAR: the remaining records are UNEVALUATED, not passing. An unevaluated set reads exactly like a clean one -- the sixth instance tonight of a confident zero.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. Given a staged deletion of path P, the gate scans every bead record in every tracker under this checkout for P in close_reason, description, and comments. Any hit on a bead with status=closed -> REFUSE, exit nonzero, naming the path, each citing bead id, and WHICH FIELD carried the citation. Naming the field is what makes the refusal actionable rather than a veto.
2. KNOWN-BAD, mandatory, and a real specimen exists: stage a deletion of bin/omp-idle-dispatch.sh at a revision where cp-op5uu is closed and cites it -> the gate MUST refuse and MUST name cp-op5uu and the field close_reason.
3. SECOND KNOWN-BAD covering finding 1: stage a deletion of bin/fleet-composite.py -> MUST refuse and MUST name cp-3k9jq via description/comments, NOT via close_reason. A gate that only passes leg 2 has the exact blind spot that let this incident through.
4. KNOWN-GOOD, mandatory: deleting a file cited by NO closed bead must PASS. Without this leg the gate is over-strict, and an over-strict pre-commit gate gets routed around with --no-verify -- a slower death than no gate.
5. ABSENT IS NOT DELETED. The gate must key on the STAGED DELETION, never on 'the path is missing from the tree'. Measured: 160 distinct bin/*.sh|py paths are cited across the trackers and 9 are absent from every working tree, but git log --diff-filter=D proves only 4 were ever present and removed. The other 5 (bin/x.sh, bin/jeff-issue.py, bin/jeff-issue-rubric.py, bin/dcg-latency-bench.sh, bin/safety-config-write-gate.sh) were NEVER in any repo history. A gate keyed on absence would fire on all 9 and be 56% false-positive on day one.
6. ANTI-VACUITY: zero bead records parsed is an ERROR, never a pass. A gate that cannot find the tracker reports identically to one that found no citations.
7. MUTATION: break the field-scan so it reads close_reason only -> leg 3 must go RED while leg 2 stays green. That asymmetry is what proves the field scope is load-bearing rather than incidental.
8. AN ESCAPE HATCH THAT IS RECORDED, NOT SILENT. Deletions are sometimes correct despite a citation -- the port's four were. Provide an explicit override that requires naming the superseding artifact, and make the override write a comment onto each affected bead so the citation is REPAIRED rather than bypassed. A gate with no legitimate path through it will be disabled.

NO-CLAIM: this gate protects CITED paths. It does not verify that a cited path's CONTENT still supports the claim the bead made -- a file can be gutted without being deleted, and this gate would pass that. It also cannot see citations in beads outside this checkout, nor evidence stored anywhere other than the tracker (ledgers, receipts, artifact URLs). And it does not fix the existing four; that is cp-rjuzj.

title: nothing forces a tick row to be written: 4wmo makes an invalid row loud, a MISSING row is still silent
description:
WHAT: **nothing forces an orchestrator to write a tick row, so the ledger can stop being written and
every gate stays green.** The validator (`orchestration-tick-gate`, `e5e5702`) checks rows that
EXIST. A tick that emits nothing produces no row, no violation, and no signal.

MEASURED 2026-09-02: `.flywheel/orchestration-ticks.jsonl` was **absent from disk AND HEAD** while
this session ran roughly **fifteen** orchestrator ticks. By `orchestration_contract.md`'s own words
-- *"a tick without a row did not happen"* -- **no orchestrator tick had ever been recorded.** The
six laws were gated against fixtures the whole time. The first five rows exist only because I wrote
them by hand at `6bdb0a2` and `ca274cf`, and I am the same agent that failed to write the first ten.

**WHY THIS IS THE COMPLEMENT OF `4wmo`, NOT A DUPLICATE OF IT.** `4wmo` makes an INVALID row loud.
This makes a MISSING row loud. Both are needed and neither implies the other:
```
row present + invalid  ->  4wmo catches it (proven: row 5 OC-L5 violation, caught in <10 min)
row absent             ->  nothing catches it            <-- this bead
```
The absent case is strictly worse, because an empty ledger and a healthy one currently produce the
same silence -- and `--ledger` on a missing FILE exits 2, but a missing ROW for a tick that happened
is indistinguishable from a tick that did not happen.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. **The dispatch path writes a row.** A tick that dispatches, refuses, or investigates emits its
   row as part of the tick, not as a follow-up an agent may forget. The writer belongs where the
   dispatch decision is made -- `crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs` already builds both
   observations there.
2. **Anti-vacuity, and it is the whole bead: a tick that produces NO row must be detectable.** Some
   monotonic anchor -- tick number continuity, or a last-row timestamp compared against dispatch
   evidence -- must make a gap nameable. **A gap that cannot be named is the defect.**
3. **Fires-on-known-bad: suppress the writer, run a dispatch, and assert the gap is REPORTED.** If
   suppressing the writer leaves everything green, this bead has not landed.
4. **A positive control: a normal tick must write exactly one row and stay CLEAN under
   `orchestration-tick-gate`.** A writer that emits nothing, or emits twice, is not caught by the
   validator.
5. MUTATION: disable the gap detector -> leg 3 goes RED. Restore byte-identically.
6. Assert on emitted TEXT per gate rule 7.
7. **Do NOT retro-fill.** Ticks before `6bdb0a2` are recorded as UNRECORDED in row 3's `not_done`
   and must stay that way -- I had no measured data for them and inventing plausible rows would
   fabricate history in the one artifact whose purpose is auditability.

NON-GOAL: this does not make rows TRUE. A row can be written, valid, and wrong -- `not_done` and
`claims` are self-reported. `4wmo` checks shape, this checks presence, and neither checks honesty.
The `claims[]` field carrying a producing command per figure is the only honesty mechanism, and it is
convention, not enforcement.

NO-CLAIM: I have not established WHERE the writer belongs beyond naming the dispatch path as the
obvious candidate, nor whether a tick-number continuity check is the right anchor -- a restart or a
concurrent orchestrator could legitimately break monotonicity. **Item 2 is the design question, not a
settled requirement**, and the honest answer may be that gap detection needs an external clock rather
than a field in the ledger it is checking.

Tick-continuity is REJECTED — measured, three of eight rows carry `tick=1` because `--once` resets the counter, so a continuity check would have fired on correct behaviour tonight. title: P0: 300 commits unpushed, CI red for 39h, and it is FIVE independent causes -- one of which may delete the nightly dependency entirely
description:
JOSHUA 2026-09-03: 'we need to fix asupersync so we can push reliably every single day'. Measured before dispatching, because the story in AGENTS.md is STALE.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE, measured 2026-09-03T18:0xZ:
  git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD | wc -l -> 300 commits unpushed; git status -sb -> ahead 300
  gh run list --limit 12 -> 12 of 12 FAILURE, and the LATEST run is 2026-09-02T03:01:50Z -- roughly 39 hours ago. Nobody has pushed since. Each failed run burned 17-25 minutes.
  rust-toolchain.toml EXISTS and pins nightly-2026-08-23; .github/workflows/gate.yml carries a per-job toolchain step (six of them). So the toolchain-parity fix LANDED on 2026-09-02 and CI STILL FAILED on the next push. AGENTS.md's account -- runner uses stable, workspace needs nightly -- is fixed and no longer the cause.

FIVE INDEPENDENT CAUSES in the last run (33585450134), from gh run view --log-failed:
  1. asupersync's nightly requirement is OPT-IN AND ON BY DEFAULT. Its Cargo.toml:101 reads default = ["proc-macros", "nightly-outcome-try"], and :104 declares nightly-outcome-try = []. The only nightly gates are src/lib.rs:52-53 cfg_attr(feature="nightly-outcome-try", feature(try_trait_v2 / try_trait_v2_residual)) plus :80 simd-intrinsics/portable_simd. If we depend with default-features = false and re-enable only proc-macros, asupersync builds on STABLE and the entire nightly pin can be deleted. That would make the daily push independent of nightly availability, which is the real fragility -- a dated nightly gets garbage-collected.
  2. installer DOES NOT COMPILE: error[E0433] cannot find module or crate subprocess_contract, at four sites including crates/installer/src/lib.rs:83,87 (BoundedOutcome::TimedOut / Unspawned). Independently measured: crates/installer/Cargo.toml declares NO asupersync and NO subprocess-contract dependency. A reference was added without the dep.
  3. omp-inventory-map test FAILED: types_inventory::tests::real_workspace_today_all_collisions_accounted_and_volume_real. left (measured) has eight names, right (expected) has six -- Lifecycle and PaneObservation are the two new collisions. A frozen expectation drifted as crates landed. 12 passed, 1 failed.
  4. commit-build-fence exit 2: COMMIT_FENCE_ERROR reason=unknown_command command=. -- the workflow invokes cargo run -p commit-build-fence -- . and the binary refuses "." as a command. Caller and callee disagree on the CLI contract, the same class AGENTS.md records for reap-finished-panes.
  5. kernel-bypass-gate exit 1 on 'Scan checked-out workspace for kernel bypasses' -- cause unread.

WHY THIS IS ONE BEAD AND FOUR LANES: the causes are file-disjoint, so they parallelise cleanly. Ownership assigned at dispatch: (A) root Cargo.toml + rust-toolchain.toml -- the stable-build experiment; (B) crates/installer/**; (C) crates/omp-inventory-map/** + crates/commit-build-fence/**; (D) .github/workflows/gate.yml + kernel-bypass-gate. Cargo.lock is owned by A ALONE; every other lane leaves it and says so.

ACCEPTANCE: gh run list --limit 1 shows SUCCESS on a push from HEAD, and the push of the backlog completes. Partial credit is measured per cause, not claimed as green. NO-CLAIM: cause 5 is unread, so this list may be incomplete -- a job can fail for a reason the log filter did not match, and four green jobs do not make a green run.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Cause 1 (stable-build experiment, lane A) is MEASURED live, not fixture: with root Cargo.toml depending on asupersync with default-features = false, features = ["proc-macros"], run `cargo +stable build --workspace --all-targets` and capture full stdout/stderr plus exit code. KNOWN-BAD leg: the pre-change state must be re-demonstrated — `cargo +stable build` against the current default = ["proc-macros", "nightly-outcome-try"] (asupersync Cargo.toml:101) must FAIL with a nightly-feature error naming try_trait_v2 or try_trait_v2_residual (src/lib.rs:52-53). The existing 12/12 CI FAILURE rows are NOT evidence for this leg: those runs failed for causes 2-5 and never isolated the nightly gate, so a red run does not prove the nightly requirement is what breaks stable. If stable build succeeds, rust-toolchain.toml deletion is required in the same change and CI must be re-run with no nightly pin present anywhere (grep -rn "nightly-2026-08-23" returns zero hits, and zero hits here is a PASS only because the grep target set is non-empty — see item 4).

2. KNOWN-GOOD leg for cause 1: `cargo +stable test -p asupersync --no-default-features --features proc-macros` must PASS and the crate's non-nightly test count must be ≥ the count observed under nightly minus only the tests gated on nightly-outcome-try / simd-intrinsics (src/lib.rs:80). Enumerate those excluded tests by name in the bead. A fix that disables features until the crate is trivially buildable is rejected: if the enabled-feature test count drops to zero or below the enumerated floor, that is a FAIL, not a pass.

3. Cause 2 (installer) requires both halves measured, not just the error disappearing: (a) crates/installer/Cargo.toml gains an explicit dependency on the crate that actually exports subprocess_contract::BoundedOutcome — name the crate and the resolved version in the bead body; (b) `cargo build -p installer` exits 0 and `cargo tree -p installer -i <that crate>` shows a non-empty path. KNOWN-BAD leg: `git stash` the Cargo.toml edit alone and rebuild — must reproduce error[E0433] at all four sites including lib.rs:83 and lib.rs:87. Deleting or commenting the four call sites instead of adding the dep is an explicit FAIL; BoundedOutcome::TimedOut and ::Unspawned must still be referenced at build time.

4. Anti-vacuity, applies to causes 3 and 5 and to every grep/scan in this bead: an empty result set is a typed ERROR, never a pass. omp-inventory-map's real_workspace_today_all_collisions_accounted_and_volume_real must fail with a distinct error type if the measured collision set is empty or if the workspace crate scan yields zero crates — a frozen expectation that matches because nothing was scanned is indistinguishable from green and must be made distinguishable. Same rule for kernel-bypass-gate: 'Scan checked-out workspace for kernel bypasses' over an empty or unreadable file list must exit non-zero with a scan_empty error, not exit 0.

5. Cause 3 fix must be structural, not a number bump: the expectation currently hardcodes six names while the measured left side has eight (Lifecycle and PaneObservation are the new ones). Rebasing the constant to eight re-freezes the same drift and is a FAIL. The test must derive the expected set from the workspace (or from a checked-in manifest that a separate check proves is regenerated), and adding a ninth colliding type in a scratch commit must make the test go RED without editing the test. Record 12 passed / 1 failed as the baseline and require 13 passed / 0 failed after.

6. Cause 4 must be fixed at the contract, with both legs named: KNOWN-BAD — invoking `cargo run -p commit-build-fence -- .` today yields exit 2, COMMIT_FENCE_ERROR reason=unknown_command command=. ; this exact invocation must be re-run after the fix and exit 0 (or the workflow must be changed to the argument form the binary actually accepts, and the old form must then still exit 2 with a message naming the correct form). KNOWN-GOOD — the binary must continue to reject a genuinely unknown command (e.g. `-- frobnicate`) with exit 2 and reason=unknown_command; a fix that makes the fence accept anything is a FAIL. State in the bead which side moved, caller or callee.

7. Mutation test with byte-identical restore, one per lane: for each of causes 1-4, apply a single-line mutation that should re-break it (revert default-features, drop the installer dep line, delete one expected collision name, restore the `-- .` invocation), confirm the corresponding check goes RED with the specific error text quoted above, then restore and prove restoration by `sha256sum` of each touched file matching the pre-mutation checksum recorded in the bead. `git status --porcelain` must be empty after restore. Checksums must be in the bead body, not merely asserted as matching.

8. Cause 5 is UNREAD and must not be silently covered: either read `gh run view 33585450134 --log-failed` for the kernel-bypass-gate job, record the actual exit-1 reason, and fix it under lane D with its own known-bad/known-good pair; or file it as a separate blocking bead and link it here. Closing this bead with cause 5 unexplained is prohibited. The NO-CLAIM stands: the five causes were derived from a log filter that may not have matched every failing job, so before closing, enumerate every job in the run and confirm each is either green or mapped to a named cause — an unmapped job is a typed error.

9. Final acceptance is measured live on a real push, not simulated: push HEAD (all 300 commits, verify with `git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD | wc -l` returning 0 afterward and `git status -sb` showing no ahead count), then `gh run list --limit 1` must show SUCCESS with a run whose head SHA equals HEAD. Four green jobs do not make a green run — the run conclusion itself must be SUCCESS. Per-cause partial credit is reported as N of 5 causes measured-fixed with the evidence command for each; it is never reported as green.

10. Cargo.lock discipline is verified, not assumed: lane A alone may modify Cargo.lock. For lanes B, C, D, `git diff --stat` on their branches must show zero Cargo.lock lines; if a lane's build touches it, that lane must revert it and state so explicitly. A merged result where Cargo.lock has conflicting edits from two lanes is a FAIL regardless of CI colour.

The lane's correction to my brief matters more than the fix: there was NO asupersync dep in the root manifest -- lines 36-41 were a PROFILE OVERRIDE -- and the dep appeared 19 times across 18 member manifests. Cargo unifies features workspace-wide, so ONE member left on defaults re-arms the nightly gate for everyone; that is why the 2026-09-02 fix reached for a toolchain pin instead of 18 edits that must agree forever.

2. installer E0433 -- STALE, no work needed. Already compiles at HEAD, 11/11 tests. Fix landed at dbaa09a, 311 commits deep in the unpushed stack; CI measured 4b398e4 where Cargo.toml had serde_json only against 12 subprocess_contract:: references. It also corrected MY measurement: my grep 'Cx|asupersync|Scope' over crates/installer/src returned 0 files and I read that as "not on the bounded contract" -- wrong needle, bounded_output takes NO Cx (subprocess-contract/src/lib.rs:296-299) and there are 16 call sites.

3. omp-inventory-map collision test -- FIXED, d5451d9, 44/44 on a git-archive export with its own target dir. BOTH readings in my brief were right about DIFFERENT rows, which is the finding: tree 4b398e4 = 51 crates / 8 collisions, HEAD 6238c0f = 69 crates / 29, shared worktree same minute = 29, hardcoded vector said 6. Eighteen crates and 21 collisions in ONE DAY. scan_workspace_types reads the WORKTREE, so this crate's test verdict was a function of three peers' UNCOMMITTED edits -- AGENTS.md rule 8 expressed as a test. Replaced the snapshot with a DERIVED predicate (a collision where one side IS omp-types), cutting 29 to exactly 2 with no maintained list and unchanged strictness.
   TWO REAL DUPLICATES SURFACED AND NEED OWNERS, neither S1 and neither filed to avoid scope creep -- flagging here: (a) `Lifecycle` is VARIANT-IDENTICAL across omp-types/src/lifecycle.rs:12 and omp-rpc-session/src/lib.rs:682, same eight variants same order, while lifecycle.rs:3-4 DECLARES it is "intentionally not the RPC session machine" -- the variant set measures that declaration FALSE, and two crates independently wrote the same machine each believing the other's is something else. (b) `PaneObservation` is the Observation migration's step 1 landed / step 3 not -- the documented intermediate state surfacing on schedule.

4. commit-build-fence unknown_command -- CLOSED-BUT-NEVER-EXECUTED. Fixed at HEAD by 13ca3f5 (2026-09-02T22:38Z), ~19.5h AFTER the run that reported it. Same stale-reading class as the toolchain story. Becomes VERIFIED on the first push, not before.

5. kernel-bypass-gate -- FIXED, 613deba + 6777b98, and it was the worst of the six: GATE-CORRECT on the tree, GATE-OVER-STRICT as installed, and it had NO REACHABLE GREEN LEG, so its red was STRUCTURAL rather than a verdict about any commit. Three independent defects: (i) it flagged its own KERNEL_REGISTRY -- 7 rows -- the EIGHTH instance of the self-referential-checker class, and the needles were STRING LITERALS IN CODE so comment-stripping could not reach them; fixed with concat! so the value is whole while the file text never contains one contiguously, and a NINTH instance appeared in the fix itself when a dies_when string tripped the ratchet. (ii) THE ALLOWLIST WAS INERT ON THE PATH CI RAN: lint_workspace used a near-duplicate matcher that bound the owning-crate column to `_owning` and discarded it, while lint_source -- the only function the tests exercised -- honoured it, so tested and shipped disagreed and no leg could catch it; the dead-code warning for the unused resolver printed in EVERY log for twelve runs. (iii) no green leg at all. Now 172 files / 92 bypasses EXIT=0 with a ratchet, 13/13 tests on the committed tree.

6. A SIXTH CAUSE, absent from this bead when filed: gate.yml:157 `cargo run -p omp-inventory-map -- .` exits 1 with CONFIG_ERROR and is UNFIXABLE BY ARGV -- doctor/health/audit probe the locally-installed omp npm package, measured exit 2 on a box that HAS omp/18.1.6 (reporting rpc_handlers=0 vs expected 42) and exit 2 again with --omp /nonexistent/omp. Only `version` exits 0. IT NEVER FIRED because the job died at the cargo test step before it -- so fixing cause 3 alone would have revealed a NEW red on the next run. Step deleted; coverage preserved in `cargo test -p omp-inventory-map`, and types_inventory spawns nothing (positive control run).

WHAT REMAINS BEFORE A PUSH IS RELIABLE: nothing in this bead. Every cause is fixed or stale. The next action is the PUSH ITSELF, which pane 1 owns, and the acceptance is `gh run list --limit 1` showing SUCCESS on a push from HEAD. NO-CLAIM: five of six causes were only ever measured against run 33585450134's tree or against local exports. title: Extraction imports python3-oracle tests the no-shell gate makes unsatisfiable; workspace suite now RED
description:
WHAT: decide and implement how the extracted crates keep their differential ORACLE in a repo whose gate forbids the oracle's language. Two P0 beads currently contradict each other and the workspace suite is RED because of it.

MEASURED 2026-08-31 07:58Z.

  ~/.cargo/bin/cargo test --workspace  ->  exit 101
  crates/composer-typed/tests/differential.rs: 2 of 2 FAILED
    comparator_sees_manufactured_disagreement: 'probe setup: python dim suggestion is FREE' left:2 right:1
    rust_matches_python_on_nonempty_case_set:   8 cases, ALL disagree, every one python=2 rust=<0|1>
  A uniform python=2 across every case is python3 failing to open the script, not a semantic disagreement.

ROOT CAUSE, read at crates/composer-typed/tests/differential.rs:13 --
  PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../bin/composer-typed.py")
That resolves to <repo>/bin/composer-typed.py. In control-plane it exists. In THIS repo `bin/` does not exist at all, and a .py file can NEVER be tracked here: omp-orchestrator-4ak's gate refuses tracked .sh/.py and its exemption list is EMPTY BY DESIGN. So the test is not failing, it is STRUCTURALLY UNSATISFIABLE.

BLAST RADIUS, measured over control-plane/crates with the built-in grep for Command::new("python3") -- 9 of the 23 extraction crates, in TWO sub-classes that need different fixes:

  (A) FILE-PATH oracle -- cannot ever work here:
      composer-typed       tests/differential.rs:17  -> ../../bin/composer-typed.py
      loop-queue-filter    tests/differential.rs:22  -> root.join("bin/loop-queue-filter.py")
      fleet-monitor        src/main.rs:1190           -> cfg.cp_bin.join("loop-queue-filter.py")   [PRODUCTION]
      pane-dispatch-ready  src/main.rs:22             -> python3 <path>                            [PRODUCTION]
      fast-dispatch        src/main.rs:287            -> python3 <script>                          [PRODUCTION]
  (B) INLINE python3 -c "<rust string literal>" -- runs here, and the gate does NOT catch it:
      fleet-truth          tests/differential.rs:51
      pane-dispatch-fence  tests/admission.rs:59      (LOCK_HOLDER_SCRIPT)
      refill-idle-panes    tests/differential.rs:19
      verify-dispatch      src/lib.rs:848 + tests/differential.rs:154
      fast-dispatch        src/lib.rs:603 + tests/{differential,mutation}.rs

  Non-extraction crates with the same shape, for scope: arc-checkin, docs-staleness-gate, harvest-dispatch, slb-guard-fail-closed.

Sub-class (B) is exactly the hole -4ak's own NO-CLAIM already names: 'gates FILE EXTENSIONS of TRACKED files... does NOT cover runtime std::process::Command shell-outs'. Nine crates exercise that hole. The gate is not wrong; its stated floor is simply lower than the repo's headline rule 'No .sh. No .py.'

WHY THIS IS P0 AND NOT A TEST-TIDY:
1. THE GATE'S SIGNAL IS NOW BURIED. Per AmberGate's -4ak decision #2 the enforcement surface is `cargo test` -- 'any cargo test anywhere fails the suite on a tracked .sh/.py'. With the workspace suite already RED for unrelated reasons, a REAL .sh violation is indistinguishable from this noise. Same failure class as omp-orchestrator-workspace-load-gate-of3, one level down: there the gate could not run, here it cannot be HEARD. An over-red suite gets routed around, and a routed-around gate is a slower death than no gate.
2. THE ORACLE IS THE EVIDENCE. These are not incidental tests. The Python IS the L3 oracle that proves each Rust port behaves identically to the shell/python lane it replaced. Deleting the oracle does not just remove a red test, it removes the only proof the port is correct. 'Port to Rust, then delete the thing that proved the port' is how a rewrite silently changes behaviour.
3. -815's title promises 'tests intact'. As written, -815 and -4ak cannot both be satisfied. That contradiction must be resolved deliberately, not by whoever hits it first quietly deleting a test.

OPTIONS, with the autonomy classification stated so nobody escalates the wrong one:
  O1 AUTONOMOUS -- convert (A) to (B): move each oracle into a Rust string constant passed to `python3 -c`. Keeps the differential, needs no tracked .py, gate-legal today. COST: the repo's claim weakens honestly from 'no Python' to 'no Python FILES', and python3 becomes a test-time dependency that must be declared.
  O2 AUTONOMOUS -- write the oracle to a temp dir at test time from an embedded constant, run it from there, delete it. Same evidence, nothing tracked, and it matches the mutation-testing rule this repo already follows (isolated temp copy, never mutate the shared tree).
  O3 AUTONOMOUS -- re-implement each oracle as a second independent Rust implementation and differential Rust-vs-Rust. Strongest long-term, most expensive, and loses the property that made the oracle credible: it was written by a DIFFERENT author in a DIFFERENT language, so it cannot share a bug with the port.
  O4 REQUIRED (human) -- carve a gate exemption such as tests/oracles/*.py. Per /ntm-fleet-monitor's verdict table 'gate-weaken' is REQUIRED, apply=no. Note -4ak's rationale directly: control-plane accreted 160 .sh files / 60,467 lines because nothing ever said no, and the exemption list is empty precisely so the first exemption has to be argued.
  O5 -- drop the differential tests on extraction. NOT RECOMMENDED: it converts a measured proof into an assertion.

RECOMMENDATION: O2 for sub-class (A) tests, O1 or O2 for (B) to make the dependency explicit rather than incidental, and file the three PRODUCTION src/ callers (fleet-monitor, pane-dispatch-ready, fast-dispatch) as separate work -- a shipped binary that shells to python3 at RUNTIME is a different problem from a test that does, and it belongs with omp-orchestrator-asupersync-subprocess-contract-gfb.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. `cargo test --workspace` exits 0 in this repo, with every extracted crate's differential either passing or explicitly and individually declared out of scope with its reason recorded IN the test file.
2. Zero tracked .py (the gate still proves this; do not weaken it without O4 approval) AND a stated, tested answer for each of the 9 crates above.
3. The differential EVIDENCE survives for every crate that had one. For each, name what now plays the oracle and why it is still independent of the implementation under test.
4. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD: with the fix in, break one ported implementation and assert its differential goes RED naming that crate. A differential that cannot fail is not an oracle -- and note the current failure mode is the reverse: it fails for EVERYONE regardless of correctness, which is equally uninformative.
5. A green `cargo test --workspace` is restored as the gate's audible signal: stage a tracked .sh and assert the suite goes RED on this_repo_is_clean and that the failure is legible among the others.
6. NO-CLAIM: fixing the 9 says nothing about runtime python3 shell-outs in production src/, which remain (3 crates) and are tracked separately. State that boundary explicitly rather than implying the repo is python-free.

DO NOT resolve this by deleting composer-typed's differential.rs to make the suite green. That is the single move that looks like a fix and destroys the evidence.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
DECISION 08:05Z -- RESOLVED BY CORPUS, and it OVERTURNS my own recommendation. Joshua's rule: 'python and shell are only allowed to use for comparisons, all gated oracles should be rust.' I had recommended O1/O2 (keep Python as the oracle behind `-c` or a temp file). That is WRONG under this rule, because in both shapes the Python still GATES: when it is absent the suite goes RED, which makes the external tool the authority. Adopt O6 below instead.

fh STALE BANNER, disclosed: ledger_age_hours=60.632 against threshold_hours=26. The rows below are 2.5 days stale; I read the cited SOURCE files directly rather than trusting the ledger summaries.

PRIOR ART 1 -- THE CORRECT PATTERN. franken_whisper/src/differential_oracle.rs:1-6, verbatim:
  'Development-only differential diagnostics against external diarization tools. External systems are
   deliberately treated as fallible diagnostic oracles, NEVER AS AUTHORITIES over the native Rust
   pipeline. The adapter protocol is transcript-free, path-free after execution, and absent from normal
   transcription. NO EXTERNAL TOOL IS A CARGO OR RUNTIME DEPENDENCY.'
How absence is handled -- this is the mechanism we need:
  - `DifferentialSkipReason::MissingExecutable` -> a TYPED SKIP, never a failure.
  - test `sortformer_observation_missing_adapter_is_stable_skip` ... .expect("missing adapter is a skip").
  - the skip carries EVIDENCE: failure_stage, version_stdout_sha256, oracle_stdout_sha256, audio_sha256.
    A skip is a recorded observation, not silence.
  - `reason_matches_stage` asserts the skip reason matches the execution stage that produced it, so a
    skip cannot be mislabelled.
  - the known-bad is an IN-TREE specimen: the program name literal
    'franken-whisper-definitely-missing-oracle' is used to prove the skip path fires.
And fh O7 (source franken_whisper/src/differential_oracle.rs:41-46): pin an external oracle by ARTIFACT
HASH + BYTE LENGTH + TOOLCHAIN VERSIONS as compile-time constants the runner must ATTEST, not by a
version string. Live example: SORTFORMER_ORACLE_ARTIFACT_SHA256, ARTIFACT_BYTES = 471_367_680,
PYTHON_VERSION = '3.12.12', NEMO_VERSION, TORCH_VERSION '2.7.1', NUMPY_VERSION '2.4.6', plus a
CONTRACT_SHA256 over the canonical JSON of the whole contract. 'The adapter must independently hash its
local bytes and attest this exact value.'

PRIOR ART 2 -- THE TRAP IN 'JUST SKIP IT', and it is already a filed CRITICAL in another franken repo.
frankenscipy bead frankenscipy-ivg5 (status: closed), audited 2026-04-22 over
crates/fsci-conformance/src/lib.rs:run_differential_test: of 12 family runners, ELEVEN invoked ZERO
scipy oracle and instead compared Rust output against HAND-TYPED case.expected fields in the fixture --
a self-check wearing a differential's name. The twelfth (stats) wired the oracle path but defaulted to
python_oracle/scipy_stats_oracle.py, WHICH DOES NOT EXIST. Every runner still populated an
`oracle_status` field, so the report looked differential while nothing differential ran.
That is our exact defect with the failure mode inverted: composer-typed FAILS loudly on the missing
oracle; frankenscipy PASSED quietly. Loud is better, but the cure for loud must not be quiet.

O6 -- THE DECISION, three parts, all AUTONOMOUS (no gate is weakened, so O4's human approval is moot):
  (1) THE GATE IS RUST, ALWAYS RUNNABLE. Verified this already holds for composer-typed: with the python
      differential set aside, `cargo test -p composer-typed --test mutation --test planted_known_bads
      --lib` exits 0 with 8 passing Rust tests -- tests::every_named_rule_is_disableable,
      tests::crate_does_not_widen_admission, mutation_fail_closed_on_empty, mutation_bright_body_is_typed,
      mutation_dim_suggestion_is_not_typed, planted_typed_line_is_typed_through_binary,
      planted_dim_suggestion_is_free_through_binary, planted_real_capture_goes_through_binary. Mutation
      legs and planted in-tree specimens: exactly the franken shape. The crate is NOT untested without
      Python.
  (2) THE PYTHON DIFFERENTIAL BECOMES A DEV-ONLY COMPARISON THAT SKIPS, WITH EVIDENCE. Missing script or
      missing interpreter -> typed skip naming the reason and the stage, printed, never a pass and never a
      fail. Model it on DifferentialSkipReason. It must NOT be a Cargo dependency and MUST NOT run in the
      default `cargo test --workspace` path as a gate.
  (3) ANTI-VACUITY, so we do not become frankenscipy-ivg5: a skipped differential MUST NOT be reported as
      a passing differential, and no runner may silently fall back to comparing against hand-typed
      expected values while still advertising an oracle_status. If the oracle did not run, the report says
      DID NOT RUN.

WHAT CHANGES IN THIS BEAD'S ACCEPTANCE:
  - Replace the O1/O2 recommendation with O6.
  - Clause 3 ('the differential EVIDENCE survives') is AMENDED: the evidence that survives in-repo is the
      RUST gate (mutation + planted known-bads). The Python comparison is a development diagnostic whose
      value is realised when someone runs it deliberately with the oracle present -- and per O7, if we ever
      pin it, it is pinned by hash + byte length + toolchain constants, not a version string.
  - NEW clause 7: for each of the 9 crates, state which side is the AUTHORITY. Any crate where an external
      tool can block the Rust suite is not fixed.
  - NEW clause 8: the three PRODUCTION src/ callers (fleet-monitor src/main.rs:1190,
      pane-dispatch-ready src/main.rs:22, fast-dispatch src/main.rs:287) are a strictly worse case than the
      tests -- a SHIPPED binary that shells to python3 at runtime makes an external interpreter a RUNTIME
      dependency, which franken_whisper forbids outright. Route with
      omp-orchestrator-asupersync-subprocess-contract-gfb and state the removal plan per call site.

NO-CLAIM: reading two franken repos establishes the house pattern; it does not prove our 9 crates can each
be converted at the same cost. composer-typed is the cheapest case precisely BECAUSE it already has Rust
mutation + planted-known-bad coverage. A crate whose ONLY test is its python differential will need the
Rust gate WRITTEN, not merely uncovered -- measure that per crate before promising a date.

title: Josh decision: BuildShared retention gap holds build volume at 2.1GiB - reaper has nothing eligible
description:
TIER-3 ROUTE (Josh): the designated build volume /Volumes/BuildShared/cargo-targets (disk3s9) is at 2.1GiB free - below the cargo mint floor's 8% container rule. The fh reaper ran and retired NOTHING: 'every root holds a single current generation... this reaper retires only SUPERSEDED generations, so it cannot act on this store at all. That is a retention-policy gap, not a transient shortfall' (measured 2026-09-01, receipt in the CARGO_MINT_CONTAINER_EXHAUSTED output).

WHY IT BLOCKS THE WAVE: the integrator cannot run the workspace suite (mint guard refuses), pushes are gated on a fresh workspace-green receipt, and per the wave contract only the integrator may run the suite - so the whole ring's commits (SilverWolf 0689154 + 4fc649a, BlueLantern 03d1324/974b05d/df1717b) sit local and unpushed.

OPTIONS FOR JOSH (any one unblocks the ring):
(a) Authorize an agent to clear current-generation build dirs of idle projects on disk3s9 (zeststream-cast et al) - two-person rule, needs your explicit yes and a named target list;
(b) Grow/repurpose another volume for build targets;
(c) Set CARGO_MINT_MIN_CONTAINER_PCT=3 for the integrator's ONE suite run (the wrapper documents this override as the sanctioned mechanism, 'expires with the shell that set it') - lowest risk, unblocks today, leaves the floor default intact.

NO-CLAIM from SilverWolf: I will not delete build generations or override the floor without your explicit call. Bead omp-orchestrator-zot closed WONTFIX documents why the floor itself is correct.
close_reason: DONE - unblocked without any Josh decision, floor override, or deletion: option (d) existed in the registered-roots file all along. /Volumes/ZestData/zeststream-offload-20260609/build-cache/cargo-targets is a REGISTERED reaper-visible root (registered 2026-08-25, demoted from default only when builds moved to BuildFH) on the disk7 container = 299.9GiB free of 2.1TB = 14.05%, ABOVE the 8% mint floor (disk3's container sits at 67.1GiB/994.7GiB = 6.7% which is why every disk3 target - BuildShared, BuildFH, BuildCast, /tmp - fails the same guard). Measured end-to-end tonight: FRANKEN_CARGO_TARGET_ROOT=<that root> -> lane collapses to session-omp-orchestrator on ZestData -> mint guard exit=0 -> real compile + receiver-receipt 18/18 on the lane. Exact integrator command handed to BlueLantern via pane receipt (FRANKEN_CARGO_TARGET_ROOT=... cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast; no CARGO_MINT override needed). The Josh-Review pending decision file is superseded - left in place (dcg guards the tree from agent moves); archiving it is a clerk action on read. DISPOSITION NOTES: options a/c were never needed; zot's WONTFIX (floor math correct) stands; the retention-policy gap on disk3 remains real but no longer blocks the wave. NO-CLAIM: this bead unblocks the suite; it does not run it (integrator-only) and does not reclaim disk3 space.

title: GATE CENSUS IS CROSS-REPO BLIND: a hardcoded list of omp-owned crates becomes BLOCKING rows for any served repo, so dispatch can never resume there
description:
## WHAT
`derived_positive_control` fixed the hardcoded CANARY (uds-k0i6, landed and confirmed live). The
same hardcoded-membership bug survives one method over: `COVERAGE_WAVE_OUTPUT_CRATES` is a const
list of **omp-orchestrator's own crate names**, and every entry is pushed as a **Blocking** census
row against whatever `repo_root` the supervisor is serving. Serving any other repo, those crates
are absent, so `unwired_gates()` is permanently non-empty and `decide()` returns `GateUnwired` on
its FIRST check -- the branch documented as UNREACHABLE-AROUND, after which nothing may dispatch.

    lib.rs:540  pub const COVERAGE_WAVE_OUTPUT_CRATES: &[&str] = &[ ... "omp-orchestrator",
                "omp-types", "pane-dispatch-fence", "tick-monitor" ];
    lib.rs:894  for crate_name in COVERAGE_WAVE_OUTPUT_CRATES {
    lib.rs:902      disposition: CensusDisposition::Blocking,

The comment at `lib.rs:905` immediately below that loop reads
`===== MEMBERSHIP IS DERIVED, NOT LISTED =====` and records `leht`'s 2026-09-02 measurement that a
hand-written list produced 25 rows against 65 crates. The derivation was applied to the loop BELOW
the banner; the coverage-wave loop ABOVE it is still the hand-written list. This is the repo's own
principle with one remaining exception, not a new idea.

## MEASURED 2026-09-06 (SageCastle), production `census_gates`, run ON THIS HOST
| served repo | positive control | BLOCKING_UNWIRED |
|---|---|---:|
| omp-orchestrator | `Some("worker-oracle-gate")` | **0** |
| uds | `Some("uds-drift")` | **17** |
| control-plane | `Some("fleet-composite")` | **12** |

uds's 17 include `finding-dispatch`, `omp-types`, `omp-orchestrator`, `tick-monitor`,
`loop-queue-filter`, `pane-dispatch-fence`, `installer`, `kernel-only-operator-hook` -- crates uds
does not contain and will never contain. So `uds-k0i6`'s acceptance clause "routes trigger repair
before dispatch resumes" is UNSATISFIABLE for uds: there is no trigger to repair for a gate the
served repo does not own.

The positive control passing everywhere is the uds-k0i6 fix working, confirmed live. It is not
sufficient, because `positive_control_passes()` and `unwired_gates()` are separate legs and only
the first was derived.

## CORROBORATION, and the live instance
`omp-orchestrator-8kel` measured this on 2026-09-05 with `--repo uds`: ~70 respawns in 20 minutes,
every generation printing `SUPERVISOR_REFUSED GATE_UNWIRED unwired=POSITIVE_CONTROL_FAILED:
no-shell-gate must be reachable`. That bead owns the RESIDENT'S REACTION to a refusal (exit vs

served repo it refused is itself worth a row.

Only `GAP-S1-02` is executable as written.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. Every `ASSUME_REVERSIBLY` row in `DISPOSITIONS.toml` gains a `falsifier` KEY (not prose inside `reason`) holding a command or an observable file state.
2. `maturity0/S*.toml`'s `unknowns[]` schema gains a `falsifier` field, required when `disposition = "ASSUME_REVERSIBLY"`.

title: The R3 unknown-detector is `resolution == ""`, so 20 still-open wave rows (4 blockers) reading 'remaining;' are invisible to the register
description:
WHAT: `docs/plan/flow/unknowns/DISPOSITIONS.toml` harvests wave disagreements by empty resolution string. A row whose resolution reads `"remaining; selection feedback is cyclic and not yet unrolled"` is non-empty, so it is read as RESOLVED and never dispositioned. 20 unresolved disagreements -- 4 of them severity `blocker` -- are therefore outside R3 entirely.

WHY (measured 2026-09-05 by AtlasArcPass3, TOML-parsed, not grepped):
- 160 `[[disagreement]]` rows across `docs/plan/flow/waves/{wave-1,wave-2}/*.toml`. All 160 carry a `resolution` key (0 missing).
- Empty resolution: **84**. `DISPOSITIONS.toml` has exactly **84** `surface = "wave.disagreement.resolution"` rows and the (file, field) key sets match with **0 symmetric difference** -- so the detector is provably `resolution == ""` and nothing else.
- Non-empty but still open: **20**, none present in `DISPOSITIONS.toml`. Prefixes: `remaining` x15, `escalated:` x2, `accepted: row stays open` x2, `accepted AND STILL OPEN` x1. Severities: 4 `blocker`, 15 `major`, 1 `major`.

- `escalated` and `remaining` are not R3 dispositions. R3 (`SKILL.md:111`) names "Open", "TBD", "investigate", "decide later" as invalid alone; `remaining` and `escalated: row stays open` are the same class of non-disposition.
- SECOND, INDEPENDENT INSTRUMENT DEFECT, and it corrects the record: `docs/plan/flow/unknowns/CENSUS.json:7` explains its own 84-vs-72 discrepancy as `"72 (undercounts missing-key rows)"`. **There are zero missing-key rows.** The real cause is 12 rows that write the empty resolution with SINGLE quotes (`resolution = ''`), all in `wave-1/SilverWolf-*.toml` (S1 x2, S2, S3, S4, S5a, S5b x2, S7 x2, S8 x2). A regex for `resolution = ""` returns 72; a TOML parser returns 84. - Timing rules out staleness as the explanation: all five files holding the 20 rows were last written 2026-09-03 <= 12:32, and `DISPOSITIONS.toml` landed at `ec2f73b` 15:26:39. The rows were on disk ~3 hours before the census ran. The detector skipped them.

title: 10 missing-representation instruments today (busy=dead, unasked=nonexistent, timed-out=unreachable, ungraded=closed): census + lint refusing bool/Option verdicts in gate crates
description:

title: PR-L1: pane-dispatch-ready is blind to the wedge marker; wedged and idle verdicts are identical
description:
## WHAT

`pane-dispatch-ready` — the readiness authority — is blind to the wedge marker
`Press up to edit queued messages`. A wedged pane and an idle pane produce a **byte-identical
verdict line** from `classify`, so a caller that trusts readiness dispatches into a pane that
accepted the packet and will never submit it.

Measured by `l1_a_wedged_pane_still_classifies_free_in_this_crate`, which asserts the two
verdicts are equal today, and by `l1_the_wedge_marker_is_detected_by_three_other_crates`.

## WHY

The marker IS detected — three times, in three other crates:

| crate | site |
|---|---|
| `fast-dispatch` | `src/lib.rs:321` |
| `fleet-monitor` | `src/lib.rs:157` |
| `tick-monitor` | `src/lib.rs:357` |

So this is not "the fleet is blind"; it is "the classifier whose only job is *can this pane
SAFELY receive a dispatch* does not ask the one question that distinguishes a pane that will
process work from one that will park it". `AGENTS.md:419` already states the failure:
*"A wedged pane accepts a packet, parks it at `Press up to edit queued messages`, and never
submits it."* Every surface `classify` reads still says free — an agent is rendering, no busy
marker in the 6-line tail, the buffer is unchanged, and the `π` prompt is present.

Scope matters here: a wrong reading of this finding sends someone to build a detector that
already ships three times over. The fix is to consult one, not to write a fourth.

## ACCEPTANCE

`run X, expect Y`:

1. `classify` must return a state that is NOT `Free` for a capture containing the marker. Prefer
   a named state over folding it into `Busy`: a wedged pane is not working, and an operator's
   action is to submit or clear the queued message, not to wait. If a new state is added, extend
   `PaneDispatchReadyState::{as_str,parse}` and the pipe-line round-trip in the same commit.
2. `cargo test -p pane-dispatch-ready --test readiness_contract` — the pinned legs
   `l1_a_wedged_pane_still_classifies_free_in_this_crate` and
   `l1_the_wedge_marker_is_detected_by_three_other_crates` go RED and must be rewritten to
   assert the new behaviour, with `docs/contracts/pane_readiness_contract.md` §PR-L1 updated in
   the same commit. Their failure is the signal the fix landed.
3. Known-GOOD arm must stay green: `l1_…` control asserts an idle pane is still `Free`. A
   detector that pins every pane non-free is a worse defect than the blindness.
4. The differential oracle must agree: `crates/pane-dispatch-ready/tests/differential.rs`
   compares against the shell original, so either the shell gains the same clause or the
   divergence is declared with a reason in that test.

Proven reachable at authoring time: adding the marker to `BUSY_RE` (single anchor asserted)
flipped both pinned legs RED — 9 passed / 2 failed — then a byte-identical restore
(sha256 `1409f2de20f241b4282544870633be5f57ff5fd643bc37921a47b07774ce8837`) returned 11 passed.

## NOT IN SCOPE

The 10-second motion window (`omp-orchestrator-readiness-l3-motion-window-53l`) and any change
to `crates/refill-idle-panes`, which another agent owns.

## NO-CLAIM

Detecting the marker does not prove a pane is healthy when the marker is absent. This closes ONE
named blindness; `safe_to_dispatch` still is not liveness, and a pane can be wedged in ways that
render no footer at all — a frozen render, a dead PTY, an unanswered approval dialog. Each needs
its own evidence.

title: PR-L3: readiness confirms FREE over a 10s window against a 75s floor
description:
## WHAT

`pane-dispatch-ready` confirms a provisional FREE with a second capture taken
**`DEFAULT_MOTION_SECS = 10`** seconds later (`crates/pane-dispatch-ready/src/lib.rs:36`, slept
at `src/main.rs:304`). The repo's own two-capture floor is **75 seconds**:

| authority | constant | value |
|---|---|---|
| `pane-truth` | `TWO_CAPTURE_MIN_SECS: i64` | **75** (`src/lib.rs:39`) |
| `tick-monitor` | `MIN_GAP_SECS: u64` | **75** (`src/lib.rs:490`) |
| `docs/contracts/pane_observation_contract.md` | `PO-L1` | two captures **≥75s** apart |
| `pane-dispatch-ready` | `DEFAULT_MOTION_SECS: u64` | **10** |

So readiness runs its motion check at **1/7.5 of the required interval**, and an unchanged buffer
over 10 seconds is what lets FREE stand.

## WHY

The floor is not arbitrary and `tick-monitor/src/lib.rs:486` records why:
*"75s, not 30s: measured, a lane deep in a long tool call has a STATIC timer"*. A pane inside a
single long tool call renders nothing for far more than 10 seconds. Its buffer is unchanged, so
`confirm_free` keeps the free read and the pane is dispatched into while it is working.

Note the asymmetry, because it decides how bad this is: `buffer_changed == true` yields BUSY,
which is fail-closed and safe at any window. The unsafe direction is UNCHANGED-over-10s reading
as idle. Shortening the window cannot produce a false BUSY; it produces a false FREE, which is
exactly the dispatch-into-working-pane failure.

## ACCEPTANCE

`run X, expect Y`:

1. Raise the window to at least 75 seconds, or make readiness CONSUME a `pane-truth` /
   `tick-monitor` observation instead of taking its own second capture. The second option is
   preferable — `AGENTS.md` KERNEL-ONLY says a capability a kernel provides must not be
   handrolled, and both kernels already carry the floor and the timer-vs-hash comparison.
2. `cargo test -p pane-dispatch-ready --test readiness_contract` — the pinned leg
   `l3_this_crates_motion_window_is_below_the_75_second_floor` goes RED naming the new value, and
   `docs/contracts/pane_readiness_contract.md` §PR-L3 must be updated in the same commit.
3. State the latency cost in the commit. A 75-second confirmation per pane is 7.5x the current
   wait, and a dispatcher that scans N panes serially pays it N times. If the answer is to consume
   an existing observation rather than sleep, that cost is zero — which is the argument for
   option 1's second form.
4. `BUFFER_MOTION_SECONDS` (`src/main.rs:266`) must not be able to lower the window below the
   floor. An env override that reintroduces the defect is the same shape as a lint nothing denies.

Proven reachable at authoring time: setting `DEFAULT_MOTION_SECS = 75` (single site asserted)
flipped the pinned leg RED — 10 passed / 1 failed — then a byte-identical restore
(sha256 `1409f2de20f241b4282544870633be5f57ff5fd643bc37921a47b07774ce8837`) returned 11 passed.

## NOT IN SCOPE

The wedge blindness (`omp-orchestrator-readiness-l1-wedge-blind-4ay`), and any change to
`crates/refill-idle-panes` or `crates/omp-types`.

## NO-CLAIM

A 75-second window does not make an unchanged buffer proof of idleness — it makes it the
evidence grade `pane_observation_contract` already defines, no stronger. A pane can hold a
static render for minutes; the floor raises the bar, it does not establish liveness. And nothing
here proves the callers of this crate wait for the confirmation rather than using the first
verdict.

title: P1: the green receipt carries no writer identity — the verifying gate cannot tell which build wrote it
description:
## WHAT

`.flywheel/workspace-green.receipt` is shared mutable state with MULTIPLE WRITERS, and
the strong gate trusts a receipt written by a weaker one. Measured 2026-09-02, inside one
session:

- `recorded_at_unix` moved `1788313519` -> `1788315601` with no action by the agent
  holding the file open.
- The newer body still carries NO `toolchain_channel` and NO `rustc_commit`, i.e. it was
  written by a build of `pre-push-gate` that predates fa7d9a4 — while
  `.git/hooks/pre-push` had already been rebuilt and reinstalled at 20:23 and writes both
  fields.
- Therefore a stale copy of the binary is still writing receipts. Most likely
  `~/.local/bin/pre-push-gate` from an earlier `installer` run; `target/debug/` and
  `target/release/` were both rebuilt, so neither is the writer.

This is the `pane-truth` class recorded in AGENTS.md, verbatim: a binary installed from
elsewhere under a name this repo documents, producing a verdict that can never match. It
is worse here, because the stale copy does not merely disagree — it writes a WEAKER
receipt, and the strong gate accepts any receipt whose fields it can parse.

## WHY — P0

Every hardening landed in fa7d9a4 is one stale binary away from silent bypass. The new
verify path refuses a receipt with no `rustc_commit` (leg
`refuses_a_receipt_that_records_no_compiler`), so TODAY the stale writer's output is
caught. That is luck, not design: the moment a stale copy exists that writes the field
with a different value, or a future field is added, the ordering flips and the strong gate
reads a weak claim as a strong one. The gate has no way to tell whose receipt it is
reading.

newest tracked source changed, and they did it with the compiler CI uses." It cannot prove
the somebody was a build that implements the checks the gate believes it implements.

- [ ] The receipt stamps its writer's identity: `writer_build_id=<OMP_BUILD_ID>` (already
      derived in `crates/omp-orchestrator/build.rs` — `git` HEAD sha plus `-dirty`), and
      verify REFUSES a receipt whose `writer_build_id` it cannot match against the
      running binary's own `OMP_BUILD_ID`.
- [ ] A fires-on-known-bad leg in `crates/no-shell-gate/tests/toolchain_parity.rs`:
      receipt stamped with a foreign/absent `writer_build_id` -> exit 1 naming the writer
      mismatch. Observed RED before the fix.
- [ ] The stale writer is located and removed or upgraded. Start with
      `shasum -a 256 ~/.local/bin/pre-push-gate .git/hooks/pre-push target/release/pre-push-gate`
      and `installer --check`, which is supposed to catch exactly this drift and did not
      report it.
- [ ] `hook_freshness` grows a leg for `~/.local/bin/pre-push-gate` if the installer owns
      that path — the pre-push hook itself had NO freshness leg until fa7d9a4 added one,
      and the installed-copy door is still unwatched.

## NO-CLAIM

The stale writer was inferred from the receipt body, not caught in the act — no `lsof`,
no fs audit, and no sha comparison of the candidate copies was run. `~/.local/bin/` is
the leading hypothesis, not a measurement. Whoever picks this up should identify the
writer before deleting anything.

Nor does the proposed `writer_build_id` fix make the receipt trustworthy: the
failing-suite count remains the caller's assertion, exactly as documented in
`pre-push-gate.rs`. This bead closes the "which binary wrote it" hole only.

comments.text:
docs(receiver-receipt): close the contract's measured gaps + a Rust validator [mutation-verified]

omp-orchestrator-receiver-receipt-contract-pwm.

## The contract already existed and already passed its own validator

`docs/contracts/receiver_receipt_contract.md`, 13,013 bytes, landed `934e196`. Its
pasteable command re-ran GREEN on all nine checks. So this is a gap-close, not a
write — and the gaps are the interesting part, because **a validator that passes
while its document is wrong is the defect, not the document.**

## GAP 1: it said SIX public types and there are SEVEN

`AckWaitVerdict` landed **the same day** in `d4e8453` (bead `iis6`, mine). The
document was stale within hours of being written, and its validator could not see
that because **the shape had not changed — only the world had.**

That is `NUMBERS.toml`'s thesis one document over: *a figure CORRECT WHEN WRITTEN and
wrong now, because the repo moved under it.*

## GAP 2: it cross-checked PO-L1 only

The acceptance asks for L1-L5 against `pane_observation_contract`. Three references
existed, all to `PO-L1-TWO-CAPTURE-DOMINANCE`. Added a cross-check table mapping every
law in both directions, each row stating the RELATIONSHIP rather than asserting
agreement:

* `RR-L1` is **stricter** than `PO-L1` — PO takes timer **or** hash; `ReceiptConfirmed`
  needs the transition-appropriate timer **and** changed content.
* `RR-L4` is `PO-L2` in receipt vocabulary — both make absence inhabited.
* `RR-L5` **consumes** `PO-L3`'s last-line rule and adds the timer-unit prohibition.
* `RR-L2`/`RR-L6` **inherit** `PO-L4` — one `PaneState` is one value, so no verdict
  claims both.
* `RR-L3` is `PO-L5`'s separation on another axis — composer arrival is not delivery.

**Unmapped in both directions, stated rather than implied:** PO has no counterpart for
`RR-L2`'s 30-second freshness bound, and this contract has no counterpart for PO's
evidence-ordering section.

## GAP 3: the pasteable command was a `python3` heredoc

In a repository whose one rule is *"No `.sh`. No `.py`."* The extension gate only sees
FILES, so a heredoc carried the same payload in a shape the gate cannot see. Every
sibling contract with a validator has a Rust one (`finding_contract.rs`,
`readiness_contract.rs`).

Replaced with `cargo test -p receiver-receipt --test receipt_contract`, and the new
suite **checks doc-to-SOURCE agreement rather than document shape**: every named enum
exists, the stated count equals `pub enum` declarations, and both quoted constants
still hold their quoted values.

## GAP 4: the bead names six types and the document named none of them

It described its RR-* IDs and never the Rust types. Added a Types table naming all
seven with the question each answers and **its inhabited failure state** — every one
has an inhabited unknown, which is the shared design rule and the reason
`AckWaitVerdict` exists at all.

## Also added: RR-L6-ACK-WAIT-DISCRIMINATES

The contract had no law for the surface I added this morning. States that exactly one
`AckWaitVerdict` arm may interrupt a human, that the discriminator is timer advance
across the 75-second floor rather than elapsed time, and that `RECEIPT_TIMEOUT` at 30s
is BELOW that floor — the old bound could not answer the question in principle.

## INSTANCE NINE, AND IT WAS MINE TWICE IN ONE SECTION

Two legs failed on **my own prose**:

* the section slicer matched `## Non-Coverage` inside my sentence *explaining that
  `## Non-Coverage` appears inside a code block*;
* the forbidden-token check found `python3` inside my sentence saying the payload
  USED to be `python3`.

Third consecutive time the sentence describing a defect contained the defect —
after `path-literal-guard` and `crates_emitting` today. **The cure is structural, not
verbal**, exactly as AGENTS.md census item 5 now says: `section_body` anchors on
`\n## <heading>\n` so only a real heading matches, and the token check reads the
FENCED BLOCK rather than the prose about it. I fixed the checker, not the prose,
because the prose is correct and a checker that cannot read structure will fail on
the next honest sentence too.

## Mutations — all five bite; doc and source restores byte-identical

```
M1 restore "six public types"        -> doc-vs-source leg RED   (the drift that shipped)
M2 python payload back in the block  -> validation-command leg RED
M3 drop one PO law from the table    -> cross-check leg RED
M4 cite a path that does not exist   -> cited-paths leg RED
M5 SOURCE moves: 75s floor -> 76s    -> doc-vs-source leg RED
```

**M5 is the one worth having.** It mutates the SOURCE, not the document, and the
document's validator goes red — which is what "the source is the authority" has to
mean to be enforceable.

## Verification

```
cargo test -p receiver-receipt              -> 35 + 7, 0 failed
cargo clippy -p receiver-receipt --all-targets -> 0 rows in my files
contract: 18,473 bytes (<= 25,000) | 23 stable RR- ids | 5 of 5 PO laws | 7 of 7 types named
```

Cleared four clippy rows that were my own debt from `iis6` this morning: two unused
imports, a `super::*` shadowed by the explicit import beside it, and a const-drift
assertion now `allow`ed with the reason stated.

## NO-CLAIM

* **The contract still does not repair the classifier**, per the acceptance: gaps are
  identified, not fixed. `ReceiptVerdict` carries no capture interval,
  `escalate_non_delivery` can be called with one observation, and the crate has no
  local `Obscured` variant. All three remain named implementation gaps.
* **The validator checks agreement, not correctness.** It proves the document's claims
  about the source are current; it cannot prove a law is mechanically enforced. The
  NO-CLAIM section says the same thing and is now asserted to be substantive rather
  than a heading over nothing.
* The cited-path leg proves paths EXIST, not that the line numbers still point at what
  the document says they do — four `lib.rs:NNN` test citations were removed rather
  than left unverifiable, because a line number is the fastest-drifting citation there
  is.

---

comments.text:
fix(scratch): remove the unattributed temp fallback for durable markers [mutation-verified]

omp-orchestrator-remove-unattributed-scratch-fallback-7bp.

## The fallback, and why announcing it was not enough

`spine_demo` resolved its durable pending-dispatch marker through `scratch-home` and
fell back to `std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("ack-spine-demo-{pid}"))` whenever the
scratch root could not be resolved, printing a stderr line saying so. The comment
argued the fallback was the lesser evil: *"a demo that refuses to run because `$HOME`
is unusual is worse than one that runs unattributed and announces it."*

**That is wrong, and mechanically rather than stylistically.** A marker under
`$TMPDIR` is **unattributable** — nothing in or beside the path says which session,
pane or agent owns it, so `ScratchRoot::reap` cannot classify it at all;
**unreapable** — the reaper cannot tell a live marker from an abandoned one, and
`scratch-home`'s contract makes missing owner metadata `UNKNOWN` and explicitly NOT
auto-reapable; and **gone on reboot**, which is the opposite of durable.

**The announcement tells the wrong audience.** A stderr line is read by a human; the
file is reaped by a program. Same shape as every other loud-but-unread signal
measured here — 178 unread ticks, a refusal printed 29 times, a workflow with no
runner.

## Fail closed, with a named refusal

`durable_pending_path(session, agent, job, owner)` returns
`Result<PathBuf, String>` and there is no fallback. Proven live:

```
$ env -u HOME ack-spine --selftest
ACK_SPINE_SCRATCH_UNAVAILABLE reason=root_unresolved detail=I/O at $HOME: HOME is unset
  owner=josh next_action=set-HOME -- refusing to write a durable marker to an
  unattributed temp path that no reaper can own
exit 1
```

Second refusal for an unresolvable job dir: `reason=job_uncreatable`.

**Failing closed here does not relocate the defect**, checked before relying on it:
`scratch-home`'s own `temp_dir` use is confined to its `#[cfg(test)]` module, and
`ScratchRoot::default` already refuses an unset `HOME` rather than guessing.

## The known-good path, and the owner metadata that is the whole point

```
$ ack-spine --spine-demo
$ cat ~/.local/state/zeststream/scratch/omp-orchestrator/ack-spine/spine-demo/.owner.json
{"schema":1,"session":"omp-orchestrator","pane_or_agent":"ack-spine","job":"spine-demo","owner":"josh"}
```

That file is what a temp path can never carry, and it is why the reaper can act.

## A ONE-SPECIMEN KNOWN-BAD PROVED NOTHING — MEASURED

`--selftest` now asserts the invariant, per the acceptance. The first version planted
a single temp path, and **M2 and M3 both stayed GREEN**: each guard individually is
redundant for that specimen, because the scratch-root check rejects a temp path too.
A leg that both guards satisfy cannot attribute either.

That is the `any()`-over-alternatives defect in sibling form, third instance today.
Fixed with **one specimen per guard**:

* **A** — under the temp root. Both guards reject it, so the leg asserts the
  **temp-specific diagnostic** (`temp_root=`). That is what the temp guard is for:
  admission is subsumed by the scratch-root check, and only the temp guard can tell
  an operator WHICH defect this is.
* **B** — `/ack-spine-known-bad-foreign`: neither under temp nor under the scratch
  root, so **only** the scratch-root requirement can reject it.

Built from the filesystem root rather than a home directory, because a hardcoded
`/Users/<name>` literal is what `path-literal-guard` refuses and a specimen that
exists on one machine is not a specimen.

## Mutations — all four bite, each attributably; restore byte-identical

```
M1 resolve the path to temp_dir           -> ACK_SPINE_DURABLE_PATH_UNOWNED, selftest exit 1
M2 disable the temp-prefix guard          -> specimen A's REASON leg fails (wrong diagnostic)
M3 drop the scratch-root requirement      -> specimen B ADMITTED, selftest exit 1
M4 restore the fallback outright          -> ACK_SPINE_DURABLE_PATH_UNOWNED, selftest exit 1
```

M1 is the mutation the acceptance names. M2 and M3 exist because the first attempt at
them did not bite.

## ANTI-VACUITY

Neither planted path may exist on disk: a check must never be satisfied by having
created the very file it forbids. And no `ack-spine-demo-*` marker remains anywhere
under `$TMPDIR` or `/private/tmp` — the fallback left nothing behind and can no
longer create anything.

## Verification

```
ack-spine --selftest                  -> PASS, exit 0, marker root under the scratch home
env -u HOME ack-spine --selftest      -> named refusal, exit 1
cargo test -p ack-spine               -> 33/6/6/10/6/6, 0 failed
cargo clippy -p ack-spine --all-targets -> 0 rows in main.rs
```

## NO-CLAIM

* **The bead cites `main.rs:184-197`; the site is now `226-237`** because I added the
  `--complete` subcommand to this file earlier today (`c39715c`). The citation
  drifted under its own bead, which is the line-number fragility I removed four
  citations for in `pwm` an hour ago.
* **`spine_demo` is a demo subcommand, not a production dispatch path.** The bead
  calls it "the production caller"; it is the only caller of `scratch-home` and the
  marker it writes is genuinely durable, so the defect was real — but no supervisor
  tick reaches this code.
* **Three `temp_dir` uses remain in `crates/ack-spine/src/heartbeat.rs`** at lines
  166/191/205. All three are inside `#[cfg(test)]` (module opens at 143) and write
  ephemeral test files, not durable markers. **Out of scope and left alone**, but they
  are not removed and this commit does not make the crate temp-free.
* The workspace has **72 `env::temp_dir()` occurrences across 43 files**. This bead
  fixes one. Nothing here surveys the rest for durability.

---

title: Escalate recurring idle-capacity incident: 0 dispatchable panes with 375 ready beads

4. Mutation test: flip the streak threshold from 3 to 4 (or invert the `dispatchable_count == 0` predicate) and show the known-bad test goes RED with the specific assertion message. Restore the file byte-identically; record `sha256` of the file before mutation and after restore in the bead comment and assert equality.

The observation *timing* (three consecutive ticks) may be driven by a fixture clock/tick injector. State in the bead comment which values were live-measured with the command used.

8. Open sub-item: the description cites "idle capacity persisted for 178 ticks" but does not specify a bound on time-to-escalate.
