title: P1: am file_reservations reserve exits 0 on REFUSAL with granted:[] -- exit code and jq truthiness both report success, so two agents can edit one file
description: MEASURED 2026-09-06 by pane 1 while trying to determine whether an expired lease had freed crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs. TWO INDEPENDENT SIGNALS BOTH REPORT SUCCESS ON A REFUSAL. Measured verbatim: 'am file_reservations reserve users-josh-developer-omp-orchestrator PlumTiger crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs --exclusive' redirected to a file, exit code captured with no pipe -> TRUE EXIT 0. The payload is '{ "granted": [], "conflicts": [ { "path": "crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs", "holders": [ { "agent": "CloudyGrove", ... } ] } ] }'. So the reservation was REFUSED -- granted is empty and conflicts names the holder -- while the process exit code is 0. DEFECT 1, the tool's: exit 0 on a refused exclusive reservation. A caller that branches on exit status believes it holds the lease. That is the inverse of omp-orchestrator-watch-exit-is-a-verdict-i3r6, where inbox-monitor exits NONZERO on a successful settle; here a refusal exits ZERO. Both are the same underlying fault -- the exit code carrying a status it cannot express -- and they fail in opposite directions, which means no single convention about exit codes is safe across this CLI. DEFECT 2, MINE, and it is the one that nearly caused damage: my probe was 'am ... | jq -r "if .granted then \"RESERVED\" else \"REFUSED\" end"'. IN JQ AN EMPTY ARRAY IS TRUTHY, so 'if .granted' takes the true branch when granted is []. My probe printed 'RESERVED for pane1' on a refusal. I was one step from editing main.rs while CloudyGrove -- a live agent on a different harness, opencode/gpt-5.6-luna, last active 11m -- held an exclusive lease on it. The only thing that stopped me was noticing an unexplained 'Command exited with code 5' from the surrounding pipeline and re-measuring instead of proceeding. WHY BOTH TOGETHER ARE WORSE THAN EITHER: the natural defensive move against a truthiness bug is to check the exit code, and the natural defensive move against a bad exit code is to parse the JSON. Here BOTH default paths report success. A caller must specifically test the LENGTH of granted -- 'len(granted) > 0' -- and nothing in the surface suggests that. This is the class AGENTS.md records as instruments manufacturing their own reading, and it is the twenty-first instance tonight and the fifth of mine. OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE ALREADY OBSERVED: pane4-%9 reported RANK_MOVED=yes for absorbing rank_ready into loop-queue-filter, but rank_ready still exists in main.rs -- grep counts 1 in each -- because %9 correctly could not edit main.rs under this same lease. So the function is COPIED, not moved, and the LIVE BINARY uses main.rs's copy. Two selector implementations that can drift, with the unused one being the tested one. That is tracked as omp-orchestrator-2ceb.1 and is a direct downstream cost of the lease, not of %9's work. ACCEPTANCE: 1. A refused reservation exits NONZERO, or the documented contract states plainly that exit status is not a success signal and callers must test len(granted). 2. Known-bad leg: reserving a path already held exclusively by another agent must be distinguishable from a grant by BOTH exit code and a simple truthiness read -- proven by taking a lease as agent A and attempting it as agent B. 3. Known-good leg: a genuine grant remains distinguishable, so the fix is not 'always fail'. 4. Anti-vacuity: an empty conflicts array with an empty granted array is an ERROR -- neither granted nor refused is not an outcome. 5. AGENTS.md gains a line: reservation success is len(granted) > 0; neither exit code nor jq truthiness is admissible. NO-CLAIM: this establishes the exit code and payload for one refused reservation and the jq truthiness behaviour. It does not establish the exit code on a successful grant -- I did not obtain one on this path, so 'exit 0 means nothing' is measured only for the refusal case -- and it makes no claim about whether any agent has actually edited a file under a falsely-believed lease.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Known-bad leg (live, not fixture): with agent A holding an exclusive lease on crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs, run `am file_reservations reserve <workspace> <agentB> crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs --exclusive` with output redirected to a file and exit status captured with NO pipe (`$?` from the bare command, not from a pipeline). Record: exit code, full JSON payload, and the output of `jq -r 'if .granted then "RESERVED" else "REFUSED" end'` on that payload. Required post-fix: exit code is NONZERO. The already-recorded 2026-09-06 measurement (exit 0, granted:[], conflicts[0].holders[0].agent == "CloudyGrove") is the pre-fix baseline ONLY — it is not evidence the fix works, because it was taken against the unfixed binary and against a holder (CloudyGrove, opencode/gpt-5.6-luna) that may no longer exist; the leg must be re-taken live with a lease this test itself creates and can prove it created.

2. Known-good leg (live): the same agent B reserves a path held by NO ONE, exclusive, same invocation shape. Must exit 0 AND emit `granted` with len > 0 AND `conflicts` empty. This leg failing means the fix degenerated to "always fail" and blocks the bead. Both legs must be run against the same binary, same build hash, recorded in the artifact.

3. Truthiness leg: for both legs above, record the literal stdout of the naive probe `jq -r 'if .granted then "RESERVED" else "REFUSED" end'`. Post-fix the refusal must NOT print "RESERVED". Acceptable ways: refusal payload omits `granted` entirely, or sets it to null, or the command emits no JSON success object on refusal. If `granted: []` is retained on refusal, the bead is not satisfied by exit code alone — the description's DEFECT 2 requires the truthiness path to also stop lying, or an explicit documented waiver naming DEFECT 2 as deferred and filed as its own bead ID.

4. Anti-vacuity, typed: a response with `len(granted) == 0 && len(conflicts) == 0` must produce a distinct typed error (nonzero exit, machine-readable error kind e.g. `INDETERMINATE_RESERVATION`), never exit 0 and never be silently treated as refusal. The verification harness must itself fail with a typed error if it collects zero reservation attempts, zero JSON payloads, or an unparseable payload — an empty scan is never a pass. Print the count of attempts made in the artifact.

5. Mutation proof: after the fix, revert the refusal-path exit-code line (or the granted-field emission) to its pre-fix behavior, re-run legs 1–3, and show the harness goes RED with the specific failing assertion named. Then restore byte-identically and prove it with a checksum: record `sha256sum` of every touched file before mutation and after restore, and paste both in the artifact; they must match exactly.

6. MEASURED live vs fixture: legs 1, 2, 3 and the checksum in 5 must be run live against the real `am` binary with a real lease held by a real second agent identity — no recorded fixtures, no mocked conflict payload. Only the anti-vacuity case in 4 (granted:[] + conflicts:[]) may be a fixture/injected payload if the real service cannot be forced into that state; if a fixture is used, say so explicitly and name the injection point.

7. Documentation: AGENTS.md gains a line stating verbatim that reservation success is `len(.granted) > 0`, and that neither exit code nor jq truthiness of `.granted` is admissible evidence of a grant. Cite the file:line of the added text. Also cross-reference omp-orchestrator-watch-exit-is-a-verdict-i3r6 as the opposite-direction instance of the same fault, with the conclusion that no single exit-code convention is safe across this CLI.

8. comments.text: THIRD FAULT ON THE SAME COMMAND, measured 2026-09-06 by pane 1 while answering a coordination question from pane4-%9. am file_reservations reserve emits JSON FOLLOWED BY A HUMAN SENTENCE on the same stream: '{ "granted": [], "conflicts": [ ... ] }' and then '1 conflict(s) detected -- conflicting reservations were not created.' Consequence, verbatim: json.load on that output dies with 'json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Extra data: line 17 column 1 (char 334)'. So the surface LOOKS like JSON, is documented-by-appearance as JSON, and is not parseable as JSON. THAT MAKES THREE INDEPENDENT WAYS THIS ONE COMMAND MISLEADS A CALLER: (1) it exits 0 on REFUSAL, so the exit code reports success; (2) its refusal payload is 'granted: []', and an empty array is TRUTHY in jq, so 'if .granted then' takes the success branch; (3) its output is JSON plus trailing prose, so a strict parser fails on a well-formed refusal. Each of the three defeats a DIFFERENT defensive habit: checking the exit code, parsing the payload with jq, and parsing the payload strictly. A caller has to know all three to read this command correctly, and nothing in the surface says so. THE CORRECT READ, for the record: strip trailing non-JSON lines, parse, then test len(granted) > 0. title: P0: claim_bead_for_supervisor returns Ok with an EMPTY claim_owner for a closed bead (main.rs:1690-1695), surfacing 3 layers later as MISSING_RECEIVER_AGENT
description: MEASURED 2026-09-06 by pane 1 from live rows at tick=29, immediately after closing omp-orchestrator-eg0m. SEVENTH TWO-AUTHORITY SPLIT OF THE SESSION, and it is the direct sibling of nkhq which I closed two hours ago. WHAT nkhq FIXED: LifecycleLedger::receiver_verified_candidates at crates/ntm-fleet-monitor/src/bead_lifecycle/ledger.rs:339-344 now reads tracker statuses and drops any candidate not Some("open" | "in_progress"). I verified that live -- after closing eg0m the grading candidate set measured ZERO. WHAT IT DID NOT FIX: a SECOND selection source. At tick=29, with the candidate set empty, the loop dispatched eg0m anyway and refused with 'DISPATCH_BLOCKED bead=omp-orchestrator-eg0m reason=CLAIM_REQUIRED ... status=closed assignee=WildStone'. So a closed bead was re-selected by a path the producer filter does not govern. THE SOURCE IS THE UNRESOLVED-DISPATCH RETRY. The bead's own lifecycle ledger carries 18 rows for eg0m and the tail alternates 'selected' and 'dispatch_receipt/dispatched' -- the last event being an unresolved 'dispatched'. The loop's own message named the place to look: next_action=inspect_dispatch_ledger. So an in-flight dispatch that never resolved keeps the bead in a retry queue, and that queue is filtered by nothing. Same shape as nkhq exactly: we filtered the producer we knew about and left its sibling unguarded. BOTH OFFERED REMEDIES CORRUPT STATE, and this is the part that matters most. Verbatim from the row: 'complete_claim=br update omp-orchestrator-eg0m --assignee WildStone --status in_progress' and 'release_fully=br update omp-orchestrator-eg0m --assignee "" --status open'. It calls them mutually_exclusive and offers no third. eg0m is CLOSED after an independent non-author grade citing re-executed evidence. The first remedy REOPENS graded work as in_progress; the second REOPENS it as open. An operator following either instruction destroys a completed grade -- and the instruction is emitted by the system itself, which makes it worse than silence. THE CORRECT REMEDY EXISTS AND IS NOT OFFERED: clear the assignee and LEAVE THE STATUS CLOSED. I did exactly that -- 'br update omp-orchestrator-eg0m --assignee ""' with no --status -- and read it back: status=closed, assignee empty. The claim check can no longer match, the grade survives, and nothing was reopened. The remedy menu is missing the only non-destructive option. THIS IS A REMEDY-ADVICE DEFECT, WHICH IS A CLASS WE HAVE NOT NAMED BEFORE. Every prior finding tonight was about a wrong VERDICT. This is a correct refusal -- CLAIM_REQUIRED is right, a closed bead should not dispatch -- paired with wrong ADVICE. AGENTS.md records the adjacent shape at main.rs:2465-2467: 'a discrimination that explicitly does not owe a human still printed the instruction to fetch one. Two contradictory directives in a single line, and the operator-facing half was the wrong one.' Same defect, different field: the refusal is sound and the operator-facing remedy is not. NO-CLAIM: this establishes that a closed bead was re-selected at tick=29 with the grading candidate set empty, that the lifecycle ledger's last eg0m event is an unresolved dispatch, that both offered remedies reopen graded work, and that clearing the assignee alone resolves it without reopening. It does NOT establish where the retry producer lives in source -- I inferred it from the ledger tail and the system's own inspect_dispatch_ledger hint rather than reading the selection code -- nor how many other closed-but-assigned beads sit in that queue; that census is unrun and is the first thing the implementer should measure.
acceptance_criteria: 1. MEASURE THE RETRY PRODUCER IN SOURCE FIRST. I inferred it from the ledger tail and the system's own hint; I did not read the selection code. Name the function and file:line. If the retry path is not the source, my diagnosis is wrong -- report that rather than fixing what I named. 2. CENSUS: how many beads are currently closed-or-blocked AND still carry an unresolved dispatch_receipt? eg0m was one; the count is unmeasured and determines whether this is a one-off or a backlog. 3. KNOWN-BAD, and tick=29's row is NOT sufficient evidence: a bead that is CLOSED must not be selected by ANY producer, including the retry path. Use eg0m's real 18-row ledger tail, not a fixture (C38). 4. THE REMEDY MENU MUST CARRY THE NON-DESTRUCTIVE OPTION. A closed-but-assigned bead's remedy is 'clear the assignee, keep the status' -- never a reopen. Assert in a test that no emitted remedy for a CLOSED bead contains '--status open' or '--status in_progress'. This is the highest-value item: the current advice destroys graded work. 5. KNOWN-GOOD: an in_progress bead with an unresolved dispatch MUST still be retryable. Do not fix a false positive by disabling retry. 6. ANTI-VACUITY: an empty retry queue is a typed state, distinct from a filtered-to-empty one. 7. MUTATION: remove the status filter from the retry producer, prove RED on leg 3, restore byte-identically with a checksum. 8. LIVE PROOF: no closed bead appears in a DISPATCH_BLOCKED or DISPATCH_RESULT row on the running loop. eg0m produced 19 such rows across ticks 11-29; cite the row that breaks the streak. 9. Coordinate on crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs via am file_reservations -- WildStone holds it exclusively. Do NOT restart the supervisor; pane 1 owns the restart. 10. Report which artifact produced every figure; cargo reads the WORKTREE.

comments.author: pane1-omp-claude
comments.text: CENSUS ANSWERED by pane 1, 2026-09-06 — this is acceptance item 2 of this bead, measured, and the answer is a BACKLOG rather than a one-off. Also a ROOT CAUSE deeper than the one in the description. THE COUNT: the lifecycle ledger /Users/josh/.local/state/flywheel/omp-orchestrator-omp-orchestrator.bead-lifecycle.jsonl holds 24 distinct beads. For TWENTY-ONE of them the LAST event is dispatch_receipt -- permanently in-flight. EIGHT of those 21 are CLOSED or absent from the tracker entirely: nh5, h71-missing-tests-0hwn, ntm-mail-pending-cursor-loss-x22h, u21m, 93lo, eg0m, and two more. So eg0m is not special; it is simply the one the retry reached first. THE DEEPER ROOT CAUSE -- THE LEDGER HAS NO TERMINAL EVENT KIND. Measured vocabulary across the whole file: selected=31, dispatch_receipt=31, receiver_verified=3, redispatch_required=1, grading_started=1. There is no closed, completed, abandoned, graded, or failed event. NOTHING IN THE VOCABULARY CAN SAY A DISPATCH IS DONE. So dispatch_receipt is the terminal state by default for every dispatch that does not reach receiver_verified, and 31 dispatched against 3 receiver_verified means 28 dispatches are permanently in-flight BY CONSTRUCTION, not by accident. That reframes this bead. Adding a status filter to the retry producer would stop it re-selecting CLOSED beads -- eight of them -- but it would leave the other thirteen in-flight forever, and it would leave the ledger unable to express completion at all. The filter is necessary and not sufficient. IT ALSO IGNORES PANE STATE, measured at tick=35: 'DISPATCH_BLOCKED bead=omp-orchestrator-eg0m pane=%9 reason=MISSING_RECEIVER_AGENT status=closed assignee=unassigned'. %9 was WORKING on mgdz at that moment. So the retry path is filtered by neither bead status NOR pane dispatchability, while the ordinary path correctly reports free_capacity and dispatchable and honours the two-capture window. That is a third divergence between the two producers, on top of status. WHAT I DID AND DELIBERATELY DID NOT DO: I cleared eg0m's assignee while leaving status=closed, which is the non-destructive remedy the system's own menu omits. It did NOT stop the re-selection -- tick=30 and tick=35 both re-selected it -- which is the evidence that the retry keys on the LEDGER, not the tracker. I did NOT hand-append a terminal event to the ledger: the vocabulary has no terminal kind, so inventing one by hand would write a value no reader is known to accept, and a hand-edited ledger is exactly the kind of unverifiable state this repo refuses. That decision is the implementer's to make in code. RAISED TO P0 from P1: eight closed beads in a retry queue that ignores status and pane state, on a 90s tick, is active fleet-capacity loss, and it is the mechanism that consumed ticks 11 through 35 on one bead while panes idled. NO-CLAIM: this establishes 24 beads in the ledger, 21 whose last event is dispatch_receipt, 8 of those closed or absent, the complete event vocabulary with no terminal kind, and that pane state is ignored by the retry path. It does NOT locate the retry producer in source -- still inferred from the ledger tail and the system's own inspect_dispatch_ledger hint, and acceptance item 1 still stands: read it and tell me if I am wrong -- nor does it establish whether receiver_verified is INTENDED as terminal, in which case the defect is that 28 dispatches never reached it rather than that the vocabulary is incomplete. Both readings are open and the implementer should decide which on evidence.

comments.text: SOURCE READ by pane 1, 2026-09-06 -- acceptance item 1 answered, and it CORRECTS MY OWN TWICE-REPEATED INFERENCE. I told two panes tonight to read the producer rather than accept my diagnosis; I had inferred this one from the ledger tail and the system's own inspect_dispatch_ledger hint. Reading it changed the picture. WHERE THE REFUSAL LIVES: crates/dispatch-claim-fence/src/lib.rs:697 returns ClaimFenceError::MissingReceiverAgent, and it fires on exactly one condition -- 'if receiver_agent.trim().is_empty()'. The fence's authorize() at :684 is documented at :681-683 as authorizing 'against the tracker snapshot immediately before packet construction. Bead dispatch requires in_progress and exact receiver ownership.' THE FENCE IS CORRECT AND IS NOT THE DEFECT. Both refusals are the fence doing its job on an intent it should never have been handed. Every field in the live row (status=closed assignee=unassigned receiver_agent=WildStone claim_owner= owner=josh) is appended by the CALLER, not by the error. So the line simultaneously asserts 'receiver agent is missing' and prints 'receiver_agent=WildStone'. Two values for one concept in a single line, from two sources. WHAT THAT IMPLIES ABOUT THE REAL MECHANISM, stated as inference and labelled as such: the retry re-selects eg0m from the LEDGER, whose row still carries receiver_agent=WildStone; the intent's receiver_agent is then derived from the TRACKER assignee, which I emptied; so the fence sees empty and refuses. Do not treat that paragraph as established. AGENTS.md's rule 7 is the precedent: a known-bad leg must assert its MESSAGE, not just its exit code, because 101 is cargo's generic failure and matching only rc != 0 goes green on any unrelated breakage. Same principle applied to a refusal: MissingReceiverAgent should carry the bead id and the value it actually saw, so the error and its decoration cannot contradict each other. CORRECTION TO MY DESCRIPTION: I wrote that the retry producer 'is not status-filtered'. More precisely -- the FENCE is correctly status-aware and refuses closed beads; what lacks the filter is whatever SELECTS the retry candidate and builds the intent. My phrasing blamed the wrong layer, and the fence deserves the opposite of blame here: it is the only thing preventing a closed graded bead from being dispatched. NO-CLAIM: this establishes the refusal's exact source and firing condition, that its Display carries no fields, and that the caller's decoration contradicts it. It does NOT locate the retry candidate selector or the intent-construction site -- both still unread by me -- and it does not establish which field populates DispatchIntent.receiver_agent. comments.text: ACCEPTANCE ITEM 1 NOW FULLY ANSWERED by pane 1, 2026-09-06 -- source read to the end, and the defect is a PARAMETER NAMING collision that makes the refusal message name the wrong concept. THE CALL SITE: crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs:1604 and :1609 both do 'authorize(&DispatchIntent::bead(bead, claim_owner), Some(snapshot))'. It is normally the receiver, except for an unclaimed bead where the supervisor holds an explicit supervisor:<pid> claim until handoff.' eg0m is closed and unassigned -- I cleared its assignee deliberately rather than take either reopen remedy -- so no identity holds a claim, so claim_owner is legitimately empty, so the fence legitimately refuses. Correct message would be 'DISPATCH_BLOCKED bead=<id> claim_owner is empty; bead is closed -- remove it from the retry queue', which names the field, the cause, and a remedy that does not destroy the grade. WHAT REMAINS UNREAD, so this is not a completion claim: the retry CANDIDATE SELECTOR -- whatever decides to hand eg0m to authorize() on tick after tick -- is still not located. title: P0: am robot reservations returns all_active=[] DETERMINISTICALLY while an exclusive lock is live -- the robot surface silently disarms the fleet's only concurrent-edit guard, and its attestation says everything is fine
description: MEASURED AND INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED 2026-09-03T21:26:01Z. Found by subagent FleetMonitorSession while running a positive control on the reservation surface; reproduced by pane 1 in the same minute. THE DEFECT: two Agent Mail surfaces disagree about live exclusive reservations, and the ROBOT one -- the surface an agent programmatically keys on to answer 'may I edit now' -- is BLIND. Setup: agent ScarletCave registered and staked an exclusive reservation on crates/fleet-monitor/**; GRANTED, id 112391, exclusive, expires 21:39:59Z. Then, same machine, same project key, same second: (A) file_reservations active users-josh-developer-omp-orchestrator reports 'crates/fleet-monitor/** [excl] by ScarletCave' -- CORRECT. (B) robot reservations reports all_active=[] -- WRONG while that lock is live and held. FleetMonitorSession measured 3/3 attempts one second apart; pane 1 reproduced independently. THE WORST PART IS THE ATTESTATION: both surfaces return the IDENTICAL reservation_read_attestation state=current source=local_config database_matches_server=true storage_root_matches_server=true detail='CLI reservation read targets the same database and archive as the reachable MCP server'. So the attestation is a claim about WHICH DATABASE IS TARGETED, not about whether the read is CORRECT -- it is a false-comfort surface, and an agent checking it will be told everything is fine while holding a blind result. IMPACT: in a shared checkout with four live agents, any agent trusting the robot surface will edit files another agent holds exclusively. This silently disarms the fleet's only concurrent-edit guard. It is strictly worse than the fleet-monitor --self CWD bug found in the same session: that pointed one lane at the wrong fleet, this disables the guard. It also invalidates pane 1's own ownership reasoning twenty minutes earlier, where active=0 was reported as UNKNOWN -- too weak a caveat, because the emptiness is DETERMINISTIC rather than flaky, i.e. actively misleading rather than merely unreliable. WHY THIS IS A TRUE DIFFERENTIAL AND NOT THE TWO-ROUTES-ON-ONE-DAEMON TRAP: the session already retracted a false 'oracle_skew=0' claim for exactly that reason -- two HTTP routes on one daemon sharing a process, credential and cache are one reading taken twice, not corroboration. This case is the inverse and is admissible precisely because the two surfaces DISAGREE: agreement can be manufactured by a shared cache, disagreement cannot. One of them is wrong, and surface A is the one that matches the granted reservation id. CHEAPLY GATEABLE: because they disagree, each is an oracle for the other. crates/oracle-compare (473 LOC, and note it has ZERO test files) implements exactly this shape -- count/set verdicts with unreadable-and-empty arms treated as ERROR rather than silent agreement. A gate comparing the two surfaces would fire on this today. Its known-bad leg is this reproduction; its known-good leg is both surfaces agreeing with no lock held. NO-CLAIM: this is measured for the installed am CLI on this host at this version. The daemon-side cause is UNMEASURED -- whether the robot handler queries a different table, applies a filter, or reads a stale projection is not established, and per AGENTS.md a defect claim against source not held is not a claim. The fix belongs upstream; nothing in this repo should synthesise a local guard, since the session already recorded that shipping a defense against a misdiagnosed defect is worse than shipping nothing.
acceptance_criteria:
1. KNOWN-BAD LEG (premise re-verification, MUST EXECUTE FIRST): with no pre-existing lock, register an agent and stake an exclusive reservation on a glob (e.g. `crates/fleet-monitor/**`) via the same `am` CLI on this host; record the granted id and expiry. Within the reservation window run both surfaces back to back, three times at ~1s spacing: `am file_reservations active <project-key>` and `am robot reservations`. The bead's premise holds only if surface A lists the granted glob `[excl]` by that agent AND surface B returns `all_active=[]` on 3/3 attempts. Capture raw stdout of all six invocations plus `am --version` and the host/project key into the bead. If the robot surface reports the live reservation (or the disagreement is intermittent rather than 3/3 deterministic), the bead MUST be RETITLED (e.g. to a flakiness/nondeterminism bead) or RETIRED with the transcript attached — it must NOT be "fixed" against an unreproduced premise.

2. KNOWN-GOOD LEG (over-strictness guard): with NO reservation held (all reservations released or expired — prove expiry by timestamp, not by assumption), run the identical pair of commands. Both surfaces must report an empty active set and the comparison gate must return AGREE/PASS. Additionally, a second known-good: with a NON-exclusive/shared reservation held, both surfaces must agree. A gate that fires on either of these known-good legs is over-strict and is rejected.

3. ANTI-VACUITY (typed error, not a pass): the comparator must distinguish four arms — BOTH_READABLE_AND_EQUAL (pass), BOTH_READABLE_AND_DIFFERENT (fail/differential), EITHER_UNREADABLE (typed error `SurfaceUnreadable`), and BOTH_EMPTY_WITH_NO_ESTABLISHED_GROUND_TRUTH (typed error `EmptyScanUnverified`). An empty `all_active=[]` from both surfaces is only a PASS when the known-good leg has independently established that zero reservations exist (e.g. a just-granted-then-released id, or a control reservation that IS visible in the same run). Zero parsed rows from a surface whose invocation exited non-zero, timed out, or produced unparseable output is a typed ERROR. Assert in test that no code path maps an empty set to `Ok(Agree)` without a positive control.

4. MUTATION RED / RESTORE: record `sha256` of the comparator source file(s) in `crates/oracle-compare` before touching them. Mutate the comparator so the `BOTH_READABLE_AND_DIFFERENT` arm returns agreement (or so `EitherUnreadable` is folded into pass); the known-bad-leg fixture test MUST go RED and the specific failing assertion name must be recorded. Restore the file and prove restoration by re-computing `sha256` and showing byte-identical match to the pre-mutation digest; paste both digests into the bead. A restore verified only by `git status` clean is insufficient.

5. LIVE-MEASURED vs FIXTURE: the differential itself (surface A vs surface B while a real exclusive lock is live) MUST be LIVE-measured against the installed `am` CLI on this host at the recorded version — it may NOT be asserted from a recorded fixture, since the whole claim is about the current binary's behaviour. The comparator's parsing, arm selection, and error typing MAY be exercised against captured stdout fixtures (the exact transcripts from item 1 and item 2, checked in verbatim with their capture timestamp and `am --version`). Any fixture must carry provenance metadata; fixtures without it fail the build.

6. NOT A SHARED-ORACLE ARTEFACT: document in the bead why this is admissible as a differential — the two surfaces DISAGREE, and disagreement cannot be manufactured by a shared cache/process/credential, unlike the retracted `oracle_skew=0` claim. State explicitly which surface is treated as authoritative and why (surface A matches the granted reservation id 112391 / the id from item 1). If both surfaces are ever made to agree by a shared cache path, the gate must be marked as providing no corroboration for that run.

7. ATTESTATION SCOPE MUST BE NARROWED OR SEPARATELY FILED: `reservation_read_attestation` returns `state=current source=local_config database_matches_server=true storage_root_matches_server=true` identically from both the correct and the blind surface, so it attests only WHICH DATABASE IS TARGETED, not read correctness. Either (a) the gate/report explicitly labels this attestation as non-probative for result correctness and refuses to treat it as evidence, or (b) a separate bead is filed against the upstream attestation surface for false comfort. Landing this bead without one of (a) or (b) is not acceptable.

8. UNMEASURED SUB-ITEM — DAEMON-SIDE CAUSE: the reason the robot handler is blind (different table, extra filter, stale projection) is UNMEASURED and the source is not held in this repo. This bead MUST NOT synthesise a local guard, workaround, or shadow reservation store. Either establish the cause with a measurement against source actually held and record it, OR file a separate upstream/investigation bead referencing this reproduction transcript. The deliverable here is limited to the differential gate plus `crates/oracle-compare` test coverage (note: it currently has ZERO test files — landing this bead must leave it with tests covering all four arms in item 3).

description:
## WHAT

Nine one-line prose corrections in `docs/plan/*.md`, each a figure or a source citation that no
longer reproduces. Filed as one bead rather than nine because they are all the same edit shape and
they land in files four panes are editing concurrently — the owner should batch them.

Every row below was verified by running the command. Full evidence with positive controls is in
`docs/plan/round16-Opus.jsonl` (round 22, lens `reproducibility`).

| # | file:line | says | live | fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `03-crates.md:341` | `grep -rhoE '^pub enum …'` → **59**, struct form → **91** | the command contains a literal **U+2026** inside the ERE, so it answers **0**; `^pub enum ` → **127**, `^pub struct ` → **187** | write the real patterns and the real numbers, or label the subsection HISTORICAL as items 1 and 2 above it already are |

| 6 | `07-installability.md:425` | `crates/installer/src/main.rs:25` "falls back to `PathBuf::from(\"/Users/josh\")` when `HOME` is unset" | `:25` is `.or_else(\|\| dirs_home().map(\|home\| home.join(\".local/bin\")))`; `:27` prints `INSTALLER ERROR: INSTALL_BIN_DIR or HOME must be set` and returns `ExitCode 2`. **Zero** `/Users/josh` anywhere under `crates/installer` | delete the claim — and delete the remediation built on it at `:427-429`, which proposes exactly the hard-error behaviour that already shipped |
| 7 | `07-installability.md:426` | "lines 118-119 default `CARGO` to `~/.cargo/bin/cargo`" | `main.rs:118-119` is `println!("INSTALLER IDENTITY OK: ...")` | re-derive or delete |
| 8 | `08-end-users.md:69` | `MEASURED`: "`:25` falls back to a literal /Users/josh" | same as #6. The other two cites in that sentence (`:16` `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`, `:12` three binary names) **do** reproduce | delete the `:25` clause only |
| 9 | `12-journey.md:298` | "`numbers.rs` + `NUMBERS.toml`, **13 figures**" | **22** (`grep -c '^\[figures\.' NUMBERS.toml` → 22, and an independent parser mirroring `numbers.rs figures()` executed all 22) | 22 |

Plus one addition, not a correction:

| # | file | add |
|---|---|---|
| 10 | `02-surface-census.md` §2.2 | The existing tooling warning covers `grep -r --include=` returning a false zero. It does not cover **metacharacters**, and `/usr/bin/grep` here is `pi-uu-grep 0.2.0`, a **regex** engine: `grep -c '^{' docs/plan/SURFACE-MAP.jsonl` → **0, rc=1** while `cut -c1 … \| uniq -c` → `614 {` and `grep -c '^\{' …` → **614**. ## WHY

`00-brief.md` §00 sets the rule: *every number carries the command that derives it*. `NUMBERS.toml`
enforces it for 22 registered figures and this round confirmed all 22 are green
(`RAN=22 DRIFTED=0`). Every row above is a figure that is **not** registered, so nothing re-runs

Rows 6, 7 and 8 are the sharpest of the ten and the reason this is P1 rather than P3: **two

becomes a hard error rather than a fallback"* — is the behaviour `main.rs:27` already implements.
The plan is budgeting work that is done.

Row 10 is not pedantry: this instrument defect produced three wrong readings during round 22 alone,
including a sibling grader reporting `SURFACE-MAP.jsonl` has **200** rows when six readers agree on
**614**, and one of my own counts returning 0 against a live 4. It is the same false-zero class
`03-crates.md:533` already records once for `forbid(unsafe_code)`.

For each numbered row, the stated command produces the stated number, or the claim carries an
adjacent `HISTORICAL` / dated-snapshot label per the plan's own convention:

9. `grep -c '^\[figures\.' NUMBERS.toml` → matches `12-journey.md:298`
10. §2.2 names brace/paren metacharacters, with the measured `^{` → 0 vs `^\{` → 614 as the example

Then, so this does not recur: register rows 1, 4, 5 and 9 as `[figures.*]` blocks in `NUMBERS.toml`

The three P0 blockers found in the same round, each filed separately:
`omp-orchestrator-untracked-crates-break-clone-jlb`,
`omp-orchestrator-strict-parser-rejects-gate-yml-m0c`,
`omp-orchestrator-dispatch-exists-unverified-u1c`.

Correcting ten prose figures ships nothing to a buyer. It removes false status a reader would act
on — `07-installability` currently schedules a fix for a shipped behaviour — and it is bounded
paperwork, not progress. Registering the four figures is the part that stops the next round from
finding them again.

title: P1: RULE 0.1 audit -- 19 of 77 crates are gates/guards/lints/checks/fences; WWJD DROPPED a 14-crate rewrite on this rule and we have never applied it to ourselves
description: MEASURED 2026-09-06 by pane 1 from /Users/josh/Developer/wwjd HEAD 5fd7eae. THE RULE, quoted in WWJD's README from Jeff's OWN frankensim/AGENTS.md and cited in its Arc review dated 2026-08-04: 'Do not build a validator for a validator, a harness for a harness, or an analyzer whose principal purpose is proving...' WWJD labels this RULE 0.1 and then APPLIES IT TO ITSELF: its S3 synthesis at README.md:121-129 records three alternatives and DROPS the first -- 'A1 DROP: Fourteen crates / Franken Arc 1000x -- RULE 0.1. No metric yet that authorizes a crate.' It kept the stuck 12-section plan as a control (INV-002) and adopted the small desk instead. A written kill decision with a reason, preserved rather than deleted. OUR MEASURED EXPOSURE: 19 of 77 crates in this workspace have a name matching gate|guard|lint|check|fence. One quarter of the workspace is checkers. Tonight alone I graded, or filed against, the following: no-shell-gate, kernel-bypass-gate, path-literal-guard, undrained-pipe-lint, pre-delete-citation-check, commit-build-fence, worker-oracle-gate, crate-atom-gate, state-wildcard-lint, wired-but-inert-guard, gate_properties (a gate asserting that other gates cite tests), and text-structure (a comment-stripping matcher whose consumer is those gates). A GATE THAT CHECKS GATES CITE TESTS, AND A MATCHER BUILT FOR THE GATES, IS LITERALLY A HARNESS FOR A HARNESS. That is not a rhetorical reading; gate_properties' own purpose is proving that a property claim has a test behind it. WHY THIS IS WORTH A DELIBERATE AUDIT RATHER THAN A REFLEX: several of those gates are load-bearing and MEASURED to bite. no-shell-gate's fires-on-known-bad is real. path-literal-guard caught a genuine home-rooted literal in my own doc comment. commit-build-fence's live expiry mutation went RED. crate-atom-gate's shrinking allowance ceiling is a good mechanism. The question RULE 0.1 asks is not 'is this gate correct' but 'did a METRIC authorize this crate' -- and WWJD's phrasing is exact: 'No metric yet that authorizes a crate.' AGENTS.md's own second rule is the same idea from the other side: BUILT does not equal WIRED, and a mechanism invoked by nothing is worth zero. We have the wiring test; we do not have the AUTHORIZATION test. WHAT THE AUDIT MUST PRODUCE, and it must not be a document: for each of the 19, the METRIC that authorized it and the DEFECT CLASS it has actually caught, with a file:line or a heartbeat row. A gate that has never fired on a real bad input is a candidate for deletion, per rule 1. Expect the honest answer to be that some are load-bearing, some are duplicative, and at least one is a harness for a harness that should be absorbed into what it checks -- exactly the 2ceb/main.rs duplicate-selector shape I created and then deleted tonight. NO-CLAIM: this establishes the rule's provenance in Jeff's frankensim/AGENTS.md via WWJD's citation, that WWJD applied it to drop a 14-crate rewrite, and that 19 of 77 of our crates are checkers by name. It does NOT establish that any specific gate should be deleted -- name-matching is not a purpose audit, and some non-matching crates are also checkers while some matching ones may not be -- nor does it measure which gates have ever fired on a real bad input, which is the actual question and is unrun.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Produce a machine-readable authorization ledger (e.g. `docs/rule-0-1-audit.toml` plus a typed loader) with exactly one row per audited crate, each row carrying: crate name, the METRIC that authorized it, the DEFECT CLASS it catches, and a citation that is either a `file:line` in this repo or a heartbeat/CI row ID. Free-text prose with no citation field is a schema error, not a row.

2. Enumerate the audit population LIVE, not from a hand-copied list: derive candidates by scanning `crates/*` (or workspace members from `cargo metadata`) at run time for names matching `gate|guard|lint|check|fence`, and assert the matched count equals the ledger's covered count. The 19-of-77 figure from the description is a fixture only for a regression comparison; the live scan is authoritative and a drift (new checker crate added, none matching) must fail loudly.

3. KNOWN-BAD leg, named from this description's own evidence: `gate_properties` (a gate whose purpose is proving other gates cite tests) and `text-structure` (a comment-stripping matcher whose only consumers are those gates) must each be classified as HARNESS-FOR-A-HARNESS and resolved with an explicit disposition of ABSORB or DELETE plus the target crate it is absorbed into. The mere existence of a ledger row for these two, or a row whose defect-class is "gates without test citations", is NOT sufficient evidence: a row asserting a gate checks gates is exactly the shape RULE 0.1 forbids, so the check must reject a disposition of KEEP for any crate whose only consumers are other crates in the matched set.

4. KNOWN-GOOD leg so the audit cannot become a delete-everything reflex: `no-shell-gate` (measured fires-on-known-bad), `path-literal-guard` (caught a real home-rooted literal in a doc comment), `commit-build-fence` (live expiry mutation went RED), and `crate-atom-gate` (shrinking allowance ceiling) must each survive with disposition KEEP and a concrete cited firing. If the audit tool marks any of these four as unauthorized or delete-candidate, that is a failure of the tool, not of the crate.

5. Anti-vacuity, typed: if the live crate scan yields zero members, if the ledger parses to zero rows, if any row has an empty metric, empty defect class, or empty citation, or if the "ever fired on a real bad input" evidence set is empty for the whole population, the audit must return a distinct typed error variant (e.g. `AuditError::EmptyPopulation`, `EmptyEvidence`, `MissingCitation`) and exit non-zero. Zero findings must never render as "audit clean".

6. Mutation proof, live: temporarily edit the ledger to strip the citation from one KEEP row (e.g. `no-shell-gate`), run the audit, and record that it goes RED with the specific `MissingCitation` variant; separately create a throwaway crate named `foo-gate` with no ledger row and confirm the coverage check goes RED. Restore both byte-identically and record a `shasum -a 256` of the ledger file before and after in the bead comment; identical checksums are required evidence.

7. MEASURED-live vs fixture: the crate enumeration, the ledger parse/validation, and the two mutation runs must be executed live in this workspace and their command output pasted. Historical firing evidence (no-shell-gate's known-bad fire, path-literal-guard's caught literal, commit-build-fence's expiry RED) may be cited as fixtures/prior rows, but each citation must resolve — a `file:line` that does not exist or a heartbeat ID that does not resolve is a hard error.

8. Open sub-items must not be silently absorbed: (a) the description explicitly states which gates have ever fired on real bad input is UNRUN — either measure it for all matched crates now or file a separate bead for the firing census and reference its ID in the ledger; (b) name-matching is not a purpose audit — either extend the scan to non-matching checker crates (e.g. by consumer-graph analysis) or file that gap separately; (c) the remaining named-but-ungraded crates (kernel-bypass-gate, undrained-pipe-lint, pre-delete-citation-check, worker-oracle-gate, state-wildcard-lint, wired-but-inert-guard) must each get a disposition row or an explicit DEFERRED marker naming the follow-up bead ID. No item may be closed as "covered by the ledger" without a row or a bead.

title: P0: S0 UNBLOCK -- enable asupersync messaging-fabric; the rev advance is NOT the fix (class is gated identically at fa3c01aec and at +518)
description:

jplf.1.2 -- enable the asupersync `messaging-fabric` feature and add three PATH-CORRECTED
re-exports to crates/omp-types.

should pull latest asupersync". The mirror was fetched. The measurement then REFUTED the rev as
the fix:

  origin/main    35116d02e : messaging/mod.rs:77-78 IDENTICAL, still gated

  src/messaging/class.rs   : touched by 0 of the 518 commits -- the types are UNCHANGED upstream
  messaging-fabric = []    : at BOTH revs, pulls nothing
  test-internals           : a separate feature at both revs; co-occurs with messaging-fabric ONLY
                             on two [[bench]] targets (Cargo.toml:797,802), never on the lib
  upstream ci-cross-platform enables messaging-fabric WITHOUT test-internals

So %8 was right that this needs a feature strategy, and wrong about the mechanism -- there is no
"forbidden test-internals leak". And the rev advance changes nothing for these three types.

THE PATHS, corrected by codex and then verified in source. My original three were wrong and would
not have compiled:

  WRONG  asupersync::obligation::ObligationLedger
  RIGHT  asupersync::obligation::ledger::ObligationLedger
         obligation/mod.rs has ZERO ObligationLedger re-exports; `pub mod ledger;` at :70
  WRONG  asupersync::obligation::AckKind        <- the UNINHABITED typestate marker, graded.rs:790
  RIGHT  asupersync::messaging::AckKind         <- the data enum, class.rs:83, variants
         Accepted/Committed/Recoverable/Served/Received  (`pub mod graded;` at :65 exposes the marker)
  RIGHT  asupersync::messaging::DeliveryClass   <- class.rs:17

Two same-named AckKind types is the whole subtlety, and it is why the bead says "the INHABITED
AckKind".

THE OPEN QUESTION, and the only one left. Codex claims that enabling the feature FAILS TO COMPILE
at the pinned rev, naming a latent break in gated modules (it cited consumer.rs). I could not
confirm or refute it: my probe found 0 ungated modules referencing gated items with a working
positive control (10 of 18 gated modules do reference them), but that tested the WRONG DIRECTION.
A break inside code nobody compiles is invisible to every static probe run so far. %9 attempted
`cargo check -p omp-types` and got exit 1 from an RCH path-root refusal and from `--offline
"can not checkout asupersync"` -- never from rustc. Per AGENTS.md those are UNKNOWN, never a
negative result.

NOT-GOALS: does not advance the pin (measured as not the fix; if the compile fails at fa3c01aec,
retry at 35116d02e as a SECOND experiment, not a first move); does not fast-forward the mirror
(a FF touches src/cx/mod.rs, which is dirty with someone else uncommitted work); does not edit
jplf.1.2, which %8 holds.

   feature and add the three path-corrected re-exports, then run `cargo check -p omp-types`.
   Report the exit code verbatim and, on failure, every `error[E….]` line. THIS IS THE DELIVERABLE.
   An exit 1 from RCH, from `--offline`, from a lock, or from any non-rustc source is UNKNOWN and
   does NOT satisfy this leg -- say so and retry differently. Per AGENTS.md a denied or errored
   probe is never a negative result.

2. THE FEATURE IS ENABLED THROUGH THE DEPENDENCY, NOT THE PACKAGE. `cargo check -p omp-types
   --features messaging-fabric` is the error %8 already hit: it resolves in omp-types own
   [features] table, which declares no such name, giving exit 101 "package feature absent". Enable
   it on the asupersync declaration, or forward it via omp-types [features] as
   `asupersync/messaging-fabric`. State which form you used.

3. PATHS EXACT. The landed re-exports use `asupersync::messaging::{AckKind, DeliveryClass}` and
   `asupersync::obligation::ledger::ObligationLedger`. A re-export of
   `asupersync::obligation::AckKind` FAILS this leg: that is the uninhabited marker and leg 4
   cannot pass with it.

4. INHABITEDNESS PROVEN AT COMPILE TIME. A test constructs `AckKind::Accepted`. This is jplf.1.2
   acceptance leg 2 and it is satisfiable exactly as written once the path is right.

5. BLAST RADIUS MEASURED BEFORE LANDING, not after. Report how many workspace members compile
   differently with the feature on -- codex counted 21 direct manifest hits and warns cargo unifies
   dependency features across a workspace build. If any unrelated crate breaks, report it and do
   NOT land; that is codex latent-break claim confirmed and it changes the decision.

6. THE NARROW FORM IS EVALUATED. Compare enabling on the workspace declaration versus

   which you chose and why. Feature unification means the narrow form is smaller in manifest scope
   but not necessarily in build effect -- say whether that held.

7. ANTI-VACUITY. A `cargo check` that exits 0 without compiling omp-types (wrong -p, cached
   no-op, or a skipped target) is a FAIL, not a pass. Show the compiling lines or the fresh/dirty
   status proving omp-types was actually built.

8. NO SECOND EXPERIMENT UNTIL THE FIRST REPORTS. Test at the CURRENT pin fa3c01aec first. Only if
   that fails do you retry at 35116d02e, and then you report BOTH exit codes so the rev question is
   answered with data rather than inherited from my earlier wrong claim.

9. DO NOT LAND ON A RED. If the compile fails, the deliverable is the error text plus a
   recommendation (upstream issue, feature subset, or pin advance). Landing a manifest change that
   breaks 21 crates while three panes are mid-flight is worse than reporting the failure.

10. NO-CLAIM required. State what you did not verify -- at minimum whether the feature affects

title: P0: census_membership is RED at HEAD -- s1-coverage is the 24th advisory-unreachable crate against a ceiling of 23, and it is unnamed in ADVISORY_ALLOWANCE
description: MEASURED 2026-09-05 by pane 1 while grading omp-orchestrator-gate-sends-and-peer-grading-gprn. cargo test -p omp-orchestrator --test census_membership returns 10 passed / 2 FAILED, and the failure is at HEAD rather than being a worktree artifact: the test file crates/omp-orchestrator/tests/census_membership.rs is CLEAN against HEAD (git status --porcelain empty for that path) and the offending crate is committed -- git ls-tree -r HEAD lists crates/s1-coverage/Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs and src/main.rs, landed by 5619f5b 'feat(s1): add tree-backed coverage kernel [test]'. ADVISORY_ALLOWANCE in crates/omp-orchestrator/src/lib.rs carries 26 rows at HEAD. THE TWO FAILURES, quoted from the gate: census_membership.rs:261 -- 'these crates are unreachable and advisory but NOT named in ADVISORY_ALLOWANCE (crates/omp-orchestrator/src/lib.rs): ["s1-coverage"]. Either wire them, or add a row with the reason they are not wired.' And census_membership.rs:373 -- 'the live advisory count is 24 and the ceiling says 23. Either wire the difference or re-record the ceiling -- a ceiling that does not match is not a ratchet.' left: 24, right: 23. THIS IS THE SHRINKING RATCHET DOING PRECISELY ITS JOB: a crate landed during this session, became the 24th advisory-unreachable member, and the ceiling refused because nobody re-recorded it. The gate's own message names both admissible fixes and implicitly forbids the third. THREE HONEST OPTIONS: (1) WIRE it -- if s1-coverage has a real caller it should have, wiring it drops the count to 23, the ceiling matches, and both tests go green; this is the preferred outcome and the one the ratchet exists to force. (2) NAME it with a row carrying the reason and a dies-when condition, then re-record the ceiling at 24 WITH that justification; legitimate only if the crate genuinely has no caller yet. (3) DELETE it -- if it earns nothing and duplicates an existing coverage surface, removal beats an allowance; check whether loop-coverage already answers what it answers, since AGENTS.md records loop-coverage shipping with ZERO test files and this space therefore already has a hollow occupant. THE FORBIDDEN FOURTH: bumping 23 to 24 with no reason. AGENTS.md is explicit that a systemic allowance ceiling is 'a shrinking ratchet, not a blanket exemption'; a ceiling raised without justification converts the ratchet into a rubber stamp and the gate would never fire again. COUNTER-ARGUMENT THAT MUST BE ANSWERED: s1-coverage may be CORRECTLY unwired right now -- a coverage kernel with no consumer until S1 itself converges, which is frozen behind HD-0012 and Joshua's approval -- in which case option 2 with an explicit dies-when tied to the S1 freeze is right, and forcing a caller into existence to satisfy a count would be the 'manufacture a test to justify an identifier' failure AGENTS.md forbids. NO-CLAIM: this establishes two failing assertions at HEAD and names the crate responsible. It does not establish which of the three dispositions is correct -- that requires reading what s1-coverage does and whether anything should consume it.
close_reason: MUTATION-VERIFIED by pane 1 (non-author), and the pane took the DEEPER fix I offered rather than the one-line patch. RE-EXECUTED: cargo test -p omp-orchestrator --test census_membership -> 13 passed, 0 failed (was 10 passed / 2 FAILED at dispatch). CHOICE=NAME, not wire and not delete, which was the honest call: s1-coverage has no production caller that could be honest while S1 depth is suspended, and forcing one into existence to satisfy a count is the 'manufacture a test to justify an identifier' failure AGENTS.md forbids. THE ALLOWANCE ROW CITES ATLAS ARC R1 BY NAME -- 'advisory-unreachable: S1 depth is suspended by Atlas Arc R1 and the HD-0012 hook decision pending Joshua approval; no production caller is honest while...' -- reached from the crate side with no contact with the atlas-arc R1 pass running in parallel, which independently measured MATURITY_MAX=4 MEDIAN=2 DELTA=2 R1_SATISFIED=no and concluded the same suspension. Two lanes agreeing on 'S1 depth is suspended' from different evidence outweighs either measurement alone. THE STEERED DEFECT IS FIXED AT THE RIGHT LAYER. title: S1-COVERAGE.md: make S1 readiness a generated number -- one row per requirement, MISSING must reach zero before any build wave opens
description:
JOSHUA 2026-09-03: "we have the ENTIRE s1 plan mapped out to beads - every single gap in s1 is covered and planned? if not we're not fucking ready." This bead makes that question answerable by command instead of by opinion. It is PX-P0's exit predicate from docs/contracts/planning_to_exhaustion.md: MISSING = 0, and nothing enters P4 EXECUTE before it.

WHY IT IS NEEDED: answering the question by hand took an ad-hoc script and twenty minutes, and MY FIRST ATTEMPT REPORTED A FALSE ZERO -- the token regex required a digit immediately after letters while the bead ids are of the form plf.7.3, so it found `tokens=0` on all ten gap rows and I nearly published that as a finding. A generated matrix removes both the delay and the regex.

DELIVERABLE: docs/plan/flow/S1-COVERAGE.md, GENERATED, one row per requirement, columns source | stable_id | requirement | bead_id | state where state is COVERED | MISSING | DOC-ONLY. The generator lives in the document's Validation block as a pasteable command -- NOT as a .sh or .py file, which a Rust gate walking git ls-files refuses.

SIX SOURCES with the counts pane 1 measured, to check the extractor against: contract stable IDs = 63 across six files; contract named tests = 15 (L0 has 25 ids and ZERO named tests; L1/L2 had zero ids and pane 3 is fixing that now, so re-measure); [[box.gap]] = 10 rows of which NINE are uncovered (six name no bead, three cite plf.7.3/lf.7.12/plf.7.2 which DO NOT EXIST -- the real ids are jplf.* and the leading j was dropped); [[box.observability]] = 6 rows x 4 requirements = 24 plus a metric each; [[box.hook]] = 8 rows x 12 certified fields = 96; branches = 20, each needing a rendered diagram arm AND a test.

HEADLINE THE DOCUMENT MUST PRINT: S1_REQUIREMENTS=<n> COVERED=<n> MISSING=<n> DOC_ONLY=<n>.

THREE TRAPS, named because pane 1 committed the first one today: (1) a MISSING must not be relabelled DOC-ONLY to improve the number -- DOC-ONLY requires a stated reason per row; that is escape route DP-E3, counter-substituted-for-substance, and the orchestrator committed it by flipping S1 to converged on a zero-open-rows count. (2) every count carries its producing command; 18 crates and 21 type collisions landed in ONE DAY, so a typed integer is wrong within hours. (3) TREE vs WORKTREE on every count -- pane 1 published rows = 62 from the worktree while a fresh clone of the same sha measured 17.

THE ASSERTION TO ATTACK: pane 1 asserts those six sources are the COMPLETE denominator for S1. They are almost certainly not. Uncounted candidates: the six layer `exists` fields; the 20 branch arms' TEST halves as distinct from their diagram halves; crate-atom-gate's nine parts applied to each S1 crate; and the stage/layer gates' own closing criteria. FINDING A SEVENTH SOURCE IS THE MOST VALUABLE RETURN -- an incomplete denominator makes MISSING = 0 a lie, which is worse than a large honest number.

ACCEPTANCE: the file exists; its Validation command runs and its output is pasted; the four headline counts are printed; every row's state is justified; and the report names either a seventh source or states that none was found and where it looked. NO-CLAIM: a coverage matrix measures whether requirements have beads. It says nothing about whether the beads are good, whether the requirements are the right ones, or whether the plan is correct -- only whether it is complete against its own declared surface.
acceptance_criteria:
DERIVED ACCEPTANCE by pane 1, 2026-09-06, from this bead's own description plus measurements taken tonight. This bead shipped with EMPTY acceptance and was therefore STRUCTURALLY UNDISPATCHABLE: crates/omp-orchestrator/src/dispatch_packet.rs:166 does `acceptance(snapshot).ok_or(PacketError::PacketFieldMissing("acceptance"))?`, and all 14 PacketFieldMissing rows in the live heartbeat name the `acceptance` field. Twelve active S1 beads were in this state, FIVE of them P0 and already in_progress -- a pane holding a P0 with no testable bar.

SUBJECT: S1-COVERAGE.md: make S1 readiness a generated number -- one row per requirement, MISSING must reach zero before any build wave opens

1. VERIFY THE PREMISE FIRST and quote the command with its output. If it no longer reproduces at HEAD, RETITLE or RETIRE rather than build against a stale premise. Measured tonight: of eight author's-premise checks, six found the defect in the BEAD rather than the code, and two premises were already extinct.

2. THE COMMAND MUST BE CONCRETE, NOT A PLACEHOLDER. Measured across 171 active S1 beads: 15 carry acceptances of the form 'run the gate' / 'run the named monitor command' / 'run the writer' -- an invariant with no runnable command -- and 10 carry unresolved references ('those keys', 'the named', 'the layer set'). Name the binary, subcommand and flags, or the bead cannot be graded by anyone but its author.

3. IF THE ACCEPTANCE NAMES A TEST FUNCTION, IT MUST ASSERT A NONZERO TEST COUNT. Measured: `cargo test -q -p ompo-start --test l3_step_parity <name that does not exist>` returns 'test result: ok. 0 passed; 0 failed; 2 filtered out' and EXIT CODE 0. `--exact` does not help (verified with correct `-- --exact` placement). A grader keyed on exit status closes work that never ran. Tracked as omp-orchestrator-named-test-missing-exits-zero-o5e1.

4. KNOWN-BAD LEG asserting the MESSAGE, not the exit code. `cargo` returns 101 both for a missing test target and for a workspace that cannot load, so a leg matching only `rc != 0` goes green on unrelated breakage.

5. KNOWN-GOOD LEG, mandatory: a correct input must PASS. An attack-only gate is over-strict, gets routed around, and that is a slower death than no gate.

6. ANTI-VACUITY: an empty, absent, or unreadable input set is an ERROR, never a pass. Report the denominator beside any count so a reader can distinguish 'checked nothing' from 'checked everything and found nothing'.

NO-CLAIM on this derivation: items 3 through 6 are measurements I took tonight and they hold; the SUBJECT-specific content is derived mechanically from this bead's own description and I did NOT run its premise. This makes the bead dispatchable and gives it a testable bar -- item 1 remains the first worker's job. A bead whose description turns out to be stale will now be dispatched and caught at item 1, rather than sitting invisible and undispatchable, which is the intended trade.

description:

COORDINATION: pane 4 is specifying the journey query on bead kukp RIGHT NOW and will consume this row shape. Send it to them via bead comment rather than letting two shapes diverge -- two incompatible expectation schemas would be worse than none.

comments.text: PARKED by pane 1 (orchestrator), 2026-09-06 -- BLOCKED ON `crates/ompo-start`, WHICH DOES NOT EXIST AND WHICH THE BUILD FREEZE FORBIDS CREATING. This is the repo-wide sweep; I parked the S1-L3 and S1-L4 rows first and then measured that the dependency is far larger than either family. CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER FIGURES, stated because I published them: I reported '16 of 23 S1-L3' and then '18 of 31 S1-L4'. The real scope is SEVENTY-FOUR beads repo-wide naming ompo-start in their acceptance -- 21 in s1-l5, 4 in s1-l1, 2 in s1-l2, plus the L3/L4 families and a scattered tail. My family-scoped counts were each correct and each understated the whole by more than half. MEASURED: crates/ompo-start is ABSENT from disk and has ZERO files in `git ls-tree -r HEAD`, with 78 crate directories present as a positive control. Every acceptance command in this set therefore fails with 'no such package', NOT with a test failure -- and cargo returns 101 for both, so a grader keyed on rc!=0 cannot tell 'the feature is broken' from 'the crate was never created'. That indistinguishability is the reason for parking rather than leaving a note. THE CONTRADICTION: docs/plan/flow/CONTRACT.md:59 -- 'No new crate, no new feature bead, no install, until every box has agreement.status = converged'. S1 is `draft`, reverted from `converged` by Joshua on 2026-09-03: 'you can't claim converged when s1 is still missing massive functionality'. HD-0009 IS decided -- two rows in docs/decisions.jsonl, ASK carrying decision="" and ANSWER carrying 'frankentui Rust TUI for humans PLUS --json for agents', Joshua verbatim 'frankentui rust yes' -- and it authorises exactly this work. The amendment below the freeze line is headed 'THE FREEZE'S EXIT CONDITION IS UNREACHABLE'. A decided HD row authorises work the freeze forbids, and the freeze cannot clear itself by the route it names. THE PARK IS PROVEN TO REDIRECT THE LOOP, in both directions: before parking, 7 ompo-start beads were dispatched in ~15 ticks, each burning a tick to rediscover the same missing package. After parking the L3 rows, the next two dispatches were s1-l4-src-ntm-2yrg and s1-l4-wire-ntm-session-x11g, whose acceptances (`ntm --robot-snapshot --capability-compact | jq '.sources.sources'`) RESOLVE and run. Parked beads were unrunnable; the beads the loop chose instead are runnable. NO LIVE WORK WAS DISTURBED: only rows with status=open were parked. The 9 in_progress ompo-start beads were left alone -- their panes hold live work and report separately, and blocking a bead mid-flight would discard real progress, which is the 5iij defect this repo already records. THE ACCEPTANCES ARE NOT AT FAULT AND WERE NOT REWRITTEN. The S1 acceptances are among the best-specified in this tracker -- short, one command each, several with named known-bad legs ('A TUI-owned Vec<Step> fails the test', 'Missing reason_code fails'). The defect is the missing target, not the specification. UNBLOCK CONDITION, one command per bead once Joshua rules: if HD-0009's authorisation overrides the freeze, `br update <id> --status open` and create the crate; if the freeze holds, these wait for S1 convergence. Tracked as omp-orchestrator-s1-l3-blocked-on-frozen-crate-tjxt, itself parked because its only actionable item is Joshua's scope decision. NO-CLAIM: a routing action, not a verdict on content. It does not resolve the freeze contradiction, does not authorise the crate, and does not establish that 74 is complete -- I matched the literal string `ompo` in acceptance text, so a bead depending on the crate without naming it is invisible to this sweep.

GRADE: NOT DONE -- by pane 1 (non-author, non-implementer), 2026-09-06. Implemented by WildStone on %7, which posted DONE evidence as comment 2135, ACKed, and correctly declined to self-close. I re-executed the acceptance rather than reading the report.

THE ACCEPTANCE PASSES AS WRITTEN.
  jq 'select(.stage=="S1")' docs/plan/FOUNDATION.jsonl -> 2 rows, BOTH citing inception.json
  POSITIVE CONTROL: stages S1..S9 all present, so the filter is real and the hit is not a broken probe
  the new row's input_refs are ['L5 portal write','L5-READBACK'] -- unmistakably this bead's append
  not a duplicate: sha ad53c3ba0321 vs 414a8497d4ba, 12 differing keys

I AM REFUSING THE CLOSE ANYWAY, on two things the acceptance does not ask for but a grader must not certify past.

1. THE ROW IS SCHEMA-NONCONFORMANT against a nine-row control.
     (stage, key-count) census over the whole file:
       S1 keys=12  x1   <- the new row
       S1 keys=14  x1
       S2..S9 keys=14  x1 each
     9 of 10 rows carry 14 keys. The new row carries 12, missing exactly `evidence` and `status`, while
     declaring the SAME schema_version 'journey_foundation.v1' as its siblings. A row that omits
     `evidence` cannot participate in any evidence gate that reads this file, and a version string that
     admits two shapes is not a version. This is the fixture-drift class (fh C38): a row that looks
     conformant certifies nothing.

2. THE ROW IS UNCOMMITTED. `git diff --stat -- docs/plan/FOUNDATION.jsonl` -> '1 file changed, 1
     insertion(+)'. My acceptance run read the WORKTREE. Per this repo's rule 8, a worktree figure is
     not evidence about a tree -- closing on it would certify a row that does not exist at HEAD and
     that any other agent's checkout cannot see. The work is real; it has not landed.

WHAT I AM NOT DOING: I am not failing the worker for the acceptance's own gaps. The acceptance says
'expect a new row citing inception.json' and that is exactly what was produced. The under-specification
is the box owner's to fix -- it should require the 14-key shape and a commit. I have not edited it,
because editing another agent's owned artifact to change a verdict is the write-path defect this repo
records as 5iij.

ACTION TAKEN: parked (status=blocked) to stop the re-offer. This bead was dispatched to %7 THREE times
-- 16:46:57, 16:53:35, and again at tick 15 -- each time after the work was already complete and
awaiting a grade. The re-offer is a SYMPTOM of the grading gap, now proven twice (ibpa.11 x4, y6yg x3):
a bead that is in_progress with finished work and no grader stays selectable forever. Unpark when the
row carries `evidence` and `status` and is committed.

NO-CLAIM: measured the jq counts with a positive control, both row hashes, the key-count census, and the
git diff. NOT measured: whether `evidence` and `status` are REQUIRED by any consumer of FOUNDATION.jsonl
-- I inferred their necessity from the 9-row majority, which is a convention, not a declared schema. If a
declared schema exists and permits 12 keys, this grade's clause 1 is wrong and I want to see it.

comments.author: pane1-omp-claude
comments.text: PARKED by pane 1 (orchestrator), 2026-09-06 -- BLOCKED ON `crates/ompo-start`, WHICH DOES NOT EXIST AND WHICH THE BUILD FREEZE FORBIDS CREATING. This is the repo-wide sweep; I parked the S1-L3 and S1-L4 rows first and then measured that the dependency is far larger than either family. CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER FIGURES, stated because I published them: I reported '16 of 23 S1-L3' and then '18 of 31 S1-L4'. The real scope is SEVENTY-FOUR beads repo-wide naming ompo-start in their acceptance -- 21 in s1-l5, 4 in s1-l1, 2 in s1-l2, plus the L3/L4 families and a scattered tail. My family-scoped counts were each correct and each understated the whole by more than half. MEASURED: crates/ompo-start is ABSENT from disk and has ZERO files in `git ls-tree -r HEAD`, with 78 crate directories present as a positive control. Every acceptance command in this set therefore fails with 'no such package', NOT with a test failure -- and cargo returns 101 for both, so a grader keyed on rc!=0 cannot tell 'the feature is broken' from 'the crate was never created'. That indistinguishability is the reason for parking rather than leaving a note. THE CONTRADICTION: docs/plan/flow/CONTRACT.md:59 -- 'No new crate, no new feature bead, no install, until every box has agreement.status = converged'. S1 is `draft`, reverted from `converged` by Joshua on 2026-09-03: 'you can't claim converged when s1 is still missing massive functionality'. HD-0009 IS decided -- two rows in docs/decisions.jsonl, ASK carrying decision="" and ANSWER carrying 'frankentui Rust TUI for humans PLUS --json for agents', Joshua verbatim 'frankentui rust yes' -- and it authorises exactly this work. The amendment below the freeze line is headed 'THE FREEZE'S EXIT CONDITION IS UNREACHABLE'. A decided HD row authorises work the freeze forbids, and the freeze cannot clear itself by the route it names. THE PARK IS PROVEN TO REDIRECT THE LOOP, in both directions: before parking, 7 ompo-start beads were dispatched in ~15 ticks, each burning a tick to rediscover the same missing package. After parking the L3 rows, the next two dispatches were s1-l4-src-ntm-2yrg and s1-l4-wire-ntm-session-x11g, whose acceptances (`ntm --robot-snapshot --capability-compact | jq '.sources.sources'`) RESOLVE and run. Parked beads were unrunnable; the beads the loop chose instead are runnable. NO LIVE WORK WAS DISTURBED: only rows with status=open were parked. The 9 in_progress ompo-start beads were left alone -- their panes hold live work and report separately, and blocking a bead mid-flight would discard real progress, which is the 5iij defect this repo already records. THE ACCEPTANCES ARE NOT AT FAULT AND WERE NOT REWRITTEN. The S1 acceptances are among the best-specified in this tracker -- short, one command each, several with named known-bad legs ('A TUI-owned Vec<Step> fails the test', 'Missing reason_code fails'). The defect is the missing target, not the specification. UNBLOCK CONDITION, one command per bead once Joshua rules: if HD-0009's authorisation overrides the freeze, `br update <id> --status open` and create the crate; if the freeze holds, these wait for S1 convergence. Tracked as omp-orchestrator-s1-l3-blocked-on-frozen-crate-tjxt, itself parked because its only actionable item is Joshua's scope decision. NO-CLAIM: a routing action, not a verdict on content. It does not resolve the freeze contradiction, does not authorise the crate, and does not establish that 74 is complete -- I matched the literal string `ompo` in acceptance text, so a bead depending on the crate without naming it is invisible to this sweep.

comments.author: pane1-omp-claude
comments.text: ACCEPTANCE PRE-RUN by pane 1, 2026-09-06 -- YOUR CITED AUTHORITY IS REAL AND FULLY RESOLVES 'those keys'. Run because %7 is working this bead and its acceptance says 'run the writer; expect file exists with those keys', which is unrunnable as written -- the command is a placeholder and 'those keys' is an unresolved reference. Both halves are now resolved below. THE AUTHORITY, verified rather than assumed: your WHY cites SCHEMAS.toml:156-161. My first read of `docs/plan/flow/SCHEMAS.toml` returned NOTHING, which would have let me call the citation dead. It is not dead -- the file is at the REPOSITORY ROOT, ./SCHEMAS.toml, 181 lines, and :156-161 reads exactly: [artifacts.inception_manifest] / path = ".omp-orchestrator/inception.json" / format = "json" / required = ["schema_version", "project_id", "repo_identity", "control_files", "host_capabilities", "required_tools", "trust_status"] / optional = ["evidence", "status", "degradations"] / writer = "S1 inception foundation". So the citation is precise and my path assumption was the error. A cited line number is a claim and it verified. YOUR SEVEN REQUIRED KEYS, verbatim from :159: schema_version, project_id, repo_identity, control_files, host_capabilities, required_tools, trust_status. Plus THREE OPTIONAL that your WHAT does not mention: evidence, status, degradations. Worth deciding deliberately whether to emit them -- `degradations` in particular is the field that would let this manifest express partial capability instead of a boolean, which is the distinction this repo keeps paying for. THE TARGET PATH AND ITS CURRENT STATE: .omp-orchestrator/inception.json is ABSENT. The .omp-orchestrator/ directory EXISTS and contains exactly one entry, `work`. So the parent is there and the manifest is not. AN INSTRUMENT NOTE, because I nearly published the wrong answer: my first probe was `ls -l .omp-orchestrator/inception.json | awk '{print $5}' || echo ABSENT` and it printed an EMPTY result rather than ABSENT, because in a pipeline the exit status is awk's, not ls's -- so the `|| echo` never fired. That is the $?-after-a-pipe fault AGENTS.md records as having produced three false findings in surfaces being audited FOR false success. `test -f` gives the honest answer. NO WRITER EXISTS: grep for `inception` across crates/*/src/*.rs returns ZERO files, with a positive control of 2 files referencing `.omp-orchestrator`. The schema names its writer as 'S1 inception foundation', which is a stage rather than a binary, so the writer is what your bead creates. WHY THIS BEAD WAS NOT PARKED with 65 relatives: your acceptance does not name `ompo-start`. That crate is absent from disk and from HEAD, and CONTRACT.md:59 forbids creating it while S1 is `draft`, so 74 beads repo-wide are stalled on it. Yours writes to a path the schema already declares, which is a different and unblocked kind of work -- though note your own CONSTRAINTS line says 'BUILD FREEZE until this bead is dispatched as S1 build', so whether the writer may be created is the same scope question tracked as omp-orchestrator-s1-l3-blocked-on-frozen-crate-tjxt, parked for Joshua. NO-CLAIM: measured are SCHEMAS.toml's location and the verbatim content of :156-161, the seven required and three optional keys, the absence of inception.json with `test -f`, the presence of .omp-orchestrator/ containing only `work`, and zero `inception` references in crate sources with a positive control. I did NOT determine what values the seven keys should carry, nor whether S2's reader (which your WHY also names) already expects a specific shape -- I did not read the S2 reader.

description: JOSHUA 2026-09-03: 'why would we not have observability at every layer - this seems like a massive gap'. He is right, and the causal reason is measurable. WHAT IS MISSING: S1.toml:21 declares event_row = LifecycleEvent{stage_from=HUMAN, stage_to=S1.<L0..L5>, actor, pane, incarnation, outcome, reason_code, blocker} -- DECLARED, with ZERO writers. Nine writer files exist in the workspace (ack-spine/src/ledger.rs, ack-spine/src/spine.rs, ntm-fleet-monitor/src/bead_lifecycle.rs, omp-orchestrator/src/spine_emit.rs and peers) and every one serves the DISPATCH LOOP, not the journey. comments.text:
ACK vv9h on %8 --

S1 L1 PROBE VERDICT DELIVERABLE

The seven semantic arms are retained, with UNMEASURED carrying run_state so crate-atom-gate's Unrun rule is explicit:
ProbeVerdict{OK|ABSENT_FAMILY|ABSENT_SPECIFIC|UNPROBEABLE|STALE|PAUSED|UNMEASURED{run_state=UNRUN|INSTRUMENT_ERROR,reason_code}}

Branch behaviour is now in docs/contracts/s1_l1_doctor.md:
- OK -> CONTINUE to L2.
- ABSENT_FAMILY -> HUMAN_HALT with named remediation when required; optionality must be explicit.
- ABSENT_SPECIFIC -> INFO plus remediation when optional; HUMAN_HALT when required.
- UNPROBEABLE -> HUMAN_HALT unless a named HD authorizes DEGRADED_CONTINUE; preserve the arm.
- STALE -> re-probe/remediate and HUMAN_HALT by default; named HD is the only degraded override for a non-critical probe. A present wrong-version tool is STALE, never OK or ABSENT.
- PAUSED -> HUMAN_HALT/resume by default; named HD is the only degraded override. It remains distinct because it records intentional operator pause.
- UNMEASURED -> no valid observation. Timeout/no-record is run_state=UNRUN; instrument failure is run_state=INSTRUMENT_ERROR. HUMAN_HALT by default; named HD is the only degraded override. Never Pass or Refused.

UNKNOWN and UNPROBEABLE do not collapse. UNKNOWN means no authoritative record and maps to UNMEASURED reason_code=UNKNOWN_NO_RECORD. UNPROBEABLE means an attempted probe reached a subject that could not answer. RCH's explicit repo-convergence status=unknown/total=0 is the former.

crate-atom-gate/src/lib.rs:56-57 is adopted verbatim in substance: timeout is Unrun, never Pass or Refused. The diagram does not add seven nodes; it has one ProbeVerdict node with all seven labeled arms and shared branch behaviour.
