title: P0: the conductor's wake was armed into a shell nobody watches, and its own drain destroys the flag the wake keys on -- two mechanical causes of every missed notification, including a 17-hour outage
description: MEASURED 2026-09-05 by pane 1 against itself, answering a question Joshua has asked for days: why can agents not message the conductor back, and why is the conductor not notified. THE PANES CAN AND DO MESSAGE BACK. Proof: am mail inbox shows 41504 from WildStone at 2026-09-05T21:21 with subject 'diq0: 36 remaining classified; class 4 is 7', plus 41481, 41476, 41475 and 41474 -- five real reports delivered. The transport works. The failure is entirely on the receiving side and it has TWO independent mechanical causes, both mine. CAUSE A -- THE WAKE WAS ARMED INTO A SHELL NOBODY WATCHES. There are two ways this conductor backgrounds a watch, and they are not equivalent. Arming through the harness returns 'Backgrounded as job bg_N; result will be delivered automatically', the harness owns the job, and its settlement delivers a turn to the conductor -- measured working four times tonight as bg_2, bg_5, bg_8 and bg_15, each of which produced a system notice that resumed work. Arming with a shell ampersand and redirecting to /dev/null -- 'inbox-monitor ... --watch ... >/dev/null 2>&1 &' -- creates no harness job, so there is nothing to deliver; the process is a child of the tool call's own shell and dies when that call returns; and its output was discarded by construction. Measured after the 17-hour gap: pgrep -f inbox-monitor returned ZERO processes alive. So the last thing the conductor did before the outage was arm a wake that could not exist and could not report. That single idiom difference is the 17-hour silence in which three lanes committed 8ee65c1, cb7f335 and 1175e47 while %7, %8 and %9 sat idle beside a 375-deep ready queue. CAUSE B -- THE CONDUCTOR'S OWN DRAIN DESTROYS THE SIGNAL. The drain idiom used all session is a loop over recent ids: for id in $(am mail inbox ... --limit N); do am mail read $id; done. That marks messages READ whether or not their content was consumed. Measured: 'Message 41504 marked as read at 2026-09-05T21:40:18Z' -- pane 9's answer arrived at 21:21 and the conductor's own drain marked it read at 21:40 without reading its body, so inbox-monitor then reported unread=0 truthfully about a message never processed. A wake keyed on the unread FLAG cannot fire for a message the reader pre-marked read, and AGENTS.md already records the underlying property: 'unread is a FLAG, not a cursor position'. The two causes compound: A means no watcher exists, B means that even a live watcher would see a manufactured zero. THE FIX, three parts. (1) NEVER arm a wake with a shell ampersand; always arm through the harness so the job is owned and its settlement delivers a turn. Verified immediately after filing: arming through the harness produced a live process where the ampersand arm produced none. (2) NEVER bulk-mark-read. Read the message BODY first -- that is the consumption -- and mark read only after the content has been acted on. (3) Key the wake on CURSOR ADVANCE rather than the unread flag: inbox-monitor already returns persisted_cursor and next_cursor, which are monotonic and cannot be destroyed by a reader, whereas unread is mutable by the reader itself. ACCEPTANCE: a known-bad leg that arms a wake the wrong way and proves no process exists; a known-good leg that arms it correctly and proves a live pid; and a leg proving a cursor-keyed wake still fires for a message that has already been marked read. FALSIFIER: mark an unread message read without reading it, then confirm a cursor-keyed wake still fires while a flag-keyed wake does not. NO-CLAIM: this establishes two receiving-side defects and that the sending side works for five measured messages. It does not establish that every pane always mails -- two panes reported by bead comment with no mail tonight and one by mail with zero comments, which is the separate three-channel gap filed as bu6f.
acceptance_criteria:
1. KNOWN-BAD LEG (wake armed via shell ampersand): the test must itself execute the exact bad idiom `inbox-monitor ... --watch ... >/dev/null 2>&1 &` from inside a tool call, let the call return, then assert `pgrep -f inbox-monitor` yields ZERO matching pids and that no harness job id (`bg_N`) was emitted. The already-observed post-outage `pgrep` returning zero is NOT sufficient evidence: it was a one-shot forensic observation with no controlled arming step, no proof the process ever started, and no discriminating comparison against a good arm — the leg must arm and re-measure live in the same run.

2. KNOWN-GOOD LEG (wake armed through the harness): arm the same `inbox-monitor --watch` through the harness, assert the returned string contains a job id of form `bg_<N>`, assert `pgrep -f inbox-monitor` yields >=1 live pid, and assert the harness settlement delivers a turn/system notice. Fix must not be so strict that this legal arm is rejected or that any long-running harness-owned background job is blocked.

3. FLAG-DESTRUCTION LEG (Cause B falsifier, live): create/pick a message; mark it read WITHOUT reading its body (reproducing `for id in $(am mail inbox --limit N); do am mail read $id; done`); then assert (a) a flag-keyed wake does NOT fire (`unread=0`), and (b) a cursor-keyed wake DOES fire because `next_cursor > persisted_cursor`. Both halves required; a passing cursor wake alone does not prove the flag wake was broken.

4. ANTI-VACUITY: every scan (`pgrep` result set, inbox listing, cursor pair) that comes back empty/absent must raise a typed error — e.g. `WakeProbeEmpty`, `NoCursorReported`, `InboxScanEmpty` — never be treated as "no violations, pass". A run where zero messages were examined, or where `inbox-monitor` returned no `persisted_cursor`/`next_cursor` fields, MUST fail with that error naming which probe was empty.

5. MUTATION / RED PROOF: mutate the guard so the ampersand idiom is accepted (or so the wake keys on `unread` instead of cursor advance), run the suite, and require items 1 and 3 to go RED with the specific failing assertion recorded. Restore the file byte-identically and record a pre-mutation and post-restore checksum (sha256) of the mutated file(s) in the run output; unequal checksums fail the bead.

6. MEASURED LIVE vs FIXTURE: the ampersand-vs-harness arm and the `pgrep` pid counts MUST be measured live against a real `inbox-monitor` process — no mocked process table. The `persisted_cursor`/`next_cursor` monotonicity and the marked-read-without-body case MAY use a fixture inbox, but the fixture must be produced by a real `am mail` invocation at least once and the recorded cursor values must be quoted verbatim in the evidence.

7. GUARD ON THE DRAIN IDIOM: add an enforced check that rejects any bulk `am mail read $id` loop that runs without a preceding body read; the check must cite the real evidence line (`Message 41504 marked as read at 2026-09-05T21:40:18Z` vs arrival `2026-09-05T21:21`) as its regression fixture, and must still allow mark-read that follows a body read (known-good leg).

8. OPEN SUB-ITEM: the three-channel gap (two panes reporting by bead comment with no mail, one by mail with zero comments) is explicitly NOT covered here — verify bu6f exists and is open and reference it in the bead's close comment; if bu6f is missing or closed, file it before closing this bead. Silent coverage under this bead's acceptance is a fail.

title: P1: the conductor's wake is mail-only, but panes report through three channels -- a 24-min watch timed out (exit 17) while two commits and a bead-comment completion landed unseen
description: MEASURED 2026-09-05 by pane 1 against its own loop. An inbox-monitor --watch bound at 1440s returned exit 17 / watch_timed_out after 133 reachable polls with unread=0, and the tool's own message is explicit that this is NOT 'the inbox is empty' (exit 0) and NOT 'could not look' (exit 13) -- the wake simply did not fire inside the window. MEANWHILE WORK WAS COMPLETING THE ENTIRE TIME. Measured immediately after the timeout: two commits had landed (51fe0c3 'feat(lifecycle): wire typed bead ledger at dispatch' from pane %8, and 5836600 'docs(planning): close-reason hex is not a commit until cat-file' from pane %9), pane %9 had gone IDLE having posted its full classification result as a BEAD COMMENT on omp-orchestrator-classify-unresolvable-close-citations-bm04 (the 2+6+0+18=26 split with a P3 severity recommendation), and pane %8 had gone IDLE after landing a 1025-line ledger plus a 372-line test file. NONE OF IT MAILED. THE DEFECT IS IN THE CONDUCTOR, NOT THE PANES: panes report completion through THREE channels -- Agent Mail, bead comments, and commits -- and the wake watches ONE. A mail-only wake is a single-input monitor on a three-output system, so its timeout is indistinguishable from silence when in fact two panes had finished. This is the same class as the tick-monitor free_capacity_streak=101 defect repaired earlier tonight (a monitor whose reading nobody consumed) and the AGENTS.md rule that 'every scheduled monitor needs a named reader'; here the monitor has a reader but is blind to two of three signal paths. CONSEQUENCE MEASURED: 24 minutes of conductor idleness beside two completed deliverables, and the timeout was initially read as a possible stalled-pane signal because the 1440s bound had been derived from measured completion times (median 10 min, max 16 min, bound = max + 50%). The bound was sized correctly for MAIL arrivals and is simply the wrong instrument for completions that do not mail. FIX OPTIONS, none yet chosen: (a) make the dispatch packet's notify-on-completion instruction mandatory and enforced rather than stated -- every packet this session did carry it, and two panes still reported by comment instead, so convention is measurably insufficient; (b) widen the wake to poll all three surfaces, which trades a blocking wake for a poll and violates the DO NOT POLL, BLOCK rule; (c) have the panes' own bead-comment write emit a mail as a side effect, moving the fan-in into the tracker rather than the conductor; (d) key the wake on the lifecycle ledger just landed at crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs:1565, since a dispatch_receipt or graded_pass row is written regardless of which channel the pane chose to talk on -- this is the option that composes with work already done rather than adding a surface. NO-CLAIM: this establishes that one 24-minute wake missed two completions on two other channels. It does not establish how often that happens, and it does not establish that any work was lost -- both completions were found intact by a manual observe immediately afterward.

title: P1: inbox-monitor --watch exit 12 is a VERDICT (mail waiting), not a failure -- restart:on-failure turns a correct one-shot into a 30s hot loop
description: MEASURED 2026-09-05 by pane 1, and the defect is in the SUPERVISION CONFIG, not the tool -- filed because the mistake is easy to repeat and it produced a self-inflicted hot loop within minutes of arming the monitor Joshua asked for. SYMPTOM: inbox-monitor --watch was started under hub with restart=on-failure. It correctly detected mail and printed 'inbox-monitor: MAIL WAITING -- 2 unread; oldest from WildStone: [ywd5] ACK ywd5 on %9' and then exited 12. The supervisor read exit 12 as a failure and restarted it every 30 seconds; measured 29 restarts, each re-notifying the SAME two unread messages, each emitting a full JSON verdict block into the log. ROOT CAUSE: exit 12 is the tool's VERDICT, not a crash. Its own JSON says so explicitly: exit_code=12 alongside verdict=mail_waiting, mode=watch, and watch.outcome=watch_settled with polls=1 and waited_secs=1. --watch is a ONE-SHOT WAITER by design: it blocks until mail exists, reports, and exits nonzero so a caller can branch on the signal. Wrapping a one-shot in restart-on-failure is a category error -- the exit that means 'I succeeded and here is the answer' is the exact condition being treated as 'I broke, run me again'. THIS IS THE SAME FAMILY AS 'A TIMEOUT IS NOT A VERDICT' from AGENTS.md's asupersync contract, inverted: there, a restrictive terminal must not be read as success; here, a successful typed signal was read as a failure. Both are the caller assigning meaning to an exit code without reading the tool's contract, and AGENTS.md already records three sibling instances -- $? after a pipe returning the pipeline's status, a cargo 101 matched on rc!=0 rather than its message, and '[RCH] remote required' exiting 103 with '0 passed 0 failed' being misread as a test result. CONSEQUENCES OBSERVED, both mine: (1) 29 restarts of a healthy binary, with the log filling with duplicate verdict blocks so a genuinely new message would have been indistinguishable from the repeat; (2) the two unread messages were never consumed, because each restart re-detected them rather than anything reading them -- the monitor was maximally loud and delivered nothing, which is the 178-writes-zero-readers pattern from ATTENTION.txt reproduced in a fresh mechanism. WHAT WAS DONE: stopped the loop, read message 41560 and 41559 bodies before marking them read (per omp-orchestrator-85ak: --unread is a FLAG not a cursor, so a bulk mark-read destroys the only signal that a message was never consumed), confirmed unread=0, and re-armed with restart=no so the one-shot stays a one-shot. ACCEPTANCE: (1) document exit 12 as a verdict in the monitor's own --help and in this repo's guidance, so the next operator cannot infer 'nonzero means broken'; (2) the arming pattern is one-shot then CONSUME then re-arm, never restart-on-failure -- a supervised long-run wrapper must distinguish 'settled with a finding' from 'crashed'; (3) known-bad leg -- a config that wraps a settling one-shot in restart-on-failure must be REFUSED or warned, not silently accepted; (4) known-good leg -- a genuine crash (nonzero for a non-verdict reason) must still restart, so the fix is not 'never restart'; (5) anti-vacuity -- zero unread with a settled watch is UNKNOWN or a clean timeout, never 'mail waiting'. NO-CLAIM: this is a defect in how pane 1 supervised the tool. inbox-monitor behaved exactly as designed and its verdict JSON was self-describing throughout -- the information needed to avoid this was in the first line of the first log entry. No claim is made that the tool needs a code change; the minimum fix is documentation plus an arming discipline, and the broader claim that hub should distinguish verdict-exits from crash-exits is a design proposal, not a measured requirement.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Known-bad leg, live: a hub/supervisor config that arms `inbox-monitor --watch` (or any settling one-shot) with `restart=on-failure` (or `restart=always`) must be REFUSED or emit a loud typed warning at arm time, not silently accepted. The existing 29-restart log from 2026-09-05 is NOT sufficient evidence — it is a post-hoc symptom of an already-armed config, not proof that the checker rejects the config; the check must be re-run live against a freshly written config file and produce a nonzero/typed refusal.

2. Known-good leg, live: a service that exits nonzero for a NON-verdict reason (e.g. binary missing, panic, exec failure — inject by pointing the unit at a nonexistent path or a `sh -c 'exit 1'` with no verdict JSON) must still be restarted under `restart=on-failure`. Record the restart count > 0. The fix must not degrade to "never restart".

3. Verdict-vs-crash discrimination must be measured on the real exit, not asserted: run `inbox-monitor --watch` live with ≥1 unread present, capture actual `$?` and the full JSON, and assert exit_code=12 co-occurs with verdict=mail_waiting, mode=watch, watch.outcome=watch_settled. If the JSON is absent or unparseable, the run is a typed ERROR, not a verdict — a bare exit code is never sufficient to classify.

4. Anti-vacuity: with unread=0 and a settled watch, the result must be UNKNOWN or a clean timeout with an explicit outcome field — never `mail_waiting`, and never an empty/absent scan silently treated as pass. A zero-length config scan, zero units inspected, or empty JSON must exit as a typed ERROR (e.g. `E_NO_UNITS_SCANNED`) with a distinct nonzero code from both "clean" and "refused".

5. Mutation proof: flip the arming config's `restart=no` back to `restart=on-failure` (or delete the verdict-exit allowlist entry for exit 12), re-run the checker, and record it going RED with the specific refusal message. Restore byte-identically and verify with a checksum (`sha256sum` before/after must match, both values pasted into the bead) and re-run to confirm GREEN.

6. Live vs fixture: the exit-12 verdict JSON and the config-refusal check must be measured live in this repo on this host. The 29-restart hot-loop reproduction MAY be a fixture (a recorded log or a synthetic supervisor loop) — it must be labeled as such and must not be cited as evidence that the refusal check works.

7. Documentation legs, both required and both verified by grep-with-evidence: (a) `inbox-monitor --help` output contains an explicit line stating exit 12 = verdict `mail_waiting`, not a failure; (b) this repo's guidance (AGENTS.md or the arming-discipline doc) records the one-shot → CONSUME → re-arm pattern and lists exit 12 alongside the existing three siblings ($? after a pipe, cargo 101, `[RCH]` 103). Paste the matched lines with file:line. If the tool's `--help` cannot be changed from this repo, that sub-item must be separately filed, not silently covered.

8. Open sub-items named in the description must be resolved or filed, never absorbed: (a) the design proposal that hub itself distinguish verdict-exits from crash-exits is explicitly NOT measured here — file it as a separate bead and link the id; (b) the CONSUME half (something actually reads message bodies before mark-read, per omp-orchestrator-85ak's "--unread is a FLAG not a cursor") is not covered by the refusal check — either demonstrate a consuming reader live or file it separately with its id recorded in this bead.

comments.author: pane1-omp-claude
comments.text: RETIRED THE MONITOR, and the second measurement is more decisive than the first. UPDATE by pane 1, 2026-09-05. After fixing restart=on-failure to restart=no, the hot loop stopped -- that part of the fix was correct. But the one-shot then produced a USER-VISIBLE 'Supervised process inbox-p1 failed with exit code 12' notice ONCE PER MESSAGE, twice within twenty minutes, both times for mail that had ALREADY reached me on channel 3 (the direct ntm --robot-send to pane %6) before the mail even landed. So the monitor's measured contribution was: zero new information, plus one false failure notice per message into Joshua's channel. NEGATIVE VALUE, not marginal value. Stopped it. DECISION: mail is consumed ON DEMAND (am inbox --unread, read bodies, mark read), and channel 3 is the live path. Both are kept -- channel 3 is FAST and mail is DURABLE, and tonight proved they are not redundant in the same direction: every ACK arrived on channel 3 first and mail confirmed it second. What is retired is the SUPERVISED WATCHER, not the mailbox. THE GENERAL DEFECT, restated more precisely than in the original filing: hub's supervision model has exactly two categories, running and failed, while inbox-monitor --watch has three outcomes -- crashed, settled-with-a-finding, and timed-out-clean. A tool whose success signal is a nonzero exit CANNOT be supervised by a system that reads nonzero as failure, in either restart mode: with restart=on-failure it hot-loops, and with restart=no it reports a healthy finding as a failure to the human. The exit code is doing double duty as both a status and a payload, which is the same conflation as 'a timeout is not a verdict' in AGENTS.md's asupersync contract and the same family as $? after a pipe returning the pipeline's status. WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY FIX IT, in preference order: (1) the tool exits 0 on a settled watch and puts the finding in its JSON verdict field, which it already emits -- verdict=mail_waiting is right there and is machine-readable, so the nonzero exit carries no information the payload lacks; (2) hub gains a notion of an expected non-zero exit, e.g. a declared success-exit set, so a verdict-exit is not surfaced as a failure; (3) callers stop supervising one-shots and invoke them inline where a nonzero exit is a branch rather than an alarm. Option 1 is the smallest and is upstream of the other two. NO-CLAIM: this is a defect in how pane 1 supervised the tool plus a genuine ergonomic mismatch between a verdict-exit tool and a binary-status supervisor. inbox-monitor behaved exactly as designed in both configurations and its JSON was self-describing throughout. No claim is made that hub is wrong; the minimum fix is documentation plus the arming discipline, and option 1 is a proposal about the tool's exit contract, not a measured requirement. Nothing here claims mail delivery is unreliable -- unread reached 0 on every consume.

title: rigor-atlas layered-enforcement-of-one-rule (process-kernel #3): 'no packet reaches a pane except through claim fence → pane fence → ACK' is enforced at one layer (doctrine) and bypassed at three (supervisor send_and_verify main.rs:1223, cron refill-idle-panes, hand packets) — sealed AdmittedSend + source lint + hook + census row + lock-owner check, each annotated with the escape it closes (ve4w, a92y, 93lo, p3f4)
description:
WHAT: **The one rule this loop's safety depends on — "no packet reaches a pane except through the admission fence (claim fence + pane fence) and the ACK stage" — is enforced at exactly ONE layer (reviewer doctrine in AGENTS.md) and bypassed at three: the resident supervisor sends with raw `tmux send-keys` / `ntm --robot-send` inside `send_and_verify` without holding `pane-dispatch-fence` (`crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs:1223-1254`; grep `pane_dispatch_fence|pane-dispatch-fence` in that file → 0 outside the census list at `lib.rs:518`), the cron dispatcher `refill-idle-panes --apply` sends unclaimed and unfenced (`crates/refill-idle-panes/src/main.rs:278-281`; grep `fence` in that crate → 0), and 26 hand packets/day are a third path with no fence at all (pass 2).** Enforce the rule at every level with the escape path each layer closes written beside it — the rigor-atlas prescription `layered-enforcement-of-one-rule`, **#3 for `process-kernel`**, which **no bead names** (0 open-bead matches for `layered enforcement|deny.toml|cargo-deny`; `ve4w` names the missing SHARED fence, i.e. the mechanism, not its enforcement).

INVARIANT (PROTOCOL L1, falsifiable): *In this workspace there is no reachable path from a bead to a pane's stdin that does not pass, in one process and in this order, `dispatch_claim_fence::authorize` → `pane-dispatch-fence` (flock held across probe→send) → transport → `ack_stage::assess`; a source file that spawns `tmux send-keys`, `ntm --robot-send`, or writes a pane's tty outside the one sanctioned sender crate fails the build, the pre-commit hook, and the gate census independently.*

KERNEL SHAPE: not one function — a sealed sender plus nets under it.
```
// layer 0 — the kernel: the ONLY type that can perform a send is unconstructible outside the sender crate
pub struct AdmittedSend { permit: DispatchPermit, fence: PaneFenceGuard, key: DispatchKey }   // fields private; no Default
impl AdmittedSend { pub fn perform(self, cx: &Cx) -> TransportReceipt }                          // consumes the guard
mod sealed { pub trait Sender {} }   // enumerated in this file and nowhere else (frankenterm's RuntimeProof shape)
```
Layers (each annotated with the hole it closes):
1. Doctrine — `AGENTS.md` "file → claim → dispatch" (already present, :159-190) — informs reviewers; closes nothing mechanically.
2. Type — `AdmittedSend` is the only path to `perform`; closes "a new crate calls tmux directly" at compile time.
3. Source lint — `kernel-bypass-gate` extended from operator commands to SOURCE: an ast-grep/`grep --no-index` rule refusing `Command::new("tmux")`/`"ntm"` with `send-keys`/`--robot-send` outside `crates/<sender>/`; closes "someone re-adds a raw send in a sibling crate".
4. Hook — `.git/hooks/pre-commit` (`no-shell-gate`'s trigger) runs layer 3; closes "the lint exists but nobody ran it".
5. Census — `census_gates` gains a row `sender-uniqueness` that counts send sites and is RED when the count ≠ 1 (anti-vacuity: 0 is an ERROR); closes "the hook is per-clone and this clone has none" (`AGENTS.md:151-155`).
6. Runtime — `pane-dispatch-fence`'s lock file records `owner={sender_crate}@{build_id}`; a send whose lock owner is not the sanctioned sender is refused by the ACK stage as `UnsanctionedSender`; closes "a stale binary from a previous install still sends".

MIRROR EXEMPLAR TO COPY (KNOW, opened 2026-09-02):
- `/Volumes/ZestData/dicklesworthstone-mirror/frankenterm/deny.toml:12-16` — *"Layered enforcement (each layer catches different escape paths): 1. AGENTS.md doctrine — informs reviewers. 2. wa_22x4r_no_tokio_test_in_supported_paths.rs — catches new `#[tokio::test]` attributes. 3. dependency_eradication.rs / forbidden_dep_guards.rs —"* … the annotation-per-layer is the transferable part.
- `frankenterm/crates/frankenterm-core/src/runtime_proof.rs:56-60` — *"Sealed supertrait. Lives in a private module so that no downstream crate (including `tokio`) can ever satisfy `RuntimeProof`. The set of types that implement `Sealed` is enumerated in this file and nowhere else."* — layer 2's shape.
- PRESCRIPTIONS.md `layered-enforcement-of-one-rule` KERNEL SHAPE: *"deny.toml (dependency ban) + sgconfig.yml (ast-grep) + runtime_proof.rs (the sealed trait and its compile_fail doctest) + docs/proofs/runtime-proof-soundness.lean (the closure proof). The sealed module is the kernel; everything else is a net under it."*

LOCAL STATE TODAY (path:line at HEAD):
- Layer 0/2 ABSENT: `pane-dispatch-fence` is a separate BINARY wrapping an arbitrary `command` (`crates/pane-dispatch-fence/src/main.rs:171-189`), so the fence is opt-in per caller; three callers opt in (`fast-dispatch/src/main.rs:834-836`, `loop-tick/src/lib.rs:429`, `tick-dispatch/src/main.rs:588-589`) and the two LIVE dispatchers do not.
- Layer 3 PARTIAL: `kernel-bypass-gate` classifies OPERATOR commands in a PreToolUse hook (`crates/kernel-only-operator-hook/src/lib.rs:1-8`), not source files.
- Layer 5 PARTIAL: `no-shell-gate/tests/wired_lanes.rs:1-9` proves lane reachability by count; the census (`omp-orchestrator/src/lib.rs:665-947`) has no sender-uniqueness row.
- Layer 6 ABSENT: `acquire` writes `owner={owner} pid=` (`pane-dispatch-fence/src/main.rs:127`) — the owner is a free string the caller chooses.

LOCAL DEFECTS THIS WOULD HAVE PREVENTED (already filed — cite, do not re-file):
- `ve4w` — cron refill and the supervisor both sent `oj6.3`, into different panes; `fc-22l` sent 82× to pane 1. Layer 2 makes the refill's raw send uncompilable; layer 6 makes its lock owner refusable.
- pass 2 (`a92y`, `elq6`) — 26 hand packets, 0/34 from a template, ACK text hand-typed in two media: the third path exists because nothing refuses a send that skipped the renderer and the fence.
- `93lo` — every dispatch omitted the ACK protocol: a sender that is not `AdmittedSend` cannot be forced to emit the ACK line; one that is, can.
- `p3f4` (closed) declared `refill-idle-panes` forbidden; it is still scheduled at `8,28,48 * * * *` (`ve4w`). A rule with one layer is a rule that was declared, not enforced — `AGENTS.md:919-931` "every gate proves it bites" applied to the dispatch rule itself.

WHY: KINDS.md process-kernel rigor pattern for ntm is *"State-machine transition guards as the only enforcement, reviewed by reading"* (:1092) — the honest floor. frankenterm's pattern is six layers for one rule, each naming its escape path. Today's loop has ONE dispatch rule that matters and it is enforced by reading. `ve4w` will land a shared fence; without layers 2–6 the next dispatcher (there have been three in two days) will bypass it the same way `refill-idle-panes` bypassed `dispatch-claim-fence`.

RESULT CLASS THAT MAY BE CLAIMED (KINDS.md:1094): *a first-party crate cannot reach the banned path by dependency, import, test attribute or sealed-bound API.* DO NOT CLAIM: that a send outside this workspace (a human at a keyboard, a control-plane binary) is prevented — layer 6 refuses its ACK, it does not stop the keystroke; that the layers prove delivery (`advisory-lease-with-written-no-claim`).

ACCEPTANCE:

One sender crate exposes `AdmittedSend` with private fields and a sealed trait; `omp-orchestrator::send_and_verify` and every other in-workspace send are rewritten to construct it (which requires the permit, the fence guard, and the key) — a `compile_fail` doctest shows a caller that builds `AdmittedSend` without the fence does not compile.

4. Layer 6: the fence lock records `owner=<sender>@<build_id>`; `ack_stage::assess` receives the owner and returns `Indeterminate { reason: UnsanctionedSender }` when it is not the sanctioned sender — a new `ReceiptReason` variant, exhaustively matched.
5. Each layer carries, beside its code, a one-line comment naming the escape path it closes (copy the `deny.toml:12` style verbatim); a test asserts all six annotations exist (structure-keyed: a marker attribute or const, not a grep for prose).
6. And the counter-case is equally measured: `main.rs` was verified to have ZERO wildcard match arms, so its exhaustive match caught a genuine omission at compile time when two new decision variants were added. title: Wire one real caller: durable Agent Mail dispatch-result notification in omp-orchestrator
description:
# WHAT

Wire ONE real caller of `agent-mail-native` into production code in
`crates/omp-orchestrator`, closing the BUILT != WIRED gap on commit `d0a88e5`.

The call site is `report_dispatch_result` in `crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs`
— on the live dispatch path, reachable from `run_cycle`, not from a test and not
from an example.

# WHY HERE

`notify_dispatch_result` already sends a dispatch-result courtesy notification
over `ntm --robot-send`, and that function's OWN doc comment records why it
cannot be trusted:

> "Pane 4 measured a `--robot-send` that returned `successful:["1"]` and never
> arrived, so the send cannot be the authority for anything."

So the orchestrator's dispatch-result notification currently rides a transport
measured to report success while delivering nothing, and its only durable trace
is a local heartbeat row. Agent Mail is durable truth with a queryable
per-recipient receipt that separates `persisted` / `signaled` / `acknowledged`.
Adding a durable notification here is therefore not decoration: it is the one
place where the existing transport is known to lie and where a durable receipt
answers the exact question the ledger row cannot.

# THE FOUR THINGS THE WIRED PATH MUST DEMONSTRATE

1. DAEMON PATH PRIMARY — the send and the receipt read-back both go through
   `agent-mail-native`'s authenticated MCP HTTP client. No CLI on the write path.
2. CLI AS DIFFERENTIAL ORACLE, NEVER FALLBACK — `oracle::cli_position_now` is
   consulted only to cross-check the daemon's cursor reading. A daemon failure
   NEVER falls back to the CLI; it degrades to a named ledger row. Falling back
   would reproduce the exact fail-open that made `am agent start` report an auth
   failure as absence.
3. RECEIVER OBSERVATION AND TRACKER READBACK STAY SEPARATE — this change adds a
   THIRD, independent fact (the mail system's own durable receipt) and merges it
   into neither `post_send_observation` (pane observation, via
   `receiver-receipt`) nor `read_ack_readback` (tracker comment read-back). No
   authority is derived from another.
4. TIMEOUT AND CURSOR RULES — the client is constructed with an EXPLICIT
   caller-owned request timeout and never inherits a default; the cursor is
   carried as a `ResumePoint` bound to its recipient, never as a bare integer.

# INVARIANTS THAT MUST NOT BE LOST AT THE CALL SITE

- `isError: true` rides HTTP 200, so the caller consumes the typed `MailError`
  terminal and never an HTTP status.
- The double decode at `result.content[0].text` stays inside the binding; the
  call site does not re-implement it.
- An absent or empty result must NOT read as a healthy no-op. An unconfigured
  sender identity produces a NAMED refusal row, not a silent skip — the
  call-site analogue of `MailError::EmptyCatalogue` making a zero-endpoint pass
  unrepresentable.
- A caller-owned deadline is what KEEPS the cursor: measured, the kernel
  self-terminates at 300.34s with `TIMEOUT` and `cursor_info` present, while an
  external SIGTERM yields `CANCELED` with the cursor gone.

# DEGRADATION CONTRACT

The ledger is the authority and must never be lost to a notification failure —
the precedent is `report_dispatch_result`'s existing unconditional heartbeat
write, added because a blocked notify used to erase the record. Every Agent Mail
failure therefore becomes a distinct `DISPATCH_RESULT_MAIL_*` heartbeat row and
is never returned as the caller's error. Critically, no failure may read as
"delivered": `Unreachable`, `Unauthorized`, `MissingCredential` and `TimedOut`
are each their own row.

# ON ack-spine (asked by SnowyCanyon)

`ack-spine::authorities` models transport / observational-delivery / ack as
non-substitutable, which is the right shape — but `AckEvidence::new` requires
one independently obtained fact from EACH of the three, and at
`report_dispatch_result` only the transport fact and the new mail receipt are in
hand; pane observation and tracker read-back happen earlier, in
`send_and_verify`. Consuming it here would mean fabricating the two authorities
I do not have, which is precisely what that crate exists to forbid. Judgment:
DO NOT couple, and record `ack-spine` as a still-open BUILT != WIRED gap rather
than close it dishonestly. A forced dependency is worse than a named gap.

# ACCEPTANCE

- `agent-mail-native` appears as a real dependency of `omp-orchestrator`, and a
  non-test call site exists in `src/main.rs` reachable from `run_cycle`.
- REACHABILITY PROVEN WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL, per AGENTS.md rule 2: a grep for
  a pattern KNOWN to be wired must hit, so a zero elsewhere is evidence of
  absence rather than of a pattern that cannot match.
- `cargo test -p omp-orchestrator` and `cargo test -p agent-mail-native` green,
  counts reported.
- Unit tests for the new pure logic: recipient resolution, sender resolution
  refusal, and the MailError -> ledger-row mapping, including a test asserting no
  failure maps to a delivered row.
- Commit path-scoped with an explicit list, verified with
  `git ls-tree -r HEAD -- <path>`, never `git ls-files`.

# ADJACENT LANE

comments.text:
COVERAGE-AUDIT — one real caller wired, and it fires live.
Implemented by AmNative (Agent Mail identity: BrightGorge, id 310).

Commits: `52c557b` (wiring, 2 files) + `a19ffb8` (live proof, 1 file).
Both path-scoped with an explicit list, both CLEAN through the multi-gate.

## THE GAP, VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY BEFORE BUILDING

I did not take the BUILT != WIRED claim on report. Measured:

- NEGATIVE: the only `agent-mail-native` mention anywhere outside the crate
  itself was a doc comment inside `path-literal-guard`. Zero consumers.
- POSITIVE CONTROL (AGENTS.md rule 2): the same grep method against a
  known-wired dependency resolved 28 files for `subprocess_contract`, so the
  zero was absence rather than a pattern that cannot match.

## THE CALL SITE AND WHY IT IS THERE

`report_dispatch_result` -> `notify_dispatch_result_durably`.

`notify_dispatch_result` already sends the dispatch result over
`ntm --robot-send`, and that function's OWN doc records why it cannot be
trusted: "Pane 4 measured a `--robot-send` that returned `successful:["1"]` and
never arrived, so the send cannot be the authority for anything." The dispatch
result's only durable trace was a local heartbeat row no third party can query.
This is the one place in the loop where the existing transport is KNOWN to lie,
which is what makes a durable notification here load-bearing rather than
decorative.

## REACHABILITY, PROVEN BY LINE NUMBER

`#[cfg(test)]` boundary is line 2153. Every hop is above it:

  main 2114 -> run_supervisor 2141 -> run_cycle 2102
       -> report_dispatch_result 1974, 1978 -> notify_dispatch_result_durably 1673

`agent_mail_native` referenced at lines 13, 16, 1587, 1596, 1599 — all
PRODUCTION. Test-only references exist at 2178/2768/2921/2943 and are
additional, not the wiring.

A PROBE OF MINE PRODUCED A FALSE ZERO DURING THIS AUDIT AND I AM RECORDING IT:
`grep -n 'cfg(test)'` returned NOTHING against a file that contains
`#[cfg(test)]`, because this harness's grep defaults to ERE and the parentheses
are a capture GROUP, so the pattern matched the literal `cfgtest`. `-F` fixed
it. That is the exact trap named in my brief and I still walked into it; the
first boundary I computed was empty, which would have labelled every line
"test-only".

## LIVE FIRE — the production function, tick 99

```
DISPATCH_RESULT_RECORDED        source_pane=99 bead=...-7n5b
DISPATCH_RESULT_NOTIFY_DEGRADED ... no-such-ntm: process not found
DISPATCH_RESULT_MAIL_PERSISTED  recipient=BrightGorge message_id=40837
                                persisted=true signaled=false cursor=5219
                                oracle_skew=0
```

THE PANE TRANSPORT FAILED AND THE DURABLE NOTIFICATION SUCCEEDED IN THE SAME
TICK, and the dispatch record survived both. That is a stronger demonstration
of authority separation than the design aimed at: the two notification paths are
independent, neither can erase the ledger, and a pane-transport failure no
longer implies the receiver went untold.

The test calls the PRODUCTION `report_dispatch_result`, not a reimplementation,
so the pass is evidence about the wired call site. It deliberately does not run
the supervisor loop — dispatching real work to real panes is not something a
test may do.

## THE FOUR REQUIRED PROPERTIES

1. DAEMON PRIMARY — send and receipt read-back both go through the
   authenticated MCP client. `message_id=40837 persisted=true` is the daemon's
   own record read back after the send. No CLI on the write path.
2. CLI AS DIFFERENTIAL ORACLE, NEVER FALLBACK — `oracle_skew=0` is
   `oracle::cli_position_now` agreeing with the daemon at cursor 5219. A CLI
   failure degrades the cross-check to `None` and leaves the daemon
   authoritative; it is never substituted. A fallback would re-create the
   fail-open where an auth failure reads as absence.
3. AUTHORITIES SEPARATE — the mail receipt is a THIRD independently obtained
   fact, merged into neither `post_send_observation` (pane observation, via
   `receiver-receipt`) nor `read_ack_readback` (tracker read-back). No
   authority is derived from another. The live run proves the separation
   empirically: one failed while the other succeeded.
4. TIMEOUT AND CURSOR RULES — an explicit caller-owned `MAIL_REQUEST_TIMEOUT`,
   never an inherited default, because owning the deadline is what keeps the
   cursor; and `cursor=5219` was read for a NAMED recipient, never as a bare
   integer.

## THE INVARIANTS THAT SURVIVED THE CALL SITE

- The caller consumes the typed `MailError` terminal, never an HTTP status —
  required because `isError: true` rides HTTP 200.
- The double decode at `result.content[0].text` stays inside the binding; the
  call site does not re-implement it.
- An absent result is NOT a healthy no-op: an unset sender identity is a NAMED
  refusal (`sender_identity_unset searched=AGENT_MAIL_AGENT,AGENT_NAME`) before
  any I/O. That is the call-site form of `EmptyCatalogue` — a supervisor that
  quietly stopped notifying looks exactly like one with nothing to report.
- Every failure gets its OWN row and none can read as delivered. `Unreachable`
  and `Unauthorized` are deliberately distinct: one means start the daemon, the
  other means find the token, and collapsing them is the defect this whole lane
  began with.

## A DESIGN CHANGE MADE FOR A MEASURED HAZARD, NOT TIDINESS

The sender identity moved into `Config` (resolved once at startup from
`AGENT_MAIL_AGENT` / `AGENT_NAME`) instead of being read at the call site. A
unit test reaching the dispatch path while `AGENT_NAME` happened to be exported
would have sent REAL mail and registered a temp fixture path as a project in
the live 136-project store. The fixture sets it empty deliberately, so unit
tests exercise the durable notification as a NAMED degradation and the real
path is proven only against the live daemon.

## PRE-EXISTING RED TEST FOUND AND FIXED — NOT INTRODUCED HERE

`dispatch_result_report_requires_a_successful_ntm_send_to_pane_one` asserted
`DISPATCH_RESULT_REPORTED`, a string NO production path has ever written.
`git log -S` shows that assertion and the actual row name
`DISPATCH_RESULT_RECORDED` were introduced by the SAME commit — `757357d`,
2026-09-01 22:02, 14 commits before this work. The test was BORN RED and had
been failing for roughly eight hours, in the dispatch path. Corrected to the
row the code emits rather than renaming two production sites to satisfy a typo.

Another instance of the class the fleet is hunting: a red test that nobody ran.

## ack-spine NOT COUPLED, WITH A REASON

`ack_spine::authorities` models transport / observational-delivery / ack as
non-substitutable, which is the right shape. But `AckEvidence::new` requires
one INDEPENDENTLY OBTAINED fact from each, and at `report_dispatch_result` only
the transport fact and the new mail receipt exist — pane observation and tracker
read-back happen earlier, in `send_and_verify`. Consuming it here would mean
fabricating the two authorities I do not hold, which is exactly what that crate
exists to forbid. `ack-spine` stays a NAMED BUILT != WIRED gap; the honest call
site for it is inside `send_and_verify`, which is BlueLantern's path.

## TESTS

`cargo test -p omp-orchestrator`: 99 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored across all
targets (39 lib + 39 bin + 1 + 3 + 3 + 2 + 8 + 4).
`cargo test -p agent-mail-native`: 61 + 8 + 2 passed + 1 doc / 0 failed /
4 ignored.
Live: `mail_notification_fires_against_the_live_daemon` 1 passed.

New unit tests cover recipient resolution (pane map wins over configured
receiver; unresolvable refuses rather than guessing), sender-identity refusal,
and the MailError -> row mapping including an assertion that NO failure maps to
a persisted row and that `Unreachable` != `Unauthorized`.

## RETRACTION I OWE THIS BEAD

My earlier claim that `persisted=true signaled=false` is a silent-notification
DEFECT is WRONG, and I propagated it three times. MailMining read the
version-matched source: `messaging.rs:4219` and `sync.rs:134-138` at v0.3.31
document that exact state for a DEBOUNCED signal — only the append-only receipt
ledger establishes `signaled`, and the mutable `.signal` file is intentionally
not read. Specified behaviour, not a gap. Consumer rule: `signaled` is not a
delivery oracle, `acknowledged` is.

Nothing shipped refuses on `signaled` — the binding only exposes a predicate
and this caller merely records the value in a ledger row — so no healthy
debounced traffic is blocked. The error is confined to my doc comments in
`agent-mail-native`, which I will correct once GreenFrog's uncommitted identity
work in that crate lands (I released my reservation there after `d0a88e5`).

## OWNERSHIP DISCLOSURE

`.flywheel/AUTONOMOUS-WAVE.md:59` assigns `%1414` BlueLantern
`crates/omp-orchestrator/**`. I edited it on SnowyCanyon's explicit assignment,
and my exclusive Agent Mail reservation on
`crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs` returned `conflict_free: true` with
`total_conflicting_reservations: 0` (ids 110970/110971, still held). The live
reservation system and the static pane map therefore disagree about that path.
Raised to SnowyCanyon to arbitrate; I will hand over and re-land through
BlueLantern if asked.

## NO-CLAIM BOUNDARY

- The live test is `#[ignore]`d, so a default `cargo test` proves the
  degradation path, not the delivery path.
- The wired notification is proven from `report_dispatch_result` downward. It
  has NOT been observed firing from a real `run_cycle` tick of the resident
  supervisor, because running the supervisor would dispatch real work to real
  panes.
- `verified_sender` is still false: the caller does not supply a
  `sender_token`, so the FROM is unproven even though it is now signed in the
  body text.
- `oracle_skew=0` is one reading at one instant, not a sustained lane.
- No claim about the pane courtesy transport being fixed. It is still the
  measured-unreliable path; this work makes its failure survivable, not absent.

VERDICT: wired, live-fired, and left `in_progress` for a non-implementer to
grade.

comments.text:
CORRECTION 2 — THE "TWO AUTHORITIES OVER ONE STORE" FINDING IS FALSE.

This is the most consequential error on this bead, because it was adopted as
the house pattern for this dependency on my evidence, and because it also
downgrades this bead's own acceptance evidence.

## WHAT THE EARLIER COMMENTS CLAIM

> The `am` CLI does not talk to the authenticated daemon. It carries no bearer
> token, gets 401 from `/mcp/`, and reads `storage.sqlite3` directly. Two
> authorities over one store.

False in its central mechanism.

## WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE

1. THE CLI CALLS THE DAEMON BY DEFAULT. Mirror 0.3.32,
   `crates/mcp-agent-mail-cli/src/lib.rs:9559`:

       check_inbox_should_use_daemon(direct, daemon_reachable) = !direct || daemon_reachable

   Without `--direct` that evaluates `!false = true`, so the daemon path is the
   DEFAULT and `inbox_events_direct` (the SQLite read) is the exception.

2. IT USES A ROUTE I NEVER PROBED: `/api/`, not `/mcp/`. Proven by pointing the
   CLI at a dead port:

       am inbox-events ... --port 9999
       rc=1
       {"status":"error","code":"inbox_events_unavailable",
        "message":"transport failure calling http://127.0.0.1:9999/api/:
                   Connection reset by peer (os error 54)"}

   A CLI reading SQLite directly cannot care about a TCP port.

3. IT HAD A TOKEN THE WHOLE TIME, AND SO DID EVERY COMMAND I RAN.
   `printenv HTTP_BEARER_TOKEN` -> SET (65 chars). `AGENT_MAIL_TOKEN` -> SET.
   `lib.rs:82140-82143` reads exactly those two variables and nothing else.

## ROOT CAUSE, AND IT IS THE WORST OF THE NIGHT

My single attempt to inspect the environment was
`env | grep -i -E 'agent_mail|AM_'`, which **dcg DENIED** as a policy
violation. I never retried. I then asserted "the CLI carries no token" as a
measured fact, built an architecture on it, wrote it into this crate's module
docs, and broadcast it to five agents.

A DENIED PROBE IS NOT A NEGATIVE RESULT. I treated a tool refusal as evidence
of absence — precisely the shape of the `am agent start` false negative I was
so pleased to have explained. `printenv` was available the entire time.

## WHAT THIS DOES TO THIS BEAD'S ACCEPTANCE EVIDENCE

The differential oracle is weaker than claimed, and the earlier comment
oversells it. `oracle_skew=0` is NOT two independent authorities agreeing about
a store. It is TWO HTTP ROUTES ON THE SAME DAEMON PROCESS, authenticated with
the SAME token, reading the same in-process state. It demonstrates that one
daemon is self-consistent across `/mcp/` and `/api/`. It does not corroborate
the store.

Everything else in the acceptance evidence stands: the live round-trip, the
cursor advance with no replay and no gap, the 45-tool enumeration with
anti-vacuity, the typed `Unreachable` refusal, the ack and the delivery
receipt.

## WHAT SURVIVES, INCLUDING TWO NEW FINDINGS

- `/api/` and `/mcp/` are distinct routes on one daemon, and BOTH require auth
  (401 without a token, verified on both).
- NEW: `--direct` is INVERTED relative to its own help text. Help says "Allow a
  direct SQLite read only when no daemon is reachable", but
  `daemon_reachable = direct && process_owner_port_reachable(...)`
  (lib.rs:9558), so passing `--direct` is what ENABLES the daemon attempt with
  SQLite as fallback, while OMITTING it takes the daemon unconditionally with
  NO fallback. The flag does close to the opposite of what it reads like.
- `am health` genuinely does build a throwaway `health-probe.sqlite3` and never
  contacts the daemon. That measurement was correct; generalising it from
  `health` to the whole CLI is where the error entered.
- The DESIGN of this crate is still right for reasons independent of the false
  premise: no subprocess per call, typed terminals rather than exit codes, the
  double decode and `isError`-on-200 handling in one place, a caller-owned
  deadline, and cursors that cannot travel without their recipient.

## FOR OTHER LANES

Any CLI-derived figure cited tonight — JourneySpine's four-recipient cursor
table, BlueLantern's census, Main's doctrine note — came from the DAEMON and is
therefore MORE trustworthy than I said, not less. Nobody needs to re-measure.
The numbers were fine; my account of where they came from was not.

## PENDING EDITS, QUEUED BEHIND A RESERVATION

`src/lib.rs` states the false architecture as measured fact. That file and
`src/journey.rs` are under GreenFrog's exclusive reservation until ~07:50Z
(K0 identity, omp-orchestrator-3kpc). Three corrections are queued for one
pass once released, requested via Agent Mail 40845 (ack_required,
verified_sender true):

1. delete the over-strict `verify_resume_continuity` guard (comment 441);
2. correct the `is_persisted_but_unsignalled` doc wording (comment 441);
3. replace the two-authorities module documentation with the corrected
   single-daemon / two-routes account above.

## THE TALLY, RECORDED AGAINST MYSELF

Four diagnosis errors: mail_pending, `signaled`, the cursor clamp, and this.
The first three were "measured correctly, diagnosed without reading the
definition of correct behaviour". This one is worse — never measured at all,
because a probe was refused and I proceeded as though the refusal were an
answer.

Two rules, then. Before calling anything a defect, read the definition of
correct behaviour. And when a probe is DENIED or errors, the result is UNKNOWN:
retry differently or say unknown, never infer the negative.

comments.text:
FOURTH CORRECTION LANDED — the decorative CLI oracle is deleted from the live
path. Commit `5084a2c`, 2 files, path-scoped, CLEAN through the multi-gate.

## WHY IT WENT

Its whole value was "a second authority corroborates the store". That
authority does not exist. The `am` CLI calls the SAME daemon on an alternate
route (`/api/` rather than `/mcp/`) with the same bearer token:
`check_inbox_should_use_daemon(direct, reachable) = !direct || reachable`, so
without `--direct` the daemon is the unconditional path. Proven by pointing the
CLI at a dead port — it fails closed with
`transport failure calling http://127.0.0.1:9999/api/`.

So the cross-check put one daemon against itself, through a process spawn,
under one credential, and reported it in a field called `oracle_skew`. It
measured ROUTE SELF-CONSISTENCY and was read as CORROBORATION. The `skew=0` in
this bead's earlier acceptance evidence never had the meaning I gave it.

MailMining's argument for deleting rather than renaming, which I accept: a
decorative oracle is worse than none, because it LAUNDERS SELF-CONSISTENCY AS
AGREEMENT. The name outlives the exchange that debunked it, and the next agent
reads `oracle` as independent evidence. Same trap as `signaled`, one layer up.

## WHAT CHANGED

- deleted the `oracle::cli_position_now` call, the `oracle_skew` field on
  `DurableNotice`, and `oracle_skew=` from the
  `DISPATCH_RESULT_MAIL_PERSISTED` row. One fewer process spawn per dispatch;
  nothing on this path shells out any more.
- corrected two false claims in the same doc block: `signaled: false` as a
  silent-delivery defect (it is documented debounce behaviour), and the
  "two authorities over one store" architecture.
- `crates/agent-mail-native/src/oracle.rs` now OPENS with
  "⛔ SLATED FOR DELETION. DO NOT ADOPT. NOT AN ORACLE." and the full
  retraction, because dropping `pub mod oracle;` needs `lib.rs`, still under
  GreenFrog's exclusive reservation (to 07:50Z). The caller is already gone,
  so nothing depends on it.

## RE-PROVEN LIVE AFTER THE CHANGE

I altered the live path, so I re-ran the production function rather than
trusting the previous run:

    DISPATCH_RESULT_RECORDED        source_pane=99 bead=...-7n5b
    DISPATCH_RESULT_NOTIFY_DEGRADED ... no-such-ntm: process not found
    DISPATCH_RESULT_MAIL_PERSISTED  recipient=BrightGorge message_id=40850
                                    persisted=true signaled=false cursor=5239

Fresh message, fresh cursor, `oracle_skew` absent. The pane transport still
fails in the same tick while the durable notification succeeds, so the
authority separation this bead exists to demonstrate is unaffected — and it
never depended on the oracle.

Tests: `omp-orchestrator` 99 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored across all targets;
`agent-mail-native` 61 + 8 + 2 passed / 0 failed / 4 ignored. The
`unused import: dispatch_silence_watch::SilenceVerdict` warning is unchanged
from HEAD (7 occurrences in both) and untouched by this diff. Five failures in
`--test packet` are a sibling's untracked work-in-progress
(`src/packet.rs`, `tests/packet.rs`), not touched and not mine.

## STILL QUEUED BEHIND GreenFrog's LOCK

journey.rs (to 07:56Z) and lib.rs (to 07:50Z):
1. delete `journey::verify_resume_continuity` and its call in `resume_from`,
   keeping `MailError::CursorExpired` purely as a DECODE of the daemon's
   refusal;
2. correct the `is_persisted_but_unsignalled` doc wording;
3. replace the two-authorities module documentation in `lib.rs`;
4. remove `pub mod oracle;`, the `oracle.rs` file, and the `#[ignore]`d
   `daemon_and_cli_oracle_agree_on_the_tail` test.

Requested via Agent Mail 40845 (ack_required, verified_sender true).

## ACCEPTANCE EVIDENCE ON THIS BEAD, CORRECTED

The `oracle_skew=0` line in comment 436 should be read as withdrawn. Everything
else there stands: the reachability proof against the cfg(test) boundary, the
live fire with the pane transport failing in the same tick, the typed
MailError->row mapping with no failure able to report as persisted, and the
named-refusal-before-I/O behaviour on an unset sender identity.

THREE CONSEQUENCES, IN DESCENDING URGENCY. (1) THE SELF-GRADE GUARD'S SOUNDNESS IS UNMEASURED. grade --claim must refuse a self-grade; if every pane resolves to one agent name then author and grader are indistinguishable by identity, and the guard's correctness depends on whatever it actually keys on. If it keys on PANE ID it is safe; if it keys on AGENT NAME it is currently UNSOUND and that is a P0 correction to work landed an hour ago, not an enhancement. Determining which is the first deliverable.   ~/.cargo/bin/cargo test -p no-shell-gate --test wired_lanes
  -> EXIT 101, and NO test result line at all. The error:
     failed to load manifest for workspace member crates/ntm-fleet-monitor
       Caused by: failed to load manifest for dependency loop-coverage
       Caused by: failed to read crates/loop-coverage/Cargo.toml
       Caused by: No such file or directory (os error 2)

PROXIMATE CAUSE: extraction (omp-orchestrator-815) copied ntm-fleet-monitor without loop-coverage. ntm-fleet-monitor holds a PATH dependency on it, so cargo cannot load the workspace. crates/ at that moment: composer-typed, fleet-composite, loop-queue-filter, no-shell-gate, ntm-fleet-monitor, pane-dispatch-fence. AGENTS.md already states the rule: '14 leaves with zero path deps; 6 with exactly one -- ntm-fleet-monitor -> loop-coverage ... Extract leaves first.' The proximate fix (copy loop-coverage; verified clean, 0 files matching /Users/josh, and itself a leaf) was dispatched at 07:37Z and is not what this bead is for.

THE ACTUAL DEFECT, and it is a gate-integrity hole: per AmberGate's -4ak decision #2, the gate's enforcement surfaces are (a) cargo test, where this_repo_is_clean re-scans the real git index on every run, and (b) CI. There is deliberately no build.rs, for a good reason (a build-script fingerprint goes stale and would fake enforcement). But that means the gate's ONLY local surface is the test harness -- and a workspace that cannot load produces NO test harness. So for the duration of a broken manifest the repo is simultaneously unbuildable AND unprotected: a tracked .sh or .py could be committed and nothing would refuse it. The guard is switched off by a mistake in a completely unrelated crate, and nothing announces it.

This is the fail-closed-vs-fail-silent distinction. 'The gate said no' and 'the gate could not run' are different outcomes that currently print the same thing: a nonzero cargo exit. An agent that sees red, assumes it is the gate, and moves on has learned nothing; an agent that sees red and assumes it is a build error deletes the wrong thing. Same shape as the anti-vacuity rule this repo already enforces (an empty scan set is an ERROR, never a pass) -- here the scan set is not empty, it is UNREACHABLE, which is worse because it is invisible.

WHY: the whole premise of -4ak landing FIRST on an empty tree was that the repo can never accrete a shell script. That guarantee is only as strong as the gate's ability to RUN. Extraction is precisely the operation that mutates the workspace 23 times, so the window in which the gate can be dark is the window in which the most files are moving.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. Extraction runs `cargo metadata --no-deps` (or equivalent) after EVERY crate copy and requires exit 0 before the next copy. A copy that breaks workspace load is reverted or completed immediately, never left overnight.
2. The gate distinguishes CANNOT-RUN from REFUSED. Running it against an unloadable workspace must produce a distinct, named outcome -- not a bare nonzero that is indistinguishable from a .sh being caught. State the exit code or marker for each.
3. A CI job asserts the workspace LOADS as its own step, before and independently of the gate step, so a manifest break is attributed to itself rather than surfacing as a mysterious gate failure.
4. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD, in-tree, both directions: (a) delete a path-dependency's Cargo.toml, assert the load check goes RED and names the missing member; (b) with the workspace loadable, stage a tracked .sh and assert the gate goes RED via this_repo_is_clean. Leg (b) must PASS while (a) is broken only if the two outcomes are genuinely distinguishable -- if it cannot even run, that is the finding, and the test must assert the distinct cannot-run code.
5. MUTATION: remove the load check and assert leg 4(a) goes RED. Restore byte-identically, sha256 both sides.
6. NO-CLAIM: this covers workspace LOADABILITY, not compilation. A workspace can load and still fail to build, and the gate's reachability under a compile error in an unrelated crate is a separate question -- measure it, do not assume it. Also: this says nothing about the CI surface's own reachability, which is -a3p's territory.

title: no gate refuses git worktree add: the zero-worktree policy is enforced only by agents reading AGENTS.md
description: AGENTS.md now carries Joshua's binding zero-worktree policy (2026-09-03, commit 62cf804) with an explicit NO-CLAIM: nothing in-tree refuses a git worktree add, and .git/hooks cannot observe a checkout being created elsewhere. Per AGENTS.md's third rule, a policy with no reachable trigger is the class this repo distrusts most -- it reads as protected while being enforced by reading comprehension. Candidate mechanisms, none built: a pre-commit leg refusing when git worktree list returns more than one entry whose path is not this checkout; a PreToolUse hook denying a Bash command matching worktree add; a periodic census row. Each needs a fires-on-known-bad leg plus a known-GOOD leg, since the sanctioned exception is a TEST that creates a worktree and deletes it -- so a gate that refuses all creation is over-strict and will be routed around. The known-good leg is the hard part and is the reason this is filed rather than built. NO-CLAIM: filing this does not enforce the policy; today the policy is honoured by convention only, and the measured state (HEAD=main, one worktree, zero branches, zero stashes, zero in-tree worktree-add call sites) is compliance without a mechanism.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Build one enforcement mechanism (choose: pre-commit leg, PreToolUse Bash-matcher hook denying `git worktree add`, or census row) and name which was chosen in the bead close-out; the other candidates must be filed as separate beads or explicitly dropped with reason, never left implied-covered.

2. KNOWN-BAD leg, measured live: from a clean checkout run `git worktree add /tmp/wt-probe-$$ HEAD` (or invoke the hook with that exact Bash command string) and show the gate refuses with a non-zero exit and a message naming the offending worktree path. The currently-measured state — HEAD=main, one worktree, zero branches, zero stashes, zero in-tree worktree-add call sites — is NOT evidence the gate works: it is a passing environment with no trigger pulled, and a gate that never runs also produces that output. The refusal must be observed against a real second worktree/command, not asserted from the compliant baseline.

3. KNOWN-GOOD leg, measured live: the sanctioned exception — a TEST that creates a worktree and removes it — must PASS. Demonstrate the actual test (or a faithful stand-in registered as such) running end-to-end under the gate with exit 0. Record precisely how good is distinguished from bad: path prefix under a temp/test root, an env marker set only by the test harness, or a same-process create+delete window. A gate that refuses all creation is over-strict, will be routed around, and fails this bead.

4. Anti-vacuity: the scan that enumerates worktrees (`git worktree list --porcelain`) must never return an empty or unparsed set silently. Zero rows, a parse failure, or a missing `git` binary must raise a typed error (e.g. `WorktreeCensusError::Empty` / `::Unparsable`) that fails the gate. Assert with a test that forces the empty/garbled case and expects the error variant, not a pass.

5. Mutation-to-RED: invert or neuter the refusal predicate (e.g. flip the `> 1` comparison, or make the Bash matcher never match `worktree add`), re-run the known-bad leg, and record the RED output verbatim. Restore byte-identically and prove it with a checksum of the changed file taken before mutation and after restore, both printed in the close-out.

6. MEASURED-live vs fixture: the known-bad refusal, the known-good pass, and the mutation RED/restore must all be run live in this repo against real `git` state. Fixtures are permitted only for the anti-vacuity error variants (synthetic empty/garbled porcelain output) and must be labelled as fixtures.

7. Ordering/reachability: prove the gate is actually reachable on the path it claims — for a pre-commit leg, show it in the hook config and show a commit attempt blocked; for a PreToolUse hook, show the hook registered in settings and the deny returned on the matching command. A mechanism present in-tree but not wired is the same NO-CLAIM this bead was filed against.

8. Update AGENTS.md to replace the NO-CLAIM ("nothing in-tree refuses a git worktree add") with the now-true statement, naming the mechanism, its trigger, and its sanctioned-exception carve-out; if any gap remains (e.g. `.git/hooks` still cannot observe a checkout created outside this repo), restate that residual gap explicitly as a narrowed NO-CLAIM and file it as its own bead.

title: Durable ledger for commit and build gate firings
description:
WHAT: Add a durable, queryable firing ledger for the commit-time and build-time gate surfaces that are not represented by the runtime heartbeat. Keep the current live census honest: runtime literals currently hit dispatch-claim-fence, while commit/build gates have separate invocation surfaces.

WHY: The original 0ayd premise claimed a 19-crate runtime census with orchestration-tick-gate as the sole emitter. That premise is invalid against current HEAD. The surviving product gap is narrower and real: no one command can answer which commit/build gate fired, what input it examined, which verdict it emitted, or which commit it guarded.

ACCEPTANCE: (1) Derive the current gate surface from the checked-out workspace and record the exact crate set, runtime-hit set, and commit/build-only set; empty discovery is CENSUS_INPUT_EMPTY. (2) Use one write_heartbeat-shaped durable writer with rows carrying gate, verdict code, input path/literal, source commit or tick, and producer surface. (3) Wire actual pre-commit and build/CI producers; a clean commit appends PASS rows and a planted no-shell or path-literal violation appends a RED row. (4) Querying no-shell-gate returns a typed row; querying a gate with no rows returns a typed EMPTY_RESULT, not a bare empty set. (5) Mutation of the gate trigger goes RED and byte-identical restoration returns the original checksum. (6) The live positive controls and runtime heartbeat remain separate authorities; no row may claim a gate never fired merely because the runtime ledger lacks that gate. (7) Record separate follow-ups for CI-only and cargo-test-only producers if they cannot land in this bead.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: derive the current gate surface and runtime-hit set from the checked-out workspace with CENSUS_INPUT_EMPTY on empty discovery; use one write_heartbeat-shaped durable writer with gate, verdict, input, and commit or tick; wire commit and build producers so clean commits append PASS rows and planted violations append RED rows; query a named gate to a typed row and a zero-row gate to typed EMPTY_RESULT; prove trigger mutation RED and byte-identical restoration; keep runtime and commit/build authorities separate; file CI-only and cargo-test-only producer followups when they cannot land here.

title: the two remaining mouth items after the inversion: wire-or-retire finding (573 LOC, 0 consumers), bitemporal+HEAD governance on StepLedger
description:
WHAT: **the two remaining mouth items after AmberGate's inversion - neither is a new crate.**

This bead originally proposed three new crates. `58u2` proved that wrong with commands, and the
scope split:
- `evidence-receipt` -> **`opsa`**: `level` + `hash` onto NUMBERS.toml's existing 34 rows. Not a crate.
- `preregistration-gate` -> **`8oz8`**: the only genuinely new crate. In flight, pane 5.
- **what remains is this bead**, and it is two wiring jobs on code that already exists.

## ITEM 1 - WIRE `finding` / `finding-dispatch`, OR RETIRE THEM WITH A REASON

**573 LOC implementing "a filed finding is a typed row", reachable from nothing.** Verified with a
positive control so the zero is not a broken probe:
```
finding           444 LOC   [[bin]]=0  main.rs=no
finding-dispatch  129 LOC   [[bin]]=0  main.rs=no
finding-dispatch as a dep in any crates/*/Cargo.toml  ->  0
positive control: subprocess-contract as a dep        -> 19    <- probe works
```
**AND THE KERNEL-ONLY RULE IS UNFOLLOWABLE BECAUSE OF IT.** AGENTS.md's KERNEL-ONLY table says file
findings through `crates/finding`, never raw `br create`. The crate ships **no bin**. Nobody can
obey the rule; every `br create` in this repo - the orchestrator's included - is an *absent
alternative*, not a handroll. AGENTS.md already confesses the shape in prose (*"which I wrote thirty
minutes earlier to make an unfiled gap impossible, then bypassed in the next tool call"*); this is
that confession with a number.

Acceptance: **either** `finding` gains a reachable entrypoint and the KERNEL-ONLY rule becomes
followable (with a fires-on-known-bad leg proving a raw `br create` is detectable), **or** both
crates are proposed for retirement with a stated reason and the AGENTS.md rule is corrected in the
same commit. **Do not leave the rule pointing at an unreachable crate.**

## ITEM 2 - BITEMPORAL FIELDS + HEAD-PARENT GOVERNANCE ON `StepLedger`, AND WIRE IT

`crates/ack-spine/src/ledger.rs` is already a 2,654-LOC append-only ledger - `StepLedger`,
`StepRecord`, `StepKind`, `to_jsonl()`, invariant at `ledger.rs:487` (*"ONE row in, ONE physical
line out"*), field-order contract hardened at `b1ce21f`. **The append-only half exists.** Absent:
```
git grep -lF when_true      -- 'crates/*/src/*'  -> 0 files
git grep -lF when_recorded  -- 'crates/*/src/*'  -> 0 files
git grep -lF valid_from     -- 'crates/*/src/*'  -> 0 files
positive control 'pub fn'                        -> 87 files
```
Atlas card `bitemporal-data`: *"Every fact carries when it was true and when it was recorded."*
Exemplar - do not re-derive: `model_guided_research/cli.py:10094,10235,10350` implements an
append-only registry whose governance check diffs the working version against the **committed HEAD
parent** and rejects history rewrite. Pull via
`./rigor evidence model_guided_research bitemporal-data`.

Acceptance: two fields on `StepRecord`; a governance check that refuses history rewrite against the
committed HEAD parent; **and `ack-spine` becomes reachable** - it is `own-bin` but unreachable from
all three installer roots (`crates/installer/src/main.rs:12` -> `omp-orchestrator`, `tick-monitor`,
`pane-truth`). Built-but-unreachable is what item 1 exists to stop; do not create a second instance
while fixing the first.

## COMMON ACCEPTANCE
1. `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, tests present.
2. Fires-on-known-bad AND a known-good leg. Attack-only ships an over-strict gate; over-strict gates
   get routed around.
3. A mutation leg anchored UNIQUELY, byte-identically restored. A benign `.replace(..., 1)` hit the
   wrong line and stayed green today: *a green mutation leg is indistinguishable from a gate that
   does not bite.*
4. Anti-vacuity: empty input is an ERROR. A skip must be visible in the DEFAULT verdict - libtest
   captures stdout of a PASSING test and `0 ignored` reads as "nothing skipped".
5. State the denominator. `--lib` hid hard breaks twice on 2026-09-02.

figure in this bead is unmeasurable until that lands, which is also why `diq0`'s 17-RED count is
currently uncomparable. The atlas mapping behind item 2 is unratified inference: `research-kernel`
covers only 2 repos and nobody has audited the stage-to-card mapping.

title: rch worker-side reaper is default-OFF and aimed at /data/projects; arm it on /Users/josh/Developer so brain stops drifting into the 5% floor
description:
WHAT: Arm rch's own worker-side reaper so `joshs-brain` stops drifting into the 5% critical floor. In `~/.config/rch/config.toml` `[remediation.pooled_target]`: `reaper_enabled = true`, `remote_base = "/Users/josh/Developer"` (our `[path_topology] canonical_root = "/"` puts pools at `/Users/josh/Developer/<repo>/.rch-target-joshs-brain-pool-*`, not the Linux default `/data/projects`), `reaper_pooled_idle_hours = 48`, `reaper_max_cache_gb = 15`; then `rch daemon restart`. Same for `zestdata-local` (the Studio, 127.0.0.1) whose pools are under the same path.

WHY: MEASURED 2026-09-01: `rch gc --dry-run --workers joshs-brain` → `base: /data/projects … would remove 0 dir(s)`; the reaper has never fired on a Mac worker. Brain held 19 GB of `.rch-target-*-pool-*` + `.rch-tmp` (5.7 G zeststream-cast, 5.1 G frankenterm-clean 3d old, 2.1 G omp-orchestrator, 2.0 G remote_compilation_helper.non-authoritative, 1.25 G control-plane/.rch-tmp …) with nothing scheduled to remove any of it; brain sits at 45.3 GB free, below rch's 5% line, so `active_project_exclusion` + `critical_pressure` leave zero admissible workers and every workspace `cargo` here exits 103. Upstream ships the reaper default-OFF "until canary-soaked"; our config never flipped it and inherited a base that cannot exist on macOS. `is_safe_reap_base("/Users/josh/Developer")` is true (rch-common/src/stale_target_reap.rs). This is the mechanism half of Josh's "impossible to get agents to clean up their build cruft" — the reaper exists and was never armed (memory: build-cruft-reapers-exist-but-are-never-armed).

ACCEPTANCE:
1. `rch gc --dry-run --workers joshs-brain` prints `base: /Users/josh/Developer` and lists ≥1 candidate dir once any pool is idle past 48h (planted known-bad: `touch -t` a throwaway `~/Developer/x/.rch-target-joshs-brain-pool-test` on brain 3 days old → it is a candidate; a 0-day pool is NOT).
2. `rch status --json | jq '.[] | select(.id=="joshs-brain") | .pressure_state'` is not `critical` 24h after arming, with `df` on brain recorded before/after in the close comment.
3. The daemon sweep is observed to fire: rchd log shows a `stale_target_reap` sweep row with `removed>0` at least once within 72h, or a typed `removed=0` with the reason.
4. Config change is recorded as an HD row (Josh approves arming an autonomous deleter on his laptop) and the diff is in the close comment. NO-CLAIM: arming the reaper caps rch's own cruft (~19 GB today); it does not free the ~780 GB of non-build data that actually holds brain under the floor.
